docs.text:
Each applied to the model, run, and restored.

weakening red W1 E2's controller puts the last enacted commandId on every record it writes, including local actions (RULES["tagOnlyEnacted"] = False) 11, among them test_links[local-dose-after-command-E2] (1/1/0 for 1/0/0), the same for E3, test_a_local_action_is_never_linked for E2 and E3, test_no_option_links_wrongly_without_a_fault, test_without_a_fault and test_note_tables_are_current W2 E2's hub drops a stored commandId on replace (RULES["keepTag"] = False) 4: test_links[effect-replaced-by-follower-E2] (0/0/1 for 1/0/0) and its E3 row, test_without_a_fault and test_note_tables_are_current

After each restore: 367 passed.

W1 is the safety case the brief named: a dose given on the phone shown as remote. Under E1 the same controller fault cannot occur, because a local action has no report; its counterpart is a report path that names the wrong record (fault-report-names-local-record), which E1 and E4 also show as a wrong link. Only E3 flags both faults. test_weakened_tagging_links_a_local_action and test_weakened_keep_tag_loses_the_link_on_replace keep both weakenings in the suite.

docs.title: 6. Safety
docs.text:
Tied to the control-loop analysis where an entry exists.

  • A local dose shown as remote, or a remote dose shown as local (HAZ-3). With no link (B0), a reader infers one, and the model shows it wrong when a local dose lands in the window or two commands are enacted in the other order: three wrong links, seven remote records shown as local. Without a controller fault, no option links wrongly, and remote records shown as local fall to 4 (E1), 1 (E2), 0 (E3) and 2 (E4). A wrong link then comes only from a controller fault in the path the option uses; E3 alone flags it.
  • A second enactment hidden (UCA-CMD-006, prevented by CM18 and CM21 at the controller). If CM21 fails, under E1 and E4 the second dose record has no link and looks like a local dose; under E2 and E3 it carries the command's id, and the command has more live records than it asked for, which a hub can show. This is the case where the record-side tag adds most.
  • An effect not yet at the hub (UCA-SYNC-SERVE-004: a caregiver sends another dose because the first has not reached the hub). Under E1, E3 and E4 the report names the effect before its record arrives, so the hub can show "enacted, record not yet received" on the command and in CM24's outstanding list; under B0 and E2 it cannot know.
  • A part-enacted command (UCA-CMD-011). With the effect listed on a failed report, a reader sees that the meal's carbs were stored although the command failed. CM7 as written would not list it.
  • A report or tag from another process (FB-CMD-002, UCA-CMD-014). E1 inherits CM7's subject check. E2's tag arrives on an ordinary record write, so a process that may write treatments may make any dose look remote unless the hub checks that the writing instance was the command's destination; under single every holder of API_SECRET is one subject, so that check sees only the instance the writer claims. E4 needs the same check on a record write.
  • The effect record changed later (UCA-SYNC-DL-003, UCA-SYNC-STORE-003). Amendment and deletion keep every option's link, because the link names the record's identity. An end written as delete and re-post loses E1's link to the new record unless the hub follows the instance (A2).

docs.title: 7. Assessment
docs.text:
E1 E2 E3 E4 links missing without a fault 4 2 0 2 where they come from no identifier before the write reply; a restart that drops the effect list; a re-post; a second enactment an uploader that cannot carry the field; a second command on the same record (a cancel) — a restart that drops the effect list; a second enactment a record shows two commands' effects yes no: one field per record yes, flagged yes changes per new command kind none one carrier, its uploader, its projection and a case as E2 none where the change lands in a controller its command module its command module and every uploader of an effect kind both its command module and one new record kind reported after final no (CM9) the record can change as E1 and E2 yes, which overlaps commands §9 item 4

E3 flags 8 pairs; 2 are wrong links, one from each controller fault, and 6 are correct links that one source did not give (a cancel on a tagged record, a re-post, a missing identifier, a restart, a second enactment, and the real dose that the faulty report left out). A reader shown a flag cannot tell the two apart without the scenario.

Three of E1's four misses have a rule that closes them. Identity's ID-ABSENT-DECISION makes identifier mandatory for registered controller instances, and every command destination is one, so upload-reply-lost-no-identifier cannot occur for a conforming controller. A rule that the controller keeps effect identities with CM21's decided ids closes restart-effects-not-kept and is one more thing CM21 already makes it keep. Resolving an effect identity to the instance it belongs to (A2) closes the re-post. The fourth, a second enactment, is CM21's failure, and only a tag on the record shows it.

docs.title: 8. Recommendation
docs.text:
A recommendation for the maintainer to decide: E1, with CM7 widened, and a record-side commandId left as an optional attribution a controller may declare later, which would make E3's flags available where it is present.

  • Why. E1 links every scenario without a fault except the four in §7, three of which have a rule that closes them. It is the cheapest to build and to keep: one member on one message, no record kind touched, seven cases, and nothing to add when a command kind is added. The change lands in the controller's command module, which is the code that must be written anyway to report; no uploader changes. It is the only option besides E4 in which the hub knows of an effect before the record arrives, which serves UCA-SYNC-SERVE-004, and the only cheap one in which a record can show two commands' effects (an override and its cancel). It follows the one path read today that names its effect record, Trio dev's reply.
  • The strongest argument against. The link lives only in the hub's command record. A record alone does not say it was remote, so an export, a second hub or a reader without command access cannot tell (in none of the 23 scenarios with a remote record, against 21 under E2), and if CM21 fails a second enactment of one command looks like a local dose, the case UCA-CMD-006 names. E2 shows both. Against that, E2 touches 12 carriers and every uploader, cannot record two commands on one record, and needs an exception to merge and PUT.
  • What would change it. Toward E2 or E3: a requirement that the remote origin of a dose survive export or travel between hubs, or evidence that controllers will fail CM21. Toward E4: a decision on commands §9 item 4 that outcomes change after a final state; then the reconciliation record is a place for both.

docs.title: 9. What the specification would say under each option
docs.text:
• E1. CM7: the report carries effect, a list of {collection, identifier} or {collection, _id} (identity I4), on any state whose command wrote a record, including failed and refused when part was enacted; the hub stores it as reported and resolves it when read; an identity that resolves to nothing is shown as not yet received. CM21: the controller keeps each command's effect identities with its decided id until its report is accepted. Identity: an effect record from a registered instance carries identifier (ID-ABSENT-DECISION). Read: a command shows its effect records; a record shows the commands that name it.
  • E2. Records: a well-known commandId field on each carrier a command can reach. Identity or sync transport: a stored commandId is kept on merge and on replace, and a write with a different value is refused. Commands: a commandId is accepted only from the destination's instance; a record from a local action carries none.
  • E3. Both, and: the hub flags a link one source gives and the other does not, when the other could have given it, and never decides between them.
  • E4. A reconciliation record kind with commandId, effect and outcome, its identifier derived from the commandId; written only by the destination's subject; re-sent and amended through the write step; shown beside the command's state, with a difference flagged.

docs.title: 10. What the prototype does not model
docs.text: Several instances or tenants, and the hub's check that a tag or report came from the destination instance. The hub following an instance across records (A2). Typed records and their projections to carriers (registration §13), where E2's field would also need a typed declaration. The late delivery failure after success (commands §9 item 4), beyond E4's ability to amend.

docs.title: Evidence-weighted approval: what a plan or proposal needs before a controller acts on it
docs.text:
Record

Record as of 2026-10-18. A point-in-time document; it is not kept up to date.

What this is: a design framework (contributor-facing). Read after the command queue and planning note (its levels in §3 and decisions in §5) and the command journeys; it leads to the commands specification, where the plan object, evidence records and approval paths would be written, and to authority §7, where standing approval becomes a grant. Snapshot — describes 2026-10-18. Status: proposed; draft for clinical review. FL1 follows the maintainer's answer of 2026-10-18 that a bounded standing bolus is acceptable with predetermined withdrawal criteria and mitigations. The risk classes (§2), the floors (§5) and the matrix (§4) are a draft that a qualified clinician reviews before anything here is relied on, specified or implemented; §9 lists exactly what that review checks. Nothing here gives a dose, a target or a setting value.

The question. CM15 refuses an approval when the hub's whole-state version differs from the proposal's basedOn. For a moment proposal that is the right check; for a plan drafted days earlier it almost never passes, because any unrelated override changes the version (journeys PL1.3, PL5.3). The maintainer's answer (2026-10-18): "We may need both, depending on different types of plans/proposals, and depending on the kinds of evidence that can be provided to confirm them. Stronger evidence for a benefit may outweigh the need for an approval with weak evidence."

The framework in one line. The approval an item needs is a function of two axes, the risk class of what it can do and the evidence class of what supports it, bounded below by floors that no evidence lowers. The controller declares the risk class; the hub enforces the approval path as process; the controller enforces the floors and everything about its own state.

docs.title: 1. Two questions evidence answers
docs.text:
An item that runs hours or days after it was drafted raises two separate questions, and evidence serves each differently:

question example in PL1 evidence that answers it Is the situation happening? (occurrence) lunch is on today's calendar and the person is at the usual place out-of-band confirmation, fresh, for this occurrence Is this change right for the situation? (appropriateness) an eating-soon target before this lunch has helped before the person's own history, an independent evaluation, a human reviewer, the controller's preview

Evidence lowers an approval path only when both questions are covered at the strength the risk class asks for. Occurrence evidence alone ("the meal is happening") says nothing about whether the change suits it; appropriateness evidence alone says nothing about today.

docs.title: 2. Axis 1: risk class (draft for clinical review)
docs.text:
A class belongs to an element kind, one separately acceptable part of a plan or proposal (an eating-soon target, a meal's carbs, a bolus), not to the plan as a whole. Severities use the S1–S4 scale of the STPA usage guide, rated higher when in doubt; hazards are those of the control-loop analysis.

class element kinds what it can do worst severity hazards and unsafe control actions R0 inform a reminder, a notification, a display of a plan or occurrence changes no therapy S1 HAZ-3 (a wrong display) R1 bounded target a temporary target, eating soon, an exercise target, each within bounds the controller declares, ending by itself moves the algorithm's target; the algorithm still decides delivery under its own limits S3 (draft) HAZ-1, UCA-CMD-003, UCA-PROP-006 R2 bounded sensitivity an override or profile percentage that scales insulin needs, within declared bounds, with an end changes how much the algorithm delivers for hours or days S3 HAZ-1, UCA-PROP-008, FB-STATE-003 R3 carbs a carb entry the algorithm may dose for announced carbs; carbs not eaten leave insulin with nothing to cover S4 (draft) HAZ-1, UCA-CMD-015, UCA-SYNC-DL-001, journey C2 R4 insulin a bolus, or any element the controller declares as delivering insulin directly delivers insulin that cannot be withdrawn once given S4 HAZ-1, UCA-CMD-001, UCA-CMD-006, UCA-PROP-007, UCA-PROP-012, UCA-SYNC-SERVE-004 R5 persistent settings basal rates, sensitivity, carb ratio, targets in the profile itself changes every later decision, with no end S4 HAZ-1, UCA-PROP-008, journey PL5 R6 safety limits the controller's own maximums (bolus, insulin on board, basal) and its closed-loop or automatic-bolus switches changes the bounds every other class is checked against S4 HAZ-1, audition §4.6

Modifiers raise the class, never lower it. An element is treated one class higher when it lasts longer than the controller's declared short duration, does not end by itself, or is outside the bounds the controller declares; and when it would increase insulin delivery where the same kind could reduce it (a lower target versus a higher one). Whether a reduction may sit one class lower than an increase is a clinical question (§9, point 4); the draft treats both alike.

Fail closed. A kind with no declared class is handled as R4. A plan's approval path is the strictest of the paths its accepted elements need, element by element (decision 4: an approval names the elements it accepts).

docs.title: 3. Axis 2: evidence class
docs.text:
Evidence is attached as evaluations (CM16): it never changes an item's state and never approves. What this framework adds is that an evaluation declares its class, so the hub can count it.

class what it is answers independent of the proposer when E0 assertion the proposer's own statement, with nothing behind it neither never E1 pattern the same situation and change recurring in the person's own history, with how often and how recently appropriateness never by itself: the proposer computed it E2 out-of-band a fresh signal for this occurrence from calendar, location, activity or the person's reply, summarised without the data (DR7) occurrence its source is not the record the proposer drafted from E3 independent review an evaluation by a subject other than the proposer: a second agent, a deterministic risk check run by another instance, a caregiver, a clinician appropriateness it is a different subject, bound to the same payload hash E4 controller preview the enacting controller's own computation for this payload on its current state, before approval (AndroidAPS client control's prepare and commit is the only precedent) appropriateness, at the moment always: it is the enactor's state, not the hub's record

Properties every evidence record carries: its class; the subject and instance that made it (for independence); the payload hash and, for a plan, the occurrence it is bound to; when it was observed and when it stops counting (freshness); and a one-line summary with no calendar titles, places or health reasons. E2 counts only for the occurrence it names and only until its stated freshness ends; E1 and E3 bind to the plan element's hash and count for its life; E4 counts only for the approval it was made for.

Combined strength, used by the matrix: weak is E0 or E1 alone; confirmed is E1 with a fresh E2 for the occurrence; reviewed is confirmed plus E3 (for a plan, an E3 attached at plan approval counts); previewed is E3 with E4 (moment items).

docs.title: 4. The matrix: from (risk, evidence) to the approval path
docs.text:
Paths, from lightest to heaviest:

path what happens N notify the occurrence runs; the person, followers and the delegate see it, and the person can end it at any time W cancel window the person is notified ahead of the occurrence and it runs unless the person or the delegate cancels before it starts A approve one approval per occurrence or proposal, by the person or a delegate under a grant, bound to the payload hash RA reviews, then approve the item's required reviews (decision 3) are attached, then A S standing, with withdrawal an occurrence of an approved plan runs within its declared bounds unless a withdrawal criterion fires or the person cancels; the person is notified ahead; if a criterion cannot be evaluated with fresh data, the occurrence does not run L local only not through the hub at all; changed on the controller by the person

Plan approval (policy level) always needs a human approval of the plan: A for R0–R2 elements, RA for R3–R5. R3 and R4 elements may be standing only under FL1's conditions, and R5 elements only per occurrence (plans PN4). No evidence makes a plan active without a human approving it.

Occurrence or moment item, for a plan already approved or a moment proposal:

risk \ evidence weak confirmed reviewed previewed R0 inform N N N N R1 bounded target A W N N R2 bounded sensitivity A A W W R3 carbs RA A A A R4 insulin RA RA A, or S under FL1 A, or S under FL1 R5 persistent settings RA RA RA RA R6 safety limits L L L L

The same matrix as a grid. N notify, W cancel window, A approve, RA reviews then approve, S standing under FL1's conditions, L local only; the heavy border marks where a row meets its floor, which no evidence lowers.

docs.title: 5. Floors evidence cannot lower (draft for clinical review)
docs.text:
# floor why FL1 Insulin runs on a standing approval only under conditions set when the plan is approved (maintainer, 2026-10-18; clinical review required). Otherwise each dose is approved per occurrence by the person or a delegate, bound to its payload hash, with a short expiry. The conditions, all recorded in the plan and checked by the controller: the dose stays within bounds the controller declares for the element kind; predetermined withdrawal criteria, such as live location or activity that contradicts the planned meal, withdraw the occurrence automatically, and an occurrence whose criteria cannot be evaluated with fresh data does not run; and at least one of: an eating-soon target with a reduced portion of the meal bolus, the rest left to a decision at the meal, or a human approval of that occurrence given within the 12 hours before it. An agent's confirmation alone never releases a dose (FL5). a delivered dose cannot be withdrawn; double and stale doses are S4 (UCA-CMD-001, UCA-PROP-007, UCA-PROP-012), and the hub's picture of doses lags the controller (UCA-SYNC-SERVE-004, FB-STATE-006) FL2 Carbs are approved per occurrence by a human while the controller may dose for announced carbs, except carbs that accompany an insulin element released under FL1, which then carry FL1's conditions with it. carbs not eaten leave insulin delivered for them (journey C2, UCA-CMD-015); a carb entry acts as a dose request (UCA-SYNC-DL-001) FL3 Persistent settings need required reviews and the person's approval, every time, accepted element by element. no end date bounds the exposure; the change outlives its evidence (UCA-PROP-008, journey PL5) FL4 Safety limits and loop-mode switches are local only. they bound every other class; changing them remotely removes the check the other floors rely on FL5 An agent never approves. Agents propose and supply evidence (E1–E3); approval is a human's or a delegate's under a grant. An approval by the proposing subject stays refused (CM14). UCA-AUTH-002, UCA-PROP-009, UCA-PROP-011 FL6 No plan is active without an end date, and no standing approval without a grant that names its purpose, expiry and revocation (§7). UCA-AUTH-003, DR3, DR6 FL7 The person can always cancel or withdraw, whoever proposed or approved the item (decision 3). HAZ-1 when the reason goes away (UCA-CMD-015) FL8 The controller validates and may refuse anything, whatever path the item took. Evidence and approval never widen a controller's limits (D18). UCA-CMD-010; the hub does not judge (CM5)

The person, a caregiver for a child, or the care team may set a stricter path for any class; none may set one below these floors.

docs.title: 6. What the hub checks and what only the controller can
docs.text:
D18: the hub routes and records; the controller validates and enacts. The approval path is process, which the hub can enforce without judging therapy; everything about the person's state at the moment is the controller's.

check hub controller the element kind's declared class, read from the controller's definition yes (never inferred from the payload, CM5) declares it required reviews present, evidence classes counted, independence (a subject other than the proposer), freshness against the hub's clock, evidence bound to the payload hash yes — the approver may send the command; not the proposer (CM14); the path's approval present per occurrence for R3–R4, or FL1's recorded conditions met yes also yes: a controller refuses an R3 or R4 element arriving without a per-occurrence approval or a plan whose FL1 conditions it holds and finds met, because the hub can be bypassed or misconfigured and CM10's hash does not authenticate the approver definitionId unchanged since the proposal yes, at approval (UCA-PROP-008) yes, at each occurrence: it enacts under its current definition or refuses intents on the plan's channels unchanged a scoped basedOn at approval (below) its own composition at enactment (S1) doses and carbs since shows them in the outstanding list; a refusal for moment proposals is the open dose check yes, at enactment, from its own records bounds, limits, the pump's state, a preview — yes, only it can

Which since check applies, per plan type and level. "Both", in the maintainer's answer, becomes a choice of check by level and class:

level R0 R1–R2 R3–R4 R5 policy (plan approval) none definitionId; intents on the plan's channels, scoped definitionId definitionId; whole-state basedOn (CM15) at the visit confirmation (hours ahead) none the plan is still active; confirmation fresh as R1–R2, plus doses and carbs since shown to the approver — moment (a proposal now) none whole-state basedOn (CM15) CM15, plus doses and carbs since basedOn (UCA-PROP-012) CM15 algorithm (enactment) none the controller's composition and limits doses and carbs since the approval, at the controller the controller's limits

A scoped basedOn versions only the active intents on the slots the plan's elements touch, by A12's rule applied to those rows. It lets a plan made on Sunday survive an unrelated override on Monday while still catching a plan that would collide with an intent on its own slot.

docs.title: 7. Standing approval is a delegation grant
docs.text:
Approving a plan whose occurrences run on N or W paths, or are confirmed by an agent, is standing approval: the agent's later confirmations are commands sent without a per-command approval, which is UCA-AUTH-002 unless it is bounded. The framework makes that bound a grant under authority §7:

grant member (DR3, DR6) for a plan grantor the person, or the delegate who approved the plan grantee the instance that confirms occurrences, usually the proposing agent purpose this plan's id and the element ids accepted, nothing else scope confirm occurrences of those elements within the plan's bounds; only classes whose cell is N or W at the evidence the grantee supplies; never R3–R6 expiry the plan's end date, required (FL6); a maximum length per class, set by clinical review revocation cancelling the plan revokes the grant: unsent confirmations are cancelled, the controller drops the plan and reports it, the mirror shows who ended it

The grant's life:

stateDiagram-v2
  accTitle: A plan's standing approval
  accDescr: A plan is proposed, reviewed and approved by the person or a delegate; the approval is the grant, scoped to the plan and its accepted elements and expiring at the plan's end. While it is in force the grantee may confirm occurrences inside its scope; a confirmation outside it is refused. The grant ends when the plan reaches its end date or when the person, the approver or the proposer ends the plan, which cancels unsent confirmations.
  state "in force: confirm occurrences within scope" as inforce
  [*] --> proposed: agent proposes the plan
  proposed --> reviewed: required reviews attached
  reviewed --> inforce: person or delegate approves (grant)
  inforce --> inforce: confirmation within scope
  inforce --> expired: endsAt (FL6)
  inforce --> revoked: plan ended (FL7), unsent confirmations cancelled
  expired --> [*]
  revoked --> [*]

This narrows UCA-AUTH-002 to a grantee that can only confirm occurrences of one approved plan, and UCA-AUTH-003 to the plan's life. It does not give the agent api:commands:create on the channel; a confirmation outside the grant is refused at the hub and, for R3–R4, at the controller (§6).

docs.text:
journey element class evidence plan path occurrence path check floor that binds PL1 eating-soon target R1 pattern; morning calendar and location; risk check and caregiver review A after required reviews N (reviewed) definitionId, scoped intents; controller since at enactment FL6, FL7 PL1 meal carbs and bolus R3, R4 as above RA, with FL1's conditions recorded S with withdrawal criteria and a reduced portion, or A within the 12 hours before doses and carbs since, at the controller FL1, FL2 PL2 exercise target R1 pattern; activity or location A W, or N once an E3 review is attached scoped intents; confirmation freshness FL6 PL3 preset override for school R2 (R1 if target only) caregiver-authored; second parent approves (E3) A by the second parent W definitionId at approval and each occurrence FL5, FL7; a child's plan may set a stricter path PL4 sensitivity with an end date R2 agent inference (E1); required human review (E3) RA W scoped intents; definitionId FL6, FL7 PL5 settings change R5 clinician proposal; risk check (E3) RA, element by element, at the visit — definitionId; whole-state CM15 FL3; FL4 for any limit among them A1 carbs from a photo R3 the agent's estimate (E0–E1); risk check — A; RA without the risk check carbs since: shown by the hub, checked by the controller FL2 A2 correction bolus R4 required risk check (E3); preview where offered (E4) — A CM15 and doses since; the controller at enactment FL1

PL1's meal element is where the framework and the planning use case meet. The agent's morning confirmation answers "is lunch happening"; the withdrawal criteria answer "is it still happening" close to the meal, from live location or activity; and the person chooses, at plan approval, between a reduced standing portion with eating soon and an approval of each day's occurrence up to 12 hours ahead. Either way the plan moves the decision from the moment to the morning or the week, which is the policy experience the planning use cases ask for.

docs.title: 9. What the clinical review checks
docs.text:
1. The class of each element kind in §2, in particular whether eating-soon and other lowered targets belong in R1 or R2, since they lead the algorithm to deliver more.
  2. Whether carbs belong at the insulin floor (FL2) for every controller, or only for those that dose automatically for announced carbs.
  3. FL1's conditions for insulin on a standing approval: the controller-declared bounds, which withdrawal criteria are adequate and how fresh their data must be, the size of the reduced portion relative to the planned bolus, whether 12 hours is the right outer window for an advance approval, and whether the fail-closed rule (no fresh data, no dose) is sufficient.
  4. Whether a change that reduces insulin delivery may sit one class lower than one that increases it, given hyperglycaemia and ketoacidosis risk over long durations.
  5. The quantities this draft leaves unset: the short duration that triggers a modifier, freshness windows for E2, the maximum plan length per class, and the recurrence that makes E1.
  6. Whether W (run unless cancelled) is acceptable for R2 at all.
  7. Whether any population (young children, pregnancy, reduced awareness of hypoglycaemia) moves every class one step stricter by default.
  8. The severities assigned in §2.

docs.title: 10. What would have to be specified
docs.text: need where riskClass, bounds, selfEnding, direction per element kind, declared by the controller (S10, S11); the hub reads, never derives (CM5); undeclared is R4 state and intent, registration §7 evidence fields on evaluations: evidenceClass, subject and instance, boundTo (payload hash, occurrence), observedAt, countsUntil, minimised summary commands CM16 the plan object with elements, each with kind, class, bounds, end date and the path recorded at approval plans PN1–PN8 the approval naming accepted elements, the path used and the evidence ids relied on commands CM13, decision 4 required reviews and the refusal when missing; who may name them commands, decision 3 a scoped basedOn beside CM15's whole-state version state and intent A12, commands CM15 a definitionId check at approval commands §9 item 7 the plan grant (§7) and a confirmation bound to one occurrence authority §7, commands §9 item 5 a controller refusal reason for a missing per-occurrence approval commands CM8 conformance cases: an R4 element on a standing approval without FL1's conditions refused at hub and controller; an occurrence whose withdrawal criteria lack fresh data not run; an advance approval older than 12 hours not counted; an evaluation by the proposer not counted as E3; stale E2 not counted; an undeclared kind treated as R4; a confirmation outside its grant refused commands §10

docs.title: 11. Open questions for the maintainer
docs.text:
1. Who declares the class: each controller per kind (proposed), or a shared table for well-known kinds that a controller may only make stricter.
  2. Enforcement at both ends: whether controllers are asked to enforce FL1 and FL2 themselves (proposed), which no controller does today for hub-originated commands.
  3. Independence: whether a second agent run by the same person or vendor counts as E3, or independence needs a different operator.
  4. A preview for plans: whether E4 should exist at the confirmation level (the controller previews tomorrow's occurrence), which no controller offers.
  5. Signatures for R3–R4 approvals: CM10's hash does not show that a hub delivered what a human approved; whether an approver signature is required at these classes.
  6. Who may make a path stricter: the person, a caregiver for a child, the care team, and how that setting is recorded.
  7. Scoped basedOn or none at plan approval for R1–R2.
  8. Where withdrawal criteria are evaluated: on the controller when it holds the data (a phone's location and steps, as AndroidAPS automation reads them), or by the agent, which then cancels the occurrence; and whether both must agree before a standing dose runs.

docs.title: Glucose units at the profile boundary
docs.text:
Record

Record as of 2026-10-21. A point-in-time document; it is not kept up to date.

Contributor- and maintainer-facing. Proposal, DRAFT for maintainer review, 2026-10-21, against cgm-remote-monitor dev 4bca2ac2 and v15.0.8 92d08342. Defect facts live in the backfix register (BF-172, BF-173, BF-174); the ecosystem survey of units is glucose unit conversion. Each claim says whether it was run or read.

docs.title: 1. What Nightscout does today
docs.text:
Stored values. Glucose readings (entries.sgv) are mg/dl, with no unit field. A profile stores its sensitivity and targets in its own units and labels them with units, both on the document and on each store entry. In the profile corpus (specs/nsschema/profile.model.json) the store-level units is on 100% of 202 documents from 11 sites, spelled mg/dL, mg/dl or mmol/L. A treatment may carry units for its glucose.

Reading the label. profile.getUnits() returns mmol for any label containing mmol, and mg/dl for everything else, a missing label included (lib/profilefunctions.js:222-226).

Display units. settings.units (mg/dl or mmol) starts as the site's DISPLAY_UNITS and is then each viewer's browser setting. The server runs the plugins with the site setting, and each browser runs them with its viewer's setting.

Where the values meet. The profile accessors (getSensitivity, getLowBGTarget, getHighBGTarget) return the stored number. Each consumer that combines it with a reading has to look up the label and convert:

consumer converts since basal profile pill (lib/plugins/basalprofile.js:65-73) yes, sensitivity #5102, 2019 OpenAPS pill, lastEnacted.bg (lib/plugins/openaps.js) yes a4e05a16, 2024 treatment tooltip (lib/client/renderer.js:613-652) yes, from the record's own units BF-124, #8801 /pebble yes BF-138, #8777 Bolus Wizard Preview (lib/plugins/boluswizardpreview.js) no BF-172; #8819 proposed Careportal Bolus Wizard (lib/client/boluscalc.js) no BF-173; fixed on bf/boluscalc-profile-units

IOB and COB multiply by sensitivity in the profile's units. Whether any of their results is later compared with a reading in display units was not examined.

Writers. AID apps upload profiles in their user's units (the survey, §1). The profile editor sets units to the editor's display units when it saves (lib/profile/profileeditor.js:557, :655) and shows and saves the stored numbers as they are. Read, not run: opening an mmol/L profile in an mg/dl browser and saving it would relabel it without converting. The editor's DOM test harness is retired (tests/profileeditor.test.js), so this is a lead to reproduce, not a register entry.

Choosing a profile. getCurrentProfile(time, spec_profile) ignores spec_profile, so every accessor, getUnits included, answers for the active profile (BF-174).

docs.title: 2. Why the defect recurs
docs.text: The number and its unit travel separately. The accessors return a bare number, the unit is a separate property, and each consumer has to remember to join them. Four consumers do this on their own; the two calculators do not. Before these fixes, no test ran a site whose profile units differed from its display units. The defect does not show on a site where the two match, which is most sites.

docs.title: 3. Proposal
docs.text:
The rule is A11 of the state-intent spec ("Units are declared, never assumed", state-intent.md), applied to glucose: keep the label that clients already write, and convert once, where values leave the profile.

step what where changes stored data U0 The local fixes: BF-174 (getCurrentProfile honours a name in the store), BF-173 (bolus calculator), BF-172 (#8819, with the review notes in the register) in-tree no U1 Accessors that answer in the caller's units. An optional last argument, e.g. getSensitivity(time, spec_profile, units), and the same for both targets. Without it, the accessor returns the stored value as today. Conversion and rounding (1 mg/dl, 0.1 mmol/L) live in one helper in lib/units.js. Then BWP, the bolus calculator, the basal profile pill and the tooltip move onto it, and the per-consumer code goes lib/profilefunctions.js, lib/units.js, consumers no U2 Labelled quantities in new code. A JSDoc type { value: number, units: 'mg/dl' \| 'mmol' } for glucose levels and sensitivities that cross a module boundary, and a units field on any new API or record shape that carries a glucose value. It applies to new code; existing plugins keep U1's numbers new modules, platform specs no U3 Declare the label as it is written. The profile schema accepts the spellings in use (mg/dl, mg/dL, mmol, mmol/L, read by "contains mmol") and names the label's two places (document and store entry). Nightscout's own writers keep writing what they write today specs/, API docs no U4 A missing label. Today it is read as mg/dl. Options are in §5; whichever is chosen is recorded as a quirk with its versions (D20), not added as a silent heuristic getUnits no U5 The profile editor. After the lead in §1 is reproduced: on save, convert the values to the label being written, or keep the profile's own label lib/profile/profileeditor.js yes, for profiles the editor saves

Not proposed: per-value unit objects in stored profiles, which every reader of today's shape would fail to parse, and a request parameter asking the server to convert profile values. Every client converts already; a parameter would add a second place for the rule to live.

docs.title: 4. Compatibility
docs.text:
"Old" means a client or record that exists today; "new" means code written to this proposal.

step old records read by new code new records read by old clients old clients writing operator-visible version class U0 BF-172, BF-173 unchanged; each value read in its labelled units the Bolus Wizard treatment's boluscalc.isf and targets are in its units (display units) where they were the profile's numbers; consistent with its own label for the first time unchanged on sites with mismatched units, the estimate, the BWP warning and the calculator's suggestion change from wrong to right patch, named in the notes U0 BF-174 unchanged a saved record's values now match its profile name unchanged with the picker shown, a chosen non-active profile is used patch, named in the notes U1 unchanged no shape change unchanged none beyond U0 patch U2 n/a new fields only, additive unaffected none follows the shape it is added to U3 unchanged unchanged unchanged; the declared vocabulary is what they write none none (documentation) U4 "keep" unchanged unchanged unchanged none none U4 "infer" or "refuse" a profile without a label changes how it is read unchanged a writer that omits the label gets the new reading yes, for unlabelled profiles minor, with a quirk entry and a note U5 unchanged a profile saved by the editor in the other units has converted values and a matching label unchanged yes, for profiles edited in the other units patch, named in the notes

Records already saved. A Bolus Wizard treatment saved on a mismatched site before BF-173's fix holds the profile's numbers next to a display-units label. Nothing in the record separates those from correct ones, so no migration is proposed. A profile already relabelled by the editor (§1) cannot be told apart from a correct one either.

Forward. Once U1 is in, a consumer added later gets converted values by passing sbx.settings.units. A test that runs one site with mismatched units (the BF-173 tests in tests/careportal.test.js, the #8819 test in tests/boluswizardpreview.test.js) is the guard against the next consumer that forgets.

docs.title: 5. Decisions for the maintainers
docs.text: # question options UD1 Do BF-173 and BF-174 go into the 15.0.9 notes as known issues, like BF-172? decided 2026-10-21: named, without ids, beside BF-172 in the rewritten release notes (9ed4a5441) UD2 Land U0 as three small PRs, or wait for U1 and land one change? U0 first, then U1 as a refactor that keeps U0's tests green / U1 only UD3 U1's form optional units argument (the smallest change, matches the existing signatures) / a converted view profile.inUnits(units) UD4 A profile without units (U4) keep reading it as mg/dl / infer mmol/L below a threshold, as oref0 (20) and Nightscout's alarm thresholds (50) do / report it as unreadable for unit-sensitive consumers (A11) UD5 The profile editor (U5), once reproduced convert on save / keep the profile's label / ask the user

docs.title: ID-BATCH: per-item results in API v1 batch replies
docs.text:
Record

Record as of 2026-10-30. A point-in-time document; it is not kept up to date.

Contributor-facing design note for ID-BATCH (queue ID-BATCH-RESULTS, plan §4.2 row ID-BATCH), written 2026-10-30. The baseline and proposal below are historical; see the implementation status for what shipped afterward. Every claim carries a mark: [M] measured, with the cell id of the write-contract matrix pin dev-e1f7ac41-idfirst.json (1,929 cells) or of its -uuidoff companion (504 cells); [R] read from source. Server file:line is at crm 9919f8ef (the #8874 head, write(intent) release 1) unless another revision is named. Client file:line is at the revision named in §2. Read-derived claims about clients are often wrong in this project; each one is a candidate for a replay cell before it is relied on.

wi is lib/storage/write-intent.js, ws is lib/server/websocket.js, wv is lib/server/write-validation.js, wp is lib/api/shared/write-payload.js.

Headline. The step already answers one result per item (WriteResult.items[], wi:1594-1599), but no API v1 route builds its reply from it: each route answers with the submitted objects as the step mutated them [R]. One route, v1 treatments under WRITE_VALIDATION=reject, already keeps one slot per submitted item with a refused member and a Warning: 299 header (crm 6e842c07, on dev since 2026-10-25) [R]. ID-BATCH generalises that shape to every v1 collection and every per-item outcome. It keeps HTTP 200 and an array with exactly one slot per submitted item, because Loop's NightscoutKit fails any other status or length (§2). Full outcomes are opt-in. The statement that no matrix cell sent a batch describes the pre-ID-BATCH pin only; the batch forms and results are now recorded below and in the release contents.

Implementation status (2026-11-01). #8889 merged the opt-in v1 per-item results and strict-v1 behavior at 4196dd45. #8894 then merged the identifier index and Q-IDX race retry at 497d08c9 (PR head cf978f4), including batch duplicate-key races under WRITE_RESEND. The batch-only matrix recorded 33 expected index-on/off differences for batch-dupkey-mid and batch-repeat-identifier under default, WRITE_VALIDATION=reject, and WRITE_IDENTIFIER=strict on MongoDB 5.0.32 and 8.0.29. The broader --batch --no-idf matrix is now complete on the merged tree: 3,443 cells per off/try lane, zero invalid cells on MongoDB 5.0.32 and 8.0.34, and the same 33 expected batch differences on both versions (24 batch-dupkey-mid, 9 batch-repeat-identifier). The remaining off/try and cross-version differences affect only cache fields; wire capture had 929/929 frames, none unattributed and no settle-bound hits. PR #8894's required hosted checks all passed. See releases/cgm-remote-monitor-16.0.0/contents.md for test counts, matrix pins, and the current release status.

Loop builds the zipped list from created while the upload passes through compactMap (Extensions/NightscoutUploader.swift:20, :128); if an item is dropped there, positions shift. docs.title: 3. The proposed rule
docs.text:
R1. One slot per submitted item, in order, on every v1 array write (POST of treatments, entries, devicestatus, profile, food, activity; PUT of food and profile, which take arrays). Each route builds its reply from WriteResult.items[] by index instead of from the mutated input. The reply's length equals the number of items submitted. A derived record (preBolus) is not given a slot of its own; open question (iv).

R2. Slot content, by outcome.

item outcome slot counted in Warning inserted, merged, replaced, unchanged the record as stored, with _id and identifier (D20 rule 5) no acknowledged, stays deleted (ID-FIRST-MATCH slice 3); deleted-record edit under WRITE_DELETED_EDIT=ignore (ID-Q3) the stored record's _id and identifier and the item's own fields; nothing written yes, "acknowledged, not applied" ID-Q6 lenient: identifier treated as absent the outcome of the remaining keys, as above, with identifier: null yes, "identifier ignored" refused, final (domain rule, _id form, WRITE_IDENTIFIER=strict, WRITE_DELETED_EDIT=refuse with status: 410, profile update permission) the item as sent, no _id, and refused: { status, message, rules? } (today's wv.refusal, generalised beyond Temporary Targets) yes

The whole-batch refusals of §1 become per-item: one non-hex _id on devicestatus, profile, food or activity, one non-string identifier or type, and profile's update permission (which today refuses the whole batch "so a refused mixed batch cannot partially write", api profile :120-122; open question (iii)). wp.normalize's size limit stays whole-request.

R3. Status. 200 when at least one item is not refused. 400 when every item is refused (today's treatments rule), with the per-item slots in the body. Not 207: it breaks Loop and three entries uploaders (§2). Not 4xx for a partial result: Loop would re-send the whole batch without limit.

R4. Transient failures stay whole-request. A storage error the step cannot attribute and resolve, or a write it cannot confirm, answers 5xx as today, never as a refused slot, because a refused slot is final for Loop and status-only clients. The client's retry of the whole batch is safe where re-send matching reaches the items (identifier, _id, entries sysTime+type); devicestatus, food and activity items with no identity are stored twice (identity reference §2.7). The ordered writes keep items before the failure stored, as today.

R5. Duplicate key mid-batch (ID-UNIQUE-INDEX). With the index built, an E11000 on identifier for item k is a re-send that raced the lookup. The step re-reads the record by that identifier, re-plans item k as a matched re-send under WRITE_RESEND (merge, acknowledge or refuse), writes it, and then re-plans and writes items k+1…n, because an ordered bulk write stops at the first error. The slot shows the matched outcome, as for any re-send. Retry once; a second E11000 on the same item is R4. Devicestatus already absorbs an E11000 on a sent _id this way (wi:823-831). An E11000 on _id (an entry re-sent under a used _id at another time) is a final refusal, refused: { status: 409 }; open question (v). Under WRITE_IDENTIFIER_INDEX=try with no index built, the race stores a second record, as today.

R6. Summary and full results. - A Warning: 299 - "<counts>" header whenever any slot is not applied as sent, extending lib/api/treatments/index.js:152-156 (for example "2 of 40 items refused, 1 identifier ignored"). No surveyed client reads it, so it is for logs and operators. - Full items[] only on request: a request header (proposed Nightscout-Write-Results: items) returns { "items": [{ index, outcome, _id, identifier, reason, warnings }], "documents": [ …R2 slots… ] }. No surveyed client sends it, so the default reply is unchanged for all of them. Header or query parameter: open question (ii).

Options weighed for where per-item outcomes go by default:

option breaks a surveyed client? trade-off fields on each slot (outcome, warnings) no (every decoder ignores unknown keys) visible to every client; a client that stores the reply element would store them (none found) header only no counts, not positions; no client reads headers opt-in object reply no the only full result; needs a client change to use 207 multi-status yes: Loop, Trio profile, tconnectsync, minimed-connect, librelink-up the HTTP-standard form

The rule takes the existing refused member, the header and the opt-in object, and adds nothing else to default slots.

docs.title: 4. Cells and tests needed
docs.text:
Matrix forms (v1 and in-process for every collection, socket for comparison). Each records status, reply length, a per-slot descriptor in order, the Warning header, and the store. - batch-mixed-valid: valid, invalid, valid. Invalid means a Temporary Target the domain rules refuse (run with WRITE_VALIDATION=reject), a non-hex _id (devicestatus, profile, food, activity), and a non-string identifier. - batch-repeat-identifier: one new identifier twice in a batch; and a batch whose second item re-sends a stored one. - batch-deleted: the second item re-sends a soft-deleted record by identifier (slice 3 baseline). - batch-placeholder-identifier: "undefined" and a 257-character value in the middle (ID-Q6). - batch-dupkey-mid: with the index, a conflicting record inserted between plan and write for item 2, extending the harness's read-failure injection (harness:330-333). - batch-storage-fail-mid: an injected write failure on item 2 (R4), the store showing item 1 kept. - batch-profile-permission: a create-only token re-sending a changed profile beside a new one.

Unit tests. - The route builds slots from items[] by index, with length equal to the submitted count, for every outcome and every collection, including when the step mutates nothing. - All refused → 400 with slots; one not refused → 200. Warning text per kind. - Opt-in reply shape; absent header → today's array byte-for-byte (G1 for the default). - R5: one retry, the slot's outcome under each WRITE_RESEND mode, the remainder re-planned, the second E11000 → 5xx. Ablation: remove the retry; batch-dupkey-mid goes red. - Client-shaped contract tests: NightscoutKit (array, equal count, _id string on non-refused slots); xdripswift (array, created_at/eventType echoed); nightscout-connect (dateString/created_at echoed). Turn tests/api.partial-failures.test.js:111 and :550 into assertions.

docs.title: 5. Where it lands, and what the ID-FIRST-MATCH slices must leave ready
docs.text: The initial plan placed ID-BATCH after ID-UNIQUE-INDEX. It needed WC-STEP-PATCH (#8874) for items[], and the batch cells of §4 pinned first. Changes made in the ID-FIRST-MATCH slices so the reply change could be isolated: - Slice 1 (no outcome change): routes read items[] and keep today's bytes. Treatments, entries, devicestatus and profile ignore it now (treatments.js:146, entries.js:157, devicestatus.js:109, profile.js:67). - Slice 2 (identifier-format): an item member for warnings. item() has only reason (wi:1594-1599), and an ignored identifier is not a refusal. - Slice 3 (stays deleted): an outcome word for "acknowledged, not applied". OUTCOMES has none (wi:54), and devicestatus answers its re-send refused "already stored" (wi:849), which R2 would show as a refusal. Open question (vi). - Slice 4 (merge on match): the batch forms report inserted or the rule's onMatch for every match (wi:1768-1770, wi:687-690); they need unchanged where nothing changed. - ID-UNIQUE-INDEX: R5's retry belongs in the write step, at the items[] level; #8894 implements that retry alongside the index so duplicate-key races do not escape as a batch-level failure.

docs.title: 6. Resolved design questions
docs.text:
The questions below record the design discussion as it stood on 2026-10-30. The maintainer's decisions are captured in the 16.0.0 decisions record; the implementation state is summarized above. In particular, question (i) was resolved by shipping v1 per-item replies in #8889 and the index-aware batch retry in #8894, rather than leaving a separate ID-BATCH integration branch on the critical path.

Mechanism and trade-off for each. IDs are allocated by session -49.

(i) Which lands first: the unique index or ID-BATCH. Plan row 9 puts the index first; ROADMAP :206 makes it depend on ID-BATCH-RESULTS. Mechanism: with the index and no per-item reporting, a duplicate key mid-batch is a 500 with earlier items stored, unless the step's retry (R5) lands with the index. Trade-off: index first with the retry in the step (the reply is unchanged and correct) against ID-BATCH first (the retry's outcome is visible per item from the start).

(ii) How a client asks for full results. A request header, a query parameter (?results=items) or an Accept media type. Mechanism: the default array is kept either way. Trade-off: a header survives proxies and URL logging rules; a query parameter is easier for scripts and shows up in access logs.

(iii) Profile's update permission per item. Today one changing re-send without api:profile:update refuses the whole batch, on purpose, so nothing is written (api profile :120-122). Mechanism: R2 makes it a refused slot, so the new profiles in the batch are stored. Trade-off: a create-only uploader's new profiles get through, against a partly applied profile set that the uploader may not expect.

(iv) The preBolus derived record in the reply. Today it is an extra element (treatments.js:202). Mechanism: R1 gives one slot per submitted item. Trade-off: dropping it from the reply fixes count-checking clients, but a client that reads the derived record's _id from the reply loses it (none found; the Glooko path of nightscout-connect is the only corpus sender).

(v) E11000 on _id. A final refusal (409) or a 5xx. Mechanism: an _id in use at another time is not a race, and a retry cannot succeed. Trade-off: a final refusal is silently treated as uploaded by Loop ("NA") and dropped; a 5xx makes Loop retry the whole batch without limit (identity reference §5 rule 4, "500 and the rest of the batch is lost").

(vi) The outcome word for "acknowledged". A new acknowledged outcome, or unchanged with a reason. Mechanism: R2 shows it as a stored record and counts it in Warning. Trade-off: a new word extends spec §2.2 and every consumer of items[]; reusing unchanged hides that the client's change was not applied. Devicestatus's refused "already stored" moves to whichever is chosen.

(vii) Refusals that status-only clients never see. Trio's array paths and xDrip+ mark every item uploaded on 2xx (§2), so a refused treatment is dropped without a client-side trace; Loop does the same through "NA". Mechanism: R3 keeps 200 for a partial result, as treatments under reject do today. Trade-off: no retry loops and no blocked queues, against a dropped record surfaced only in the server log, the Warning header and the opt-in results. Whether a refused dose or carb entry should also be shown on the site (an announcement or status-page count) is open.

Decided elsewhere, carried here (maintainer, 2026-10-30, ID-STRICT-V1). WRITE_IDENTIFIER=strict refuses an invalid identifier on API v3 and the socket from slice 2 on. On API v1 and in-process it is enforced with this item's per-item replies; until then those paths treat an invalid identifier as absent, as under lenient (IDENTIFIER_STRICT in lib/storage/write-intent.js, 'v1/internal': 'absent'). The reply-format prototype includes strict on v1 as a case.

docs.title: 6b. Lab evidence (2026-10-30)
docs.text:
The reply-format prototype (crm proto/id-batch-replies 7d81e1c1, local; no write rule changed, 0 matrix cells moved with the opt-in off) and the client lab (tools/lab/id-batch-replies, RESULTS.md, synthetic data) give findings for (ii)–(vii); the maintainer decides:

  • (ii) A header and a query parameter behave the same; an Accept opt-in is dropped on any .json path (lib/middleware/express-extension-to-accept.js:30-36), which Trio and nightscout-connect use.
  • (iii) Per-item profile refusal stores the rest of the batch; today's whole-batch 401 loses a new profile too.
  • (iv) Keeping the derived preBolus record in the reply makes Loop re-send forever and, run for real, makes nightscout-connect lose a later record (BF-219); omitting it fixes both.
  • (v) A duplicate _id answered 5xx leaves the items after it unstored while clients re-send (BF-220); 409 stores the rest.
  • (vi) acknowledged and unchanged give byte-identical slots; keeping refused turns a lone device-status re-send into a 400.
  • (vii) Under reject, Loop, Trio, xDrip+ and nightscout-connect count a refused treatment as uploaded; xDrip4iOS re-sends it while it is among its latest 50.
  • Strict on v1 turns "stored without the identifier" into "record dropped" for every client except xDrip4iOS.

Corrections to §2 from the lab: xDrip+ treatments are PUT one object at a time, not batched; the NightscoutKit pin inside LoopWorkspace is the standalone checkout 4ec9fd12a1; Loop's retry has no bound.

docs.title: ID-FIRST-MATCH: the re-send rule on every path, cell by cell
docs.text:
Record

Record as of 2026-10-29. A point-in-time document; it is not kept up to date.

Contributor-facing design note for ID-FIRST-MATCH (plan §4.2), written 2026-10-29. Design only: no cgm-remote-monitor code was changed or run for it. Every claim carries a mark: [M] measured, with the cell ids of the write-contract matrix pin dev-e1f7ac41-idfirst.json (dev e1f7ac41, 1,929 cells: 456 earlier and 1,473 new; companion -uuidoff, 504 cells); [R] read from source, file:line at crm e8224807 (the #8874 head, write(intent) release 1 with slices 4 and 6) unless another revision is named; [R, prediction] a value the rule is expected to give, read and not run. Read-derived predictions are often wrong in this project; the implementation slices measure every one of them.

wi is lib/storage/write-intent.js, ws is lib/server/websocket.js, tfk is lib/server/treatment-fallback-key.js, all at e8224807. The full cell list is the appendix id-first-match-design-note-2026-10-29-cells.md.

Headline. The four decisions can be expressed without moving any of the 456 earlier cells [R, prediction; §2 (e)]. Under them, 417 of the 1,473 new cells change (option M below). One ordering constraint is not optional. If identifier-first lands on the socket before the chart-drag split stops copying identifier onto the new half (BF-212), moving the insulin or carbs of a treatment that carries an identifier loses data. Under the merge outcome, the moved half is merged back into the original at the new time. Under the keep outcome, it is dropped after the original has already lost that field (treatments ws idf-split-written: today 2 records [M], predicted 1 [R, prediction]). Merge on match does not fix BF-212 on API v1 and in-process, and identifier-first extends it to the socket and to API v1 profile, food and activity (§5).

docs.title: 0. The decisions, as the plan records them
docs.text:
From plan §4.2 (main, 2026-10-29):

  • "Merge on match (2026-10-29). When a re-send matching a stored record is applied, fields it leaves out are kept (RFC 7386), and PUT replaces. The census reads replace on several paths today. The extended matrix measures each path first, and each path that changes is listed cell by cell."
  • "Re-send after delete, every path (2026-10-29). 'Acknowledged, stays deleted' applies on every path, and the spec text is corrected. Every changed cell is documented, so the change can be reverted or adjusted as cohort feedback arrives."
  • "Records without an identifier. Natural keys for device status and profile are a separate item, ID-NATURAL-KEY, with its own corpus check of what would merge. Food and activity have no natural key."
  • "Socket edits and removes, and activity. Identifier addressing is added where it changes nothing for writes that carry no identifier: socket dbUpdate, dbUpdateUnset and dbRemove accept an identifier when there is no _id, and activity creates match on identifier. This is conditional on the extended matrix showing every existing form unchanged."
  • Rules in force from earlier: "Fallback. A v1 entries re-send whose identifier matches nothing still matches on sysTime+type; treatments never fall back. A devicestatus re-send whose identifier is stored writes nothing and is answered with the stored _id." "Format (2026-10-29). 1 to 256 URL-safe characters; a UUID is recommended; placeholders (invalid, undefined, null, NaN) are refused."
  • Plan §1a row 9: "ID-FIRST-MATCH where it changes no outcome, and ID-BATCH", 16.2.0, or 16.0.0 through the entry bar.

docs.title: 1. The rule, as entries in the step's rule table
1.1 Three shared rules (new)
docs.text:
1. identifier-format (rule 1, in plan(), after the _id form). It checks the identifier the write will be matched by. That covers a sent one, one that UUID_HANDLING moved from a non-hex _id (DOC_ID_FORMS['treatment-uuid'], wi:271-287), and on API v3 a sent one before resolveIdentifier computes one for a write that has none (lib/api3/shared/operationTools.js:182-189). What a bad value gets, refused or treated as absent, is open question (vi). No pin cell sends a bad value [M: every idf- identifier is crypto.randomUUID(), harness tools/qc/write-contract-matrix.js:723-731].
  2. identifier-match (rule 2, first). Filter: identifier = X. Under UUID_HANDLING, on entries and treatments, also _id = X, as today (wi:297-307, wi:434-438). On API v3, also the shown-_id clauses for records with no identifier, as today (lib/api3/storage/mongoCollection/utils.js:155-165,193-206). Soft-deleted records are included. When more than one record matches, the pick is open question (v). The predictions use P1: each path keeps today's pick, and a path that newly matches on identifier picks the first stored record.
  3. on-deleted: acknowledged. A soft-deleted record (isValid: false) reached by any match key of a create is not written. The reply names the stored record with a 2xx. There is no data-update, no storage-socket event and no storage-write-committed, and srvModified stays, so API v3 history does not show it. On API v3 the reply takes the shape acknowledge.js gives devicestatus today (200, identifier, isDeduplication, lastModified; lib/api3/generic/create/acknowledge.js:38-61).

When identifier-match finds nothing, each path's remaining order runs as it does today (decision 3), and any of its keys that reaches a soft-deleted record gives acknowledged (decision 2; open question (iv) is about the keys that hide deleted records today).

docs.title: 2. Impact, cell by cell, computed from the pin
docs.text:
The classification reads each new cell's measured store and shape (the harness labels: merge, replace, not-written, new; seeds carry wck: 1, re-sends wcv: 2; harness:86-93). It applies §1:

  • A re-send carries an identifier for the idf-identifier-*, idf-*-identifier, idf-split-* forms; for idf-uuidid-* on v1 and in-process entries and treatments (moved under UUID_HANDLING); and on API v3 always, computed when none is sent. A computed identifier reaches only an API v3 seed.
  • A path new to identifier matching (socket; v1 / in-process profile, food, activity) turns a second record into one.
  • Today's replace becomes merge (not on devicestatus).
  • A soft-deleted seed that a key reaches is acknowledged.
  • Split cells use pick P1.

The earlier cells that re-send and replace today are listed in group (a). The cache field is set aside, as for every pin. The full list, with today's value and the prediction per cell, is the appendix.

group cells where (a) the write changes, no recorded value is predicted to change 62 56 earlier cells whose re-send replaces an identical body today; settings v3 resend-identity; 5 devicestatus socket cells now matched by identifier instead of created_at (b) identifier now matches where a second record was stored 88 socket (entries, food, activity, profile -time, treatments -amt/-time, devicestatus -time); v1 / in-process profile, food, activity; same path and across paths (c1) replace becomes merge, same record 216 v1 / in-process treatments; API v3 every collection; socket profile; in-process food / activity by a string _id (c2) kept becomes merge, socket treatments (option M only) 4 treatments ws idf-identifier-same and its three cross cells (d1) revived becomes "acknowledged, stays deleted" 36 v1 / in-process treatments and entries; API v3; socket profile (d2) a new record beside a deleted one becomes "acknowledged, stays deleted" 23 socket treatments and devicestatus (plain and identifier); socket entries and food, v1 / in-process profile, food, activity (identifier forms only) (g) two records share one identifier (split family, BF-212), pick P1 50 + 1 not visible §5 (h) unchanged as read, in question 12 devicestatus x {v1,inproc,ws} x v3 idf-{syncIdentifier,id,uuid,NSCLIENT_ID}-same, the API v3 fallback replace; open question (ii)

417 new cells change under option M (b 88 + c 220 + d 59 + g 50). Under option K, 415 do: c2's four cells keep their store but srv goes from C=M+ to C=M= and hist from valid to absent, and two split cells keep their values. The appendix lists the 12 cells whose prediction differs between M and K.

(a) No outcome change: 62 cells. The 56 earlier cells are resend-*, legacy-* and the cross cells (<c> x A x B) that re-send an identical body through a path that replaces today: v1 / in-process treatments, food and activity, API v3 and the socket's profile. Merge and replace of an identical body store the same document. API v3's cached updateOne emits the same cache update as replaceOne for a valid record (mongoCachedCollection/index.js:41-68 at e8224807), so ev is predicted equal. Examples: treatments v1 resend-identity, food v1 resend-hex, profile ws resend-identity, entries x v1 x v3 [M today: one record; R, prediction: equal].

(b) to (d) examples (today [M] → predicted [R, prediction]): - profile v1 idf-identifier-same: n=2 OID,OID:v2 · not-written,new → n=1 OID:v2 · merge. - treatments ws idf-identifier-amt: n=2 · not-written,new → n=1 OID:v2 · merge (K: n=1 OID · not-written, the other amount is dropped). - devicestatus ws idf-identifier-time: n=2 → n=1 OID · not-written. - treatments v1 idf-identifier-amt: n=1 OID:v2 · replace → n=1 OID:v2 · merge (c1). - treatments v1 idf-softdel-plain: n=1 OID:v2 · replace, srv C=M+ → n=1 OID:inv · not-written, srv C=M= (d1). - treatments ws idf-softdel-plain: n=2 OID:inv,OID:v2 · not-written,new → n=1 OID:inv · not-written (d2).

(e) The additive items (decision 4). Earlier cells that move: none [R, prediction]. Every earlier socket dbUpdate, dbUpdateUnset and dbRemove form sends an _id (harness:435-437, 651, 658, and update-twin, harddelete-custom with a string _id, harddelete-num with a number). Today a request without an _id is refused with { result: 'Missing or invalid _id' } (ws:365-369, ws:376-378), and no form sends one. The same holds for everything else in §1: of the 456 earlier cells, none is predicted to move, and 56 change only how they are written (group a).

(f) Dedupe-gate fixtures that change (tests/websocket.dedupe-gate.test.js at e8224807, 58 tests; titles are the same at ac5d77fb, where #8877 flipped three others). The stored profile carries NSCLIENT_ID and the write does not, so a merge keeps it. The fixture's plain(after[0]).should.eql(expected) then fails (decision 1). Its sibling replaces the stored profile with the same NSCLIENT_ID sends every stored field and is predicted to pass unchanged.

The 16 cells that differ between the two pins [M] are idf-uuidid-* cells, where the flag decides whether the UUID becomes the identifier. With the flag off they are re-sends with no identity, so identifier matching cannot reach them.
