docs.title: 4. What the matrix still cannot see, and the unit tests needed
docs.text:
1. Which record a reply names. The harness records [1 _id], not which one (harness:403-416). devicestatus ws idf-split-second keeps its values under P1 while the reply names A instead of B. Unit test: under each pick rule, every outcome replies with the matched record's _id and identifier (I4).
  2. Field-level merge. The wck/wcv probe shows only whether a left-out field survived. Unit tests per path: a nested object (profile store; RFC 7386 merges objects member by member), an explicit null in a create re-send (removes on merge on match, plan "Null removes"), a field left out on purpose.
  3. Identifier format. No form sends a placeholder, an over-length value, a character outside the set or a 24-hex identifier that is not the record's own _id. Harness forms first (slice 2), then unit tests of identifier-format per path, including a placeholder _id that UUID_HANDLING moves.
  4. Races. Two creates with one new identifier at once: both miss the lookup and both insert. Only a unique index stops this (open question (v)). Integration test with concurrent writes, before and after the index.
  5. A live and a deleted record sharing one identifier. The pick between them. Unit test.
  6. PUT or save with an _id and an identifier that name different records (identity: "identifier decides"), and PUT or save on a soft-deleted record (v1 save replaces and so revives; v3 PUT answers 410). Unit tests.
  7. Socket addressing by identifier (decision 4): dbUpdate, dbUpdateUnset, dbRemove with only identifier, with both (_id decides), with a placeholder, with two records sharing it, with a deleted record. Today's refusal of a request without _id (ws:365-369) is the baseline. New gate fixtures, one ablation each.
  8. A v1 batch with a repeated identifier, or one deleted (ID-BATCH): per-item outcomes. Unit tests.
  9. storage-write-committed. The official harness does not record it. Unit test: an acknowledgement commits nothing.
  10. WRITE_VALIDATION=reject. The pin runs with it off. A merge whose result fails the domain rules, and the conditional validated update (lib/storage/validated-update.js). Unit tests.
  11. Cross-path deletes and -amt across paths. The delete forms and -amt run on the same path only (harness:845-866). Unit tests for a v1 seed deleted through the socket and re-sent through API v3, and so on.
  12. An API v3 delete of a shared identifier. filterForEveryForm matches every record with that identifier (utils.js:179-182), so one DELETE reaches both halves of a split [R]. Unit test.
  13. The chart split end to end. The client sends dbUpdateUnset, maybe dbUpdate, then dbAdd (lib/client/renderer.js:1014-1040,1046-1072, lib/client/treatmenttime.js:60-73). The matrix's idf-split-written is two dbAdds. Use the BF-212 probe with and without identifier-first on the socket.

docs.title: 5. BF-212: the shared-identifier data loss, and a rule for it
docs.text:
Today [M]. Two stored treatments A and B share one identifier, B two minutes later with another amount. On API v1 and in-process, a re-send of B lands on A: treatments v1 idf-split-second is n=2 OID:v2,OID · replace,not-written, the first record (A) replaced. treatments v1 idf-split-first is the same. treatments v1 idf-split-written is n=1: B's own write already replaced A. Entries do the same with merge (entries v1 idf-split-second merge,not-written). On API v3, the lookup picks B (treatments v3 idf-split-second not-written,replace), and a re-send of A is refused 400 because B's date is immutable (treatments v3 idf-split-first). The socket picks by time: treatments ws idf-split-second stores nothing new and the similar match finds B. Socket entries, food and activity and v1 profile, food and activity store a third record (n=3).

Under identifier-first plus merge, pick P1 [R, prediction; appendix group g]. - Kept on v1 / in-process treatments and entries: 4 -second cells. Merge keeps only the fields the re-send leaves out. A and B carry the same fields, so A still takes B's amount and time (treatments v1 idf-split-second → merge,not-written). - Worsened on 11 -second cells, where a re-send of B now overwrites A: treatments ws, profile ws, {entries,food,activity} ws, {profile,food,activity} {v1,inproc}. Today these either land on B (socket treatments and profile) or store a duplicate. - Collapsed on 12 -written cells, where B's own write is matched to A: today 2 or 3 records, predicted 1. On the socket this is the chart split's dbAdd. - Unchanged on API v3: B is picked, and A is refused 400.

So the rule as decided keeps BF-212 and widens it. It is fixed only by a pick that tells the two records apart, by stopping the split from creating them (slice 5), or by both.

A rule for two records that share one identifier (proposed for open question (v)): 1. The server does not create a second record with an identifier that is stored, on any path. Under identifier-match everywhere, a create carrying a stored identifier is a re-send by definition. The remaining ways in are a race, a PUT/save or dbUpdate that sets another record's identifier, and the records that already exist. 2. When an identifier names more than one stored record, the pick is P4: the record whose time key equals the re-send's (created_at for treatments, devicestatus, food, activity; date/sysTime for entries; startDate for profile), else the newest by _id (API v3's order today), and every such match is logged. Under P4 [R, prediction]: -first and -second land on their own record on every path where the time survives to the lookup. API v1 food overwrites created_at with the server time (lib/server/food.js create, census F1), so food falls back to the newest. * v3 idf-split-first changes from 400 to a merge into A. -written still collapses (rule 1). 3. The chart split stops copying identifier, syncIdentifier, id and uuid onto the new half (treatmenttime.js:60-73 deletes only _id and NSCLIENT_ID). This is the register's control: with the copy stripped, the shared-identity effects go [M, BF-212 entry]. It must land before slice 6. With the copy unchanged and identifier-first on the socket, option M merges the moved half back into the original at the new time, so both halves move. Option K drops it after dbUpdateUnset has removed it from the original, so the insulin or carbs is lost. Both apply only to records that carry identifier: API v3-written records, and the 505 Loop treatments with an identifier in the 12-site corpus (docs/60-research/tenancy/identifier-format-2026-10-17.md §2).

Unique index consequences (ID-UNIQUE-INDEX, plan §4.2; read, with the pin where it applies): - Existing duplicates. ID-DUP-MEASURE found 0 across the 12-site corpus (plan §4.2). That corpus has no API v3 writer (format research §2), and every chart split of an identifier-carrying treatment makes one. A unique createIndex fails on the first duplicate. The server needs a defined path: report and run without the index, or a migration. A migration cannot choose between two split halves, which are both real doses. - Soft-deleted records. Decision 2 means they count. A deleted identifier is acknowledged, never re-created, so the index covers deleted records too. A partial filter can then be identifier: { $type: 'string', $gt: '' }, which also leaves out the empty values that tfk:32-34 and API v3's emptyIdentifier treat as absent. Excluding deleted records would need isValid stored as a positive value, because partial filters do not take $ne (the supported operators per MongoDB version are to be verified against the floor version, node-version policy). - Twins. A string and an ObjectId copy of one record (BF-130) carry the same identifier, so a stored twin fails the index. Twins are removed on write by the step today (rule 5). Stored twins from earlier versions need the same migration. - Scope. Per collection, with the tenant in the key under multi (plan "Scope"). API v3's computed identifiers (UUID v5 of device, date, eventType, operationTools.js:141-158) already make records that share those one record. That is consistent with the index. - A duplicate-key error from a race must become a re-read and match, never a 5xx (I4).

docs.title: 6. Open questions
docs.text:
Mechanism and trade-off for each. IDs are allocated by session -a5.

(i) Socket treatments: merge or keep on an identifier match. Decision 1 says merge. The socket's exact match keeps the stored record today and drops an edited re-send (identity reference §2.7, gate treatments: 1.). Mechanism: SOCKET_ADD.treatments.onExact is unchanged; the new identifier-match needs its own outcome. Trade-off: merge (M) applies an edited dose re-sent over the socket, and with the chart split unfixed it moves both halves. Keep (K) never lets a socket re-send change a stored dose, and with the split unfixed it loses the moved half. The 12 cells that differ are listed in the appendix.

(ii) Devicestatus: acknowledge, merge, or replace. Identifier matches acknowledge (I6, "devicestatus never merges"), which agrees with decision 1 only if devicestatus is an exception. The API v3 fallback match (created_at+device against a status with no identifier) replaces today (create/operation.js:56-60). The 12 group (h) cells keep that, as read. Mechanism: three outcomes on one collection, chosen by which key matched. Trade-off: merging a status into another folds Loop's distinct statuses that share created_at+device (identity §3 counts 3,078 groups). Acknowledging there also changes those 12 cells. Spec Q3 (i) (a differing body is a new record) is ID-NATURAL-KEY's, by decision 3.

(iii) "Stays deleted" against API v3's revive and history. API v3 POST brings a soft-deleted record back today. PUT and PATCH answer 410. v1 entries revive on purpose (wi:497-500). Under decision 2 nothing is written, so the re-send leaves no history entry and a client cannot undo a delete by re-sending. It needs a new identifier. Mechanism: on-deleted in identifier-match and in each remaining key. Trade-off: a deleted dose cannot come back through a retry or a full re-upload (UCA-SYNC-STORE-003). A record deleted by mistake cannot be restored through the API it was written with. v1 PUT/save on a deleted record still replaces, and so revives. Should "every path" cover edits, or only re-sends?

(iv) Stays deleted on keys other than the identifier. The socket's fallback key (no amounts), its ±2 s similar match, devicestatus created_at and profile startDate hide or revive deleted records today. Applying decision 2 to them moves the d2 plain cells and five fixtures. Mechanism: those keys are not identities, so a new record can share one with a deleted record. Trade-off: applying it means a new carb entry at the same created_at and eventType as a deleted one is acknowledged and not stored. Not applying it keeps today's second record beside the deleted one (4 cells and 4 fixtures stay as today), and for the socket profile today's revive.

(v) Two records with one identifier: the pick, and a unique index (§5). Options: - P1: each path keeps its pick (A on v1, B on v3). Changes nothing today and keeps BF-212. - One order everywhere: oldest or newest. One path changes and the loss moves to the other half. - P4: time key, then newest. Fixes -first/-second where the time survives; changes 400 to a merge on * v3 idf-split-first. - Refuse when ambiguous: a refusal per item. Safest for the data, but a retrying client loops (D-LOOP-ID rule 3).

Plus whether to add the partial unique index, and when: after the split fix and a duplicate report. Mechanism: identifier-match assumes I6, and the split and earlier writes break it. Trade-off: as listed, with the index making ambiguity impossible going forward at the cost of a migration for sites that already have duplicates.

(vi) Identifier format: where, and what a bad value gets. Where: identifier-format in plan() after the _id form (§1.1). Without that placement, a placeholder _id such as "undefined" that UUID_HANDLING moves on v1 treatments and entries is not checked. Today it becomes identifier and is matched first, so two clients sending that _id already share one record on v1 treatments [R: wi:276-280, wi:298-307]. The two options: - Refuse: HTTP 400 on API v3, as for an empty one (create/validate.js:19); a refused item on v1 (needs ID-BATCH, else the whole batch); { result: … } on the socket. - Treat as absent: match by the remaining order, and do not store the value. Storing it would put many records under one identifier and fail the unique index. On API v3 a computed identifier replaces it.

Cell impact from the pin: 0 cells under either option, because no form sends such a value (§4 item 3). Clients: none in the corpus is known to send a placeholder as identifier. The 12-site corpus's identifiers are 16 UUIDs and 489 32-hex values (format research §2). G7SensorKit's literal "invalid" is a Loop CGM syncIdentifier, and Loop sends no identity on entries (format research §1). The definition of "URL-safe" is open too. nightscout-connect sends glooko:<kind>:<sha256> and librelinkup:sensor-start:<sha256> (lib/sources/glooko/map.js:35-40, lib/sources/librelinkup.js:317 at 04102f9). Loop dose keys can hold / and spaces. Identifier conventions C3 allows : and /; RFC 3986's unreserved set does not. Trade-off: refusing makes a client that retries a refusal loop, and treating as absent silently changes what the client named.

(vii) Merge of nested objects. RFC 7386 merges object members, so a profile re-send that drops a named profile from store keeps it. v1 profile POST already merges (Q1b). The socket's profile and API v3's dedup replace today (c1). Mechanism: decision 1 applies RFC 7386 to the whole document. Trade-off: keeping fields another writer added, against a client that removes a profile by leaving it out and finds it still there.

(viii) _id re-sends on v1 food and activity create. These are upserting replaces by _id today. Decision 1 makes them merges: 18 of group (a), no value change in the pin. Mechanism: Q-H, "create on v1 has always been allowed to replace". Trade-off: one rule for every create, against keeping v1 POST by _id as a replace like PUT.

(ix) How additive decision 4 is. It holds for every earlier form (§2 (e)). Two consequences go beyond "unchanged". A socket request with no _id and an identifier is refused today and would be applied. No client is known to send one: AndroidAPS 3.4.2.x's v1 sync addresses by _id and sends no identifier (BF-209 register line). Activity identifier matching changes 24 new cells. Mechanism: "additive" is measured against existing forms, not against every input. Trade-off: shipping 6a with slice 1 (both "no existing form changes") or after slice 6, where the plan's "lands first where it changes no outcome" puts it.

(x) Addressing by an identifier two records share. A socket dbUpdate or dbRemove by identifier reaches one record or all of them. API v3 DELETE reaches all (§4 item 12). _id addressing reaches every stored form of one record (socketIdMatch, many: true). Mechanism: the pick of (v) or the every-form filter. Trade-off: deleting both halves of a split by one request, against an update that lands on the half the pick names.

(xi) When outcome slices ship. Plan row 9 puts "where it changes no outcome" in 16.2.0. D-LOOP-ID: "a default changes only in a major (16.0.0 if it clears the entry bar, otherwise 17.0.0)". Slices 3 to 6a each change a default. Mechanism: each slice is its own revert, so each can clear the bar or roll separately. Trade-off: 16.0.0 gets protections (slice 3) while the major is open, and 17.0.0 gives cohorts a release of notice.

docs.title: 6a. Question ids and answers (session -a5, 2026-10-29)
docs.text:
The questions in §6, numbered in order: (i) is ID-Q1, (ii) ID-Q2, (iii) ID-Q3, (iv) ID-Q4, (v) ID-Q5, (vi) ID-Q6, (vii) ID-Q7, (viii) ID-Q8, (ix) ID-Q9, (x) ID-Q10 and (xi) ID-Q11.

  • ID-Q5, decided by the maintainer:
  • the chart split stops copying identity fields, as a 16.0.0 backfix under BF-212;
  • identifier-first picks between existing duplicates by P4 (the time key, then the newest);
  • identifier-first never creates a second record with an identifier already stored;
  • a unique index comes later, after a per-site duplicate report and a cleanup step.
  • ID-Q4, decided: "stays deleted" applies only when the match is on an identity (identifier, syncIdentifier, id, uuid, NSCLIENT_ID, _id). A match on a time key against a deleted record stores the new record. The socket profile's revive is a separate small question.
  • ID-Q1, decided: socket treatments merge on an identifier match, after the split fix.
  • ID-Q3: the maintainer leans to refusing edits of a deleted record on every path, with a separate restore action. He asked first which clients that would affect and what the AndroidAPS authors intend. A client survey is under way.
  • ID-Q2, decided: device status follows the same default as the other collections (merge on an identifier match). The re-send switch (ID-RESEND-SWITCH) can select acknowledge, and the maintainer noted that the switch is the place for that choice. This changes only dev's unreleased behaviour since #8859 (acknowledge); 15.0.9 stored a duplicate. Loop sends no device-status identifier, and AndroidAPS creates each status once. API v3's created_at+device fallback is left to ID-NATURAL-KEY.
  • ID-Q6, decided:
  • no character restriction. Any string up to 256 characters (MongoDB's index key limit) is accepted, and the docs say an identifier used in a URL path must be percent-encoded;
  • a placeholder (undefined, null, invalid, an empty string) or an over-length value is treated as absent: it is ignored for matching, not stored, and answered with a warning;
  • strict refusal is available behind a setting, off by default;
  • the check runs right after the _id step, so a placeholder _id moved into identifier by UUID_HANDLING is caught as well.
  • ID-Q7, decided: a matched profile re-send replaces store as a whole, and its other fields merge. No released client depends on a merge of store: 15.0.9 refused that re-send (BF-166), and API v3 and the socket replace. This adjusts the dev-only Q1b rule for store.
  • ID-Q3, decided after a client survey:
  • an edit of a soft-deleted record over API v1 (PUT, the socket's dbUpdate, in-process save) is answered 2xx and not applied, so the record stays deleted. Today it revives;
  • API v3 keeps its documented 410;
  • a setting, off by default, makes v1 refuse instead (410);
  • the spec documents both, and client authors are asked to handle a 410, starting with AndroidAPS, whose upload queue stalls on a 410 PATCH;
  • a deliberate restore is a separate item.

Why 2xx on v1: every surveyed v1 editor retries a 4xx without limit, and Loop and xDrip+ then block other uploads. The server also cannot tell an xDrip+ edit from its retry, because both are a PUT. - ID-Q8, decided: merge, one rule. A matched v1 food or activity create merges, and only PUT replaces. - ID-Q9, decided: both additive items ship with slice 1 (a socket edit or remove by identifier without _id; activity creates matching identifier). No existing request changes. - ID-Q11, decided: data protection first. The slices go to the 16.0.0 entry bar in the order 1 (with the additive items), 2, 5, 3, 4, 6, 6a. Whatever has not cleared the bar at the tag rolls to 17.0.0 if it changes a default, otherwise to 16.1.0 (rule of 2026-10-30). - ID-Q10, decided: an edit addressed by an identifier that two stored records share lands on the record the P4 pick names. A delete addressed that way reaches every record sharing it, as API v3 DELETE does today. - Unique index, decided 2026-10-30: in 16.0.0 behind WRITE_IDENTIFIER_INDEX=try|require|off (default try). - try: build a partial unique index per collection (records with an identifier, soft-deleted included, built online). On existing duplicates, log counts and show them on the status page, then run without the index; the ID-Q5 write rule still blocks new duplicates. - require: refuse to start without the index. - off: skip it. - An operator-run tool reports duplicate groups and resolves them by the P4 pick. - **Settings, proposed by session -4f and confirmed by the maintainer (2026-10-29). They follow WRITE_VALIDATION: a WRITE_ prefix, and modes rather than booleans, with the default first: - WRITE_RESEND=merge|acknowledge|refuse; - WRITE_IDENTIFIER=lenient|strict; - WRITE_DELETED_EDIT=ignore|refuse.

All four, WRITE_VALIDATION included, are parsed by one module and read once, and an unknown value refuses to start. Per-client D20 quirks select a WRITE_RESEND mode for one registered client. Under multitenancy they are policy rows (D22), a question for the tenant-config schema.

docs.title: 7. How this was produced
docs.text:
• Inputs: the pin and -uuidoff pin (alignment 2258c458c, branch qc/matrix-idfirst), the harness at the same commit, session -4f's fact tables, the ID-FIRST-MATCH census (read-derived; where it disagrees with the pin, the pin is used: v1 profile after a soft delete stores a second record, profile v1 idf-softdel-plain n=2; API v3 create after a soft delete revives except on devicestatus, devicestatus v3 idf-softdel-plain n=1 OID:inv; the split target is deterministic, A on v1 and B on v3). Code: crm e8224807 for the step, the socket, API v3 and the gate. #8877 at ac5d77fb for the similar match's identity rule.
  • The classification is tools/qc/idfirst/classify.py <pin.json> [M|K] (option M or K for socket treatments), and the appendix is tools/qc/idfirst/render.py <out-M> <out-K> <out-uuidoff-M> <appendix.md> over its outputs for the pin, option K and the -uuidoff pin. Nothing was run against a server, and no prediction here is measured.

docs.title: Identifier conventions: one identifier per real thing
docs.text:
Living document, last changed 2026-10-29 at b982fbdd8.

Contributor-facing. Living draft, as of 2026-10-30. Decisions recorded here are the maintainer's of 2026-10-18, with the scope and absent-identifier decisions of 2026-10-27 and the format decisions of 2026-10-29 (D-LOOP-ID rule 1 and ID-Q6, in the 16.0.0 decisions) marked where they apply; the templates in §4 are proposals unless a cell says otherwise. Read after the identity specification (L0), whose format section this page fills in. Evidence: identifier format research (§1 per-app identity, §3.4 URL-form identifiers measured, §7 the G7 counter) and identifier duplicates. Queue: ID-CONVENTIONS, ID-FORMAT-DECISION, ID-ABSENT-DECISION, ID-SCOPE-DECISION.

identifier names the real thing a record describes (this CGM reading, this pump event, this carb entry), written in URL syntax whose scheme says where the thing comes from: the manufacturer for things that exist outside any app (dexcom://g7/<serial>/<offset>), the app for things made inside it (loop://carbs/<uuid>). The server treats the value as opaque, enforces one record per identifier in each collection and publishes the limits; clients compute the values, and this table is how two apps that see the same sensor or pump arrive at the same value. Measured 2026-10-18 at 15.0.8 and dev: URL-form identifiers work on API v3 when percent-encoded as one path segment, and on API v1 find[identifier]=; a raw / in a v3 path is 404.

Marks: [R] read from code at the commit given; [M] measured (the cited page says how); [proposed] a template or rule for the maintainer and client developers to confirm; [decided] the maintainer's decision of 2026-10-18, or of the date given.

docs.title: 1. Decisions
docs.text:
# decision status 1 identifier becomes mandatory at a future version boundary, and for registered instances of controllers (registration §8). Until then the legacy paths keep the time-key fallback for a write that carries none (entries sysTime + type, treatments created_at + eventType). The version boundary and how a hub tells a registered instance's writes apart are open (ID-ABSENT-DECISION). Until the boundary, identifier is SHOULD for legacy writers and MUST for registered controller instances (2026-10-27); what a hub answers a registered instance's write without one is open (identity §5, ID-REGISTERED-NO-IDENTIFIER). [decided] 2 Meaning. _id identifies the stored record (uniqueness in the database). identifier is the record's semantic identity in the data model: two uploads of the same real thing carry the same identifier, whichever device or app sends it. The server enforces uniqueness and states the format; clients compute the values. This refines the wording of D20 rule 5 ("the sync identity the client assigns") without changing its mechanics. [decided] 3 Format. Opaque to the server, one rule for every collection, plus this published table per record kind so different apps converge on one value. URL syntax: <scheme>://<segment>/<segment>/…. [decided] 4 Scheme. Things that exist outside the app (sensor readings, pump events) use a source scheme: the manufacturer is the scheme and the model is the first segment (dexcom://g7/…, dexcom://g6/…, abbott://libre3/…). Things created inside an app (manual carbs, boluses, overrides, temporary targets, device status) use an app scheme (loop://carbs/…). [decided] 5 A controller's own format. A controller may use one format of its own across collections for the records it creates, for example loop://carbs/<uuid>, loop://tempbasal/<syncId>, loop://override/<uuid>, loop://devicestatus/<uuid>. Constraints: unique per collection, within the limits of §2, stable across re-sends. A registered instance declares the format it uses (§5). [decided]

Why a source scheme. The maintainer's first example, loop://g7/<serial>/<sensor offset>, names the uploading app. Loop and xDrip+ reading one G7 would then produce two identifiers for one reading, which is the opposite of what decision 2 asks. With the manufacturer as the scheme, every app that reads the sensor's own serial and counter produces the same bytes. One scheme per vendor covers all its models, serial numbers are a manufacturer's namespace, and the shape matches loop://g7/….

Scope, decided (maintainer, 2026-10-27; ID-SCOPE-DECISION). Uniqueness is per collection, with the tenant in the key under multi, while values are globally unique by convention: the kind segment (carbs, tempbasal, devicestatus, or the model for a source scheme) keeps two collections from ever holding the same value. Each collection's partial unique index on identifier is in 16.0.0 under WRITE_IDENTIFIER_INDEX=try|require|off (maintainer, 2026-10-30; identity §3).

The kind segment fixes a measured hazard. 13 Loop syncIdentifier values are each on 2 to 4 treatments in the corpus; 9 of them are a Suspend Pump and a Temp Basal at the same created_at (identifier duplicates §2.2) [M]. Sent as identifier today, the second would replace the first. loop://suspend/<id> and loop://tempbasal/<id> differ. The other 4 values are Temp Basals only (groups spread over more than a day, and one pair 1 s apart); a kind segment does not separate those, and the cause on Loop's side is not known.

docs.title: 2. The rule the server states
docs.text:
# constraint status C1 a JSON string with at least one non-whitespace character enforced on API v3 create today [R] C2 at most 256 characters; a longer value is treated as absent, with a warning [decided] 2026-10-29 (D-LOOP-ID rule 1, ID-Q6); an indexed value near 1 KB fails the insert on MongoDB before 4.2 [M] C3 characters from A-Z a-z 0-9 - . _ ~ : /; no %, ?, #, space or control characters [proposed] as the set clients build values from; the server applies no character restriction and an identifier in a URL path is percent-encoded ([decided] 2026-10-29, ID-Q6). / and : are in the set because the URL form needs them and the measurement below holds C4 not exactly 24 hex characters, unless it equals the record's own _id [proposed]; both APIs read a 24-hex value as an _id too [R] C5 not history, . or .., and no client placeholder (invalid, undefined, null, NaN, unknown) placeholders: [decided] 2026-10-29 (ID-Q6) for undefined, null, invalid and an empty string, which the server treats as absent with a warning (refused under WRITE_IDENTIFIER=strict); NaN and unknown are open (identity §5, ID-PLACEHOLDER-LIST); the path words are [proposed] C6 one identifier, one record, per collection, for as long as the record is stored identity rule I6 C7 compared exactly: case-sensitive, never trimmed or normalised identity rule I6 C8 URL syntax <scheme>://<segments>: scheme lower case, [a-z][a-z0-9+.-]*; segments separated by /; no empty segment [proposed]; the server does not parse it, so this is a convention for clients, not a check

Writing one in an API v3 path. Percent-encode the whole identifier as one path segment (encodeURIComponent in JavaScript: : becomes %3A, / becomes %2F). At 15.0.8 92d08342 and dev fade2299, an encoded URL-form identifier works on v3 GET, PATCH, PUT (update and create) and DELETE, ?identifier$eq= search finds it, and v1 find[identifier]= finds it encoded or raw; a raw / in the path is 404 [M, §3.4]. A path helper that leaves / unescaped (Foundation's urlPathAllowed set allows /) builds the wrong route. v1 by-id routes (DELETE /api/v1/treatments/:id, find[_id]=) understand UUID- and ObjectId-shaped values only, so a client deletes over v1 with the _id the write reply returns. Reverse proxies that decode or refuse %2F were not measured; behind one, reads work through search and find[identifier]=.

Build the string, do not normalise it. In RFC 3986 terms the first segment after // is the authority; some URL libraries lower-case or re-encode it. Clients should build the value by concatenation from the convention's parts and send those exact bytes, since the server compares them exactly (C7).

docs.title: 3. How two apps converge
docs.text: They converge only when every input of the template comes from the device itself (the sensor's serial and counter, the pump's own event record), not from the receiving phone's clock or a random generator (format research §1). A record created inside one app (a carb entry typed on the phone) has one origin, so there is nothing to converge: an app that reads it back from Nightscout keeps the identifier it received and never mints a new one. If an input is missing (no serial yet, no counter), send no identifier and let the time key apply; never a partial value or a placeholder.

docs.title: 5. How a registered controller declares its convention
docs.text:
Decision 5 says a registered instance declares the format it uses. Where it goes is a proposal: the registration grammar v1 has no member for it.

  • An instance carries no meaning of its own; it names a stored definition by definitionId (registration §8), and a definition is where a product says what its data means (registration §7). So the declaration belongs in the definition, as a meaning member, for example identifiers: [{collection: treatments, kind: carbs, template: "loop://carbs/{uuid}"}, …]. Being meaning, a changed template would need a new definition version (§7's "one element at one version has one meaning").
  • A hub can then check a registered instance's writes against its own declaration (scheme and kind segment) and, under decision 1, refuse one with no identifier. It cannot check that a value names the right real thing; that stays the client's contract.
  • Source schemes (§4.1) are not a product's to declare: they belong to this table, and a definition that uses one names it rather than restating it, as a well-known kind is named by wellKnownRef today.

docs.title: 7. Open
docs.text:
• The version boundary at which identifier becomes mandatory on legacy paths, how a hub recognises a registered instance's write on a legacy path (ID-ABSENT-DECISION), and what it answers one without identifier (ID-REGISTERED-NO-IDENTIFIER).
  • Placeholders beyond ID-Q6's four (NaN, unknown, a whitespace-only value), and the form of the warning a write gets when its value is treated as absent (ID-PLACEHOLDER-LIST, ID-WARNING-FORM).
  • The client developers' answers: whether the source-scheme templates work for them, and each app's scheme spelling (Loop is asked first, reply).
  • Unknown cells in §4: Dexcom ONE+ and Stelo model segments, the Libre 2 serial source, AndroidAPS per-driver pumpId origin, Trio override ids, a per-cycle device status id for Trio, AndroidAPS and oref0.
  • The G7 two-display capture (format research §7.6) before any client relies on dexcom://g7/… converging.
  • Proxies: whether common reverse-proxy setups pass %2F through to v3 paths.
  • The UUIDv5 bridge: format research §4 proposed hashing a source-derived name into a UUIDv5 for today's v1 by-id routes. With URL-form identifiers the readable form is the identifier; whether a v5 form is still offered for v1-only clients is open.

docs.title: Integration questionnaire: default answers for Loop, Trio, AndroidAPS and OpenAPS, read from their source
docs.text:
Record

Record as of 2026-10-18. A point-in-time document; it is not kept up to date.

Contributor-facing. Snapshot — describes 2026-10-18. Status: current; every answer is a default for the project named in its column to correct. Repository facts are read at this repository's 57a6db95; controller facts at the commits in §1, each checked against the project's current branch head through the GitHub API on 2026-10-18. Every cell is marked R (read-derived: from source; a hypothesis about behaviour), M (measured: the 11-site corpus) or H (history: a release, tag or branch fact from the GitHub API). Current decisions: execution plan §1.

The question. docs/proposals/integration-questionnaire.md is part of the earlier draft in cgm-remote-monitor's docs/proposals (with agent-control-plane-rfc.md, bridge-rules.md and conflict-resolution.md), which this repository's specifications are proposed to supersede. It asks AID controller projects 16 questions (A1–G16) in 14 tables; each response section reads Pending. Read at cgm-remote-monitor a8888f0d; the file is unchanged on dev fade2299 since db32bdc6 (2026-01-19). The maintainer decided on 2026-10-18 that every answer is filled, for every controller, with a default read from that controller's source and history, and from the corpus where it applies. This page is that fill.

docs.title: How to use this
docs.text:
• Each cell is a default for the project to correct. It states what the cited source does at the cited commit. A project corrects a cell by saying what is different; the corrected cell then cites the project and the date.
  • To send a correction: open an issue or pull request on this repository naming the question id and column (for example "C7, Trio"), or answer on cgm-remote-monitor with the label agentic-control-plane as the questionnaire asks. A source link or a test is the fastest correction; a sentence is enough.
  • Where source cannot settle a question (G15 timeline, G16 concerns), the cell gives the default the evidence supports and names what only the project can correct.
  • Columns. The questionnaire's tables carry an OpenAPS column only in A1 and A3; its response list names OpenAPS. Every table here has an OpenAPS column, read from oref0 (the rig).
  • Corpus coverage. The corpus is 11 Nightscout sites (snapshots 2026-04-01 and 2026-04-26), 9 of them Loop. One site carries openaps.* devicestatus, and its openaps.recommendedBolus, pump.bolusIncrement and Exercise treatments are Trio's (M: census paths below; landscape §3.2). The AndroidAPS column is read from source only: the corpus has no AndroidAPS closed-loop site (M: no pump.extended or openaps.enacted.requested path in the devicestatus census). The OpenAPS column is read from source only: the corpus has no oref0 rig (M: no mmtune or preferences path). Census counts are reads across both snapshots, which overlap, so they bound distinct documents from above.

docs.title: Appendix A. iAPS
docs.text: The questionnaire does not list iAPS. The intent landscape (§1, iAPS 6cb69e7, 2026-10-04) covers it; its defaults, from that page, are: separate override presets and an append-only override log, presets not sent to Nightscout (A2); override and temp target concurrent, temp target wins the target (A4); ends on expiry, carbs, glucose thresholds or a chained preset, reason in the debug log only (G16); remote intent arrives as Nightscout Announcement treatments, authorised by Nightscout write access, with no acknowledgement (F13). All read-derived; not re-read here.

docs.title: Which interface owns which API: single-tenant and hosted multitenant
docs.text:
Record

Record as of 2026-10-27. A point-in-time document; it is not kept up to date.

Contributor-facing. Snapshot, 2026-10-27: cgm-remote-monitor dev 7abe1cf6, with draft PRs read at their heads (#8857 f7a43fed, #8865 1dafe2a5). Drafted by session -ee's research agent from the sources listed below; two code claims re-checked by -ee (#8857's INSTANCES_HREF, #8865's serve api mounts). Nothing here is decided beyond what its sources record; §5's questions are for the maintainer. "Read" means read from the path given. "{C}" is the deployable components document, "exec plan" the execution plan, "v4 doc" the v4 surface, "§F.1" the tenant-owner configuration surface.

Current architecture clarification, 2026-11-08 (read-derived): the REST component contract places v1/v2/v3 routers/adapters together in one stateless REST API component. Replicas and Compose/Kubernetes placement are separate dimensions. The questions below retain this snapshot's historical alternatives; §5 question 7's separate v1-role option is superseded by that component direction. Its original source claims are not current route-acceptance claims. Owner and operator audiences retain their existing listener/privilege boundaries.

Summary. On dev today one listener serves everything: API v1, v2 and v3, the socket.io channels, the pages and, in #8857 behind a flag, /.well-known and /api/v4. API_SECRET is both the device credential and the owner credential.

The decisions split hosted multitenant along two axes: - Audience gives three listeners (D16): ns-api for the data path, ns-tenant-admin for the tenant owner, and ns-admin for the platform operator. - Workload gives the roles api, evaluator, realtime and vcpool (D5).

D21 packages them as nightscout multitenant <roles>; nightscout single remains the single-tenant monolith. This CLI naming amendment does not make any multitenant role available.

Most v1, v2, v3 and v4 data operations stay on the data listener. Owner actions and owner configuration move to the tenant-owner listener. Tenant lifecycle exists only on the operator's credential-free plane.

The sources leave several things unplaced or in conflict (§4): - v1's hosted home; - the socket's listener and its write events; - the split of /api/v2/authorization; - the pages; - paths served on two listeners.

docs.title: 3. What moves between single-tenant and multitenant, and why
docs.text:
1. The credential root. Under single-tenant, API_SECRET grants ['*'] and acts as the owner (AU2). Under multitenant no deployment secret exists on any interface (D13).
  2. Each tenant holds its own root credential and signing key (D14).
  3. Subject tokens are re-rooted on the tenant's credential, because today they hash API_SECRET (exec plan §2.8).
  4. The reason: one install-wide secret and key cannot separate tenants. With per-tenant keys, a token presented to another tenant fails its signature check, not just a claim check.
  5. The configuration source. single reads the environment; hosted roles read per-tenant configuration from the database (D15). That is why the tenant-owner listener exists: under single-tenant the environment is the owner's interface, and under multitenant that interface has to be an authenticated, row-scoped API. Which settings a tenant owns is the census (264 on dev).
  6. The owner's actions. The paths stay the same; they move from "one listener plus API_SECRET" to ns-tenant-admin (authority §4). The boundary is stated per credential (AU7), so a hub with one listener can conform.
  7. The operator plane appears. Single-tenant has no operator. Multitenant adds tenant lifecycle on a credential-free, unroutable listener (D7). No credential means nothing to phish, leak or reuse; the cost is one operational rule: that port is never routed.
  8. Workloads split. Sockets move to realtime, alarms and plugins to evaluator, connectors to vcpool, and stateless HTTP stays in api (D5). The listener count is per deployment, not per tenant.

docs.title: 4. Gaps and contradictions
docs.text:
1. The v4 doc is stale about #8857. At f7a43fed, #8857 serves GET /api/v4/instances (index.js:28, products.js:376), and its test asserts that the older GET /api/v4/registrations/instances answers 404 (tests/registration.instances.test.js:316-327). The v4 doc still describes 3be98536 in §5, the §5.1 follow-up table and §7 row 3's evidence.
  2. One path prefix, two listeners. /api/v4/instances takes PUT and DELETE on data and GET on tenant-admin, and DELETE on a product is on both listeners (v4 doc operation 6). Authority §4 says the listener, not the path, decides. But no routing table states which methods each listener mounts; #8857 mounts one router with an isOwner check (products.js:307).
  3. /api/v2/authorization mixes two audiences. request/:token is data-path, while subjects, roles and permissions are owner configuration (§F.1). #8865 mounts the whole router on the consumer listener (serve/api.js:35), and no source splits it.
  4. The scope of serve api. The three sources disagree, and none dates v1's hosted home:
  5. D21's table says "express and storage", configured per tenant from the database.
  6. {C} §2.1 says v3, v1, v2 summary, auth and tenant resolution.
  8. Decided 2026-10-27 (maintainer): serve api serves API v1, API v3, the v2 summary and authorization, and tenant resolution, as {C} §2.1 says. v1 joins once its storage paths run without the in-memory cache. The socket stays with the realtime role (question 3 below is unchanged). As a consequence, the 15 API v3 tests that write to a record created through API v1 keep running under serve api.
  9. The socket's listener and its writes. The sources disagree on where the socket lives:
  10. CM28 puts it "on the hub's existing listener".
  11. D16 groups ns-api and ns-realtime in one row.
  13. The tenant-admin plane. D16 decided "a second bound socket inside ns-api", and D21 lists serve tenant-admin as a role. #8865 still marks it plane consumer "until D16's third listener is designed" (roles.js:9-10), so no listener rule keeps it off the data listener's address. That comment is stale.
  14. Names. Exec plan §2.3 uses ADMIN_BIND; #8865 uses ADMIN_HOSTNAME.
  15. The healthcheck. D21 rule 5 names nightscout healthcheck as the image's healthcheck. #8862 ships no image HEALTHCHECK, by the maintainer's decision: a boot-error page must not be restarted away. D21's text is stale.
  16. Discovery when hosted. The v4 doc puts well-known on the data listener, but #8857 mounts it only in single's app.js, and #8865's api app answers 404 to everything else. Whether CONTROLLER_REGISTRATION is per deployment or per tenant under D15: not found.
  17. The pages. No source assigns /, /admin, /profile, /food, /report or /clock to a listener or role under multitenant. /admin is the owner's UI today, and it calls owner endpoints.
  18. Stale lines in the v4 doc.
    • §1 says the owner's path "is not settled", while §0 and §7 record it as decided.
    • The §2 note says the commands specification names no listener, but CM32 now names the data listener.

docs.title: 8865 serves only v3 and the v2 authorization router, reading the environment. v1 is absent
docs.text: until ST-V3-DECOUPLE (M3), which is also why 81 API v3 suites fail under serve api.

docs.title: 8865 gives realtime its own REALTIME_* listener.
docs.text: D21 also says realtime makes "no storage writes", but the root namespace takes dbAdd, dbUpdate, dbUpdateUnset and dbRemove (websocket.js:447-992).

docs.title: 5. Open questions for the maintainer
docs.text:
1. Is a composed serve of every role part of the multitenant target (D21, open)?
  2. (a) A supported topology, tested in TEN-LAB.
  3. (b) A small-hoster convenience only.

Recommended: (a) for api,realtime,tenant-admin,evaluator, with admin always in its own process, as exec plan §2.3 and §F.1 require. #8865 already keeps one listener per role, so composing roles changes processes, not boundaries. TEN-LAB runs both shapes. 2. Where do tenant-owner actions live under single-tenant? - (a) As now: one listener, API_SECRET, the same paths, configuration from the environment. - (b) An optional TENANT_ADMIN_PORT under single-tenant. - (c) Credential-only (AU7), with no listener rule.

Recommended: (a). It is decided for registration (AU2) and keeps D1. Offer (b) only if self-hosters ask. 3. Is the socket part of the data listener, or its own realtime role? - (a) The ns-api listener, as CM28 words it. - (b) Its own REALTIME_* listener, with the edge routing /socket.io/ on the same public host.

Recommended: (b), as #8865 encodes. Amend CM28 to read "the hub's public host". Amend D21's realtime row: socket writes go through the storage interface in realtime, or are refused under multitenant with a stated status. 4. Where is the identity-provider adapter boundary (D17 as amended)? - (a) An OIDC token contract (issuer, audience, key set) turned into a subject. - (b) A per-provider plugin (Kratos session check, Clerk session). - (c) An identity-aware proxy passing a signed header.

Recommended: (a) as the contract, with (b) only for Kratos, which the Ory proof measured. The adapter sits on the tenant-owner listener's exchange. Its output is a subject plus a tenant_members lookup, and nsjwt mints the per-tenant token (D14). The data listener never accepts provider credentials (AU1). Owed: the list of properties each hoster must supply. 5. Should /api/v2/authorization be split under multitenant? - (a) request/:token on data; subjects, roles and permissions on tenant-admin. - (b) Whole, on data, guarded by permissions.

Recommended: (a), following §F.1 and AU7. Single-tenant is unchanged. 6. How are paths served on two listeners routed? - (a) A per-operation listener table generated from nightscout-v4.yaml, mounted on both listeners, with the data listener answering 403 not-authorised to owner operations. The conformance cases owner-action-on-data-listener and instances/owner-transfer-role-data-listener exist. - (b) A separate owner prefix.

Recommended: (a). The same paths on every deployment is decided (v4 doc §7 decision 1). 7. Where and when does v1 go hosted? - (a) Into serve api after ST-V3-DECOUPLE (M3). - (b) A separate v1 role. - (c) No v1 under multitenant.

Recommended: (a), since {C} §2.1 already assigns it there. The multitenant preview needs it: the apps in authority §9 item 7 authenticate with the hashed api-secret header. 8. Which of today's credential forms are accepted under multitenant (authority §9 item 7)? - (a) The tenant's root credential, in today's hashed api-secret header and the v1 socket secret. - (b) New token forms only.

Recommended: (a), so uploaders need no change (D1), with subject tokens re-rooted per D13.

docs.title: Next-gen platform: one write path, four tracks
docs.text:
Living document, last changed 2026-11-08 at f70852564.

Contributor-facing living plan. Reconciled 2026-11-08 to the published operation-window acceptance family and release record. Draft #8898 carries ed2ced00c80bd0a6a7d75f834d2c6e2af8c71364, based on dev 4a482627. Native/browser, corpus and cold-deployment campaigns retain their actual source heads. Current milestone claims live in the delivery dashboard; release placement lives in release allocation. This is a map of bounded capabilities and remaining work, not production admission.

The interactive version, with the dependency map, is the site page nightscout-next-gen-platform.html.

This plan covers the work that follows the 16.0.0 modernization:

  • storage behind one write path;
  • the client and server identifiers Loop asked to separate;
  • controller registration, from a read-only catalogue to typed writes;
  • multitenant Nightscout.

It names each piece of work, what it needs first, where it goes in the code, and the check that pins it.

docs.title: 1. Where things stand
docs.text:
The tenancy reading guide identifies the current plan, decision owners and historical evidence. Start with the dashboard for sequencing; use this map to see how the platform tracks meet.

Scope Current recorded acceptance What remains Foundations, data and tenant authority R72 retains M0 and promotes M1–M4: admitted PG ports/import, actual typed/versioned owner settings, tenant refusal and route separation, pinned headless clients and source-pattern replay. Wider owner catalogue/lifecycle and production resolution trust; Android emulator and resource bounds in C. No all-client claim. Durable runtime R73 accepts functional M5 on one host: separate roles, polling/snapshots, durable suppression and reference notification handoff. Live provider/device delivery, multi-node ownership and capacity/freshness/egress budgets. Tenant-local recovery and shared-process restart Operation-window acceptance accepts same-ID logical restore with forward client history, public-ID preservation, fail-closed uncertainty and B continuity while A remains suspended, including fresh service processes. Native evidence is on c23; cold Compose/UI/socket/restore and pinned-client evidence is on ed2. Fixed trusted process cohort, private ingress and direct PG connections bound this proof. Dynamic membership, transaction pooling, multi-host coordination, arbitrary direct SQL writers and automatic orphan clearance remain outside it. Deployment artifact and verification The published ed2 draft has an exact-source Compose image and cold synthetic deployment acceptance. Final full-suite and pinned-client campaigns are on ed2; native/default-browser on c23 and entire enabled corpus on 39f4 retain their source attribution. Whole M6 stays blocked. Draft publication, dev merge, operator release, default enablement and production admission are distinct boundaries. Optional shared human identity Shared OIDC/session capability is fixed on a separate local source branch with bounded source checks and controls. Actual signed native DB/Vault/HTTPS/browser and reference-provider acceptance are UNMEASURED. It has not joined the published Compose candidate. Independent single/nonresident profile R55 accepts private acquisition on 2ee8b493, with caller policies and the physical subscriber retained. The computed-single branch remains separate; full writer/alarm/clinical coverage, freshness, cost and its own entry bar remain. Default single stays resident.

The acceptance family owns exact source/instrument identities and immutable failed and successful runs; the release record owns programme disposition. This reconciliation is read-derived from those records, not a rerun of the application. Recorded-evidence gates replay archived captures; they do not execute a fresh native/current-HEAD campaign.

docs.title: What is complete enough to inform a decision?
docs.text:
Use an accepted capability to answer the question it exercised. An implementation can settle a bounded design question while its parent queue item remains open. A production decision additionally needs an operating envelope, deployment trust and failure recovery under the selected topology.

Decision you can make from current evidence Evidence supports Evidence still needed to unlock broader use Keep API, realtime and evaluator as explicit cooperating roles Functional one-host M5 and later cold Compose demonstrate consumed role boundaries and restart behavior. Fixed-roster API scaling needs instance-complete drain/invalidation and endpoint trust, separately from singleton evaluator ownership. Multi-host/HA adds failover and partition acceptance; platform placement/assignment does not replace application operation lifetime. Keep restore tenant-local in the reference topology Actual restore/history convergence and B continuity, including B startup while A stays suspended. Broader membership, orphan resolution policy and production recovery objectives. The adopted ownership contract excludes independent direct SQL writers; stronger fencing is not a production prerequisite for the supported cooperative topology. Continue the admitted PostgreSQL backend and migration path Tenant-scoped native/HTTP/storage controls and append-only allocator migration/restore work. Supported production workloads, pool limits, noisy-neighbor behavior, capacity and restore/upgrade budgets. Scope a reusable current-property result Derived-output characterization finds selected evaluator/API properties agree, with time/settings/identity-sensitive controls. A reusable result interface and expiry/invalidation checks. Raw realtime frames remain a different product; no publication service or distributed result store is selected. Choose resident versus computed execution for single-tenant sites The independent prototype demonstrates bounded functional behavior and failures worth guarding. Quiet steady-state cost, full caller/clinical coverage and per-profile reliability before changing placement or defaults. Select an identity/deployment reference for acceptance Adopted generic OIDC, Vault progression and per-deployment trust/probe contracts define what to build and test. Native signed/session/provider acceptance, service-login renewal and live edge/Vault probes. Source checks alone do not admit a production identity system.

The deployment guide separates tenancy, backend, execution profile, service placement and host topology. These are independent choices: more processes improve operational separation, while a shared host, PostgreSQL service, Vault or edge can still fail all tenants. The current M5/M6 decision list owns remaining policy questions; the release decisions own adopted answers. A deferred decision keeps its prototypes and benches running.

docs.title: Current architecture clarifications
docs.text:
For current module/worker placement, read the logical REST/API map and the database ownership visual review. REST v1/v2/v3, authorization and owner REST form one logical stateless request-serving API component, retaining version-specific adapters and audience/listener contracts. This grouping neither splits services by protocol version nor admits routes outside the recorded compatibility scope. Realtime, singleton evaluation, connector work and private operator maintenance have separate workload roles; API participants consume admission/invalidation hooks rather than run restoration orchestration. This is a clarification of responsibilities, not a new process layout.

Endpoint transport and fixed-roster API scaling are queued source capabilities; Kubernetes/Jsonnet proof and evaluator partitioning are deferred. Operator activity/resource policy is proposed and undecided, separate from existing maintenance safety and observed health. The map's acceptance states and historical measurements remain unchanged.

Earlier overview Retained evidence R62–R72 overview at the prior revision Earlier publication checks, prototype failures and small clock HTTP evidence; the integration record and named capsules retain their original verdicts. R49–R55 platform checkpoints at the prior revision Native and cumulative campaigns, capacity HOLD and cleanup captures, original replica failure and focused clock repair. Their named reports remain authoritative for those runs.

docs.title: 1. 16.0.0 scope (maintainer, 2026-10-30)
docs.text:
16.0.0 targets every single-tenant item of this plan, through the entry bar and in priority order. A miss rolls to 16.1.0, or to 17.0.0 if it changes a default. - The identity work is the core. It is the substance of the agreement with the Loop maintainers: identifier-first on every path, re-sends recognised, the format rules, and one record per identifier. - The unique index on identifier is in 16.0.0, behind WRITE_IDENTIFIER_INDEX=try|require|off|drop (default try). - Under try, boot attempts a partial unique index per collection: records with an identifier, soft-deleted ones included, built online. If existing duplicates block it, the counts per collection (never the values) are logged and shown on the status page, and the server runs without the index. - The write rule (ID-Q5) still refuses to create a second record with a stored identifier. - require refuses to start until the index exists. off skips building it but leaves any existing index enforced; drop removes the index at boot, then runs as off. - An operator-run tool reports duplicate groups and resolves them by the P4 pick. - Multitenant items may ship dormant, labelled alpha behind explicit multitenant configuration, or not ship.

Feasibility, from the 7 days to 2026-10-30: 53 PRs merged into dev, and 14 of this plan's 36 items went to done. Build speed is not the limit. Time on dev, cohort checks and review are, so items land in priority order and early, and the tag is gated by the bar, not by a date.

docs.title: 1a. Priority and merge order (2026-10-29)
docs.text:
The release allocation owns release ordering, the release contents own merged and tested state, and the queue owns item claims. Identity and the write path remain the single-tenant release priority; a multitenant prototype passing its own campaign does not bypass that release entry bar.

The detailed October merge-order and per-commit execution table is retained in the captured platform revision. It preserves the original source heads, matrix results, cohort requests and release hypotheses. It is historical context, not a current dispatch queue.

docs.title: 2. Why the tracks meet at the write step
docs.text:
Every track changes what happens when a record is written:

track what it needs from the write step Identity a single place that matches a re-sent record on identifier first, then on the time key, for v1, v3 and the socket alike Registration a single place that applies a controller's declared schema to its typed writes, and leaves unregistered writers byte-identical Validation a single place for #8841's rules, so the socket and the v1 modules are not checked separately Tenancy a single place that carries the tenant binding, so no path can write without one

docs.title: 8854 built that place as a boundary at the driver call, and the storage interface sits above it. Each later slice adds one rule there. Every slice must keep the following:
docs.text:
must hold pinned by the _id forms: ObjectId, upper- and lower-case hex, UUID, and UUID_HANDLING moving a non-hex _id to identifier #8854's matrix rows; tests/identity-matrix.test.js the API v3 create and deduplication reply (status, identifier, isDeduplication, lastModified), and AndroidAPS's string-matched refusal texts tests/write-validation.test.js; the v3 suites Loop's syncIdentifier and Trio's id stored and returned untouched write-contract matrix v1 treatment upsert on created_at + eventType write-contract matrix

The forward constraints are two mature backends behind one interface (D2–D4), the closed query operator set as a filter tree (D8), a source label and later a tenant binding on every write, and one commit fact the change feed can carry (D6; D-EVENT decided 2026-10-31: one in-process event per write, named from WriteResult.items[], and the per-database-call event kept as backend instrumentation; delivery between processes is decided with the serve roles; its card in §5). Under #8854's merge conditions, the commit event stays internal and unstable, and the intent layer gets its own name. The later B7 recovery direction uses a durable feed and the adopted bounded full current-state snapshot backstop; the time-only alarm tick remains separate from that reconciliation schedule.

docs.title: 3. The map
docs.text:
For multitenant status and sequencing, use the multitenant delivery dashboard. It owns M0-M6 prerequisites, parallel lanes, bounded slices and current acceptance. The roadmap defines milestone criteria and boundaries. The integration record and named reports retain execution evidence. This map summarizes their bounded implications.

Read a node's reference and remaining scope before treating its color as a verdict. Done means the named item/component is complete or merged to dev; it says nothing by itself about an operator release. In progress/blocked can contain accepted useful slices with broader work remaining. Arrows show prerequisites, not runtime communication, fault domains or percentage complete. Milestone promotion belongs to the dashboard; deployment admission belongs to the selected deployment's trust record and measured probes.

docs.title: 4.1 Storage
docs.text:
Done, in 16.0.0: PR-8854, QC-MATRIX-TT (360 cells), ST-FILTER, ST-READS, ST-WRITES, ST-COUNT-ONEPATH, ST-V3-DECOUPLE, WC-STEP-PATCH (release 1).

item builds needs check WC-STEP-PATCH release 1 merged as #8874 (368e6c23, no behaviour change); release 2 merged as #8886 (51d38f9f, 2026-11-01), resolves filter writes to ids and gives API v3 the same write shape (Q9, Q-U, Q-A); the reached ids come back in WriteResult.removed and .updated, and items[] stays one slot per input (maintainer, 2026-10-31): write(intent) -> WriteResult.items[] above the interface; matching, server dates, the null-removes rule and validation move into it; compare-and-set behind an adapter method ST-WRITES write-contract spec G1 ST-V3-DECOUPLE merged with #8865 (991b0654): dependency decoupling of API v3 from API v1's modules, socket and cache. docs.title: 4.2 Identity
docs.text:
Done, in 16.0.0: DEV-8845, ID-SIMPLE-MATCH. Done in this repository: SPEC-ID-AMEND (2026-10-30).

item builds needs check SPEC-ID-AMEND a conformance case for the mandatory identifier on registered instances; identity I2 and §6 state API v3's refusal of a client _id (BF-170) #8845 tools/nsschema cases ID-FIRST-MATCH identifier-first on every collection and path ID-SIMPLE-MATCH, WC-STEP-PATCH (D-LOOP-ID's rules decided 2026-10-29) write-contract matrix; the re-send table, identity reference §2.7 ID-BATCH v1 per-item reply behavior and index-dependent duplicate-key retry for batch writes WC-STEP-PATCH, ID-UNIQUE-INDEX implemented across #8889 and #8894, including tests in tests/api.id-batch-replies.test.js and tests/api.batch-race-item-level.test.js; the old local branch is not a separate release-critical PR ID-RESEND-SWITCH site-level WRITE_RESEND and WRITE_DELETED_RESEND modes, defaulting to current behavior ID-FIRST-MATCH and compatibility B merged as #8892 (3c773ee5); local matrix showed 0/4,916 default-mode changes relative to its base; required hosted checks passed ID-UNIQUE-INDEX partial unique index on identifier, per collection (with the tenant under multi); duplicate-key races follow the selected resend mode (Q-IDX), including batch item retry ID-FIRST-MATCH, ID-RESEND-SWITCH merged as #8894 at 497d08c9 on dev; all required hosted checks passed. Full --batch --no-idf matrix: 3,443 cells per off/try lane, zero invalid cells, same 33 expected batch differences on MongoDB 5.0.32/8.0.34; remaining differences are cache-only.

Rules in force (maintainer, 2026-10-26 and 2026-10-27; updated 2026-10-31):

  • Null removes. An explicit null removes a field on a merged re-send (WRITE_RESEND=merge-except-treatments), API v3 PATCH and the socket's dbUpdate (RFC 7386; write contract §6.1). It never does so on PUT or create, and devicestatus never merges.
  • Fallback. A v1 entries re-send whose identifier matches nothing still matches on sysTime+type; treatments never fall back. A devicestatus re-send whose identifier is stored replaces the stored record by default (compatibility B, 2026-10-31; it merged from ID-Q2, 2026-10-29); WRITE_RESEND=merge-except-treatments keeps that, and WRITE_RESEND=acknowledge the rule before it (write nothing, answer with the stored _id).
  • Absent identifier. identifier is SHOULD for legacy writers, and the time-key fallback stays. It is MUST for registered controller instances. Revisited as adoption grows.
  • Scope. Uniqueness is per collection, with the tenant in the key under multi. Values stay globally unique by convention.
  • Re-send after delete. It is acknowledged with a 2xx naming the stored, deleted record, and the record stays deleted. WRITE_DELETED_RESEND=revive (default stay, 2026-10-31) restores 15.0.9's re-send that revives a deleted record.
  • Format (2026-10-29, D-LOOP-ID rule 1 and ID-Q6). Any string of 1 to 256 characters, with no character restriction, percent-encoded in a URL path; a UUID is recommended. A placeholder or over-length value is treated as absent with a warning; refusing it is WRITE_IDENTIFIER=strict, off by default. 2026-10-31 (compatibility A): API v3 refuses a malformed identifier with 400 by default, as 15.0.9 did; API v1, the socket and in-process stay lenient. Which placeholders are named is open (ID-PLACEHOLDER-LIST, identity specification §5).
  • _id (2026-10-29). A client may still send an ObjectId _id over API v1 (legacy). Going forward the server sets _id and the client sets identifier.
  • Replace on match (2026-10-31, compatibility B; supersedes merge on match of 2026-10-29). A re-send matching a stored record replaces it on every collection, as slice 4 does for treatments. Extended the same evening: every re-send matched by identifier replaces on every path, including the identifier-first matches for profile, food, activity and device status over v1, in-process and the socket; entries over v1 and in-process keep merging, as on 15.0.9. Merge stays for edits: API v3 PATCH and the socket's dbUpdate. WRITE_RESEND=replace|merge-except-treatments|acknowledge|refuse (default replace) and WRITE_DELETED_RESEND=stay|revive (default stay) are built before the tag as opt-in ways back, parsed with the other WRITE_* settings; per-client D20 quirks may select a WRITE_RESEND mode. Each path that changes is listed cell by cell.
  • Re-send after delete, every path (2026-10-29). "Acknowledged, stays deleted" applies on every path, and the spec text is corrected. Every changed cell is documented, so the change can be reverted or adjusted as cohort feedback arrives.
  • Records without an identifier. Natural keys for device status and profile are a separate item, ID-NATURAL-KEY, with its own corpus check of what would merge. Food and activity have no natural key.
  • Socket edits and removes, and activity. Identifier addressing is added where it changes nothing for writes that carry no identifier: socket dbUpdate, dbUpdateUnset and dbRemove accept an identifier when there is no _id, and activity creates match on identifier. This is conditional on the extended matrix showing every existing form unchanged.
  • Re-send with changed fields. Compatibility B/C and the selected WRITE_RESEND mode above govern current behavior. The client survey retains the reason changed Loop/Trio POSTs must be handled deliberately; it does not override the adopted mode.

The rules are in the identity specification and the identifier conventions; the conversation with the Loop maintainers is in upstream-asks-loop-identifier.

docs.title: 4.3 Registration
docs.text:
slice builds needs check REG-S0 capability document and catalogue, read-only, flag off by default specs schema validation; flag off is byte-identical to dev REG-S1 submit, etag, retire; MongoDB store; single mode REG-S0 negotiation conformance cases against a booted server (25 of 32 pass, 6 mapped, 1 not applicable) REG-S2 definitions, leased instances, channels and roles; instances on one flat root, /api/v4/instances/{instanceId} REG-S1 instance conformance cases REG-S5 owner actions on a single-tenant site with API_SECRET REG-S1, REG-S2 owner-action conformance cases REG-S3 typed writes and read selection REG-S2, WC-STEP-PATCH, SPEC-ID-AMEND unregistered writers byte-identical REG-S4 projected views for older readers REG-S3 projection cases HUB-REG-CRM-SEAM registrations under tenant scope REG-S2, ST-PG, T30-WIRING per-mode cases (SPEC-REG-MODES)

S0, S1, S2 and S5 need no storage work and are one single-tenant PR, draft #8857 (f7a43fed). S5 comes before S3 because only S3 waits on the write step. #8857 lets a devicestatus-upload token register its controller; that role choice is the maintainer's, in the PR. It keeps one holder document per (scope, channel, role), so each role has one live instance. Of the 186 conformance cases, 35 pass, 88 are mapped and 0 fail (at 3be98536); the rest wait for later slices. The hub implementer's guide maps each slice to modules on dev; the controller guide is the same flow from the controller author's side.

docs.title: 4.4 Tenancy
docs.text:
The dependency map shows selected work items and their bounded component state. Its blocked markers preserve unmet acceptance prerequisites even where a useful preview already passes. The M0–M6 dashboard is authoritative for milestone gates; accepted slices are not completion percentages. The adopted M2 bar is tenant-local config/versioned writes, unknown-tenant refusal, A's token failing on B by signature, no environment/root/key leakage, and separate owner/data/operator routes. R72 accepts that bounded versioned-write and route-separation bar; wider catalogue and human-session acceptance remain M6. M4's bar is executed headless clients plus source-pattern replay for the rest, with no all-client claim; Android emulator work moves to C and iOS is outside the automated lab. M4 still depends on M3. The promotion decisions own these scope changes. Headless owner config.ownerPolicy is retained writer policy, distinct from the withdrawn authorization reader option.

The architecture and compatibility comparison contains request-flow, isolation and historical-comparison diagrams.

item builds needs PLAT-ENTRY one executable, bin/nightscout.js: single (today's server, every old start path unchanged) and the operator tools; image ENTRYPOINT, and no image HEALTHCHECK so a boot-error page is not restarted away (D21) dev PLAT-SERVE Merged multitenant CLI namespace (#8899); R72 accepts bounded M1–M4 preview contracts on draft #8898. R73 accepts functional M5, and later ed2 Compose/restore acceptance is bounded; M6 and production/default admission remain open PLAT-ENTRY, ST-READS T30-RESEARCH the tenant-owner configuration surface: 264 settings on dev, 12 contested D-T30 T30-SCHEMA-CONFIG Adopted owner-authority writer policy and transactional proposed-grant fencing are retained. Reader clamping is removed; R72 accepts M2 tenant-local config/versioned writes and route separation; wider lifecycle belongs to M6. Selected preview services do not finish this item; historical old-seam gate fails its D15 predicate T30-RESEARCH TEN-RESOLVE Direct/canonical preview resolution accepted; full production trust, durable mapping and operator lifecycle still blocked MT-CONFIG-MIN, MIG-RUNNER, PLAT-SERVE T30-WIRING Current persisted authority composes with actual CLI/REST. Adopted local new-format token verification keeps per-operation PG session/key/grants; writer proposed-grant fencing is retained; optional reader clamping is withdrawn. Management issuer/refresh, existing-grant lifecycle policy and production trust are M6 work TEN-RESOLVE, MT-SECRETS-CONTRACT TEN-LAB R72 promotes M3 after M1/M2, then M4 at the adopted headless/source-pattern scope; no all-client or M6 claim ST-PG, T30-WIRING, MIG-RUNNER

Single-tenant on MongoDB stays first-class (D1, D4). The subcommand selects tenancy (maintainer, 2026-10-27): nightscout single is single-tenant and the nightscout multitenant namespace selects multitenancy (#8899), so the API preview requires explicit multitenant configuration and TENANCY_MODE retires as an operator setting. The interface ownership proposal retains its original questions; current separate-process composition and restore boundaries are in the architecture comparison. The settings census on dev is t30-census-dev. The decisions D1–D23 are in the execution plan.

Tenancy and execution are separate axes (D-EXEC-PROFILE, 2026-10-31). The subcommand selects tenancy; whether a site keeps a resident ddata or computes its views from bounded queries is a second choice. R72 accepts request-local loader/cache frames at its bounded M1–M4 scope; R73 accepts the functional multitenant evaluator/realtime reference; M6 retains lifecycle and wider admission work. This does not establish a universal computed execution profile. The independent single/nonresident prototype retains properties between cycles; R50 now measures acquisition races, failed-cycle retention and recovery through actual triggers. R49/R50 retain the measured differences in bounds, frame/future behavior, identity unions, statistics and failure lifecycle. Cost remains unmeasured and default single remains resident. R54/R55 accept a shared private allocation helper behind those separate caller policies. R62/R64 retain the published REST side. The whole independent profile branch remains separate; a private helper/evaluateCycle hunk is reused in the multitenant candidate. R67 bounds recovered clinical constructor evidence. R73 promotes functional M5; the independent computed-single profile retains its separate entry bar. Input acquisition and clinical result persistence are not one atomic operation.

docs.title: 5. Decisions and remaining questions
docs.text: Cards labelled decided describe adopted constraints. Other cards retain their question and owner; an option marked recommended is a proposal. Select Show on the map to see affected items. The current M5/M6 decision list linked above contains later tenancy policies; this map does not create a second decision log. Release questions (the 16.0.0 quiet period, cohort requests, when dev reopens) are Q13–Q16 in the release allocation.

docs.title: 6. How the work moves
docs.text:
• Pull requests. Sized by milestone, not by slice: the single-tenant registration PR (S0, S1, S2, S5); storage slices grouped into few PRs. A track with many pieces in flight uses an integration branch with child PRs, the way #8605 carried 109 children. Dev is merged into a branch, not rebased, and a PR's merge records that the merged tree matches the reviewed tree.
  • What pins behaviour. #8854's CRUD matrix and this repository's write-contract matrix (tools/qc/write-contract-matrix.js; v1, v3, socket and in-process). A slice that changes no behaviour changes no cell; a slice that changes behaviour lists the cells it changes and why.
  • Red controls. Every new test is shown failing against the code it guards before the change, with the original symptom.
  • Conformance. The registration and identity cases in specs/sync/conformance/ run against a booted server by a harness in this repository (D12), reported case by case as passed, mapped or not applicable.
  • Agents. Agents build slices in their own worktrees, run the checks and hand back a branch, a PR body and the push commands. They never push. Maintainers push, open, review and merge.
  • Releases. #8865 (one executable, the image's start and stop, the boot split; multitenant is the current namespace after #8899; the explicitly configured separate-process Compose preview is implemented in #8898) merged into 16.0.0 on 2026-10-30. Since 2026-10-30 every single-tenant item of this plan targets 16.0.0 through the entry bar (§1); a miss merges after the tag, one theme per minor; the 16.0.0 quiet period starts when its merge list is closed, not on a date. Components shipped before they are mature are labelled alpha; the label belongs to the multitenant bindings, not to code every single-tenant site runs.
  • Records. Each landed slice updates its queue item (queue/work-queue.yaml) and this plan's data file, and the page is re-rendered.

The test workflow runs only on pull requests to dev or master, so #8886 (base feat/id-first-match) shows only auto-close until it is retargeted.
