docs.title: Hub-and-spoke sync for AID controllers: the original sketch
docs.text:
Record

Record as of 2026-09-11. A point-in-time document; it is not kept up to date.

What this is: an analysis (contributor-facing), the first sketch of the design the platform specifications now state. Read after therapy effects and versioning; leads to its successors, the controller-descriptions and replay-fidelity proposals and the specifications. Snapshot — describes 2026-09-11. Status: current as analysis; the design it sketches is carried forward by PROPOSAL-controller-descriptions and PROPOSAL-replay-fidelity-changes. Current decisions: execution plan §1. Corrected in place 2026-10-12: §3.1's description of stateSpans and the schema field list in §5.2 now match the schema as extended for D18 from intent and workflow across the landscape §9. Also 2026-10-12: §3.1 lists extensions and the D18 addendum grammar rules 1–5 (SCHEMA-REG-EXT). Also 2026-10-12: §3.5 specifies negotiation, D18 addendum rule 6 (SPEC-REG-NEGOTIATE): the capability document, the submit, update and retire contract, the fallback rule, authorisation with open questions, and the conformance cases. Also 2026-10-14: §3.5's ten open questions are decided ("Decisions"), with the contract changes they imply listed for SPEC-REG-DECISIONS; §5.2's kind/instance split is adopted as D19. Also 2026-10-15: §3.5 is amended for those decisions (SPEC-REG-DECISIONS): first-to-claim namespaces, binding to the creating subject, the owner's actions on ns-tenant-admin and the blocked state, the credential kind, carrier views and dual-write links, and refused typed writes; 53 conformance cases. Also 2026-10-15: §3.6 specifies D19 (SPEC-REG-INSTANCE): content-addressed definitions, leased instances, channel roles with provenance and one source of record, labels under dev.nightscout/ (corrected from D19's nightscout.dev/), read selection, the projected view for older readers and retention; 86 instance cases, and the 26 accepted or partial §3.5 cases gained definitionId. §3.5's file table said 53 cases after the amendment that made them 55; corrected in place. Also 2026-10-17: §1 embeds the drawings 3·hub-sync and 3·delegation. 2026-10-18: §3.5–§3.7 are maintained in the registration and identity specifications; each section here keeps its heading, a pointer and a link to its full text at b3536bbf.

Date: 2026-09-11. Fifth in a series with Typed schemas, Extending the document model, devicestatus and profile fidelity and Settings, extensibility and delegation.

The deliverable is a design to argue with, and the measurements that make it arguable.

docs.title: TL;DR
docs.text:
The ask has four parts and they turn out to be one design: controllers register a live state model, the hub derives a sync contract from it, the wire stays composite so edge devices make few requests, and storage decomposes into primitives so queries stay bounded and replay stays possible.

Five measurements that shape it:

# Finding Evidence 1 The three controllers have three different sync designs, and two have none. AAPS uses v3's lastModified watermark and history/{from} deltas. Loop and Trio are on v1 with no watermark and no delta endpoint at all §2 2 Cost is dominated by per-collection fan-out, whichever API version. Up to 5,760 requests/day for AAPS, 2,016 for Loop, 1,440 for Trio, against 576 for a two-request-per-cycle batched design §2.1 3 Replay completeness is 20% for Loop and 50% for oref0 derivatives — the share of declared dosing inputs actually recorded. Including derivable inputs: 55% and 72% §4.2 4 A real replay consumer already works around this. oref-digital-twin reads settings from screenshots with a vision model, or from AAPS's encrypted preference export, because Nightscout does not carry them. max_iob is in its REQUIRED_SETTINGS and is recorded by no controller anywhere §4.1 5 The state machine primitive already exists. Nocturne's StateSpan — category, state, start, end, source, supersession — is the shape needed to observe modes, overrides, exclusions and coordination between sources §5

The design in one sentence. A controller registers its state model once; the hub answers with a sync contract — one cursor endpoint in, one batch endpoint out, filters fixed in advance — and decomposes what arrives into primitives, so the edge device gets fewer round trips while the hub gets queryable, replayable, inspectable state.

What makes it tractable rather than a rewrite: every piece exists somewhere already. v3 has the cursor. Nocturne has the decomposer (99.99% of treatments route) and StateSpan. activity is already a type-discriminated composite collection. What is missing is the registration that ties them together, and the settings resource that nobody publishes.

docs.title: 1. What exists today, across four API generations
docs.text:
Documenting this was half the question, and the answer is less unified than the version numbers suggest.

v1 v3 v4 (Nocturne) Shape four fat collections the same collections, plus a metadata envelope typed primitives Identity _id identifier, server-assigned typed keys plus LegacyId Change tracking none srvCreated, srvModified inherited Delta read none GET /{collection}/history/{from} per-resource Watermark none GET /lastModified, all collections at once — Batch write array POST per collection array POST per collection per-resource Deletes destructive soft, isValid: false soft State over time point events only point events only StateSpan

Who uses what. AAPS is on v3 and uses it as intended. Loop (NightscoutKit/NightscoutClient.swift) and Trio (Trio/Sources/Services/Network/Nightscout/NightscoutAPI.swift) are on v1 only — seven and five endpoints respectively, no watermark, no delta. This is the single most important fact about "unifying v1/v3/v4": v3's sync machinery is already there and two of the three major controllers do not use it. A new version that nobody adopts would be the third such layer.

The corpus agrees. Every document in it was fetched from /api/v1/, and the v3 metadata envelope is absent from all 1.97 million of them — which is why the census reports identifier, srvCreated and srvModified as "v3-only metadata, not observable via the v1 endpoint", rather than as missing.

Drawn 2026-10-17, from the source revisions in the technical loops note: who writes and who reads each kind of record, with requested state kept apart from applied state, and the path a remote command takes to the controller. Both drawings are in the overview's gallery too.

docs.title: 2. What sync costs now
docs.text:
make schema-sync-cost counts the distinct endpoints each client's sync path can call, from its own source, and prices them at the five-minute cadence the corpus shows.

Client API Endpoints Watermark Delta endpoint AndroidAPS v3 20 yes yes Loop / NightscoutKit v1 7 no no Trio v1 5 no no

docs.title: 2.1 Against a batched design
docs.text:
Client Upper bound/day Batched (2/cycle) Factor AndroidAPS 5,760 576 10.0× Loop 2,016 576 3.5× Trio 1,440 576 2.5×

This is a source-derived upper bound on distinct endpoint calls per cycle, not a packet capture: a cycle with nothing to upload makes fewer calls, a catch-up after an outage makes more. It is a fair basis for comparing sync designs, which is what it is for, and it should not be quoted as a measured traffic figure.

The shape of the result matters more than the magnitude: AAPS, the client using v3 correctly, has the worst fan-out, because v3 gives it a delta per collection and it syncs more collections. Cursor-based sync solved the "what changed" problem and left the "how many round trips" problem untouched.

docs.title: 3.1 Registration
docs.text:
A controller declares its live state model once, against specs/sync/controller-state-model.schema.json:

  • documents — the composite wire documents it writes, each with a structural discriminator (a devicestatus carrying a loop object rather than an openaps one) and the primitive types it decomposes to
  • stateSpans — the intent kinds it exposes, one entry per kind: the slot it occupies and which slots coexist, its states and end reasons, the wire carrier today's documents use (eventType, identity, duration unit, indefinite sentinel, how "ended" is encoded), where the request and the applied effect are each recorded, the initiator vocabulary, the definitions it is made from, and which hub-originated intent the controller accepts. Each entry carries evidence marked read (from source) or measured. What each member means is maintained in the state and intent specification. The 2026-09-11 form was categories with states and a supersession rule; that form still validates. (Corrected 2026-10-12.)
  • composition — how overlapping intents combine, declared as reported by the controller (reportedBy: controller, hubComputes: false), with where the result is published or null. Under D18 the hub records the result and does not compute it. (Added 2026-10-12.)
  • commands — how remote commands reach the controller: transport, whether the hub is in the path, authorisation, expiry and acknowledgement. (Added 2026-10-12.)
  • replayInputs — every dosing input it could supply, with status and a path; an input it has but does not publish is declared with a null path, which is what makes completeness measurable rather than guessed. An input may also carry a type (below). (Typing added 2026-10-12.)
  • settings — the configuration snapshot it will publish, effective-dated. fields takes a name, as before, or a typed field declaration (below). (Typing added 2026-10-12.)
  • extensions — controller-specific data, keyed by a reverse-DNS namespace the controller owns, each with its own version and typed fields. An extension or field without a type declaration is rejected. (Added 2026-10-12.)
  • cadence and queryProfile

Grammar rules (added 2026-10-12, SCHEMA-REG-EXT; D18 addendum, execution plan §2.6.1; maintained in the registration specification §3). Within nightscout.dev/sync/v1 a reader ignores members it does not know: it keeps them as written and does not interpret or serve them, so no object in the schema is closed (tools/nsschema/sync_model.py unknown_grammar_fields lists them). A field declaration carries type — a restricted JSON Schema fragment (type, enum, minimum, maximum, format, items, properties, required; closed; an object must list its properties) — or typeRef to a Nightscout-published definition such as a ControllerSettings field, plus unit, range, horizon, sensitivity (the two-axis label of specs/sync/sensitivity.yaml) and evidence. A field with no label falls under sensitivity.unlabelledPolicy, withhold when absent. endedEncoding, command transport, replayInputs[].status and the discriminator test take a shared value or {value: other, controllerTerm}, and endReasons gains other. Each stateSpans kind and each extension may declare version or versions (served, one stored, optional lossless mappings); without a mapping nothing is converted. Documents, kinds, fields, settings and extensions may declare a horizon (cycle, span, effective-dated, definition, aggregate) with its own cadence and retention, and availability gains experimental. The generated registrations gained typeRef only where the ControllerSettings definition was read from the controller's own algorithm family, and horizons only for the devicestatus document (cycle) and settings (effective-dated); specs/sync/registrations/fixtures/example-testcontroller.yaml is a synthetic registration that uses every rule.

Worked registrations for Loop, Trio and AndroidAPS are in specs/sync/registrations/, generated from the census, the vendor surfaces and the dosing-input map rather than hand-written, so they cannot claim more than was measured. make schema-sync-model regenerates them and --check fails on drift.

The discriminator is structural on purpose. The free-text device string is the field this work spent the most effort de-identifying, and it is not reliable: one site's device strings read like a controller while its treatments showed no automated dosing at all.

Read the registration as an affordance, not a constraint. §3.2 says a controller never negotiates a query shape at request time; that is about timing, not about who decides. What a controller may sync, how often, and which filters it uses are declared by the controller in its own registration — cadence and queryProfile are per-controller fields, not hub policy. A controller with an idiomatic channel says so there. The hub's job is to honour a declaration it can bound, not to impose a uniform shape.

The catalogue is the default, and it is served. The hub ships registrations for controllers that have not declared one (specs/sync/registrations/) and serves them at a well-known path, so the common case needs no controller action at all — see the controller-descriptions proposal §2.1. Precedence is controller-published, then operator-declared, then structurally inferred.

What the registration describes is a controller kind, not a running instance. That distinction is the subject of §5.2 and is where this design is least complete.

docs.title: 3.2 The contract the hub returns
docs.text:
The sync read, write and cursor rules are maintained in the sync-transport specification §4; the measured cost in its §3.

Everything the hub offers is derived from the registration, so a controller never negotiates a query shape at request time:

GET  /api/v4/sync?cursor=<opaque>     → one envelope, every registered
                                        collection, changes since cursor,
                                        plus the next cursor
POST /api/v4/sync                     → one batch, composite documents,
                                        mixed collections, idempotent on
                                        (dataSource, syncIdentifier)

Two requests per cycle, whatever the controller syncs. The cursor is a server watermark and opaque, so the hub can change its implementation — a srvModified scan today, a logical replication slot later — without a client release.

Why this is not just v3 with fewer paths. The envelope is derived from a registration, so the hub knows which collections this controller cares about, what page size suits its cadence, and which filters it may use. v3's lastModified tells a client what changed everywhere and leaves it to fan out; a registered contract lets the hub answer the whole question once.

And it does not need a registration to start. A collection-agnostic GET /api/v3/history/{lastModified} plus a single batch write gets the same two-requests-per-cycle result on v3 today, with no registration, no new version, and no controller-side model — lastModified.js already loops every collection with a per-collection permission check and history/operation.js is already generic in opCtx.col. That is the cheapest first step and it is specified in the replay-fidelity proposal §1, including the merged-cursor rule that makes it correct under per-collection page limits.

docs.title: 3.3 Composite on the wire, primitive in storage
docs.text:
Maintained in the records specification R1–R3.

The edge device sends what it has, in the shape it has it. The hub decomposes on write:

  • a treatment carrying insulin and carbs becomes a Bolus and a CarbIntake sharing a correlation id
  • a devicestatus becomes an ApsSnapshot, a PumpSnapshot and an UploaderSnapshot
  • a profile becomes TherapySettings plus four schedules

This is measured, not hypothetical: replaying Nocturne's routing over the corpus places 99.86% of treatments by eventType alone, 0.13% by the data present, and leaves 22 documents unroutable — all of them one event type, for a spelling bug rather than a design limit.

Keep the composite too. Round-tripping to a legacy client, and answering "what did the device actually send", both need it, and the extensibility evaluation found exactly five leaf field names with no typed home — a small, known residue rather than an open-ended one.

docs.title: 3.4 Bounded queries are part of the contract, not a later hardening
docs.text: The registration's queryProfile fixes the filterable fields, the operators and the page size in advance. This is not tidiness: §6.5 of the multitenancy discussion found the re/$regex operator reaching MongoDB with no pattern guard, no index requirement and no maxTimeMS anywhere in the query path. A sync API that accepts arbitrary filters inherits that. One that answers only the shapes a registration declared does not.

docs.title: 3.5 Negotiation
docs.text: The capability document, the product resource, per-element results, the controller's fallback, and the binding, credential kind and owner's actions are maintained in the registration specification §4–§6 and the authority specification §3–§5, with 54 conformance cases. The text of this section as specified through 2026-10-17, with its decisions and case table, is at b3536bbf.

docs.title: 3.6 Definitions and instances
docs.text: Content-addressed definitions, leased instances, channels, roles and provenance, labels, typed writes, read selection, projected views and retention are maintained in the registration specification §7–§14, with 103 conformance cases; the definition and instance ids are in the identity specification §2. The text as of 2026-10-17 is at b3536bbf.

docs.title: 3.7 Version-scoped quirks and the two ids
docs.text: Rules 1–4 (versions a quirk affects, catalogue mappings and sameAs, recorded mappings, the lifecycle) and the shared slot list are maintained in the registration specification §9 and §16; rules 5–8 and the receipt-time rule in the identity specification §1. 29 conformance cases. The text as of 2026-10-17 is at b3536bbf.

docs.title: 4. Replay, and why physicians cannot see the settings
4.1 The workaround that proves the gap
docs.text:
externals/oref-digital-twin is an advisory tool that replays the real determine-basal under altered settings. To do that it needs the settings. It cannot get them from Nightscout, so it gets them from a screenshot, via a vision model, or from AAPS's client-side-decrypted preference export. Its own settings module says so plainly, and its replay code names the one input it cannot proceed without:

REQUIRED_SETTINGS = ("max_iob",)

max_iob is the input measured as recorded by no controller anywhere. A serious replay tool, written independently, hits the gap this series measured. That is the physician complaint in code form.

One correction to an earlier reading of this file. Its module docstring also lists currenttemp and insulin activity as unrecoverable from devicestatus and approximates both. Neither claim survives measurement: activity is already read by its own _iob_data_from_cycle when openaps.iob.activity is present, and currenttemp is published — openaps.iob.lastTemp carries rate, duration and started_at on 73,891 documents, the dosing map classifies it as recorded, and OBS-OREF-006 checks for it. The tool still substitutes a zero temp basal. That is a consumer fix, not a Nightscout gap, and it is the cheapest fidelity gain identified anywhere in this series — see the replay-fidelity proposal §6.

docs.title: 4.2 Completeness as a published number
docs.text:
Because a registration declares every dosing input with a status, the hub can report completeness per controller, per cycle:

Declared inputs Recorded Recorded or derivable Loop 20 20% 55% Trio / AndroidAPS (oref0) 40 50% 72%

A "derivable" input is recomputed from stored history, which gives a value and not necessarily the value the controller used — it saw a different window, with different de-duplication and different noise handling. A replay built on derived inputs tests the replayer as much as the algorithm, so the two columns should never be collapsed.

docs.title: 4.3 Settings as a first-class, effective-dated resource
docs.text:
Maintained in the records specification R5–R8 and §5.

The missing piece is small and additive. A ControllerSettings snapshot, versioned and effective-dated, published on change rather than per cycle:

  • effective-dated, because a setting that changed mid-history invalidates a replay that assumed one value
  • versioned with the build, because algorithm behaviour changes between releases — which is why OBS-LOOP-006 and OBS-OREF-007 ask for the version at all
  • declared in the registration, so "this controller publishes nine settings and withholds none" is checkable

The generated registrations already list what each controller would have to add: nine fields for Loop, four for the oref0 family.

docs.title: 5.1 Spans, not point events
docs.text:
Point events cannot answer "was the pump suspended when this dose was skipped". Nocturne's StateSpan can: Category, State, StartTimestamp, EndTimestamp, Source, Metadata, and — the part that matters for coordination — SupersededById, CanonicalId and Sources.

Categories already modelled there cover the AID state machine: PumpMode (automatic, limited, manual), PumpConnectivity, Override, TemporaryTarget, ProfileState, DataExclusion, Activity.

Two properties worth keeping in any adoption:

  • Supersession, not last-write-wins. When a human and a controller both set an override, or two controllers overlap, the resolution has to be recorded rather than implied. The controller resolves them and declares how (supersedes, state and intent S3); the hub records the result.
  • DataExclusion as a first-class span. A sensor warm-up or a known-bad stretch is not missing data, it is data known to be unusable, and a replay that cannot tell the difference will silently score itself against noise.

specs/openapi/statespan-v3-extension.md in this repo documents a hypothetical v3 backport and records that Nocturne's author prefers StateSpan stay v4-only. That preference is worth respecting: the span model is the clearest thing to put behind a registered contract rather than to retrofit into the collection API.

docs.title: 5.2 Liveness and channel ownership — open here, already drafted upstream
docs.text:
(2026-10-14: answered by D19 — execution plan §2.6.2 — which adopts the RFC's kind/instance split with the reconciliation's identity correction and settles two writers on one site; what follows is the map as written on 2026-09-11.) (2026-10-15: specified in §3.6 (SPEC-REG-INSTANCE): the instance carries an opaque controller-supplied id and no hardware identifiers, devicestatus.device is a withheld observed alias, liveness is a lease, and channel ownership is one device-provenance holder per (channel, role).)

This section is an open question, not a design. It is written as a reconciliation target because the honest finding is that cgm-remote-monitor has drafted most of it already, and this series had not noticed.

The control-plane supersession map names the specification rule proposed to supersede each object of the earlier draft below.

The question is real and this design does not answer it. A registration says what a controller kind writes. It does not say which controller is running right now, which one owns a given channel, or what to do when two of them write. §7 records "cursor semantics under concurrent writers" as unmeasured, and that is the whole of what this series has to say on the subject.

cgm-remote-monitor/docs/proposals/ (added 2026-01-01) already carries the missing half, and it carves the problem at a joint this series did not:

Their concept What it is Our nearest thing Verdict ControllerKindDefinition Per product: supported features, pumps, CGMs, eventCapabilities.minimalEventSet ControllerStateModel (specs/sync/) Complementary, not competing. Theirs says what a controller can do; ours says what it writes. Neither contains the other's half ControllerInstanceRegistration Per running instance: instanceId, pumpBinding.connectedSince, cgmBinding, registeredAt, lastSeenAt nothing This is liveness, and we have no equivalent CapabilitySnapshot Liveness over time: pumpConnected, closedLoopEnabled, suspended, lastLoopTime, reservoir, battery StateSpan categories PumpConnectivity, PumpMode Same phenomenon, different container — theirs a point snapshot, ours a span. Reconcilable; a span is the stronger form for replay bridge-rules.md detection if (devicestatus.loop) … if (devicestatus.openaps) … our structural discriminator Independently identical. Two efforts reached the same answer, which is the strongest evidence in this document that it is the right one Authority hierarchy, composition, delegation grants conflict-resolution.md docs/10-domain/authority-model.md Composition is the controller's (state and intent S1); delegation's requirements are authority §7; authority-model.md keeps the credential rationale and a worked grant Global monotonic event cursor assignEventCursor, /events?cursor= §3.2's opaque server watermark Same role, different implementation. Whether they are one cursor is an open design question

The kind/instance split is the answer to the liveness question, and it is theirs, not ours. A catalogue entry describes the kind; liveness belongs to the instance. Adopting that split costs this series one new field group in specs/sync/controller-state-model.schema.json — which today has cadence, documents, stateSpans, composition, commands, replayInputs, settings, queryProfile, sensitivity, extensions and nothing about instances at all. (composition and commands added 2026-10-12; extensions added 2026-10-12 by SCHEMA-REG-EXT, see §3.1.)

Two corrections we can offer back, because we measured them. Both are small and both are the kind of thing only a corpus can catch:

  1. bridge-rules.md detects Trio with if (devicestatus.trio) return 'trio'. No document in the corpus carries a top-level trio key. The observed top-level devicestatus objects are loop, openaps, pump, uploader and override. Trio is an oref derivative and writes under openaps — which our own generated specs/sync/registrations/trio.yaml and androidaps.yaml both confirm, since both discriminate on openaps and are therefore not distinguishable from each other at the top level. That is a limit in our work as much as a bug in theirs, and it should be stated in both.
  2. CapabilitySnapshot sets controllerInstanceId: devicestatus.device — the free-text device string. That is the field this series found least reliable (§3.1), and using it as an instance identity makes liveness inherit the unreliability. If instances need identity, it should not come from that string.

What should happen before anyone builds this. Ask, rather than design: the integration-questionnaire.md in that same directory is addressed to Loop, AAPS and Trio implementers and asks a version of this question already. Writing a competing liveness model before answering it would be the exact duplication this work exists to prevent.

docs.title: 6. Sequencing
docs.text:
Ordered so nothing depends on an unmade decision, and each step is useful alone.

  1. Publish settings. Additive, no migration, no new API. Closes the physician complaint and the digital-twin workaround. The registrations name the fields, and for Loop it is eight more keys in the loopSettings block it already writes on 200 of 202 profile documents — see the replay-fidelity proposal §3.
  2. Registration and the derived contract, read-only first. A controller registers; the hub offers the cursor envelope. No write path yet, so nothing can be corrupted by an early adopter.
  3. Batch write. Idempotent on (dataSource, syncIdentifier), which Nocturne's V4 already uses as its update key.
  4. Decomposition behind the contract. Already measured at 99.99% for treatments; devicestatus and profile decomposition are unmeasured and should be before they are relied on.
  5. StateSpan behind the contract, for the categories a registration declares.
  6. Retire nothing. v1 stays. Every argument in this series for aliasing over renaming applies at the API layer too.

docs.title: 7. What is not measured
docs.text:
• Whether two requests per cycle is achievable in practice. §2.1 is an upper bound on endpoint calls, not a measurement of traffic, and payload size may trade against request count.
  • devicestatus and profile decomposition coverage. Only treatments were replayed. devicestatus is where the vendor subtrees live, so it is the one most likely to behave differently.
  • Round-tripping. Whether a decomposed set recomposes into a document a legacy client accepts is the question that decides whether decomposition can happen behind the existing API at all.
  • Cursor semantics under concurrent writers. Two controllers plus a care-portal user writing to one site is the normal case, and srvModified ordering under that load is unexamined. conflict-resolution.md upstream proposes optimistic locking on srvModified plus a global monotonic cursor; neither is measured here, and whether that cursor and §3.2's watermark are the same object is undecided (§5.2).
  • Liveness and channel ownership entirely. No measurement, no design — see §5.2. Nothing in the corpus can say which controller was running when, because nothing records it. The upstream ControllerInstanceRegistration is the nearest thing to an answer, and its instance identity is taken from the device string, which §3.1 found unreliable — see the reconciliation §3.3.
  • Anything about AndroidAPS from data. Still no AAPS closed-loop site in the corpus.
  • The registration's own lifecycle. How a controller updates a registration when it ships a new build, and what the hub does with in-flight data under the old one. (2026-10-12: specified in §3.5 — update by If-Match, retire keeps stored data and the frozen declaration. Not measured: no hub implements it.)

docs.title: Intent, workflow and entity management across the AID controller landscape
docs.text:
Record

Record as of 2026-10-09. A point-in-time document; it is not kept up to date.

What this is: an analysis (contributor-facing). Read after the platform index and glossary (§2 and §9 first); leads to the identity specification. Snapshot — describes 2026-10-09. Status: current; the evidence for D18. Every claim is read-derived (from source, a hypothesis about behaviour) unless marked measured. Sources and commits are in §1. Current decisions: execution plan §1. Corrected in place 2026-10-12: §5 is measured on both hubs (TL;DR and §12 follow it); the §10 rows for the hub-sync design and specs/sync/registrations/ record what the registrations now declare and what remains; the registrations row also records the D18 addendum grammar (SCHEMA-REG-EXT, 2026-10-12). Also 2026-10-18: §2 records the maintainer's decision on agent initiators (P5); the AndroidAPS items marked 4.0.0 prerelease ship in 4.0.0-beta1 and 4.0.0-rc1 (§1); §4 and §5 carry figures generated from the registrations and the lab results (tools/diagrams), and §4 an animation (tools/animations) of the instances changing as records arrive. §6.1 draws the remote-command paths of §6 as sequences (channels and acknowledgements only). The rules this evidence supports are maintained in the state and intent specification.

The question. Nightscout's API v1 and v3 manage entities: create, read, update and delete documents in treatments, devicestatus, profile. AID controllers increasingly manage intent: a named preset is activated, several intents run at once and combine, the controller applies something that may differ from what was asked, and the intent ends for a reason. This document finds, per controller and per hub, where the two differ, so that a controller registration can describe the difference.

The direction this serves (maintainer, 2026-10-09). Registration has two tiers: well-known declarations shipped with the hub, for backwards compatibility, and controller-owned typed registrations, for extensibility. Adoption follows the WHATWG pattern — specify what happens now, leave room to extend. The hub (Nightscout, Nocturne) is responsible for observability; the controller is responsible for sending data accurately and for syncing and reconciling. Recorded as D18 in the execution plan (§2.6.1).

docs.title: TL;DR
docs.text: Finding Single records Entity CRUD works. Every controller keeps one document per instance and amends or deletes it. Each encodes identity and "ended" differently (§4) Six things CRUD cannot carry definition identity, concurrent intent slots with a composition rule, requested vs applied, end reason, initiator, and the command → acknowledgement → outcome link (§2) Every controller already built them each in its own place: AAPS on the NS settings collection (4.0.0 prereleases), Loop and Trio over APNs replies and failure Notes, iAPS over NS Announcement treatments. None of it is typed, and most of it is invisible to the hub (§3, §6) The hubs disagree on "what is active now" Measured on both hubs: cgm-remote-monitor and Nocturne differ on temp-target cancel, devicestatus override duration units, profile fallback after a timed switch, AAPS timeshift units, and out-of-order override backfill; they agree on Temporary Override Cancel (§5) Composition is controller-specific Loop: pre-meal target wins, override factor applies. Trio/iAPS: temp target wins the target, override factors apply. AAPS: temp target replaces targets, profile-switch percentage has already scaled basal/ISF/CR. No hub composes, and under the stated roles none should (§7) Cowpaths already exist Loop and Trio publish preset definitions in the profile document; Nightscout's careportal builds its remote-override picker from Loop's. AAPS dev publishes scene and automation definitions plus active-scene state. These are registrations in all but name (§8)

The corpus holds no AAPS closed-loop site and no Trio profile document, so every AAPS statement and every Trio preset-join statement is read-derived.

docs.title: 2. Where intent differs from entity management
docs.text:
Six properties. A controller's intent model has each of them; an entity collection has none.

# Property What it means Why CRUD loses it P1 Definition identity an activation refers to a preset by a stable id presets are copied into the instance, or referenced by name only P2 Concurrent slots and composition several intents active at once, combined by a controller rule one collection, one "latest wins" reading per eventType P3 Requested vs applied what was asked, what the device or algorithm accepted, what it computed one document is both request and effect, or the effect is elsewhere and unlinked P4 End reason expired, cancelled, superseded, deleted before start, ended by a trigger (carbs, glucose, loop off) "ended" is encoded as a shortened duration, a delete, or a zero-duration record P5 Initiator phone, watch, shortcut, automation, caregiver, remote recorded locally or in debug logs; on the wire only free-text enteredBy P6 Command lifecycle request → validate → apply → acknowledge, with a correlation id no request record; success visible only as the resulting entity; failure as free text

P5, decided 2026-10-18 (maintainer): no agent value is added to any initiator vocabulary; an agent initiator is written in the open-vocabulary form {value: other, controllerTerm}, as the registration specification (§9) does for an agent's roles. No controller records an agent as initiator today. The registrations are built for needs that are latent but measured and demonstrated — in the corpus, in controller source and in the labs — not only for what apps send now; the open form lets a controller, simulator or lab record an agent initiator today, and a shared value can be named once the corpus or a lab shows one in use. (execution plan, row 17; agents in the ecosystem §4.2).

docs.title: 3.1 Loop
docs.text:
• Override wire shape. eventType: "Temporary Override", reason = preset symbol and name, duration (minutes) or durationType: "indefinite", correctionRange (mg/dL), insulinNeedsScaleFactor, remoteAddress, _id = the instance UUID. No syncIdentifier field is sent. Whether the UUID _id survives depends on the server's UUID_HANDLING setting; without it the upsert falls back to created_at + eventType.
  • Pre-meal is not on the wire. Not a treatment, not in the profile; devicestatus override.active is false when only pre-meal is on. Its target replaces the override's while it lasts; the override's scale factor still applies.
  • Scale factor. basal × f, ISF × 1/f, CR × 1/f. Target replaces the scheduled target.
  • Pump suspend uploads as Temp Basal rate 0, reason: "suspend"; resume is not uploaded.
  • Measured (distinct documents, make schema-effects). 2,428 Temporary Override treatments, all with effect and motivation. Of 55,938 active devicestatus overrides: 42,799 effect + motivation, 2,176 effect only (custom overrides have no name), 10,892 motivation only.

docs.title: 3.2 Trio and iAPS
docs.text:
• Override wire shape. eventType: "Exercise" for every override regardless of purpose; notes = the preset name (or "Custom Override"); duration with indefinite sentinel 43200 (Trio) or 2880 (iAPS). Percentage, target, ISF/CR scope and SMB settings are not sent. The struct's id is excluded from its coding keys. The wire identity is created_at + eventType.
  • Measured. One site carries all Trio Exercise documents: 399 distinct _id, 389 distinct created_at, 81 with duration: 43200. Applied ISF, CR, target and sensitivityRatio are present on all 73,898 of that site's openaps devicestatus documents.
  • Recovering the effect needs a time join to devicestatus (post-composition, unattributed) or, for presets only, a name join to profile.overridePresets. The second is untestable in this corpus.
  • Temp targets. Trio sends notes = name; iAPS drops it. Trio ends a TT by re-posting the same created_at with the actual duration; iAPS writes a zero-duration TT one second before the next start. Trio's halfBasalTarget is not uploaded.
  • Composition (Swift and JS agree). The override target applies only when no temp target is set; the override percentage and ISF/CR scaling still apply alongside a temp target.
  • Trio also downloads Temporary Target treatments entered by other clients and enables the newest one directly, with no acknowledgement record — an entity used as a command.
  • dosingMode {closed, open, lowGlucoseSuspend, basalTesting} is in devicestatus.openaps.dosingMode (Trio); the change itself is not a treatment. Pump suspend/resume are Note treatments with notes: PumpSuspend | PumpResume.

docs.title: 3.3 AndroidAPS
docs.text:
• ProfileSwitch → EffectiveProfileSwitch is the ecosystem's clearest request/effect pair. A PS is written by a user, SMS, automation, scene or NS sync; the profile is pushed to the pump; only if the pump accepts is an EPS written. A failed or pending change is visible on the wire only as a PS with no following EPS. The EPS is uploaded as eventType: "Note", recognised by originalProfileName; its profileJson is scaled, the PS's is the base profile. 4.0.0 prerelease: EPS.originalPsId links the two locally and is not sent.
  • percentage scales overall insulin needs. ProfileSealed.convertToNonCustomizedProfile: basal × p/100, ISF × 100/p, IC × 100/p; targets only time-shifted (pinned by ProfileSealedTest.kt:136-141; same maths at the 3.4.2.6 tag). With Dynamic ISF the percentage enters the TDD-based ISF formula instead.
  • RunningMode has a requested layer and a constraint-forced layer (autoForced: true, reasons), both uploaded as OpenAPS Offline; open-ended DISABLED_LOOP is sent with a 10-year duration and originalDuration: 0. 4.0.0 prerelease: RunningModeReconciler drives the pump from the mode record and re-checks drift at startup.
  • Temp targets have a closed reason vocabulary (Custom, Hypo, Activity, Eating Soon, Automation, Wear); a new TT ends the running one; inbound merges are shorten-only.
  • Accepting remote intent is opt-in per type. The pump-owning phone applies NS-originated PS, TT and RunningMode records only if NsClientAcceptProfileSwitch, …TempTarget, …RunningMode are on; all default off.
  • Client control and scenes (4.0.0 prerelease). Commands and acknowledgements travel as documents in the NS v3 settings collection under fixed identifiers; scene and automation definitions are published under aaps, active-scene state (with the NS identifiers of the records the scene created) under aaps-state. Scene revert shortens only records the scene still owns.

docs.title: 4. Identity and end encoding, side by side
docs.text:
Instance key on the wire "Ended" is Cancel before start Loop override _id = UUID (server-dependent) amended duration DELETE Trio override created_at + eventType delete + re-post, new _id delete iAPS override created_at ± 5 min + enteredBy delete + re-post delete Trio TT created_at + eventType (server upsert) re-post, same created_at — iAPS TT — zero-duration TT at next start − 1 s zero-duration TT AAPS PS / TT / RunningMode identifier (v3) shortened duration, same identifier v3 soft delete Careportal / nightguard TT — zero-duration TT zero-duration TT

The registrations' stateSpans declarations, drawn: for each intent kind, the records the controller writes to end an instance early or cancel it before its start, and the instance a hub derives from them under state and intent §6.1. The iAPS and careportal rows have no registration and no figure.

Read-derived, specs/sync/registrations/loop.yaml (Loop c2fddb76, LoopKit 325bd820, NightscoutKit 4ec9fd1, NightscoutService fe075ef). Generated by make diagrams-svg.

Read-derived, specs/sync/registrations/trio.yaml (Trio e41c9db37). Generated by make diagrams-svg.

Read-derived, specs/sync/registrations/androidaps.yaml (AndroidAPS 7e1d537d49). Generated by make diagrams-svg.

How a hub's instances change as records arrive, for four of those encodings (an end by a zero-duration record, a delete received before the start, a backfilled earlier override, a timed running mode over an open-ended one): records land in the order the hub received them, the instances update after each, and a cursor visits each query time.

Rules A5–A8 of state and intent §6.1, one synthetic conformance case each: a zero-duration record ends the target active at its time (cancelled); a delete received at 10:30 removes an 11:00 override before it starts (deletedBeforeStart, never active); an override backfilled at 10:00 after one at 11:00 is ended at 11:00 (superseded), whatever the arrival order; a 30-minute running mode applies over an open-ended one, which is active again when it ends. Instances after each record are the reference decision function's (tools/nsschema/active_state.py); after the last record they equal each case's expected block, drawn statically in A5, A6, A7 and A8. Synthetic; proposed rules. Rendered by make animations.

docs.title: 5. How the hubs decide what is active
docs.text:
cgm-remote-monitor recomputes active state on every load; Nocturne materialises StateSpans on write and supersedes open spans within exclusive categories.

Status 2026-10-12: every row below is measured on both hubs by the lab tools/lab/hub-active-state (cgm-remote-monitor fade2299, Nocturne 42275c812 on SQLite, one synthetic record set, a control per case where the hubs agree). Against the 2026-10-09 text, whose Nocturne cells were read-derived: the "Agree?" cells of the cancel rows change, the same-millisecond Nocturne cell is corrected, the backfill row is new, and the other cells are confirmed. The careportal storage claim in the override-cancel row is still read-derived. "Agree?" means the two hubs report the same active state at the lab's query times; for Nocturne, "latest span" is GetActiveAtAsync(category, state: null, t) and "list" is GetStateSpansAsync over t, which hides records deduplication marked non-primary.

Intent cgm-remote-monitor Nocturne Agree? Temp target + later cancel cancel truncates the earlier target (measured: 60-min target + cancel at 20 → one 20-min window) cancel becomes a separate span with state Cancelled and no end; the timed target keeps its 60 min (measured) latest span: yes (it is the Cancelled one); Active-state and list reads: no until the target's own end, and the open Cancelled span stays in list reads afterwards Temporary Override Cancel not stored by careportal (APNs request only, read-derived); a stored one has no duration and is ignored (measured) not classified; produces no record (measured) yes: in both, the override runs its full duration Loop devicestatus override latest devicestatus override; timestamp + duration read as seconds (measured) one span per devicestatus, starting at devicestatus time, duration read as minutes; spans are not superseded, and active: false closes nothing (measured) no (30-min override: active at +40 and +120 in Nocturne only) Timed profile switch after a permanent one falls back to the permanent profile when the timed one expires (measured) closes the permanent span at the timed start; no span after expiry, so basal resolves against profile Default (measured) no AAPS timeshift milliseconds (AAPS 3.x wire unit); schedule read at t − shift (measured) hours, modulo 24: a millisecond value becomes 0; an hours value is applied as t + shift (measured) no for any non-zero shift Same-millisecond temp targets keeps the first, drops the second (measured) both stored; deduplication marks the second arrival non-primary, so list reads show the first; GetActiveAtAsync sees both (measured) list: yes; latest span: no once the first-arrived target ends before the second Out-of-order backfill of two open overrides no truncation of Temporary Override treatments in either order (measured) supersession closes only spans starting at or before the new one, so the backfilled earlier span stays open: two open spans (measured) list: yes out of order, no in time order (Nocturne supersedes); latest span: no

The same lab results, drawn per case: the records as written, the windows cgm-remote-monitor reported and the spans Nocturne stored, and each hub's reading at each query time.

Measured, tools/lab/hub-active-state, run 2026-10-12: cgm-remote-monitor fade2299 (15.0.9), Nocturne 42275c812. Generated by make diagrams-svg.

Two hub writes do not reach any controller: Nocturne POST /api/v4/state-spans writes Override, TemporaryTarget or Profile spans directly, and careportal or nightguard temp targets are honoured only by controllers that download them (Trio; AAPS behind an opt-in).

docs.title: 6. The remote-command lifecycle
docs.text:
Path Request recorded at hub Acceptance visible Success visible Failure visible Careportal or Nocturne → Loop (hub → APNs) no no as the resulting entity Note with free text LoopFollow → Loop (direct APNs) no no reply to sender only Note LoopFollow → Trio (direct APNs) no no reply to sender only Note LoopCaregiver "Remote Commands 2" (status Pending → InProgress → Success/Error) expects a hub collection; neither hub has one — — — Any client → iAPS (Announcement treatment) the request is the treatment no no no Careportal / nightguard TT → Trio, AAPS the request is the treatment no indistinguishable from enacted no AAPSClient → AAPS (4.0.0 prerelease, NS settings) yes, signed Executing ack Done/Ok ack Done/Failed, Expired, Delivery/Failed

Neither hub forwards a reply channel in the APNs payload it builds, so hub-routed commands cannot receive a reply; that channel exists only on direct APNs. The RFC's DeliveryRequest.requestType covers tempBasal, bolus, suspend and resume; the commands caregivers actually send — override, temp target, carbs, loop mode — have no request object, and OverrideInstance.status has no requested or rejected state.

docs.title: 6.1 The paths as sequences
docs.text:
Added 2026-10-18. One sequence per path in the table above. Solid arrows are requests and records; dashed arrows are replies and reads. Each drawing shows channels and acknowledgements only. Every drawing is read-derived; captions give the rows they are drawn from, at this repository's commit b081a15c.

Hub-relayed, to Loop. The sender gets no reply; the hub learns the outcome only as the record Loop uploads or a free-text Note.

sequenceDiagram
  accTitle: Hub-relayed command to Loop
  accDescr: A careportal, Nocturne or LoopCaregiver sender asks the hub, which pushes through APNs to Loop without a return address. Loop validates, then uploads the resulting record or a free-text Note. The sender reads records to infer the outcome; no acknowledgement is correlated with the command.
  participant S as Sender: careportal, Nocturne or LoopCaregiver
  participant H as Hub
  participant P as APNs
  participant L as Loop
  S->>H: command
  Note over H: no request record is kept
  H->>P: push, no return address
  P->>L: notification
  Note over L: duplicate check, expiry when present,<br/>one-time code for bolus and carbs only, limits
  alt enacted
    L->>H: resulting treatment or devicestatus, uploaded after enactment
  else refused or failed
    L->>H: Note treatment, free text
  end
  S-->>H: reads records to infer the outcome
  Note over S,L: no acknowledgement correlated with the command

Source: landscape §6 row 1 (docs/30-design/platform/nightscout-intent-workflow-landscape-2026-10-09.md:201) and technical control loops §3.3 path A (docs/60-research/structures-2026-10-17/technical-loops.md:234), at b081a15c. Read-derived.

Direct, from LoopFollow to Loop or Trio. The reply goes to the sender over APNs and carries no command id; the hub sees a Note on failure.

sequenceDiagram
  accTitle: Direct APNs command from LoopFollow to Loop or Trio
  accDescr: LoopFollow reads the controller's push token from the hub profile and pushes through APNs itself. Loop replies to LoopFollow when given return information, without a command id, and uploads the result or a Note. Trio decrypts a payload sealed under a shared secret, replies before enactment and again once the pump accepts, and writes a Note only on error.
  participant F as LoopFollow
  participant H as Hub
  participant P as APNs
  participant C as Loop or Trio
  H-->>F: push token, read from the profile
  alt to Loop
    F->>P: push with return information
    P->>C: notification
    Note over C: checks as on the hub-relayed path
    C-->>F: reply over APNs, no command id
    C->>H: resulting record, or Note on failure
  else to Trio
    F->>P: push, payload encrypted under a shared secret
    P->>C: notification
    Note over C: decrypts, timestamp window ±600 s,<br/>bolus limits, no one-time code
    C-->>F: reply over APNs: initiating, before enactment
    C-->>F: reply over APNs: started, once the pump accepts
    C->>H: Note, on error only
  end

Source: landscape §6 rows 2–3 (…landscape-2026-10-09.md:202-203) and technical control loops §3.3 paths B and C (…technical-loops.md:235-236), at b081a15c. Read-derived.

Treatments downloaded by the controller. The request is the record; nothing distinguishes enacted from ignored.

sequenceDiagram
  accTitle: Treatment written to the hub and downloaded by Trio, iAPS or AndroidAPS
  accDescr: Any client with hub write access stores a treatment, such as a temp target or, for iAPS, an Announcement. The controller downloads it and applies it only if its download setting allows. No acknowledgement exists; enacted and ignored look the same on the hub.
  participant W as Hub writer: careportal, nightguard, any client
  participant H as Hub
  participant C as Trio, iAPS or AndroidAPS
  W->>H: treatment: temp target, or Announcement for iAPS
  Note over H: the request is the record
  C->>H: downloads treatments
  Note over C: Trio and AndroidAPS apply it only if download<br/>of that type is on (off by default), within limits
  Note over W,C: no acknowledgement, enacted and ignored look the same

Source: landscape §6 rows 5–6 (…landscape-2026-10-09.md:205-206) and technical control loops §3.3 path D (…technical-loops.md:237), at b081a15c. Read-derived.

SMS, to AndroidAPS. The hub is not on this path; the reply is an SMS to the sender.

sequenceDiagram
  accTitle: SMS command to AndroidAPS
  accDescr: A sender on the allowed list texts a command; AndroidAPS asks for confirmation, the sender answers with a one-time code and PIN within five minutes, and AndroidAPS replies by SMS with the result. The hub is not on this path.
  participant S as Sender phone, on the allowed list
  participant A as AndroidAPS
  S->>A: SMS command
  Note over A: remote commands on (off by default),<br/>number on the allowed list
  A-->>S: SMS asking for confirmation
  S->>A: SMS: one-time code and PIN, within 5 min
  Note over A: bolus constraints, minimum time<br/>between remote boluses
  A-->>S: SMS reply with the result

Source: technical control loops §3.3 path E (…technical-loops.md:238) and the questionnaire defaults F13 (docs/30-design/platform/integration-questionnaire-defaults-2026-10-18.md:285-288), at b081a15c. Read-derived.

Client control, to AndroidAPS (4.0.0 prerelease). The only path with a request record on the hub and acknowledgements correlated with it.

sequenceDiagram
  accTitle: Client-control command from AAPSClient to AndroidAPS through the hub settings collection
  accDescr: A paired AAPSClient writes a signed command to the hub settings collection. AndroidAPS verifies it and writes signed acknowledgements, Executing then Done with Ok, Failed or Expired, and a late Delivery Failed if the pump delivery fails afterwards, all correlated by the command counter. A bolus is two commands, prepare and commit; the prepare's acknowledgement carries the dose preview and the commit delivers it at most once.
  participant C as AAPSClient, paired
  participant H as Hub: settings collection
  participant A as AndroidAPS
  C->>H: signed command
  H-->>A: synced
  Note over A: signature, increasing counter,<br/>clock skew, validity window
  A->>H: signed ack: Executing
  A->>H: signed ack: Done, Ok or Failed or Expired
  opt delivery fails after Done
    A->>H: signed ack: Delivery Failed
  end
  H-->>C: acks, correlated by the command counter
  Note over C,A: a bolus is prepare then commit: the prepare's Done<br/>carries the dose preview, the commit delivers it at most once

Source: landscape §6 row 7 (…landscape-2026-10-09.md:207) and technical control loops §3.3 path F (…technical-loops.md:239), at b081a15c. Read-derived.

LoopCaregiver's "Remote Commands 2" (row 4) is not drawn: it expects a command collection with a status (Pending → InProgress → Success/Error) that neither hub has.

docs.title: 7. Composition: who combines overlapping intents
docs.text:
Controller Rule Loop target = pre-meal if active, else override, else schedule; basal ×f, ISF ×1/f, CR ×1/f from the override only, applied over the history window Trio, iAPS target = temp target if set, else override target (unless 0 or 6), else profile; override percentage and ISF/CR scope apply regardless; a high or low TT separately sets sensitivityRatio via halfBasalTarget (the multiplication order with the override factor is not traced) AAPS TT replaces min/max/target; PS percentage has already scaled basal, ISF, IC in the EPS; one PS, one TT, one RunningMode, one Scene at a time cgm-remote-monitor no composition; draws bands per kind Nocturne no composition; exclusive within Override, TemporaryTarget, Profile; Exercise/Illness/Travel may overlap

No two controllers share a rule, and the rules depend on algorithm settings (Dynamic ISF, AutoISF, halfBasalTarget). Under the stated roles the hub records the controller's result rather than computing it. The RFC's companion conflict-resolution.md composes overlapping overrides inside the hub; that section is inconsistent with the roles and would need revising.

docs.title: 8. Cowpaths: what controllers already publish as definitions
docs.text:
Controller Where What Missing Loop profile.loopSettings overridePresets (symbol, name, duration, target, scale factor), preMealTargetRange, dosingEnabled, dosingStrategy, APNs coordinates preset id; workout target; GBAF, IRC Trio profile overridePresets (name, duration, percentage, target), APNs coordinates ISF/CR scope, SMB settings, id iAPS a non-Nightscout service presets everything, as far as the hub is concerned AAPS (4.0.0 prerelease) NS settings, identifiers aaps and aaps-state scene, automation, QuickWizard and insulin definitions; active scene with component record identifiers a schema other software can read

Nightscout's careportal already builds its remote-override picker from profile.loopSettings.overridePresets. Each row is a registration in practice: a controller publishing its definitions to the hub, in a controller-private shape, overwritten as a snapshot.

docs.title: 9. What a registration has to be able to declare
docs.text:
Derived from §3–§8. Each element is something at least one controller does today.

  1. Definitions with stable ids and typed fields, per intent kind (override preset, TT preset, scene, mode), including controller-unique fields (Trio SMB schedule, iAPS end conditions, AAPS scene actions).
  2. Intent slots: which kinds exist, which are exclusive within themselves, which coexist.
  3. States and end reasons: scheduled, active, ended {expired, cancelled, superseded, deleted before start, ended by trigger}, with the trigger vocabulary (carbs, glucose above/below, loop off, chain).
  4. The wire carrier: how today's documents map onto the declared kinds — eventType, the discriminating fields, indefinite sentinels, units, and how "ended" is encoded (§4).
  5. Requested vs applied: where the controller reports the applied effect (AAPS EPS, Loop and Trio devicestatus) and how it links back to the request.
  6. Composition result, as reported by the controller (§7), not a hub-side rule.
  7. Initiator vocabulary: the controller's own (Loop EnactTrigger, Trio AdjustmentSource, AAPS Sources).
  8. Command contract: vocabulary, authorisation, expiry, acknowledgement states and correlation id; whether the hub is in the path.
  9. Acceptance policy: which intent the controller accepts from the hub (AAPS opt-in per type, Trio TT download, iAPS announcements).

docs.title: 10. What this means for the existing design series
docs.text: Document Consistent Needs revising Controller descriptions kind/instance split, decomposesTo (D11), .well-known catalogue §4 ("static, not CRD-style, no new endpoints") is superseded in part by D18; it describes the well-known tier Hub-and-spoke sync registration-derived contract, cursor + batch stateSpans in the schema has no slots, end reasons, initiators or command contract. 2026-10-12: the schema now has them (see the next row); the document is corrected in place Effects and versioning effect vs motivation; TherapyEffect as a span AAPS percentage is an insulin-needs scale; Trio "481" is 399 distinct; Trio notes is a preset name specs/sync/registrations/{loop,trio,androidaps}.yaml structural discriminators. Since 2026-10-12 (make schema-sync-model, schema extended additively): every intent kind declares its slot and which slots coexist, states, the wire carrier (§4), requested vs applied, initiators, definitions and acceptance policy, each with read/measured evidence; composition is declared as reported by the controller and commands per §6. Added: Loop pre-meal (declared with wire: null, not published), Loop dosingEnabled, Trio dosingMode (§3.2; the dosingMode in this row's original text is Trio's), AAPS RunningMode, the AAPS PS → EPS pair, AAPS Scene (4.0.0 prerelease). AAPS Override removed. Also 2026-10-12 (SCHEMA-REG-EXT, D18 addendum rules 1–5): the grammar is must-ignore with typed, reverse-DNS-namespaced extensions, typed field declarations, other + controllerTerm for the open lists, per-kind versions and declared horizons; the three registrations gained typeRef to ControllerSettings definitions read from their own algorithm family, a cycle horizon on the devicestatus document and an effective-dated horizon on settings; a synthetic fixture (registrations/fixtures/) uses every rule still undeclared, because this document does not establish them: iAPS (no registration exists); end-reason vocabularies for Trio override and temp target and for AAPS profile switch; AAPS Sources values; command vocabularies; where AAPS reports the composed target; a scheduled state for any kind except Loop's override. The declarations are read-derived except the counts §3 marks measured. Not typed, rather than guessed: per-cycle state, and suspendThreshold, whose ControllerSettings definition is labelled oref0 but was read from Loop's source; no generated field carries a sensitivity label, so each falls to unlabelledPolicy: withhold Upstream RFC Definition/Instance, DeliveryRequest/Observation/Reconciliation, kind vs instance request types for override/TT/carbs/mode; requested/rejected states; hub-side composition in conflict-resolution.md; bridge-rules.md reads devicestatus.loop.override and AAPS devicestatus.configuration, neither of which is on the wire Nocturne StateSpan right container for observed state; supersession; overlap for activity categories no request/applied distinction, no end reason, metadata untyped; the §5 unit and cancel differences
