docs.text: # question options recommendation holds Q1 How is dev kept stable before the 16.0.0 tag (the soak is informal, §2.1)? (a) dev takes release fixes only until the tag; feature PRs stay draft. (b) cut release/16.0.0 from dev now; soak and tag from it; dev takes the seam. (a): the soak and the Docker dev image both run from dev today, and a second long-lived branch doubles the merge work for a few weeks #8861, #8863, #8865, #8857 merge dates Q2 #8862 (one executable) in 16.0.0? (a) yes, if merged with time on dev before the tag; (b) 16.1.0 (a): the image's start changes form, and a major's release notes already ask operators to check their start; if the soak has started, (b) the soak start Q3 The seam slices in 16.0.0? (a) hold to 16.1.0; (b) merge now Superseded by Q12 (decided 2026-10-27): in, through B6's entry bar, merged to dev once its measured items pass (§2.1); otherwise 16.1.0 tenancy start date by the time the soak takes Q4 #8857 in 16.1.0, off by default? keep CONTROLLER_REGISTRATION on/off, or a staged mode (D-REG-FLAG) 16.1.0 with whichever flag the PR review settles REG-S3 Q5 Is ID-UNIQUE-INDEX (with duplicate cleaning) 17.0.0 material? (a) yes; (b) add the index as opt-in in a minor, enforce in 17.0.0 (b): an opt-in index lets operators measure their duplicates first. Decided 2026-10-30 (maintainer), neither: in 16.0.0 through the entry bar, behind WRITE_IDENTIFIER_INDEX=try\|require\|off, default try (built where no duplicates block it; counts logged and shown otherwise), with an operator-run report and clean tool ID-UNIQUE-INDEX, the PostgreSQL key Q6 Does multi mode ship in 16.x minors behind TENANCY_MODE=multi? (Since 2026-10-27 the gate is nightscout serve, not a setting. 2026-10-30: multitenant items may also ship in 16.0.0, dormant and labelled alpha behind serve, or not ship.) (a) yes, labelled preview; (b) wait for 17.0.0 (a), §4.3 TEN-LAB's release Q7 How is v4's stability declared? (a) per path in the capability document; (b) a /api/v4-unstable prefix; (c) no marker (a): the capability document is already the place a client reads what the hub serves REG-PROPOSE Q8 WRITE_VALIDATION default (a) stays off; (b) log in a minor; (c) reject in 17.0.0 (b) then (c), after #8841's open items (contents, item 7) 17.0.0 contents Q9 D-EVENT: commit event per call or per driver operation per the plan's decision card Deferred, maintainer 2026-10-27: no shape adopted; the event stays counts-only and internal; reopened when WC-STEP-PATCH's WriteResult.items[], a named first subscriber, the BF-164 websocket cursor re-measure and a count of replica-set sites are in hand. Research continues as input: a post-write variant, with a capped pre-read as the comparison (session -2e). 2026-10-30 (maintainer, via session -7d, on the cache catch-up lab): "the cache needs records named" is dropped as a reason to reopen D-EVENT; the four reopen conditions stay for its other subscribers (sync, alarms, screen refresh), and when it reopens it names records from the same WriteResult.items[]. For release 2 the write step resolves every write by filter (v1 delete by query, update by filter, socket filter writes) to ids first, writes {filter AND _id in ids}, returns the ids in items[], and the cache removes or re-reads exactly those; over 1,000 ids it falls back to today's per-type reload; no timestamp watermark (this replaces the srvModified watermark proposal). One behaviour change: a matching record inserted during a delete by query survives. Condition: a lab arm confirms the {filter AND ids} write first (session -7d, on dev 305a6533). Q-A adopted for release 2 (maintainer, 2026-10-30: adopt once the conditions are met; both remaining conditions met the same day, session -7d: the cache-announcement fixture on proto/v3-unify 3b7f054a, and cache lab round 3 exact in all 15 v3 scenarios at both sizes with its break-it arm flagged 10/10). Its rule-copy reduction is a follow-up (of the 23 pairs: 3 become removable with one shape, 9 follow their own release-2 decisions, 11 are wiring). Earlier record, kept: leaning towards one write shape, conditional: API v3's writes by identifier become the simplest filter write resolved to ids (its identifying read supplies the _id; the step writes {identifier AND _id}; items[] returns the document; the cached wrapper's filter methods go), decided only when a v3 prototype slice shows (1) backward compatibility (G1 0/360, the commit-event copy 0, socket tests green), (2) quality (fixtures that fail without each kept behaviour: Q-S every stored form, PUT/PATCH on writeFilter's pick, duplicate-_id refusal; fewer duplicated rule copies than today's 23) and (3) the cache lab's round 2 confirms the resolved write is exact; if any fails, two write shapes stay. Q-U decided: autoPrune goes through the write step with id resolution (up to 1,000 resolved and named; when the prune days exceed the cache's retention for that collection the pruned records are already out of the cache, so nothing reloads, and where they are shorter the named ids are removed from the cache (BF-222 is today's gap there); over 1,000 the unscoped delete and today's reload); no change for users or clients. The 1,000 cap is a fixed named constant shared by v1, the socket, v3 and autoPrune, not a setting and not a D22 policy entry; revisited only on a measurement 2026-10-31 (maintainer, via session -81): the fourth reopen condition, a count of replica-set sites, is dropped: "The number of sites using mongo replica set is not relevant; many using Mongo Atlas are using a replica set, practically all using some nightscout as a service solution, but many DIY or 'Google NS' folks do not use replica set. It's optional." Consequence: change streams cannot be the required source of the event; the write's own result (WriteResult.items[]) is the source on every site, and change streams can at most be an optional transport. Three conditions remain (items[], a named first subscriber, the BF-164 re-measure); the rest of D-EVENT is being walked through with the maintainer one question at a time (session -81). D-EVENT question 1 (scope) decided, 2026-10-31 (maintainer, via session -81): the in-process commit event names its records' ids from the write step's own WriteResult.items[]; that source is complete because every supported write goes through Nightscout ("Nightscout does not support other writers to mongodb; xdrip's mongodb upload is considered deprecated by Nightscout authors"). Delivery between processes is deferred to the serve roles. A timer runs only for time-driven alarms (stale data, not looping), never to catch up on writes. The event stays internal and unstable until a subscriber outside lib/ exists. Follow-up topic, not answered here: the CLI run-and-subcommands pattern, nightscout single [roles,...] against nightscout multitenant [roles,...] (maintainer: "the serve roles do exist, and are planned soon"), which would make roles orthogonal to tenancy (ties to D21 and D-EXEC-PROFILE). Maintainer's rationale (2026-10-31): partly to unify, recognising that a single-tenant site already has a "headless" API v3, so nightscout single [roles,...] and nightscout multitenant [roles,...] would give single and multitenant one theory of operations in a simple way, while the default stays the monolithic single-tenant site. D-EVENT question 2 decided, 2026-10-31 (maintainer, via session -81): option C, both. One event per write(intent) call, carrying that write's WriteResult.items[], for subscribers; the per-driver-call event stays as instrumentation ("seems better for long term maintenance? Won't we need the instrumentation if we want to do differential analyses against different backends?"). Reading recorded by -81: the per-write event is the logical contract and must be identical on MongoDB and PostgreSQL, so differential tests compare it across backends; the per-call event is backend-specific instrumentation (driver calls on MongoDB, statements on PostgreSQL), not a contract. D-EVENT question 3 decided, 2026-10-31 (maintainer, via session -81): each record entry in the per-write event carries _id, identifier, outcome (inserted, replaced, merged, deleted, refused, not-found) and, for a refused record, its problems list; the event carries collection, source and counts. No document contents and no filter, so no health data is in the event. Above the 1,000 cap the event lists no records, says it is collapsed, and readers reload. Under multitenancy every event carries the tenant once the tenancy binding lands. D-EVENT question 4 decided, 2026-10-31 (maintainer, via session -81): "we haven't meant to rule anything out of 16.0.0.... we are in a sprint to see what can make it in. 1/2/3 as appropriate." The per-write event ships with write(intent) release 2, aimed at 16.0.0 through the entry bar; subscribers are added as each clears its gates: (1) the one-person profile's alarm check, (2) the cache, (3) the socket's dataUpdate. The walk-through is complete ST-EVENT, the change feed, WC-STEP-PATCH release 2 Q10 D-T30: approve the tenant configuration surface walk through the DECISION sections start once 16.0.0 is tagged, after re-measuring the 277 settings on dev T30-SCHEMA-CONFIG, TEN-RESOLVE Q11 Review capacity #8857, #8859, #8861, #8862, #8863 and #8865 add 17,794 lines against their bases (§2) review in theme order (16.1.0 first), one stacked chain at a time every row of §4.3 Q12 Put prototypes in 16.0.0 to soak them as alpha? Decided, maintainer 2026-10-27: the seam slices go into 16.0.0 if feasible and B6's entry bar is met with time on dev before the tag (§2.1); building them to that bar is worth doing whether or not they ship, because it prepares the work that follows. Components that ship before they are mature are labelled alpha in the release notes. Still open: Q12a B6 the soak start, BFQ-72 Q12a If the slices ship, how is an alpha label made meaningful for code on the default path? Decided, maintainer 2026-10-27: option (a). The slices are default on in the single-tenant release, named in the release notes as new internals, with the rehearsed revert as the fallback. Once verified, exercised on dev and released, that code is trusted for what single-tenant sites run. The alpha label belongs to the multitenant bindings only: serve roles, tenant resolution and scope, per-tenant credentials, and the PostgreSQL backend. Trust covers the paths real clients exercise; code no single-tenant site runs (the filter tree's SQL translation, the tenant binding the interface carries, rarely used endpoints without a cohort check) does not inherit it — the release notes' wording Q13 When does the quiet period start? Corrected by the maintainer, 2026-10-27: not now; merging is still under way. Proposed: it starts when the 16.0.0 merge list is closed: what is in flight for 16.0.0 (#8872 BF-194, merged 2026-10-27 as db3b9e4e; #8855 translations, BF-72 and BF-161 through their forks) plus whatever the maintainer adds to it, with #8865 decided either way. Until then dev keeps taking 16.0.0 work, and the cohort requests (Q14) start now, because M1 and #8859 are already on dev #8865 in (maintainer, 2026-10-27 night). Open: the rest of the merge list the tag date; #8865, #8857 merge dates Q14 Who asks the cohorts, and when? (a) now, one request per cohort in B6's table, naming M1 and #8859 as what changed; (b) after the alarms check (a): the cohort confirmations are pre-tag item 2 and the slowest, because they wait on other people RT-16-RIG-SOAK Q15 #8865's base (a) retarget to dev now and merge dev in, still draft; (b) close it and reopen with ST-V3-DECOUPLE (a), by the maintainer; re-measure serve api after PLAT-SERVE, ST-V3-DECOUPLE Q16 When does dev reopen for 16.1.0 work? (a) the day 16.0.0 is tagged; (b) a release/16.0.0 branch for fixes, dev reopened earlier (a), as Q1 (a); (b) only if the quiet period runs longer than about two weeks every 16.1.0 row

docs.title: 6. Scenario briefs
docs.text: Each brief states what the scenario is, who it reaches, and what to measure before choosing it.

docs.title: B1. 16.0.0 with the seam held (recommended)
docs.text:
• What happens. dev takes only #8859, #8856, #8864, #8866, #8858 and the two advisory fixes; the soak runs; the tag follows; the seam chain merges the next day.
  • Who it reaches. Operators get the modernization and the write boundary. Uploaders (AndroidAPS, Loop, Trio, xDrip+) see #8859's re-send matching and the null-removes rule, which the client notes list.
  • Measure first. The soak and live delivery checks (RT-16-RIG-SOAK, RT-16-LIVE-ALARMS); the 67-shape client replay on the candidate with #8859 merged.

docs.title: B2. 16.0.0 with the seam included
docs.text:
• What happens. #8861 and #8863 merge to dev as soon as their checks pass (now the decided path, Q12). 16.1.0 starts from a dev that already routes v1 through the interface.
  • Who it reaches. The same as B1, plus every v1 read and write on every site going through new code.
  • Measure first. The write-contract matrix, the HTTP and v1 read diffs and the client replay on the merged tree; dev users exercise them from the merge (§2.1). The gain is about one release of lead time for tenancy; the cost is less time on dev for the rest of 16.0.0's changes to be told apart from the slices if something regresses.

docs.title: B3. Identity first
docs.text:
• What happens. After 16.0.0, the next work is SPEC-ID-AMEND, the Loop reply (D-LOOP-ID) and the six ID-*-DECISION items, with WC-STEP-PATCH built to them.
  • Who it reaches. Controller authors: Loop (syncIdentifier), Trio (id), AndroidAPS (keeps the server's identifier). Nocturne, through D-NOCTURNE-ID.
  • Measure first. ID-DUP-MEASURE (duplicates by identifier across the corpus) and the replay of each controller's re-send.
  • Why it comes first. It fixes the PostgreSQL key and the v4 typed paths; an answer that arrives after the tables exist is a migration.

docs.title: B4. Tenancy first
docs.text:
• What happens. ST-PG and TEN-RESOLVE are built before the identity decisions, with identifier as an unconstrained column.
  • Who it reaches. Tenants of a multitenant Nightscout only; single-tenant sites are unaffected.
  • Risk. The unique key and the typed record paths are decided later, against tables that hold data. It also puts PostgreSQL behind an interface that has had no release under real traffic.
  • When to choose it. If a hosting partner needs a dated preview before the identity answers arrive; then TEN-LAB is labelled preview and ID-UNIQUE-INDEX is a migration step in the plan.

docs.title: B5. Registration and v4 as their own minors
docs.text:
• What happens. #8857 ships in 16.1.0 off by default; v4 statistics in 16.2.0; typed paths when decision 12 is settled.
  • Who it reaches. Controller authors who opt in; Nocturne, as the second hub the contract is proposed to.
  • Measure first. The conformance cases against a booted server (35 pass, 88 mapped, 0 fail at 3be98536); flag off is byte-identical to dev.
  • Effect on tenancy. None until HUB-REG-CRM-SEAM; registrations are per tenant (AU6), so the store gains a tenant column when ST-PG lands.

docs.title: B6. Prototypes in 16.0.0, labelled alpha (asked 2026-10-27)
docs.text:
Decided, maintainer 2026-10-27: the seam slices go in if feasible and the entry bar below is met; components that ship before they are mature are labelled alpha (Q12, Q12a).

The question: if a prototype of every REST API behind the storage interface, and a prototype of multi mode, exist within days, are they worth shipping in 16.0.0 with their status noted, so the release soaks them; and how does that weigh against releasing as soon as the candidate is ready?

  • The candidate is not ready to release now, so the choice is what is on dev long enough before the tag. Unmet on 2026-10-27: the real-rig soak (not started), the live delivery check, the BF-72 and BF-161 fork fixes, #8859 (needed in 16.0.0, draft), #8866 (dev CI red until it merges) and master's protection (#8824 blocked). The soak is informal (§2.1): dev users exercise whatever is merged, so a change merged sooner is soaked longer.
  • The two prototypes behave differently in a release.
seam slices (#8861, #8863) multi-mode prototype reached by a self-hoster every v1 read and write, by default only with TENANCY_MODE=multi or serve soak value from shipping high: every site exercises it none: nobody running single runs it can be labelled alpha no; code on the default path is either fit to ship or not yes new public surface none (behaviour-neutral) subcommands and settings, which become semver surface (S3) once released security exposure none new tenant isolation and per-tenant credentials (T30-WIRING, D13, D14) unbuilt; a hoster can turn it on from a released image overlap with 16.0.0's required work 7 files with the BF-72 fork fix (adv/r3gv-1600), 6 with #8859, 1 with BF-161's (git diff --name-only against dev 8dbb60c2) none measured
  • The seam slices: in, only through an entry bar, merged to dev as soon as items 1, 3, 4 and 5 pass.
  • BF-72's fix re-merged onto the seam inside its private fork and its tests re-run there. The fix stays out of public branches until the release publishes it.
  • The write-contract matrix (360 cells, off and reject) and the 67-shape client replay equal to the candidate without the slices.
  • A read and write latency comparison on the corpus, with and without the slices. Not measured yet: v1 reads now translate each query into the filter tree and back.
  • A one-step fallback: reverting the slices' merge commits restores the current paths, rehearsed once. Not met with time on dev before the tag → 16.1.0, as in §3.
  • Results, 2026-10-27: all five items met on local candidates (session -2e's agent; Node 22.23.4, MongoDB 5.0.33; dev 2dc0c1bc, #8859 5c6ceabb, #8861 48e7e101, #8863 38b910d7). Item 2 met the same day by session -e4, inside the private forks (below).

No measurable change. Not measured: concurrent load, larger databases, MongoDB 8, Node 26 5. revert cand/with-reverted cf762dd0: one commit reverting the three merges; its tree equals cand/without's (7a6f5c20, checked by session -ee) and npm test gives 4575/0/3 2. advisory fixes BF-72's and BF-161's fixes merged onto cand/with in their private forks, local only (session -e4; Node 22.23.4, MongoDB 8.0.34). The candidates are local. On dev 94899828 (#8866 and #8859 merged) the slices are re-merged as 479e33d1 and a3f74a08; outside the 11 files #8866 changed, their trees equal the measured ones (checked by session -ee). Re-run on a3f74a08 (session -2e): npm test 4687/0/3 and test:all 5015/0/3, the same totals as cand/with; the 360-cell matrix equals dev 94899828 in off and in reject (off vs reject differ in 12 cells on each). The client replay, v1 HTTP differential and latency are not re-run: their inputs are the non-CI tree, which is unchanged. Before anything is pushed, the conflict resolutions go onto the PR branches (dev and #8859 merged into feat/storage-filter and feat/storage-writes, the count commit added to #8863), and the maintainer merges #8859 before #8861 and #8863. Merge order to dev, agreed 2026-10-27 (maintainer; sessions -2e and -e4): #8859, then #8856 (BF-193), then #8861 and #8863. #8856 is resolved against the slices on prep/writes-plus-8856 699a70c4 (npm test 4694 passing, 0 failing, 3 pending; session -2e). - Cohort checks to request once the slices are on dev (they move every v1 read and write onto the interface):

cohort what to check why AndroidAPS (API v3 client) uploads, re-sends and deletions sync without duplicates or refusals v3 already uses the adapter the slices extend Loop and Trio (v1 treatments, syncIdentifier, id) carbs, boluses and temp targets appear once; edits and deletes take effect ST-WRITES moves v1 treatment writes xDrip+ and other v1 entries uploaders readings appear on time, no gaps after a reconnect v1 entries writes and the dedup key follower apps (LoopFollow, Nightguard, Nightscout watch faces) current reading, IOB and COB match the site v1 reads through fromMongo report users (Nightscout Reporter, the site's reports) long-range reports load and match 15.0.9's numbers large v1 queries; the latency item mmol/L sites values and targets shown in the right unit units handling on the paths that moved
  • The multi-mode prototype: shipped, but not in the 16.0.0 artifact. Shipping it inside 16.0.0 gives it no soak and makes its names public surface. Ship it as a prerelease instead (16.1.0-alpha.1 image and tag from a branch, its status in the tag message), run in TEN-LAB and by a hoster who agrees to run alpha. If the maintainer still wants it in the tree for 16.0.0, the minimum is: unreachable without an explicit experimental setting, refused at boot without per-tenant credentials (no API_SECRET under multi, D13), and named in the release notes as outside the versioning policy.
  • Weighed against releasing at once. Including the seam adds the entry bar's work (one or two days of agent time plus maintainer review of about 3,000 lines) before merging to dev, in exchange for one release of real traffic on the interface before PostgreSQL relies on it. If the gates are met before the bar is, release without the slices.

docs.title: 8859 and the seam chain merged together, the overlap resolved once.
B7. Close the merge list, then a short quiet period, then the tag (recommended, evening 2026-10-27)
docs.text:
• What happens. The 16.0.0 merge list (Q13) is merged; then dev takes release fixes only for a few days with the final candidate. The cohort requests (Q14) and the live alarms check start now and run in parallel; BF-72 and BF-161 are brought up to dev inside their forks. D-T30 and the remaining identity questions are settled while dev is quiet.
  • Who it reaches. Every 16.0.0 user, through M1 and #8859, which are new code on every v1 read and write; B6's cohort table is the check list.
  • Measure first. The cohort confirmations; a 360-cell matrix and client replay on the final candidate, which will include the fork fixes.
  • Effect on tenancy. 16.1.0 work (ST-V3-DECOUPLE, registration, and PLAT-SERVE unless it joins the merge list) builds on branches and merges when dev reopens.

docs.title: B8. Take #8865 into 16.0.0 (it supersedes #8862) — decided 2026-10-27 night
docs.text:
• What happens. #8865 joins the 16.0.0 merge list (Q13) and merges before the list closes; #8862 is closed as superseded.
  • Who it reaches. Every Docker site. Measured 2026-10-27 night on images built from dev dcf20bfb and #8865 9bb1f0b4 (tools/lab/image-start-forms): every docker run form that started a server on dev starts the same server, with the same entrypoint, user, workdir and environment, one node process and no HEALTHCHECK; status.json is identical apart from the server time. What changes: docker stop takes 0.13 s and exits 0 instead of 10.1 s and 137; SIGINT and SIGTERM, ignored by node as PID 1 on dev, now shut the server down; nightscout single and nightscout healthcheck work as commands.
  • Measure first. Nothing left to measure on the image. The release notes name the one case the lab cannot reach: a supervisor that sends SIGTERM itself under restart: on-failure (the site used to keep running; it now exits 0 and stays down), and tooling that matches PID 1's command line.
  • Trade. A cleaner stop for every Docker site in the major, against one more PR in the merge list; serve is reserved for a multitenant Nightscout and refuses every role until one is multitenant (maintainer, 2026-10-27 night).

docs.title: B9. Multitenant roles in 16.0.0 as alpha
docs.text:
• What happens. ST-V3-DECOUPLE is built and #8865 merged before the tag, serve api labelled alpha.
  • Why not. Nobody under single runs it, so the release gives it no soak (B6), its names become public surface, and the quiet period moves out. The prerelease route in B6 (16.1.0-alpha.1 from a branch, run in TEN-LAB) gives the same exposure to the people who would run it.
  • Outcome (2026-10-30). #8865 merged with ST-V3-DECOUPLE (991b0654); serve still refuses every role. The 16.0.0 scope allows multitenant items to ship dormant, labelled alpha behind serve, or not ship.

docs.title: API v4: which parts to share with Nocturne, and which listener serves each
docs.text:
Record

Record as of 2026-10-26. A point-in-time document; it is not kept up to date.

Contributor-facing. Snapshot, 2026-10-26: alignment main 6e6223f26 (specifications; amended the same day for the maintainer's decisions in §0), cgm-remote-monitor draft PR #8857 at 3be98536, Nocturne main 89dcaf1dd. Every Nocturne statement below was read from source at 89dcaf1dd and nothing was run against it (read-derived). The proposed surface is described in specs/openapi/proposed/nightscout-v4.yaml; the current API in specs/openapi/upstream/cgm-remote-monitor/. Nocturne paths are relative to src/API/Nocturne.API/ unless they begin with Core. (under src/Core/Nocturne.) or tests/. Nothing here has been sent to either project.

The maintainer asked, on 2026-10-26, three things: how much of API v4 to unify with Nocturne, how much is split by scope between the operator's and owner's listeners and the app listener, and whether controller registration and instances belong on v4 endpoints. The maintainer's direction the same day: Nocturne's v4 surface is to be split, and parts of it will sit on different listeners. This page therefore treats Nocturne's surface as material to partition, group by group, and states for each group which listener it belongs on in our specifications and whether it is a candidate for a shared contract.

docs.title: 0. Decided, 2026-10-26
docs.text:
The maintainer decided four points the same day, and seven more in a second round (decisions 1, 2, 5, 8, 9, 10 and 11 in §7); the sections below are amended for them.

point decision where it is applied statistics served on v4 under statistics (/api/v4/statistics/...), matching Nocturne 89dcaf1dd's StatisticsController for hub compatibility: its paths, parameters, response shapes, tenant time-zone bucketing, the under-ten-readings rule and its read scopes. The design stays open for discussion: what a shared contract fixes and what it leaves to each hub, and whether the compute-over-a-posted-body actions join later operations 32–41; specs/openapi/proposed/statistics-v4.schema.json; §6.4; dated notes on the two older texts registration scope registration of products, definitions and instances is a per-tenant API that affects only that tenant's site and data, never a platform or operator action; the owner's listing and actions are tenant-scoped (tenant-admin under multi, the one listener under single); controller actions and commands are on the data listener authority AU6; registration's opening note instance paths one flat root: /api/v4/instances/{instanceId} is the instance resource, its command fetch /api/v4/instances/{instanceId}/commands, and the owner's listing GET /api/v4/instances; creating an instance names the product in the body registration §7 amendment; commands §7.1; the instance schema's product; operations 8–10; §5.1 softwareId proposed in the registration's metadata, in Nocturne's RFC 7591 software_id form, for compatibility; its rules stay open for discussion controller-state-model.schema.json; registration §5.1; §5 owner paths (1) a controller registers with the credential it already holds: the role a hub issues by default to a device or uploader credential includes api:registrations:create and :delete, and the owner may withhold them. The owner's actions are for exceptions and use the same paths on every deployment (/api/v4/registrations/…/<action>, /api/v4/instances), on tenant-admin under multi and the one listener under single authority §4, §5; registration §5.1; registration-submit.schema.json request retire (2) both: the bound controller retires with DELETE on the product, the owner with POST …/retire, as #8857 serves them registration §5.1, §5.5; operations 6 and 11 commands (5) on the data listener; the tenant owner marks the subject acting for the person, as subject configuration on the owner's listener, and the hub reads the mark; a client cannot assert it commands CM14, CM32 owner boundary (8) stated per credential: an owner action is refused to any credential issued to a device or an app; a separate listener is one way to meet it. To be reviewed as the design matures authority AU7 data sources and connectors (9) on the owner's listener: configuring a vendor cloud connection, triggering a sync and listing who sends data change or describe the runtime and its resources, unlike an AID controller's registration §6.1 operator and self-service (10, 11) both hub-specific, outside the shared contract; in cgm-remote-monitor the operator keeps D7's tenant lifecycle with no access to members' credentials, and creating tenants stays the operator's. Revisit once D17 row 2 lands §6.1

docs.title: 1. The answer in brief
docs.text:
• Registration and instances on v4: yes, already. The specifications put the product, definition and instance resources under the capability document's submit.href, and #8857 serves it at /api/v4/registrations (lib/registration/index.js:25); the command paths of commands §7.1 are under /api/v4/ too, and instances have their own flat root (§0). Registration is per tenant (AU6). Discovery stays at /.well-known/nightscout/ (RFC 8615). What is not settled is the path the owner's actions take on ns-tenant-admin (§7, decisions 1–2).
  • Split by listener. Of the 41 proposed operations, 30 are on the data listener, 10 on the tenant-owner listener, and one (retire) on both, by caller. None is on the operator listener: the operator's plane (tenant lifecycle, export) is not a v4 surface in our design (D7). Nocturne serves all three audiences from one API and divides them by scope and role (§4).
  • What to propose to Nocturne first: discovery, the registration grammar with its product, definition and instance resources, the command and proposal paths, and statistics reads, all on the data listener. The owner's actions are shared as rules, not as a listener: each hub keeps its own way of refusing them to device and app credentials. Typed record and state-span paths come second, after the identity decisions. Everything else in Nocturne's v4 stays hub-specific (§6).

docs.title: 4. How each side divides the audiences
docs.text:
audience our specifications Nocturne at 89dcaf1dd devices, uploaders, apps the data listener with a native per-tenant credential (AU1); permissions are shiro strings, api:<collection>:<action>, and reading is one bit (AU5); the new names api:registrations:*, api:commands:*, api:proposals:* are proposals the same API; OAuth clients registered by RFC 7591 hold category scopes in two tiers, glucose.read / glucose.readwrite and so on (Core.Models/Authorization/Scope.cs:31-133) the tenant owner its own listener, ns-tenant-admin; an owner action on the data listener with any other credential is 403 not-authorised (AU2); on single, API_SECRET the same API; the tenant-administration atoms (roles.manage, members.invite, members.manage, tenant.settings, sharing.manage, audit.read, audit.manage, Scope.cs:93-106) are grantable to a member's role and are not requestable by an OAuth client: "there is no per-client scope ceiling to bound a request for them and no consent screen that could meaningfully describe them" (Scope.cs:17-21, sets at :140, :171, :182). Maintenance controllers require the full-access scope * (Attributes/PermissionAttributes.cs:96) the operator ns-admin, its own process and port, no credential, unreachable from tenants (D7, after ORY's public and admin ports) the same API under /api/v4/admin/* with [Authorize(Roles = "platform_admin")]; the role is taken only from a credential that "is the person" (session, OIDC token, legacy JWT, platform-access token), never from a grant, API secret or OAuth token (Core.Models/Authorization/PlatformAdminCredentials.cs:10-45; Middleware/AuthenticationMiddleware.cs:114-131, :151-154). Server-to-server cross-tenant calls use X-Instance-Key only (Attributes/RequireInstanceKeyAuthAttribute.cs:6-36) an anonymous viewer none on v4 public share links hold reports.read, so statistics compute calls are reachable without an account (Extensions/ServiceRegistrationExtensions.cs:457-461)

Where they agree. Both refuse owner powers to a credential issued to a device or an app. Ours does it by the listener the request arrives on (AU2); Nocturne's by keeping the owner atoms out of the set an OAuth client may request (Scope.cs:17-21) and the operator role out of every delegated credential (PlatformAdminCredentials.cs). Both keep the operator's powers out of every tenant credential.

Where they differ. Ours separates audiences by socket; Nocturne by scope and role on one API. A search of src/API for Listen*, RequireHost and MapWhen finds none; Program.cs:81 configures Kestrel only for the request body limit. Our operator plane has no credential at all; Nocturne's operator is a person holding platform_admin. Our registration permissions are collection-style strings; Nocturne's scopes are per data category, which is closer to the scoped reads authority DR1 asks for.

The consequence for a shared contract. A rule written as "on ns-tenant-admin" cannot be met by a hub with one listener. A rule written as "an owner action is refused to any credential a device or app holds, with 403 not-authorised" is met by both: by AU2's listener, and by Nocturne's atom partition. The conformance cases owner-action-on-data-listener and instances/owner-transfer-role-data-listener already state the refusal; their listener member is how a hub with listeners runs them.

docs.title: 5. Registration and instances on v4
docs.text:
Decided. D18 (two tiers: well-known and controller-owned), its addendum (the extensible grammar), D19 (definitions and instances) and D20 (version-scoped quirks and the two-id rule), with the maintainer's decisions of 2026-10-14 to 2026-10-17 (execution plan §2.6); the owner's actions on ns-tenant-admin and API_SECRET as owner on single (AU2, decided 2026-10-14 and 2026-10-16). The product resource is <submit.href>/<vendor>/<product>; the capability document says where submit.href is. On 2026-10-26 the maintainer decided that registration is per tenant and never an operator action (AU6), and that instances have one flat root, /api/v4/instances/{instanceId} (registration §7 amendment).

What #8857 serves at 3be98536. The capability document, the catalogue and each well-known registration (lib/registration/index.js:136-157); the product resource, definitions and instances under /api/v4/registrations (lib/registration/products.js:266-289), instances nested under the product (:283, :289), which the flat-root decision changes (§5.1); the owner's actions as POST …/<action> (:307-333) with retire among them (negotiate.js:742); the owner's listing at GET /api/v4/registrations/instances (products.js:295). The owner is recognised only as API_SECRET (products.js:313), since no ns-tenant-admin exists. Its capability document offers submit and instances and no commands (index.js:93-107).

What Nocturne does. It registers who an app is, not what its data means. POST /api/oauth/register is RFC 7591 dynamic client registration: "Every call issues a new client" (Controllers/Authentication/OAuthController.cs:973-984); a software_id names the app, and a bundled directory of 12 known apps keyed on reverse-DNS software_id (org.loopkit.loop, org.nightscout.trio, info.nightscout.androidaps, …) "provides the identity a dynamic registration receives when its redirect URIs prove it is the app it names" (Core.Models/Authorization/KnownOAuthClients.cs:5-15; matched at Services/Auth/OAuthClientService.cs:143). What each controller's documents mean is compiled into the server.

Whether they compose. They answer different questions and do not overlap: Nocturne's registration says who is writing and with what scopes; ours says what the writes mean and which copy wrote them. PROPOSAL-controller-descriptions §2.2 proposes joining them on the reverse-DNS software_id. On 2026-10-26 the maintainer decided to propose it in Nocturne's form for compatibility: metadata.softwareId is now in controller-state-model.schema.json, marked proposed, optional, compared exactly as Nocturne's directory lookup compares it (KnownOAuthClients.cs:214-215), and not part of the registration's identity (registration §5.1). Nocturne's registration request carries it as software_id with no format check (Models/OAuth/ClientRegistrationRequest.cs:41-44). Composed, a Nocturne client registered as org.loopkit.loop would submit a registration whose metadata names the same id, and a hub could read both halves from one key. On our side the binding is to the subject (AU4), which under Nocturne's model would be the OAuth client's subject. Open for discussion: whether two products may share one softwareId, and whether a hub checks it against the credential's registered client.

docs.title: 5.1 Are registrations and instances redundant?
docs.text:
The maintainer asked whether registrations and instances are redundant, or whether one is for the kind and the other for the running copy, and if redundant whether one should go. They are not redundant (registration §7–§8, D19):

resource says identity lifetime product registration, with its immutable definitions what a controller's data means: the kind, per vendor and product, per release (vendor, product); each definition by the hash of its content as long as the controller publishes it; definitions are never changed instance which running copy is connected: its definition, its roles on channels (source of record, command sink), its labels a random UUID v4 the copy generates once a lease the copy renews; a lapsed instance holds no roles

Several instances run one definition (a phone and a lab rig, or the old and the new phone during a migration), and one instance is the destination of commands for a channel. Removing either loses something: without the product there is nothing to say what the writes mean; without instances there is no way to tell two copies apart or to route a command to one.

The wrinkle was two path roots for one instance. Options considered:

option form evidence (a) keep both roots /api/v4/registrations/{vendor}/{product}/instances/{id}, fetch at /api/v4/instances/{id}/commands commands.fetch is a URI template in the capability document, so clients do not hard-code it; #8857 serves the nested form (b) nest the fetch under the product …/{vendor}/{product}/instances/{id}/commands every fetch would carry the vendor and product, which the fetch rules (CM18, CM26) never use (c) one flat root /api/v4/instances/{id} and /api/v4/instances/{id}/commands an instance id is a random UUID v4 (identity §2), so it names one copy without its product; the copy keeps one path for its life

Decided, maintainer 2026-10-26: (c). Creating an instance names the product in the body (product: {vendor, product} in controller-instance.schema.json), not by a create on the product resource that answers with a flat Location. The evidence for the body: the instance id is chosen by the controller and the create is a PUT to it (registration §8), so create, renew and release use one path with no redirect; the order of checks already reads the product's registration, binding, block and retirement for every PUT, and the stored instance and the owner's listing already carry vendor and product (registration-submit.schema.json storedInstance.identity, instanceSummary); and the conformance cases model an instance request with its identity separately from the path, so none changes. A renewal naming another product is 422 invalid-instance. Nocturne has no instance resource; the nearest, its client devices, is flat: /api/v4/client-devices/{id} (ClientDevicesController.cs:21, :127, :150).

The follow-up for #8857. Its routes at 3be98536 that change:

#8857 today after the decision PUT /api/v4/registrations/:vendor/:product/instances/:instanceId (lib/registration/products.js:283) PUT /api/v4/instances/:instanceId, product from the body's product DELETE /api/v4/registrations/:vendor/:product/instances/:instanceId (:289) DELETE /api/v4/instances/:instanceId GET /api/v4/registrations/instances (:295) GET /api/v4/instances (the owner's listing) lib/registration/schemas/controller-instance.schema.json (vendored) refreshed from specs/sync/controller-instance.schema.json, which gains product

docs.title: 6.2 The minimum shared v4 contract
docs.text:
1. Discovery: GET /.well-known/nightscout/sync and /controllers, with the capability document's schema.
  2. Registration: the grammar (controller-state-model.schema.json), the product, definition and instance resources with their etag and precondition rules, the element results, and the fallback rule; the owner's actions as rules with the refusal stated per credential (§4).
  3. Commands: the command record, the outstanding list, fetch and report, cancel, and the proposal in front of a command.
  4. Statistics: Nocturne's ten reads over stored data, with its time-zone and minimum-data rules and read scopes (decided, §6.4).

Second wave, after the decisions they depend on: typed record paths (G3) and state spans (G4).

docs.title: 6.3 Credit
docs.text: The record catalogue is Nocturne's V4 model (records §3). The partition of scopes into what an OAuth client may request and what a tenant role may confer (Scope.cs:17-21) is the closest prior art for stating the owner boundary as a rule on credentials rather than on sockets; §4 proposes exactly that. The reverse-DNS software_id directory is Nocturne's. The leases, labels and selectors, the declared-versus-observed split and the resource-with-etag style are taken from Kubernetes (PROPOSAL-controller-descriptions §4); the operator plane secured by unreachability is ORY's public and admin port split (D7).

docs.title: 6.4 Statistics
docs.text:
Decided, maintainer 2026-10-26. Statistics are on v4 under statistics, matching Nocturne 89dcaf1dd's StatisticsController for hub compatibility: its paths, parameters, response shapes, time-zone bucketing, the under-ten-readings rule and its read scopes. The OpenAPI file has its ten GET reads over stored data (operations 32–41, anchored per operation to Controllers/V4/Analytics/StatisticsController.cs), with response shapes read from Nocturne's models into statistics-v4.schema.json (83 types; read-derived from property declarations, nested types not checked by hand). Not included: its 15 POST actions that compute over a posted body, and its five stateless calculators (gmi/{meanGlucose}, estimated-a1c/{averageGlucose}, clinical-targets/{population}, and the two unit conversions).

Its read rule. Each read is admitted on reports.read; periods and punch-card on glucose.read or reports.read, and a response that merges categories is narrowed to the caller's: insulin and carb aggregates need reports.read or treatments.read (Authorization/AnalyticsReadScopeGuards.cs:314-331). Public share links hold reports.read. cgm-remote-monitor has no such scopes: reading is one bit, readable (AU5), so how these map onto its permissions is part of the open design.

Open for discussion (maintainer, 2026-10-26): what a shared contract should fix and what it leaves to each hub (for example the population default, the canonical-stream choice across CGMs, caching), and whether the compute-over-a-posted-body actions join later.

The two older texts. The statistics API proposal (REQ-STATS-001 to 005) wrote /api/v3/stats/{daily,daily/{date},summary,hourly,treatments,current}, and the reporting needs analysis (GAP-REPORT-001) /api/v3/statistics/{tir,daily,a1c,agp}. Both now carry a dated note pointing at this decision and are otherwise unchanged. The proposal's MCP resource provider (REQ-STATS-005; ECOSYSTEM-PROGRAMME "Statistics and agents") would sit on top of the v4 reads.

Why v4 rather than v3, the evidence before the decision: API v3 is a per-collection contract (/{collection}, /{collection}/{identifier}, /history, with version, status and lastModified beside them, api-v3.yaml), mounted per enabled collection (lib/api3/generic/collection.js:42-57, lib/api3/index.js:66), so a documented client would read /api/v3/stats/daily as a record of a collection stats; and Nocturne already serves statistics under v4.

Why a server API now. cgm-remote-monitor's reports compute in the browser: the report client fetches raw entries and treatments over API v1 (lib/report/reportclient.js:343, :380, :417, :697) and 14 plugin files of 6,169 lines compute from them, for example the A1c estimates and quartiles in lib/report_plugins/dailystats.js:126-130 and GVI in glucosedistribution.js:524, using the statistics helpers in lib/report/statistics.js that six plugins import (all read at

docs.title: 8857's 3be98536). The proposal's 2026-05 status records that tests/reports.test.js was retired
docs.text:
on the assumption that statistics move to a server API, and asks for a parity test against the plugin math.

The rules the decision adopts, and how the older proposal compared. Read from Nocturne's tests:

question statistics API proposal Nocturne at 89dcaf1dd which days and hours not stated buckets local days and hours on the tenant's zone; without a zone it withholds the day-dependent figures and says why (tests/Unit/Nocturne.API.Tests/Controllers/V4/Analytics/StatisticsControllerTimeZoneTests.cs:83-437, including the long daylight-saving day at :285) too little data not stated a period with fewer than ten readings carries no figures (StatisticsControllerAggregationTests.cs:75) which readings not stated the canonical stream across CGMs unless one device is named (StatisticsController.cs:486-490) compute over posted data not offered POST actions compute over a caller-supplied body up to 100 MB (StatisticsController.cs:55-60), limited to 60 a minute per tenant host because public share links can reach them (ServiceRegistrationExtensions.cs:457-472), guarded by StatisticsComputeLimitTests.cs:27-98 who may read readable reports.read, held by public share links caching per-endpoint durations (proposal "Caching Strategy") 60-second client cache on three GETs, five minutes server-side on periods (StatisticsController.cs:34-36)

docs.title: 7. Open decisions for the maintainer
docs.text:
Each is a placement or a rule the evidence above does not settle. All but row 12 were decided on 2026-10-26 and keep their numbers; what remains open in them is stated.

# decision evidence 1 The owner's action paths on ns-tenant-admin. Decided, maintainer 2026-10-26: the same paths on every deployment, served on the owner's listener; and a controller registers with the credential it already holds (the default device or uploader role includes the registration permissions; the owner may withhold them), so setting up a controller needs no owner action. registration-submit.schema.json request says "POST <admin registrations path>/<vendor>/<product>/<action>"; the hub-implementer guide §4.6 and #8857 put them under the same router as the controller's (/api/v4/registrations). This was a mismatch between two of our texts; the schema text now names the controller's paths. 2 The owner's retire: DELETE or POST …/retire. Decided, maintainer 2026-10-26: both, as #8857 serves them: DELETE for the bound controller, POST …/retire for the owner. registration §5.1 and the schema's request say DELETE; #8857 serves POST …/retire (negotiate.js:742). On single, one API_SECRET holder may be both the bound controller and the owner, so DELETE alone cannot tell which is acting. 3 The owner's listing path. Decided, maintainer 2026-10-26: GET /api/v4/instances, tenant-scoped (AU6), on tenant-admin under multi and the one listener under single. registration is per tenant (AU6); the flat instance root (§5.1). #8857 serves GET /api/v4/registrations/instances. 4 One root for instance paths. Decided, maintainer 2026-10-26: one flat root, /api/v4/instances/{instanceId}, the product named in the body. §5.1, with the #8857 follow-up. 5 State the commands listener, and who marks the subject acting for the person. Decided, maintainer 2026-10-26: the data listener; the tenant owner sets the mark as subject configuration, and the hub reads it. Open: whether more than one subject may hold it. commands §7.1 names no listener; CM14 and CM25 rely on a mark no specification places. 6 Statistics. Decided, maintainer 2026-10-26: v4, statistics, matching Nocturne's reads. Open for discussion: what the shared contract fixes and what each hub keeps; whether compute over a posted body joins later; how reports.read maps onto cgm-remote-monitor's permissions. §6.4. 7 softwareId in registration metadata. Decided, maintainer 2026-10-26: proposed, in Nocturne's software_id form. Open for discussion: whether two products may share one; whether a hub checks it against the credential's registered client. §5; registration §5.1, §18. 8 State the owner boundary per credential in the shared contract, so a one-listener hub can conform. Decided, maintainer 2026-10-26: yes (authority AU7), to be reviewed as the design matures. §4. 9 The data-source listing: data listener or owner's listener. Decided, maintainer 2026-10-26: the owner's listener, with connector configuration: they change or describe the runtime and its resources, differently from an AID controller's registration. Nocturne's /api/v4/services at 42275c812 (Controllers/V4/Platform/ServicesController.cs) mixes reads open to any signed-in credential (class [Authorize], :29; the data-source list :106, connectors, uploader setup) with actions that require the owner atom tenant.settings: deleting a source's data (:321-322), deleting a connector's data (:395-396), a connector sync (:438-439) and a cursor reset (:489-490). Our listing of instances, bindings and overlaps is the owner's (authority §4). 10 Operator actions on a tenant member's credentials. Decided, maintainer 2026-10-26: hub-specific, outside the shared contract; cgm-remote-monitor's operator has none. Nocturne's operator can list and remove a member's passkeys and OIDC identities and issue login and recovery codes (TenantController.cs:186-310); tenant-owner surface §F.1 lists create, list, suspend, activate, delete and export for the operator. 11 Self-service tenant creation. Decided, maintainer 2026-10-26: hub-specific; in cgm-remote-monitor creating a tenant stays the operator's. Nocturne allows it behind AllowSelfServiceCreation (PlatformController.cs:56-66); §F.1 makes tenant creation the operator's. 12 Typed record paths: start from Nocturne's v4 routes or define our own. Deferred, maintainer 2026-10-26, until the identity decisions are settled; the two options are compared, with benchmark criteria B1–B9, in v4-typed-record-paths-comparison-2026-10-27.md. records §3 shares the model; the identity decisions (ID-FORMAT-DECISION and the others in the hub-implementer guide's backlog) decide how a typed write is matched and re-sent. Nocturne issue #1932 (open) records that its v3 POST ignores a client's identifier and never upserts.

docs.title: 8. How this was produced
docs.text:
• Our side: the specifications under spec/, the JSON Schemas under specs/sync/, the tenancy execution plan and the tenant-owner surface, read at 6e6223f26; #8857 read at 3be98536 in a read-only checkout.
  • Nocturne: cloned at 89dcaf1dd into a scratch directory; controllers parsed for [Route], [Http*] and authorization attributes, then read by hand where a row above cites a line. Nocturne issue #2130 (open), "One record-changed seam instead of four write-notification mechanisms", bears on sync-transport T12 and is not used above.
  • The OpenAPI file lints with 0 errors under make openapi-lint (Redocly CLI 1.34.0), which now includes specs/openapi/proposed/; a copy with one broken $ref fails with "Can't resolve $ref".

docs.title: API v4 typed record paths: Nocturne's routes with our rules, or paths of our own
docs.text:
Record

Record as of 2026-10-27. A point-in-time document; it is not kept up to date.

Contributor-facing. Snapshot, 2026-10-27: alignment main ef5bfb426 (specifications), Nocturne main 89dcaf1dd (read in a detached worktree of externals/nocturne, fetched for this page), xDrip+ 1ed760048 (externals/xDrip). Every Nocturne and xDrip+ statement was read from source and nothing was run (read-derived); the API v3 measurements quoted from tools/lab/nocturne-parity are that lab's. Nocturne paths are relative to src/API/Nocturne.API/ unless they begin with Core. (under src/Core/Nocturne.) or Infrastructure. (under src/Infrastructure/Nocturne.Infrastructure.Data/). Operation counts were made by parsing [Http*] attributes and are read-derived. Nothing here has been sent to either project. Supports decision 12 of v4 surface §7.

docs.title: 1. What is being decided
docs.text:
Decision 12 asks whether typed record writes and reads on API v4 start from Nocturne's v4 routes or from paths we define. Records §3 already shares Nocturne's model: its sixteen primitives are Nocturne's V4 classes (records §3). What is not shared is how a typed write is addressed, matched, attributed and re-sent. The maintainer deferred the decision on 2026-10-26 because the identity decisions in the hub-implementer guide's backlog (ID-FORMAT-DECISION, ID-ABSENT-DECISION, ID-SCOPE-DECISION, ID-DELETE-REUSE-DECISION, guide §5) decide how a typed write is matched, and asked for a comparison of two options that can be benchmarked later:

  • Option 1, Nocturne's routes, our rules. Start from Nocturne's typed-record route names and resource shapes, and require our identity rules as behaviour: identifier-first matching, upsert on re-send, an instance id on every typed write.
  • Option 2, paths of our own. Paths built around registration's instance header (registration §11, §12) and records R1–R9, mapped onto Nocturne afterwards.

Option 2 has no paths yet. Where this page needs one to compare, it uses two sketches, labelled 2a (one path per primitive, our names) and 2b (one path addressed by the registered element, <vendor>/<product>/<element>, the channel form of registration §9). They are illustrations for comparison, not proposals.

docs.title: 2.1 Controllers and routes
docs.text:
The v4 surface page's group G3 counts 24 controllers and 182 operations, including health series, Sleep, Battery, DeviceAge, Reservoir*, Foods and MealMatching. The fourteen controllers that carry the record primitives of records §3 declare or inherit 110 operations (parsed: own [Http*] attributes, plus nine inherited per V4CrudControllerBase subclass and two per V4ReadOnlyControllerBase subclass):

controller route base ops SensorGlucoseController api/v4/glucose/sensor (Controllers/V4/Glucose/SensorGlucoseController.cs:34) CRUD 9 BGCheckController api/v4/observations/bg-checks (Glucose/BGCheckController.cs:29) CRUD 9 MeterGlucoseController api/v4/glucose/meter (Glucose/MeterGlucoseController.cs:31) CRUD 9 CalibrationController api/v4/glucose/calibrations (Glucose/CalibrationController.cs:27) CRUD 9 BolusController api/v4/insulin/boluses (Treatments/BolusController.cs:33) CRUD, plus DELETE by-sync-id (:159) 10 BasalInjectionController api/v4/insulin/basal-injections (Treatments/BasalInjectionController.cs:39) CRUD, plus DELETE by-sync-id (:142) 10 BolusCalculationController api/v4/insulin/calculations (Treatments/BolusCalculationController.cs:27) CRUD 9 NoteController api/v4/observations/notes (Treatments/NoteController.cs:28) CRUD, plus DELETE by-sync-id (:76) 10 DeviceEventController api/v4/observations/device-events (Devices/DeviceEventController.cs:39) CRUD, plus DELETE by-sync-id (:181) 10 NutritionController api/v4/nutrition (Treatments/NutritionController.cs:49): carbs, carbs/{id}, carbs/bulk (:154), carbs/by-sync-id (:261), carbs/{id}/foods, meals (:398, :518) hand-written 13 TempBasalController api/v4/insulin/temp-basals (Treatments/TempBasalController.cs:31): list, get, POST an array (:103) hand-written 3 ApsSnapshotController api/v4/device-status/aps (Devices/ApsSnapshotController.cs:28), POST an array (:47) read-only, plus POST 3 PumpSnapshotController api/v4/device-status/pump (Devices/PumpSnapshotController.cs:27), POST an array (:46) read-only, plus POST 3 UploaderSnapshotController api/v4/device-status/uploader (Devices/UploaderSnapshotController.cs:27), POST an array (:46) read-only, plus POST 3

The route pattern is api/v4/<category>/<kebab-case plural>, with three categories in use for primitives (glucose, insulin, observations) and two more for nutrition and device status. The four settings primitives and TherapySettings are under the profile controllers (G5), and StateSpan under api/v4/state-spans (G4); neither is compared here. CarbIntake is nutrition/carbs.

docs.title: 2.2 What the base controllers give
docs.text:
V4ReadOnlyControllerBase (Controllers/V4/Base/V4ReadOnlyControllerBase.cs):

op route notes GetAll GET / (:43, :47) from, to, limit (default 100), offset (default 0), sort (timestamp_desc or timestamp_asc, else 400, :76-77), device, source (:48-51) GetById GET /{id:guid} (:92, :96) 404 when absent

V4CrudControllerBase (Controllers/V4/Base/V4CrudControllerBase.cs) adds seven:

op route notes Create POST / (:85, :92) one record; 201 with Location; a (dataSource, syncIdentifier) held by a record the owner deleted is 409 (:81-83; Filters/RecreationBlockedFilter.cs:36) CreateBulk POST /bulk (:127, :132) at most 1000 (V4BulkValidation.cs:27); "per-item, not all-or-nothing" (:114); 201 with the written records Update PUT /{id:guid} (:162, :169) by hub id; 404 when absent Delete DELETE /{id:guid} (:199, :205) soft delete; 204 or 404 ListDeleted GET /deleted (:228, :233) the recycle bin, gated on the write scope "although it reads" (:223-226) Restore POST /{id:guid}/restore (:255, :262) 409 when a live record now holds the key BulkRestore POST /restore (:287, :293) restored and conflicting ids listed separately

Every write is gated on the controller's declared write scope (:50, WriteScope), and every read on the class-level category scope: glucose.read / glucose.readwrite, treatments.read / treatments.readwrite, devices.read / devices.readwrite (Core.Core.Models/Authorization/Scope.cs:31-39).

docs.title: 2.3 Paging and envelope
docs.text:
A list answers PaginatedResponse<T>: {data, pagination: {limit, offset, total}} (Core.Core.Models/V4/PaginatedResponse.cs:8-27). limit is clamped to 100,000 rather than refused (V4ReadLimits.cs:16-18, :33); a from–to span over 366 days is 400 (:65). Paging is by offset over a timestamp sort. total is counted over from and to only (V4ReadOnlyControllerBase.cs:58), while the page also filters by device and source (:57). Errors are RFC 7807 problem details (Problem(...) throughout, e.g. V4BulkValidation.cs:45).

There is no modified-since read on the typed routes: the list parameters are the seven above, and no v4 typed controller takes a cursor (searched for since, modified, cursor on [FromQuery] under Controllers/V4). Records carry ModifiedAt (Core.Core.Models/V4/IV4Record.cs:97). Change delivery for v4 records is a SignalR broadcast of create, update and delete events per category (Core.Core.Contracts/Events/IV4RecordBroadcaster.cs:15-25). A modified-since read exists for the legacy projection that serves API v3 history (Services/V4/V4ToLegacyProjectionService.cs:113).

docs.title: 2.4 How a write is matched and re-sent
docs.text:
• Hub id. Every record's Id is a hub-assigned UUID v7 (IV4Record.cs:36-39); every by-id route constrains it as {id:guid}.
  • Sync key. The upsert key is (DataSource, SyncIdentifier) within the tenant (Models/Requests/V4/IBulkUpsertRequest.cs:14-18), backed by a partial unique index on (tenant_id, data_source, sync_identifier) (Infrastructure.Repositories/V4/SyncUpsertRepositoryBase.cs:189-191). A bulk item with SyncIdentifier and no DataSource is 400 (V4BulkValidation.cs:89-90). IV4Record itself has no SyncIdentifier member; it is on the types that have one.
  • Which types upsert. Twelve repositories derive from SyncUpsertRepositoryBase: bolus, basal injection, sensor glucose, BG check, note, device event, carb intake, temp basal, the three snapshots and profile activation (parsed from Infrastructure.Repositories/V4/). Calibrations, meter readings and bolus calculations always insert (V4CrudControllerBase.cs:114-119).
  • Single create is an upsert too. CreateAsync is sealed to UpsertAsync (SyncUpsertRepositoryBase.cs:68, :72-101): a matched live row is updated in place. The repository reports whether it inserted (SyncUpsert<T>(Record, Created), Core.Core.Contracts/V4/Repositories/ISyncKeyedRepository.cs:49); the controller answers 201 either way (V4CrudControllerBase.cs:107).
  • Bulk. Items without both halves of the key are never collapsed; within a batch the last item per key wins (SyncUpsertRepositoryBase.cs:168-175). An item whose key is held by a deleted record is skipped and absent from the response; for a one-item array the answer is 201 with an empty array (TempBasalController.cs:91-96 states it for every v4 bulk endpoint). The response is the array of written records; no per-item outcome or match key is returned.
  • A matched upsert moves the record's timestamp to the new one (ISyncKeyedRepository.cs:34-36).
  • Without a key a create inserts. Sensor glucose then runs post-commit deduplication that links rows to canonical groups (Infrastructure.Repositories/V4/SensorGlucoseRepository.cs:473-478).
  • Update by id maps the whole record. BolusController takes SyncIdentifier from the request (Treatments/BolusController.cs:129); SensorGlucoseController keeps the stored one (Glucose/SensorGlucoseController.cs:144).

docs.title: 2.5 Deletes and tombstones
docs.text: Deletes are soft. A deleted record holds its sync key: a re-create is 409 on the single path and skipped on the bulk path, and the owner brings it back with Restore (V4CrudControllerBase.cs:81-83, :255). Five types also delete by sync key with dataSource and syncIdentifier as query parameters (§2.1). TempBasal and the three snapshots have no v4 delete or update. On the v3 history projection a deleted treatment is served with isValid: false (Services/V4/LegacyTreatmentTables.cs:953-954).

docs.title: 2.6 How a record names its writer
docs.text: The record carries three client-supplied strings: Device, App and DataSource (IV4Record.cs:60-73); the request maps them from the body (BolusController.cs:91-93). The authenticated subject, token id and auth type go to the mutation audit log, not to the record (Core.Core.Contracts/Audit/IAuditContext.cs:9-13). Device attribution (PatientDeviceAttribution, BolusController.cs:149-151) links a record to a patient device; the snapshots are not attributed (ApsSnapshotController.cs:43-45).

docs.title: 2.7 Decomposition and projection
docs.text: API v1–v3 treatment writes reach the typed tables through the decomposers. A treatment's identity is its _id, else its syncIdentifier, else a hash of its defining fields (Services/V4/TreatmentDecomposer.cs:130-159). Reads of v1–v3 treatments are projected from typed records: "every treatment read projects records of both provenances, since treatments have no legacy table left" (V4ToLegacyProjectionService.cs:29). A projected treatment's id is the typed record's UUID as a string (LegacyTreatmentTables.cs:961) and it carries syncIdentifier (:978). Whether a v1–v3 write aimed at a projected treatment is refused or edits the typed record was not checked.

docs.title: 2.8 A client written against these routes
docs.text:
xDrip+ 1ed760048 has a Nocturne uploader (app/src/main/java/com/eveningoutpost/dexdrip/nocturne/NocturneUploader.java, 717 lines; NocturneOAuthService.java, 454) built on a generated SDK, org.nightscoutfoundation:nocturne-java:0.2.4 (app/build.gradle:281). Read from it:

  • DATA_SOURCE = "xdrip" for treatments (:76); sensor glucose sends the collection method preference as dataSource (:484) and no syncIdentifier (:476-492), so its readings carry no sync key.
  • A treatment with several doses uploads under suffixed sync identifiers, uuid, uuid-2, … (:686-687).
  • A delete tries four resources by sync key in turn, because "a treatment's uuid may exist in any of these resources" (:324-341); its comment says basal injections have no delete by sync key "yet (pending upstream)" (:329-330), which 89dcaf1dd now has (BasalInjectionController.cs:142).

docs.title: 3. What our specifications require of a typed write and read
docs.text:
concern requirement anchor instance id a hub that advertises instances requires an instance id on every typed write, proposed as a request header; without one, 422 instance-required, a definite refusal; the instance must be live (409 not-live) and hold source on the element's channel (409 role-held / role-not-granted) registration §11 attribution an accepted typed record carries its instance, definition and the role's provenance; writes with no instance go to an implicit unregistered instance of the product; a namespace string proves nothing registration §11; §9 two ids identifier is the controller's record id in the typed API; _id is the hub's identity I1 reply every write answers per item identifier, _id and matchedBy; on a typed write this is write.ids; a duplicate is never a 5xx or an empty acknowledgement identity I4 re-send matches on identifier first; a matched re-send stores no second copy and answers with the stored ids, so a client keeps no cache of server ids identity I5, I6 match scope a typed write matches a stored typed record of the same (vendor, product) with the same identifier, whichever instance sent it identity I7; the typed index on (vendor, product, identifier), guide §5 identifier form opaque, URL syntax, source and app schemes; C1–C7 proposed (256 characters, A-Z a-z 0-9 - . _ ~ : /) identity §4; identifier conventions §2 identifier mandatory for registered instances and at a future version boundary identifier conventions §1 decision 1 one write step every path writes through one step with outcomes inserted, merged, replaced, unchanged, deleted, not-found, refused sync-transport T1–T2 batch POST /api/v3/batch takes [{collection, doc}], answered per item, idempotent per record (proposed; typed batch not specified) sync-transport T7 sync read one history read across collections with an opaque cursor and a low watermark; a page carries the definitions its records need sync-transport T5, T6, T8, T9, T14 socket subscribe by product and channel; each event carries the record, both ids, definition, instance, provenance and the cursor sync-transport T11 versions a stored record keeps its definitionId; a re-send under a new definition with the same identifier replaces it sync-transport T13, T15 read selection per versioned element: capability limit, owner's pin, newest version run by a live device source, newest stored; a label selector narrows to matching instances registration §12 projected views a served element is projected to v1 and v3 as a carrier-shaped document labelled projectedFrom, read-only (409 projected-read-only), with an ObjectId _id assigned at the typed write registration §13; identity I8 composite on the wire the hub keeps the composite and decomposes it into primitives; decomposition is declared by the registration records R1–R3 permissions our specifications name api:registrations:* and api:commands:create; no permission name for a typed write authority (searched)

The proposed OpenAPI file lists no typed record operation (specs/openapi/proposed/nightscout-v4.yaml, info.description). The conformance cases model a typed write without a path: identity (vendor, product), write.element (stateSpans/ExampleOverride), write.instanceId and recordId (specs/sync/conformance/instances/typed-write-attributed.yaml; specs/sync/conformance/quirks/typed-write-resend-same-ids.yaml). Either option can be bound to them.

docs.title: 4. Side by side
docs.text:
"Cost" is the work the option leaves for our specifications, cgm-remote-monitor, or a shared contract; "compatibility" is what a client of the other hub sees.

concern Option 1: Nocturne's routes, our rules Option 2: paths of our own compatibility consequence path shape fixed: api/v4/<category>/<plural>, fourteen roots for the primitives (§2.1), two write forms (POST / + POST /bulk, or POST / taking an array) free: 2a one root per primitive; 2b one root per registered element; either can be advertised in the capability document as commands' fetch is (a URI template, registration §4) Option 1: a client written for Nocturne (xDrip+ §2.8) reaches both hubs on the same paths; Option 2: needs an alias table or a discovered template on one side resource naming Nocturne's names (bg-checks, meter, calculations, device-status/aps); CarbIntake is nutrition/carbs records §3's primitive names, or element ids records §3 already uses Nocturne's class names, so 2a can match names without matching categories coverage beyond primitives none for controller-owned extensions or versioned kinds: Nocturne's types are a closed set 2b addresses any accepted element, including extensions (registration §3, G2, G4) Option 1 needs a second path family for extensions; 2b has one family for both create and upsert Nocturne already upserts on a key for twelve types (§2.4); the rule to change is the key (identifier-first, I5) and the three types that always insert specify once: every typed create is an upsert on identifier (I5, I7) under Option 1 the same route has two match rules on two hubs until both agree; a test fixture that passes on one can fail on the other per-item reply Nocturne answers records, 201 always, skipped items absent (§2.4); our I4 needs identifier, _id, matchedBy per item write.ids per item from the start (I4) Option 1 changes the response body of existing Nocturne routes, or adds a header/field next to it; xDrip+ ignores the body of its bulk call (NocturneUploader.java:195) batch per type, POST …/bulk, 1000 items; a mixed cycle is one request per type can be per type or one typed batch across types (as T7 does for v3) round trips per cycle differ (benchmark B3) identity match key becomes identifier within (vendor, product); DataSource is a body string today and half of Nocturne's key key is (vendor, product, identifier) (guide §5) Option 1 must say which wins when the body's dataSource and the instance's product disagree (§7, Q3) writer attribution add the instance header to routes whose bodies already carry device, app, dataSource the instance header is the attribution; body strings are data under both, a client that sends no header is the product's unregistered instance (registration §11); Option 1 keeps three body strings that registration says prove nothing hub id {id:guid}, UUID v7 the hub's _id; identity I2–I3 fix 24-hex only on legacy surfaces, so v4 may use another form a by-id route works only with the id that hub assigned; I5 makes that rare for a sync client read by identifier Nocturne reads by sync key only through delete; a by-identifier read needs a new route or a query parameter (identifier is not a GUID) define it; identifiers with / and : go percent-encoded as one segment (C3), or as a query parameter as Nocturne's by-sync-id does a query parameter avoids proxies that refuse %2F, which were not measured (conventions §2) read, query, paging from, to, limit, offset, sort, device, source; {data, pagination}; offset paging, total open; T6's cursor rules exist for history a shared list contract has to settle the envelope either way; v3 already differs between the two hubs (lab question 2) read selection no slot for a definition or version; §12's choice would be a query parameter or header built in: element and version are part of the address (2b) or the query (2a) without it, a reader of a versioned element on Option 1 sees whatever was stored last deletes and tombstones Nocturne: soft delete, deleted key refused on re-create, recycle bin and restore (§2.5); five types also delete by key ID-DELETE-REUSE-DECISION is open; cgm-remote-monitor v3 resurrects a soft-deleted record on POST (identity §5) adopting the routes brings Nocturne's answer (refuse) with them, which is one of the three options the decision lists sync no modified-since or cursor on typed routes; SignalR events; history only through the v3 projection (§2.3) T5–T10 and T14 apply to typed records by design under Option 1 a typed-record cursor is new on both hubs; under Option 2 it is new on Nocturne projection to v1–v3 both hubs project typed records to v1–v3; Nocturne's projected id is the record's UUID (LegacyTreatmentTables.cs:961), ours is an ObjectId assigned at the typed write (I8) with projectedFrom and 409 projected-read-only the same rules; path choice does not change them a legacy client sees a 36-character _id on one hub and a 24-hex one on the other under either option (v1 by-id routes understand UUID and ObjectId shapes, conventions §2) auth scopes three category scopes per direction (glucose, treatments, devices) unnamed today; cgm-remote-monitor's permissions are api:<collection>:<action> a shared contract needs a mapping table under either option; Option 1 makes Nocturne's categories the grouping

docs.title: 5.1 A client
docs.text:
client today Option 1 Option 2 Loop (NightscoutKit 4ec9fd12a1, v1, 7 endpoints) and Trio (0b29cd5341, v1, 5 endpoints), per sync-transport §3 adopt Nocturne's per-type routes, send identifier (the conventions table gives loop://… templates) and the instance header; one request per type per cycle, or the bulk route per type adopt our paths; the same identifier and header; one request per type (2a) or per element (2b), or one batch if a typed batch is specified AndroidAPS (7e1d537d49, v3, 26 endpoints, delta read per collection) as above; its delta reads have no typed equivalent on either hub yet (§2.3) as above, with T5/T6 for reads once served xDrip+ (1ed760048): a Nightscout uploader and a separate Nocturne v4 uploader (§2.8) its Nocturne uploader works on both hubs once cgm-remote-monitor serves the routes; it adds syncIdentifier → identifier, the instance header, and a sync key for readings, which it does not send today it keeps one uploader per hub until Nocturne serves our paths or an alias

Under both options a client registers its product and instance first (registration §5, §8) and reads the capability document at launch. Under both, the identifier convention it follows is the same table; neither option changes what the identifier is.

docs.title: 5.2 A hub implementer
docs.text:
• cgm-remote-monitor, Option 1. Serve Nocturne's route set for the primitives (110 operations on fourteen controllers by the parse in §2.1, or a declared subset), with its envelope and paging, behind S3's checks (guide §4.4). The extension path family and read selection are designed separately.
  • cgm-remote-monitor, Option 2. Serve our paths behind the same S3 checks. Nocturne compatibility, if wanted, is an alias layer from Nocturne's routes onto ours.
  • Nocturne, Option 1. Its routes stay. Behaviour changes: identifier-first matching with (vendor, product) scope, a per-item reply, an instance header, a typed-record cursor; the three always-insert types upsert. Issue #1932 (open since 2026-09-30) records the same identifier and upsert question for its API v3 POST.
  • Nocturne, Option 2. Serve our paths beside its own, mapped onto the same repositories; the behaviour changes above apply to the new paths.
