docs.title: WC-STEP-PATCH: mapping the write step onto dev db3b9e4e
docs.text:
Record

Record as of 2026-10-27. A point-in-time document; it is not kept up to date.

Contributor-facing design note, milestone 1 of WC-STEP-PATCH (decision Q6 (a), first release: the step with today's write matrix pinned, no behaviour change). Written 2026-10-27 against cgm-remote-monitor official/dev db3b9e4e (the merge of #8872). Every claim carries a mark: [M] measured in this milestone (commands in §7), [R] read from source at db3b9e4e, not run. file:line is at db3b9e4e unless it names the branch feat/write-intent.

The specification is docs/30-design/tenancy/write-contract-spec-2026-10-07.md (§2 the step, §5 gates, §6.1 decisions). It was written against 43289dde, before the storage seam landed. This note says where its pieces are now, and what the step has to do on the code as it is.

docs.title: 0. The rule, and the gate that holds it
docs.text:
Decided 2026-10-27 (maintainer): a new write rule goes into lib/storage/write-intent.js, not into a route. This applies from now on, before every collection is enrolled. §3 below lists the copies that already exist outside any step; the slices move them in.

Two gates hold it:

  • G2 (scripts/check-write-intent.js on the branch): an enrolled module writes only through write(intent). Its coverage grows as each slice enrols a module.
  • Write-rule copies (tools/queue/gates/write-rule-copies.js, control write-rule-copies-control.sh): for seven rule modules (merge-patch, the BF-194 units helper, write-validation, validated-update, srv-dates, object-id-forms, the treatment fallback key), it counts the lines in each other file under lib/ and bin/ that use the rule. It fails on a new (rule, file) pair or a grown count against write-rule-copies.baseline.json. The baseline was measured on dev db3b9e4e: 47 pairs. On feat/write-intent (slice 1) it reads 45: food's srv-dates and object-id-forms copies are gone. The count can only go down; the baseline is re-written after a slice moves a copy into the step, never to make a failure pass.

Progress, 2026-10-27 late. Slices 1-3 are built on local feat/write-intent (2b9d3687, 84e21a66, f0d51ee7, a0e7fcac), each with G1 at 0 of 360 cells. The slice list below is revised: slice 3 covers the socket's generic dbAdd (entries, food, activity) and dbRemove (all six); a new slice 6 takes the socket's dbAdd for treatments, devicestatus and profile (the near match, WRITE_VALIDATION, BF-194, the refused/failed slots) plus dbUpdate/dbUpdateUnset, retiring idMatch (new question Q-I: until then the step's id-match duplicates it). Matrix gaps found: no form PUTs over a stored string twin, reads an _id that fails, or removes by a custom or numeric _id; those are covered by unit tests only.

Release-1 answers (maintainer, 2026-10-27). For release 1 (Q6 (a): no behaviour change), Q-A to Q-I are answered "keep today's behaviour, unify in release 2": the step encodes each path's current way as data, and G1 proves nothing moved. Each becomes a deliberate change, with its own decision, in release 2. Slice 5 proceeds; slices 4 (v3) and 6 (the socket's treatment handling and updates) are held until the maintainer has reviewed the explanation of the questions.

Progress, 2026-10-28. Slice 5 is built: treatments, entries, devicestatus and profile on API v1 and in-process (5d97fb59, 869a7de1, 6115c755, daaa3db9), plus 0671b430 marking every release-2 variant in the rule table. G1 holds on both pins (on v2, only the two racy cache cells differ). The step gained plan() (synchronous rules at the moment the module ran them, so a bad eventTime still throws) and check() (WRITE_VALIDATION); treatments create has three forms (batch, one, prebolus); entries and treatments share one _id rule (they were identical). New questions for release 2: Q-J (a re-send not written is refused for devicestatus, unchanged for profile), Q-K (keep plan()'s synchronous throws, or make every rule error an asynchronous refusal), Q-L (devicestatus on v1 has no natural key), Q-M (the treatments fallback key reads created_at two ways), Q-N (the shared _id rule), Q-O (devicestatus inserts unordered, profile ordered), Q-P (does an authorization input, canUpdate, belong in an intent).

Maintainer, 2026-10-29. Slices 4 and 6 are released. Slice 6 has an extra gate, because its rules decide whether a treatment is a duplicate (websocket.js:743-860): a wrong move would drop a real second bolus or carb entry, or store a re-send twice. Each rule needs a fixture that keeps today's result and an ablation that goes red: exact NSCLIENT_ID and fallback-key (BF-121) match, the 2-second similar match at its edges, each BF-09 zero case, a different eventType being a second record, soft-deleted records never matching, the similar match setting only created_at and srvModified, and WRITE_VALIDATION reply slots. Any difference is stop-and-report. On slice 4: as built, it keeps v3 writing by identifier through the cached wrapper (mongoCachedCollection), which updates or removes only the record written, so it adds no cache flush and no MongoDB load. Q-A for release 2 is open, with research continuing, on the maintainer's proposal: instead of the full flush a query-based write causes today (a remove with no ids empties all three caches, lib/server/cache.js), the step would read the collection back from a srvModified watermark. This rests on three things on dev. Every server write path stamps srvModified (since 718efddc, in 15.0.9). srv-dates.js issues those values in increasing order. Every v3 collection indexes the field (mongoCollection/index.js:147-150). The record's own time (date, created_at) cannot serve as the watermark: it is the event time a client set, so late uploads, edits and future-dated clocks would be missed. Hard deletes leave nothing for the watermark to find, so they keep reading ids before the delete. Single-tenant Nightscout supports writes to MongoDB only through its own APIs (maintainer, 2026-10-29), so every write the catch-up must see carries srvModified. A since-watermark arm is to be added to the D-EVENT bench (tools/lab/commit-event-bench).

Progress, 2026-10-29: slice 4 is built (local feat/write-intent-s4: 00f93946 rule table, 3cad3508 v3 through write(intent)). v3 uses only the cached wrapper's identifier methods (insertOne, replaceOne, updateOne, updateEveryForm, deleteEveryForm). Server dates, BF-194 units, subject/modifiedBy, duration, the merge patch and the write calls moved into the step. Permissions, validation, the identifying read, acknowledge.js, HTTP shaping, storage-socket emissions and autoPrune stayed in the modules; writeFilter's twin choice stayed below the interface. G1 shows 0 of 360 cells differing, and the commit-event copy 0. npm test gives 4960/0/3 (+41). Each ablation goes red only in v3 cells; four breaks the matrix cannot see are caught by the unit tests. Cache emissions are unchanged. A control that swaps in a query-based method turns them into remove (reload), and its reach extends to socket cells in three collections. Rule copies fell from 37 to 28. New release-2 questions: - Q-S: a v3 delete reaches every stored form, while PUT/PATCH write the one writeFilter picks. - Q-T: the intent carries the authenticated subject (by); compare Q-P. - Q-U: autoPrune (collection.js:158, deleteManyOr) is a query-based v3 delete outside the step. It is a candidate for Q-A's watermark catch-up.

Progress, 2026-10-29: slice 6 is built, and #8874 is push-ready. Slice 6 is local feat/write-intent-s6 82dd0c83: the dedupe gate a9cfa83f, the rule table 9babbbeb, then dbAdd, dbUpdate and dbUpdateUnset through write(intent) in 7b145960, plus a guard 82dd0c83. G1 shows 0 of 360 cells. npm test gives 5097/0/3. No dedupe fixture changed, and all 40 dedupe ablations, re-targeted at the step, go red as before. idMatch is gone (Q-I closed). Rule copies fell from 28 to 23. The push-ready head is feat/write-intent-release e8224807: slices 1 to 6, merged with dev e1f7ac41. It gives npm test 5106/0/3 against dev's 4759/0/3, the matrix and the commit-event copy differ in 0 cells from dev, and a rehearsed revert restores dev's tree exactly. New release-2 questions: - Q-V: dbUpdate by a hex _id writes every stored form but announces only one. - Q-W: BF-194's unit conversion runs in the socket's check but in v1's write. Putting it in one place changes either the socket's reply slots or v1's order of validation. - Q-X: dbUpdate of a record that does not exist replies success. The step knows it found nothing. - Q-Y: prepareDbAddDocument's defaults (eventType <none>, created_at now) stay outside the step, so a re-send without created_at can never exact-match.

Cache lab, 2026-10-29 (tools/lab/cache-value, dev e1f7ac41; 3 real hours, 5 parallel arms). The cache cuts bytes returned by MongoDB about 32 times: 2.0 MB an hour against 63.9 MB bypassed. Operations barely change. Without the cache, the modelled site exceeds MongoDB Atlas M0's published transfer limit of 10 GB per 7 days; with it, the site uses 3.3 to 3.7 % of that limit. Pool size 5 against 100 made no latency difference. This supports keeping the cache for single (D4), and it makes Q-A's watermark catch-up, which avoids full reloads, worth building. The lab also reproduced the over-broad flush, BF-211.

Slice 6 dedupe gate, 2026-10-29. Session -4f's gate (test/ws-dedupe fe1aee82, 58 tests, an ablation per rule) pins today's socket behaviour and found four differences from the rule list. They were re-run on v15.0.9 c6a0d8ed. 1. The similar match ignores client identity apart from NSCLIENT_ID (same on 15.0.9). Filed as BF-209. The maintainer asked for it to be fixed for the pending release candidate, so the gate's fixtures for it change deliberately when the fix lands. 2. In reject mode, a similar-matched temp target stores durationInMilliseconds and endmills, and the reply omits them (dev only): Q-Q, release 2. 3. A soft-deleted profile is matched, and so revived, by a socket dbAdd with the same NSCLIENT_ID or startDate (same on 15.0.9): Q-R, release 2. Measured on dev e1f7ac41 with an AndroidAPS-shaped profile (AndroidAPS 3.4.2.6's v1 NSClient sends startDate, never NSCLIENT_ID). It is reachable only by a sequence no app was found to start. The profile must be soft-deleted through API v3 (the profile editor and every v1 path delete hard, and no client in the corpus calls the v3 profile delete). After that, no local edit, and then an NSClient full sync, a database reset or a lost acknowledgement. 4. An amount field the write does not carry is not part of the match (same on 15.0.9). Filed as BF-210, then withdrawn by the maintainer the same day as not a defect: absorbing a nearby matching upload is intended, and treating a missing amount as none would double-count a carbs-only re-send. Meal grouping belongs in the display layer.

A side finding: the chart-drag split (treatmenttime.js splitRecord) keeps the original's client identity on the new half. This is reproduced on dev e1f7ac41 (probe probe/split-ident-2026-10-29 95570d41, local, with a control). Two stored records then share one syncIdentifier or identifier. API v3 lookups and dedupe resolve to the new half. A v1 upsert by identifier replaces the original but replies with the new half's _id. Separately, and also with the identity removed: a full re-upload of the original by the client that still holds it writes the moved insulin back, so the insulin appears twice. Not run on 15.0.9. The maintainer's direction: editing is mainly for fixing broken records, so a lossy edit of a record that an automated controller claims (one with a client identity) should need an extra manual confirmation. Filed as BF-212 in the backfix register.

docs.title: 1. Placement: two layers, not one
docs.text:
The spec (§2.1) puts write(intent) in lib/storage/write-step.js, "applied in collectionFor above both adapters". On db3b9e4e that file name is taken by a different layer, and collectionFor does not exist.

What exists [R]:

 lib/server/{entries,treatments,devicestatus,profile,food,activity}.js   (API v1 + in-process)
 lib/server/websocket.js  dbAdd / dbUpdate / dbUpdateUnset / dbRemove      (socket)
 lib/api3/generic/{create,update,patch,delete}                             (API v3)
          |                                   |
          |  lib/server/storage-writes.js     |  lib/api3/storage/mongoCachedCollection
          |  (v1 query doc -> filter AST)     |  (cache events, then delegates)
          v                                   v
 lib/api3/storage/mongoCollection  = THE STORAGE INTERFACE (one per collection and source label)
   writes: insertOne, insertMany, replaceOne(identifier), updateOne(identifier), deleteOne,
           updateEveryForm, deleteEveryForm, deleteManyOr, deleteMany(ast), updateMany(ast),
           replaceFiltered(ast), bulkUpsert(ops)
          |
          v
 lib/storage/write-step.js  = THE PERSISTENCE BOUNDARY: a Proxy over the driver collection;
   one driver call -> one `storage-write-committed` event; socket treatment validation;
   the conditional validated update (compare-and-set) for treatments in reject mode
          |
          v
 MongoDB driver collection
  • The storage interface is MongoCollection (lib/api3/storage/mongoCollection/index.js:20-101). Its writes are listed at index.js:68-100; each is handed col, the write-step proxy (index.js:43). API v1 and the socket acquire it through lib/server/storage-reads.js:34-37 with a source label (MongoCollection.SOURCES, index.js:140-145: v1/internal, v3, socket, internal). API v3 reaches it through mongoCachedCollection (lib/api3/storage/mongoCachedCollection/index.js:10-159), which adds cache data-update emissions around the same methods. [R]
  • lib/storage/write-step.js is below the interface: collection() (write-step.js:96-107) wraps the driver collection; write() (write-step.js:70-94) makes one driver call and publish() (write-step.js:57-68) emits storage-write-committed once per call. [R]
  • The next-gen plan already records the naming decision: "the intent layer gets its own name" (next-gen-platform-plan.md:45) [R].

So the step is a second layer, above the interface. In feat/write-intent it is lib/storage/write-intent.js. It calls only storage-interface methods, never the driver, and it emits nothing; the commit event stays exactly where #8854 put it. Nothing in this milestone changes write-step.js or the event (D-EVENT is deferred, and session -2e's crm-devent-* trees prototype that change).

Adapter methods the step calls, against the spec's seam list (§2.1: findFiltered, insertMany, bulkUpsert, replaceFiltered, updateMany, deleteMany) [R]:

path today interface methods it writes with in the seam list? v1 / in-process (via storage-writes.js:21-70) bulkUpsert, replaceFiltered, updateMany, deleteMany, insertMany (devicestatus devicestatus.js:196, profile profile.js:153) yes socket (websocket.js) insertOne (websocket.js:784-787), updateMany and replaceFiltered and deleteMany via storage-writes insertOne is not API v3 (api3/generic/*) insertOne, replaceOne(identifier), updateOne(identifier), updateEveryForm, deleteEveryForm (create/insert.js:40, update/replace.js:46, patch/operation.js:116, delete/operation.js:60,87), all through the cached wrapper none of these

Slice 1 (food, v1/in-process) calls findFiltered (through srv-dates carryForReplace), bulkUpsert and deleteMany: all in the seam list. Bringing the socket and v3 paths in either keeps two method families under the step, or re-expresses v3's identifier-addressed writes as filter writes, which changes the driver calls and, for v3, the cache events of mongoCachedCollection (its five filter methods reload the whole cache, index.js:147-159). That is question Q-A (§5).

docs.title: 2. Where each rule of §2.3 lives today
docs.text:
Paths: v1 (API v1 routes), in (in-process callers: the same lib/server/<col>.js module as v1, under the same v1/internal label), ws (socket), v3. All [R].

Rule 1, _id form. - v1/in: object-id-forms.js helpers per module: food create toStoredId (food.js:59-64), food save new ObjectId(id) falling back to a fresh one (food.js:28-34,126), activity the same pair (activity.js:18-24,51,100), treatments normalizeTreatmentId (treatments.js:530-560), entries normalizeEntryId (entries.js:505-525), devicestatus toStoredId (devicestatus.js:89), profile toStoredId (profile.js:137). - ws: storeIdAsObjectId (websocket.js:773-780), keeps an existing string form. - v3: refuses a client _id with 400 (opTools.refuseClientId, create/operation.js:36; BF-170).

Rule 2, target resolution (natural key, twins). - v1/in: treatments upsertQueryFor identifier -> _id -> fallback key (treatments.js:494-517); entries sysTime+type (entries.js:460-478) plus identifier match (entries.js:187-203); devicestatus identifier rule (devicestatus.js:105-148) then stored _id (devicestatus.js:62-96); profile stored _id (storedByKey, profile.js:54, used at profile.js:115-127); food and activity by _id only, as an upsert filter (food.js:65, activity.js:52). - ws: treatments NSCLIENT_ID or fallback key (websocket.js:800-822) then the +-2 s similar match (websocket.js:824-873); devicestatus NSCLIENT_ID or created_at (websocket.js:910-930); profile NSCLIENT_ID or startDate (websocket.js:954-985); entries, food, activity: none, a plain insert (websocket.js:1008-1030). - v3: identifyingFilter + findOneFilter (create/operation.js:47-49), dedup fallback fields per collection. - Twins: v1 food/activity/treatments-batch append one deleteMany of string forms after all replaces in one ordered bulk write (object-id-forms.js:131-137); treatments/profile/activity save make a separate remove call after the replace (treatments.js:426, profile.js:211, activity.js:107); v3 sorts the ObjectId copy first and writes only it (modify.js:46-52).

Rule 3, outcome. Not computed anywhere as a value. Each path infers it from what it did: v1 food/activity/treatments from bulkUpsert's upsertedIds (food.js:88-92); devicestatus and profile from their match step; ws from which branch ran; v3 from result.length (create/operation.js:54-64) and acknowledge.applies for devicestatus (acknowledge.js:31-49). v3's immutable-field check (update/validate.js:28-100) is the only refused-style outcome besides WRITE_VALIDATION.

Rule 4, server dates (srv-dates.js). v1/in: carryForReplace (food.js:21, treatments.js:172,266,316,423, profile.js:208), stampCreated (devicestatus.js:190, profile.js:152), stampModified + $setOnInsert srvCreated (entries.js:153-160); activity none. ws: stampCreated / stampModified / carry per handler (websocket.js:477-481, 598-604, 868, 889, 933, 969, 988, 1010). v3: srvDates.next() in insert.js:32, replace.js:32, patch/operation.js:90, delete/operation.js:81.

Rule 5, adapter write and twin removal. Covered under rule 2; every write reaches the driver through write-step.js:70-94.

Rule 6, one change event. There is no step-level change event. What exists: per-path data-update emissions (15 write-side processRawDataForRuntime calls in treatments.js, entries.js, devicestatus.js, websocket.js; the cached wrapper's forCache, mongoCachedCollection/index.js:184-200); v3's storage-socket-* emissions (insert.js:55, replace.js:67, patch/operation.js:125, delete/operation.js:70,96); per-path data-received; and, below the interface, storage-write-committed once per driver call. v1 food and activity emit no data-update at all [M: the baseline matrix, food and activity v1/in columns, ev –].

docs.title: 3. What of §2/§3/§6.1 is already on dev

docs.title: 4. Proposed slicing
docs.text:
Every slice holds G1 (the matrix equals the pinned file, apart from the known racy cache field) and npm test equal to baseline plus its own tests, and runs node scripts/test-tiers.js check: a new test file is in no tier until tests/tiers.json names it, and test:all then silently skips it (slice 1 hit this; fixed in 84e21a66). Every slice that moves a rule re-targets the matching ablation of write-contract-ablate.sh at the step and shows it red.

  1. Slice 1 (built, feat/write-intent): food, API v1 + in-process. write(intent) and WriteResult.items[] in lib/storage/write-intent.js; lib/server/food.js writes only through it. Rules moved: _id form (both of today's spellings, create and save), target by _id, carryForReplace server dates, string-twin removal, the bulkUpsert/deleteMany call. COLLECTION_RULES is keyed by collection and source label, holding today's per-path rules (not the spec's §2.2 target table, which is release 2). G2 check scripts/check-write-intent.js with ENROLLED = ['lib/server/food.js']. Why not food on every path: the socket handlers (websocket.js:449-1078) and v3 operations (api3/generic/*) are collection-generic; enrolling one collection there means a per-collection branch inside shared code, which is a bigger and riskier diff than the shape needs to be proven. Those come as path slices.
  2. Slice 2: activity, v1 + in-process (activity.js is food's twin minus server dates: create = food create, save = replaceFiltered + separate twin remove activity.js:100-108). Exercises a second source of twin-removal timing (separate call vs appended op) as data.
  3. Slice 3: socket dbRemove and generic dbAdd for entries/food/activity (one path, the generic branch websocket.js:1008-1030 and 1038-1076): the step's first refused outcome (a duplicate _id insert answers [] today, C6) and its first non-seam method (insertOne).
  4. Slice 4: API v3 generic create/update/patch/delete, every v3 collection at once (one code path), after Q-A is answered.
  5. Slices 5-8: treatments, entries, devicestatus, profile on v1/in, one per PR, each with its own matching rules and data-update emissions; then the socket's per-collection branches.
  6. Last: rule 6, the one change event, only after D-EVENT, since it is where the step would start to carry WriteResult.items[] into an event (ST-EVENT).

docs.title: 5. Contradictions and open questions for the maintainer
docs.text:
The step has to pick a side on each of these. Picking would change a matrix cell or an emission in every case marked (cell), so none is picked here; slice 1 keeps each path as it is.

  • Q-A, two method families. The spec's step calls only filter methods (§2.1); v3 writes by identifier through the cached wrapper (table in §1). Re-expressing v3 as filter writes changes the driver calls and the cache behaviour (the wrapper reloads the whole cache after any filter write, mongoCachedCollection/index.js:147-159) (emission: data-update changes from update with docs to remove with no changes). Keep both families under the step for release 1, or accept the cache change?
  • Q-B, twin removal timing. Spec rule 5: "directly after the write it belongs to (BF-130)". Code: food, activity create and treatments batches append one deleteMany after all replaces in the same ordered bulk write; treatments/profile/activity save make a separate driver call. Unifying changes the number of storage-write-committed events per request (not a matrix cell, but an emission the brief forbids changing). Which form is the rule?
  • Q-C, v1 and in-process share one label. The spec's origin.path distinguishes v1 and internal; on dev both write as v1/internal (index.js:140-145) through the same module, and the module cannot tell them apart. Is that distinction needed before release 2? Adding it changes the commit event's source value (D-EVENT territory).
  • Q-D, _id rule on a PUT/save with a non-hex id (cell, in-process only). v1/in-process food and activity save turn a non-hex _id into a fresh ObjectId (food.js:28-34), i.e. a "save" of a custom-id record inserts a new record; create keeps the custom id (toStoredId). The spec's rule 1 says a non-hex string keeps today's per-collection rule; the per-op difference inside one collection is not mentioned. The v1 route refuses non-hex ids with 400 before this (api/food/index.js:92-96), so only in-process callers reach it. Slice 1 keeps both spellings as named rules (objectid-or-new, stored-or-new).
  • Q-E, identical re-send outcome (cell). Q2 decided (b1) "status quo per path". In the step's vocabulary, today's v1 food re-send is replaced (srvModified advances, [M] baseline food v1 resend-hex C=M+), the socket's is a refused insert (empty, C=M=), v3's is 400 (BF-170). Slice 1 labels the v1 one replaced. Confirm that unchanged is reserved for release 2 and that labelling today's no-ops does not count as a behaviour change.
  • Q-F, WRITE_VALIDATION has two homes. The plan row says validation moves into the step; part of it already sits below the interface (write-step.js:27-42, the conditional update at write-step.js:79-86), and moving it up would move code out of the file whose publish() the D-EVENT prototypes rewrite. Should validation's lower half stay in the persistence boundary (it is the compare-and-set), with only the above-interface checks (treatments.js:43-58, websocket.js:685, operationTools.js:100-112) moving into the step?
  • Q-G, the spec's §1.3 table is stale. Against the spec's own result file (tools/qc/results/write-contract-matrix/dev-43289dde.json) the db3b9e4e baseline differs in 65 cells [M] (BF-170's v3 400s, #8859's profile merge, devicestatus identifier rule, BF-194, and MongoDB 7 vs 8 under the harness). G1 for this work pins db3b9e4e, not the spec's file; the spec's tables should be re-generated before release 2 decisions cite them.
  • Q-H, the step's name for "create" on v1. v1 POST for food and activity is an upserting replace by _id, not a create; treatments' is a replace by natural key. The intent says create; the rule table says onMatch: replaced. The spec's create + near vocabulary fits; noting only that create on v1 has always been allowed to replace.

docs.title: 6. What the matrix does not see
docs.text:
• storage-write-committed: the upstream harness taps only data-update and storage-socket-*. This milestone ran a scratch copy of the harness that also records every commit event per cell (field commit) [M], so the event's count, source, operation and counts are part of the G1 comparison for slice 1.
  • The order of driver calls and their exact arguments: covered for slice 1 by a unit test that runs the pre-move food.js logic and the step over the same recording driver and compares the calls and the commit events (tests/write-intent.test.js).

Not vacuous; the script's lists need the TT cells, or --no-tt.

docs.title: Add a setting in your controller's next release: declare it typed, submit it, fall back, write it and read it back
docs.text:
Living document, last changed 2026-10-18 at 5a47b91eb.

Contributor-facing. Living guide, current at main 127f69e1 (2026-10-18). Uses the platform specifications; terms are in the glossary. Status: the specifications are proposed and not implemented; until HUB-REG-CRM is, each step is checked against its conformance case, not run against a hub.

For a Loop, Trio or other controller developer who adds a setting or feature in a release and wants a Nightscout hub to store and show it typed. Expect the decisions to make before writing code, a walk-through in three tables (declare and submit, write and read back, the release after), what older hubs and older readers see, a checklist, and the steps no case covers.

docs.title: 1. What you will have at the end
docs.text: Your release declares the setting in a controller-owned registration, submits it to any hub that takes submissions, and learns element by element what the hub accepted. For each accepted element it writes typed records, attributed to the running copy of your app and to the definition they were written under. For everything else, and on every hub that predates the specifications, it writes the same documents it writes today, so no site loses data and no older reader breaks. What older readers see of an accepted element (a read-only projection, a linked carrier copy, or nothing in the carrier's shape) is a choice your declaration makes (§4).

docs.title: 2.1 The worked example
docs.text: The example setting is fictional. Its declaration is taken from the synthetic fixture specs/sync/registrations/fixtures/example-testcontroller.yaml, whose extension com.example.testcontroller.adaptiveTargets holds a typed schedule and a typed on/off setting. The conformance cases use two other synthetic products with an extension of the same shape: Example/NegotiationController with com.example.negotiation.targets, and Example/ControllerA with com.example.controllera.targets. Read "your extension" for any of the three. None of them describes a real controller.

docs.title: 2.2 Choose the shape: a typed settings field or an extension
docs.text:
The hub accepts four kinds of element (registration §5.3). Two of them carry a setting:

your setting declare it as element id when the hub does not accept it one that ControllerSettings already defines (records §5) a typed settings.fields[] entry with typeRef to its definition settings.fields/<name> written where it is today, name-only (write: untyped) one unique to your app a field of an extension under a reverse-DNS namespace your app holds extensions/<namespace> written as the extension's declared carrier

The well-known Loop registration already names Loop's ControllerSettings fields this way:

name: automaticBolusApplicationFactor
typeRef: https://nightscout.dev/schemas/sync/controller-settings.json#/properties/settings/properties/automaticBolusApplicationFactor

The rest of this guide follows the extension path, because the conformance cases cover it. The typed settings field path follows the same steps; §6 lists what its cases do not show.

docs.title: 2.3 Which hub answers what
docs.text:
Your app meets four kinds of hub. It finds out which from the capability document, GET /.well-known/nightscout/sync, read at launch and after an app update, never on a timer, on a lease renewal or because a request was refused (registration §4).

the hub what your app does answers 404 for the capability document (every hub released before HUB-REG-CRM) submits nothing; writes every element as its carrier publishes the document with no submit member submits nothing; writes every element as its carrier publishes submit and no instances submits; writes accepted elements typed, with no instance id publishes submit and instances submits; registers an instance; writes accepted elements typed, with its instance id

The parts of a hub your app calls (C4 containers; under TENANCY_MODE=single one listener serves all three):

The members your app reads before it submits are grammar.versions, typeFragment and submit:

href: /api/v4/registrations
tiers:
- controller-owned
permissions:
  submit: api:registrations:create
  retire: api:registrations:delete

keywords:
- type
- enum
- minimum
- maximum
- format
- items
- properties
- required
- description

docs.title: 3. The walk-through
docs.text: Each step names the rule it follows and the conformance case that shows it. Case paths are relative to specs/sync/conformance/ unless they start with specs/.

docs.title: 3.1 Declare and submit
docs.text:
step you do the hub answers rule case 1 Read the capability document at launch. With no document, or no submit, skip to step 9 and write carriers. the document, or 404 registration §4, registration §6 accepted.yaml, older-hub-no-capabilities.yaml, hub-without-submit.yaml 2 Check that your grammar major is in grammar.versions and that every type keyword and format your fields use is in typeFragment. Do not submit a major the hub does not list. a keyword outside the subset rejects that element unsupported-type-keyword; an unlisted major rejects the whole registration G2, registration §5.2 rejected-type-keyword-outside-subset.yaml, rejected-unsupported-grammar-major.yaml 3 Declare the setting as a field of your extension: a type fragment (or typeRef), a unit where it has one, and a sensitivity label. A field with no label falls under unlabelledPolicy, which is withhold when absent. an extension with an untyped field is rejected untyped-extension G2, R9 specs/sync/registrations/fixtures/example-testcontroller.yaml, rejected-untyped-extension.yaml 4 Put the extension under a reverse-DNS namespace that your credential's namespace roots cover and that no other product on the site holds. namespace-not-owned or namespace-claimed for that element; first to claim holds it registration §5.3, authority §5 rejected-namespace-not-owned.yaml, rejected-namespace-claimed.yaml, accepted-first-to-claim.yaml 5 Give the extension a version and a horizon. A setting is configuration published on change, so its horizon is effective-dated, as the settings document's is (R5, registration §3); a value computed each cycle is not a setting and belongs to the cycle's record (R7). Leave availability out for a released setting; experimental is stored only by a hub that lists it. the version is what version-conflict and read selection compare later G4, G5, R5, R7 specs/sync/registrations/fixtures/example-testcontroller.yaml, accepted.yaml, rejected-unsupported-availability.yaml 6 Declare the extension's carrier: the document you write today for this setting. It is your fallback and the mapping any projected view uses. an element with no carrier falls back to none, and no view of it can be served registration §5.3, registration §13 rejected-untyped-extension.yaml, instances/carrier-view-needs-mapping.yaml 7 PUT the registration to <submit.href>/<vendor>/<product> with If-None-Match: * the first time. A retry after a lost response sends the same body again. 201 with an outcome, the definitionId and an element result per element; a retry of stored content is a 200 no-op registration §5.1, registration §5.2, D18 accepted.yaml, create-retry-noop.yaml 8 Read each element's result and keep the write plan for this release. Treat accepted and accepted-with-ignored-members as accepted; anything else, or a value you do not know, as not accepted. accepted, accepted-with-ignored-members (members kept as written), or rejected with reasons; outcome accepted or partial registration §5.3, registration §6, G1 accepted.yaml, accepted-with-ignored-members.yaml, extensions-not-interpreted.yaml 9 For each element not accepted, and for every element on a hub from step 1 that takes no submission, keep writing today's carrier document. the hub stores the carrier as it does today registration §6, registration §17 rejected-untyped-extension.yaml, older-hub-no-capabilities.yaml, hub-without-submit.yaml 10 For an accepted element, read carrierView. served: write typed only. Not served and the element declares dualWriteLink: write typed and as its carrier, linked by your record id. Not served and no link: write typed only. older readers get the projection, the linked carrier copy, or nothing in the carrier's shape registration §6, registration §13, I7 accepted-dual-write-view-served.yaml, accepted-dual-write-view-not-served.yaml, instances/dual-write-linked.yaml

The declaration, from the fixture (steps 3 to 6). The fixture marks its extension experimental to exercise that rule; a released setting omits it:

com.example.testcontroller.adaptiveTargets:
  version: '1'
  availability: experimental
  horizon:
    class: definition
  carrier:
    collection: settings
    documentIdentifier: example-targets
  fields:
  - name: targetSchedule
    type:
      type: array
      items:
        type: object
        properties:
          startMinute:
            type: integer
            minimum: 0
            maximum: 1439
          target:
            type: number
        required:
        - startMinute
        - target
    unit: mg/dL
    sensitivity:
      level: descriptive
      category: therapy-setting
  - name: adaptationEnabled
    type:
      type: boolean
    sensitivity:
      level: descriptive
      category: therapy-setting

The request (step 7), as the cases model it:

action: submit
identity:
  vendor: Example
  product: NegotiationController
preconditions:
  ifNoneMatch: '*'

Every element accepted (step 8):

- element: stateSpans/ExampleOverride
  result: accepted
- element: extensions/com.example.negotiation.targets
  result: accepted

The same extension with an untyped field: rejected, and the write plan sends it as its carrier (steps 8 and 9):

element: extensions/com.example.negotiation.targets
result: rejected
reasons:
- code: untyped-extension
  path: spec.extensions.com.example.negotiation.targets.fields.0

stateSpans/ExampleOverride:
  write: typed
extensions/com.example.negotiation.targets:
  write: carrier
  carrier:
    collection: settings
    documentIdentifier: example-targets

docs.title: 3.2 Write the typed record and read it back
docs.text:
step you do the hub answers rule case 11 On a hub that publishes instances, create an instance: a random UUID v4 generated once per running copy, the definitionId from step 7, and a source role with device provenance on your extension's channel, <vendor>/<product>/extensions/<namespace>. On a hub without instances, skip this step. 201 with the lease and a result per role registration §8, registration §9, D19 instances/instance-create.yaml, instances/typed-write-hub-without-instances.yaml 12 Renew the lease with If-Match before it lapses. A renewal is not a reason to re-read the capability document. 200, noop: true when only the lease moved registration §8 instances/instance-renew.yaml 13 Write the typed record with your instance id and your own record id, which the hub keeps as identifier. 200 with the record attributed to your instance, its definition and provenance, and both ids; a write with no instance id on a hub with instances is refused 422 instance-required registration §11, I1, I4 instances/typed-write-attributed.yaml, quirks/typed-write-assigns-objectid.yaml, instances/typed-write-instance-required.yaml 14 Re-send with the same record id after a lost reply. No cache of server ids is needed. the stored ids, matchedBy: identifier, no second record I5, I7 quirks/typed-write-resend-same-ids.yaml 15 Handle a refused typed write. 429 or any 5xx: retry with backoff, no sooner than Retry-After, never as a carrier. Any other refusal: send that record as its carrier at once and treat the element as not accepted until the next launch or app update. load refusals change nothing; a definite refusal changes the plan for that element registration §6 typed-write-load-503.yaml, typed-write-load-429-retry-after.yaml, typed-write-blocked-by-owner.yaml, typed-write-route-404.yaml, instances/typed-write-role-held.yaml 16 Read which version of your extension the site's views show. the owner's pin, else the version the live device source runs, else the newest stored, within what the hub's capabilities accept registration §12 instances/select-live-device.yaml, instances/select-newest-stored.yaml, instances/select-owner-pin.yaml 17 Read back what you wrote as a carrier through history, from the cursor your last read returned. A record received by event and by history is kept once. pages of records above the cursor, complete when nothing was truncated T5, T6, T10 sync-transport/single-page-complete.yaml, sync-transport/duplicate-delivery-is-one-record.yaml

A role on the extension's channel (step 11), and the hub's result for it:

channel: Example/ControllerA/extensions/com.example.controllera.targets
role: source
provenance: device

channel: Example/ControllerA/extensions/com.example.controllera.targets
role: source
provenance: device
result: granted

The reply to a typed write (step 13). The case writes the override kind of the same product; the reply has the same shape for any element:

accepted: true
as: typed
attributedTo:
  vendor: Example
  product: ControllerA
  instanceId: 00000000-0000-4000-8000-00000000000a
definitionId: sha256:ee552930b207551ed46bbbe4e1065e3c67773415193f3a067ef46816201da2ab
provenance: device
ids:
  identifier: 00000000-0000-7000-8000-0000000000b2
  _id: 6ad0c04000000000000000a1
matchedBy: null

The versions a default view shows while the phone runs the first definition (step 16):

extensions/com.example.controllera.targets:
  version: '1'
  by: live-device
stateSpans/ExampleOverride:
  version: '1'
  by: live-device

A typed record keeps the definitionId it was written under, and the hub converts nothing between versions without a lossless mapping your definition declares (T13, G4). A sync page carries the definitions its records reference (T14). No case shows a typed record read back through the sync read; §6 lists it.

docs.title: 3.3 The release after
docs.text:
step you do the hub answers rule case 18 At the next release, PUT the same product resource with If-Match and the stored etag. Identity is vendor and product; versionRange is an attribute. 200 and a new etag; a stale etag is 412 and changes nothing registration §5.1, registration §5.4 update-accepted.yaml, update-stale-etag.yaml 19 When a meaning member of the setting changes (type, unit, range, horizon, sensitivity, carrier), raise the extension's version. Description and evidence may change at the same version. the same version with a different meaning is rejected version-conflict for that element, which then goes as its carrier registration §7, G4, D19 instances/definition-extension-version-conflict.yaml, instances/product-update-new-version.yaml, instances/definition-same-meaning.yaml 20 When builds of two releases run on one site, each instance names its own definition; a build that is not the current registration adds its definition with PUT …/definitions/<definitionId> and If-None-Match: *. 201; the product's etag does not change; both definitions stay stored registration §7, D19 instances/definition-put.yaml, instances/definition-retry-noop.yaml 21 When an earlier release wrote the setting in a shape that deviates (a unit, a slot name, a vocabulary), the deviation belongs in the quirks registry (specs/quirks/) as an entry with an affects range over your version strings, stated only where the corpus or source shows it. A newer definition declares its own mapping instead (sameAs for a slot). the hub applies a catalogue mapping only to writers whose version it knows and is in range, and records every mapping it applies Q1, Q2, Q3, D20 quirks/catalogue-mapping-applied.yaml, quirks/catalogue-mapping-version-outside.yaml, quirks/same-as-definition-accepted.yaml

The extension retyped at the version a stored definition already uses (step 19):

element: extensions/com.example.controllera.targets
result: rejected
reasons:
- code: version-conflict
  path: spec.extensions.com.example.controllera.targets

To move stored records to a new version, your app sends them again under the new definition with the same identifier; the re-send matches and replaces their content and definitionId (T15).

docs.title: 4. What older apps see
docs.text:
The per-app answers are in compatibility: the L2 table for attribution and projected views, the L1 table for records, and where an answer changes. For the setting your release adds:

who sees rule case a hub that predates the specifications your carrier documents, exactly as today registration §17, registration §6 older-hub-no-capabilities.yaml, instances/carrier-write-older-hub.yaml an older reader (a follower app, a report, the hub's own web pages) when the element's view is served a projected document in the carrier's shape, labelled projectedFrom, with the same _id on every read; it cannot write to it registration §13, I8 instances/project-served.yaml, instances/write-projected-read-only.yaml an older reader when the view is not served and the element declares dualWriteLink the carrier copy your app writes beside the typed record registration §6, I7 accepted-dual-write-view-not-served.yaml, instances/dual-write-linked.yaml an older reader when the view is not served and the element declares no link nothing in the carrier's shape: the record exists only typed registration §6, registration §13 instances/carrier-view-needs-mapping.yaml an earlier release of your own app on the same site nothing changes for it: its carrier writes are stored, attributed to the product's unregistered instance and never refused for exclusivity registration §11, registration §17 instances/carrier-write-older-controller.yaml, instances/carrier-write-claimant.yaml

A projection, as the case for the override kind serves it (the mapping comes from the element's declared carrier; for your extension that is the settings document it names):

collection: treatments
document:
  identifier: 00000000-0000-7000-8000-0000000000b1
  _id: 6ad0b23500000000000000b1
  created_at: '2026-10-15T11:00:00Z'
  eventType: Temporary Override
  duration: 60
  projectedFrom:
    definitionId: sha256:ee552930b207551ed46bbbe4e1065e3c67773415193f3a067ef46816201da2ab
    element: stateSpans/ExampleOverride
    entities:
    - 00000000-0000-7000-8000-0000000000b1

So the choice in step 10 decides what followers see. If followers must keep showing the setting on hubs that serve no view of it, declare dualWriteLink.

docs.title: 5. Checklist
docs.text:
• The setting has one home: a typed settings.fields[] entry with typeRef when ControllerSettings defines it, else a field of your extension.
  • Every field has a type or typeRef within the hub's typeFragment, a unit where it has one, and a sensitivity label.
  • The namespace is reverse-DNS, covered by your credential's roots, and yours alone on the site.
  • The extension has a version, a horizon and a carrier that is the document you write today.
  • The app reads the capability document and its registration only at launch and after an app update.
  • The write plan is per element, from this registration's response only; anything unknown is not accepted.
  • Carrier writes continue for every element not accepted and on every hub without submit.
  • On a hub with instances, every typed write carries a live instance id holding source on the element's channel.
  • Typed records carry your own stable record id as identifier.
  • Load refusals retry; definite refusals send that record as its carrier.
  • A change of meaning raises the element's version.
  • You have decided what followers see: a served view, a dual write, or typed only.

docs.title: 6. Gaps
docs.text:
Steps a developer needs that no conformance case shows. Each is a gap in the cases, not in this guide's steps.

  1. Typed settings fields. No case submits a typed settings.fields[] entry, so neither its element result nor its write: untyped fallback (registration §5.3) is shown, and none writes a ControllerSettings snapshot (records §5).
  2. The typed record itself. The typed write route is not specified ("the typed API the hub derived", registration §6), and the write cases model the request with no body, so no case shows the content of a typed extension record. Under instances/, every typed write case writes a stateSpans kind; none writes an extension element.
  3. Reading a typed record back. The sync read (T5), typed records on the socket (T11), the definitions a page carries (T14) and moving stored records to a new version (T15) have no case with a typed record.
  4. Projecting an extension. instances/project-served.yaml projects a stateSpans kind to a treatment; no case projects an extension to its settings carrier document.

docs.title: Implementing registration in cgm-remote-monitor: where each slice goes, in what order, and how it is checked
docs.text:
Living document, last changed 2026-10-29 at d9f9526e1.

Contributor-facing. Living guide, current at main f1119d4c (2026-10-26) and cgm-remote-monitor official/dev 47723cda (the merge of #8605). Uses the platform specifications; terms are in the glossary. Status: the specifications are proposed and not implemented; this guide plans HUB-REG-CRM and its backlog. Every module path that is not on dev is marked proposed, and every route and permission name is a proposal, as the specifications say.

This guide is the hub-side companion of bring a new controller onto a hub and add a setting in your next release. Those tell a controller author what to send. This one tells a cgm-remote-monitor contributor, human or agent, where each piece of the registration and identity specifications goes in the code at official/dev 47723cda, in what order, and how each slice is checked before review.

Each slice names the rules it implements, the conformance cases under specs/sync/conformance/ that check it, the reference function in tools/nsschema/ that decides those cases, the existing modules a reviewer will expect the code beside (file:line at 47723cda), and, for the slices that need the shared write boundary or multi, where that work stands. The write boundary is draft PR

docs.title: 8854 (wip/architecture-data-contracts, 880b7369, by Andy Low), which is not on dev; the
docs.text: maintainer's direction is that the storage seam will most likely be built on it. The local seam chain (seam/*, tip 65ce54b9) is reference only: it shows what multi needs, and none of it is on dev.

docs.title: 1. What the hub does and never does
docs.text:
The hub records, routes and refuses. It never decides whether a change to therapy is safe, never alters what a sender asked, and never doses (D18). It checks structure; the controller owns policy. dev already draws the same line for record validation: lib/server/write-validation.js:13-17 keeps "ranges a controller chooses for itself" with the controller, and a typed record's check against its declared type fragment (G2) is the same kind of structural rule.

Three invariants hold on every slice:

  • Unregistered writers see nothing change. Every client that writes today (Loop, Trio, AndroidAPS, xDrip+, uploaders, the careportal) writes no registration. Their writes on API v1, API v3 and the socket must stay byte-identical with the flag off and with it on (§6.4).
  • Nothing happens without the flag. With the flag off, the hub serves no capability document and no new route, as every hub released before HUB-REG-CRM does.
  • Single-tenant first, mode-aware from the first commit. The first implementation runs with TENANCY_MODE unset on MongoDB. Every invariant that multi will need (namespace claims, role exclusivity, etag preconditions) is built as a single-document conditional write or a unique index, never a multi-document transaction, so the port to multi changes the store and not the rule (HUB-REG-CRM note 6).

docs.title: 2. The slice order
docs.text:
slice serves queue item waits on S0 the well-known catalogue and the capability document, read-only, behind a flag HUB-REG-CRM nothing on dev S1 the product resource: submit, etag, retire; the MongoDB collections HUB-REG-CRM S0 S2 definitions, instances, roles and leases HUB-REG-CRM S1 S5 the owner's actions and listing on single with API_SECRET HUB-REG-CRM S1, S2 S3 typed writes, attribution of every write, and read selection HUB-REG-CRM S2, #8854's write boundary, and its first follow-up (full write intent) S4 projected views for older readers HUB-REG-CRM S3 S6 multi through the storage seam and ns-tenant-admin HUB-REG-CRM-SEAM, HUB-REG-CRM-ADMIN S0–S5, the storage seam, SPEC-REG-MODES, SPEC-REG-MIGRATE, T30-TENANT-ADMIN

The slices keep the numbers S0 to S6; the build order puts S5 before S3. The specifications give the owner's actions (block, unblock, release, transfer, retire, free namespaces, transfer a role, pin a version, the listing) no dependency on typed records: they act on the product resource (S1) and on instances (S2) (authority §4). S3 cannot start until every write passes one boundary that can attribute it and answer with both ids (§4.4):

docs.title: 8854 draws the boundary, and the per-item write intent is the first follow-up it lists. Building
docs.text:
S5 while S3 waits closes 31 cases that need nothing from the boundary. The one coupling is the owner's pin: S5 stores it, and S3's read selection reads it (instances/select-owner-pin.yaml), so that case is green only after both.

S3 and S4 both need the single write boundary, for two reasons the specifications state:

  • Attribution reaches every write path. A write with no instance id is attributed to the product's unregistered instance and is never refused for exclusivity (registration §11); a catalogue mapping for an older writer is recorded on the reply and the stored document as quirksApplied (Q2, Q3); and every write reply returns both ids (I4). dev writes through six v1 and in-process storage modules, API v3 and the socket, each with its own matching and reply policy (measured on dev 43289dde in the write contract §1, before the cuts, and not re-measured at 47723cda). Only a boundary every one of them passes through can attribute every write; the write contract's proposed write(intent) returns WriteResult.items[] with _id, identifier and a per-item outcome (write contract §2.2).
  • A projected document is read-only on every path. A write aimed at either id of a projected document is refused projected-read-only (I8, registration §13), which only a check inside the boundary makes true for v1, v3 and the socket at once.

The 12 cases that check carrier writes on today's paths (both ids, UUID_HANDLING's move, the identifier-first re-send) are the identity track, not a registration slice: they land with the write boundary and the ID-* items (§5). The 10 command-routing cases under instances/ belong to SPEC-REG-COMMANDS and need S2's command-sink roles; the command record itself is outside this guide (commands).

flowchart LR

  accDescr: S0 leads to S1, then S2. From S2 the owner's actions S5 can be built at once, while typed writes S3 also wait on the write boundary of draft PR 8854 and its first follow-up, the full write intent. S4 follows S3. S6 needs all of S0 to S5 plus the storage seam, the mode contract and the tenant-admin listener. The identity track lands with the write intent.

  s1 --> s2[S2 definitions, instances, leases]

New tests go in tests/ and each needs a tier in tests/tiers.json (unit, core, integration and the rest, #8839).
