They check that the cases are self-consistent. They are not a hub, and a hub that disagrees with one on a case is either a hub defect or a gap in the specifications, which is reported rather than fixed by editing the case.

docs.title: 4.1 S0: the catalogue and the capability document
docs.text:
What. GET /.well-known/nightscout/sync (the capability document, unauthenticated, cacheable, about the software and never a person) and GET /.well-known/nightscout/controllers (the well-known registrations) (registration §2, §4). The document is validated against specs/sync/hub-capabilities.schema.json. In S0 it carries grammar, horizons, typeFragment, limits and wellKnown, and no submit and no instances: a controller reading it writes every element as its carrier (hub-without-submit.yaml).

Where. The flag is parsed beside WRITE_VALIDATION (lib/server/env.js:123-127); its name and default are the maintainer's, and the conservative default is off, under which both routes answer 404 exactly as on dev. The routes mount in lib/server/app.js after the boot-error branch (:209-215) and before /api (:298). The catalogue is the three generated registrations, specs/sync/registrations/loop.yaml, specs/sync/registrations/trio.yaml and specs/sync/registrations/androidaps.yaml (make schema-sync-model), with the shared slot list specs/sync/shared-slots.yaml. They ship inside cgm-remote-monitor as data files, proposed under lib/registration/well-known/; a check in this repository compares the shipped copy with the generated one, so the product repository keeps no generator (D12).

Seam. Nothing. The document is deployment-level in every mode; whether the flag, limits and instances.leaseSeconds are per deployment or per tenant is SPEC-REG-MODES point 4.

docs.title: 4.2 S1: the product resource
docs.text:
What. PUT, GET and the controller's DELETE on <submit.href>/<vendor>/<product>, with the order of checks in registration §5.2: authorisation and binding, then the precondition (428, 412), then the owner's block, then the registration as a whole, then each element. S1 adds submit to the capability document.

Where.

  • Authorisation uses ctx.authorization.resolveWithRequest (lib/authorization/index.js:106-113) and checkMultiple (:123), not isPermitted alone, because the binding needs the result: a subject (:249-264) binds to subject._id; a request authorised by API_SECRET (:178-184) has no subject and binds api-secret, which exists only on single (D13).
  • The etag and the definition id are SHA-256 over RFC 8785 canonical JSON. dev has no canonicalisation library and no JSON Schema validator in its dependencies; whether to add one is the maintainer's choice. The values the cases use are strings, integers, booleans, null and short decimals, so a short canonicaliser that sorts keys by UTF-16 code unit (JavaScript's default sort) is enough, and the cases' stated etags and definitionIds, computed by negotiate.canonical_json, check it.
  • Storage: one MongoDB collection for products, proposed registrations, keyed by (vendor, product) with a unique index; the stored document holds the registration, state, boundTo, credential kind, binding event and claimed namespaces. Namespace claims are a second unique index over the claimed namespace, so "first to claim holds it" (accepted-first-to-claim.yaml) is decided by MongoDB, not by a read before the write. An update is one conditional replace on {_id, etag}; a replace that matches nothing is 412.
  • The collection name is read in setStorage() (lib/server/env.js:167-176) like the others; the store is built in setupInternals (lib/server/bootevent.js:252).

Write boundary and seam (neither on dev). The registration store is control-plane state, not records: it is written by etag compare-and-set, never by a record write's merge-on-match. #8854's boundary passes a driver call through unchanged (write-step.js:81-100), so a conditional replaceOne on {_id, etag} keeps its meaning behind it. On the seam chain, which is reference only, a store gets its collection from collectionFor (lib/storage/collection-for.js:22 at 65ce54b9), and on PostgreSQL replaceFiltered throws by name (lib/api3/storage/pgCollection/index.js:318). HUB-REG-CRM-SEAM carries both points.

docs.title: 4.3 S2: definitions, instances and leases
docs.text:
What. PUT …/definitions/<definitionId> (immutable, If-None-Match: * only), PUT and DELETE /api/v4/instances/<instanceId> (the flat path, maintainer 2026-10-26; #8857 serves it under the product today), per-role results, exclusivity among live device instances, labels, leases (registration §7–§10). The capability document gains instances. "One element at one version has one meaning" uses the meaning table in §7; negotiate.version_conflicts and negotiate.meaning are the reference.

Where.

  • Two more collections, proposed registration_definitions (keyed by definitionId, content addressed, so a retried PUT is a no-op) and registration_instances (keyed by instance id).
  • Exclusivity is one holder per (channel, role) among live device instances. A lease that lapses holds no roles with no housekeeping, so the holder is computed from leaseExpiresAt at the time of the request, and a claim is one conditional update on the instance document. Two claimants racing for one channel must leave one holder; the HUB-REG-CRM-SEAM gate (c) states the concurrent test and its control, and the same test belongs in S2 on MongoDB.
  • The instance id is a lowercase UUID v4 the controller supplies; the hub refuses any other form (instances/instance-invalid-id.yaml) and never derives one from a device name.
  • The observed alias (devicestatus.device seen in an instance's writes) is stored withheld: absent from the default listing and from the capability document.

multi (reference only). Under multi, the channel scope of a product's own slot and the shared slots are per tenant. Cache compiled validators by definitionId, which means the same on every tenant, never by (vendor, product) (HUB-REG-CRM note 7).

docs.title: 4.4 S3: typed writes, attribution and read selection
docs.text:
What. The typed write: an instance id on every typed write (proposed as a request header), 422 instance-required without one, 409 not-live, role-held or role-not-granted, the record attributed to its instance, definition and provenance, and both ids in the reply (registration §11, I4, I5, I7). Every carrier write is attributed too: to its instance, or to the product's unregistered instance, and a catalogue mapping for a known older version is applied and recorded (Q2, Q3). Read selection picks the version a view shows: capability limit, owner's pin, live device source, newest stored (registration §12). Retention refuses to remove a definition a record or a live instance uses (§14).

Base: #8854's write boundary, draft, not on dev. At 880b7369, lib/storage/write-step.js puts every driver write from the six v1 and internal storage modules, the legacy socket and API v3 behind one Proxy (:103-114), checks selectors, keeps the driver's result and errors, and emits a data-free storage-write-committed event per changed driver operation (:68-79); scripts/check-write-boundary.js fails when one of the eight adapter files (:6-8) bypasses it. Matching, server dates and reply policy stay in each adapter, by design (the PR's data-contracts.md, "Implemented boundaries").

That boundary is where S3 attaches, and it is not yet enough for S3. The PR's own follow-up list names what S3 needs as separate, measured slices:

  • Follow-up 1, full write intent and event fan-out: matching, server-date allocation, stale-id cleanup and request-level outcomes move behind the boundary. Per-item outcomes with both ids (I4), the unregistered instance's attribution (§11) and quirksApplied (Q3) are request-level outcomes, so S3 waits on this slice; the write contract's write(intent) → WriteResult (§2.2) is one proposal for its shape. Today's event carries counts, not documents, so typed records on the socket and in v3 history (T11, sync-transport §5) need the fan-out half of the same slice.
  • Follow-up 4, delivery and cursors (Q-D): the cursor rules typed records share with history.
  • Follow-up 5, units and identity (Q-E): _id versus identifier precedence and mandatory identifiers at a version boundary (§5).
  • Follow-up 2, atomic validation: a type-fragment check that reads before it writes races like today's v3 checks; S3 keeps its own checks to the record in hand.

The queue item for the first release of a single write step is WC-STEP-PATCH, which the queue blocks on SEAM-REFRESH; with the seam built on #8854, the item's base becomes that boundary.

Where. The type-fragment check of a typed record sits beside lib/server/write-validation.js, in its pattern (pure check, refusal shape, a log line with field names and never values), and covers only the keywords the capability document's typeFragment lists. The typed collection gets its driver collection through #8854's collection(raw, context) with a source label of its own, and its adapter joins the boundary gate's list. On the socket path, #8854 already routes dbAdd (lib/server/websocket.js:507 on dev, four insertOne calls at :678, :722, :777, :799) through the boundary.

multi (reference only, seam chain 65ce54b9). The filter AST (lib/storage/filter.js: validate :58, toMongo :118, toSql :200, fromMongo :402) is how a typed query and a label selector reach both backends. Under multi, an emission with no tenant bound is withheld (lib/server/socket-tenancy.js:258-266), so typed records on the socket need the request's tenant in hand.

docs.title: 4.5 S4: projected views
docs.text:
What. For an accepted element whose carrierView is served, each typed record is served to API v1 and v3 readers as a document in the carrier's shape, labelled projectedFrom, never stored as a source, read-only (409 projected-read-only), with the same _id on every read; without a declared mapping, not-served in the submit response and 409 no-carrier-mapping (registration §13, I8). Until S4, S1 reports not-served for every element, which the cases model as their carrierViews input.

Where. v1 reads are each collection's list (for treatments lib/server/treatments.js:343); v3 reads go through lib/api3/storage/mongoCollection/find.js and its normalizeDocs (:19-24). The _id of a projection is assigned at the typed write and stored with the typed record, so a projection is a read-time merge, not a second stored copy. The read-only refusal is a check behind the write boundary against the projected ids (instances._projected_ids is the reference), so it holds on v1, v3 and the socket at once.

docs.title: 4.6 S5: the owner's actions on single
docs.text:
What. Block (including a pre-emptive block of an identity with nothing stored), unblock, release, transfer, retire, free namespaces, transfer a role, pin and unpin a version, and the owner's listing with overlaps, slotNameObservations and withheld members (authority §4). Each changes the product's or the instance's etag, so two owner actions racing meet 412; pins are their own resource with their own etag (§12).

Where. On single there is one listener; the owner is whoever presents API_SECRET (lib/authorization/index.js:178-184). 28 cases name ns-tenant-admin and run on single with API_SECRET, as registration §5.2 step 1 and the HUB-REG-CRM gate state. The two cases that name ns-api for an owner action (owner-action-on-data-listener.yaml, instances/owner-transfer-role-data-listener.yaml) have no single-mode form until SPEC-REG-MODES states one; on single they are reported not applicable. The owner routes are proposed under the same router as S1, as POST …/block and the others in registration §5.1.

docs.title: 4.7 S6: multi
docs.text:
What. The same contract under TENANCY_MODE=multi: registrations, definitions, instances, pins and overlaps are tenant data; the capability document is the same on every tenant host; there is no API_SECRET (D13), so no api-secret binding; owner actions move to ns-tenant-admin (AU2), which does not exist anywhere yet.

What the seam chain shows (reference only, at 65ce54b9, not on dev). The seam itself will most likely be built on #8854; these are the pieces of the old chain a multi implementation needs an answer for.

piece where on the seam chain used for the tenant binding lib/storage/tenant-scope.js:51 SINGLE_TENANT, :106 withTenant, :137-150 requireTenant every registration read and write runs bound; single resolves to SINGLE_TENANT, which is not a tenant id the mode flag lib/server/env.js:176-198 setTenancy, TENANCY_MODE default single, TENANT_CONTEXT_MAX :195 the harness's mode parameter maps onto it store selection lib/server/storage-backends.js:82 selectBackend; lib/storage/collection-for.js:22 the registration store on MongoDB or PostgreSQL tenant resolution lib/server/tenant-middleware.js:204 create, :332 fromEnv host to tenant before any registration route export and delete lib/admin/platform-store.js:191-203 tenantScopedTables, :56 NOT_TENANT_DATA the registration tables must appear in the list (HUB-REG-CRM-SEAM gate d) credential kinds lib/admin/platform.sql:139-141 tenant_secret with kind root the tenant root credential, which has no credentialKind yet (SPEC-REG-MODES point 2) _id on PostgreSQL lib/api3/storage/pgCollection/sql.js:64-78 mints a 24-hex ObjectId-shaped _id I2's 24-hex _id on every legacy surface, on PostgreSQL

lib/admin/ on the seam chain is the platform operator's plane (ns-admin), not ns-tenant-admin. How a site's registrations travel when it moves into a tenant is SPEC-REG-MIGRATE.

docs.title: 5. Identity for registered instances
docs.text:
The two ids (identity I1–I9, D20 rule 5 in the hub-sync design §3.7): identifier is the sync identity the client assigns, the real thing a record describes; _id is the storage key the hub assigns, 24 hex on every legacy surface. In the typed API, identifier is the controller's record id. Three ids are easy to confuse in this code:

id who assigns it where it lives rule instance id the controller, a random UUID v4 per running copy the instance resource, and the header of each typed write identity §2 identifier the controller, from the same inputs on every device that writes the record the typed record and every carrier document I1, I6, identifier conventions _id the hub, at the write; its time is the receipt time every stored record, and every projection of a typed record I2, I3, I8

What the slices owe.

  • S3 answers every typed write with ids: {identifier, _id} and matchedBy; a re-send with the same identifier for the same product matches the stored typed record whichever instance sent it (I7), so a controller keeps no cache of server ids (quirks/typed-write-resend-same-ids.yaml).
  • identifier is mandatory for registered controller instances (maintainer, 2026-10-18, identifier conventions §1 decision 1). On the typed path the hub can refuse a typed write that carries no record id. On a legacy path, how the hub recognises that a carrier write comes from a registered instance is open (ID-ABSENT-DECISION): §11 proposes the instance id only on typed writes. No case and no reference function states the refusal yet (§7, item 2).
  • A registered instance's convention (its identifier templates) is proposed as a meaning member of its definition (identifier conventions §5); the grammar v1 has no member for it. If it is adopted, S2's meaning table gains it, so a changed template needs a new definition version.
  • S4's projection carries the typed record's identifier and the _id stored at the typed write (I8).

What dev already does (#8845, merged in 47723cda). API v3 refuses a body _id with 400 (BF-170, lib/api3/shared/operationTools.js:197-203), keeps a client identifier as sent and otherwise computes a UUID v5 (:209-216, :168-185); its reads serve identifier and drop _id (lib/api3/storage/mongoCollection/utils.js:10-16). API v1 treatments answer a re-send with the stored _id on an identifier match and on a fallback-key match (BF-165, lib/server/treatments.js:185-224). UUID_HANDLING (lib/server/env.js:111, default on) moves a non-hex string _id to identifier on treatments and entries; the identity track records that move as quirksApplied (I9).

Where the ID-* items land.

item state in the queue lands relative to the slices ID-SIMPLE-MATCH not started, unblocked since RT-1 merged v1 entries and devicestatus match on identifier, on dev before the write intent and independent of every slice WC-STEP-PATCH blocked on SEAM-REFRESH in the queue the one write step, today's behaviour pinned; BF-165's _id in every reply #8854's boundary is its likely base and follow-up 1 its content; S3 and S4 wait on it; the identity track's 12 cases are checked when it lands ID-FIRST-MATCH, ID-BATCH-RESULTS, ID-VALIDATE, ID-V1-LOOKUP blocked on WC-STEP-PATCH identifier-first matching on every path, per-item batch results, identifier validation, v1 lookup by any identifier beside S3, behind the boundary; ID-VALIDATE's checks apply to typed record ids once ID-FORMAT-DECISION decides C1–C7 ID-UNIQUE-INDEX in 16.0.0 scope (2026-10-30), after ID-FIRST-MATCH slice 5 a partial unique index on identifier, behind WRITE_IDENTIFIER_INDEX=try|require|off no longer waits for S3; the typed collection's index on (vendor, product, identifier) is S3's own ID-FORMAT-DECISION, ID-ABSENT-DECISION, ID-CLIENT-OID-DECISION, ID-V3-IMMUTABLE-DECISION, ID-DELETE-REUSE-DECISION needs decision the maintainer's ID-ABSENT-DECISION decides how S3 recognises a registered instance on a legacy path ID-SCOPE-DECISION needs decision per collection, across collections, per tenant S6: the per-tenant scope is a column in the key under multi

docs.title: 6.1 The harness lives here
docs.text:
The harness that runs the conformance cases against a booted cgm-remote-monitor lives in this repository (D12), not in the product repository. It does not exist yet; HUB-REG-CRM builds it. It boots the slice's worktree in process, as tools/qc/write-contract-matrix.js does (WC_WORKTREE, WC_MONGO, a fresh database per run, liveness asserted before and after every measured step), so a "nothing happened" result cannot come from a dead server.

For each case it:

  1. seeds the case's hubState into the slice's collections (the seed is written against the slice's storage shape, so it changes with the slice);
  2. sends the case's request with the case's submitter as its credential (API_SECRET for an api-secret submitter, a subject's token otherwise);
  3. compares the response, and the stored state where the case states stateAfter or storedAfter, with expected; detail strings are not compared.

docs.title: 6.2 The mode is a parameter from the first commit
docs.text: The harness takes the mode as a parameter on day one, even while only one value runs: single on MongoDB for S0 to S5; single on PostgreSQL and multi on PostgreSQL with two tenants for S6 (the HUB-REG-CRM-SEAM gate). Each case runs in each mode SPEC-REG-MODES assigns it, so adding a mode later adds runs rather than rewriting the harness.

docs.title: 6.3 Every case is reported by name
docs.text:
Each case prints as passed, mapped or not applicable, by name, and none is dropped. A case is red when its response or stored state differs. The mappings on single at 47723cda:

case or group reported why the 28 cases that name ns-tenant-admin mapped: run on single with API_SECRET registration §5.2 step 1; HUB-REG-CRM gate owner-action-on-data-listener.yaml, instances/owner-transfer-role-data-listener.yaml not applicable single has one listener; SPEC-REG-MODES states the form update-token-rotated.yaml mapped: a new JWT for the same subject, or a changed API_SECRET on dev a subject's access token is derived from its _id and the secret (lib/authorization/storage.js:285-290), so the subject survives either carrier-write cases whose sent document carries a client _id mapped: sent over API v1 API v3 refuses a body _id (BF-170) typed-write-load-429-retry-after.yaml, typed-write-load-502.yaml, typed-write-load-503.yaml not applicable beyond the status the hub sends they check the controller's retry, not a hub decision any case in a slice not yet built not applicable, with the slice named so the run's totals always add to 186

docs.title: 6.4 The unregistered writer is the control
docs.text: Run tools/qc/write-contract-matrix.js on the base commit and on the slice's branch, with the flag off and with it on, and compare with --compare: every cell must be identical for a client that never registers. Red when any cell differs. This is what keeps today's apps unchanged, and it is the answer the compatibility tables give for every older app. #8854 adds an in-repository companion, tests/api.crud-by-id.matrix.test.js (336 cells with stated replies and stored id forms, CRUD_MATRIX_OUT for a before-and-after report); run both. From S3 on, the base is the matrix as pinned by the write intent slice.

docs.title: 6.5 Non-vacuity: remove each hub check
docs.text: Each hub check the cases exercise is removed in turn, and its cases must turn red with the expected code, not with any error: the binding (not-registration-owner), the preconditions (428, 412), the owner's block (blocked-by-owner), the namespace claim (namespace-claimed), role exclusivity (role-held), instance-required, and the projection's read-only refusal (projected-read-only). Perturb one cell of the write matrix and the §6.4 control must turn red. A red for the wrong reason (a crash, a 500, a dead server) does not count; show that the one removed check is the cause.

docs.title: 6.6 Before review
docs.text:
• python3 -m pytest tools/nsschema/test_registration_negotiation.py tools/nsschema/test_registration_instances.py tools/nsschema/test_registration_quirks.py stays green: the harness reads the cases, never edits them.
  • In cgm-remote-monitor, every new test file has a tier in tests/tiers.json, and npm run test:smoke passes after merging the latest official/dev.

docs.title: 7. Where the specifications and dev differ
docs.text:
Measured at 47723cda (and 65ce54b9 for item 6); each is reported to the specification's owner rather than worked around.

  1. API v3 reads and _id. Identity I2 says API v1 and v3 serve a 24-hex _id, and that API v3 refuses a client _id with 400, as dev does since #8845 (lib/api3/shared/operationTools.js:197-203). API v3's reads drop _id (lib/api3/storage/mongoCollection/utils.js:10-16, applied by find.js:19-24), so on dev I2's "v3 serves a 24-hex _id" and I8's "every read of that projection carries the same _id" hold on API v1 only.
  2. A typed write with no identifier. The decision that identifier is mandatory for registered instances has no case, and instances.write accepts a typed write that carries no record id (tools/nsschema/instances.py:1009). None of the five instances/typed-write-*.yaml cases carries recordId, and the accepted ones expect accepted: true.
  3. Token rotation. AU4 and update-token-rotated.yaml assume a token can rotate on one subject. On dev a subject's access token is a function of its _id and the API_SECRET hash, so it rotates only when the secret does, for every subject at once; a JWT re-issued from the same access token is the per-subject case. The binding holds either way (§6.3).
  4. Credential kind on API v3. lib/api3/security.js accepts a bearer JWT only (:21-31) and grants * with no subject when API3_SECURITY_ENABLE is off (:15-18). The registration routes need the subject and the credential kind, so they use the v1 resolution (lib/authorization/index.js:106-113).
  5. Indexes that hold an invariant. lib/storage/mongo-storage.js:263-295 builds key-only indexes and treats a failed build as a slowdown. A namespace claim or a role holder enforced by a unique index is a correctness property, so its index is built with unique: true outside that helper and a failed build is a boot error.
  6. The seam chain's write methods on PostgreSQL. At 65ce54b9 (reference only), PgCollection throws for insertMany, updateMany and replaceFiltered (lib/api3/storage/pgCollection/index.js:308-318); an etag compare-and-set has no method on PostgreSQL yet. This is an input to HUB-REG-CRM-SEAM.

docs.title: 8. Checklist
docs.text:
• The flag defaults off; with it off, both well-known routes and the registration router answer 404 as on dev.
  • The capability document validates against specs/sync/hub-capabilities.schema.json and advertises only what the built slices serve (submit from S1, instances from S2).
  • Binding is to a subject's _id or api-secret, never a token.
  • Every invariant across documents (namespace claim, role holder, etag) is one conditional write or one unique index, and no multi-document transaction.
  • Typed and carrier writes go through the one write boundary, and every new adapter is on the boundary gate's list; no slice adds a write path of its own.
  • The harness reports all 186 cases by name as passed, mapped or not applicable, with the mode named.
  • The unregistered-writer matrix is identical to the base, flag off and on.
  • Each hub check, removed alone, turns its cases red with the expected code.
  • New tests have tiers; npm run test:smoke passes after merging official/dev.

docs.title: Bringing a controller onto a hub: register it, hold a lease, receive commands and report outcomes
docs.text:
Living document, last changed 2026-10-26 at 36487a5dd.

Contributor-facing. Living guide, current at main 127f69e1 (2026-10-18). Uses the platform specifications; terms are in the glossary. Status: the specifications are proposed and not implemented; until HUB-REG-CRM is, each step is checked against its conformance case, not run against a hub.

This guide is for a developer bringing an automated insulin delivery controller, or a controller app, onto a Nightscout hub that implements the platform specifications. It follows one fictional controller, Example TestController, whose registration is the synthetic fixture specs/sync/registrations/fixtures/example-testcontroller.yaml, from the first request to the outcome of a remote command.

Each step names the rule it follows and a conformance case under specs/sync/conformance/ that shows it. The examples are copied from those cases by python3 -m tools.nsschema.guide_examples and never typed by hand, so they name the cases' own fictional products (Example ControllerA, NegotiationController) where TestController would stand. Times in the command cases are seconds from the start of the case. Paths and permission names are proposals, as the specifications say.

docs.title: 1. What the hub does and never does
docs.text:
The hub records, routes and refuses. It never decides whether a change to therapy is safe, never alters what a sender asked, and never doses (D18). Your controller validates and enacts.

the hub your controller accepts or refuses each element of your registration, and stores typed records for what it accepts (registration §5) writes everything the hub does not accept in today's document shapes, its carriers (registration §6) grants each (channel, role) to one live device instance and records overlaps (registration §9) keeps running when a role is refused, and writes that channel's records as carriers checks a command's channel, routing, expiry, size and the sender's permission, and nothing else (CM5) checks the payload hash, the expiry by its own clock, its own limits and the doses and carbs since the command was made (CM10, CM23) records the command, its state and the outcome you report (CM1, CM7) decides each commandId once, across restarts (CM21), and reports what it did reports overlapping intents as the controller reported them (state and intent S1) arbitrates between the person, the algorithm, caregivers and agents acting on one pump

The control-loop analysis lists the entries that only the controller can prevent: validating a remote command against its own limits and recent local actions, assigning identifiers that are unique per record, acting on its own state where the hub's lags, failing a command it cannot deliver to the pump, and, for plans, the checks it makes at each occurrence. No hub rule replaces any of them.

Your app in context (C4 context; roles, not products):

docs.title: 2. Before you start: credentials and roles
docs.text:
Your controller is a device. It holds a native per-tenant credential, which belongs to a subject, and never signs in through the caregivers' identity service (AU1). Everything the hub binds to you is bound to that subject, never to a token, so rotating the token changes nothing (AU4).

you need for who grants it rule case a credential whose subject is your controller's every request below; the binding of your product and instances the tenant: a native per-tenant credential for a device AU1, AU4, authority §3 accepted.yaml, update-token-rotated.yaml api:registrations:create creating and updating the product, adding definitions, creating and renewing instances included in the role a hub issues by default to a device or uploader credential (API_SECRET on single); the tenant owner may withhold it on the owner's listener authority §5, registration §7 not-authorised.yaml, instances/instance-create.yaml api:registrations:delete retiring the product, deleting an instance as api:registrations:create authority §5, registration §5 retire.yaml, retire-not-authorised.yaml to be the product's bound subject updating or retiring the product, adding a definition, holding a device command-sink the first create binds it; the owner can release or transfer it authority §3, authority §6 update-not-registration-owner.yaml, instances/instance-command-sink-not-registration-owner.yaml no command permission fetching your own commands and reporting their outcomes: the hub checks that you are the destination's bound subject — CM7, CM18 commands/fetch-naming-another-instance.yaml, commands/report-from-other-subject-refused.yaml (senders) api:commands:create; (followers) api:commands:read sending a command; reading a channel's outstanding list the tenant owner, to caregivers and follower apps CM5, CM24 commands/command-without-permission.yaml, commands/outstanding-lists-open-items.yaml

Under TENANCY_MODE=single there is one listener and API_SECRET may register; the product is then bound to {kind: api-secret}, and any holder of the secret may update it (authority §3). Every holder of API_SECRET is one subject, so another app holding it can fetch your commands or report their outcomes; commands §9 lists this as open (UCA-CMD-014). Give the controller a credential of its own.

Under TENANCY_MODE=multi each tenant has its own credential root and signing key (AU3). A registration is per tenant, so a controller that serves two tenants registers twice. A fetch-now signal is sent only inside a request bound to the command's tenant (CM19), and carries nothing (CM27); fetch is the path that always works.

docs.title: 3. Walk-through
docs.text: The parts of a hub your app calls (C4 containers; under TENANCY_MODE=single one listener serves all three, and API_SECRET acts as the owner):

docs.title: 3.1 Read the capability document
docs.text:
GET /.well-known/nightscout/sync is unauthenticated, cacheable and about the hub software, not a person (registration §4). It tells you where to submit and with which permissions:

href: /api/v4/registrations
tiers:
- controller-owned
permissions:
  submit: api:registrations:create
  retire: api:registrations:delete

and, on a hub that serves definitions and instances, the lease length, the instance id form, and the roles and channels it grants:

leaseSeconds: 900
instanceId: uuid-v4
roles:
- source
- command-sink
channels:
- slot
- element
labels:
  maxLabels: 8
  maxKeyLength: 96
  maxValueLength: 64
step you do the hub answers rule case 1 Read the capability document at launch and after a controller release; never on a timer, on a lease renewal or because a request was refused the document, the same for every tenant on the deployment registration §4 accepted.yaml, typed-write-load-503.yaml 2 If it answers 404, submit nothing and write every element as its carrier — (an older hub) registration §6, registration §17 older-hub-no-capabilities.yaml 3 If it has no submit, submit nothing and write carriers — registration §6 hub-without-submit.yaml 4 If your grammar major is not in grammar.versions, submit nothing a submission would be 422 unsupported-grammar-major registration §6, registration §5.2 rejected-unsupported-grammar-major.yaml 5 If it has no instances, skip §3.3: typed writes need no instance id typed writes accepted without one registration §17 instances/typed-write-hub-without-instances.yaml 6 Predict element results from horizons, typeFragment and limits; the fixture's experimental DailyAdaptation kind is refused where experimental is not listed the response is authoritative G5, registration §6 rejected-unsupported-availability.yaml

With no capability document the controller's plan is carriers for every element:

stateSpans/ExampleOverride:
  write: carrier
  carrier:
    collection: treatments
    eventType: Temporary Override
    durationField: duration
    durationUnit: minutes
extensions/com.example.negotiation.targets:
  write: carrier
  carrier:
    collection: settings
    documentIdentifier: example-targets

docs.title: 3.2 Register the product and its definitions
docs.text:
The product resource is <submit.href>/<vendor>/<product>; its identity is (metadata.vendor, metadata.product), and versionRange is an attribute, so a release updates the same resource (registration §5). TestController's identity:

vendor: Example
product: TestController
algorithmFamily: other
tier: controller-owned
versionRange: 0.0.1-test
source: synthetic fixture for tools/nsschema/test_registration_grammar.py

A create is a PUT with If-None-Match: *:

action: submit
identity:
  vendor: Example
  product: NegotiationController
preconditions:
  ifNoneMatch: '*'

The response names the definition id the hub computed, the etag, the binding to your subject, and a result per element:

apiVersion: nightscout.dev/sync/v1
kind: RegistrationResponse
status: 201
outcome: accepted
noop: false
definitionId: sha256:a72ab7f1cf322ebd8b226ce78a030d86865a1c1b8c5b647e670c9ac17b0f064d
registration:
  vendor: Example
  product: NegotiationController
  versionRange: 1.0.0-test
  state: active
  etag: sha256:3aaaa298028f1593078375fd1ade48a265aedf04f1d5bd2b5d20b40d3a231c5d
  boundTo:
    kind: subject
    subject: subject-test-controller-a
  credentialKind: subject
ignored: []
elements:
- element: stateSpans/ExampleOverride
  result: accepted
- element: extensions/com.example.negotiation.targets
  result: accepted
step you do the hub answers rule case 1 PUT the registration with If-None-Match: * 201 accepted or partial, definitionId, etag, boundTo your subject registration §5, D18 accepted.yaml 2 Expect the checks in order: permission and binding, preconditions, the owner's block, the registration as a whole, then each element 403, 428, 412, 403 blocked-by-owner, 422 or 413 with nothing stored registration §5.2 not-authorised.yaml, blocked-pre-emptive-create.yaml, rejected-limit-exceeded.yaml 3 Read each element's result; write typed only what is accepted or accepted-with-ignored-members, and treat an unknown result or reason as not accepted per-element results; ignored members listed as dotted paths and kept as written registration §6, G1 accepted-with-ignored-members.yaml, extensions-not-interpreted.yaml 4 Declare every extension field with a type; the namespace (com.example.testcontroller.adaptiveTargets) is first to claim per tenant untyped-extension, namespace-claimed or namespace-not-owned for that element only G2, authority §5 accepted-first-to-claim.yaml, rejected-untyped-extension.yaml, rejected-namespace-claimed.yaml 5 Unknown terms in your vocabularies (end reasons, transports, initiators) go in the form {value: other, controllerTerm} rendered "other: term", never a rejection G3, S8 specs/sync/registrations/fixtures/example-testcontroller.yaml 6 Retry a create whose response was lost with the same body 200 noop: true with the stored etag registration §5.4 create-retry-noop.yaml 7 On a controller release, PUT again with If-Match: <etag> 200 and a changed etag; 412 stale-etag if the etag is old registration §5.4 update-accepted.yaml, update-stale-etag.yaml 8 Give an element a new version whenever its meaning changes (a unit, an end encoding, a vocabulary) the same version with another meaning is version-conflict for that element G4, S12, registration §7 instances/product-update-new-version.yaml, instances/product-update-version-conflict.yaml 9 Add a definition for another build that runs beside the release: PUT …/definitions/<definitionId> with If-None-Match: *, where the id is sha256: over the RFC 8785 canonical JSON of the body 201, the product's etag unchanged; 422 definition-id-mismatch when the hash is not the path id registration §7, identity §2 instances/definition-put.yaml, instances/definition-id-mismatch.yaml 10 Retire the product with DELETE and If-Match when the controller stops using it; write carriers from that moment 200 retired; stored data kept; namespaces held until the owner frees them registration §5 retire.yaml

To receive commands, declare it. A kind carries a command-sink role only when it declares acceptsFromHub.channels with command (S10); the cases' override kind does:

channels:
- command
default: false

The fixture's override kind declares the same, so TestController may hold command-sink on the override slot. Its commands[] declares how commands reach it (S11): a path of its own, with an other transport and the hub optional, and the hub's command record (nightscout-commands), with a fetch bound of 60 s and the live transports it listens on for fetch-now signals (CM28, CM29):

- transport:
    value: other
    controllerTerm: example-relay
  hubInPath: optional
  availability: experimental
- transport: nightscout-commands
  hubInPath: 'yes'
  availability: experimental
  fetchIntervalSeconds: 60
  liveTransports:
  - socket
  - value: other
    controllerTerm: example-broker
step you do the hub answers rule case 11 Declare acceptsFromHub with command on each kind you accept commands for, and commands[] for each path commands reach you by; for the hub's command record, a nightscout-commands entry with fetchIntervalSeconds if you fetch more often than once a cycle and the liveTransports you listen on a command-sink claim on any other channel is refused not-a-command-channel S10, S11, CM28, CM29, registration §9 instances/instance-not-a-command-channel.yaml, instances/instance-create.yaml, commands/fetch-bound-declared.yaml

docs.title: 3.3 Create an instance, hold and hand off its lease
docs.text:
An instance is one running copy of your controller: the phone that doses, a development build, a simulator, the old and the new phone during a migration (registration §8). It names a stored definition, claims roles on channels and renews a lease. TestController's override slot is the shared slot override, so it contends with any other product's instance on that slot; its extension's channel is its own, Example/TestController/extensions/com.example.testcontroller.adaptiveTargets.

apiVersion: nightscout.dev/sync/v1
kind: ControllerInstance
definitionId: sha256:ee552930b207551ed46bbbe4e1065e3c67773415193f3a067ef46816201da2ab
roles:
- channel: override
  role: source
  provenance: device
- channel: override
  role: command-sink
  provenance: device
- channel: Example/ControllerA/extensions/com.example.controllera.targets
  role: source
  provenance: device
labels:
  dev.nightscout/purpose: therapy
  dev.nightscout/build: release
step you do the hub answers rule case 1 Generate a random lowercase UUID v4 once per running copy; never derive it from a device name, model or serial 422 invalid-instance-id for any other form identity §2, registration §8 instances/instance-invalid-id.yaml 2 PUT /api/v4/instances/<instanceId> with If-None-Match: *, naming your product (product: {vendor, product}) and a stored definitionId, each role as {channel, role, provenance}, and labels 201 with leaseExpiresAt and a result per role; 422 unknown-definition for a definition the product does not store registration §8, registration §9 instances/instance-create.yaml, instances/instance-unknown-definition.yaml 3 Use labels to distinguish copies: keys are <reverse-DNS namespace>/<name>, dev.nightscout/ is reserved for purpose, build and migration-group; never put names, device names or serials in them 422 invalid-label registration §10 instances/instance-label-not-namespaced.yaml, instances/instance-label-reserved-unknown.yaml 4 Give every role a provenance: device for the copy that doses, simulated for a simulator simulated roles never contend with device roles and are never a command destination registration §9, commands §2 instances/instance-role-simulated.yaml, instances/command-no-destination-simulated.yaml 5 When a role is refused role-held, keep running and write that channel's records as carriers 201 partial; the overlap is shown on the owner's listing registration §9, registration §6 instances/instance-role-held.yaml, instances/instance-overlap-listed.yaml 6 Renew before leaseExpiresAt with If-Match: <instance etag> and the same body 200 noop: true; the lease moves on; a renewal is not a capability re-check registration §8 instances/instance-renew.yaml 7 On 412 at renewal, read the instance and renew again: a role was moved or dropped 412 stale-etag with the current etag registration §8, authority §6 instances/instance-renew-after-transfer-stale.yaml, instances/rebind-release-drops-command-sink.yaml 8 To hand the pump to another phone, delete the old instance, or renew it without the role; the new phone claims the role on its own next renewal, and both may carry one dev.nightscout/migration-group label 200 released; the claimant's renewal is granted registration §9, registration §10 instances/instance-delete.yaml, instances/instance-handoff-release.yaml 9 Expect a holder that stops renewing to lapse; its role goes to no one until a claimant renews, and commands meanwhile have no destination 409 no-command-destination for a command in that window registration §9, commands §2 instances/instance-handoff-lapse.yaml, instances/lapsed-role-not-auto-assigned.yaml 10 Run a development build under its own subject; it gets source roles, and a device command-sink only if the owner transfers it 201 partial, command-sink refused not-registration-owner authority §6 instances/instance-command-sink-not-registration-owner.yaml, instances/owner-transfer-role-other-subject.yaml

A refused role changes the write plan for that channel only. Here the override kind goes as its carrier and the extension stays typed:

stateSpans/ExampleOverride:
  write: carrier
  carrier:
    collection: treatments
    eventType: Temporary Override
    durationField: duration
    durationUnit: minutes
extensions/com.example.controllera.targets:
  write: typed

A lease is minutes long (registration §8), longer than moving a pump to another phone takes, so a command can reach the old phone in that window. §3.5 step 15 says what holds then.

docs.title: 3.4 Write typed records with attribution
docs.text:
On a hub that advertises instances, every typed write names the writing instance (proposed as a request header), and the instance must be live and hold source on the element's channel (registration §11):

as: typed
element: stateSpans/ExampleOverride
instanceId: 00000000-0000-4000-8000-00000000000a

The accepted record carries its instance, its definition and the role's provenance:

accepted: true
as: typed
attributedTo:
  vendor: Example
  product: ControllerA
  instanceId: 00000000-0000-4000-8000-00000000000a
definitionId: sha256:ee552930b207551ed46bbbe4e1065e3c67773415193f3a067ef46816201da2ab
provenance: device
step you do the hub answers rule case 1 Write an accepted element typed, naming your instance 200, attributed to the instance, its definition and its provenance registration §11 instances/typed-write-attributed.yaml 2 Never send a typed write without an instance id to a hub that advertises instances; on 422 instance-required, send that record as its carrier 422 instance-required, a definite refusal registration §11, registration §6 instances/typed-write-instance-required.yaml 3 On 409 role-held or role-not-granted, send that record as its carrier 409 registration §11 instances/typed-write-role-held.yaml 4 On 429 or any 5xx, retry the same record with backoff, no sooner than Retry-After; never write it as its carrier and never drop it the record is stored once when the retry succeeds registration §6 typed-write-load-503.yaml, typed-write-load-429-retry-after.yaml 5 On any other refusal (blocked-by-owner, a typed route answering 404, an unknown 4xx), send that record as its carrier at once and treat the element as not accepted until your next launch or release 403, 404 registration §6 typed-write-blocked-by-owner.yaml, typed-write-route-404.yaml 6 Give every record an identifier that is yours, stable across retries and unique per record; re-send with the same one a matched re-send stores no second copy and is answered with the stored ids I1, I4, I5, I7 quirks/typed-write-resend-same-ids.yaml, quirks/typed-write-assigns-objectid.yaml 7 When the element's carrierView is served, write typed only; when it is not served and the element declares dualWriteLink, write typed and as its carrier older readers see one document either way registration §6, registration §13 accepted-dual-write-view-served.yaml, accepted-dual-write-view-not-served.yaml 8 Write from a simulator under its simulated source role provenance simulated, which default views and exports do not treat as therapy data registration §9, registration §11 instances/typed-write-simulated.yaml 9 Keep writing carriers whatever your roles: exclusivity never blocks a carrier write 200 registration §11 instances/carrier-write-claimant.yaml

How writes are matched, ordered and delivered over REST and the socket is sync-transport; a typed record keeps the definition it was written under (T13).

docs.title: 3.5 Receive a command, check it, enact it once, report the outcome
docs.text:
A command names a channel. The hub sends it to the live device instance holding command-sink on that channel, on the command's tenant, and fixes that destination when it accepts the command (commands §2, CM2). A sender's command, as a case writes it, carries a payload and an expiry:

at: 10
kind: command
tenant: A
subject: s-care
channel: override
product: ControllerA
payload:
  action: start
  preset: example
expiresAt: 600

The capability document's commands member says whether the hub offers the command record, and where (CM31). The paths are proposed in commands §7.1 (CM32): you fetch at GET /api/v4/instances/{instanceId}/commands and report at POST /api/v4/commands/{commandId}/reports. The steps name the operation; the cases model calls, not requests.

step you do the hub answers rule case 1 Hold command-sink with device provenance on each channel you accept commands for (§3.3) the command is routed to you; never to a lapsed holder, a simulator or the newest instance commands §2, CM1, CM2 commands/route-to-holder.yaml, commands/route-lapsed-holder-not-destination.yaml 2 Read the capability document's commands member at launch and after a release; without it the hub offers no command path, so keep your own transports with no member, every command path is 404 CM31 commands/discover-without-commands-capability.yaml, commands/discover-with-commands-capability.yaml 3 Fetch with your own credential, naming your own instance, at least once per cycle or within the fetchIntervalSeconds you declare; a fetch returns each command, and each cancel carried to you, until you report, so a lost reply costs one fetch 200 with your commands only, again until you report; an empty list once you no longer hold the role; 403 not-registration-owner for another instance; the sender sees your bound as fetchWithinSeconds CM18, CM26, CM29, CM30 commands/fetch-returns-own-commands.yaml, commands/fetch-reply-lost-refetch-delivers.yaml, commands/refetch-after-acknowledged-empty.yaml, commands/fetch-after-role-lost-is-empty.yaml, commands/fetch-bound-default-cycle.yaml 4 To fetch sooner than your bound, listen for fetch-now signals on a transport the hub lists in commands.liveTransports and you list in your liveTransports; answer a signal by fetching. A signal carries nothing, and a lost one delays a command until your next fetch a signal goes to your instance only, inside a request bound to your tenant; a platform push only with your tenant's own credential; none when you share no transport with the hub CM27, CM28, CM19, CM20 commands/signal-to-destination-only.yaml, commands/signal-lost-fetch-delivers.yaml, commands/signal-unbound-withheld-under-multi.yaml, commands/signal-platform-push-no-tenant-credential.yaml, commands/signal-without-live-transport.yaml 5 Do not read a signal or fetched as success; only your report sets an outcome the command stays pending after a signal and fetched until you report CM17, CM7 commands/signal-and-fetch-are-not-success.yaml 6 Refuse a command at or past expiresAt by your own clock, with reason expired without your report, a fetched command reads unconfirmed after its expiry CM10, CM3, CM8 commands/enact-after-expiry-refused.yaml 7 Recompute payloadHash (sha256: over the RFC 8785 canonical JSON of the payload you received) and refuse hash-mismatch when it differs from the command's your report is recorded as reported, with the record marked a mismatch CM10, CM7 commands/enact-hash-mismatch-refused.yaml, commands/request-id-reordered-keys-same-hash.yaml 8 Authenticate the sender by your own means where you require it; the hash detects a payload changed in transit or storage, and does not authenticate the sender or show what an approver approved the hub carries authentication material unread CM10, D18 commands/hub-does-not-judge-payload.yaml 9 Apply your own limits and your acceptance preference; refuse with limit or not-accepted the hub never checks a dose, a limit or the therapy state, and never changes the payload CM5, CM8, S10 commands/hub-does-not-judge-payload.yaml, commands/report-after-final-refused.yaml 10 Before enacting a dose or carbs, compare the doses and carbs you hold since the command was made, and refuse doses-since when your own rule says the command is no longer wanted the rule and its threshold are yours CM23, D18 commands/enact-dose-refused-doses-since.yaml, commands/enact-dose-no-doses-since.yaml 11 Decide each commandId once: record it when you first enact or refuse it, keep the record across restarts until expiresAt by your clock, and answer any later delivery without enacting it and without a second report — (a fetch returns a command until you report, so delivery is at least once) CM21, CM26 commands/enact-refetched-once.yaml, commands/enact-after-restart-once.yaml, commands/enact-refused-then-redelivered-ignored.yaml 12 Treat two commandIds with the same payload as two commands; enact-once does not catch a second send, your doses-since check does each is enacted unless your checks refuse it CM21, CM4, CM23 commands/enact-two-commands-same-payload.yaml 13 Report acknowledged if you want the sender to see it (optional), then one final state: succeeded, failed or refused, with the payloadHash you computed, a reason when refused or failed, and when enacted the identity of the record that shows the effect 200; a report from any other subject is 403 not-registration-owner; a state other than the four is 422 invalid-state CM7, CM9 commands/acknowledged-then-succeeded.yaml, commands/report-from-destination-accepted.yaml, commands/report-state-fetched-invalid.yaml 14 Give a reason from the shared list (hash-mismatch, expired, not-accepted, limit, doses-since, cancelled) or as {value: other, controllerTerm}; send one final state only a bare unknown string is 422 invalid-reason; a second final report is 409 already-final CM8, CM9 commands/report-reason-other-accepted.yaml, commands/report-reason-bare-string-invalid.yaml, commands/report-after-final-refused.yaml 15 When you hand the pump to another phone with a command outstanding: a command the old phone fetched stays with it, which decides it and reports; one it never fetched becomes undeliverable, whatever signals were sent, and nothing is re-routed your report is accepted from the destination's bound subject even after the role moved CM2, CM7, CM9 commands/fetched-before-holder-changes.yaml, commands/undeliverable-not-rerouted.yaml, commands/fetched-then-lapse-report-accepted.yaml, commands/signalled-then-lapse-undeliverable.yaml 16 Expect no cancel for a command cancelled before hand-over: it is final and never delivered the sender gets 200 cancelled; your fetch returns nothing CM25 commands/cancel-pending-is-final.yaml 17 When a fetch carries a cancel for a command you have not decided, refuse it with reason cancelled and report; when you have already decided it, your outcome stands. Each fetch carries the cancel until you report the sender got 202 with cancelRequested; after your final report a cancel is 409 already-final CM25, CM21, CM26 commands/cancel-after-fetch-is-a-request.yaml, commands/cancel-carried-until-report.yaml, commands/cancel-after-outcome-refused.yaml

A command fetched twice before a report, decided once (step 11). The answers below follow the case's calls in order: the sender's command, the first fetch, the first enactment, the next fetch that returns the command again, and the second enactment, answered ignored with nothing enacted:

- status: 201
  commandId: c1
  state: pending
  fetchWithinSeconds: 30
- status: 200
  commands:
  - c1
- state: succeeded
- status: 200
  commands:
  - c1
- state: ignored
  reason: duplicate

A cancel after hand-over (step 17). The answers follow the case's calls in order: the sender's command, your fetch, the sender's cancel (202), your next fetch carrying the cancel, your refusal and your report:

- status: 201
  commandId: c1
  state: pending
  fetchWithinSeconds: 30
- status: 200
  commands:
  - c1
- status: 202
  state: fetched
  cancelRequested: true
- status: 200
  commands: []
  cancels:
  - c1
- state: refused
  reason: cancelled
- status: 200

A refusal reported in the controller's own term (step 14):

at: 20
kind: report
tenant: A
subject: s-ctl-a
command: c1
state: refused
reason:
  value: other
  controllerTerm: example-busy

A command may also come from an approved proposal; it reaches you the same way and carries the proposal's proposalId and basedOn (CM13). The hub checks the proposal's state version and the doses that reached it after the proposal (CM15, CM22); those checks see the hub's record, which lags your upload, and do not replace yours (CM23).

docs.title: 4. What older hubs and older apps see
docs.text:
The compatibility table says, for every app the corpus holds and every layer, what the app does today and what it sees from a hub that implements the specifications; its overview, its L3 table and where an answer changes are the parts a controller author reads first. For TestController:

who sees rule case a hub with no capability document today's documents, written as carriers; nothing is negotiated registration §17 older-hub-no-capabilities.yaml, instances/carrier-write-older-hub.yaml a hub with capabilities and no instances typed writes with no instance id; no roles and no command destination registration §17 instances/typed-write-hub-without-instances.yaml a hub with no commands member in its capability document no hub command path; commands reach you only by the transports you have CM31 commands/discover-without-commands-capability.yaml an older reader or follower on API v1 or v3, where the element's view is served a projected document in the carrier's shape, labelled projectedFrom, read-only registration §13, I8 instances/project-served.yaml, instances/write-projected-read-only.yaml the same reader where no view is served the carrier you dual-write, linked to the typed record registration §6, registration §13 accepted-dual-write-view-not-served.yaml, instances/project-no-mapping.yaml an older controller of another product on the shared override slot its writes go to its product's unregistered instance and are never refused for exclusivity registration §11, Q2 instances/carrier-write-older-controller.yaml, newer-hub-older-controller.yaml a follower that reads the queue each open proposal and command not yet final on a channel, with its sender and the doses and carbs since CM24 commands/outstanding-lists-open-items.yaml, commands/outstanding-excludes-final.yaml

Follower apps read today (LoopFollow, LoopCaregiver, nightguard) do not read the outstanding list; the table marks the command record and the list opt-in for them.

docs.title: 5. Checklist
docs.text:
• The capability document is read at launch and after each release; with none, no submit, an unlisted grammar major or no instances, the controller writes carriers.
  • Every element in the registration is typed where it must be, versioned where its meaning can change, and uses {value: other, controllerTerm} for terms outside the shared lists.
  • Each kind that takes commands declares acceptsFromHub with command, and commands[] lists how commands reach the controller.
  • Each running copy has its own random UUID v4, a provenance on every role, labels without names or serials, and renews its lease before it lapses; a 412 at renewal is followed by a read.
  • A refused role or element sends that channel's or element's records as carriers; a load refusal is retried, never written as a carrier.
  • Every record has an identifier unique to it and stable across retries.
  • Fetch is implemented, at least once per cycle or within the declared fetchIntervalSeconds; a fetch-now signal is answered with a fetch and carries nothing.
  • Before enacting: the hash, the expiry by the controller's own clock, its limits and acceptance preference, and the doses and carbs since the command was made.
  • Each commandId is decided once, recorded across restarts until its expiry, and reported once with one final state and a reason from the shared list or in the other form.
  • A cancel carried by a fetch refuses a command not yet decided; a command already decided keeps its outcome.

docs.title: 6. Where to go next
docs.text:
• Plans: a recurring intent approved once, held and run by the controller and mirrored by the hub.
  • Commands §9 and the control-loop analysis: what is open, including a late failure after succeeded and an outcome per part of a command.
  • Command journeys: caregivers, followers and agents acting on one pump, step by step.

docs.title: Gaps
docs.text:
Steps this guide needs that no rule or no case covers:

  1. The effect record in a report. CM7 asks a report of an enacted command to carry the identity of the record that shows the effect; no case shows a report with it.

docs.title: Writing to storage through write(intent)
docs.text:
Living document, last changed 2026-10-27 at 32e337cc6.

Contributor-facing guide for cgm-remote-monitor's write step (queue WC-STEP-PATCH). Drafted 2026-10-27 against local branch feat/write-intent a0e7fcac (slices 1-3). It moves into the cgm-remote-monitor repository with the step's first pull request. Design: write-contract spec §2, design note.

docs.title: The rule
docs.text:
A write rule goes into lib/storage/write-intent.js, not into a route. A write rule is anything that decides what gets stored for a write: the form of _id, which stored record a write targets, whether a match merges, replaces or is refused, server dates (srvCreated, srvModified), unit conversion, validation, removal of duplicates. Routes (API v1, API v3, the socket, in-process callers) say what they want written and pass it to the step; they do not call the storage adapter's write methods.

Why: when the same rule lives in each route, a fix lands on one path and misses another. BF-194's unit conversion had to be added in four places, and WRITE_VALIDATION sits in five. The step puts each rule in one place.

docs.title: How a route writes
docs.text:
const writeIntent = require('../storage/write-intent');
const step = writeIntent.forCollection(storage, 'food', 'v1/internal');

const result = await step.write({ op: 'create', docs: [doc] });
// result.items: one per document, in order:
//   { index, outcome, _id, identifier, reason }
//   outcome is one of: inserted, merged, replaced, unchanged, deleted, not-found, refused

Operations today: create and update (with docs), and delete (with target: { _id }). The source name ('v1/internal', 'socket') selects that path's rules.

docs.title: How rules are written
docs.text:
Each collection has a row in COLLECTION_RULES, keyed by source and operation. A row is data, built from a small vocabulary defined in the same file:

field what it says values today id the _id form to write under stored-or-new, objectid-or-new, stored-string-or-objectid target the filter that names an existing record id-eq, id-plain, none onMatch what happens when a record matches replaced (release 1) twins removing a record stored under the other spelling of the same id remove-string-forms, remove-string-forms-after dates server dates carry, stamp-created, none write the storage call default bulk replace, replace-one, insert-one delete target which stored forms a delete removes every-form, id-match

To change a rule, change the row. To add a rule the vocabulary lacks, add a named entry to the vocabulary and use it from the row, rather than writing code in a route.

Release-2 variants. Release 1 changes no behaviour, so where two paths do the same job differently today, the table keeps both, for example remove-string-forms and remove-string-forms-after. Each such variant carries a comment // release-2: Q-x, naming the queue item (WC-R2-QA ... WC-R2-QH) that will unify it. Do not "tidy" a variant without that item's decision.

docs.title: Enrolling a module
docs.text:
1. Route the module's writes through forCollection(...).write(...).
  2. Add the module (or, in a file that still has other writers, the functions) to ENROLLED in scripts/check-write-intent.js (G2). G2 then fails if the module calls a write method directly.
  3. Prove nothing changed (below).

docs.title: Proving nothing changed
docs.text:
From the alignment repository, with a MongoDB the worktree's tests use:

WC_WORKTREE=<your worktree> WC_MONGO=mongodb://127.0.0.1:<port> \
  node tools/qc/write-contract-matrix.js --out after.json
node tools/qc/write-contract-matrix.js --compare tools/qc/results/write-contract-matrix/dev-db3b9e4e-v2.json after.json

G1 must report 0 differing cells, setting aside the cache field, which is racy (more so for records seeded straight into MongoDB). The v2 pin (456 cells) adds forms for an update over a stored string twin, a failed _id read on the socket, and deletes by a custom or numeric _id; its 360 older cells equal the first pin. A differing cell is a behaviour change: stop and find out why, and never edit the pin to make it pass. Then:

  • break each rule you moved and show the matrix (or, where no matrix form reaches it, a test) goes red only where you expect;
  • run npm test and node scripts/test-tiers.js check;
  • run node tools/queue/gates/write-rule-copies.js --ref <your branch> in the alignment repository. The count of write-rule copies outside the step may only go down.

docs.title: What the step does not do
docs.text:
• It does not emit or change storage-write-committed. That event belongs to the persistence boundary below the storage interface (lib/storage/write-step.js), and its contents are an open decision (D-EVENT).
  • It does not call the driver. It calls the storage interface.
  • Routes keep authorization, request parsing and reply shaping.
