Red on 699eb5fa and v15.0.8 (10): a late v3 bolus in IOB, late v3 carbs in COB, a late v3 bolus after PATCH and PUT, the page data over the socket, time order with mixed v1 and v3 writes, "last carbs" after an edit (BF-133), the COB total against the time-ordered one; a late v3 status in the default v1 device status read, the whole held set read in time order, and the same with DENORMALIZE_DATES on (which rewrites created_at in place on the cached records; mills still matches the record's time over repeated reads). Green on all trees (5): a v1 bolus of the same age, a v3 bolus dated now, a v1 status of the same age in its place, a v3 status dated now first, and the page data holding the late v3 status with its time. Break-it: deriving the fields and then dropping mills gives the same red (7 for treatments, 3 for device status); deriving them only on create turns the PATCH/PUT test red; leaving device status out (db99bba4) gives the 3 device status tests red. Full suite 3473/0/3 on a fresh database (699eb5fa 3458/0/3; db99bba4 3467/0/3), no existing test changed. Treatment probes (same-time-carbs, same-time-resend-shapes, retry-keeps-srvcreated, v1-writes-v3-history) give the same output on 699eb5fa, db99bba4 and d235bdf6; v1-writes-v3-history exits 1 on its v1 DELETE arm on all of them.

Not measured. Chart placement (the renderer uses a record's own date before mills), temporary basals from v3 in the basal display, and reports (which read MongoDB, not the cache). Older releases: the v3 wrapper emits the stored document since 14.1.0 (read, not run).

docs.title: BF-147 · two overrides hold ajv and request's form-data inside advisory ranges
docs.text:
overrides["ajv@^6.0.0"] = "6.12.6" was set by 907fc5b4 ("Fix dev-mode bundle after PR #8518 merge: scope ajv overrides by version", 2026-05-14). GHSA-2g4f-4pwh-qvx6 (ReDoS with the $data option) was published on 2026-02-11 and ajv 6.14.0, its fix for the 6.x line, on 2026-02-20, so the value was inside the advisory's range when it was written. overrides.request["form-data"] = "2.5.5" came with 5ab0af7a (2026-05-10), when 2.5.5 was the newest 2.x; form-data 2.5.6 was released on 2026-06-12 and GHSA-hmw2-7cc7-3qxx (CRLF injection through multipart field names and filenames) was published on 2026-06-15, so this pin went stale after it was written. Both are on v15.0.8 and on dev 295f1177.

Because overrides takes precedence over every declared range, npm audit cannot propose the patch releases: it reports form-data (and through it request, minimed-connect-to-nightscout and share2nightscout-bridge) as having no fix, and the ajv finding (with har-validator, schema-utils, style-loader, eslint and @eslint/eslintrc) as needing style-loader 4, a major. Nothing reports that the override is the cause. This is the BF-43 and BF-87 mechanism a third time.

Reach. ajv 6 is loaded by webpack loader option validation (schema-utils), by eslint, and by har-validator inside request. The webpack schemas are the repository's own configuration. form-data 2.x is reached only through request, which only minimed-connect-to-nightscout (mmconnect) and share2nightscout-bridge load; in 15.0.9 the bridge runs only with DEXCOM_BRIDGE_USE_LEGACY=true (lib/server/bootevent.js, lib/server/bridge-connect-compat.js). Neither package builds a multipart body (read from node_modules/share2nightscout-bridge/index.js and node_modules/minimed-connect-to-nightscout/nightscout.js). Exploitability through Nightscout is not measured; severity low.

Merged 2026-09-27 via PR #8786 (merge 7000eb18, 20:40Z; head 64a9cc13 on bf/override-advisory-pins, one commit on 295f1177). npm audit --package-lock-only on origin/dev 7000eb18: 7 (7 moderate), 5 with --omit=dev. The fix as run before the push: override values 6.14.0 and 2.5.6, then npm update browserslist baseline-browser-mapping postcss-selector-parser (their fixes are inside the declared ranges; the lockfile is stale, no override is involved). npm audit --package-lock-only goes from 17 (1 low, 13 moderate, 3 high) to 7 (7 moderate). Nine lockfile versions change, all patch or minor: ajv 6.12.6 → 6.14.0, request/node_modules/form-data 2.5.5 → 2.5.6, browserslist 4.28.2 → 4.29.1, baseline-browser-mapping 2.10.29 → 2.11.26, postcss-selector-parser 7.1.1 → 7.1.6, and caniuse-lite, electron-to-chromium, node-releases, update-browserslist-db with them. npm ci and the bundle build succeed (webpack 5.106.2, 3 warnings, as in RC runs 018 to 020); the full suite is 3473 passing, 0 failing, 3 pending on Node 24.15.0 with MongoDB 7.0.43 (a dedicated container, version read with db.version()), the same as RC run 020. Only one Node/MongoDB cell was run. The commit adds tests/dependency-overrides.test.js, which checks the resolved ajv 6 copies (under har-validator, style-loader's schema-utils and eslint) and request's form-data, and that form-data escapes line breaks in multipart field names and filenames: 5/5 on the branch, 0/5 on 295f1177's installed tree, each failing on the old version or the unescaped header. It was written after the suite run and was run on its own.

On the modernization line the question disappears: rh/cut2 02205d91 has neither finding, and rh/cut4 135faa3b, rh/cut35 cd93d8e8 and cut 5 b1bdaca0 audit at 0 including dev dependencies.

A gate that fails when an overrides value satisfies a published advisory range would have caught BF-87 and this entry; tools/qc/connector-pin-agreement-gate.js (which found BF-43) checks declared ranges only.

docs.title: BF-164 · writes outside API v3 never reach the v3 storage socket
docs.text:
Reproduced 2026-10-07 on dev 43289dde and v15.0.8 92d08342 by tools/qc/write-contract-matrix.js, which boots the shipping module and subscribes a real client to /storage. Every v1, socket and in-process write cell recorded wire: none (0 of 190 on dev); v3 create in the same run recorded wire: create, which is the control that the subscriber was live and listening. The emitters are the v3 handlers only (row, where).

BF-122 made these writes visible to API v3 history by stamping srvModified on every path; a client that polls history therefore sees them. A client that relies on the socket instead does not. Consumer, read, not run: AndroidAPS NSClientV3 defaults ns_use_ws on and stops polling after its first load, so on a site that also takes v1 writes (careportal, Loop, Trio, xDrip+, nightscout-connect) it would miss those treatments, readings and temp targets until it reloads. Fix direction: one change event per write from every path, which is item 5 of WRITE-CONTRACT (plan §4.1); a narrower fix on dev emits the storage-socket event from the shared data-update path. Evidence: write-contract spec §1.5, §7 C4.

Reclassified 2026-10-12 (maintainer): under question, not a defect to fix yet. The AndroidAPS authors indicate the v3-only emission may be intended, because API v3 validates what it accepts and v1 does not. Against that, read on dev fade2299: v3 reads and v3 history already return records from every path (BF-122), so the omission changes when AndroidAPS sees a v1 record, not whether [contradicted 2026-10-25 for websocket-mode AndroidAPS, below]; and the header of lib/api3/storageSocket.js (from #4250, 2019) calls it a "broadcaster of any storage change". Two things settle it: a lab run of AndroidAPS NSClientV3 in websocket mode timing the arrival of a v1-written carb (never, on reconnect, or after a reload interval), and the AndroidAPS authors' answer to whether the storage socket announcing v1, socket and careportal writes would help or harm them. Until then the write contract does not change the emissions (spec §6 Q6).

Re-measured 2026-10-27 on dev dcf20bfb (session -4f, same lab, MongoDB 8.0.34): all 11 cells as in the table below, so the seam slices and #8854 changed nothing here. The AndroidAPS cursor rule is unchanged on its dev 22fb0eeac2 (read). The maintainer's 2026-10-27 framing: AndroidAPS receiving only API v3 writes over the socket is intended by its authors, because API v1 accepts loosely typed records that v3 was meant to eliminate. What remains is that the same record is delivered through catch-up history unless a v3 write in that collection lands first. Delivery therefore depends on timing, not on a v3-only rule.

Lab, 2026-10-25 (session f4's API v3 contract lane; dev b29f1bf7, Node v22.23.4, two real servers, nightscout-connect 0.1.0 writing into one of them, MongoDB 8.0.34). The client follows AndroidAPS's websocket mode as read from its source: subscribe; a catch-up history round on every (re)connect; no polling while the socket is up; each pushed frame sets the collection's history cursor to that document's srvModified (ws/NsFrameHandler.kt:105-111). AndroidAPS itself was not run.

write path socket up, 45 s reconnect, no v3 write in that collection between reconnect after a v3 write in that collection v3 create (control) received in 0.01–0.05 s — — v1 (the careportal's path) not received received through catch-up history not received; the record is in v3 history main socket dbAdd not received received through catch-up history not received; the record is in v3 history nightscout-connect (in process) not received received through catch-up history not received

The pushed v3 frame moves the cursor past the earlier record's srvModified, and the catch-up round asks for history after the cursor, so the earlier non-v3 record is delivered only by a full sync. On a site where the master uploads through API v3, a websocket-mode follower can therefore miss careportal, v1-uploader and connector records, not only receive them late; the 2026-10-12 line above is contradicted for that mode. The question to the AndroidAPS developers is drafted (one combined note with BF-152's, not sent). No code change yet (maintainer, 2026-10-25).

Decided 2026-10-25 (maintainer, "plan C"). /storage stays v3-only for now. Records from the other write paths will be announced on it only after write checks (log mode, MOD-WRITE-VALIDATION) cover every write path, and then only records that pass the type checks; there is no unfiltered broadcast. The evidence is session f4's AndroidAPS-side safety research, at mechanism level: records from the other paths already reach AndroidAPS through history; some of them cannot be decoded by AndroidAPS; and a pushed frame that AndroidAPS 3.4.2.6 cannot decode is expected to end the app process (read-derived, not run). The note to the AndroidAPS developers is now drafted as a public issue and a private report; neither is sent. Queue state: blocked on that coverage; the filter and path-naming details are still open for decision.

docs.title: BF-165 · a treatment re-send matched by its fallback key is answered without _id
docs.text: Reproduced 2026-10-07, both refs: matrix cells treatments v1 resend-identity and treatments inproc resend-identity answer 200 with one document carrying no _id; the data-update document lacks it too, and cache.js keeps only documents with _id (read). Consumer, read, not run: NightscoutKit stores "NA" when the reply has no _id, and skips a later PUT/DELETE for that id, so Loop cannot later edit or delete the retried entry on the site. Fix direction: answer with the stored record (its _id and identifier), which is the identical-re-send rule proposed in the write-contract spec §3. Evidence: §7 C3.

docs.title: BF-166 · a profile re-sent with its own _id answers 500
docs.text: Reproduced 2026-10-07, both refs: profile v1 resend-hex answers HTTP 500 and profile inproc resend-hex raises a duplicate-key error; nothing is stored twice. BF-116 fixed the same shape for devicestatus (200, nothing written). Evidence: write-contract spec §7 C7.

docs.title: BF-167 · devicestatus remove()'s filter is not pinned by any test
docs.text: Reproduced 2026-10-07 on dev 43289dde: with two matching records, one soft-deleted, tools/lab/seam-propagation/ds-remove-softdeleted.js reports deletedCount 2; swapping stored_query_for for query_for in remove() gives 1, and the full suite stays 3564/0. The fix is test-only: assert that remove() deletes soft-deleted records too. Evidence: seam propagation rehearsal §7 C3.

docs.title: BF-169 · API v3's swagger says clients must not supply identifier; the server keeps one
docs.text: Reproduced 2026-10-17 at module level on v15.0.8 92d08342 and dev fade2299: resolveIdentifier from lib/api3/shared/operationTools.js, given a document with identifier: "client-supplied-0001", keeps it and calls console.warn once; given the same document without one, it sets the UUID v5 that calculateIdentifier returns. Create's validation (generic/create/validate.js:19) requires only a non-empty string. Not run over HTTP. lib/api3/doc/ and README.md at fade2299 do not repeat the sentence. Fix: in both swagger files, say the server computes an identifier from device, date and eventType when the client sends none and keeps one the client sends; keep the immutability note. Documentation only.

docs.title: BF-170 · API v3 stores a client's 24-hex body _id as a string
docs.text:
Mechanism. API v3 create (lib/api3/generic/create/operation.js:35-37 at v15.0.8 92d08342 and dev fade2299) purifies the body, parses the date and resolves identifier, then either replaces a matched record or inserts (:55). insert.js adds server dates and subject and calls col.storage.insertOne(doc); mongoCollection/modify.js:12-21 passes the document to MongoDB's insertOne unchanged. No step reads _id, so a 24-hex body _id is stored as that string, in the case it was sent. v3 addresses records by identifier and never returns _id, so a v3 client sees nothing wrong.

Reproduction. tools/lab/record-identity (results 2026-10-18), cases "v3 treatments POST: 24-hex _id in body, no identifier" and "v3 treatments POST: identifier + 24-hex _id in body": 201, stored n=1 [_id:string=sent …] on both builds. The write-contract matrix (tools/qc/results/write-contract-matrix/, v15.0.8-92d08342.json and dev-43289dde.json) has the same for entries, treatments, devicestatus, profile and food: <col> v3 resend-hex stores str, <col> v3 resend-upper stores STR (upper-case string).

15.0.8 against dev. The write is the same on both. What differs is v1 afterwards, and that is read, not measured: on 15.0.8 find[_id]=<hex> becomes an ObjectId equality (lib/server/query.js:95-123, 131-134), so it misses the string record, as the by-id routes that convert with ObjectID() do (the BF-99 to BF-102 pattern; the lab's "devicestatus v1 GET find[_id]=" case measures that miss on 15.0.8 for a string stored by v1). On dev, matchEitherForm (lib/server/object-id-forms.js:108-113) widens that equality to the ObjectId, the lower-case hex and the spelling asked, so v1 finds the record, except an upper-case string asked for in lower case (the module's stated limit). On dev this is the one HTTP path that still creates string _ids; the module's header says upper-case ones exist only from older releases.

Reach. Low. No client in the corpus sends _id to API v3 (write-contract note §7, C1). The Loop reply's rule 1 says a client-created ObjectId _id holds over API v1 only; on v3 a client uses identifier.

Fix direction, options, not decided. (a) v3 create converts a 24-hex body _id to the ObjectId it names, as v1 does on dev since #8758 (object-id-forms.toStoredId); natural in the one storage-level rule of OID-STORAGE-HELPER. (b) v3 refuses a body _id with 400, as the field is not part of its contract. (c) v3 drops a body _id and lets MongoDB assign one. (a) keeps every stored byte except the _id type and case; (b) refuses an input that answers 201 today. Either way, C2 of the same note (a {"$oid": …} body _id answers 500) is the same code path.

docs.title: BF-171 · a bearer token whose subject was deleted stops the server — merged 2026-10-20 (PR #8815)
docs.text:
Mechanism. A JWT is signed with the key lib/server/enclave.js:30 reads from node_modules/.cache/_ns_cache/randomString, written at install or bundle time, so a restart keeps it and a rebuild replaces it; tokens live 8 h (:59). The JWT carries the subject's access token. authorization.resolve (lib/authorization/index.js on v15.0.8 92d08342; dev fade2299 in brackets) verifies the JWT, and whenever it verifies, counts the request as a success and returns what resolveAccessToken returns (:202-206; :207-211). resolveAccessToken returns null when no stored subject has that access token (:231; :255). Every caller then reads .shiros from that null: API v1's isPermitted (:260; :284), the websocket authorize handler (lib/server/websocket.js:135; :142), the alarm socket subscribe (lib/api3/alarmSocket.js:131-132; :233-234) and verifyauth and adminnotifies through resolveWithRequest. The throw happens inside the async resolve (or the async check), so it is an unhandled rejection, which stops the process on Node 15 and later. API v3 checks the result before reading it and answers 403.

Why it loops. Boot loads the subjects before the server listens (lib/server/bootevent.js setupAuthorization, then lib/server/server.js listen), so a restart comes up cleanly. A client that keeps its JWT (followers' apps poll every few minutes) sends it again and the server stops again. The client cannot get a new token, because its subject is gone, so the loop ends when the token expires (at most 8 h after it was issued), when the client is stopped, or when a rebuild replaces the signing key.

Two triggers. The database is dropped or restored without its subjects, then the server restarts without a rebuild (issue #8225); or an admin deletes a subject, that is, revokes a token, while the server runs. The second needs nothing unusual.

Reproduced 2026-10-20 on a dedicated MongoDB 7.0.43 container, Node 24.15.0, AUTH_DEFAULT_ROLES=denied (the probe is held outside version control):

build API v1 request with the token after a restart, 3 times websocket authorize API v3 v15.0.8 92d08342 server exits exits each time not run 403 dev fade2299 server exits exits each time server exits 403 #8815 93a74ce5 401, server up 401 each time refused, server up 401

Each exit logs TypeError: Cannot read properties of null (reading 'shiros') from isPermitted. #8815's three tests in tests/api.security.test.js, copied onto fade2299, fail there (two time out, one fails its assertion) and pass on 93a74ce5 (19 passing).

Since when. Read, not run: before #6596 (7fe8e321, 2020-12-11, first released in 14.1.0 on 2021-01-06) resolve handed a missing subject to its callback as an error, and isPermitted read the shiros of resolveSubjectAndPermissions, an empty list, so the request fell back to the default roles. 14.0.7's lockfile no longer installs, so it was not run. From 14.1.0 the defect is present in every release; on Node 12 and 14, the supported runtimes then, an unhandled rejection only warns, so the request hung instead of stopping the server. 15.0.0 (2023-10-18) supports Node 16, and dev requires Node 20 or later.

Fix. #8815: resolve accepts the token only when resolveAccessToken finds a subject; otherwise it takes the existing failed-credential path (the failed-request delay for that address, the "Failed authentication" admin notification, 'All validation failed' and {}), so callers get the same answer as for a wrong token. API v3 answers 401 instead of 403 for such a token. Not done there, and not needed for the fix: a guard in each caller against a result without shiros, and wording in the admin notification for a token whose subject is gone.

docs.title: BF-172 · the Bolus Wizard Preview mixes profile units with display units — merged 2026-10-25 (PR #8819), known issue of 15.0.9
docs.text:
Mechanism. boluswizardpreview.calc (lib/plugins/boluswizardpreview.js, identical on v15.0.8 92d08342 and dev 4bca2ac2) takes the last reading scaled to the site's display units (sbx.lastScaledSGV(), :153) and subtracts iob * profile.getSensitivity() (:167), then compares the outcome with getHighBGTarget() and getLowBGTarget() and divides by getSensitivity() (:178-197). The profile functions return the values as the profile stores them, in the profile's own units; nothing in the plugin converts them. When the two units are the same, as on most sites, the arithmetic is right. When they differ, the sensitivity and targets are off by the mg/dL↔mmol/L factor (18.0156), so the estimate, the "aiming at" target line (:304), the target line (:252) and the BWP warning, whose high-target test (:89) uses the same unconverted target, are wrong.

Reproduced 2026-10-21, in the plugin's own unit harness (tests/boluswizardpreview.test.js, which runs the real plugin, sandbox and profile functions), Node 24.15.0, not in a browser: #8819's new test, copied onto each tree, sets an mmol/L profile (sensitivity 3, targets 5 to 7) on an mg/dL site with a 250 mg/dL reading and 1.0 U on board.

tree estimate test v15.0.8 92d08342 80 U fails (expected 1.29 U ± 0.01) dev 4bca2ac2 80 U fails (expected 1.29 U ± 0.01) dev 4bca2ac2 with #8819's boluswizardpreview.js 1.29 U passes (14 passing)

The reverse case (an mg/dL profile on an mmol/L site) was read, not run.

Since when. Read, not run: the plugin has never converted profile units; it is not a 15.0.9 regression. BF-124 (#8801, tooltip BG) and BF-138 (#8777, /pebble) fixed the same kind of unit mix elsewhere.

Disposition. Known issue of 15.0.9 by the maintainer's decision of 2026-10-21; #8819 converts the sensitivity and both targets to the display units before use, as lib/plugins/basalprofile.js does for sensitivity. It is based on fade2299 and needs dev merged in before it lands.

Since when, by history (added 2026-10-21). The plugin arrived in 0.8.0 (c298320d, 2015-05-24); profiles gained units later in the same release (26a0d40c, 2015-07-13, getUnits). The plugin was written when the profile's values were the site's units and was never changed when the label arrived. The same kind of mix was fixed one consumer at a time in basalprofile.js (#5102, 2019), lastEnacted.bg (a4e05a16, 2024), the treatment tooltip (BF-124) and /pebble (BF-138); the Careportal Bolus Wizard has it still (BF-173).

Review notes on #8819 at 18319a9f (read, and run where stated).

  • getUnits(sbx.time) passes a time where getUnits takes a profile name. Today the name is ignored (BF-174), so it has no effect. With BF-174's fix the number is not a name in the store and falls back to the active profile, so #8819's test still passes: run 2026-10-21 on a scratch merge of bf/profile-spec-honoured, bf/boluscalc-profile-units and #8819 on dev 4bca2ac2, 266 passing across the profile, bolus calculator, Careportal, BWP, IOB, COB and plugin suites. Dropping the argument is clearer.
  • Converted values are not rounded, so the pop-up would show a target such as 90.078 and a sensitivity such as -54.0468 mg/dl/U. basalprofile.js and BF-173's fix round to 1 mg/dl or 0.1 mmol/L.
  • The reverse case (an mg/dl profile on an mmol/L site) has no test.
  • It fixes one of the two calculators; BF-173 is the other. The boundary these three share is the subject of the glucose units design note.

docs.title: BF-173 · the Careportal Bolus Wizard mixes profile units with display units — merged 2026-10-25 (PR #8825), a known issue of 15.0.9
docs.text:
Mechanism. boluscalc.gatherBoluscalcData (lib/client/boluscalc.js) loads getLowBGTarget, getHighBGTarget and getSensitivity for the chosen profile (:361-372) and uses them against record.bg, which is in the display units: the sensor reading is scaled by client.utils.scaleMgdl (:71) and a typed value is taken as entered. The correction is (bg - target) / isf (:409-420). When the profile's units differ from client.settings.units (each viewer's setting, starting from the site's DISPLAY_UNITS) the targets and sensitivity are off by the mg/dl to mmol/L factor. The result is shown as the suggested insulin and saved in the Bolus Wizard treatment with the values used.

Reproduced 2026-10-21 in the headless client (tests/fixtures/headless.js, which loads the webpack bundle built from the tree under test, jsdom, Node 24.15.0; not a browser). Each tree's bundle was built from its own source; a first run that used another tree's bundle through a shared node_modules was discarded. Display units set on the client, a 250 mg/dl reading, no IOB, no carbs:

display units profile BG entered v15.0.8 92d08342 dev 4bca2ac2 dev + fix ee0cc4f7 right answer mg/dl mg/dl, sens 54, 90–126 250 2.30 U 2.30 U 2.30 U 2.30 U mmol mmol, sens 3, 5–7 13.9 2.30 U 2.30 U 2.30 U 2.30 U mg/dl mmol, sens 3, 5–7 250 81 U 81 U 2.30 U 2.29 U mmol mg/dl, sens 54, 90–126 13.9 −1.41 U −1.41 U 2.30 U 2.30 U

The fix converts to the display units and rounds to 1 mg/dl or 0.1 mmol/L, as basalprofile.js does and as the values are shown, so the mmol/L-profile case gives 2.30 U (sensitivity 54, target 126) where the unrounded arithmetic gives 2.29 U.

Since when. The calculator arrived in 0.9.0 (71b09361, d0cb934e, 2015) and has never converted units (git log -S MMOL_TO_MGDL -- lib/client/boluscalc.js finds only the fix).

Fix. bf/boluscalc-profile-units ee0cc4f7, one commit on dev 4bca2ac2 (+11 in boluscalc.js; 4 tests added to tests/careportal.test.js, which already hosts the calculator's tests and its headless setup; a separate headless test file breaks the next headless suite in the same mocha process). Break-it: on a bundle without the fix the two mismatch tests fail (expected 3 to be 54, expected 54 to be approximately 3) and the two same-unit controls pass. 257 passing across the profile, bolus calculator, Careportal, BWP, basal profile, IOB, COB, plugins, profile editor, units, sandbox, Loop and OpenAPS suites. Not pushed; worktree externals/work/crm-bf173.

docs.title: BF-174 · the bolus calculator's profile picker is ignored — merged 2026-10-25 (PR #8826), a known issue of 15.0.9
docs.text:
Mechanism. profile.getCurrentProfile(time, spec_profile) (lib/profilefunctions.js:200-220 on dev 4bca2ac2) takes the profile from activeProfileToTime(time) and uses spec_profile only in its cache key. getValueByTime, and so getSensitivity, getCarbRatio, the targets and getDIA, and getUnits, all go through it. The bolus calculator passes the picker's value as spec_profile (lib/client/boluscalc.js:347-367, and to iob.calcTotal and cob.cobTotal), saves it as record.profile, and gets the active profile's values whichever profile was chosen. No other caller passes a name.

Since when. 0.9.0 (d0cb934e, 2015-10-30) read spec_profile || activeProfileToTime(time).

docs.title: 5572 (802d9868, 2020-06-12) returned spec_profile itself, the name rather than the profile;
5729 (7283560e, 2020-07-02, "Fix for boluscalc issue") removed that branch. Both are first in
docs.text:
14.0.0. Read from history, not run on those releases.

Reproduced 2026-10-21 in the headless client, as BF-173: two profiles in the store (Default sensitivity 54, carb ratio 10; Other 27 and 5), Other chosen. On v15.0.8 92d08342 and dev 4bca2ac2 the record says profile: 'Other' with isf: 54; with the fix, isf: 27, ic: 5 and a correction of 4.59 U.

Fix. bf/profile-spec-honoured 292f909a, one commit on dev 4bca2ac2 (+5/−1 in profilefunctions.js; tests/profile.spec-profile.test.js, 5 tests; 2 tests in tests/careportal.test.js). A string that names a store entry is used; anything else, including a name not in the store and a number, gives the active profile as before. Break-its: without the fix the named-profile unit test fails (expected 54 to be 1.5) and the picker test fails (expected 54 to be 27); the controls pass. 260 passing across the same suites as BF-173. Not pushed; worktree externals/work/crm-bf174.

Effect of the fix, read. getValueByTime skips the CircadianPercentageProfile and AndroidAPS profile-switch adjustments whenever spec_profile is set, and the bolus calculator always sets it, so the calculator already uses the unadjusted profile today; the fix does not change that. Whether the calculator should apply an active switch's percentage is a separate question, not run.

docs.title: BF-175 · temp targets converted from mmol/L only on an exact 'mmol' — closed 2026-10-25, not a defect
docs.text:
Mechanism. ddata.processTreatments converts temp targets with convertTempTargetTreatmentUnites (lib/data/ddata.js:455-485 on dev 04d435eb). It converts targetTop and targetBottom from mmol/L to mg/dL when t.units == 'mmol' (:466), an exact comparison, so a record whose units are spelled mmol/L takes the other path. That path converts any record with a target below 20, whatever its units say, and marks it mg/dL. A temp target in mmol/L is below 20 in practice, so the fallback reaches the same result. The same comparison is at :320 on v15.0.8 92d08342.

Status. Read, not run. Found 2026-10-21 next to BF-157, which has the same exact comparison in the chart and report and is fixed on bf/treatment-bubble-units a9c6b3d1; that branch does not change ddata.js. Whether any record escapes both the comparison and the fallback is not established, so the queue item BFQ-175 is unsettled.

Measured 2026-10-25, closed as not a defect. On dev b29f1bf7 (Node v22.23.4, in process, no MongoDB), 51 temp targets through ddata.processTreatments, by unit spelling:

units sent targets result mmol any pair, including 20 and above correct mmol/L, mmol/l, MMOL either target below 20 correct, through the below-20 fallback (:478) mmol/L, mmol/l, MMOL both 20 or above (360 mg/dL and up) wrong: left unconverted (6 cases) mg/dl, mg/dL both 20 or above correct mg/dl, mg/dL either below 20 wrong: multiplied by 18.016 (8 cases) none any ambiguous by construction; below 20 is read as mmol/L

The run's table (before.md) marks 14 of the 51 wrong; the lane's hand-back summary said 12.

Which clients write temp targets, by reading. AndroidAPS sends "mg/dl" within 72–180.16; Trio sends no units, in mg/dL, or mmol/L values below 20 that the fallback converts correctly; nightguard sends "mg/dl"; the careportal sends mmol or mg/dl and caps targets at 18 mmol/L. Loop, xDrip+ and nightscout-connect write no temp targets. No client produces a wrong row. The converted value is read only by the chart's temp-target bars and tooltip (lib/client/renderer.js:477, :328-334); no plugin reads it. The careportal flow showed a separate defect, a double conversion when a hidden BG value is left filled: BF-180.

docs.title: BF-176 · axios is only a devDependency and lodash is undeclared, so a production install of dev (cut 1 merged) stops at boot with IMPORT_CONFIG — merged 2026-10-25 (PR #8834), pre-release
docs.text:
Mechanism. augmentSettings in lib/server/bootevent.js runs require('axios') only when IMPORT_CONFIG is set (:140 on v15.0.9 c6a0d8ed and dev 04d435eb, :114 on cut 1 806ff2f0). package.json lists axios only under devDependencies on all three. Production installs keep only runtime dependencies: the Dockerfile runs npm ci --cache /tmp/empty-cache --omit=optional --force and then npm prune --omit=dev --omit=optional; bin/azure-deploy.sh runs npm install --production. On v15.0.9 and dev, minimed-connect-to-nightscout (and its axios-cookiejar-support) depend on axios, so npm hoists that copy to node_modules/axios (0.34.0, by the overrides pin) and the lockfile does not mark it dev. nightscout-connect's own axios 1.20.0 is nested under its directory and cannot be found from lib/server. Cut 1 removes the MiniMed bridge; its lockfile marks node_modules/axios dev: true, and npm ls axios --omit=dev shows only the nested 1.20.0.

Reproduced 2026-10-22 (Node 24.15.0, npm 11.12.1, MongoDB 7.0.43 in a container, a fresh test database per arm, a generated API_SECRET, NODE_ENV=production; IMPORT_CONFIG pointed at a local HTTP server that served {"settings":{"customTitle":…,"theme":"colors"},"extendedSettings":{…}}; the effect read from /api/v1/status.json):

tree install IMPORT_CONFIG exit boot log imported settings v15.0.9 c6a0d8ed npm ci --omit=dev unset running Listening on port … n/a (defaults) v15.0.9 npm ci --omit=dev set running Getting settings from …, extending settings with { customTitle: …, theme: 'colors' } applied v15.0.9 Dockerfile's two commands set running as above applied v15.0.9 full npm ci (control) set running as above applied v15.0.9, node_modules/axios moved aside by hand npm ci --omit=dev set 1 Executing augmentSettings, then Error: Cannot find module 'axios' from bootevent.js:140 — cut 1 806ff2f0 npm ci --omit=dev unset running Listening on port … n/a cut 1 npm ci --omit=dev set 1 Error: Cannot find module 'axios' from bootevent.js:114 — cut 1 Dockerfile's two commands set 1 same — cut 1 full npm ci (control) set running extending settings with … applied cut 1 with axios moved to dependencies npm ci --omit=dev set running extending settings with … applied fix branch 43ed462a (on dev) npm ci --omit=dev unset / set running Listening on port … / extending settings with … n/a / applied

The failure is a crash, not a silent skip: the require is outside the promise chain whose catch records a boot error. dev 04d435eb differs from v15.0.9 in package.json and the lockfile only by the version string, so it was not re-run. The hand-removed arm shows what the crash looks like on 15.0.9; it is not a state any 15.0.9 install reaches.

Fix. Local branch bf/axios-runtime-dependency 43ed462a on dev 04d435eb (not pushed). Route, 2026-10-22: its own PR to dev, which #8828 takes in its next catch-up merge of dev. axios moves to dependencies at ^0.34.0; lodash is declared as exactly 4.18.1, the version the existing overrides entry pins (a caret range fails npm install with EOVERRIDE, and the override stays as it is). The lockfile changes its root lists and one flag: npm marks node_modules/@types/tough-cookie "dev": true when it recomputes the tree. That package is TypeScript declarations only (index.d.ts); its only dependents are the root devDependencies and a peerDependency of axios-cookiejar-support, which npm does not follow under the repository's legacy-peer-deps=true; cut 1's lockfile already carries the same flag. Five tests in tests/dependency-axios.test.js check that every package bootevent.js loads, and lodash for lib/utils.js, is under dependencies; two fail on the axios-only commit without lodash, and the axios ones fail on 04d435eb. Full suite 3574/4/0 (baseline 3569/4/0). With npm ci --omit=dev on 43ed462a, IMPORT_CONFIG boots and applies the imported settings, and npm ls --omit=dev lists axios@0.34.0 and lodash@4.18.1 at the top level. The branch conflicts with 806ff2f0 in package.json and package-lock.json; on cut 1 the move also drops the dev flag from node_modules/axios and node_modules/proxy-from-env.

lodash, measured. Undeclared on v15.0.9, dev and 806ff2f0. npm ls lodash --omit=dev: on v15.0.9 it comes through @parse/node-apn → jsonwebtoken, minimed-connect-to-nightscout and node-cache; on 806ff2f0 through jsonwebtoken and node-cache. Nothing fails from it today; the declaration keeps it in a production install if those packages drop it.

Gate. tools/queue/gates/runtime-requires-declared.js scans every literal require in server code (server.js, bin/*.js, lib/** except the browser-only lib/client, lib/report and lib/report_plugins) and requires each package to be under dependencies. webpack-dev-middleware and webpack-hot-middleware are allowed only inside lib/server/app.js's NODE_ENV === 'development' block. On v15.0.9, dev and 806ff2f0 it reports axios and lodash, nothing else; on the fix branch 45 checked, 0 failing. Its control also appends a stray require('webpack-hot-middleware') outside that block and the gate goes red. Cut 2 (d660e272) moved axios independently, found by its tools/validate-pruned-runtime.js; the gate still reports lodash there, and webpack as a devDependency required inside the development block (lib/server/app.js:340), which is for cut 2's catch-up.

2026-10-25: reproduced on dev eb72a1d3, after #8828 merged before the fix (Node 24.22.1, npm 11.19.1, MongoDB 7.0.43; the BF-176 session's run). With IMPORT_CONFIG set, the Dockerfile's install commands and npm ci --omit=dev both exit 1 with Cannot find module 'axios' at bootevent.js:114; unset, both boot; full npm ci with it set boots and applies the imported settings. dev's push CI (run 40211895500) published the dev Docker image, so the image carries it; no release does. The fix branch bf/axios-runtime-dependency is f3d73f43 (43ed462a plus a merge of eb72a1d3; 0 behind, 2 ahead, 3 files; PR #8834 to dev, opened 2026-10-25): every arm boots with the imported settings applied. Tests with TZ=UTC: the branch 3384/3/0, dev 3379/3/0; tests/dependency-axios.test.js 30 passing on the branch, 4 failing with dev's package.json. The gate on eb72a1d3: 41 checked, 2 failing (axios, lodash); on the branch 0 failing.

docs.title: BF-177 · a glucose distribution report test depends on the machine's time zone — merged 2026-10-25 (PR #8838), test only
docs.text:
Seen 2026-10-25 by the dependency refresh session on dev eb72a1d3 (Node 24.22.1, npm 11.19.1, MongoDB 7.0.43): npm test is 3378 passing / 3 pending / 1 failing in America/Los_Angeles, and the failure is glucosedistribution report includes the first selected interval when earlier hours are excluded, "expected '213.5' to be '117.5'"; with TZ=UTC it passes (3379/3/0 on dev in the BF-176 session's UTC run). The case was added by ba5f7f4b ("test(reports): cover distribution counts and statistics"), the head commit of #8812 (cpruijsen, issue 7659, merged 2026-10-25 as bb56989c).

Mechanism, read. The test makes 288 readings five minutes apart from 2025-01-01T00:00:00Z with values 100 to 387 and selects only hour 1. The report keeps a reading when enabledHours[profile.applyTimezone(moment(r.displayTime)).hour()] is set (lib/report_plugins/glucosedistribution.js:251-252). The test's client stub defines applyTimezone(value) as moment(value), which takes the machine's local zone. In UTC, hour 1 holds readings 12 to 23 (values 112 to 123, mean 117.5); at UTC−8 it holds readings 108 to 119 (values 208 to 219, mean 213.5), which is the failing value.

The report, read-derived. lib/profilefunctions.js applyTimezone converts to the profile's time zone (mom.tz(tz), or utcOffset for a fixed offset) and returns the moment unchanged when the profile has none, so the hour filter follows the profile's zone, or the viewer's browser zone without one. That is the intended reading of "filter by hours"; no wrong number in the report itself was found. Not run in a browser.

Fix, UNVERIFIED. Test only: build the readings at local times (for example from moment('2025-01-01T00:00')), or make the stub apply a fixed zone (moment.utc(value) or moment(value).utcOffset(0)), and run the file under two TZ values. Queue BFQ-177.

Merged 2026-10-25 through #8838 (89d19b5b; merge 2bc298b9). The case's stand-in is now a UTC profile, and two new cases run the report with the real lib/profilefunctions.js and a named profile zone: America/Los_Angeles gives 213.5 (the original failure's number) and Pacific/Auckland 249.5. The file passes, 8 cases, under TZ=UTC, America/Los_Angeles, Pacific/Auckland and Asia/Kolkata; with the old stand-in the original case fails in the three non-UTC zones, and with the report reading the hour in UTC both new cases fail in every zone (the PR's runs). That verifies by running it that the report applies the profile's zone and only the test was wrong; the read-derived paragraph above stands confirmed. A profile with no time zone (the browser's zone) is not exercised.

docs.title: BF-178 · the legacy reports browser test hangs in hosted CI, almost always Firefox — open, cause not found, test only
docs.text:
Seen 2026-10-25 in the GitHub Actions history of nightscout/cgm-remote-monitor, while checking why dev's CI was red. In the 109 completed runs of "CI test and publish Docker image" created from 2026-10-18 (the first is 2026-10-19), browser jobs are 426 success, 19 failure, 17 cancelled: Firefox 18 of 150, WebKit 1 of 147, Chromium 0 of 148. Eleven of the Firefox failures are this case, legacy reports in a real browser "should produce some html": dev a20469dc (three jobs), dev 93f152bd, deps/16.0.0-security-refresh 341b843a (two), wip/dev-security-fixes be806a57 and e0872924, and chore/retire-jsdom 13507b38 (three, at the earlier 15-second limit). The other seven Firefox failures are six browser-launch failures on one chore/retire-jsdom commit (76c73056) and one hashauth "Target page, context or browser has been closed" (15a84907). The WebKit failure is this case too (chore/retire-jsdom 6a146a4c, 2026-10-25, 15-second limit), with the same signature but on the refresh after a saved treatment edit (legacy-reports.test.js:173 there), not the third.

What the failure is. The case refreshes the report for 2015-08-08 to 2015-09-07 three times; idle waits for $.active === 0, the Show button and an empty #info. In the failing jobs the first two refreshes finish (about 6 s each, mostly rendering) and the third, the treatments tab (tests/browser/legacy-reports.test.js:149 on a20469dc, :148 on 13507b38; all eleven Firefox failures), times out at 30 s with "active" 1 to 12 and #info stuck on "Loading device status data of 2015-08-xx", errors: [] and failures: []. In seven sampled passing Firefox jobs the third refresh took 255–472 ms, and in four sampled Chromium and WebKit jobs 313–343 ms. So the requests stop; they are not slow. 12154df9 ("test: allow bounded Firefox month-report completion", 2026-10-25) raised the wait from 15 to 30 s on the reading that Firefox was still making progress; failures continued at 30 s.

Ruled out by running (local, dev 2bc298b9, Node 24.15.0, Playwright 1.63.0, Firefox build 1543, 16 cores). No failure in 51 Firefox runs: 15 of the case alone; 18 six at a time (the first two refreshes slowed to 10–13 s, the third stayed under 0.6 s); 15 with the fixture server's keepAliveTimeout set to 1, 3, 5, 6 and 7 s; three full Firefox browser suites in parallel (457 passing each). A per-refresh count of requests reaching the fixture server is the same in Firefox and Chromium on every refresh (treatments 35, entries 31, devicestatus 31, profiles 3), so the browser's HTTP cache is not answering any of them. Not tried: the hosted runner's Playwright Noble container image itself.

A fixture defect found on the way, reproduced. Every page request goes through withPage's context.route handler, which calls route.fetch({timeout: 5000}) and then route.fulfill. If the handler throws, Playwright rethrows from its route event listener and nothing aborts or continues the route, so the request stays pending in the page and no failure is recorded anywhere. Planting one unanswered device-status response on the third refresh produces exactly the hosted signature (active 1, #info stuck, no errors, no failures) in Firefox and Chromium. That does not show the hosted hang is a fixture timeout; it shows the current diagnostics cannot tell.

Instrumentation, local, not pushed. test/browser-request-stage-trace 99627097 over dev 2bc298b9 (in externals/cgm-remote-monitor-official): withPage records each unfinished request's last stage (issued, routed, fetched, fulfilled) and route and browser request errors, and returns them as traffic(); the legacy report fixture records server requests without a finished response; a completion timeout's message carries all three. A throwing route handler now records the error and aborts the request, so the page sees a failure. Red control: with the planted unanswered response the message names the request, stage routed, "route.fetch: Timeout 5000ms exceeded", and the same request as unanswered by the server (4 of 5 planted runs exactly so; one run instead reported several requests failed with NS_ERROR_FAILURE and none unanswered, not explained). Without the plant: Firefox and Chromium full browser suites 457 passing each; WebKit not run locally (host libraries missing). docs/test-specs/browser-tests.md gains the account above. The next hosted failure will say whether the stuck requests never reached the route handler, stalled in route.fetch, or were fulfilled and never delivered.

Fix, UNVERIFIED. None until the trace names a stage. Raising the wait again is not a fix. Queue BFQ-178; the branch belongs in a test-themed PR (the test tier PR #8839, or the next test hygiene PR), not one of its own.

docs.title: BF-179 · postinstall runs webpack, now a devDependency, so a production install of dev fails — merged 2026-10-26 (#8844), pre-release
docs.text:
Mechanism. package.json:47 on dev b29f1bf7: "postinstall": "webpack --mode production --config webpack/webpack.config.js && npm run-script post-generate-keys", with no guard. Cut 2 (#8837) moved webpack and its loaders from dependencies to devDependencies. An install that leaves out development packages (npm ci --omit=dev, npm install --production, NODE_ENV=production or NPM_CONFIG_PRODUCTION=true) still runs postinstall, and webpack is not installed. v15.0.9 c6a0d8ed has the same script with webpack under dependencies.

Reproduced 2026-10-25 by session f4 (Node v22.23.4):

tree command exit output dev b29f1bf7 npm ci --omit=dev 127 sh: 1: webpack: not found v15.0.9 c6a0d8ed (control) npm ci --omit=dev 0 —

Reach, read. The first-party Dockerfile (npm ci --include=dev … then npm prune --omit=dev --omit=optional --ignore-scripts) and bin/azure-deploy.sh (npm ci --include=dev, then npm prune --omit=dev --ignore-scripts) install development packages before the build, so they are not affected. Third-party guides and hosts that install production-only are (defaults calendar, D4). Not in any release.

Fix, UNVERIFIED. Guard postinstall (skip the build when webpack is absent and a built bundle is present), or ship the prebuilt bundle. Queue BFQ-179.

docs.title: BF-180 · a careportal temp target on an mmol/L site is converted twice when the hidden BG field holds a value — open, safety-relevant
docs.text:
Mechanism. On an mmol/L site the careportal's normalisation converts the temp target's targetTop and targetBottom to mg/dL (lib/client-core/careportal/normalize-treatment.js:66-70), but the record still carries the site's units, mmol (lib/client/careportal.js:321). The Temporary Target form hides the BG field; filterInputs resets other hidden fields but not #glucoseValue (careportal.js:145-161), and gatherData reads it (:305). The v1 prepareData removes units only when no glucose is given (lib/server/treatments.js:566-570). With a leftover glucose the record is stored with mg/dL numbers labelled mmol, and ddata.js:466 multiplies them by 18.016 again for the chart.

Reproduced 2026-10-25 through the real functions, not in a browser (dev b29f1bf7, Node v22.23.4, no MongoDB; the careportal flow run by session f4's BF-175 lane):

site typed BG field posted (bottom, top, units) stored charted (ddata) mmol/L 5.5/5.5 empty 99.09, 99.09, mmol 99.09, 99.09, units deleted 99.09 mg/dL mmol/L 4,4/8 empty 79.27, 144.12, mmol units deleted 79.27/144.12 mg/dL mg/dL 80/140 empty 80, 140, mg/dl units deleted 80/140 mg/dL mmol/L 5.5/5.5 6.1 99.09, 99.09, mmol 99.09, 99.09, mmol 1785.09 mg/dL

Consumers, read, not run. AndroidAPS (externals/AndroidAPS 7e1d537d) converts a treatment whose units are mmol by ×18 (core/nssdk/src/commonMain/kotlin/app/aaps/core/nssdk/localmodel/treatment/NSTreatment.kt asMgdl), giving about 1784 mg/dL here, and drops a temp target outside 72–180.16 mg/dL with only a debug log line (plugins/sync/src/commonMain/kotlin/app/aaps/plugins/sync/nsclientV3/NsIncomingDataProcessor.kt:172-179). The target the user entered in Nightscout never reaches AndroidAPS, and nothing on either side says so. Other clients read the raw numbers with a mmol label. v15.0.9 has the same code by reading.

Fix. Both options, on local branch bf/16.0.0-client-alarms bb1ad38e (head b7bf55e8, not pushed): the careportal clears the hidden glucose field and labels converted targets mg/dl. 2026-10-25, later: reproduced in a real browser on dev b29f1bf7 and on v15.0.9 c6a0d8ed (1785.09 charted) by session f4's alarms lane; severity set to medium (silently ignored by AndroidAPS, charted far off-scale). What other uploaders do with a refused write, if Nightscout were to refuse such a record, is in the upload-refusal note. Queue BFQ-180.

docs.title: BF-181 · one future srvModified pins the shared write clock ahead, across restarts — open
docs.text:
Mechanism. lib/server/srv-dates.js: next() returns max(Date.now(), last + 1); at boot restore() (BF-144's fix, a28fcecb, in v15.0.9) seeds last from the largest numeric srvModified stored in entries, treatments, devicestatus, profile, food and settings. One stored value in the future therefore lifts every later write to just above it. Those writes are future-stamped too, so deleting the first record does not release the pin; only removing every future-stamped record does. On dev every live entries write path replaces or refuses a client-sent srvModified (BF-95's 2026-10-25 note), but v15.0.8 stores one sent on a v1 entries POST verbatim, so an upgraded database can already hold one.

Reproduced 2026-10-25 (session f4's srvModified lane; dev b29f1bf7 and v15.0.8 92d08342, Node v22.23.4, MongoDB 8.0.34, booted server, AUTH_DEFAULT_ROLES=denied):

arm result dev: one record stored with srvModified +24 h later writes stamped 86,400,000 ms ahead dev: that record deleted, server restarted later writes still ahead (the writes since carry the pin) v15.0.8: v1 entries POST with a client srvModified of 2100-01-01 stored verbatim dev booted on that database new writes stamped at 2100-01-01

Not measured. The effect on API v3 history cursors (AndroidAPS takes the largest srvModified it received as its cursor), treatments and devicestatus written by 15.0.8, a v15.0.9 boot on such a database, and a real clock step. Also seen, not filed: API v3 read and search report srvModified = date for a record stored without one, and /lastModified for entries reports the newest of srvModified and date, so a future-dated reading shows as the future. No fix prescribed. Queue BFQ-181.

docs.title: BF-182 · on cut 3 (driver 7), boot against MongoDB 4.2 or older retries forever — merged 2026-10-26 (#8844), pre-release
docs.text:
Mechanism. Cut 3 moves the MongoDB Node driver from 5.9.2 to 7 (package.json ^7.6.0; 7.7.0 on wip/cut3-onto-16.0.0), whose minimum server is 4.4. Against an older server, server selection fails with a MongoServerSelectionError whose message says the server "requires at least 9 (MongoDB 4.4)". isRetryableConnectionError (lib/storage/mongo-storage.js:48) returns true for every MongoServerSelectionError that is not an authentication failure, so boot backs off and retries without end. The HTTP server never listens and no boot error page is shown; the host log repeats the retry line. Kind (b).

Reproduced 2026-10-25 (session f4's defaults-calendar lane, entry C3-2; probe driver-floor.js and init()):

code server result wip/cut3-onto-16.0.0 72c156fb, driver 7.7.0, mongo-storage.js init() mongo:4.2 (4.2.24) not resolved after 45 s, still retrying same mongo:4.4 (4.4.24) connected in 28 ms dev, driver 5.9.2 4.2.24 connected in 32 ms

The maintainer asked for confirmation that compatibility with MongoDB 3.6 to 4.4 holds. The driver × server matrix (MongoDB server matrix) answers it: driver 7.7.0 refuses 3.6.23, 4.0.28 and 4.2.24; 4.4.24 to 8.0.34 boot and pass the integration tier. Not on dev and not in any release.

Fix. -f8's cut 3 agent is adding a fatal boot-error path: wip/cut3-onto-16.0.0 99fa8b1e ("BF-182: stop retrying at boot when the driver refuses the MongoDB server", lib/storage/mongo-storage.js and tests/mongo-storage.retry.test.js), local, not pushed, not checked by this entry. Queue BFQ-182.

docs.title: BF-183 · the API v3 storage socket logs the supplied credential on a failed authorization — merged 2026-10-26 (#8847)
docs.text:
Mechanism. lib/api3/storageSocket.js subscribe: when resolveAccessToken fails it logs the accessToken from the subscribe message (:63), and when the message carries no token it logs the whole message (:76). The server log then holds the credential a client sent, valid or not. lib/api3/alarmSocket.js has the same two paths and redacts them on dev; cut 4 changes the lines in alarmSocket.js only. Same code in storageSocket.js on dev b29f1bf7 and v15.0.9 c6a0d8ed.

Status. Reproduced live and fixed 2026-10-25 on local branch bf/183-storage-socket-log-redaction f6704b8a (for cut 4): the alarm socket's redacted wording; tests/api3.storage-logging.test.js. Severity low: reading it needs access to the host's logs. Queue BFQ-183.

docs.title: BF-184 · API v3 /status reports only wildcard permissions — open
docs.text:
Mechanism. lib/api3/specific/status.js builds apiPermissions with for (let col in cols) (:43), which iterates the keys of the collections map, and permsForCol checks 'api:' + col.colName + ':<verb>' (:17-31). colName of a key string is undefined, so each check is against api:undefined:<verb>, which only a wildcard permission matches. The same loop is on v15.0.9 and v15.0.8.

Reproduced 2026-10-25 on dev b29f1bf7 by session f4's API v3 contract lane (in-process, the API v3 test fixture, three tokens):

token's permissions apiPermissions api:treatments:read only {} api:*:read r for every collection api:*:* crud for every collection

Reach, read. AndroidAPS does not rely on it for settings rights (NSAndroidClientImpl.withSettingsRights). Severity low. Fix, UNVERIFIED: iterate the map's values, or use the key as the collection name. Queue BFQ-184.

docs.title: BF-186 · API v3 logs a whole record when a client's identifier differs from the computed one — merged 2026-10-26 (#8845)
docs.text: Mechanism. lib/api3/shared/operationTools.js resolveIdentifier, :126-127 on dev b29f1bf7 (:119-120 on v15.0.9): when the client's identifier is not the UUID v5 the server would compute, it logs a warning with both and then console.log(doc), the whole record. Since BF-169's wording, sending one's own identifier is the documented path, so every such write puts health values into the server log. Found by session f4's identity lane, read and seen in the test output. Fix b34f6703 on bf/16.0.0-record-identity, in PR #8845 to dev. Queue BFQ-186.

docs.title: BF-187 · an over-long entries pattern segment answers 500 — open
docs.text: Mechanism. BF-151's guard on /api/v1/times, /api/v1/times/echo and /api/v1/slice parses the segment with braces.parse before counting the patterns it expands to. braces refuses input over its own maximum length with a SyntaxError, which nothing catches before the error handler, so the reply is 500. A malformed request should get 400. Reproduced on dev code; v15.0.9 has the same guard by reading. Mechanism only in this repository, because the routes are covered by a private advisory (BF-161). Queue BFQ-187.

docs.title: BF-188 · no client bundle, unexplained boot exit — open
docs.text: Mechanism. lib/server/app.js resolves the bundle directory with require.resolve (resolvePath, :19) while creating the app (:362 on dev b29f1bf7). If the bundle was never built, boot ends with Error: Cannot find module '/node_modules/.cache/_ns_cache/public' and a stack through bootevent.js. Reproduced by session f4's cut-fixes lane on bf/179-omit-dev-install 1cf70838. A clearer boot error would name the bundle and the build command; BF-179's fix already stops such an install at postinstall with a message. Queue BFQ-188.

docs.title: BF-189 · tests/security.test.js fails depending on file order — open, test only
docs.text: In the 38-file selection test:affected --since official/dev --depth 4 (the BF-183 lane), two API_SECRET cases fail with expected 401 to be 'ok' (tests/security.test.js:110), with the BF-183 change and with dev's file alike; the file passes alone. The test that leaves the state behind is not identified. Queue BFQ-189.

docs.title: BF-190 · an alarm on a page without a current reading cannot be silenced — merged 2026-10-26 (#8842)
docs.text: Mechanism. lib/client/index.js clearCurrentSGV (:656 on dev b29f1bf7) removes the alarming urgent warning classes on every redraw (at least every 15 s and on new data) when there is no current reading. The alarm sound loops on, but the BG button opens the silence menu only while the page is alarming. Measured with BF-92's presentation change: alarming: false, playing: 1. On v15.0.9 (read): a page whose latest reading is more than 15 minutes old. Fix on local branch bf/16.0.0-client-alarms 5fb199b3: the classes stay while an alarm is in progress; stopAlarm is the only path that removes them. Queue BFQ-190.

docs.title: BF-191 · a stored treatment can stop the server process — open, mechanism only
docs.text: Mechanism. A record stored with an unexpected field type through a write path that does not check types can stop the server process, and the stored record keeps doing so after a restart until it is removed. Writing it needs a credential with treatment write access. Found 2026-10-25 by session f4's AndroidAPS-safety lane; reproduced on dev b29f1bf7 and v15.0.9 c6a0d8ed. Severity: availability, high (persistent), needs a credential. Status. Open; fix in preparation on a local branch, to ship in 16.0.0 (maintainer decision 2026-10-25), through the maintainer's private advisory process. 2026-10-25: a second record kind of the same class was found and is covered by the same fix; the fix is prepared on a local branch (private) and API v1's refusal of such a record will answer 400 with its message instead of 500 (maintainer decision 2026-10-25). 2026-10-25: the fix also refuses such values on write for the second record kind, and tolerates on read a related field that working sites may hold (maintainer decision). DISCLOSURE: live on v15.0.9, so this entry describes the mechanism only, as for BF-72; the reproduction is held outside version control. Queue BFQ-191.

docs.title: BF-192 · the populated reports browser test measured a drawn report — merged 2026-10-26 (#8843), test-measurement blind spot
docs.text:
What failed. tests/browser/page-populated.test.js "initializes populated reports and bounds retained V8 heap" loads the reports page with data and compares the V8 heap it retains with a ceiling. On dev 428b20b7 it failed: "reports: retained heap ~6.19 MB exceeds 4850000" (session f4's lanes, Node 22.23.4: 6192136 and 6189568 bytes; session -f8, Node 24.22.1: b29f1bf7 ~4.45 MB, 428b20b7 ~6.20 MB, cut 3 12d1f645 ~5.94 MB, cut 4 99b6f68b likewise). Browser CI ran zero tests from #8839 until the runner fix e767ce4e in #8843, which is why dev's CI did not show it.

Corrected 2026-10-25 (session -b7): not a product regression. Since #8542 the reports page draws its first report (AGP plus seven daily charts, 576 readings) as soon as the profile loads, so the populated test measured a drawn report, not an empty form. Measured, before #8542 → after: loaded 4.43 → 6.19 MB; after one Show 9.24 → 7.18 MB; after five Shows 9.93 → 7.46 MB. Fix 0a33b7c7, folded into PR #8843 by the maintainer and pending his push: the test waits for the first report (an svg under #pluginchartplaceholders and an empty #info), and the reports ceiling goes 4,850,000 → 6,800,000 bytes = 1.097 × the maximum of 7 samples (6,181,516–6,197,116), recorded in docs/test-specs/page-bundles.md. Open note: both revisions grow slowly with repeated Shows (~170 KB per run before, ~70 KB per run after). Queue BFQ-192.

docs.title: BF-193 · the realtime socket and other write paths log every record written through them — merged 2026-10-27 (#8856), reproduced by its test
docs.text:
Mechanism. lib/server/websocket.js logs LOG_WS + '<handler> client ID: ', the socket client id and the whole data argument at the top of the dbUpdate (:368), dbUpdateUnset (:440), dbAdd (:508) and dbRemove (:827) handlers on dev 47723cda, before the collection or permission checks. Every record a client writes over the socket therefore reaches the server log with its health values. The same lines are on v15.0.9 (:816 for dbRemove). Found 2026-10-26 by a read-only compatibility audit. It is the socket's counterpart of BF-186, which #8845 fixed for API v3. Other lines that log whole records on dev 47723cda: the socket's two Got results lines and nine refusal lines; the v1 treatments POST (lib/api/treatments/index.js:146) and PUT; Profile saved (lib/api/profile/index.js); Activity measure saved (lib/api/activity/index.js); lib/server/profile.js's save error; lib/data/treatmenttocurve.js; lib/profilefunctions.js; and the treatmentnotify and loop plugins.

Decided 2026-10-26 (maintainer): debug-gated payload logging through one gate. The gate is the existing DEBUG_LOGGING (env.debug.logging), with no new setting. The summary (operation, collection, client, record reference, and eventType or the item count) is always logged; the record only with DEBUG_LOGGING on. Refusal lines may come from an unauthenticated caller, so they are bounded and redacted.

Fixed 2026-10-26 on branch bf/16.0.0-log-privacy 8ae43eb4, one commit on dev 47723cda, in draft PR #8856 to dev (opened 2026-10-26 by the maintainer, head 8ae43eb4). Every site above logs through recordForLog in lib/server/log-privacy.js, beside urlForLog and errorForLog; plugins and the profile conversion read the same setting from the sandbox. With DEBUG_LOGGING on, a refusal line's payload has credential-named fields replaced and credential values redacted, and the line is bounded to 8192 characters, as errorForLog does. The README's DEBUG_LOGGING entry says debug logs then contain health data. Runs on the branch (Node 22.23.4): npm test 4289 passing, 1 failing, 3 pending, where the failure is environmental (tests/development-watch.test.js, ENOSPC on file watchers); npm run test:all 4617 / 1 / 3, the same failure. The new test fails 6 of 7 cases with the source reverted. A trial merge with #8854 fa22d573 is clean. Log lines change text, so anything parsing WS: dbAdd client ID: or Treatment saved sees the summary format.

Open follow-up, read-derived, not filed as an id. Storage error lines that log whole MongoDB error objects (lib/server/treatments.js:173, :284 and :452, lib/server/entries.js:208 on dev 47723cda) may include the document that failed to write. Not covered by the branch; unverified. Queue BFQ-193.

docs.title: BF-194 · API v1 drops the units of a temp target with no glucose value — merged 2026-10-27 (#8872), reproduced
docs.text:
Mechanism. API v1's prepareData (lib/server/treatments.js:639-643 on dev 47723cda, :566-570 on v15.0.9) deletes glucose, glucoseType and units when glucose is 0 or not a number. A Temporary Target carries no glucose, so its units is removed before WRITE_VALIDATION (#8841) checks it. Its targets keep the numbers sent, so targets sent in mmol/L are stored as bare numbers that read as mg/dL. Reproduced 2026-10-26 by the client replay in the 16.0.0 integration record R15: a v1 Temporary Target with units mmol/L and 6.0 is stored with units undefined on v15.0.9 and on dev under every WRITE_VALIDATION mode; an mmol batch item with mg/dL numbers is stored under reject for the same reason. BF-180, the careportal case, goes through the same lines. The fix needs a maintainer decision (keep, convert or refuse). Queue BFQ-194.

Fixed 2026-10-27 on local branch bf/16.0.0-tt-units as 7b74110c ("Store a Temporary Target in mg/dL, labelled mg/dl, on every write path (BF-194)"), one commit on dev ca1652d6, merged with dev dcf20bfb as 355b4f14 and opened as PR #8872 to dev on 2026-10-27, merged the same day as db3b9e4e (23:45Z). Decided 2026-10-27 (maintainer): convert and always label. One helper, lib/treatmentTargetUnits.js, runs after each path's WRITE_VALIDATION step on API v1 POST and PUT and the in-process calls (through prepareData), API v3 POST, PUT and PATCH, and the socket's dbAdd and dbUpdate. Targets labelled mmol or mmol/L are multiplied by MMOL_TO_MGDL unless one is above 30; unlabelled targets are converted when one is below 20, the rule lib/data/ddata.js applies at read time; the label is then mg/dl (the server's canonical spelling and AAPS's exact GlucoseUnit.MGDL text). Stored records are not migrated. Red control: the new tests over ca1652d6's lib/ fail 45, each a value or label left unconverted. npm test 4750 passing, 0 failing, 3 pending; test:all exit 0 (Node v22.23.4, MongoDB 7.0).

docs.title: BF-195 · a stale profile is pushed over the socket after a profile re-send — merged 2026-10-27 (#8859), reproduced
docs.text:
Mechanism. When a profile is re-sent and merged into a stored one, lib/server/profile.js emits data-received (:171 on dev 47723cda, :90 on v15.0.9) before the merge write has finished. The data reload that the event triggers can therefore read the profile as it was, and the socket's dataUpdate carries that old profile to connected pages and followers; the stored profile is correct, and the next update corrects what they show. Reproduced 2026-10-26 by the Q1b study, 2 of 2 runs on dev 47723cda and on lab branch lab/q1b-null-removes 63c33a0e: a socket client received the earlier profile after a re-send. v15.0.9 by reading. Fix direction, UNVERIFIED: emit the event once the write has completed. It lands with the Q1b change (a null in an update removes the field) on branch bf/16.0.0-null-removes, in progress.

Fixed 2026-10-26 on branch bf/16.0.0-null-removes as 1bdce62c ("Announce a profile write after it finishes, not when it starts"), in draft PR #8859 to dev (opened 2026-10-26 by the maintainer, head fc170a4c; five commits over dev 47723cda: ID-SIMPLE-MATCH 8d0f9a22, Q1b 913d0895, this fix 1bdce62c, the merge cf2a2a67 and the devicestatus identifier rule fc170a4c). The profile path emits data-received once the write has completed. Measured by session -66: npm test 4375 passing, 0 failing, 3 pending and test:all 4703 passing, 0 failing, 3 pending (re-run on fc170a4c 2026-10-26 on Node 22.23.4 and MongoDB 5.0; the first run, before push, had 1 environmental failure, tests/development-watch.test.js ENOSPC on the host's file-watcher limit). Queue BFQ-195.

docs.title: BF-196 · API v1 /notifications/ack refuses with 500, not 401 — open, reproduced
docs.text: Mechanism. ctx.authorization.isPermitted('notifications:*:ack') refuses a caller by calling res.sendJSONStatus (lib/authorization/index.js:294). The notifications router (lib/api/notifications-api.js) is an express.Router that never installs wares.sendJSONStatus, so the refusal throws TypeError: res.sendJSONStatus is not a function and the error handler answers 500. The refusal holds: the handler does not run and nothing is acknowledged. Reproduced 2026-10-26 by the route audit for cgm-remote-monitor PR #8858 on its branch d46ef808 (dev c08cbe03 plus documents), with AUTH_DEFAULT_ROLES=denied and readable: no credential → 500, API secret → 200. v15.0.9 by reading (:24, same router). PR #8858's API v1 document states the 500 as it is. Fix direction, UNVERIFIED: install wares.sendJSONStatus on the router. Queue BFQ-196.

docs.title: BF-197 · API v1 /echo/{storage} answers 500 for an unknown storage name — open, reproduced
docs.text: Mechanism. echo_query (lib/api/entries/index.js, :368-382 on d46ef808, :437-451 on v15.0.9) builds its answer from ctx[storage].query_for(query) with no check that ctx[storage] is a storage layer, so /api/v1/echo/notastore throws a TypeError and is answered 500. The route needs read access and returns only the query it would run. Reproduced 2026-10-26 on d46ef808 with the API secret; v15.0.9 by reading. Fix direction, UNVERIFIED: answer 404 for a name that is not a storage layer. Queue BFQ-196.

docs.title: BF-198 · API v1 delete-by-id for profile, food and activity ignores storage errors — open, read
docs.text: Mechanism. DELETE /api/v1/profile/{id} calls ctx.profile.remove(id, function ( ) { res.json({ }); }) (lib/api/profile/index.js:193-194 on d46ef808, :176-177 on v15.0.9): the callback takes no error argument, so a failed delete is answered 200 {}. lib/api/food/index.js:117-118 and lib/api/activity/index.js:114-115 follow the same pattern. Found 2026-10-26 by the route audit for PR #8858; read, not run, because it needs a storage fault. Fix direction, UNVERIFIED: pass the error on with next(err), as the treatments and entries deletes do (lib/api/treatments/index.js:173-177). Queue BFQ-196.

docs.title: BF-199 · the README's API v1 default read window says two days; the server reads four — open, reproduced
docs.text: Mechanism. lib/server/query.js:46-49 sets opts.deltaAgo = TWO_DAYS * 2 when a query has no date filter, so API v1 reads (and deletes without a date filter) cover four days. The README's Nightscout API section says "the most recent 10 values from the last 2 days" (README.md:220 on d46ef808, :210 on v15.0.9). Reproduced 2026-10-26 on d46ef808: the echo query shows $gte now − 345,600,000 ms. BF-71's detail measures the same default from the tenancy side. PR #8858's API v1 document says four days; the README sentence is outside that PR. Queue BFQ-196.

docs.title: BF-200 · on dev, an unusable time on API v2's data-snapshot route stops the process — merged 2026-10-27 (#8868)
docs.text: Mechanism. /api/v2/ddata/at/:at turns at into a date with moment and hands it to dataloader.update without a check (lib/data/endpoints.js:56-60 on dev 2dc0c1bc). A value moment cannot parse becomes an Invalid Date, ddata.lastUpdated becomes NaN, and each loader's new Date(...).toISOString() throws; a time at the edge of the Date range does the same through the profile-switch loader's 372-day look-back. On v15.0.9 the first throw happens while the request handler is still running, Express answers 500, and async.parallel starts no further task. On dev, lib/utils/callback-tasks.js (from 26d0908a, 2026-09-06) has already advanced its cursor when a task throws, so the next storage callback starts loadProfileSwitchTreatments, whose throw at lib/data/dataloader.js:346 nothing catches, and the process exits. The only path that brings a caller-supplied time to the loader is this route; bootevent.js:375 passes Date.now(). Reproduced 2026-10-27 on dev 2dc0c1bc, feat/storage-writes 38b910d7 and v15.0.9 c6a0d8ed (not affected: 500, process alive). Fix on bf/16.0.0-ddata-at-crash 434c0157: the route answers 400 for an unparseable time, and update() reports an error before changing ddata or querying when the time or its look-back is outside the Date range; responses for valid times are byte-identical (four times compared on one seeded database). Removing either half fails its tests. Follow-up, UNVERIFIED: make callback-tasks.parallel stop starting tasks after a synchronous throw, as async did.

docs.title: BF-201 · nodemon watches nearly the whole repository — merged 2026-10-27 (#8866), developer tooling only
docs.text:
What happened. package.json's nodemonConfig ignored tests/*, node_modules/* and bin/* and watched everything else: 1,502 inotify watches at dev 2dc0c1bc. On 2026-10-26 tests/development-watch.test.js failed with ENOSPC: System limit for number of file watchers reached, the per-user Linux watch limit rather than disk space. The maintainer raised the machine's limit and asked for development tooling to use fewer watches.

Fix in PR #8866 as 5d9f84b5 (from #8867, merged into #8866 as 7a96b912; prepared as 426d2835 off dev 2dc0c1bc): nodemon watches lib, views, translations, webpack and package.json (385 watches). The server reads the last three at startup (lib/server/server.js loads the localization, lib/server/app.js requires the webpack configuration, lib/server/env.js reads package.json). static/ is left out: it is served as files, and in development webpack-dev-middleware rebuilds the client bundle inside the running server. The watch probe's fixture gains views, translations and docs files; the test fails at docs/unlisted.js with the previous configuration. npm test 4483 passing, 0 failing, 3 pending (Node 22.23.4, MongoDB 8.0.34). Queue BFQ-201.

docs.title: BF-202 · CI's MongoDB 8.0 jobs fail on runners with Linux 6.19 or newer — mitigation merged 2026-10-27 (#8866), CI only
docs.text:
What happens. MongoDB 8.0 refuses to start on Linux 6.19 and newer (SERVER-121912, no fix version; the issue is in MongoDB's memory allocator). GitHub's hosted runners are moving to that kernel one host at a time, so a MongoDB 8.0 job fails when it lands on one, and the same job passes on a re-run that lands elsewhere. Without a readiness check every database test then timed out in its before-all hook: #8866's run 40532337252 took 47 minutes to report 212 failing. #8867's run 40557880084 printed MongoDB's own refusal through the new wait step, while the 8.0.29 job in the same run started.

Diagnosis aid. PR #8866 carries tools/wait-for-mongodb.js, which fails within about 90 s with the container log, and prints the runner's kernel on success and failure (e0cfbd0c). On run 40569101512 both 8.0 jobs ran on 7.0.0-1017-azure and refused to start, 8.0.29 included, so holding an older 8.0 patch would mean going back to about 8.0.4; the 5.0 and 6.0 jobs on 6.17.0-1022-azure passed. ubuntu-24.04 image 20261026.354 moves its kernel from 6.17 to 7.0; ubuntu-22.04 is on 6.8.

Mitigation in PR #8866 as f6884342: the MongoDB 8.0 jobs run on ubuntu-22.04. On run 40569981396 both passed on 6.8.0-1064-azure. Revisit when the runners' kernel reaches 7.0.14 (MongoDB lifts its refusal there), when MongoDB supports 6.19 and newer, or before GitHub retires ubuntu-22.04. MongoDB documents no flag that bypasses the check. MongoDB 5.0 and 6.0 jobs are not affected. Operators running MongoDB 8.0 on such a kernel meet the same MongoDB defect, independently of Nightscout. Queue BFQ-202.

docs.title: BF-203 · an editor watches every sibling worktree without a jsconfig.json — merged 2026-10-27 (#8871), developer tooling only
docs.text:
What happens. An editor's TypeScript server, opening a file from a cgm-remote-monitor checkout that has no jsconfig.json, puts it in an inferred project at the workspace root. When that checkout sits inside a larger workspace (here the alignment repo, with many worktrees under externals/work/), the project watches all of it: 450,689 inotify watches and 1.4 GB, measured with tsserver 5.9.3 started with --useInferredProjectPerProjectRoot, JavaScript enabled for inferred projects and the workspace as project root. The per-user limit was 65,536 (raised to 524,288 on 2026-10-26), so one editor could exhaust it.

Fix in PR #8871 (tooling/jsconfig-watch-scope f28d40bb): an 8-line jsconfig.json (module commonjs, target es2022, checkJs false; exclude node_modules, coverage, .nyc_output, tmp). The same probe: 2,007 watches and 358 MB. exclude only, so new folders are covered. Nothing the server, build or tests read changes. The editor-side companion of BF-201. Queue BFQ-203.

docs.title: BF-204 · API v2's data-snapshot route returns the live 48 hours, not data framed at the requested time — merged 2026-10-28 (#8873), reproduced
docs.text: Mechanism. The route reloads data framed at the requested time, but the reload goes through the shared in-memory cache: the framed results are merged into the live cache and the whole cache is returned. The cache keeps 48 hours measured from the current time, so the answer is the live window, and framed results older than that window are dropped. Reproduced 2026-10-27 on dev db3b9e4e by session -65's ST-VIEWS census (MongoDB 7.0.43, synthetic fixture, clean cache). v15.0.9 has the same shape by reading. Distinct from BF-200 (an unusable time stopping the process), which is fixed. Fix direction, UNVERIFIED: a framed snapshot reads into its own structure rather than the shared cache; ST-VIEWS' bounded views are the natural home. Evidence: docs/60-research/platform/st-views-census-2026-10-27.md §4 item 1 (branch lab/views-census).

docs.title: BF-205 · same-timestamp records are ordered differently between in-memory loads — merged 2026-10-28 (#8873), reproduced
docs.text: Mechanism. The loader runs its queries in parallel and appends results as each finishes; the sort by mills is stable, so records with equal mills keep the finish order, which varies. Reproduced by the ST-VIEWS census: a Sensor Start and a Meal Bolus with equal mills swapped between loads. Read-derived, not reproduced: processDurations keeps the first record per mills, so which of two same-time duration records (temp basal, temp target, profile switch) from different queries survives could vary between loads. Fix direction, UNVERIFIED: a total order (for example mills, then a stable key). Evidence: census §4 item 2.

docs.title: BF-206 · a device IOB without a timestamp is dated now — merged 2026-10-28 (#8873), reproduced
docs.text: Mechanism. iob.fromDeviceStatus dates an OpenAPS or Loop IOB by its timestamp field, and an absent field becomes the current time, so the record passes the 30-minute recency check whatever the device status's own created_at says. Reproduced as nondeterminism on a corpus fixture (the IOB time differs by milliseconds between two loads). (Corrected 2026-10-27: the recency check uses the device status's own time, so an old status cannot pass as current. What does happen, reproduced by a unit test: within the 30-minute window an untimestamped IOB, dated now, sorts as newest and wins over a newer timestamped one, for OpenAPS and Loop. IOB feeds the bolus wizard preview (bwp) and its high-alarm snooze.) On a real payload shape (2026-10-28): #8873's CI failed on the captured AndroidAPS IOB pill golden (tests/client-core/pill-goldens.test.js, outside npm test's glob). Those device statuses, sanitised from a real export, carry no IOB time, so on dev every IOB in the window is dated now, in array order, and the pill shows the oldest recent status's IOB and basal instead of the newest. The committed golden had recorded the bug; it is regenerated with the fix (1c50c29a). Current AndroidAPS source writes the time, so this affects some uploads, not all. Fix direction, UNVERIFIED: fall back to the device status's created_at. Evidence: census §4 item 5.

docs.title: BF-207 · sensor age keeps the earliest of a same-hour burst of Sensor Starts — merged 2026-10-28 (#8873), display only
docs.text:
Mechanism. sensorage.js walks the Sensor Start (and related) events and replaces the one it holds only when the new event's whole-hour age is strictly smaller. Events within the same whole hour have equal ages, so the first one found, the earliest, stays. Observed on a corpus fixture by session -65's ST-VIEWS census: four Sensor Starts within 9 s, earliest kept; the emitted alarms were identical on every fixture. (Corrected 2026-10-27: the read-derived claim that a burst crossing a whole-hour boundary would move the sage WARN and URGENT alarms was wrong. Across the boundary the newer start already wins, with the smaller age; within one hour every start has the same whole-hour age, which the alarms use. The defect is display only: the shown date, notes and minute fractions.) Intended behaviour (maintainer, 2026-10-27, decided in session -65 and relayed): the newest Sensor Start is the correct one. ST-VIEWS' bounded view therefore differs from today's resident value here by design. Fix direction, UNVERIFIED: prefer the newer event on equal whole-hour age. Alarm path: any fix is checked against the alarm fixtures. Evidence: census §4 item 4.

BF-204 to BF-207, merged 2026-10-28 to dev as e1f7ac41 (#8873, head 1c50c29a); built 2026-10-27 on branch bf/16.0.0-views-data (session -65; 6b47afa9, df95900f, 675560ab, 80a414c7 on dev db3b9e4e; npm test 4759/0/3 against dev's 4750, as reported by -65; the four new test files re-run by session -4f: 39 passing on the branch, 7 failing with lib/ at db3b9e4e). Corrections from running the fixes: BF-205's duration consequence and BF-206's newest-wins consequence are now reproduced by unit tests; BF-206's recency check uses the device status's own time, so an old status cannot pass as current; BF-207's alarm consequence was wrong, and it is display only.
