docs.title: BF-208 · an API v1 delete by a non-hex id can answer 200 without removing anything — open, measured
docs.text: Measured 2026-10-27 on dev db3b9e4e by the write-contract matrix's new forms (harddelete-custom, harddelete-num; records written straight to MongoDB with a custom string or numeric _id, then deleted through each path). On API v1, entries answers 200 with a delete count for both, emits a removal reload, and the record stays: the path segment is read as an entries query, not an _id (read). Treatments with a numeric _id answers 200, emits a removal for that id, and the record stays; a custom string id is deleted. Devicestatus, profile, food and activity answer 400. API v3's permanent delete answers 404 for a numeric _id. The socket's dbRemove and in-process removes delete both forms. Exposure: the API paths the client survey covers do not create such ids; imports and scripts can. Fix direction, UNVERIFIED: a delete that matched nothing answers as not found, and emits nothing. Related: BF-198.

docs.title: BF-212 · a chart-drag split leaves two records with one client identity, and a re-send can overwrite one — open, reproduced on dev
docs.text:
Reproduced 2026-10-29 on dev e1f7ac41 with synthetic data, by a local probe that replays the socket messages the chart sends for "Move insulin" (crm probe/split-ident-2026-10-29 95570d41). The original record loses the moved field through dbUpdateUnset, and the new half is stored through dbAdd from splitRecord's copy, which keeps every client identity field except NSCLIENT_ID. Two effects:

  • Shared identity. Two stored records carry one syncIdentifier or identifier. API v3 reads and deduplication by identifier resolve to the new half; a v1 upsert by identifier replaces the original and replies with the new half's _id, so the reply names a record other than the one written.
  • Double count on re-upload. A client that still holds the original re-uploads it in full; the upload matches the original and writes the moved insulin back, while the new half also holds it. The chart and its IOB then count that insulin twice.
  • Overwrite of a shared-identifier record [M]. Measured by session -4f's write-contract matrix extension (QC-MATRIX-IDF, pin tools/qc/results/write-contract-matrix/dev-e1f7ac41-idfirst.json, dev e1f7ac41), with two stored treatments A and B sharing one identifier, B two minutes later with another amount. On API v1 and in-process, a re-send of B lands on A, the older _id: A is overwritten with B's body, so two records hold B's body and A's amount is lost. A re-send of A also lands on A. On API v3 the lookup picks B instead, and a re-send of A is refused with 400. The split is one way two records come to share an identifier.

Control: the same run with the copy stripped of syncIdentifier, id, uuid and identifier removes the shared-identity effects and leaves the double count, so the two need separate fixes. Not run on v15.0.9, where splitRecord is the same code (read). Fix direction, UNVERIFIED, from the maintainer's direction of 2026-10-29: a lossy edit of a record that carries a client identity asks for a manual confirmation. Related: BF-103, BF-209.

docs.title: BF-217 · an override with no reservoir value throws in the pump plugin — merged to dev (#8880)
docs.text: Reproduced 2026-10-30 by tests/pump-level-override.test.js on dev 991b0654: a non-Omnipod pump status carrying reservoir_level_override with no reservoir value throws in prepareData; the plugin runner catches it, and no pump pill or pump alarm appears while that status is the newest. Fixed in the BF-213 commit 0e5c25be.

docs.title: BF-213 · the URGENT pump reservoir alarm is refused when the level comes from reservoir_level_override — merged to dev (#8880)
docs.text: Reproduced 2026-10-30 by the ST-VIEWS replay lab (crm lab/views-replay b4762955, local) on one corpus export, on both the resident path and the bounded view, so it is not a view difference. The refusal is reproduced; the cause is read from code: prepareData in lib/plugins/pump.js takes the level from reservoir_level_override when the status carries no reservoir message and leaves title undefined, and requestNotify refuses an incomplete request. Fix being built with a synthetic red control on bf/16.0.0-alarm-display. Not run on v15.0.9.

docs.title: BF-214 · a device-status delete by query leaves its cache empty until the next heartbeat — merged to dev (#8880)
docs.text: Measured 2026-10-30 by session -7d's cache catch-up lab on dev 991b0654 (5 reps, about 56 s until consistent with the lab's 120 s cadence; on a site the gap is what remains of the 60 s heartbeat unless another write comes first, read). lib/server/devicestatus.js remove() emits data-update (op remove, no changes) but no data-received, which the entries and treatments removes emit. A delete by _id names its record and does not trigger it (read). Fix direction, UNVERIFIED: emit data-received as the other removes do, keeping BF-211's per-collection flush. Related: BF-93, BF-195, BF-211.

docs.title: BF-215 · a numeric identifier on a v1 treatment answers 500 — open
docs.text: Measured 2026-10-30 by session -4f's QC-MATRIX-IDFMT cell treatments v1 idfmt-number-single on dev 991b0654: 500, nothing stored. Entries, device status, profile, food and activity store it; API v3 answers 400. Fixed in ID-FIRST-MATCH slice 2 (#8879) under the WRITE_IDENTIFIER setting.

docs.title: BF-216 · two apps sending the same placeholder identifier share one record — open
docs.text: Measured 2026-10-30 by the QC-MATRIX-IDFMT *-twoapp cells on dev 991b0654 (pin tools/qc/results/write-contract-matrix/dev-991b0654-idformat.json): when the second write lands on API v1 or in-process, entries merge, a treatment overwrites the other app's, and a device status is answered 200 and not stored. The socket keeps both, API v3 refuses the second with 400, and profile, food and activity keep both. Fixed in ID-FIRST-MATCH slice 2 (#8879) with the placeholder list decided by the maintainer on 2026-10-30. Not run on v15.0.9.

docs.title: BF-228 · the deletion ceremony's ledger check admits two of six lifecycle tables — fixed on a preview branch, not pushed
docs.text:
Mechanism. ready() in lib/tenant-lifecycle/ceremony.js first checks that the ledger namespace's schema_migrations equal the lifecycle candidate catalogue, then asks assertRelationInventory to confirm the namespace holds exactly the expected relations. It passes only tenant_lifecycle_requests and tenant_lifecycle_ceremony. The candidate's migrations 0003 and 0004 create four more tables in the same namespace (operation windows and restore control), so on a namespace migrated with the whole catalogue the inventory finds relations it was not told about and the ceremony refuses with LIFECYCLE_RELATION_UNADMITTED. The two checks together cannot both pass once 0003/0004 exist.

Reproduced 2026-11-10 by the MT-KEY-RETENTION lane: a native probe on base dc795bd1 against PostgreSQL 16 with the full candidate applied refused requestDeletion with LIFECYCLE_RELATION_UNADMITTED: lifecycle.tenant_lifecycle_operations; the same probe on the lane head ed46cc43 is accepted. Reverting the fix on the lane head turns 20 unit and 5 native cases red with the same code, and restoring it returns 31 and 6 passing. Evidence.

Why it was not seen. The ceremony's unit tests run against a recording double of the database that models only the two tables, and the native suites that applied the full catalogue did not call the ceremony. The lane's native suite now does.

Fix. The readiness check takes LEDGER_TABLES from lib/tenant-lifecycle/key-retention.js, which lists every table the candidate creates (including the new key-retention table from migration 0005). Status: fixed on the lane branch and joined into the M6b candidate; it reaches #8898 when the maintainer pushes that candidate. Never in dev or a release, so operators are not affected.

docs.title: BF-229 · owner revocation can remove the last usable owner — fixed on a preview branch, not pushed
docs.text:
Mechanism. On the owner-policy path, remove() in lib/subject-admin/postgres.js verifies that the acting owner may revoke subjects (decision owner-may-revoke-subjects) and locks the target subject. It never asks whether the target is the site's last usable owner. With one owner, a revoke of that owner's subject succeeds; with two, each owner revoking the other locks a different row, so both deletes commit and no usable owner remains.

Reproduced 2026-11-10 by the M6b follow-ups lane on b70ad83f against PostgreSQL 16, in tests/owner-subject-policy.integration.test.js: 23 passing, 2 failing (the last-owner delete returned 200 where 409 was expected; the concurrent race ended applied, applied). The race is a real interleaving: a holder connection takes LOCK TABLE audit IN SHARE MODE and the test waits until pg_stat_activity shows both sessions blocked before releasing. With the fix: 25 passing, 0 failing. Removing the guard reproduces both failures; keeping the guard but removing the owner lock fails only the race. Evidence.

Fix. Before locking the target, remove() locks every usable owner's subject in subject-id order and refuses with SUBJECT_ADMIN_LAST_OWNER (HTTP 409) when the target is the only one. Revoking a co-owner, or one's own subject while another owner remains, still works. The legacy writer (no ownerPolicy) is unchanged; it is not reachable through any shipped composer and its handling is a pending maintainer decision. Status: fixed on codex/m6b-followups-20261110 65657a62, not yet joined into a #8898 candidate. Never in dev or a release, so operators are not affected.

docs.title: BF-230 · the Compose restore driver fails inside the claim and leaves the tenant suspended — fixed on a preview branch, not pushed
docs.text:
Mechanism. Key retention (ed46cc43, joined into b70ad83f) made restoreLogical require the retention ledger namespace and refuse LIFECYCLE_RETENTION_LEDGER_REQUIRED without it (lib/tenant-lifecycle/key-retention.js:109). The Compose restore driver (deploy/multitenant/restore.js:111) still calls restoreLogical without ledgerNamespace. The call runs inside the maintenance controller's claim, after the tenant is suspended, so the refusal leaves the tenant suspended, which is the controller's fail-safe for an incomplete restore. Passing the namespace exposes a second gap: the deployment plan's operator identity holds no grant on tenant_lifecycle_key_retention, and the restore fails 42501 permission denied at the same point.

Reproduced 2026-11-10 by the admin-lifecycle lane in its native suite on 9ef3ffa4 (base b70ad83f; the lane's changes do not touch the driver or the operator grants), PostgreSQL 16. A probe that passed the namespace and gave the operator a test-only SELECT, UPDATE(phase, restored_at) on that table ran the logical restore of tenant A to activated with the admin role connected (replaced 1, deleted 1; tenant B unchanged). The probe is evidence, not the fix. Evidence.

Why it was not seen. The operation-window acceptance family ran on heads before key retention, and the key-retention lane's native suites called the ceremony and destruction, not the Compose restore driver.

Fix. The driver passes ledgerNamespace: config.control.namespace (66655756). The operator identity gets the columns the two restore-path statements use and nothing else: SELECT(request_id, tenant_id, phase, retained_at, retain_until), UPDATE(phase, restored_at) on tenant_lifecycle_key_retention (565a96aa); it cannot read key names or references. Regression test: the shipped restore() with the admin role connected reaches activated (replaced 1, deleted 1; A equals its capture, B unchanged, retention record restored). Controls: driver without the namespace, grant removed, and each of four grant columns removed, all refuse with the tenant left suspended. Status: fixed on codex/admin-lifecycle-20261110, not yet joined into a #8898 candidate. Never in dev or a release, so operators are not affected.

docs.title: BF-231 · evaluator timer publications make the alarm consumer refuse or stall — fixed in part on a preview branch
docs.text:
Mechanism. Each evaluator cycle, including a time-only one, publishes a new output revision (lib/server/serve/evaluator-runtime.js:82), and the recovery and time timers do not wake the realtime consumer (:169-170; only the acquire/tick wrapper does, evaluator-preview.js:49-52). The notification producer requires the evaluator output to be unchanged between selecting and committing (lib/tenant-notifications/producer.js:21-28, checked at :32 and :46). A timer publication inside that window refuses the selection NOTIFICATION_PRODUCER_STALE. On the drain path the consumer sets EVALUATOR_CONSUMER_REFUSED and does not re-queue (evaluator-consumers.js:37,49-53); on the attempt path the request is already committed attempting (component.js:79) and is picked up again only after attempt_until (postgres.js:125).

Reproduced 2026-11-10 on b70ad83f (consumer-refusal lane, PostgreSQL 16). The failure is locked to the test's own timer phase, which is why it first looked interval-bound. At the deployed intervals (deploy/multitenant/config.js:96-103: evaluator and consumer 1000 ms, attempt timeout 10 s) with random phase, 5 of 10 runs showed a refusal and all deliveries completed late (185-305 ms). Two controlled-interleaving unit cases in tests/notification-producer.test.js go red on b70ad83f, green with the fix, red under the control (no re-selection). Evidence.

Fix (stale path). producer.select re-runs the selection on NOTIFICATION_PRODUCER_STALE up to three more times, then refuses as before; freshness checks are unchanged (1adb17f8). Open (freshness-gate path). eligible() requires the same outputRevision across its two selections (component.js:38-43); a time-only publication between them cancels or defers the attempt (:83, :92), and nothing wakes the consumer to retry. Under 150 ms churn a changed reading was delivered in 3/5 to 5/6 runs with the fix. The options are waking the consumer on timer publications, or comparing emitted effects instead of revisions; a maintainer decision. Never in dev or a release, so operators are not affected.

docs.title: BF-232 · the tenant environment drops plugin extended settings, so the stale-data alarm cannot be enabled — fixed on a preview branch, not pushed
docs.text:
Mechanism (read-derived). lib/server/tenant-app/environment.js builds each tenant's settings from the tenant's values and copies, of all extended settings, only devicestatus.days (lines 56-58). The timeago plugin raises the stale-data alarm only when extendedSettings.timeago.enableAlerts is set (lib/plugins/timeago.js:20), so a multitenant tenant cannot turn it on; a single site can. Other plugins that read extended settings for their alerts are likely affected the same way; not yet surveyed.

Reproduced 2026-11-10 on b70ad83f (extended-settings lane): with extendedSettings: {"timeago":{"enableAlerts":true}} the evaluator refuses the configuration ("invalid explicit evaluator preview configuration", evaluator-config.js:53-54) and the serving process drops it (preview-config.js:149; tenant extendedSettings is {}); with the setting forced into the environment the same evaluator raises "Stale data, check rig?", so the harness is not the cause. Evidence.

Fix. environment.js carries a frozen, typed catalogue of plugin extended settings (the names a single site reads from <PLUGIN>_<SETTING>), copied into a fresh object per tenant; the status route shows them as a single site does; the evaluator refuses unknown or mistyped keys. Provider credentials (pushover, maker, loop push keys), connect/bridge integrations, cors and the D22 dbsize floor are not carried. Per the adopted owner surface (owner-settings-projected-catalogue) these remain operator-supplied. Tenant A's alarm fires and B's does not; controls for a dropped projection, a shared object leaking A into B, and unknown keys accepted all go red. Status: fixed on codex/tenant-extended-settings-20261110, not yet joined. Never in dev or a release, so operators are not affected.

docs.title: BF-233 · after a multitenant realtime restart, stock browser clients stay disconnected — fixed on a preview branch, not pushed
docs.text:
Mechanism (reproduced 2026-11-10, realtime perf lane). On graceful shutdown the multitenant realtime role disconnects every socket from the server side (lib/server/realtime/protocol.js shutdown path). socket.io reports that to the client as io server disconnect, after which socket.io-client does not reconnect by design, and the stock browser adds no handler. Every viewer of every tenant on that process therefore stays dark until the page is reloaded. Measured on the Compose reference: after a realtime restart, stock clients recovered 0 of N on both the base cb1b751d and the perf head 6f31c94b; clients that reconnect on their own recovered 1000/1000 in 32.8 s. Single-site shutdown behaviour was not checked. A second symptom on the same path, not yet explained: with sockets attached, graceful shutdown overruns its 10 s bound (still open 10000 ms after SIGTERM). Evidence.

Fix. Shutdown closes the transport (io.close()) instead of a server-initiated disconnect, so the client sees a transport close and reconnects; no client change. The overrun came from server-disconnected polling sockets keeping TCP sockets and timers open. Status: fixed on the preview branch and joined at 0392acf9, not pushed; never in dev or a release, so operators are not affected.

docs.title: BF-234 · registry retry accepts an incomplete existing tenant — fixed on a preview branch
docs.text:
Mechanism (read-derived; native repair-ablation reproduced). The original registry provisioning retry predicate does not require all the durable rows needed by serving roles. It can return existing when activity, D15 settings/history, or required public key/checkpoint state is absent. This is an unreleased multitenant-preview path.

The repair at cced60f1 checks the complete required set before reporting success. Disabling only that new completeness decision makes the native missing-state assertions fail; restoring it passes. This is a repair ablation, not a pristine-original native run. Initial activity-fixture foreign-key setup failure is excluded from evidence. Source attribution and controls. Status: fixed on local codex/m7-join-20261111; deployment and final joined acceptance remain pending. No release exposure is claimed.

docs.title: BF-235 · registry realtime ignores persisted display preferences — fixed on a preview branch
docs.text:
Mechanism (reproduced). Registry realtime builds its environment from constant settings while the HTTP API reads persisted D15 settings. A valid saved mmol/L display preference is reported by HTTP, but realtime reports the default mg/dL preference. The discrepancy concerns display configuration: canonical glucose readings and stored thresholds remain mg/dL; this repair does not rewrite glucose readings.

1c49ea6f2 requires realtime's read-only tenant-settings capability and applies the shared persisted presentation reader. Native checks compare actual HTTP status and socket dataUpdate status, tenant isolation, changed identity and missing-state refusal. A constant-environment mutation reproduces the mismatch and restored source passes. Exact-source evidence. Status: fixed on local codex/m7-join-20261111, not released; final joined deployment and client acceptance remain pending.

docs.title: BF-236 · hot-file caches miss changed bytes and the current bound — fixed on a preview branch
docs.text:
Mechanism (reproduced). A nanosecond stat key is not a content identity: an actual same-size in-place write can change bytes while device, inode, size, modification/change times and mode remain equal. The frozen realtime cache returns old parsed authority in that case. Realtime and evaluator outer caches also omit the current byte limit, allowing the inner bounded reader to be skipped. Original platform witness. The evaluator defects are separately reproduced against exact D5 modules, rather than attributed to the later descriptor repair.

The final cache source 9f7e6bca2d39cb8d37fd9ac5918a9785eba0116e preserves arbitrary in-place edit freshness for legacy hot files with bounded read-through and parsing only changed bytes. Production registry paths keep their authoritative database reads and avoid per-tenant boot-file reads/scans. Only controlled atomic placement publication opts into a metadata cache; one owned descriptor pins the accepted inode against reuse. Explicit stop/refusal/replacement and failed-config paths release it; secondary evaluator parses borrow the boot-owned transport. Repair, resource-ownership controls and evaluator follow-up. Status: fixed on a local preview branch, not merged or released; full joined acceptance remains pending. No glucose or threshold persistence change.

docs.title: BF-237 · lifecycle snapshot races storage initialization — fixed on a preview branch
docs.text:
Mechanism (reproduced). Actual realtime status can return unavailable just after a successful invalidation. An actual PostgreSQL constructor held between backend connection and role/datastore observation reproduces a null live-record identity; releasing initialization restores the same identity. This is an unreleased multitenant lifecycle path, not a malformed client request. Exact source, actual role symptom and native discriminator.

Source 43b6b99d196e48eed2a228cdda9999b535eac7e9 waits for every initializer in one explicit record-set cut under a monotonic bound. A later constructor does not extend that cut or block healthy tenant traffic. The unchanged SQL census may trigger one further peer observation; it accepts only exact original actor PID/role/birth tuples with every source/window/placement/datastore pin rechecked. The 5487e4b9cde3adffcd8b8150d4db3056703899d9 follow-up preserves initial admitted evidence when an actor closes during that refresh. Failed, timed-out, mismatched and persistent unknown actors still refuse; there is no unknown-role exception, retry loop or global database-fence claim. Status: fixed on a local preview branch, not released. Focused/native constructor controls pass; fresh shipping-role restore under continuing B traffic and final joined acceptance remain separate gates. Earlier suspended diagnostic state is retained rather than silently reopened.

docs.title: BF-238 · evaluator independent scheduling inherits a closed parent — fixed on a preview branch
docs.text:
Mechanism (reproduced). A due callback created inside the evaluator's clinical operation-window body retains its asynchronous parent context. After that body closes, the callback's fresh admission is refused with LIFECYCLE_WINDOW_SCOPE_INVALID, masked as EVALUATOR_WINDOW_REFUSED. Actual PostgreSQL/window/runtime and an independent recording-port probe each stop after one successful body. A test-owned boot resource around only the due callback allows repeated bodies while the unchanged guard still refuses ordinary late application work. Immutable original source, actual-role failure and controls.

An actual clinical-alarm probe timed out with valid current settings and healthy membership; the membership-two to membership-three move was not issued. The capture does not attribute every canceled notification solely to this mechanism. The algorithmic memory-projection comparison is a separate coverage scope and cannot clear this scheduling defect.

Status: fixed on local core 195c932293f3abc648da8fbe4356bf7360acd002, not released. Repair and failed-prototype controls preserve active same-parent coalescing and strict expired/foreign-caller refusal, with four bounded owned/borrowed ticket slots. A pre-existing independent-job parent join now refuses before mutation instead of hanging. Boot contexts refuse ambient authority; the original operation-window execute body is byte-identical. Native lifetime-pool-max-one and separate outbox-pool-max-one checks pass. Independent review and observer and actual bounded listener qualification prove ongoing completed work within their explicit scopes. Inspection does not drive work, borrowed/no-window cycles earn no strict completion credit, and foreign rows remain observable. Separate BF-239 is now fixed locally; its causal and paired clinical proofs retain their source scopes. Final joined acceptance and capacity remain pending.

docs.title: BF-239 · unavailable models discard the alarm-repeat deadline — fixed on a preview branch
docs.text:
Mechanism (reproduced). The durable producer retains prior output and alarm state during clinical-model unavailability but removes its repeat deadline. Identical eligible recovery is no longer fresh output, yet its missing deadline is treated as already due. Actual accepted duplicate normal effects after an evaluator membership transition match the exact source repeat-without-clock origin. One tenant's identical effects are 4,438 ms apart without a new clinical write; the other has a legitimate changed reading plus identical new-payload effects 543 ms apart, against a 60-second heartbeat. These are not cancelled requests or control clears. No device receipt is inferred from accepted routing handoff. Original failed paired boundary and typed source-origin match.

Independent actual reducer scenarios reproduce the unavailable-to-identical transition and isolate retention of the known clock, with ACK/clear, normal empty output, configuration reset and genuine due-repeat controls. The actual PostgreSQL/window/outbox warm-gap discriminator reproduces the early identical effect before repair and passes on local core cd4629159809fb3cffbc6f57626f98f3ffdbdda7. It retains a genuine repeat at its original deadline. The independent repair review preserves unavailable-effect refusal, ACK/clear, configuration and due-repeat behavior. No per-tenant ownership fence or write-path index was added.

Status: fixed on a local preview branch, not merged or released. The failed source/image/state remain retained. Remote comprehensive campaign C was cancelled before tests and cleaned up. Coordinator independently runs both registered native causal suites together on cd462: five passing, zero pending, zero failing, with owned fixture cleanup. The subsequent cd462/0f paired clinical qualification passes its exact scope. Final joined native and comprehensive acceptance remain open; prior or focused repair qualification does not replace those gates. The corrected clinical oracle permits the intentional changed payload while refusing early identical accepted effects.

docs.title: BF-240 · empty-registry evaluator inspection is schema-refused — fixed on a preview branch
docs.text:
Mechanism (reproduced at the schema/transport boundary). Dynamic registry boot permits zero configured tenants, but private evaluator inspection previously required at least one in its configured-state DTO. Empty-summary observation is therefore refused despite a valid state. This is not an observed native empty-role startup failure. The prior-schema red and actual UDS empty-summary control keep that coverage distinction explicit.

Status: fixed locally in 195c932293f3abc648da8fbe4356bf7360acd002 through the v2 private DTO. Zero configured tenants is described honestly; selector, member, source and response limits are unchanged. No public client or clinical protocol is relaxed; final acceptance remains pending.

docs.title: 3. How to use this register
docs.text:
1. Anything found while doing multitenancy work that is also broken today gets an entry here, at the time it is found, with its evidence link. The register is the mechanism that keeps that promise.
  2. Prefer landing these independently. Each one is small, each ships to every current operator, and none needs a tenancy decision.
  3. Release-note the behaviour changes. BF-02 and BF-03 change what queries return. That is the point, and it should arrive as a documented fix. The note is in cgm-remote-monitor's CHANGELOG.md under [Unreleased] / Fixed, naming the collections and fields whose results change, with before/after examples.
  4. Keep severities honest. "Wrong answer with HTTP 200" is worse than "slow", and both are worse than "noisy". The table is sorted by that, not by effort.
  5. Allocate an id by reading the highest in §1/§1b at the moment you write it — never the one your brief quoted, because concurrent sessions file here.
  6. Check it is not a restatement before you file it. BF-12 is closed as invalid and is kept rather than deleted precisely because a deleted wrong entry gets raised again. Several of the entries filed on 2026-09-15 began as separate proposals and were merged into one, or folded into an existing entry as an amendment — the bulkUpsert scope findings amend BF-21 rather than taking ids, and three separate "everything says 15.0.9" proposals became one BF-60.
  7. Put it in §1 or §1b by the ships-to-operators-today test, not by how important it feels. §1 means present in what an operator runs today, which is master / 15.0.8 — not dev, not a cut branch, not an unmerged bf/* branch. That test is the only thing making §1 mean anything, and widening it would cost more than the entries it would admit.
  8. Say whether a prescribed fix has been run. An unrun prescription is marked UNVERIFIED in place rather than left to look settled.

docs.title: 4. Where this file sits
docs.text:
document relationship execution plan the reasoning, the decisions and the task definitions. Its §0 is the map of every other document queue/work-queue.yaml, queue/QUEUE.md, queue/README.md authoritative for item STATE, because its state is measured by a gate rather than asserted by an editor. This register is authoritative for defect facts and ids PR sequencing how the ten Phase 0 branches land maintainer release brief the same batch, presented as one decision semver and release versioning policy what version number each of these fixes forces

One gap in that policy is worth knowing while reading this file. Its surface ladder has no question for what the client computes and shows a person, so BF-35 — the bolus calculator's quick-pick chooser resolving the wrong record, graded high here — classifies as a patch under it and carries no operator-facing note obligation at all. The HTTP bytes are identical and the defect is entirely in the browser. BF-36 is the same case. The policy document records this as an open decision rather than silently adopting a fix; it is flagged here so that a severity in this register is not quietly downgraded by a version number somewhere else.

docs.title: BF-87 · the qs override holds the connector below its range and pins the server's query parser
docs.text:
overrides.qs = "6.15.1" and overrides.request.qs = "6.15.1" were added by 5ab0af7a ("Remediate runtime dependency CVEs", 2026-05-10), when 6.15.1 was the remedy. Since then the connector raised its own floor to ^6.15.3 and three advisories were published whose ranges include 6.15.1. overrides suppresses the ERESOLVE that would report the connector's range, so nothing says so — the BF-43 mechanism with a different package. Because the override is at the root, the single resolved copy is also the one express's and body-parser's query-string parsing uses, so the question is wider than the connector.

Not reproduced as a runtime failure or an exploit. What is asserted is the silent range violation and the advisory ranges.

Merged 2026-09-23 via PR #8749 (merge 9fd4600e; bf/qs-6.16 46b20b38): both override values are 6.16.0, the only version outside all three ranges. The documented query shapes parse identically and the suite is unchanged; only malformed bracket keys change. It changes the parser every request passes through.

docs.title: BF-227 · a no-longer-held Pushover receipt makes a handled callback answer 500 — merged to dev (#8895), not released
docs.text:
The callback route maps pushoverAck's false return to HTTP 500 on 15.0.9. Receipts can expire, be cancelled, disappear on restart, or be removed after acknowledgment. A later callback is a no-op, not a server failure.

Fixed on dev, 2026-11-01: #8895 merged at 17:45:01Z as bb85d10f. The route calls the existing handler and answers 200 when it returns normally. A known receipt still acknowledges the active alarm exactly once and removes the receipt. The unknown-receipt diagnostic is unchanged. Body-parser errors and a handler exception are not converted to success.

Evidence: the final merged route and tests at dev 61eb3733: externals/cgm-remote-monitor/lib/api/notifications-api.js:13-17, externals/cgm-remote-monitor/tests/notifications-api.test.js:90-140; retained diagnostic externals/cgm-remote-monitor/lib/server/pushnotify.js:87-88. Recorded local results: 54 focused / 59 integration-tier tests passed on Node 22.23.4 / MongoDB 8.0.29; lint, tier-map and whitespace checks passed. Both integrated CI and CodeQL runs passed. No live delivery/phone acceptance is claimed. Latest release remains 15.0.9; queue BFQ-227 is merged-upstream, with ships_to_operators_today: true meaning the defect is present on that release, not that dev's fix has shipped.

docs.title: BF-88 · the modernization branch's TRUST_PROXY-unset default changes the client address in four cases
docs.text:
395f3207 ("Restore proxy compatibility by default", lib/server/client-ip.js on origin/chore/nightscout-modernization b1bdaca0) does not reproduce the address forwarded-for gives on origin/dev 74fc6619 in four cases: an IPv6 entry after the first in a comma-and-space X-Forwarded-For chain; an IPv4 address with a non-numeric port suffix; a request with no socket remote address; and a request carrying more than one forwarding-header family (dev's precedence depends on which family earlier requests used; the branch's order is fixed).

Reproduced by a differential probe. bf2/auth-hardening 8b975b41 pins dev's behaviour for the unset default, and restoring 395f3207's client-ip.js there fails exactly 7 of 48 tests/client-ip.test.js cases (re-run 2026-09-22). Severity: low — edge-case inputs, but the address is the failed-authentication delay's key and the setting is presented as compatibility-preserving, so an upgrader has no warning.

Decided 2026-09-23 (maintainer): the cuts keep 15.0.9's unset default, forwarded-for as on dev; 395f3207's fixed-precedence normalisation is not taken, and cut 5's four tests/client-ip.test.js expectations are replaced by 15.0.9's when the cuts are rebased. No flag for the other normalisation: with TRUST_PROXY unset the forwarding headers come from any peer, so neither answer is a security boundary; an address list (proxy-addr) is the deterministic path. The unset path is revisited when TRUST_PROXY's default is flipped.

docs.title: Phase 0: how to land ten branches as pull requests
docs.text:
Record

Record as of 2026-09-15. A point-in-time document; it is not kept up to date.

Snapshot, 2026-09-15/16, against cgm-remote-monitor origin/dev a8888f0d. Historical: the plan was carried out. Merged into dev: bf/merge #8734, bf/food #8735, bf/parms #8736, bf/coercion #8737, bf/reads #8738, bf/alarms #8739, bf/cache #8740. bf/auth (P0-C) and the BF-30 throttle (P0-J) are carried by #8754 bf2/auth-hardening, open. bf/connect-pin was replaced by #8762, which pins nightscout-connect exactly 0.1.0. Connector fix/connect-timer-jitter merged as nightscout-connect #68 and is in 0.1.0; no 0.0.14 exists. Nothing past 15.0.8 is released. Current state: queue/work-queue.yaml items P0-*, BF2-AUTH and RT-0, and the backfix register. Branch SHAs, pins and counts below are as of 2026-09-15/16.

Contributor-facing.

The plan is nine independent PRs onto dev, plus one independent PR in nightscout-connect (the earlier two-deep stack existed only because of a CHANGELOG.md collision, removed at the maintainer's instruction — §0b, §3a).

docs.title: The set, measured
docs.text:
Ten branches: nine in cgm-remote-monitor, one in nightscout-connect. All nine cgm-remote-monitor branches sit directly on origin/dev at a8888f0d in worktrees under externals/work/. There is no branch in this set based on another branch in this set.

repo branch tip commits what it is cgm-remote-monitor bf/alarms 5dcf783f 3 BF-28, BF-29, BF-31 — alarm delivery cgm-remote-monitor bf/auth 56ed29d2 3 BF-17, BF-30 — security. Third commit added 2026-09-16, see below cgm-remote-monitor bf/cache 4f86bab1 2 T0.2, T0.3 — cache clone cost cgm-remote-monitor bf/coercion b7234753 2 T0.5 — query filter typing, plus BF-40's $exists inversion. Amended and combined 2026-09-16, see below cgm-remote-monitor bf/connect-pin 0807eb1c 1 connector pin → the v0.0.14 tarball (one file, +1/−1) cgm-remote-monitor bf/food 73495331 1 BF-16, and BF-35 surfaced while fixing it cgm-remote-monitor bf/merge b06c6faf 1 BF-36 cgm-remote-monitor bf/parms eb0bc918 3 BF-37, BF-38, BF-39 cgm-remote-monitor bf/reads 2ecfeb53 6 six read-path fixes — BF-01, BF-05, BF-13, BF-14, BF-15, BF-33 nightscout-connect fix/connect-timer-jitter c1cce2a2 — T0.4 start jitter + BF-34

Plus, prepared locally in nightscout-connect: branch release/v0.0.14 and an annotated tag v0.0.14, both at 649a7de2.

The SHAs that moved, and why. bf/coercion 88d1f8a4 → ab197bf8 (9 files, code only; 40 CHANGELOG lines removed) → b7519fc7 (2026-09-16: two code comments and one paragraph of the commit message stated BF-32's refuted mechanism as fact) → f829ea11 (same day: BF-68, a regression the branch introduced — $type's operand is a BSON type code and excluding it from conversion turned a working find[sgv][$type]=2 into an HTTP 500). 29 passing. bf/reads 0d19bb31 → 2ecfeb53 (the changelog-only commit dropped, and the branch un-stacked from bf/coercion and rebased directly onto origin/dev, which is why it now carries 6 commits rather than 8). Safety refs bf/coercion.bak-changelog (88d1f8a4) and bf/reads.bak-changelog (0d19bb31) are kept until the PRs merge, as is the older bf/reads-prerebase (824380a0). Verified at the time of the strip: git range-diff shows all six bf/reads commits content-identical (=); bf/coercion differs from its backup by exactly the 40 changelog lines and no code; messages, authorship and dates preserved.

A third SHA moved, 2026-09-16, after this document was written. bf/auth 64db1f35 → 56ed29d2, and the branch now carries 3 commits rather than 2. The new commit removes a console.log('Loading', opts) from lib/authorization/storage.js — a per-request debug print of request-derived values, the same defect class as the count-path filter leak fixed on bf/reads. The line is not introduced by the branch; it is on origin/dev at storage.js:84, and it was taken here because it sits in a file this branch already rewrites. It was the last failing gate on queue item P0-C, which now reports 3/3 runnable gates passing. 64db1f35 still exists on the branch and is still the BF-17 commit, so references to it as the BF-17 commit elsewhere remain correct; only the tip and the commit count moved. The diff is still ten files.

origin/dev has not moved. Re-fetched live during this rewrite: origin/dev is a8888f0d, dated 2026-09-09, and git rev-list --count a8888f0d..origin/dev is 0. Every branch here shares that base and none of them is drifting from anything. (A cached FETCH_HEAD a day old is the stale-ref trap to avoid when re-checking this.)

So the argument for landing these is not a clock. It is that nine branches deep is a review-queue problem on its own terms, that the marginal find is now worth less than the marginal landing, and that nine of the defects in this batch were ones no register entry predicted — which says the register has stopped being the bottleneck.

docs.title: 0. Publishing is manual, deliberately
docs.text:
Nothing in this document pushes, tags remotely, merges or publishes. A human does each of those steps, so that each one gets reviewed. Agents and automated sessions prepare branches, commits and tags locally and stop. That is a standing rule for this programme, not a property of this particular batch — see the execution plan's handoff block.

This matters more than usual here because pushing some branches publishes artefacts, and because the code goes to people who dose insulin using it.

docs.title: Which branches are safe to push — measured, not assumed
cgm-remote-monitor
docs.text:
target safe to push? what happens dev NO — publishes .github/workflows/main.yml job docker-build, if: (github.ref == 'refs/heads/master' \|\| github.ref == 'refs/heads/dev') && github.repository_owner == 'nightscout', logs into Docker Hub with secrets.DOCKER_USER/DOCKER_PASS and pushes an image master NO — publishes same job, same condition chore/nightscout-modernization yes no push: trigger matches it. PRs targeting it run full CI (main.yml and CodeQL both list it under pull_request) any other branch on origin yes main.yml and codeql-analysis.yml both trigger on push only for master and dev. A feature-branch push runs nothing the bewest fork remote yes, lowest footprint git@github.com/bewest/cgm-remote-monitor.git, already configured as remote bewest

So: push the nine cgm-remote-monitor Phase 0 branches to origin (or to the fork) and open PRs against dev. Never push the branch onto dev. The PR is what gets reviewed; the merge is what publishes.

The CodeQL row, re-measured 2026-09-15. On origin/chore/nightscout-modernization, codeql-analysis.yml line 17 is push: branches: [ dev, master ] and line 19 is pull_request: branches: [ dev, master, chore/nightscout-modernization ] — reading only the push: line gives the wrong answer. main.yml on that branch lists the third branch too, and carries four jobs dev lacks (maintained-mongo, replica-test, browser-test, plus a concurrency group).

One trap worth knowing about the fork route. close-accidental-sync-prs.yml auto-closes a PR when all three hold: it comes from a fork, its title matches sync|merge|update|pull|new, and its diff is empty. A real PR is never auto-closed because the third condition fails — but several natural titles for this batch contain those words, so if a PR ever vanishes, that is why.

docs.title: nightscout-connect
docs.text:
target safe to push? what happens any branch, including main yes the repo has exactly one workflow, test.yml, on: [push, pull_request], permissions: contents: read. It runs the suite on Node 22 and 24. No secrets, no registry, no publish tags yes there is no release workflow at all. Pushing v0.0.14 runs the same tests and publishes nothing

npm publish for the connector is entirely manual. Nothing automates it, so cutting and pushing the tag is safe and reversible; the publish is a separate, deliberate human act.

docs.title: The review rule this encodes
docs.text:
• Prepare locally, push a branch, open a PR, let a human merge. Two of five prescribed fixes in the backfix register turned out to be wrong when someone actually ran them, and four register entries had claims that did not survive contact. Review is where that gets caught.
  • dev and master are publication events, not branches. Treat a push to either as shipping.
  • A release is three separate human decisions — merge the code, push the tag, publish the package — and this batch needs all three, in that order.

docs.title: 0b. CHANGELOG.md is a release output. Branches never hand-edit it.
docs.text:
This is the maintainer's rule, and it is why two branches in this set were rewritten.

CHANGELOG.md is generated by GitHub tooling between releases. It is an output of the release process, not an input to it. No branch in this programme may add to it, edit it, or create it.

Release notes for this batch live in this control-surface repository, under releases/, as release assets:

path what it is releases/cgm-remote-monitor-15.0.9/release-notes.md operator-facing notes for the 15.0.9 candidate releases/cgm-remote-monitor-15.0.9/contents.md what is in it, per branch, with the measurements releases/cgm-remote-monitor-15.0.9/tag-message.txt the annotated tag body releases/cgm-remote-monitor-15.0.9/verification-record.{md,json} per-item evidence grade releases/nightscout-connect-v0.0.14/ the same three for the connector release releases/_template/ the shape a new release directory takes

Per-PR description text lives in reports/phase0-pr-bodies/ — one file per branch, named for the branch.

Measured after the strip: none of the nine cgm-remote-monitor branches touches CHANGELOG.md. git diff --name-only origin/dev...<branch> | grep -c '^CHANGELOG.md$' is 0 for every one of bf/alarms, bf/auth, bf/cache, bf/coercion, bf/connect-pin, bf/food, bf/merge, bf/parms and bf/reads. (Reproduced.)

Three consequences:

  1. bf/food no longer needs to avoid creating the file. The old instruction — "it deliberately does not create CHANGELOG.md because bf/reads and bf/coercion both add it" — described a collision that no longer exists. Nothing adds it. BF-35's release note belongs in releases/cgm-remote-monitor-15.0.9/.
  2. bf/auth gets no CHANGELOG entry. The BF-17 rotation note and the replaceOne narrowing are operator-facing and belong in the release notes and in reports/phase0-pr-bodies/bf-auth.md.
  3. For bf/reads, correct the release note, which is where the too-narrow scope statement now lives. See §4.

docs.title: 1. There is no stack. All nine are independent.
docs.text:
The instinct with ten related branches is a stack — each PR based on the last. Measured, that would be wrong here.

All 36 unordered pairs among the nine cgm-remote-monitor branches merge clean, and all nine merge clean against origin/dev. Reproduced during this rewrite with git merge-tree --write-tree over every pair and against origin/dev: 9 clean against dev, 36 pairs, 0 conflicts, bf/connect-pin included. bf/coercion and bf/reads are among those 36 and they merge clean with each other.

The measurement is not vacuous, and proving that took two attempts — the first control was mis-scoped and is recorded rather than hidden.

  • Mis-scoped control (reported as such, per rule 2). The obvious control, bf/reads.bak-changelog × bf/coercion.bak-changelog, came back clean. That is not evidence the harness is blind: bf/coercion.bak-changelog is an ancestor of bf/reads.bak-changelog (the backup preserved the stacked shape), so the pair could not conflict. The ablation was wrong, not the check.
  • Re-scoped control, which fires. bf/reads-prerebase × bf/coercion.bak-changelog exits 1 and names CHANGELOG.md:
CHANGELOG.md
Auto-merging CHANGELOG.md
CONFLICT (content): Merge conflict in CHANGELOG.md
Auto-merging lib/server/activity.js
Auto-merging lib/server/devicestatus.js
Auto-merging lib/server/entries.js
Auto-merging lib/server/profile.js
Auto-merging lib/server/treatments.js

So the harness does detect a conflict when there is one; the 36 clean results are a fact about the branches, not about the command.

bf/coercion and bf/reads share five files — lib/server/activity.js, devicestatus.js, entries.js, profile.js and treatments.js — and none of them ever conflicted. (Earlier revisions said six by counting "the query path" as a shared file; it is not shared. lib/server/query.js, query-coercion.js and query-coercion.json are bf/coercion's alone, and lib/server/aggregate.js and count.js are bf/reads' alone. Reproduced with comm -12 over the two name lists.) The only collision this batch ever had was both branches appending to the same ### Fixed heading under [Unreleased] in CHANGELOG.md, and §0b removed the file from both.

A stack costs serial review and serial merge. Buy it only where there is a real dependency. After the strip there is none, so: nine independent PRs off dev, mergeable in any order, plus one independent PR in nightscout-connect.

What a clean merge does not buy you is at §3b. bf/coercion and bf/reads compose correctly, but that is a separate fact from merging cleanly, and it was established by inspecting the merged tree rather than by the absence of a conflict.

docs.title: 2. The batch, in the order worth reviewing it
docs.text: Order is a review recommendation, not a dependency. Every one of these can be opened, reviewed and merged without reference to any other. The ranking is by consequence to a person using the software.

docs.title: First, because it reaches an operator only through a pin move
docs.text:
branch repo what it is fix/connect-timer-jitter c1cce2a2 nightscout-connect T0.4 (start jitter) and BF-34 bf/connect-pin 0807eb1c cgm-remote-monitor moves the pin to the v0.0.14 tarball, one file, +1/−1

BF-34 is the highest-value fix in the whole Phase 0 set and it is easy to miss because it is in the other repository. backoff() merges its options as { ...config, ...defaults } — the spread order is reversed, so every value any caller passes is discarded. All five vendor sources configure a 2.5-minute retry interval and every one gets the 256 ms default, 586× faster, with use_random_slot forced false so a pool that fails together retries in exact lockstep. Measured: 100 actors delivered the same 800 requests across 3 s before and 67 s after.

A vendor that is refusing requests gets hammered by every account at once, which is precisely when it can least afford it — and the behaviour is invisible to the operator whose account is being rate-limited. Land this one first if anything is landed first.

BF-34 has a second half that the register entry does not carry, established by the E1 Dexcom comparison. The same { ...config, ...defaults } merge also makes the ceiling 74.6 hours, because exponent_ceiling caps the exponent, not the delay. So the one defect produces a retry storm first and a three-day dark window second, and the dark-window half is the one that stops a person's data arriving. Both halves ship on dev today. See E1 and the register's BF-34.

T0.4 also corrected its own premise: the actors do not stay phase-locked, because all four vendor drivers already spell an 18-second random window into the timestamp they align to. The start is the burst, and it does not repeat.

docs.title: Then, because it puts a wrong number in front of a person
docs.text:
branch what it is bf/food 73495331 BF-16 and BF-35. PR #8735, opened 2026-09-16. Its SOURCE_ASSERTIONS prerequisite is discharged (f9046bab) and no longer gates the merge — see the corrected item 2 below. See register BF-16

BF-35 — the bolus calculator's quick-pick chooser resolves the wrong record. Verified independently against origin/dev:

lib/client/boluscalc.js:648-652   records.forEach(r => { if (r.type == 'quickpick') quickpicks.push(r); });
lib/client/boluscalc.js:654-657   for (var i = 0; i < records.length; i++)          // UNFILTERED
                                    $('#bc_quickpick').append($('<option>').val(i)  // index into records
                                      .text(r.name + ' (' + r.carbs + ' g)'));
lib/client/boluscalc.js:579       var qp = quickpicks[parseInt(qpiselected)];        // FILTERED
lib/client/boluscalc.js:580       foods = JSON.parse(JSON.stringify(qp.foods));      // the carb source

The option's label comes from records[i]; the foods the calculator totals carbs from come from quickpicks[i]. Different records, no mismatch reported. The list also offers plain foods that are not quick picks at all, and selecting a late option throws because qp is undefined.

This is the most consequential defect found in Phase 0. Everything else in this batch returns a wrong answer to a query or fails to raise an alarm. This one puts a carbohydrate total the user did not choose into a bolus calculation, under a label they did read.

It has shipped in every release since 3457de5b (2017-10-16) — eight years. The same commit removed the only caller of /api/v1/food/quickpicks. In loadFoodDatabase the type filter moved into the loop and stayed correct; in loadFoodQuickpicks it became a separate pass and the loop kept iterating the original array. Before that commit the source was the quickpicks endpoint, where every record was a quick pick — so the code was right when written and made wrong by a change that did not appear to touch it. It only bites a site whose food database holds at least one plain food, which is why it survived.

A detail worth keeping: line 655 carries /* eslint-disable-next-line security/detect-object-injection */ // verified false positive. Somebody examined that exact line, correctly cleared it of the thing the linter flagged, and did not see the indexing bug beside it.

BF-16 confirmed; its reachability claim did not hold. The lexicographic position sort was real and reached nobody: /api/v1/food/quickpicks has no consumer in the tree. The order users actually see was broken by the chooser not sorting at all. The type ambiguity is real and is now reproduced over HTTP rather than read. A fourth site the entry did not name, restoreBoolValue, mapped === 'true' and so turned a real boolean true into false, silently un-hiding a hidden quick pick on every editor load — the only one of the four losing a setting rather than failing to read one.

What whoever lands this branch needs to know:

  1. The release note is required and it does not go in the branch. The quick-pick list changes contents and what selecting an entry does, so anyone who had learned to work around the mislabelling will see different behaviour. Write it into releases/cgm-remote-monitor-15.0.9/release-notes.md. See §0b.
  2. A drift tripwire fired when this branch was prepared, and it is DISCHARGED as of 2026-09-16 (f9046bab). tools/nsschema/code_model.py's SOURCE_ASSERTIONS deliberately pins the quoted 'false' in lib/server/food.js and record[key] === 'true' in lib/food/food.js, so that fixing them forces the food model to be revisited. Both are gone on bf/food.

The anchors were not simply flipped, and BF-16's prescription was not followed. Flipping the anchors to the post-fix spelling would have failed the check against both source roots, which still carry the pre-fix text because bf/food has not merged; the check would have been off across exactly the window it is least affordable to lose. Each anchor now accepts the pre-fix and post-fix spelling and nothing else, and lib/food/quickpick.js's isTrue sits in a separate SOURCE_ASSERTIONS_IF_PRESENT tuple that arms when the file appears. Measured: make schema-code-drift exits 0 against crm-seam, cgm-remote-monitor-official and crm-bf-food; the last failed on exactly these two anchors beforehand. Ablated three ways, each break confirmed to land first: { hidden: false } fails, Boolean() fails, renaming quickpick.isTrue fails.

Owed at merge, not before: delete the pre-fix arm of each anchor and promote the SOURCE_ASSERTIONS_IF_PRESENT entry, or a revert passes the drift check silently.

docs.title: Then, because the user ends up with no page at all
Then the query and read paths
docs.text:
branch commits what it is bf/coercion b7234753 2 T0.5 — query filter typing, and BF-40's $exists=false inversion. The largest change in the batch bf/reads 2ecfeb53 6 BF-01, BF-05, BF-13, BF-14, BF-15, BF-33

These two are not a stack. They merge clean with each other and with everything else, and they compose correctly — but that composition is a property of the pair, not of either PR, and it is the one thing in this batch a reviewer cannot see from a single diff. §3b is the check that covers it, and it survives the dissolution of the stack.

bf/reads, in branch order:

4772b983  count/:storage/where counted nothing because it built its filter from the defaults   (BF-01)
3b588098  Every count request printed its filter, and the filter's values, to stdout           (BF-05)
5a5269a3  v3 paging lost and repeated documents whenever the whole sort chain tied
12207df3  v3 answered a dotted ?fields= with an empty document and HTTP 200
06b133a7  ?count=0 asked for no documents and was answered with the whole collection
2ecfeb53  v3 ?limit=0x10 removed the bound and returned the whole collection                   (BF-33)

Ordering constraint inside the branch: BF-05's commit must follow BF-01's. They share two files — lib/server/aggregate.js and tests/api.count-where.test.js — and the branch is already in that order. (Reproduced with git show --stat on both commits: 4772b983 then 3b588098.)

Every other commit on every branch lands alone.

docs.title: Then availability, not correctness
docs.text:
branch what it is bf/merge b06c6faf BF-36. One lib file, one new test file. Its test is one of the 52 files neither local script runs — use npm test, not npm run test:unit; see register BF-53

BF-36 — mergeTreatmentUpdate reads past the array it is splicing. Verified against origin/dev:

lib/client/receiveddata.js:99    var m = cachedDataArray.length;   // captured ONCE
lib/client/receiveddata.js:104     cachedDataArray.push(no);       // grows it
lib/client/receiveddata.js:107     for (var j = 0; j < m; j++) {   // stale bound
lib/client/receiveddata.js:109       if (no._id === cachedDataArray[j]._id)   // throws
lib/client/receiveddata.js:111         cachedDataArray.splice(j, 1);          // SHRINKS it

A remove splices the array while m stays put, so the next received item that matches nothing walks j past the end and dereferences undefined._id. It needs a splice followed by a miss, which is why it survived: two removes do not do it (the second matches and breaks first), and an insert does not either (push grows the array past the bound rather than below it). Deleting a treatment and editing another that is outside the client's two-day window does.

Severity is medium, and the reasoning is worth keeping because it sets the priority order. The throw escapes receiveDData into dataUpdate, which has no try/catch, so the page stops advancing until reloaded. But it is not silent: updateClock runs on its own setTimeout chain, so the time-ago indicator keeps working and marks the page stale.

BF-35 tells you a wrong thing. BF-36 stops telling you things, visibly. That is the distinction that puts one at the front of this batch and the other with the availability entries.

The two functions had drifted apart. mergeDataUpdate, thirty lines up in the same file, re-reads its bound (l = newArray.length, :25) before its second loop and walks its purge backwards. mergeTreatmentUpdate does neither. Both are exported with //expose for tests and neither had a single test; both are now pinned.
