docs.title: Deferred and separate lanes
docs.text: Candidate Lane Boundary / dependency Historical anonymous resource ownership Historical captures and later closure receipts Original failures and their ownership limits remain immutable. Later campaign/publication records retain their actual cleanup receipts. Do not turn an earlier residual inventory into a current live count or infer global leak freedom. Stronger consistency and broader evaluator/runtime acceptance R73 functional one-host M5 accepted R73 joins bounded current-state/evaluator, durable alarm/request and actual consumer proofs with complete final-tree verification. Broader clinical workloads, operating envelope, selected providers, multi-node ownership and production/default admission remain separate; historical R54/R55 source attribution is unchanged. Broader settings/client and resource acceptance R51 bounded settings accepted 33870764 accepted for bounded settings; full7089/80pending/0failure/browser684/prcheckOK and archived controls. Regex/dotted predicates refusePG500, performance unmeasured; no all-query/client parity. Wider owner catalogue and lifecycle M6 lifecycle scope / reader option withdrawn Optional subject-reader mode is withdrawn after R63 legacy-root incompatibility. Existing-grant clamping, if reconsidered in M6, must preserve existing credentials. Human issuer/refresh, durable lifecycle, production resolution trust and wider catalogue remain M6 work. Operator inactivity/resource eligibility is a separate open policy topic, not inferred from restore suspension. Writer config.ownerPolicy is retained. Replica history outside the selected clock contract Clock correctness accepted in R60; wider replica contract open The original unclocked timestamp characterization remains a failed exclusive-history guarantee. Joined commit-coupled clock paths have bounded correctness acceptance; clock default enablement, performance and general replica interchangeability are not inferred. Read existing Nightscout data through its API Entries / import This is a one-time database population, not ongoing NS-to-NS synchronization; no durable checkpoint is required. Use bounded pagination, duplicate-safe reruns and best-effort srvModified reconciliation. Physical hard deletes may be undetectable, so do not claim exact deletion reconciliation or raw-backup fidelity; nightscout-connect remains the separate ongoing sync pipeline. Human identity and next-generation execution Separate source and acceptance boundaries Shared optional OIDC/owner implementation is local source work; actual signed native DB/Vault/HTTPS/browser acceptance remains UNMEASURED. Independent computed-single and derived-output characterization do not select a universal profile or publication service. See current release contents for ownership. Resource/performance budgets and Android emulator lab Batch C by maintainer decision M1 resource bounds deferred, measured in C; no approved numeric threshold. Controlled quiet steady-state benchmark needs independent stored-count oracle. M4 uses headless actual/source-pattern coverage with no all-client claim; Android emulator belongs to C.

docs.title: Updating this dashboard
docs.text:
1. Update queue/work-queue.yaml for work states and real prerequisites. Do not duplicate those edges in the status overlay.
  2. Record measured evidence in the integration record or a dated report; set each slice's evidence to its document and heading. Update multitenant-delivery-status.json for dated slice stages, integration tip, lanes and remaining milestone gates. Use explicit commit/results; do not promote on ancestry alone.
  3. Run python tools/queue/multitenant_dashboard.py, then python tools/queue/multitenant_dashboard.py --check, make queue-check and make site-check. Commit the source and generated view together. Publishing remains a separate maintainer action.

docs.title: Multitenant delivery roadmap
docs.text:
Living document, last changed 2026-11-10 at 4917b2d4a.

Contributor-facing living plan. Reconciled 2026-11-10 to the M6a/M6b joined acceptance records and adopted release decisions, without a new application campaign or milestone promotion. This page owns delivery boundaries and promotion criteria. The dashboard owns recorded milestone claims; the queue owns item states, gates and blockers.

docs.title: Reading and execution order
docs.text:
Use the reading guide to select a contract. Use the completion schedule for current batch ownership, implementation order and verification depth. The integration record owns executed heads, failures, controls and campaign limits; release contents owns publication and cycle updates. A source branch, an incorporated change, an accepted batch and a promoted milestone are distinct claims.

Delivery uses three completion stages: A, data/control/clients through M4; B, durable runtime for M5; C, synthetic operations for M6, split on 2026-11-09 into M6a–M6d, followed by M7 production readiness. Independent implementation and early uncertainty proofs may proceed in parallel. Freeze one coherent candidate for comprehensive acceptance; do not rerun accepted campaigns merely because a new session resumes. Promotion requires the complete criterion list below, with actual commands, source/instrument revisions, artifacts and verdicts on the applicable final tree.

Use the current M5/M6 decision list for remaining human questions and measurement prerequisites. Prefer a minimal working reference with explicitly deferred enhancements; do not substitute a component pass for a milestone.

docs.title: Supported boundary and owner journeys
docs.text:
The supported owner deliverable is a headless, documented, versioned API, with conformance independent of vendor UI. A first-party owner UI is deferred; vendor UI must use the same validation and floors and must not put an all-tenant service credential on the owner's request path. Existing single/Mongo behavior remains first-class. The multitenant target uses PostgreSQL/RLS; single PostgreSQL, multitenant MongoDB and SQLite/Celld are outside this delivery series. Multitenant completion is not a 16.0.0 tag prerequisite; placement of a reviewed dormant slice remains separate from enabling its roles.

Initial lifecycle operations are private-operator actions: provision, suspend, export and delete, without public signup. An owner may export or request deletion; the operator authorizes and executes deletion. A request never bypasses confirmation, retention or recovery policy. The preview deletion ceremony requires explicit operator confirmation, allows cancellation before execution starts, and imposes no mandatory waiting period. Ownership changes are operator-assisted for the first preview; self-service co-owner addition and transfer follow separately. Operator execution still preserves last-owner protection and owner-secret boundaries.

Owner journey Required contract Capability boundary Understand configuration Effective value, source/default/pin/constraint, stored owner value and explicit ignored/rejected reasons No raw secrets in config reads Change units, timezone and display Reviewed typed catalogue, validation, version/precondition, audit attribution, live invalidation and rollback Small reviewed catalogue first Manage uploaders/followers Tenant-local subjects/roles, root and subject-token rotation/revocation Preserve legacy credentials; distinguish root from least privilege Configure connectors/push targets Typed integration kinds, bounded egress, tenant-owned secret references, split owner/operator credential parts and health Admit each kind only after its consuming runtime gate Export/request deletion Tenant-local export, request/confirmation status and private operator execution No foreign rows or secret plaintext in the artifact Change alarm settings Preview/confirmation, ordered thresholds, units, evaluator version and invalidation Unavailable until multitenant alarm acceptance

Controller registration, commands/intents and delegated-access journeys have their own contracts. Their later runtime is not implied by a configuration API.

docs.title: Configuration, authority and secrets
docs.text:
Owner authority, including its shared OIDC integration, owns management authority, delegation, session/reauthentication and local-verification amendments. Preserve D22's order: code floors, then operator defaults/bounds/pins, then permitted owner values. Refuse unsupported names explicitly; role deployment values stay in the environment and credentials are not settings. Full catalogue claims need a fresh census. Names, API paths, preconditions and refusal shapes belong to the reviewed configuration contract, rather than being selected ad hoc by a lane.

Grant removal or token revocation takes effect on the next protected operation across workers, at a defined authoritative-read linearization point. If current state cannot be established, refuse. An unexpired token or stale cached grant is insufficient; an operation already authorized/in flight is not retroactively undone. Socket writes, subscription changes and protected delivery share this boundary, including reconnect, cache invalidation and authority-outage controls.

Preserve each tenant's legacy hashed api-secret header, subject tokens and socket secret forms. Resolve and authorize the tenant before credential verification; there is no process-wide multitenant root secret. Data credentials do not imply owner management or delegation authority. Audit records name the verified subject/root principal rather than inventing a human identity. Human login uses an interchangeable reviewed identity provider, not a new password/recovery system.

The promotion decisions drop the incompatible optional subject-reader clamping mode. Any replacement must preserve existing tenant-root credentials. Proposed-grant management enforcement and full lifecycle authority are separate contracts.

The secrets component owns recoverable secrets and private signing keys. New asymmetric tokens may verify locally with trusted public keys and current PostgreSQL authority; private keys remain protected. Vault Transit does not store submitted application data: tenant-bound ciphertext/references, scoped consumers, key versions, redacted audit, renewal and recovery remain necessary. Owner reveal is an explicitly authorized audited action, not a data-API decrypt. The built-in encrypted development/small-operator option remains adopted; production adapters must meet the same contract. A disposable Vault lab does not establish TLS, unseal/recovery, production identity, HA or operational suitability. Failures never fall back to plaintext, another tenant's key or an unapproved signer. The deployment and trust decisions keep Vault Transit at every stage and admit a deployment by trust record plus live probes. Connectivity is a Vault Agent sidecar with one AppRole per deployment; core reads the token from the sink file per call (MT-VAULT-TOKEN-FILE) instead of carrying a service-login adapter.

docs.title: Tenant identity, migrations and import
docs.text:
Keep permanent or disposable public aliases, durable DNS-friendly internal names and stable tenant IDs distinct. Deployment-owned mapping binds internal name to ID; alias rotation does not recreate a tenant or transfer credentials/data. DNS discovery is not authority. The public-name binding contract adds explicit authentication/anonymous/group-policy requirements for shareable addresses; their concrete policy and schedule semantics still need acceptance. Preserve direct-alias mode and make canonical ingress explicit: only trusted transport may supply the configured internal selector; forwarded public aliases cannot override it. Conflicting/spoofed selectors and trust loss refuse. Durable allocation, collision, rename/reassignment/deletion and mapping consistency require explicit contracts before operator-writer admission. Consul, Kubernetes and vendor discovery are optional adapters, not dependencies adopted by this roadmap. Public domains, certificates and private edge implementation remain deployment concerns. The reference deployment trusts its edge by immediate peer address, one list for tenant selection and client IP.

Multitenant schema migration is explicit operator execution. Serving checks compatibility read-only and refuses stale/unsafe schema; it never migrates at boot. Keep committed catalogue bytes/checksums immutable. Two-store runner acceptance covers locks/leases, fencing, ledger/drift, crash/restart and supported steps; standalone/index/quiescence and chunking guarantees need their own gates. This does not alter the separately decided single-site boot behavior.

The source-Nightscout API importer is one-time database population, not schema migration over HTTP or ongoing synchronization. Bounded pagination and duplicate-safe reruns start from the beginning; a durable checkpoint is not required. Offset pagination plus srvModified history is best-effort, not a point-in-time snapshot. Hard deletes can leave stale or missing target rows, legacy rows may lack history, and API projections may omit stored fields. Preserve ObjectId/string distinction and refuse ambiguous repeated textual IDs; accept JSONB logical equality without claiming BSON field-order fidelity. This importer is not a raw backup. nightscout-connect remains the separate ongoing synchronization path.

Apply the restore identity and cloning decision. Operational restore labs retain original-tenant bindings. Clinical API population and synchronization do not migrate credential authority. Cloning implementation and native acceptance remain UNMEASURED.

docs.title: Milestones and continuous integration
docs.text:
R72 records M0–M4; R73 records functional M5. The later operation-window family records restore/restart and packaged reference acceptance; the dashboard displays milestone claims. The criteria below retain their adopted scope.

The release promotion decisions fix the scope of these bars. In particular, M2 is its table cell; human issuer/refresh, existing-grant clamping, full lifecycle and production-resolution trust belong to M6. Numeric resource/performance budgets are deferred to C; M1 may promote with that deferral stated. The PostgreSQL sort-key cap remains 5, an intentional PG-only difference. No threshold is invented by a passing lab.

Milestone Build / dependencies Acceptance before promotion M0: foundations Current-dev integration; PG transaction binding and RLS; migration/secrets contracts may proceed independently Non-bypass application role, overlapping IDs, unbound reader, read/write isolation, rollback/error cleanup, demonstrated pool reuse and paired breaks. No default or production role enabled; explicit D21 lab preview permitted. M1: entries adapter ST-PG on M0; current filter/read/write/identity contracts; reviewed DDL through MIG-RUNNER Applicable backend tests execute against both stores; no pending-as-pass. Explicit unsupported collections/operations. Null, ordering/pagination, resend/delete and batch outcomes; preserve source labels/events. Reviewed import contract and populated identity/order fidelity. Resource bounds may be explicitly deferred to C by the adopted decision. M2: tenant control plane MT-CONFIG-MIN, MT-SECRETS-CONTRACT, MIG-RUNNER, TEN-RESOLVE, T30-WIRING Tenant-local effective config and versioned writes; unknown tenant refuses; A token works on A and fails on B by signature; no environment/root/key leakage; separate owner/data/operator routes. M3: two-tenant HTTP lab Complete M1 + M2; TEN-LAB Actual authorized entries-v3 requests and independent stored outcomes for both tenants, positive/negative controls; startup refuses stale/unsafe schema. A bounded lab alone is not the complete multitenant preview. M4: existing-client surface M3; further collections and v1/storage wiring, v2 exchange, tenant-local history/indexes Executed headless clients plus source-pattern replay for the rest, pinned uploader/follower shapes, no coordinated client upgrade, tenant-local identity and correct batch/retry/refusal semantics. State explicitly that this is not an all-client claim. Android emulator acceptance is in C; iOS execution is outside the automated lab. M5: realtime and evaluator MT-RUNTIME-PLAN; computed views; durable interprocess delivery/recovery; settings/secrets consumers Socket authorization/reconnect/write compatibility, tenant-local rooms/caches, replay-equivalent views, durable ack/snooze and restart/double-delivery checks. Live notification acceptance is separate. M6a: identity and owner API M4 + M5; combined owner/OIDC candidate joined to #8898 Nine-stage native matrix passes on the frozen candidate through the disposable harness (Vault single/multi, Mongo and PG sessions, Mongo HTTPS, owner consumer, authority, browser, compatibility) with its red controls; then the joined candidate passes full, default-browser, enabled-corpus, pinned-client and prcheck. Enabled/disabled parity and legacy-client controls per the M6 bounded owner API family. M6b: lifecycle and keys M6a Operator-assisted ownership add/transfer/recovery (tenant-bound, audited, no orphan, no silent replacement); retained-key destruction after the 30-day window and after-window refusal; export/delete ceremony as adopted. One SQL/HTTP family each, each with a red control. M6c: deployment trust (nightscout-deploy) M6a; core tokenFile change Vault Agent sidecar with auto-auth, sink and renewal; Authentik profile over HTTPS with synthetic people; live spoof, host/selector conflict and outage probes against the Compose edge and Vault; written trust record from the template. Admission is per deployment by record plus probes. M6d: connector sync M6a nightscout-connect pulls from a tenant with a pre-issued reader credential; independent stored/history outcomes; revocation stops the pull. Outbound first; inbound tenant-side connector is a later contract. M7: production readiness M6a–M6d Measured, not declared (decision): benchmark the one-host reference at stepped tenant counts with a hot tenant and publish the numbers; contrast against N single-tenant processes and the per-site model at equal synthetic load; prove each component scales horizontally or vertically as intended with a binding inventory (any binding is a file:line finding); evaluator partitioning by member count and ordinal with a pool-membership table (decision). Realtime tenant sharding and controlled recovery, including checkpoint and complete participant coverage; larger single-tenant connection fanout remains separately bounded. Android emulator lab; selectable endpoints and fixed-roster API scaling; Kubernetes binding equivalence. Limits follow the measurements. Required before a production cohort, not before the dormant alpha release.

M6 was split into M6a–M6d and M7 on 2026-11-09 (decision). The acceptance families below keep their text; the family-to-milestone mapping is: bounded owner API → M6a; operator-assisted ownership, lifecycle and trust (keys, deletion) → M6b; deployment trust rows → M6c; operations and clients → M7 (Android) with populated backup/restore retained in M6b; operating envelope and final review → M7.

CI is cumulative: keep default single/Mongo tests green and run explicit PG suites as they become applicable. Publish pending/unsupported inventory. Each isolation property needs positive own-tenant behavior and a meaningful red control against the actual implementation. A component pass is not a parent milestone pass.

Use the adopted durable event contract for D6/D-EVENT reconciliation. A process-local event is not a durable bus. Before consumer admission, prove commit coupling, durable checkpoints, ordering, complete cohorts, duplication/deletion/config invalidation and crash/replay boundaries. The event carries the transaction's final floor, as decided in the B7 record. Time-only ticks drive time-based alarms. The separately scheduled bounded snapshot reconciliation recovers current rows and absence after missed wakes; neither mechanism promises recovery of every intermediate transition. D23 forwards socket writes/acks unchanged from the reader realtime role to the internal api write endpoint with the socket source label; client behavior and current authority must be measured at that boundary. Failed forwarding yields no acknowledgement so the existing client no-ack retry applies.

For deletion, the adopted retention decision keeps Transit keys and the export artifact for a 30-day window, then an operator destroys the keys. The artifact must contain every ciphertext/key reference before secret/audit rows are removed. The decision is in the promotion record; implementation and destroy/after-window refusal evidence remain separate.

docs.title: Current bounded proof and remaining admission
docs.text:
R73 accepts the functional M5 reference on one host and records its final comprehensive verification. These synthetic native records retain their declared executed heads; runnable RECORDED-EVIDENCE gates replay archived physical observations, not a fresh current-HEAD campaign. The later accepted ed2 reference is published on draft PR #8898; its publication and alignment CI record is distinct from dev merge, release and production/default admission.

Recorded proof Boundary and remaining work M5 PostgreSQL Current-state/evaluator recovery, restricted-role durable alarm/request state and controlled consumer handoff. Actual roles/browser have their separate home below. M5 reference roles/browser Separate API/realtime/evaluator roles on one host using scheduled snapshot polling, typed write compatibility, current recipient/configuration authority, alarm controls and a controlled same-origin browser. Server handoff, recipient event and browser presentation are separate observations; no evaluator-to-device journey, LISTEN handshake, notification-transport latency or live provider delivery is established. M6 SQL operations Populated catalogue/artifact fidelity, supported upgrade/rollback, interruption and deletion ceremony under fixture quiescence. This earlier whole-deployment restore proof does not establish tenant-local restore; later evidence is listed separately below. Whole-deployment rollback includes other tenants. Native tenant-local restore and restart c23 fixed-cohort separate-role controller proof: restore with forward history, rollback/uncertainty refusal, B continuity and fresh shared-role restart while A remains suspended. Direct SQL writers and multi-host coordination remain outside this cooperative protocol. Packaged Compose and clients ed2 exact image/cold UI/main+alarm sockets, tenant-local restore/client convergence, actual pinned clients and full nonbrowser acceptance. Browser/native c23 and enabled corpus39f4 retain their own attribution. This answers feasibility and bounded compatibility questions; capacity, HA and production admission remain open.

| M6a joined candidate | Owner/OIDC, the disposable-harness OIDC matrix and the internal service contracts joined to #8898. Real identity-provider interoperability is synthetic only. | | M6b joined candidate | Listener composition, key retention, operator-assisted ownership and single-site OIDC provisioning on one frozen head. Ownership in a serving role, real role processes over Compose and the production key custodian remain open. | | Vault Agent sidecar, connector sync | M6c Vault connectivity and the M6d outbound connector lab. Identity-provider profile, live trust probes and the remaining connector scope are open queue items. |

Publication state, CI and the open boundaries of each candidate are in the release contents; the dashboard lists the M6a–M6d and M7 items with their claimed state. Measured operating budgets are M7 work. The current decision index separates human choices from implementation and measurement work.

docs.title: M5/M6 acceptance families
docs.text:
These refine the milestone cells above into observable results. They are required coverage, not new passing measurements. The coordinator records actual source, command, control, artifact and verdict per family on the assembled candidate. A deferred enhancement is named explicitly; it does not silently lower another bar.

Family Required observable result M5 current-state recovery Bounded full typed identity/absence reconciliation in one consistent tenant snapshot recovers hard deletes and unstamped activity after missed wakes/restart and at an unchanged floor. Preserve producer timestamps and replies. Concurrent paging cannot combine snapshots; foreign tenant state is unchanged. Row/byte/transaction failure refuses without partial projection/checkpoint replacement. M5 evaluator recovery The actual evaluator consumes recovered inputs. Acquisition or commit failure preserves last good state; downstream clinical failure may leave newer committed inputs while retaining the prior clinical result/time. A later cycle retries computation even at an unchanged floor. Settings/plugin-version changes cannot reuse an incompatible result. Do not claim atomic input-plus-clinical-output persistence. M5 live reference Separate roles on one machine exercise subscription startup races, missed/duplicate wakes, process death/restart and explicit scheduling. Time-only alarm ticks and current-state reconciliation are distinct work. A transport wake is not delivery evidence; a checkpoint lock is not a multi-node lease. M5 socket compatibility and authority Actual D23 API forwarding preserves namespace, source, replies and ack/no-ack retry behavior; realtime has no storage-write authority. Current authorization covers operations, reconnect and protected delivery. Tenant rooms/caches and settings invalidation remain isolated. M5 durable alarm state Apply the adopted tenant-wide group/level suppression contract: API-persisted state and original expiry survive restart, active-window repeats do not extend suppression, and existing default/level effects remain. No indefinite post-expiry deduplication is inferred from the unchanged client protocol. Exercise persistence failure and restart boundaries against actual client behavior. Live external notification delivery remains a separate gate; enabled durable request handoff needs its own crash/retry oracle. M5 durable notification handoff Apply the durable request/retry decision: tenant-bound intent persisted before dispatch, stable identity across restart/ambiguous retry, no new ordinary/alarm request from a failed clinical cycle. Independently committed authorized ACK/snooze controls may produce a control-clear. Verify joined notification consumers for ordinary alarm, snooze/repeat window, restart, ambiguous acceptance, foreign authority/configuration and shutdown. Preserve normal dedup/suppression and single behavior. Distinguish possible duplicate external effects from duplicate clinical records; uploader compatibility is not notification acceptance. Live provider/device delivery remains separate. M6 bounded owner API Implement the adopted first-preview catalogue and refusals: projected display settings, bounded owner thresholds, single-tenant-equivalent credentials (wildcards accepted as single tenant does) under the ceiling, no owner integrations. Shared optional OIDC/provider-backed renewal provides equivalent single/multitenant human authentication with separate authority adapters; single opt-in prefers ENABLE=oidc. Human issuer/renewal implements adopted lifetimes, current authority, reauthentication and cross-worker revocation through synthetic identities. Enabled/disabled parity and legacy-client controls are required. Apply the adopted session contracts: management-only idle scope, local-first logout, fenced renewal, cookie-default dual transport; outage behavior follows the provider-outage row. Operator-provisioned credentials alone do not close human identity. M6 operator-assisted ownership Private-operator addition/transfer/recovery is tenant-bound, explicit and audited. Concurrent changes cannot orphan a tenant or silently replace an owner; unauthorized operations have no effect. Recovery grants no automatic secret reveal. Self-service co-owner/transfer is not a preview gate. M6 lifecycle and trust Provision/suspend/export/delete and restore respect current authority and trusted tenant resolution. Artifact fidelity is independently checked; capture required ciphertext/key references before deletion. Exercise retained-key recovery, operator destruction and after-window refusal. Same-ID restore and new-secret cloning remain distinct. Apply the adopted request/operator-confirmation/cancellation/no-wait policy. Verify confirmation bound to tenant/request/artifact; committed cancellation prevents execution, and cancellation/execution cannot both win. Refused or interrupted execution cannot leave partial deletion. M6 operations and clients Populated backup/restore and upgrade/rollback cover interruption, supported schema/catalogue and failure recovery on the assembled tree. Retain the Android emulator acceptance and the explicit iOS/all-client exclusions. A representative entries/clock lab does not cover the whole catalogue. M6 operating envelope and final review Declare synthetic workload and freshness/recovery expectations, then measure shared-pool/hot-tenant interference, row/byte limits, scan cadence, latency and egress refusal before approving bounds. Complete the final criterion matrix and review. Functional passes do not establish capacity.

The accepted M5 reference does not select a live external notification provider or promise retained every-transition history; the first-preview channel decision admits no push provider and makes Nightscout-to-Nightscout synchronization the first external channel. Multi-node failover, every-transition history and self-service ownership are separate enhancements. Real identities/data, production/default role enablement and release admission keep their existing explicit approval boundaries.

docs.title: Compatibility and parallel contracts
docs.text:
Direct comparison Purpose Released single/Mongo vs current dev Explain intentional RC corrections, defined edge cases and preserved client quirks through release decisions/register Current dev vs PR single/Mongo Detect shared seam/composition regressions independently of PG differences PR single/Mongo vs PR multitenant/PG Exercise admitted routes, stored outcomes, identity, isolation and current authority directly Pinned client workflow vs each applicable endpoint Exercise ordinary handshake/read/write/retry/refusal, defaults, ordering, batch and delete/history behavior

Every case identifies its client/source pin, endpoint/settings, expected observable behavior, allowed incidental normalization and intended-change basis. Compare logical contents, status/headers, identity, per-item replies and history; retain omitted/null/zero/false and failure-category distinctions. Classify unchanged, intended RC correction, preserved quirk, explicit unsupported capability, unexpected regression or unmeasured. An unclassified difference fails. A broad allowlist or a transitive old-release-to-PG inference is not acceptance. Index-off duplicate fixtures and index-on/race campaigns retain separate scope.

Registration/instance identity, typed commands and delegation contracts may advance independently. Their runtime admission still needs tenant storage, authorized owner/action routing, registered destinations where required, durable state, idempotency/reconciliation and reviewed human/delegated authority. Device tokens do not implicitly grant command authority. These tracks and optional OIDC research are not blanket prerequisites to the initial storage/HTTP lab or v1/v3 compatibility. The hub observes/routes; the AID controller owns dosing decisions/reconciliation.

docs.title: Retained execution evidence
docs.text: The archived delivery journal retains the original dispatches, acceptance commands, failed experiments, controls, capacity holds and source-scoped checkpoints. It describes its captured period, not today's assignment or acceptance. Its unique evidence remains retrievable; future measurements belong in the integration/release records, and current coordination belongs in the dashboard and completion schedule.

docs.title: Multitenant integration batching plan
docs.text:
Record

Record as of 2026-11-06. A point-in-time document; it is not kept up to date.

Contributor-facing living coordination plan, refreshed 2026-11-10. This page owns capability boundaries, integration order and verification depth. The queue owns claimed item state; the dashboard owns recorded milestone claims; release contents and the integration record own actual source, acceptance and publication. The retained batching journal preserves the original dispatch and all captured evidence.

docs.title: Completion-focused coordination
docs.text:
Maintainer direction, 2026-11-06: organize lanes around complete capabilities and adopted milestone criteria. A helper, fixture repair or individual control belongs to its capability lane; an independently deliverable capability or material architectural unknown may have a separate owner.

  • Give each lane one observable deliverable, owner, exit criterion, focused positive/negative checks, unresolved decisions and next integration boundary. Confirm the head commit and that the task remains open before starting. Stop and report a mismatch rather than reaching for the nearest thing that works.
  • Run changed-code lint and affected/focused checks during implementation. Keep meaningful controls for isolation, authorization, clinical behavior and compatibility, followed by restoration. A setup failure is not a semantic red.
  • Resolve architectural unknowns with bounded early proofs whose question and stop condition are explicit. Incorporate their result into the capability; a proof does not become a separate comprehensive campaign.
  • Freeze the coherent joined candidate for one full nonbrowser, default-browser, enabled-corpus and applicable native/client campaign, then final prcheck. Preserve failed campaigns, diagnose narrowly, join planned repairs and repeat final acceptance when material inputs changed. A leaf commit, resumption or documentation update does not trigger a new comprehensive campaign.
  • Reuse evidence only with exact source/instrument attribution and an explicit affected-input analysis. Ancestry establishes incorporation, not execution. Source-identical evidence retains its original executed head and limits.
  • Maintain one evolving lane handoff and one programme acceptance update per coherent batch. Record substantive failures, decisions and ownership transfers promptly. Report capability/criterion closure, remaining blockers and the next integration owner with the evidence link; counts are supporting observations.

docs.title: 1. Evidence and ownership
docs.text:
Use the current acceptance bundle for the published restore/Compose candidate, and the M5/M6 decision index for adopted policy and open implementation/measurement work. A dated journal or local handoff does not assign new work. Confirm active ownership with the programme coordinator before claiming an existing lane; the release record links the evolving local handoffs.

The source owner integrates original committed lane histories by fast-forward or ordinary merge. Check ancestry and patch equivalence first; resolve overlap explicitly. Do not cherry-pick/rebase patches and later merge their original history solely to make evidence commits reachable. Continue the existing draft #8898; the adopted integration direction does not authorize a cleanup rewrite or replacement PR.

The original measured basis retains the older PR/CI snapshots. They are historical observations, not the current publication state.

docs.title: 2. Acceptance ladder
docs.text:
Stage Required evidence Record owner Locally accepted Focused capability checks and meaningful red/restored controls on the lane's actual head Capability owner, in the lane handoff Incorporated Original lane history is an ancestor of the joined candidate; overlap and affected checks resolved Source integration owner Integrated acceptance recorded Coherent frozen candidate passes its applicable regression/native/client campaign and final prcheck Acceptance coordinator, with exact source and instrument attribution Milestone promoted Every adopted milestone criterion has an explicit verdict; deferrals have an adopted basis Maintainer decision, reflected in dashboard/status sources

Implementation, functional preview acceptance, publication, merge to dev, operator release and production/default enablement are separate claims. A promoted component or milestone supplies evidence for decisions within its tested scope; it does not establish capacity, high availability or a new deployment.

docs.title: 3. Batch rules
docs.text:
1. Keep default single/Mongo regression and explicit multitenant corpus coverage. Reconcile the enabled-suite inventory with source before each freeze; publish named pending/unsupported cases. A pending benchmark is not a functional pass.
  2. Changes to existing shipping paths, migrations, dependencies, tier registry or shared fixtures are assessed on the coherent joined candidate. Material changes invalidate the affected final acceptance; they do not require a full campaign for every intermediate commit.
  3. Run focused jobs only with positive ownership of schemas, ports, processes and containers. Local comprehensive campaigns share the coordinator's serialized runtime slot. Parallel native jobs need measured capacity and isolation; unknown resources remain untouched. Quiet performance work gets a separate controlled window.
  4. Use the complete opt-in corpus command for corpus acceptance; an archived gate or a filtered focused suite cannot establish whole-corpus acceptance. CI and local campaigns keep their actual source/environment attribution.
  5. Gates read; they never mutate another session's checkout. Update queue refs only after the applicable measured acceptance, retaining native evidence pins. Without a required database/runtime, report UNMEASURED, not green.
  6. Every capability brief includes source head, outcome, integration boundary, focused tests, meaningful controls and remaining decision boundaries, plus the standing confirm-head/open-task and stop-on-mismatch instructions above.
  7. Publication remains a separately authorized action. This plan supplies no authority to publish application source, enable defaults or admit real data.

docs.title: 4. Retained dispatch
docs.text: The B1–B7 dispatch preserves original branch identities, commands, predictions, failures, controls and ownership. Those completed/older lanes are evidence inputs, not today's task list. The schedule below governs further work.

docs.title: 5. Current completion schedule (adopted 2026-11-06)
docs.text: Completion stage Accepted capability and evidence Remaining integration boundary A — data, control and clients (M0–M4) R72 retains M0 and promotes M1/M2, then M3/M4, at the adopted bounded scope. The later pinned-client campaign belongs to its own source/instrument. Preserve legacy root/subject behavior and supported PG differences. Android emulator and measured operating limits remain C; no all-client claim. A's closed criteria are not new prerequisites to re-run for the documentation refresh. B — durable runtime (M5) R73 accepts the functional separate-role reference on one host: current-state/evaluator recovery, current socket authority, durable suppression/request handoff and reference consumers. Keep the accepted reference distinct from live external delivery, retained every-transition history, multi-node ownership and capacity. Changes to a consumed runtime contract need affected checks and coherent joined acceptance. C — synthetic operational preview (M6, now M6a–M6d) Operation-window acceptance records separate-process tenant-local restore, ordinary forward history/client convergence and B continuity, plus cold Compose/UI/restore acceptance. Earlier SQL backup/upgrade/deletion evidence retains its captured scope. Split on 2026-11-09 into the capability items below. Accepted one-host recovery is not multi-host/HA admission. M6a — identity and owner API MT-M6A-JOIN acceptance on the joined candidate, including the internal service contracts and the disposable-harness OIDC matrix. Real identity-provider interoperability is synthetic only. Publication and CI state: the release contents and the queue item. M6b — lifecycle, keys and the joined candidate MT-M6B-JOIN acceptance joins listener composition, key retention, ownership operations and single-site OIDC provisioning. Ownership in a serving role and its deploy grants, real role processes over Compose and the production key custodian remain open; the release contents carry the full list. M6c — deployment trust (in nightscout-deploy) Vault Agent sidecar and the core tokenFile read. Identity-provider profile and live trust probes (DEPLOY-IDP-PROFILE, DEPLOY-TRUST-PROBES). Bench, contrast, scale-unbound, evaluator partition, realtime sharding, Android lab and Kubernetes binding items in the queue.

docs.title: 2026-11-09: M6 split and capability items
docs.text: Stage C above is now four milestones and a production milestone, M6a–M6d and M7 (roadmap, decision). Each has one to four queue items with one gate each; the dashboard lists them with their claimed state. Native acceptance runs through a disposable harness; no lead reservation or grant is required.

docs.title: Criterion matrix for the next frozen candidate
docs.text:
The coordinator records actual source, instrument, command/selector, artifact, control and verdict for each applicable roadmap acceptance family. Name the carried evidence, changed input and why reuse is valid for each retained criterion. Record explicit deferrals before milestone promotion. A count, a waiver inferred from a prototype, or an incorporated source change cannot replace that matrix.

For production-quality deployment, keep four questions separate: whether the component behaves correctly under tested faults; whether its chosen deployment preserves those assumptions; whether its measured workload meets approved bounds; and whether it is admitted for release/operation. The deployment guide explains topologies and fault domains. Remaining measurement work continues under adopted policy; a deferred policy question retains its prototypes and benches.

The production dependency map continues beyond C through actual deployment qualification and release/admission. It proposes sequencing and closing evidence, without assigning new lanes or changing the adopted milestone bars.

docs.title: 6. Lane ownership and coordination
docs.text:
The programme coordinator owns criterion closure, source freeze, queue/status integration. Each capability has one source owner and one next integration boundary. Native acceptance runs in a disposable harness that records the source head, requires a clean tree and removes its containers (decision); the earlier grant/reservation ceremony is retired.

Local evolving handoffs remain under externals/work/HANDOFF-<lane>-<date>.md. The latest release update points to current combined ownership; the archived lane roster retains earlier responsibilities and traps. Never take an old “active” label as a present assignment. Preserve peer drafts and existing worktrees; inspect the shared index and commit only owned paths.

docs.title: 7. Scope and retention
docs.text: This plan changes no adopted milestone bar, release placement, backend default, provider selection or operator admission. The full captured predecessor at alignment 8792fc7a3d62f59629ed94bac168dcad5d9aa3c7 is retained in the batching journal, including its unique measurements, failed predictions and historical assignments. Git retains intermediate revisions. Correct coordination here, decisions in their canonical home and new acceptance in release/integration records; do not append execution journals to the current schedule.

docs.title: Multitenant REST v1–v3: design and parallel implementation plan
docs.text:
Record

Record as of 2026-11-04. A point-in-time document; it is not kept up to date.

Current-use guide, 2026-11-06: Use the dashboard for acceptance and the batching plan §5 for current sequencing. This page retains the route/domain design and original implementation packets; its original heads and next steps describe that dispatch.

2026-11-04 · Contributor-facing proposal · implementation delivery, not REST readiness.

Deliver one runnable API listener with tenant-safe versions of the actual v1, v2 and v3 surfaces below. Implement by collection/domain across versions, reusing shipping handlers, query construction and write rules. Do not build three new APIs or wait for a universal framework, production registry, owner lifecycle or a chain of administrative packets.

Current delivery status lives in the dashboard and release acceptance record. The November 5 priority packets and compatibility matrix sequence current administration, wider REST and parallel historical/current compatibility execution. Their expected-change rules preserve intended RC fixes and measured client quirks; the historical source inventory is not current admission. The source inventory and initial package assignments below retain their captured baseline; already accepted domain implementations must not be rebuilt from those historical missing/pending labels. The continuation lanes carry derived reads, pinned-pattern replay and independent authority review.

docs.title: 1. Basis and boundaries
docs.text:
All source findings in this document are read-derived from cgm-remote-monitor c527fb7e0d309b7fc567861a41e8f3862e0922df. Every lib/, tests/, scripts/ and migrations/ citation below refers to that CRM tree, not the alignment repository. Line numbers are pinned to it; inspect with git show c527fb7e:<path> | nl -ba. Swagger is not the route inventory. No application tests were executed for this design; proposed parity, throughput, client compatibility and completeness are UNMEASURED.

Anchors verified before writing:

tree/reference observed anchor accepted cumulative CRM / PR #8898 c527fb7e0d309b7fc567861a41e8f3862e0922df; PR OPEN, draft CRM official/dev 4a482627bfdafb1fef8dcbe0ac6c484811cae563 alignment main 4714b1a7409403c91ec2c0f812cd0a21611491f6 this plan's alignment base 3982d589a2d28da4bf831f1182e93858e7eb4c59

The release decisions authorize a bounded runnable preview and entries CRUD in parallel. They do not authorize an all-REST capability claim. Candidate 16.0.0 release acceptance is a separate process. The delivery roadmap, execution plan, storage seam and write contract supply prior art. Historical census figures in those documents are not a current count or a reason to redo work already in source.

Accepted bounded composition: actual API3 entries GET/search and POST through injected storage/current authority, compatible v2 credential exchange, and the canonical resolver seam. This statement identifies the accepted lane boundary, not a new verification run. lib/server/tenant-app/data-access.js:26–38 admits only entries GET/list/address and POST/list; history is deliberately reserved. Its v3 bridge rejects legacy query/body credential carriers. lib/server/tenant-app/index.js:137–168 mounts exchange and a protected v3 data router, not the complete single application. An API3 Collection constructor or a storage primitive does not establish admission for its other routes.

Active implementation, delivery pending: the entries CRUD lane owns API3 mutation/history handler intent seams, entries tenant bridge/admission, required storage primitives and tests; the runnable CLI lane owns nightscout multitenant api, strict operator preview configuration, PG/Vault/current-authority boot, read-only readiness, owned shutdown and child-process tests. Do not duplicate these changes or infer their acceptance from their briefs. Subsequent code starts from their clean, integrated, accepted head when it needs their seams. Neither lane waits for this plan.

docs.title: Reading the matrix
docs.text:
Paths are relative to /api/v1 or /api/v2 in the legacy table and /api/v3 in the v3 table. Every v1 row is also mounted in v2, because lib/api2/index.js:14 mounts the entire v1 application before its extras. A regex app.all dispatch is not an implemented business method: only the child registrations below count. Express supplies implicit HEAD for GET and automatic OPTIONS; include these in HTTP regression checks rather than inventing PUT/PATCH routes. Trailing-slash and case behavior follow the shipping Express configuration. The common legacy suffix set is json/svg/csv/txt/png/html/tsv; status additionally recognizes js through its own middleware. A recognized suffix does not guarantee every handler renders that format: retain its negotiated refusal/redirect as well as export successes. API3 has a different suffix-to-MIME parser and JSON/CSV/XML renderer (lib/api3/shared/renderer.js:65–107).

Readiness: A accepted bounded seam; P active implementation pending; M missing tenant implementation; X deliberately excluded from the initial runnable preview, still accounted for in the full-surface goal. X is not completion. Owners are future packages in §5.

Dependency shorthand: S tenant-scoped collection storage; Q existing query/filter/ projection/sort/count dialect; W existing write-intent and per-route validation/replies; E tenant-scoped history, bus and cache invalidation; R derived runtime snapshot; C tenant-safe settings/environment view; I current identity/authority; N notification/connector side effects. These are requirements, not available capabilities.
