If the target fails to warm, do not publish it as ready. With partial/stale route publication, keep backend owner admission authoritative and expose routing generation disagreement; affected requests may refuse rather than silently falling back. Recovery or rollback is a fresh admitted generation/move with old-owner exclusion re-established. Never republish an old incarnation/map or restore old checkpoint data to make rollback appear successful. Preserve accepted and uncertain outbox outcomes. Until a valid target is ready, the affected shard can remain unavailable while unrelated shards continue.

If old-owner exclusion cannot be established, keep the affected shard unavailable. Automatic partition failover is a later option requiring an effective platform fence/defined bounded-overlap contract and its own adversarial proof. A database epoch check or private network address alone cannot retract an already buffered socket emission. Do not promise instantaneous exclusive delivery from a lease.

Failure Required outcome Worker crash with confirmed termination Route affected tenants through admitted replacement; reconnect, current authorization and full snapshot. Other owners continue. Old owner unreachable but possibly alive No speculative active replacement in this first scope; report unavailable/uncertain ownership. Wrong/stale consumer or alarm route Refuse before protected effects when assignment can be established; otherwise retain uncertainty. Never forward to an arbitrary URL. PostgreSQL/API dependency failure Preserve existing current-state/authority refusal; do not mark old frames fresh or invent write/notification success. Worker or hot tenant overload Bound connections/work/queues and expose pressure; do not silently route to a non-owner or allow one tenant to starve unrelated owners.

docs.title: Alarm acceptance and reconnect semantics
docs.text:
Current alarm acceptance means handoff to realtime fanout, not durable storage of an event for every device. Default Socket.IO delivery does not replay events a disconnected client missed. A reconnected current-state snapshot is not proof of alarm-event replay. See Socket.IO delivery guarantees.

Preserve existing durable pending/uncertain attempt recovery. A changed owner address alone must not change clinical config identity, retire/mint an equivalent notification, or make an already accepted request pending again. A late old-owner success response still belongs to its original attempt; do not reinterpret it as a fresh new-owner attempt. A lost response remains ambiguous. Current generic transport errors do not prove pre-effect refusal, so routing changes cannot justify an immediate transparent retry. Re-resolution for the next permitted durable attempt retains its logical request/attempt semantics.

Explicitly choose and test the product's future delivery guarantee before claiming no missed alarms across moves. Durable per-client offsets/event replay would be additional protocol/state work, not a property supplied by sharding or successful handoff. Do not fabricate device receipts, replay historical alerts blindly or replay uncertain clinical mutations. Existing supported-client behavior and operator-visible gaps must be evaluated in acceptance.

docs.title: Maintenance coverage must change with sharding
docs.text:
Current cohort code assumes each role/participant covers the same tenant set. API can continue covering every tenant while realtime workers cover subsets; this requires a real cohort/manifest contract change, not merely a route table.

For tenant maintenance, enumerate every actual actor that may hold work/state for that tenant, including old/draining owners during a move. Validate complete assignment/role coverage against the admitted generation, retain actual datastore and backend census, pin incarnations and await all required invalidations. Self-reported subset membership is not proof of completeness. Shared processes may host different role coverages; account for each actual role and backend.

A pinned attempt freezes the relevant placement revision or refuses observed change. New owner admission cannot bypass invalidation, and old actors cannot vanish because they are unready or absent from service routing. A fresh attempt follows the existing uncertainty/suspension and cleanup rules.

docs.title: Capacity and the hot-tenant limit
docs.text:
Tenant sharding spreads tenants, not every tenant's viewers. Measure connection count, serialization/bytes, refresh/checkpoint costs, per-recipient authority calls, event-loop lag, dependency pools, reconnect bursts and per-tenant interference. A busy shard can move to a larger/dedicated worker; that still leaves a single tenant's delivery bounded by one worker. More CPU cores alone do not parallelize one JavaScript event loop.

If one tenant exceeds a suitably sized worker, qualify connection-sharded fanout as a second capability: multiple connection owners for that tenant, maintained Socket.IO adapter/distribution, per-recipient current authority and defined projection ownership. Do not introduce a mandatory broker before that workload requires it, or assume an adapter replaces the current local-client delivery loop. Polling affinity remains required for the supported fallback transports; see multiple-node guidance.

The private operational API reports intended versus observed assignments, incarnation/generation, active/draining/ready state, connection and tenant counts, checkpoint/refresh progress, handoff outcomes, pressure and dependency health. Bounded inspection must work during refusal and must not acquire ownership.

docs.title: Implementation and acceptance
docs.text:
One MT-REALTIME-SHARDING owner keeps assignment, routing adapters, parser/runtime, checkpoint migration, cohort coverage, fixtures and controls together. Prototype with the incorporated private API foundation; consume shared listener/operational composition when it is integrated. Deployment-companion changes render routing and worker placement. No Kubernetes installation or new scheduler is required for the native fixed-roster proof.

Criterion Positive experiment Intended semantic red control Single-worker compatibility Same clients, frames, polling/upgrades, namespaces, credentials and ACK/write behavior with one worker owning all shards. Change a reply or skip current authorization; independent client/store assertions fail. Multi-owner coverage Two real owners, synthetic tenants across both and a trusted edge; verify every connection and notification reaches the assigned owner. Independent edge/alarm map mismatch or non-owner admission causes missing/foreign delivery assertion failure. Stable logical assignment Add a worker without changing logical shard count; only explicitly moved shards change owner. Derive bucket count from process count and observe unexpected tenant/session churn. Checkpoint continuity Kill/move an owner, inspect physical checkpoint/digest and reconstruct current state on the target. Reset consumer/checkpoint or admit overlapping checkpoint writers; continuity/ownership assertions fail. Polling and namespace affinity Repeated polling, upgrades and main/storage/alarm sessions stay on the admitted incarnation; move requires fresh sessions. Route an existing session ID to another incarnation; compatibility assertion fails. Controlled drain and partition refusal Hold a response during a move; establish old-owner termination/fence before target admission. Exercise an unknown-alive partition. Activate solely on a route/lease change; observe old/new protected output or premature activation. Partial cutover and rollback Fail target warmup or route publication between stages; recover through a fresh admitted generation without rolling back durable outcomes. Reactivate an old incarnation/map, reset checkpoints or fabricate readiness; ownership/continuity assertions fail. Empty and suspended assignments Start an idle worker, activate an admitted assignment, and suspend its only tenant while another owner progresses. Fabricate a tenant/job, route to an unready owner or globally block unrelated work; readiness/progress assertions fail. Notification ambiguity Hold/drop and deliver late old-owner responses; inspect original durable request/attempt and independent delivered outcomes. Reset accepted state, change logical identity on move or synthesize success; duplicate/false-outcome assertion fails. Cohort coverage API full coverage plus realtime subsets and a draining owner; restore A while B continues. Omit a former owner or accept only a sampled service endpoint/self-report; complete census/invalidation assertion fails. Isolation and progress Suspension, dependency outage, reconnect pressure and hot shard do not expose another tenant or starve unrelated owner progress. Broad readiness deferral or unbounded scheduling makes B's progress/freshness oracle fail. Composition choice Run the selected colocated/separate-role profile with independent clinical and viewer load. Block delivery/event loop or duplicate assignment; scheduler-lag/ownership bounds fail.

All experiments and limits are UNMEASURED. Choose finite workload/budget inputs, retain failed predictions and inspect independent durable/output outcomes. Join a coherent candidate before applicable full/browser/enabled-corpus/native/client acceptance and final prcheck. MT-SCALE-UNBOUND consumes this capability for horizontal realtime measurements; it does not substitute for its correctness gates.

docs.title: Runtime topology: zones, components and private APIs
docs.text:
Living document, last changed 2026-11-12 at 3cbf37c82.

Living contributor-facing architecture guide, reconciled 2026-11-12. Structure is read-derived; measured acceptance retains its exact source in the linked records. This Markdown generates the site's runtime-topology.html. The endpoint/API work plan owns remaining implementation and acceptance criteria; the queue owns claimed work state. A diagram is not deployment or capacity acceptance.

docs.title: Reuse the components across profiles
docs.text:
A deployment profile selects where the same roles run and how they share work. Configuration can select a supported capability. It cannot supply missing ownership, migration or recovery behavior.

flowchart TB
  R["Reusable roles: API, evaluator, realtime, admin and change feed"]
  R --> S["Small group<br/>Roles can share a host"]
  R --> O["Operator deployment<br/>Scale roles separately"]
  R -.-> F["Proposed fleet<br/>Several bounded deployment groups"]
  S --> C["Same authority, write, ownership and recovery contracts"]
  O --> C
  F -.-> C

The arrows show composition choices, not an upgrade sequence or a capacity claim. Fleet placement and tenant moves need separate design and qualification. The scale envelopes define the evidence needed for each profile. The deployment guide distinguishes experimental rigs from operating recipes.

Term Meaning here Role A responsibility, such as serving API requests or evaluating tenant data. Replica Another instance of a role. It needs a valid work-assignment rule. Cohort The declared processes that cooperate on a workload and its maintenance. Instance / incarnation An actual process / one lifetime of that process. A replacement has a new incarnation. Shard / partition A selected share of tenant work. The role's assignment rule determines its owner. Cell A proposed bounded deployment, datastore and recovery unit. Several cells could form a fleet. Admission / fencing Checks that permit work / controls that prevent an old or invalid actor from continuing it. Hint / checkpoint A signal to inspect authoritative state / a position or revision in a named input stream or snapshot. Its contract states what completion it proves.

docs.title: Component inventory and operator-topic readiness
docs.text:
The component boundaries are clear enough to organize operator reference topics. They do not imply separate binaries, containers or production qualification. The inventory below groups existing responsibilities; release records own their current acceptance. Role launch details remain in the application source.

Read-derived source check, 2026-11-12: cgm-remote-monitor ff5156b984424f1ef34bcef22d5bfa0071354cfa, lib/server/serve/roles.js, lib/cli/index.js and lib/cli/commands/multitenant.js. The role registry declares API, evaluator, realtime, vcpool, tenant-admin, admin and feed-reader. UI, maintenance jobs and backing services have different entry points.

Component or responsibility Boundary and state ownership Natural reference topic API REST version adapters and canonical clinical writes; current client authority. Each instance has pools, caches and in-flight requests. Request service, authority, pool limits, replica routing and drain. Evaluator Tenant acquisition and clinical/plugin computation; input checkpoints, eligible output and notification production have separate completion meanings. Assignment, scheduling, freshness, output eligibility and recovery. Realtime Client connections, subscriptions and record fanout; forwards authorized writes to API. Owns its projection and connection state. Socket service, authority checks, tenant placement and reconnect/recovery. vcpool Tenant connector actors. Reads scoped configuration and sends tenant-bound writes through the API. Connector membership, credentials, outbound limits and retries. Tenant-admin Tenant owner management with a separate credential audience; distinct from clinical DATA and operator ownership control. Owner settings, delegation and management listener. Admin Private operator ownership, pool and provisioning operations with scoped backing identities. It is not a lifecycle participant. Operator control, provisioning, credentials and refused operations. UI Page and asset delivery in the selected deployment binding. It is not a role in the inspected CLI registry. Browser endpoint, routing and asset configuration. Maintenance jobs/controller Explicit migration and restore operations; exact participant roster, incarnation and operation claims. Migration, backup/restore, fencing, uncertain outcomes and recovery. Feed-reader Dedicated metadata slot reader that emits change hints. It runs alone, outside tenant-operation cohorts. Reader ownership, slot retention, hint transport and recovery. Projections and durable delivery Library/protocol responsibilities used by workers; input positions and effect completion have separate contracts. Replay, checkpoints, retained work and delivery guarantees. Edge and backing dependencies Deployment-selected ingress, PostgreSQL, Vault and optional identity/monitoring services. Their availability and custody affect the whole deployment. Binding, credentials, retained data, resource budgets and dependency recovery.

Use the communication guide for output and checkpoint ownership. Use the deployment guide for resource bindings and the production path for operational closure. Proposed cell/fleet control remains a design topic; it is not another implemented service in this inventory.

A component passes the operator-topic maturity test when a reader can identify its purpose, inputs, outputs, authority, retained state and owner. The same topic must explain configuration, startup refusal, readiness, shutdown, failure recovery, compatibility and operating limits. Follow existing contract and evidence links for each answer; mark missing answers as unmeasured or proposed. These are review questions for the existing design, not another status checklist.

The inspected CLI already selects multitenant roles and provides migration, healthcheck, environment, diagnostic and operator-client commands. Its top-level multitenant summary still names only API and tenant-admin, while the registry supports more roles. The admin summary advertises provisioning but omits its removal verb. These are discoverability gaps, not evidence of missing implementations. The admin client and admin server role have different responsibilities. A healthcheck response also does not prove tenant progress or completed evaluation. Role-specific reference material is still spread across source documents and guides. Measured resource limits, remote placement and recovery qualification also remain source/profile-specific. The architecture is ready for coherent topics; a complete production operations manual would need those answers joined for a selected profile. No new command, help option or man page is required for this documentation work.

docs.title: Read the diagrams
docs.text:
The three plates preserve different architectural scopes: the historical accepted deployment, the November private-listener composition, and a fixed-roster scale placement example. Their captured heads and publication labels belong to those plates; use release contents for current implementation and acceptance. Read downward through client ingress, edge, service destinations, actual role processes and backing resources. Components sit on a grid; named terminals and a communication ledger replace long crossing connectors.

A trust zone is not a host or Pod. A logical API contract, bound listener and deployable process are separate boundaries. Ordinary service destinations and the exact instance endpoints needed for maintenance are also different identities.

docs.title: Historical accepted one-host reference
docs.text:
PNG preview · SVG source

The ed2 cold Compose record measures synthetic UI/socket/ordinary restore; the c23 native matrix retains its separate-role restore and restart scope. The reference publishes lab HTTP and uses TLS for Vault. Those captured runs are not relabelled as new-head, OIDC, network transport, scaling or production measurements.

docs.title: Private API composition: one internal listener per role
docs.text:
PNG preview · SVG source

The plate illustrates the adopted listener composition. In this composition, each process that serves private contracts has one private listener. Explicit contract modules select its operations. The listener evidence and shared-transport acceptance retain their executed heads and controls. Their source-scoped passes do not qualify every network, topology or later candidate. Current integration/publication belongs in release contents, not in a second chronological account here.

Both application and lifecycle operations are private APIs. The labels name purpose, not different networks or mandatory sockets:

Dimension Meaning Audience Consumer DATA, owner management, or private component/operator access. A backend-only owner port still has a different contract from lifecycle control. Contract family Application authority/mutations, notification delivery, lifecycle status/invalidation; operational health/readiness/metrics can be another family. Binding HTTP over UDS or an explicitly selected TCP/HTTP origin, with a separately configurable bind address. The deployment chooses reachability and access policy. Instance addressing Ordinary calls may target a service destination; maintenance must reach every actual participant and pin its incarnation.

Each process that serves private contracts opens one serve.internal. API serves socket-authority and lifecycle-participant; realtime serves alarm-delivery and lifecycle-participant; evaluator and tenant-admin serve lifecycle-participant. A process with no contract (UI) opens none. The default is a unix socket under the runtime directory; host/port is set explicitly by environment. On shutdown the listener finishes in-flight calls up to a deadline (graceful shutdown). The admin role serves ownership operations on its operator listener (ADMIN_HOSTNAME/ADMIN_PORT). It uses the ownership_operator database identity. It is not a lifecycle participant (restore census, same address, different port). Evaluator's in-process health() result is not a remote metrics endpoint.

The private arrows show specific calls. evaluator → realtime delivers notifications. realtime → API checks current permissions and forwards authorized writes and acknowledgements. Realtime owns Socket.IO semantics, subscriptions and fanout. It also checks recipients' current permissions during delivery. That synchronous authority dependency is read-derived; its latency, load and failure effects need measurement.

docs.title: Fixed-roster API-scale placement example
docs.text:
PNG preview · SVG source

Bind public, management and private interfaces separately. Each process that serves private contracts has one serve.internal listener under the adopted decision. The role's code selects its contract modules. Configuration selects a socket or host/port; it cannot move or merge contracts. The default is a Unix socket. On SIGTERM, the listener drains in-flight calls up to a deadline. Operational inspection is another explicit private contract; its existence does not imply a public metrics endpoint or complete production monitoring.

The plate shows equivalent REST replicas behind a service destination, with directly addressable private instance endpoints for maintenance. Implementation and bounded native checks for fixed API rosters, evaluator partitions and realtime placement are recorded in the release contents. Qualification still belongs to the exact source/image, transport and deployment; this example does not establish multi-host, Kubernetes, capacity or failover admission. Realtime sharding and recovery uses tenant ownership; evaluator partitioning uses its selected membership/ordinal policy. A replica count alone establishes neither assignment nor safe handoff.

docs.title: Logical REST cohesion and worker placement
docs.text:
REST APIs v1/v2/v3 form one stateless request-serving component. Version adapters remain inside each equivalent replica. Data, authorization and owner REST modules may co-locate while retaining their credentials/audiences/listener rules. Process layout is a deployment choice; request pools, caches and in-flight work still make every real instance a maintenance participant. The placement/admission review owns the detailed assessment and the separate open activity-policy proposal.

Nginx already performs reverse proxying and Socket.IO upgrade/tunnelling in the reference. An optional nginx auth_request or Oathkeeper decision adapter would need its own private HTTP status/metadata/trusted-header contract. The socket /authorize operation is not that adapter: it can return HTTP success with a JSON denial. A gateway's initial connection decision also does not authorize later messages, subscriptions, delivery recipients or database writes. Existing current-client, tenant, RLS, ACK transaction and lifecycle gates remain.

This is a response-adaptation boundary, not a requirement to redesign existing application-to-application authentication. Direct component clients can consume the current JSON decision efficiently; nginx can consume a selected projection through status and response headers. Existing roles-gateway header handlers demonstrate that separation. The work plan records that prior art and keeps this optional edge integration independent of direct private service calls.

HTTP network reachability is deployment-owned; contract/version headers are not credentials. The current application adapter implements HTTP, not direct HTTPS. A selected TLS proxy/mesh can supply a deployment boundary; no new bearer login, credential-renewal system or mandatory gateway is implied by these diagrams.

docs.title: Ownership and placement constraints
docs.text: Responsibility Boundary to preserve Private listener composition Server-owned method/path registry, collision checks, per-operation schemas and service/version rules. No arbitrary URL-selected handler. Operation lifetime API work and delivery retain tenant admission through actual response completion. Lifecycle status/invalidation and operational probes need their own policy; do not blanket-wrap them in the tenant work they must inspect or invalidate. Restore coordination Complete supplied roster, direct instance reachability, actual datastore/backend/incarnation pins, drain and every invalidation acknowledgement. A sampled load-balanced endpoint is not a census. Placement/discovery Platform lifecycle and configured inventory are inputs. Native acceptance uses a fixed roster; no custom scheduler/discovery service is required. Unready or terminating actors with outstanding work cannot disappear from the roster merely because they left a routing table. Backing resources Follow the component ownership map: scoped reads and component-owned state can use storage; cross-component commands use admitted APIs. UI/nginx receive no blanket database/Vault authority. Workload ownership Size replicas for measured load/availability, and define ownership separately. API replicas do not require evaluator partition leases. The selected evaluator partition work has its own membership/conflict criteria.

docs.title: Scale envelopes and fleet planning
docs.text:
Post-baseline planning clarification, 2026-11-12; evidence below is UNMEASURED. Cell/fleet arrangement is PROPOSED, requiring explicit maintainer adoption. This adds no gate or prerequisite to current acceptance or the pilot.

10,000 tenants is an arbitrary experimental point and current preview bound, not an overall product goal. Planning covers small groups of 10–100 tenants and operators with hundreds or thousands. It also needs a credible path to 100,000+ tenants across a fleet. Record tenants, human users, concurrent sockets, active evaluation tenants and active alarm/delivery demand separately; none is a multiplier implied by another. A cohort is the selected workload/participant scope. A proposed cell is a bounded deployment/datastore and recovery unit; fleet totals must not be presented as one cell's or one PostgreSQL instance's capacity.

Reuse the same API, evaluator, realtime, PostgreSQL and change-feed components across qualified profiles. Experimental rigs isolate variables; they are not production recipes. Fleet routing, placement, cross-database tenant moves and control-plane recovery are additional responsibilities: adding replicas does not implement them. The existing deployment/fault-domain guide keeps per-tenant cells distinct from shared-cohort and multi-host choices.

Envelope Evidence needed Next bounded proof and owner Small group Whole-stack fixed and marginal cost at idle and steady load. Include application, database, secrets and platform resources. Measurement and deployment owners compare two selected profiles after the baseline. Use one population and workload; change one axis. Operator fleet Density and total cost within freshness, correctness and recovery limits. Include capacity after the declared node or dependency failure. Measurement and deployment owners test one stated failure on a selected topology. Check independent tenant progress and recovery before recommending a recipe. Large fleet, proposed Bounded routing, provisioning, database growth, maintenance and recovery across deployment groups. Total fleet size is not one database's capacity. Architecture and storage owners first inventory boundaries. A two-group synthetic move/recovery proof can inform an explicit placement and migration decision.

Small-profile cost differences can justify packaging changes. They do not adopt a new production profile. Fleet experiments require independent stored-data and ownership checks. They do not prove fleet capacity or adopt a cell architecture.

Keep the same behavior across topology choices. Preserve current tenant authority and revocation, committed write outcomes and uncertainty. Preserve owned work, checkpoints, lifecycle fencing, response drain, timer rules and public client contracts. Proposed compatibility seams are versioned internal contracts/capabilities or explicit coordinated-upgrade refusal, not a blanket mixed-version promise. Keep role instance/incarnation distinct from a service address, durable tenant identity distinct from a worker, and hints distinct from durable truth. Transport adapters share a behavioral contract; these seams do not require a universal framework or a new broker.

Each design brief states the required property, affected code and smallest necessary change. It names the owner and explains compatibility, migration and failure behavior. It specifies one discriminating control and the evidence needed to justify infrastructure changes. Classify it as required correctness/compatibility, measured optimization, bounded prototype or deferred hypothesis. This is a proposed tracking rubric, preserving adopted decisions rather than choosing a fleet topology or adding current acceptance requirements.

Comparative baselines and savings remain ASSUMPTION until reproduced with whole-stack resource/cost accounting, workload, retention, prices and availability scope. Before raising a preview limit, inventory work that scans the whole tenant roster. Account for connection pools, file descriptors, queues, backpressure, WAL retention and database growth. Include every maintenance participant. Identify bounded work per request/tick and explicit degraded recovery; extra worker count does not remove these constraints. The maintainer adopts later architecture/profile choices from those measurements with the named owners. These envelopes neither raise current limits nor infer PostgreSQL HA, automatic realtime failover or a production capacity claim.

docs.title: Qualification and delivery boundaries
docs.text:
The work plan retains the implementation seams and intended failure controls. Consult the queue and release records before treating a listed seam as missing implementation. The durable qualification questions are:

  1. Does the selected private binding preserve authority, exact operations, response completion, shutdown and commit/response uncertainty?
  2. Do all actual API instances initialize the relevant tenant and participate in maintenance, including actors outside ordinary service routing?
  3. Do evaluator partition changes and realtime moves preserve checkpoints, current authority and durable effect identity without duplicate protected output?
  4. Is successful evaluator work distinguished from healthy quiet state, failed work and inspection? A health response is not proof of per-tenant progress.
  5. What workload and resource envelope does the admitted topology meet, including restart, dependency outage and other-tenant interference?

These are separate from production/default admission. Gateway hooks, additional brokers and new fleet protocols are selected by a concrete requirement or measured constraint, not by diagram shape. This page explains components and topology. The deployment guide owns binding responsibilities. The production guide explains admission order. The queue and release records own current state.

Figures are generated by render_tenancy_topologies.py. Use --png to render previews and --check to detect stale vector outputs. Review the figures with contract/listener or deployment changes. Rendering checks freshness and layout, not application runtime acceptance.

docs.title: Evaluator inspection and workload ownership
docs.text:
The private evaluator inspection contract exposes bounded read-only state and successful-completion observations. Its schema and current implementation are owned by the source capability and release evidence. It does not drive evaluation or turn a process health check into workload proof. Membership/assignment health and workload progress are distinct concepts; a field must name the actual rule and observation rather than inventing a generic ring.

The interpretation and any extension of that contract must distinguish:

  • Configured mode and assignment rule/version, member count, this instance's ordinal and actual incarnation, and intended hash slice.
  • Observed peer membership/heartbeat expiry, agreement/conflict, the observation time and whether this instance is currently eligible to evaluate, with a reason when blocked. Configuration alone is not observed ring health.
  • Workload counts and progress: assigned/active/suspended tenants, current jobs, last successful acquisition/tick, lag/backlog and notification-handoff health. Aggregate metrics and bounded private drill-down serve different inspection needs.

In standalone Compose mode the intended assignment is all configured tenants (the complete assignment space); no membership lease should be fabricated when partitioning is disabled. With N configured members and one distinct eligible ordinal per member, each handles its assigned hash slice, approximately 1/N of a well-distributed tenant population. Equal hash slices do not guarantee equal tenant counts or computational load. A StatefulSet can supply ordinals; the application's selected membership/assignment policy decides eligibility. For the initial modulo-style assignment, an ordinal owns a hash bucket/predicate, not necessarily a contiguous token interval on a consistent-hash ring. Inspection must name the actual rule rather than inventing token-range metadata.

Stable assignment intends one evaluator owner per tenant. The adopted M7 policy allows a bounded overlap window with idempotent effects during membership change; it does not establish instantaneous exactly-once execution or automatic takeover. Transition and duplicate-effect claims require their actual source-scoped evidence. The operational API must report conflicts and blocked work, including when evaluation refuses. Inspection must not create work, acquire ownership or clear suspension.

Evaluator is not the only component with ownership-sensitive state. A ring is one possible assignment mechanism, not a universal scaling rule:

Component/work Relevant ownership unit Scaling implication Clinical evaluator Tenant's scheduled acquisition/time-based evaluation Selected M7 member-count/ordinal assignment; partition inspection belongs here. Notification producer/consumer Tenant/consumer state and individual durable delivery attempts Current consumer timers are serialized per tenant within each process; the store locks state and records attempt tokens/deadlines. Co-located consumers must follow the evaluator's admitted assignment, or have a separately qualified work-claim distribution model. A ring alone does not establish exactly-once external delivery. Connector actors Tenant/source account, polling cursor/session and upstream effects Tenant-side workers need explicit assignment or claims to avoid duplicate polling/ingestion. External connector-to-tenant and tenant-side connector directions have separate evidence; use the release record for joined scope rather than infer either direction from the other. Realtime Client connections/rooms and per-tenant projection/checkpoint consumers It has scheduled refresh work and retained state. Replication needs affinity, checkpoint ownership and complete notification fanout; it is not ordinary stateless replication and does not inherently require one realtime instance per tenant. REST/owner request serving Individual admitted request/transaction, plus instance drain state Equivalent replicas serve tenants without assigning each tenant to exactly one API. Every actual replica still participates in maintenance. Maintenance jobs Exclusive claim for the affected tenant/operation Existing database/lifecycle claim and census rules serialize destructive work; a tenant ring is not required for all maintenance jobs. PostgreSQL/Vault/edge/UI Their native storage, connection or request responsibilities Scale with their own mechanisms and resource bounds; the application evaluator ring does not assign their per-tenant ownership. They are not assumed to have tenant-independent cost.

These mechanisms are read-derived from the inspected runtime. The next owner must measure placement transitions, duplicate effects, recovery and cost before claiming another worker type is safe to replicate. Shared infrastructure may scale with tenant load even when it has no per-tenant scheduler.

docs.title: Private API composition, deployment bindings and fixed-roster scaling
docs.text:
Living document, last changed 2026-11-10 at 4917b2d4a.

Living contributor-facing implementation plan, refreshed 2026-11-10 for the adopted internal listener shape and graceful shutdown. Current mechanisms are read-derived from joined application dc795bd1; carried measurements retain their original source/instrument in the linked evidence. Remaining criteria are UNMEASURED until their instruments run. Queue homes: MT-ENDPOINT-TRANSPORT, MT-API-FIXED-ROSTER; scaling and partitioning retain MT-SCALE-UNBOUND and MT-EVALUATOR-PARTITION. Read with the runtime topology. No production/default enablement follows from implementation or a diagram.

docs.title: Implemented foundation and remaining boundary
docs.text:
The internal API implementation and joined dc795bd1 acceptance carry the shared transport, three service registries, executable request/response schemas, named clients, strict public/private separation and consuming-role configuration. UDS and actual loopback HTTP tests exist; the joined regression, browser, enabled-corpus and OIDC records have their own executed scope.

Surface Current implementation Remaining adjustment or proof Private contracts Socket authority/mutations, alarm delivery and lifecycle participant operations have named clients and schemas. Compose explicit contract modules on a component-private listener without weakening ownership or lifetime checks. Binding UDS or explicit http: origin; optional independent bind address (per-contract references, replaced by serve.internal). Qualify a selected private network deployment, not merely a helper's loopback behavior. Direct https: is not implemented. Trust UDS permissions/UID/inode protections or explicit deployment-owned network reachability. Service/version headers identify the contract, not a caller identity. Exercise the selected deployment's reachability/access boundary. TLS/mesh/proxy integration, if selected, belongs to the deployment; no new bearer protocol is required. Listener allocation One service contract per listener. Public/management interfaces are separate. Adopted 2026-11-10: one private listener per role process, serve.internal, whose contract set the role's code decides; configuration cannot move or merge contracts. The public listener stays separate. Worker operations Evaluator has lifecycle control and in-process health(); realtime has a consumer-app health route. Define and integrate an operational health/readiness/metrics contract. A GET metrics endpoint and its response format do not already exist. API replicas API work is request scoped; fixed participant identity/drain mechanisms exist. Run two real equivalent APIs behind a service destination and prove all-instance maintenance, replacement and compatibility. Runtime cost Realtime obtains current authority during recipient fanout. Measure latency, request amplification, dependency failure and aggregate resource limits under MT-SCALE-UNBOUND.

Private application calls and private lifecycle control are different purposes inside the same private API surface. They need not create separate transports, services or deployment processes. Data/authorization/owner REST modules may co-locate under existing audience and credential rules. REST v1/v2/v3 remain version adapters inside one logical request-serving component.

docs.title: Endpoint and compatibility contract
docs.text:
Adopted configuration (decision, 2026-11-10, multitenant only). Each role process has one private listener, serve.internal, configured in the style of Ory Kratos/Hydra's serve.public/serve.admin: host/port or socket, each overridable from the environment (NS_SERVE_INTERNAL_HOST, NS_SERVE_INTERNAL_PORT, NS_SERVE_INTERNAL_SOCKET), with a default. The default is a unix socket under a runtime directory, because the internal listener trusts its network (trust:'network') and has no authentication of its own; network exposure requires an explicit host/port. Callers receive peer addresses (for example NS_API_INTERNAL_URL). The preview is unreleased, so the change carries no compatibility shim.

Current code (dc795bd1, read-derived), which this replaces. Each contract has its own socketPathEnv or endpoint-descriptor reference with no default (lib/server/internal-api/endpoint-config.js:11-30; callers realtime/private-config.js, serve/operation-cohort-config.js, serve/evaluator-consumer-config.js), with service descriptions under contracts/ and usage in docs/internal-service-api.md. A Kubernetes Service DNS name can be the dial origin while a listener binds its own interface; a configured link-local/private address is supported, and loopback is not an architectural restriction. Public request content cannot choose private destinations. Credentials in URLs, unexpected paths/query/fragment components, unsupported schemes and implicit trust/fallback refuse, and the adopted shape keeps those refusals.

Shutdown (decision). On SIGTERM the internal listener stops accepting connections, lets in-flight calls finish and send their responses up to a configurable deadline below the platform's termination grace, then force-closes what remains; callers still treat a force-closed call as uncertain. Reproduced on the listener-composition lane (Compose, d69b873a): close() dropped a held call at 176 ms while the server still drained its handler.

Private operation payloads retain current tenant, credential, RLS, ACK and lifecycle semantics. Current service/version headers require a coordinated internal-peer upgrade; preserving the public client protocol does not establish mixed-version peer compatibility. Listener consolidation must specify any header, operation-path or schema migration explicitly; a URL must not be inferred from a malformed socket field.

UDS-specific filesystem checks remain inside its adapter. HTTP reachability is supplied by the selected deployment policy. If established TLS termination or a service mesh is chosen, document its trust boundary and test the selected binding; do not infer process identity from a DNS name, port, header or successful probe. No new application cryptographic login, discovery service or orchestrator is needed to keep these contracts well defined.

docs.title: Remaining work and acceptance
docs.text:
These owner roles name integration boundaries, not a new reservation ceremony. Confirm actual HEAD, current item openness and ownership before starting; stop and report a mismatch rather than substituting the nearest working mechanism. Keep each capability's helper, fixtures and meaningful controls in its lane.

Step / queue owner Concrete change Focused gate and intended semantic control Private API composition — MT-ENDPOINT-TRANSPORT Build one explicit registry of supported (method,path) routes and contract modules on each role's serve.internal listener, configured as adopted above, with graceful shutdown. Enforce duplicate/missing/extra registration, schema/content-type and service/version ownership. Bind independently from public/management HTTP. Actual UDS and HTTP calls succeed only on their intended private routes; public routes return 404. Inject a duplicate route, foreign contract/header, extra handler, malformed request or response and show the corresponding assertion turns red before unauthorized effects. Shutdown: a held call's caller receives its response within the deadline; restoring the early drop turns that assertion red. Per-operation lifecycle policy — same owner, with restore integration Preserve application tenant admission through response completion. Lifecycle status/invalidation and operational probes need their own explicit policy, rather than inheriting a blanket tenant-work window. With A in maintenance/suspended, status and the admitted invalidation still execute under the controller's existing rules while A application work refuses and B progresses. Hold an application response after SQL completion: drain must still wait. A blanket-window mutant must fail the lifecycle assertion, not merely a setup check. Operational module — same composition owner Specify liveness, readiness and metrics semantics, supported methods/response formats, dependency/tenant readiness behavior and scrape access. Retain useful existing health behavior or migrate it explicitly. Exercise actual GET/operational responses and any metrics content type. Wrong method/schema/format and false-ready dependency mutants go red. The JSON POST RPC client is not silently used as a metrics client. Naming endpoints is not implementing a collector or inventing new metric values. Deployment binding — endpoint owner with deployment-companion owner Select UDS or private HTTP independently for application and direct-instance calls. Render actual service/dial and listen addresses, access policy and upgrade configuration, using the adopted serve.internal settings (the preview carries no shim for the per-contract references). Run real separated processes on the selected network. Compare current authority, stored effects/absence, schema responses, byte/deadline/cancellation bounds, disconnect/no-retry behavior and shutdown. Remove the selected boundary/config check or synthesize an acknowledgement after commit/response loss: the intended refusal/uncertainty oracle must fail. Fixed roster — MT-API-FIXED-ROSTER Consume two equivalent real APIs, one ordinary service destination and a complete roster of exact participant endpoints, with pool inventory. Controller addresses each actual instance even when contracts share its private port. Observe which API handles each direct/service call. Missing/duplicate/service-aliased participants, wrong datastore/birth/incarnation/nonce, replacement during an old pin and omitted instance invalidation must refuse. Sampling a load-balanced destination is a deliberate failing control. Joined replica behavior — same API owner Preserve concurrent current authority, response/callback drain, tenant-local invalidation, lost-ack/commit uncertainty, replacement and B continuity. No transparent mutation replay. Revoke/change state through one API and exercise both direct APIs/service; hold the other API's response; lose a commit or invalidation reply; replace an incarnation. Stale authority, early lifetime release, ignored uncertainty or missing B progress must each fail its own independent outcome assertion. Coherent integration — existing candidate coordinator Join original lane histories, freeze the chosen code/config/instrument candidate, then run applicable full/default-browser/enabled-corpus/native/client acceptance and final prcheck. Preserve exact source/instrument attribution and named pending cases. A source-identical carried result stays attributed to its original run; new inputs require affected acceptance. No comprehensive campaign per leaf commit.

Lifetime composition is a substantive code change. Current API and alarm listeners supply an operation window; lifecycle control deliberately does not. Read-derived from tenant-lifecycle/operation-window.js, shared work admission refuses during exclusive/suspended maintenance. Wrapping lifecycle operations in that same policy would make control unavailable when it is needed. This is a predicted failure to reproduce with the control above, not a reported deadlock.

docs.title: Optional gateway decision adapter
docs.text:
Direct application-to-application calls retain the existing authentication and authorization semantics. Listener composition or using TCP instead of UDS does not inherently require changing those semantics. A native client can consume JSON; an edge integration can project selected decision fields into HTTP status and headers without making every private application call traverse a gateway.

Read-derived prior art: inspected nightscout-roles-gateway 90840acee1ec641d881512e91f1728f7ed8f7817. Its GET/HEAD Warden chain uses the existing policy decision and then sets upstream routing headers (x-upstream-origin, x-forwarded-host); its token header adapter sets X-NSJWT. Nginx can consume response headers through auth_request_set without interpreting the JSON body. These code mechanisms are inspected, not a newly executed gateway or interoperability campaign.

Nginx already handles public proxying and the Socket.IO upgrade. A selected auth_request/Oathkeeper-style integration would add a private decision contract: HTTP allow/deny/error semantics, original-request metadata, tenant resolution and which injected identity headers the application trusts. Reuse the existing authority component; do not duplicate its policy or use JSON {denied:true} as an HTTP allow. Client-supplied identity headers must not become trusted inputs.

This adapter is a separately bounded optional deployment integration until its contract is selected. It is not an extra prerequisite for selectable UDS/HTTP transport. Connection admission does not replace subsequent message, subscription, recipient, exact mutation/ACK or current credential authorization. Deployment binding/trust work owns an adopted gateway profile; core owns its stable decision hook if one is selected. No new mandatory gateway or authentication product is selected by this plan.

docs.title: Evaluator workload and membership inspection
docs.text:
The operational listener supports a read-only evaluator module whose payload is owned by MT-EVALUATOR-PARTITION. It reports configured mode/rule/version, member count, ordinal/incarnation and intended slice separately from observed membership/heartbeat agreement, freshness, conflicts and current eligibility. Expose aggregate assignment/progress/lag and handoff health, with bounded private drill-down where needed. Endpoint names and executable response schemas are still to be implemented; existing cohort status is not relabelled as ring health.

Standalone mode reports all configured tenants without inventing a membership lease. Partitioned mode reports the actual slice and observed membership basis; ordinal configuration alone cannot make a stale/conflicting member healthy. Introspection remains callable while evaluation is blocked, does not schedule clinical work or acquire ownership, and does not clear lifecycle suspension.

Acceptance uses actual evaluator processes and independently enumerated tenant assignments: member-count one covers the configured set; distinct members cover it without stable-state gaps/overlap; stale/mismatched count or duplicate ordinal is visible and blocks the affected computation. A mutant reporting only intended configuration as observed health must go red. Exercise membership-change overlap, recovery and duplicate durable/external effects under the existing M7 policy; the inspection API must not claim exactly-once execution from a hash mapping.

The ownership inventory also covers notification attempts, future connector actors, realtime projections and maintenance claims. The shared operational module does not impose one common ring on these different work units or make them all stateless replicas.

docs.title: Service destinations, participants and workload owners
docs.text:
Ordinary request-scoped calls may use an equivalently configured API service without pinning to the API that handled a prior request. A service must not retry an uncertain mutation automatically or route to an undeclared participant.

Maintenance consumes a complete relevant roster, directly reaches each instance, checks actual datastore/backend and role/namespace identity, pins incarnation, drains actual operations and awaits every invalidation acknowledgement. Logical participant IDs can survive replacement; an old pin cannot accept a new process. A lost peer or uncertain commit/ack retains the affected tenant's suspension. A fresh authorized attempt follows existing cleanup/registration rules; this is not automatic restore resume or orphan clearance.

Use supplied configuration/platform inventory. A routing table may exclude unready/terminating actors that still own operations, so it cannot automatically serve as the maintenance census. The native proof uses explicit endpoints; a Kubernetes/platform adapter is separate deployment work. No new membership or consensus service is required for the API capability.

Evaluator and realtime replication remain separate semantics. MT-EVALUATOR-PARTITION carries the adopted optional member-count/ordinal and pool-membership contract; the default remains one workload owner. Realtime scale-out is scoped by the separate sharding/composition proposal, which owns placement, checkpoint and subset-aware maintenance changes and their acceptance. Neither is a reason to split REST version adapters into separate services or to block the already accepted foundation.

docs.title: Measurement and documentation boundaries
docs.text:
MT-SCALE-UNBOUND owns synchronous authority fanout/dependency cost and aggregate API pools, database/Vault pressure, failure/recovery and healthy-tenant progress. Benchmarks retain synthetic workload, actual source/config, latency/queue/freshness and independent durable outcome oracles. Functional success is not a capacity or availability target. Metrics endpoint implementation does not itself supply that measurement, and a proposed cache must retain current-authority guarantees.

Native runs use the adopted disposable harness and owned resource cleanup; there is no grant, lead reservation or freshness-attestation ceremony. Capture exact code/config/instrument identities, direct/service topology, complete participant coverage, real listener/transport and each red/restored symptom. Preserve failed predictions and distinguish actual clients/native processes from source doubles.

The runtime topology owns figures and audience/purpose/binding terminology. This page owns remaining work/acceptance; the queue owns claimed state. Correct superseded living prose in place and link retained measurements; do not create a second current plan or rewrite captured evidence.

docs.title: Single and multitenant Nightscout: architecture and compatibility
docs.text:
Living document, last changed 2026-11-10 at 0fb666fca.

Contributor-facing living explanation, groomed 2026-11-08; header 2026-11-10. The restore/Compose reference this page explains is cgm-remote-monitor ed2ced00c80bd0a6a7d75f834d2c6e2af8c71364, recorded in the publication measurement. Draft PR #8898 has since moved on (M6a and M6b joins); its current head and verification are in the release contents, and private service composition is in the runtime topology guide. PR #8898 remains open/draft, not merged or released. Architecture interpretation is read-derived; linked runtime results are recorded reproductions, not new executions for this document. The retained shared-code/module survey is explicitly pinned to 83582e87; it does not describe every file in the current candidate. Current delivery and milestone claims live in the delivery dashboard.

docs.title: What the proofs can inform
docs.text:
The useful result is an executable one-host multitenant reference with separate services and tenant-local restore. It gives current architecture decisions a measured basis. Production qualification and additional deployment models still need their own evidence; an accepted component is not a completed platform track.

Capability Recorded basis Useful for decisions now Remaining admission Separate API/realtime/evaluator/admin and packaged UI ed2 cold Compose acceptance One-host role composition, existing client/browser routes and private control channels work together. Multi-host discovery, replicas/failover, production ingress/service identity and operating limits. Tenant-local restore and shared-role restart c23 native acceptance, plus ed2 packaged ordinary restore above A can stay suspended while B progresses; forward correction/deletion history allows tested clients to converge without a global pause. Automatic orphan clearance, supported suspended-restore resume and production recovery bounds under the application ownership contract. Functional durable evaluator/realtime reference R73 Bounded snapshots, durable suppression and stable notification-intent identities support the one-host runtime direction. Provider/device delivery, distributed producer ownership and capacity/freshness/egress budgets. Existing client compatibility ed2 actual pinned clients; 39f4 enabled corpus Use the admitted API/history/credential shapes and the named clients' stored outcomes. Wider/mobile clients, other query shapes and all-client acceptance. Derived calculation reuse f0 characterization Selected evaluator/API current properties agree; time, settings and input identity matter. Realtime raw frames remain a separate product. A shared immutable-result interface, full authorization/clinical equivalence and publication-service ownership/freshness. No service is selected by the characterization. Nonresident single-site execution or another backend Independently attributed R43 and later profile records in the platform plan Inform seam and acquisition research within their measured caller policies. Separate profile/backend admission; neither a computed-single default nor single-site PostgreSQL, multitenant MongoDB or SQLite/Celld follows.

A prototype answers a bounded feasibility or semantics question. An integrated functional reference proves cooperating components on a named topology. A production server additionally needs its actual trust and identity setup, credential/lifecycle recovery, selected workload limits and operator procedures accepted together. Merge, release and default enablement are separate decisions. The deployment/fault-domain guide compares the independent tenancy, backend, computation, process and host axes.

The maintainer reaffirmed separate service processes, including containers with shared private sockets where appropriate. Compose is implemented and functionally accepted for the one-host synthetic preview; a Jsonnet generator remains an optional packaging tool.

Component paths describe the reference source, with executed acceptance bounded by its named record above. Realtime's raw record frames and evaluator-derived values are distinct products; see the characterization. Existing client protocols do not change when these roles move into containers. The default single-tenant process retains its existing composition.

During tenant A restoration, each participating process must stop admitting A's new work, finish admitted work, and acknowledge clearing A's retained state before reactivation. Tenant B has its own operation window. The implemented fixed cohort registers actual separate processes through configured private participant endpoints. A PostgreSQL advisory lock protects participating code. A database-enforced fence would reject bypassing operations in PostgreSQL itself. Process separation and that stronger fence are separate questions; neither a process list nor a configuration assertion proves exclusive credential custody. The native matrix exercises the actual separate processes and uncertainty/restart cases under its declared fixed trusted-cohort boundary. Arbitrary direct SQL actors remain outside that proof and are unsupported under the exclusive application ownership contract. The database ownership map distinguishes cross-component commands from admitted reads and owned persistence. The tenant-local startup requirement prevents a suspended tenant from blocking another tenant's shared-role restart. The c23 native acceptance reproduces fresh API/realtime/evaluator startup and B operation while A remains suspended in the tested failure scenarios. It does not clear claims or provide automatic uncertain-outcome recovery.

See deployment/rig scenarios, evaluator/realtime communication and SQL/migration architecture for runnable preparation, sequence diagrams and storage/recovery boundaries. Documentation checks do not establish an executed deployment or capacity/recovery guarantee.

docs.title: What the write seam made possible
docs.text:
Shared single-tenant code did change. The storage/write seams let the multitenant preview reuse shipping domain rules and version-specific handlers while injecting a different store and tenant context. They did not make every service tenant-safe automatically, or freeze the code used by single.

The compatibility objective is to preserve the existing default MongoDB behavior when no trusted replacement is injected. That objective is supported by tests; it is different from claiming no shared source changed or every possible request behaves identically.

There are two related seams: reads/counts use a storage interface, and mutations use shared write-intent rules and a write boundary. Tenant resolution, credentials, current grants, settings, caches, derived views and service lifecycle also require explicit boundaries. The clinical-record write seam is not a universal wrapper around operator policy, secrets or every side effect.

docs.title: Isolation extends beyond the write boundary
docs.text:
flowchart TB
  Request["Request with Host<br/>and selected credential"] --> Resolve["Resolve stable tenant<br/>verify tenant-bound credential"]
  Resolve --> Grants{"Current authority<br/>allows operation?"}
  Grants -->|"no / unavailable"| Deny["Version-specific refusal<br/>no handler mutation"]
  Grants -->|"yes"| Handler["Reused handler and intent rules<br/>trusted request context"]
  Handler --> Transaction["Owned PostgreSQL transaction<br/>tenant binding and forced RLS"]
  Transaction --> Outcome{"Commit or<br/>rollback?"}
  Outcome -->|"rollback"| Error["Version-specific error<br/>no committed row change"]
  Outcome -->|"commit"| Reply["Version-specific reply<br/>local post-commit notification"]
  Reply -.-> Local["A local event is not a<br/>durable interprocess feed"]

Tenant identity must also bind reads, settings, history/lastModified clocks, secrets, cache frames and returned derived values. PostgreSQL/RLS is defense in depth alongside request-bound application context; it does not replace request authorization. Static host maps and loopback lab trust do not establish durable provisioning or production transport/service identity.

Current grants are checked again on the next protected operation, rather than frozen into an exchanged token. This does not promise cancellation of work already authorized. The shipping read-then-write precondition behavior is retained; the preview does not claim a new atomic compare-and-swap guarantee.

Properties/ddata retain shipping entries-and-treatments permission semantics, including secondary profile/device/activity/food snapshot arrays. Summary retains its wildcard read requirement. Those are inherited compatibility boundaries, not new declarations that every exposed field has an independent collection grant.

Compatibility question Supported answer Existing clients using established API shapes against the new server? docs.title: Hypothetical third-backend smell test
docs.text:
Read-derived at ded254b9, 2026-11-05, and the resolver anchor re-read at 83582e87 on 2026-11-06 (collection at line 34, resolve at 41, intent at 54); no SQLite adapter, isolation or performance experiment was run. A third backend has a clearer insertion point than the Mongo-only base: trusted ctx.storagePorts.resolve supplies storage and an intent factory (lib/server/storage-reads.js:34–56), and the PG adapters call the shared write-intent.forCollectionResolved rules. Existing shipping routers, validation and client quirks therefore need not be copied into another API. This improves reuse; it does not establish a backend-neutral runtime.

There are concrete consolidation candidates:

Source at the pinned CRM head Smell / bounded improvement lib/storage/postgres-entries-intent.js:16,30,84 and postgres-collection-intent.js:24,47,142 Related filter/projection helpers and transaction/event wrappers are repeated. Generalize only their measured common contract; entries-specific and legacy query/natural-order differences are intentional until disproved by tests. lib/server/tenant-app/entries.js:20, treatments.js:18, profile-food-errors.js:13 Repeated PG error classification and representation-refusal translation can drift. A shared adapter helper is plausible, guarded by existing HTTP error tests. lib/server/tenant-app/domain-catalogue.js:7–13 Domain factories are coupled to PG candidate migrations. A hypothetical additional backend needs trusted backend-specific factory/schema/readiness selection behind the same domain capabilities. PG intent adapters' fromMongo/toMongo dialect bridge and api3/storage/mongoCollection/utils import The boundary still carries Mongo-shaped legacy semantics and Mongo-named normalization helpers. Separate API/document semantics from backend query lowering before treating this as a neutral database plugin interface. Renaming alone proves nothing. lib/storage/postgres-connection.js:26–50 and tenant authority/secrets persistence PostgreSQL RLS, roles, tenant-bound transactions and control-plane persistence are a separate protection contract. A cell/file/container isolation primitive would need equivalent tested ownership, lifecycle, failure and authority boundaries; substituting the data adapter alone is insufficient.

For a hypothetical celld/SQLite design, keep the domain/write semantics above the backend; implement query/identity/document representation, atomic writes and commit hooks below it. Reuse the Mongo/PG differential corpus for a third adapter, including refusal cases. Isolation placement, concurrent writers, crash recovery, migration/backup and durable event delivery each need a new measured contract. This is easier at the handler/write-rule layer, still substantial at the storage and runtime layers. No claim of SQLite equivalence, operational advantage or celld adoption follows. The current REST/compatibility wave comes first; measured duplication can be consolidated without introducing a third backend.

docs.title: Remaining evidence gaps and next work
docs.text:
The dashboard retains M0–M5 at their adopted functional scope and M6 blocked. The accepted one-host runtime, tenant-local restore/restart, cold Compose and pinned-client capabilities inform ongoing design; they do not close wider identity/lifecycle, production trust, workload limits, HA or whole-M6 admission. See the current decision index, release contents and completion schedule for policy, actual source acceptance and ownership rather than old survey tasks.

Historical old-seam gates and unmeasured broader cards must retain their real instrument status. A failing old configuration-table predicate is distinct from accepted new-tree persisted settings/authority; neither a prototype nor this diagram promotes the larger configuration catalogue. Run make queue-status for current gate measurements. This documentation change runs no new application or deployment campaign and adopts no new architecture or safety policy.

docs.title: SQL, migrations and tenant recovery architecture
docs.text:
Living document, last changed 2026-11-10 at a2dacd669.

Living contributor-facing architecture guide. Source reading verified 2026-11-07 against cgm-remote-monitor 151de0248a1e4301c85b5c638185eec3ca8c38e6 (tree 3bb46431a19e604dc028768f0e72e6ad29616c26). Mechanisms and diagrams below are read-derived unless a linked record says reproduced. These are branch implementation mechanisms, not a released operator feature. Commit-pinned application links identify that inspected revision; executed measurements retain their own source. Decisions live in the tenancy contracts and release decisions; acceptance lives in the release contents. Ownership/API guidance updated 2026-11-08 under the maintainer's exclusive application ownership decision. Design recommendations and Kubernetes scale-out assessment are read-derived; no new runtime or cluster campaign was run. This guide explains their SQL implementation and does not promote M6.

Refreshed 2026-11-10 against draft PR #8898 head 16a1fc2d45e59602eb6ec3e3bf6f506f35bcc5b1: tenant activity, key retention and export-file removal, the restore census and the ownership_operator identity. docs.title: Scope and evidence
docs.text:
For diagram-first review, open the database and component ownership visual review. It renders the tables and diagrams below from this guide, with the source revision recorded.

The explicit multitenant PostgreSQL deployment shares physical tables among tenants. It maps each selected catalogue to an operator-configured schema; a schema is a component/domain namespace, not a new schema for each tenant. Single-tenant and MongoDB entrypoints retain their separate composition. The deployment catalogue selection is the concrete reference for the preview; the storage seam and write contract own admitted port behavior.

Evidence What it establishes Boundary b029 native acceptance Reproduced: all 17 stated native operation-window criteria on b029f5d81f539a4846e51ab88e540cb4511910fa, including separate roles, forward-history restore, running B progress and fault refusals. Different source from this guide. It does not measure the new tenant-local startup admission or whole M6. c23 native matrix Reproduced: separate-role restore and fresh shared-role restarts with B progress while A remained unavailable in the recorded failure cases; unsafe-clock API startup refused; independent physical closure. Exact c23 executed source, fixed trusted cooperative cohort. No automatic orphan clearance, suspended-restore resume command or production recovery bound. ed2 cold Compose measurement Reproduced: packaged A restore preserved clinical value/public identity, forward history and B rows while B committed work; actual controller committed/reactivated; independent configuration/resource/process closure. Exact ed2 source/image, fixed cooperative one-host reference. Client and final regression gates remain separate. Application startup source guide and startup controls The 151de024 source defers genuinely suspended tenants while retaining shared readiness failures and later full initialization. Source/protocol reading; actual runtime measurements retain their c23 attribution above. Counter analysis and clock proof plan Rationale, alternatives and invariants, with individually scoped experiments. Their earlier source anchors and feasibility results do not replace current catalogue/readiness verification.

docs.title: Supported database ownership contract
docs.text:
The exclusive application ownership decision defines supported writers. Nightscout collectively owns its selected namespaces: multiple internal processes and controlled maintenance tools may use PostgreSQL, but every supported participant follows the relevant application contract. External direct writers are unsupported and their effects are undefined behavior, consistent with single-tenant Nightscout's external MongoDB writer boundary. Other applications may own unrelated namespaces; this does not require exclusive ownership of an entire PostgreSQL server.

Exclusive application ownership does not confer unrestricted SQL rights on each component. Retain effective privilege/readiness checks, tenant-bound transactions, forced RLS, current authorization and narrowly scoped credentials. Internal clinical writes must use the canonical write path; lifecycle participants must honor admission, drain and invalidation. The advisory-lock protocol coordinates these supported participants. A direct writer ignoring it is outside the contract, not a reason to require a stronger database fence for the supported topology. PostgreSQL documents advisory locks as application-coordinated locks.

docs.title: One logical REST/API component
docs.text: REST v1, v2 and v3 belong to one logical stateless request-serving API component, together with credential authorization and owner-management modules. Version-specific adapters retain their request, authorization and response semantics; protocol versions are not separate application services. Stateless means durable authority/data are external and request state is reconstructible, not that the process has no in-flight work or retained readiness state. This logical grouping does not prescribe a single listener, process or privilege set. Owner management retains its own audience and listener contract and may be colocated with API serving under the existing owner-authority boundary. The accepted separate-role reference remains one concrete composition, not a requirement that every REST responsibility become a separate service. Grouping the versions does not admit additional routes: the recorded compatibility scope and admitted handler/storage contracts still bound actual coverage.

docs.title: Headless workload owners
docs.text: Realtime owns live connections; the evaluator is a headless worker and remains one current workload owner. Connector actors (vcpool) belong to background polling/egress work and submit clinical writes through the canonical API boundary; the ed2 role declaration has no runnable start. Evaluator partitioning and realtime replication are separate future capabilities, not prerequisites for the queued request-serving API scale-out.

docs.title: Private maintenance execution
docs.text: The lifecycle/restore controller executes as a private operator CLI, job or worker; the ed2 operator tool composes it outside API serving. Each serving instance supplies generic operation-admission, lifetime and invalidation hooks; those hooks do not place a restore engine or maintenance credentials in every API replica. A future command/status REST surface could request or observe maintenance while the privileged worker executes it separately; no new endpoint or process layout is selected here. The logical placement map owns the broader component explanation.

docs.title: Maintenance safety is distinct from desired activity
docs.text: The existing claim/generation-bound maintenance window determines whether an operation can run safely during recovery. Operator-controlled resource/activity policy asks which serving, ingestion, evaluation or connector work should run at all. That policy is decided as two durable flags, pause and suspend (activity-is-pause-suspend), and stored in tenant_activity beside, not inside, the maintenance window; see tenant activity. A maintenance phase named active is not evidence of activity eligibility, and clearing the restore hold never changes the activity flags (policy module). Observed health is a further separate fact.

docs.title: Component ownership and internal application APIs
docs.text:
Read-derived architecture direction: place commands at the component that owns their semantics, and let that component persist its state. An internal API can be a module interface within a process or a private application protocol between processes. The reference's process transport is private HTTP/JSON over Unix sockets; network endpoint selection requires the separately described transport binding. The following ownership map does not introduce a generic SQL-over-HTTP service.

Operation / state Owner and internal boundary Existing reference or recommended direction Clinical documents, public write outcomes and history stamps API executes canonical writes, including a writer's current authority. Socket/connector/other component commands enter the same application write boundary. Document, clock and insertion changes retain their transaction coupling. API clinical writes and D23 socket forwarding exist. Additional internal command producers must use the admitted path; their implementation/acceptance remains separately scoped. Alarm acknowledgement / snooze Realtime forwards the original client authorization and event to API; API persists suppression through its acknowledgement admission. Evaluator reads current suppression. Existing private authorization and mutation protocol; realtime must not edit suppression rows as a substitute. Clinical acquisition and consumer recovery state Evaluator and realtime each read through tenant-bound storage interfaces and own separate projection/checkpoint namespaces. Existing bounded snapshot acquisition. Direct admitted reads and atomic projection/checkpoint persistence remain appropriate; sending every read through API would add dependency and transport cost without establishing stronger semantics. Notification intent, attempts and handoff Evaluator's notification component owns durable producer/request/attempt state; realtime owns connected-browser fanout. Deliver an application handoff with stable request identity and durable retry outcome. Existing notification handoff. Other components should not insert producer requests or edit attempt rows to impersonate its protocol. Credentials, owner configuration and current policy Management/authority components own mutation checks, audit and invalidation. Consumers use their admitted authority/settings interfaces; data-plane requests retain their own current authorization. Separate management audience and component interfaces exist. Cross-process consumers should invoke owned commands rather than edit these tables; this is not a claim that every authority operation has a new network endpoint. Maintenance exclusion, restore, deletion and activation Private operator lifecycle controller coordinates each actual participant through its control API and owns controlled maintenance transactions. Explicit migration/provisioning tools own their separate catalogues and grants. Existing fixed-cohort restore protocol. A table update or clinical API write alone cannot drain in-flight responses, clear another process's cache or authorize a deletion ceremony.

docs.text:
Read-derived ownership matrix. Each row is an admitted component's storage responsibility, not a mandatory process or a separate physical database.
