docs.title: RT-VERSION — Two artefacts claim version 15.0.9 with different Node floors
docs.text:
state (claimed) answered repo cgm-remote-monitor branch - base - worktree externals/cgm-remote-monitor-official semver n/a review maintainer register BF-60

Blast radius. package.json "version" on official/master, official/dev and all five cut tips.

What an operator sees. The next release changes which versions of Node (the program Nightscout runs on) it will start on, and removes two older built-in ways of getting CGM data in (the Dexcom Share and MiniMed CareLink bridges). It will be called 16.0.0, so the version number tells you which kind of build you have. Some unreleased development branches still call themselves 15.0.9, the same number as the current release; they get new numbers before any of them is released.

Why n/a. this item IS the versioning decision

Gates.

  • [static] node tools/queue/gates/version-collision.js
  • FAILS while two of official/master, official/dev and the five cut tips carry the same package.json version string with different engines.node (GT4's finding, as a measurement). Reads official/* since 2026-10-21; official/master was added the same day, because the released version is the one an operator reports.
  • NO GATE — Both cut-4 migration shims emit error text saying "retired in Nightscout 15.0.9", but on the adopted train 15.0.9 is the bug-fix release and retires nothing. Nothing checks error strings against the release they name.

Evidence.

  • docs/60-research/modernization/gt4-semver-classification-2026-09-15.md

Notes. 2026-10-21 (maintainer): settled. Cut 1 lands on dev now and the next release is 16.0.0: cut 1 is semver major (the enforced Node floor ^22.12 || >=24 exits at boot on Node 20, 21, 23 and 22.0-22.11; the legacy Dexcom Share and MiniMed CareLink bridges are removed; MongoDB 4.4 is no longer tested). Cut 1 at official/chore/retire-jsdom 806ff2f0 (#8828) declares 16.0.0 and dev 04d435eb declares 15.0.10, so cut 1 no longer collides with dev; once #8828 merges, dev is cut 1 and declares 16.0.0. Gate re-run 2026-10-21 on official/ (3 checked, 1 failing): 15.0.10 only on dev, 16.0.0 only on cut 1; 15.0.9 is still claimed by official/master c6a0d8ed (>=20.x) and by cuts 2-5 (b6e8c7cd, ebb690cf, b80aa147, b1bdaca0; ^22.23.2 || ^24.20.0). The remaining collision is cleared by the existing rule that each cut is renumbered at its catch-up merge (RT- REBASE). Read against the stale origin/ refs (origin/dev 4bca2ac2, origin/chore/retire-jsdom bce12ecc) the same script reported all six refs at 15.0.9. 2026-10-02 (maintainer): no longer in RT-0's blocks_on; this item holds the cuts (RT-1 onward), not 15.0.9. The version is decided; the gate is red on the cut tips. The dev to master release is 15.0.9 (dev package.json says 15.0.9 at 153e5658). Each modernization cut still declares 15.0.9 too, which is what version-collision.js measures; the cuts are renumbered when they are rebased. Decisions: - 2026-09-22, amended 2026-09-23 (maintainer): the dev to master release is 15.0.9. #8743 ships as-is. #8738 is amended before the tag (RT-COUNT0): ?count=0 answers an empty list, malformed counts stay HTTP 400, saves and updates ignore count, and a delete with an invalid count (0 included) is still refused. Both are declared as corrections in the release notes. - 2026-09-24 (maintainer, RT-COUNT-COMPAT): reads tolerate the count shapes oref0 and GluPredKit send, each tolerance behind its own setting, on by default; 15.0.9 stays a patch. With the default, count=0 on a read is not an empty list (see RT-COUNT-COMPAT). - 2026-09-23 (maintainer): each cut is renumbered when it is rebased; see releases/cgm-remote- monitor-15.0.9/decisions.md. The version number is the first thing an operator checks, so builds that differ must not share one.

docs.title: RT-COUNT0 — v1 ?count=0 answers an empty list, amending #8738 before 15.0.9
docs.text:
state (claimed) released repo cgm-remote-monitor branch bf/count-zero-empty base origin/dev@74fc6619 worktree externals/work/crm-count-zero semver patch review maintainer

Blast radius. Tip ce9503ac, two commits, 5 files - lib/server/count.js (isZeroCount; applyCount answers zero without querying), lib/api/index.js validateCount (GET/HEAD - zero allowed; DELETE - dev's rule, zero refused; POST/PUT/PATCH - not checked), lib/api/devicestatus/index.js (kept 0 instead of its default 10), lib/server/profile.js list(), and tests/api.count-parameter.test.js.

What an operator sees. 15.0.9 will refuse a request for a nonsense number of records (for example "abc" or "-3") with an error, where earlier versions guessed a number. A request for zero records no longer returns the whole collection by accident: with the default settings it returns every record in a date range when one is given, as 15.0.8 did, and otherwise the usual default number of records; switched off, it returns an empty list. Uploading data is not affected.

Why patch. narrows #8738's new refusal before any release has shipped it

Gates.

  • [static] git -C externals/cgm-remote-monitor-official merge-tree --write-tree official/dev bf/count-zero-empty >/dev/null
  • Merges into origin/dev with no conflict.
  • [integration] cd externals/work/crm-count-zero && TEST=api.count-parameter npm run test-single
  • 36 cases at ce9503ac (the env file expects mongo on 127.0.0.1:27087, which must be started first). Break-its, re-run 2026-09-23 at ce9503ac - zero back to unbounded (applyCount only) fails 8, zero back to 400 on reads fails 11, deletes skipping the check (the first commit) fails 6, deletes letting zero through fails 3, deletes refusing every count fails 1. The 8 delete cases pass on dev by design; they pin dev's rule.

Evidence.

  • releases/cgm-remote-monitor-15.0.9/decisions.md

Notes. 2026-10-21 - released in 15.0.9 (tag v15.0.9, master c6a0d8ed, the merge of #8598; tree c53c2c7f = dev 4bca2ac2). Merged into dev by #8748 (42c5e21e, head fc2d25ca, 2026-09-23); not released. CI and CodeQL green on the merge commit. Amended on 2026-09-24 by #8761 (RT-COUNT-COMPAT) for the forms oref0 and GluPredKit send. Nothing is owed on this item. What #8748 made of count on API v1: a read with count=0 answers an empty list; malformed counts (0x10, 2.5, -3, 1e2, abc, MAX_SAFE+1, %2B5, count=1&count=2) stay 400; saves and updates ignore count; a DELETE carrying a count that is not a whole number of 1 or more, count=0 included, is refused with 400 and deletes nothing, as on dev; a valid count on a DELETE is accepted and, as on dev, does not limit it. #8761 then made two read shapes tolerated by default, each behind its own setting: with API_V1_COUNT_ZERO_WINDOW (default true) a read with count=0 returns the whole range when the find bounds one date field from both sides and the endpoint default otherwise; the empty-list answer applies when that setting is false. See RT-COUNT-COMPAT. Measured for the maintainer on the branch (read matrix of 30 entries, 120 treatments, 30 devicestatus, 15 profile, 15 activity, counted in mongo): the only change from dev on reads is the 0 and 00 columns, now 200 with no rows on every v1 read route. Routes that never apply count (/entries/current, /count/.../where, /status, /echo, /food) answer count=0 normally instead of 400. v1 accepts zero while v3 limit=0 stays 400, so FU-LIMIT's "two implementations that agree" no longer holds. PR body: reports/phase0-pr-bodies/count-zero-empty.md. Decisions: - 2026-09-23 (maintainer): "count=0 should return a 0 length array of results." Malformed counts stay 400; saves and updates ignore count; ships in 15.0.9. For reads, the default answer to count=0 was re-decided on 2026-09-24 (RT-COUNT-COMPAT); the empty list remains the answer with API_V1_COUNT_ZERO_WINDOW=false. - 2026-09-23 (maintainer): a DELETE with an invalid count, 0 included, is refused with 400 as on dev.

Blast radius. The v1 count rule from #8738 as amended by #8748 (lib/server/count.js, lib/api/index.js validateCount), and the number 15.0.9 ships under.

What an operator sees. OpenAPS (oref0) and GluPredKit keep working with 15.0.9 as they did with 15.0.8. OpenAPS asks for its latest treatment with extra text after the number, and 15.0.9 reads the number, as 15.0.8 did. GluPredKit asks for "zero" records over a date range meaning "everything in the range", and gets everything in the range. Both answers carry a deprecation warning, because a future major release may refuse these shapes.

Why patch. Decided 2026-09-24 - the shapes real clients send are read as 15.0.8 read them, so no input a real client sends is narrowed (section 3.2's test); only shapes no known client sends stay refused.

Gates.

  • NO GATE — The branch is local (not pushed), so no gate can read it from a remote. Evidence is the count suite (49/49) and the full suite in six cells (Node 20 / 22 / 24 x mongo 4.4 / 7, 2466/0/3 each), with two break-it controls, and the consumer-replay lab's P1 and P2 re-run on the branch in both auth modes. Not yet run - a combined run with #8754 and #8758; a real OpenAPS rig or GluPredKit install (the lab replays their requests, not the programs).

Evidence.

  • docs/30-design/modernization/semver-and-release-versioning-policy-2026-09-15.md

Notes. 2026-10-21 - released in 15.0.9 (tag v15.0.9, master c6a0d8ed, the merge of #8598; tree c53c2c7f = dev 4bca2ac2). Merged into dev by #8761 (f1591069, head 516f971a, 2026-09-24); not released. CI green on the head (tests on Node 20/22/24 x MongoDB 4.4/5/6, CodeQL, npm and Docker validation). The combined run on dev f1591069 (which carries #8761) + the exact connector pin + #8754 ef3404fd + #8758 passes 3046/0/3 in all six Node x MongoDB cells (docs/30-design/remedial/rc-15.0.9-integration-record.md). Not run: a real OpenAPS rig or GluPredKit install (the lab replays their requests, not the programs). Decisions: - DECIDED 2026-09-24 (maintainer, -59) - tolerate the shapes real clients send and keep 15.0.9 a patch. oref0's "N?..." reads N (only digits followed by ?; abc, -3, 2.5, 1e2, 0x10 stay 400, with or without a ?). count=0 on a read was re-decided the same day, after 15.0.8's code showed it had meant NO limit (a truthy "0" reached .limit(0)) and the entries default of 10 would cut GluPredKit's 576 to 10 without an error: no limit when the find bounds one date field from both sides, the endpoint default otherwise. Both answered with Deprecation: true and a 299 Warning, logged once per process, without the value (oref0's contains its credential). - SETTINGS 2026-09-24 (maintainer - "one boolean per quirk") - API_V1_COUNT_LEADING_NUMBER and API_V1_COUNT_ZERO_WINDOW, both default true with a "switch to false in a future release" comment; false gives #8748's answer for that shape. README documents both. What ships: lib/server/count.js (leadingCount, hasDateWindow, NO_LIMIT_COUNT) and lib/api/index.js (validateCount rewrites the two shapes on GET/HEAD before checking). count=0 inside a two-sided date window becomes a limit of 2147483647, the largest 32-bit limit; outside one it is dropped so the endpoint default applies (activity has no default, so it reads unbounded there, as it already does with no count). Deletes are unchanged. Evidence at 516f971a: count suite 53/53, env suite green; full suite 2471/0/3 in all six Node 20/22/24 x MongoDB 4.4/7 cells; break-it with the settings ignored fails 3 of the 4 new setting tests (the fourth is a control); earlier break-its (tolerance off: 18 new tests fail; window rule off: the 2 entries window tests fail). One unexplained run of the count+env pair failed 8 array-length assertions; seven reruns and the six-cell matrix were green, and its log was not kept. -6a's replay lab as slot d, readable and denied: P1 oref0 200 in hashed and token modes, the cull keeps 1 of 57; P2 GluPredKit 1 / 137 / 576, equal to 15.0.8 and the count=100000 control. Why it was needed (docs/60-research/remedial/consumer- impact-15.0.9-2026-09-23.md): oref0 (dev d219baf9, master 88cf032a) sends count as "1?" from latest-openaps-treatment, which 15.0.8's parseInt read as 1 and #8748 answered with 400; through oref0's own jq/date pipeline the rig then re-uploads 57 treatments per loop instead of 1, with no duplicates (the created_at+eventType upsert is idempotent), but a Nightscout- side edit to a rig treatment from the last 24 h is overwritten on the next loop. GluPredKit sends count=0 meaning "no limit" (15.0.8: 1 / 137 / 576 in a 50 h window), which #8748 answered with []. Under the semver policy rule (section 3.2) both narrowings would have made the release major as written.

docs.title: RT-LOOP-REMOTE-ADDRESS — Loop remote commands carry the proxy's address as their sender label
docs.text:
state (claimed) released repo cgm-remote-monitor branch rt/trust-one-source base official/bf2/auth-hardening@708af170 worktree - semver patch review maintainer, and a Loop maintainer for anything that changes the value blocks on RT-TRUST-ONE-SOURCE

Blast radius. lib/api2/notifications-v2.js:34 (passes req.connection.remoteAddress) and the 'remote-address' field lib/server/loop.js puts in every Loop push (overrides, override cancel, carbs, bolus). Downstream: Loop's NightscoutService decodes the field as a required String on every V1 remote notification, stores it on a remote override's enactTrigger, and uploads it back to Nightscout as the Temporary Override treatment's remoteAddress with enteredBy "Loop (via remote command)" (LoopWorkspace NightscoutService fe075ef, read 2026-09-24).

What an operator sees. When a caregiver sends a remote command to Loop through Nightscout (a temporary override, carbs or a bolus), Nightscout tells Loop where the command came from, and Loop saves that on the override it records back in Nightscout. On most hosted sites that "where" is the address of the hosting company's own proxy, not the caregiver's, so it says nothing useful. After this change it is the caregiver's address, worked out the same way as everywhere else from your TRUST_PROXY setting. That address is then saved on each remote override in your Nightscout data, where anyone who can read your site's data can see it. Nothing about whether a command is accepted depends on it.

Why patch. Changes the value of a label in the Loop push payload and in treatments Loop uploads; no API shape changes, and the key Loop requires is kept.

Gates.

  • [static] ! git -C externals/cgm-remote-monitor-official grep -nE "req\.(connection|socket)\.remoteAddress" official/dev -- lib/api2
  • On dev, lib/api2 no longer reads the connection's peer as the sender's address; notifications-v2.js uses clientIPFor(env). At e3354218 the same grep matches notifications-v2.js:34.
  • [static] git -C externals/cgm-remote-monitor-official merge-base --is-ancestor 71987bb4 official/dev
  • Containment: in dev through #8764 (into rt/trust-one-source), #8765 (into bf2/auth-hardening, 2026-09-25T01:26Z) and #8754 (into dev as 4f705217, 01:33Z). dev's tree is identical to 71987bb4's.
  • NO GATE — Tests, measured and recorded rather than re-run here: the branch worktree was removed after the merge. notifications-v2: 48 passing at 71987bb4 (43 at e3354218): the address Loop receives for TRUST_PROXY unset, 1, a proxy list and false, and through the real lib/api2 app. Break-it, each reverted: the peer address again -> 3 failing; lib/api2 not passing env -> the wiring test. On dev 4f705217: 2577/3/0 on Node 20.20.0, 22.22.0 and 24.15.0 against MongoDB 7.0.43, and in all nine CI jobs. The pre-merge run at 71987bb4 (2577) was on MongoDB 3.6.8, not MongoDB 7 as its commit message says.
  • NO GATE — Decided 2026-09-24 (maintainer): option 2 of the three recorded here - route the label through clientIPFor(env) so it follows TRUST_PROXY. Not chosen: (1) leave the proxy's address; (3) send a fixed label and no address. The accepted cost: the caregiver's public address is stored on remote overrides in the treatments collection, readable by anyone with read access, including anonymous visitors where AUTH_DEFAULT_ROLES grants reading. With TRUST_PROXY unset it is the forwarded-header address the caller sent (the endpoint requires notifications:loop:push). Loop decodes remote-address as a required String; the value is still a string whenever the request has a socket peer, as before.

Evidence.

  • reports/phase0-pr-bodies/rt-loop-remote-address.md
  • reports/phase0-pr-bodies/rt-trust-one-source-into-8754.md

Notes. 2026-10-21 - released in 15.0.9 (tag v15.0.9, master c6a0d8ed, the merge of #8598; tree c53c2c7f = dev 4bca2ac2). docs.text:

Blast radius. 15.0.9 is everything in origin/master..origin/dev: master 92d08342 (tag 15.0.8) to dev 7000eb18 (merge of #8786), measured 2026-09-27: 507 commits, 86 first-parent merges (all PR merges), 297 files, +28363/-1722. Among them the programme's backfix PRs (#8733-#8740 and #8743-#8746 from 2026-09-17 to 2026-09-21; #8748-#8753, #8755-#8757 and #8759 on 2026-09-23; #8760-#8762 and #8754 (with #8763 and #8765 folded in) on 2026-09-24; #8758 and #8766-#8770 on 2026-09-25; #8771-#8777, #8779, #8780, #8783 and #8784 on 2026-09-26; the test-only #8785 and #8786 (BF-147) on 2026-09-27), #8741, #8778 and #8781 from outside contributors on the same work, #8568, #8419 and #8530 carried by the 2026-09-25 decision, the D3 5.16 -> 7.9 chart migration (RT-D3), the opt-in debug logging change (#8726), the connector pin to exactly 0.1.0 (#8762), profile, treatment-query and clock fixes, report and chart fixes, dependency updates and translations. Crowdin #8730 is held out. The candidate is dev 7000eb18: RC run 020 ran on ce30a94d; #8785 changes only tests/boluswizardpreview.test.js, and #8786 changes two dependency overrides and nine locked versions (its own nine-cell CI; the production bundle is byte- identical). Reproduce with git -C externals/cgm-remote-monitor-official log --first-parent --oneline origin/master..origin/dev and git diff --shortstat origin/master origin/dev.

What an operator sees. Version 15.0.9 is the next Nightscout release. Nothing below reaches your site until 15.0.9 is released and your site is updated to it - if you run 15.0.8 today, every problem listed here is still present for you. ALARMS: the urgent "insulin reservoir change overdue" reminder could never appear and now can. If a feature name in your ENABLE setting (the list that switches features on) is misspelled or uses a file name instead of the feature's short name, Nightscout now warns you instead of silently leaving that feature off. The clock view now shows concern when a low reading is falling. These change whether an alarm or warning can appear, not the thresholds you set. BOLUS CALCULATOR QUICK PICKS: quick picks are saved food shortcuts in the Bolus Wizard (the calculator that suggests insulin for carbs). Picking one could load a different quick pick's foods or show foods meant to be hidden; that is corrected. The quick-pick list, which on 15.0.8 always showed (none), now shows your saved quick picks each time you open the Bolus Wizard; a food changed elsewhere while a page is open still appears only after that page reloads. TREATMENT DRAG: dragging a treatment into the "Move carbs" or "Move insulin" area to split it now stores the new time, so insulin on board and carbs on board follow the move. DATA SHOWN AND SEARCHED: many searches and counts that quietly returned nothing, or the wrong records, now return the right ones - for example filtering treatments by insulin, carbs, temporary basal rate or duration, and "records missing this field" searches. Profiles without a name and profile switches carrying their own schedule are handled correctly. Pages that read recent glucose values load faster. The carbs-on-board (COB) figure now uses the value reported by the system that uploads it (for example your phone app) when that system provides one, so the COB you see may differ from before. The main charts are rebuilt on a newer version of their drawing library, and several report and display fixes are included. SECURITY OF THE LIVE-UPDATE CONNECTION: the connection that pushes new readings and alarms to open pages had two gaps - recent device status could be sent to a page that had not signed in, and alarm messages went to every connected page. Both are closed, including on sites set to require sign-in. The "readable by world" warning also appears again in one setup where it had been hidden. CGM CONNECTOR: the built-in connector that fetches readings from CGM vendors' online services moves to version 0.1.0, which stops writing your CGM account's username, password, session tokens and readings into the server log, and stops a CareLink "no reading" marker being stored as a glucose value of 0. If Nightscout 15.0.8 fetches your readings from a CGM vendor's online service (for example with Dexcom Share or LibreLinkUp settings), treat that account's password as exposed: change it, and change it anywhere else you have used it. OLDER APPS: OpenAPS and GluPredKit keep reading data the way they did on 15.0.8, with a deprecation warning; badly formed record counts are refused with an error. DATABASE: MongoDB 4.4 still works and is still tested, but is deprecated; plan to upgrade. DEBUG LOGGING QUIETER: detailed debug logging is now off unless it is switched on (the DEBUG_LOGGING setting), so server logs are shorter; if you or a helper rely on those logs to diagnose problems, switch it on. This is not medical advice. If a change to alarms or to a number such as carbs on board affects how you manage diabetes, talk it through with your care team.

Why minor. GT4: cannot be a patch, for reasons INDEPENDENT of D3. lib/server/env.js gains DEBUG_LOGGING and CONNECT_DEBUG, debug logging flips to off by default (removing log lines an operator relies on when diagnosing), and a new API file lib/api2/loop-notification-errors.js appears.

Gates.

This rebuilds the candidate, origin/dev merged with the open 15.0.9 PR heads, and fails if any browser-side file, or any package outside a server-only list, differs from 8d797ba4. docs.title: RT-1 — Cut 1 - chore/retire-jsdom, PR #8828, merged to dev 2026-10-25 (16.0.0)
docs.text:
state (claimed) merged-upstream repo cgm-remote-monitor branch chore/retire-jsdom base official/dev@04d435eb worktree externals/cgm-remote-monitor-official semver major review maintainer plus a human reviewer; low blast radius is the reason it is second on the train, not a reason to skip review register BF-55, BF-58

Blast radius. At 806ff2f0 (#8828): 120 commits ahead of official/dev 04d435eb, 0 behind; the commit list is in RT-REBASE's notes. Before the catch-up merge, bce12ecc was 99 commits. Incremental production diff 11 files +68/-54 (GT2, 2026-09-15), not the 21 files +91/-123 the release-readiness §5 table publishes - that row was measured on a different basis from rows 2-5 and counts dev's own commits as deletions. Total 106 files, not 163.

What an operator sees. Planned as release 16.0.0. TWO THINGS TO CHECK BEFORE UPGRADING. First, it will refuse to start on older versions of Node (the program Nightscout runs on). You need Node 22.23.4 or newer within Node 22, Node 24.22.1 or newer within Node 24, or Node 26.12.1 or newer. Node 20 no longer works, and neither do Node 21, 23 or 25, nor the earlier releases of Node 22, 24 and 26 - the requirement is three ranges, not a single minimum. The official Docker image already carries a Node that meets it. If Nightscout stops starting after this upgrade, that is why. Second, the older built-in Dexcom Share and MiniMed CareLink bridges are removed; CGM data from those services comes in through Nightscout Connect instead. If old bridge settings are left in place, the site stops at a page naming the settings that work. Merged into the development branch is not released: nothing changes for a running site until 16.0.0 is released and installed.

Why major. GT4: the ENFORCED floor today is Node >=16 in bootevent.js, not the >=20 that engines declares - engines is not enforced on dev or master. Cut 1 introduces runtime-policy.js, which reads engines.node and calls process.exit(1). So the enforced floor jumps SIX majors, the declared range becomes ^22.12 || >=24 (decided 2026-09-21; in cut 1 since dfbb611b, the published bce12ecc declared ^22.23.2), excluding Node 21, 23 and 22.0-22.11, and the check becomes a hard exit. Cut 1 also removes the legacy Dexcom Share and MiniMed CareLink bridges and drops MongoDB 4.4 from CI. Maintainer 2026-10-21: the next release is 16.0.0 (RT-VERSION); 806ff2f0 declares it. 2026-10-25: AndyLow91's 6a146a4c ("require Node Brotli security patches", on the cut 1 branch before the merge) raises engines.node to ^22.23.4 || ^24.22.1 || >=26.12.1, a patch floor, superseding ^22.12 || >=24; it also excludes Node 25 and 26.0-26.12.0.

Gates.

  • [static] git -C externals/cgm-remote-monitor-official merge-base --is-ancestor 12154df9 official/dev
  • official/dev contains #8828's head 12154df9 (merged 2026-10-25 as eb72a1d3); red if dev is rewritten or the merge is reverted out of history
  • [static] NODE_FLOOR_REF=official/chore/retire-jsdom node tools/queue/gates/node-floor-consistency.js
  • "Trivially revertible - the engines field plus a boot check" is mechanically true and operationally misleading. Six other files state the floor independently (.nvmrc, bin/setup.sh, azuredeploy.json, README.md, CONTRIBUTING.md, docs/meta/architecture-overview.md). This gate checks they agree; a one-field revert would leave them stale.
  • NO GATE — Dockerfile is node:22-alpine on both dev and cut 1. Under the published bce12ecc's ^22.23.2 that was a floating major tag against a patch floor; under 806ff2f0's ^22.12 || >=24 the tag cannot resolve below the floor, and node-floor-consistency.js (above) now checks the tag against the range: 9/9 ok on 806ff2f0, red on bce12ecc. Nothing pulls or builds the image here.
  • NO GATE — 2026-10-21: ported under option C. 65248bed moves the 15.0.9 clock regression tests to tests/browser/clock-client.test.js (which on 806ff2f0 mentions concern and falling), fcd90f26 the D3 chart tests and 853b4145 the pill-title tests; the browser suite is 444/0 on Chromium 153 at 806ff2f0. No queue gate re-runs the browser suite. Earlier text, kept as the record: the clock-client concern/falling coverage is lost in the conflict resolution (RT-REBASE). Porting it to the Playwright suite is real work nobody has scheduled, and release-readiness §2 Option 1's "one CI run plus a cherry-pick of tests/browser/" undercosts it - cut 1 also deletes tests/dependency-d3.test.js, tests/fixtures/d3.js, tests/fixtures/d3-chart.js and tests/client.renderer.test.js, and its browser suite requires a playwright-core fixture and a module builder that dev does not have.

Evidence.

  • docs/60-research/modernization/gt2-cut-remeasure-2026-09-15.md
  • docs/60-research/modernization/gt4-semver-classification-2026-09-15.md

Notes. 2026-10-25: merged. AndyLow91 merged #8828 into dev at 16:29:06Z as eb72a1d3 (head 12154df9; gh pr view 8828). Between 806ff2f0 and the merge, AndyLow91 added to the branch 2c46e35b (runtime-upgrade guide connector version), 6a146a4c (engines.node ^22.23.4 || ^24.22.1 || >=26.12.1, "require Node Brotli security patches"), d49a81f7 (CI resolves the newest Node patch, check- latest), 32489dc5 (Dockerfile FROM node:24.22.1-alpine for builder and runtime, .nvmrc 24.22.1), the dev catch-up merge 43eb6066 (dev 1cae31e1, after the ten other 2026-10-25 merges), 36fa3121 (keeps a Node 22 x MongoDB 4.4 test cell as the existing required check "until branch protection is updated separately"; the matrix is otherwise MongoDB 5.0 and 6.0), 76c73056, 13507b38 (CI) and 12154df9 (a bounded Firefox month-report test). Test matrix on eb72a1d3: Node 22.23.4, 22, 24.22.1, 24, 26.12.1 and 26 x MongoDB 5.0 and 6.0, plus 22 x 4.4; browser tests on the same six Node versions x Chromium, Firefox and WebKit. CI on eb72a1d3: the pull_request run 40211897810 and the push run 40211895500 passed every test and browser cell; the push run's Publish to Docker Hub job succeeded, so dev's image is published. Not re-run locally on eb72a1d3. The node-floor-consistency gate below now reads 8/9 on chore/retire- jsdom 12154df9 and official/dev: it parses .nvmrc "24.22.1" as the majors 24, 22 and 1, so its one BAD line is the gate's parser, not a floor disagreement (every other file states 22, 24 or 26, and the Dockerfile is pinned to a patch). The gate is left as it is. #8823 also merged on its own the same day (4c1a5f1a, before #8828): on eb72a1d3 lib/server/bridge-connect-compat.js has one bridgeServerToConnect and is byte-identical to 806ff2f0's, and tests/bridge-connect-compat.test.js carries the BRIDGE_SERVER mapping describe block twice (lines 127-182 and 184-239, identical), so those cases run twice; no code is duplicated. The maintainer pushed chore/retire-jsdom as a fast-forward of official/chore/retire-jsdom bce12ecc -> 806ff2f0 and opened #8828 (chore/retire-jsdom -> dev, "Cut 1: retire jsdom, Node floor ^22.12 || >=24, retire the legacy Dexcom and MiniMed bridges (16.0.0)"). Decided the same day: cut 1 lands on dev now and the next release is 16.0.0 (RT-VERSION). RT-REBASE's cut 1 part is done (dev 04d435eb merged in as 4b617f78; 0 behind, 120 ahead), so RT-REBASE is removed from blocks_on. Tests on 806ff2f0: npm test 3224 passing / 3 pending / 0 failing (Node 24.20.0, MongoDB 7.0.43 in a container); browser suite Chromium 153 444/0. On 8c117dd4, before the last two commits: Node 22.12.0 3209/3/0, Firefox 155 444/0, test:core 286/0. WebKit did not launch on the host; #8828's CI run 39704672667 on 806ff2f0 reports Browser tests (22, webkit) and (24, webkit) as success, with all Run Tests cells (Node 22 and 24 x MongoDB 5 and 6) and the other browser cells passing, and the two Docker validation jobs still in progress when read. dev baseline on 04d435eb: 3569/4/0. Gates on official/: node-floor-consistency 9/9 ok (red on bce12ecc), connector-pin- exposure ok at v0.1.0 (bce12ecc pinned the v0.0.13 tag), cut 1 contains dev. #8823 ("Fix BRIDGE_SERVER=US/ous/URL mapping in bridge-connect compatibility", no queue item of its own) is folded into cut 1 as 42a2729e with its authorship kept; its 15 tests are unchanged and 7 of them fail with the fix reverted. It is closed in favour of #8828; the close comment is the maintainer's (#8823 still read OPEN at f75f9401 when measured). Follow-ups from cut 1, each its own item: RT-CONNECT-TEARDOWN (the redundant connector teardown listener in bootevent.js), BFQ-158 (the count=0 tests on a reused database). RT-JSDOM-REST and RT-D3-SUITE already wait on this item. 2026-10-21: 15.0.9 is released, so RT-0 is removed from blocks_on; cut 1 waits on its catch-up merge (RT-REBASE, in progress on wip/cut1-onto-15.0.10, not pushed). Cut 1 is first in the cycle's priorities (maintainer, 2026-10-21). Decided the same day: option C (port the D3, clock-client and pill-title coverage to tests/browser in cut 1, keep the jsdom harness for the rest, retire it later: RT-JSDOM-REST); the Node floor ^22.12 || >=24 (ed21961f) and the legacy bridge removal (c043fb2d) come into the merge; the connector teardown listener stays, its removal a follow- up. The clock-client no-gate below is the coverage option C ports. Blocked on 15.0.9 (RT-0) and the rebase (RT-REBASE). The published cut 1 (origin/chore/retire-jsdom bce12ecc) is 175 commits behind dev 153e5658 and conflicts in nine paths (RT-REBASE). docs.title: RT-3 — Cuts 3+5 combined - dependency release
docs.text:
state (claimed) merged-upstream repo cgm-remote-monitor branch chore/nightscout-modernization base chore/build-runtime-separation worktree externals/cgm-remote-monitor-official semver major review maintainer plus a human reviewer register BF-64, BF-88 blocks on RT-2

Blast radius. Cut 3: 63 commits, prod 23 files +294/-54 (MongoDB driver 7, jQuery UI). Cut 5: prod 36 files +397/-131 (Express 5, Helmet, EJS, Axios, Mocha 12, Swagger); of its 154 commits as §5 counted them, 95 are modernization work and 59 were dev's, pulled in by the merge 0a4109f6 (GT2, 2026-09-15). Cut 5's tip is b1bdaca0: an external contributor merged dev into it as e3b22034 ("Merge dev into modernization and reconcile regression coverage") and added two fixture commits, so it carries the Phase 0 PRs merged before 2026-09-21. Measured 2026-09-24 against origin/dev 153e5658: origin/chore/nightscout-modernization is 51 behind dev and 498 ahead, and its trial-merge into dev conflicts in nine paths (see RT-REBASE, which measures all five cuts). This item is PR #8605, declared in pr:.

What an operator sees. A dependency upgrade release. The database driver, the web framework and several libraries move to new major versions. You should see no difference in what Nightscout does. The bundled Docker setup moves from MongoDB 5.0 to 6.0; MongoDB 5.0, 6.0, 7.0 and 8.0 are all still tested, so no database version you are running today stops being supported.

Why major. Cut 3 alone is minor - GT4 verified the CI matrix runs 5.0.32, 6.0.27, 7.0.40 and 8.0.29, so NO tested server is lost; only the bundled docker-compose default moves. Cut 5 is classified major on dependency major bumps (Express 4->5, Helmet 4->8) and a 36-file production diff, NOT on a measured contract break. Combined, the release is major.

Gates.

  • [static] git -C externals/cgm-remote-monitor-official merge-base --is-ancestor a77cb146 official/dev

  • NO GATE — Express 4->5 and Helmet 4->8 are classified major on dependency version numbers and diff size, not on any measured contract break. Nobody has run a contract test against the route surface.
  • NO GATE — Combining cuts 3 and 5 skips cut 4 in the middle of a LINEAR stack. Cut 5 is a descendant of cut 4, so "3+5 without 4" is not a prefix and the parcel-as-prefix property the whole plan rests on does not hold for this step. Nobody has measured what that costs.
  • NO GATE — Retired 2026-10-26: the trial-merge gate (git merge-tree --write-tree origin/dev origin/chore/nightscout-modernization). Cut 5 is in dev (#8605, 47723cda), so the trial merge is clean and cannot go red for the reason it was written; the ancestry gate above replaces it.

docs.title: RT-4 — Deprecation release - folded into 15.0.9's release notes (maintainer, 2026-09-23)
docs.text:
state (claimed) released repo cgm-remote-monitor branch - base chore/nightscout-modernization worktree externals/cgm-remote-monitor-official semver minor review maintainer - this release exists to buy operators time before cut 4 blocks on RT-3

Blast radius. New code, not just a warning string. lib/server/mmconnect-connect-compat.js does NOT exist on dev or master - it is born in cut 4, the same branch that deletes lib/plugins/mmconnect.js.

What an operator sees. A warning release. If you get your CGM data through the built-in Dexcom Share or MiniMed CareLink connection, a future release removes both of them, and you will need to move to the nightscout-connect connector first. This release tells you whether that applies to you and what to change. If you use MiniMed CareLink you will also need to set your country, because Nightscout cannot work it out from your existing settings. Nothing stops working in this release. Your glucose data continuing to arrive is the thing at stake, so please do not skip this one.

Why minor. adds warnings and a migration shim; removes nothing

Gates.

  • [static] node tools/queue/gates/minimed-deprecation-path.js
  • FAILS while dev carries no named MiniMed escape hatch. GT4 measured the asymmetry: Dexcom HAS one - bridge-connect-compat.js is on master AND dev with five DEPRECATION WARNING lines, one naming DEXCOM_BRIDGE_USE_LEGACY. MiniMed's only warning today is a generic "PLEASE CONSIDER nightscout-connect instead." naming no setting.
  • NO GATE — Nobody knows how many operators run MMCONNECT_, or how many run BRIDGE_ and MMCONNECT_* together. Both populations are what decides how long this release has to sit before cut 4 follows it, and neither can be measured from here.

Evidence.

  • docs/60-research/modernization/gt4-semver-classification-2026-09-15.md

Notes. 2026-10-21 - released in 15.0.9 (tag v15.0.9, master c6a0d8ed, the merge of #8598; tree c53c2c7f = dev 4bca2ac2). Merged into dev by #8757 (d0d6b433, 2026-09-23): the MiniMed warning names every replacement setting (the names match the connector's extendedSettings keys). Not released. The notice itself is in the 15.0.9 release notes; the removal is on cut 1 (RT-1). The gate stays red by design: #8757 satisfies its warning half, and its other half checks for the migration shim, which ships with the removal on cut 1. Measured 2026-09-27: that move has not been made on any branch. lib/server/mmconnect- connect-compat.js exists only on cut 4 (official/chore/mime-exposure-review b80aa147), and lib/plugins/mmconnect.js is still present on the published cut 1 (official/chore/retire-jsdom bce12ecc) and on both local rehearsals, rt/cut1 and rh/cut1. Decisions: - 2026-09-23 (maintainer): no separate deprecation release. The notice goes in 15.0.9's release notes (MiniMed users: move to CONNECT_SOURCE with your CareLink country; Dexcom legacy-flag users: the escape hatch goes when the bridge is removed). - 2026-09-23 (maintainer): the legacy bridge removal moves onto cut 1 (relayed in -1f). The maintainer confirms (2026-09-22, operational knowledge) that legacy mmconnect does not work, and Dexcom BRIDGE_* settings have been served by nightscout-connect by default since 15.0.8 (a91e8ee4, with a deprecation warning and the DEXCOM_BRIDGE_USE_LEGACY escape hatch), so no working path is left for a separate release to protect. BF-44/BF-45 are graded low. The MiniMed shim is real code and ships with the removal.

docs.title: RT-5 — Cut 4 - chore/mime-exposure-review, the one to slow down on
docs.text:
state (claimed) merged-upstream repo cgm-remote-monitor branch chore/mime-exposure-review base chore/compose-mongodb6 worktree externals/cgm-remote-monitor-official semver major review maintainer, a human reviewer, AND a deliberate hold. Its own evidence document says "No real Dexcom account or live database has been used and no live migration is claimed." register BF-61, BF-62 blocks on RT-3

Blast radius. 79 commits, prod 66 files +324/-511. DELETES TWO CGM INGESTION PATHS (legacy Dexcom Share and MiniMed CareLink), trusted proxies, DOMPurify, Moment/tz. Caveat: the maintainer stated on 2026-09-21 that mmconnect has been broken for some time (operational knowledge, not measured here) and that legacy Dexcom Share is intended to map to nightscout-connect, so whether both deleted paths are working today is not established.

What an operator sees. READ THIS BEFORE UPGRADING. This release removes the built-in Dexcom Share and MiniMed CareLink connections. If you have not moved to the nightscout-connect connector, your glucose data stops arriving. If you use MiniMed CareLink and have not set a country, Nightscout will not start at all - not just the CGM part, the whole site, showing an error page instead. The same happens if you currently use Dexcom Share AND MiniMed CareLink together, which works today and does not after this release. If your data stops arriving you may not have a glucose reading when you expect one; please make sure you have another way to check your glucose before upgrading, and talk to your care team about what you rely on Nightscout for. This is not medical advice.

Why major. GT4 EXECUTED the shims. An MMCONNECT operator with no CONNECT_COUNTRY_CODE gets {migrated:false,error:...}; bootevent.js pushes it to ctx.bootErrors; app.js:202 then installs app.get('', bootErrorView) and returns, and server.js:61 returns before websocket setup. The WHOLE deployment serves the boot-error page - no API, no sockets, no charts. Separately, running BRIDGE_ and MMCONNECT_* together - two independent boot stages today - gets the same total outage, because there is now one CONNECT_SOURCE and the second source has nowhere to go. That is a capability removal (concurrent multi-source CGM ingestion) absent from every summary of the cut.

Gates.

  • [static] git -C externals/cgm-remote-monitor-official merge-base --is-ancestor 35fc8167 official/dev
  • official/dev contains #8847's head (cut 4) 35fc8167 (merged 2026-10-26 as e34efdef); red if dev is rewritten or the merge is reverted out of history
  • [static] node tools/queue/gates/cut4-total-outage.js
  • Decision A (2026-09-23): runs both legacy shims in bootevent.js order over six env shapes with the ENABLE rule modelled. FAILS unless every shape that stops the site names a fix, names no release number, and boots once that fix is applied as written. Ref from QUEUE_GATE_REF, default rh/cut1-retire-legacy (where the removal now lives).
  • NO GATE — "No real Dexcom account or live database has been used and no live migration is claimed" - the cut's own evidence document. No gate can substitute for a real migration, and nothing in this repository may use real credentials (rule 0).
  • NO GATE — Cut 4 deletes bridgeUseLegacy and the log line naming it, so DEXCOM_BRIDGE_USE_LEGACY becomes accepted-and-ignored. Credentials are still migrated so ingestion continues; only the operator's expressed intent is discarded silently. Nothing checks for accepted-and-ignored settings.
  • NO GATE — Retired 2026-10-26: the trial-merge gate (git merge-tree --write-tree origin/dev origin/chore/mime-exposure-review). Cut 4 is in dev (#8847, e34efdef), so the trial merge is clean and cannot go red for the reason it was written; the ancestry gate above replaces it.

Evidence.

  • docs/60-research/modernization/gt4-semver-classification-2026-09-15.md
  • docs/60-research/modernization/gt2-cut-remeasure-2026-09-15.md

Notes. 2026-10-26, 12:15:29Z: merged. AndyLow91 merged #8847 (cut 4, head 35fc8167, retargeted to dev after cut 3 merged) into dev as e34efdef (gh pr view 8847); 135 files, +5981/-1286 against its first parent 900abf7a. It carries BF-183's fix as 54115e95 (BFQ-183). With TRUST_PROXY unset, address resolution is 15.0.9's (BF-88; the PR body). CI: push run 40321153797 passed and published at 12:24:54Z; pull_request run 40321160053 passed. The legacy bridge removal this item was written for shipped in cut 1 (#8828). 2026-10-25: cut 2 merged (RT-2, #8837, dev eb44a9c2), so cuts 3-5 are next. Against dev b29f1bf7, official/chore/mime-exposure-review b80aa147 is 532 behind / 142 ahead with 35 conflicting paths, and cut 3 (compose-mongodb6 ebb690cf) 532 / 63 with 10 (RT- REBASE, measured 2026-10-25, 23:49Z); the catch-up merges are in progress in a peer session, not pushed. Last on the adopted train, after RT-3 (policy §8.3). The legacy bridge removal has moved to cut 1 (RT-1), so cut 4's remainder is trusted proxies, DOMPurify, Moment, MIME, webpack and ESLint; a trial merge of the rehearsal rh/cut4 into the lifted cut 1 conflicts only in legacy files and manifests. The published cut 4 is 175 commits behind dev 153e5658 with 22 conflicting paths (RT-REBASE, 2026-09-24). Decisions: - 2026-09-23 (maintainer): BF-61's hard stop is intended. MMCONNECT_* is usually the primary data source, so a misconfigured one shows the error page naming the fix. Under that decision the named fix must boot (CONNECT_COUNTRY_CODE alone does not, unless connect is in ENABLE), the messages must not name a release number, and cut4-total-outage.js passes only when each stopping shape names a fix that boots. All three are done on rh/cut1-retire-legacy c043fb2d, where the gate is green (it is red on rh/cut4). - 2026-09-23 (maintainer): deprecate and remove mmconnect as early as possible (it does not work and carries deprecated dependencies); RT-4's separate release is dropped. If a Connect migration misbehaves, the symptom is that a user's glucose data stops arriving: a data-availability failure for someone managing diabetes, which is why this cut is the one to slow down on.

docs.title: ID-SIMPLE-MATCH — API v1 entries and devicestatus match on identifier like treatments (the simple contract)
docs.text:
state (claimed) merged-upstream repo cgm-remote-monitor branch bf/16.0.0-null-removes base official/dev@47723cda worktree externals/work/crm-idmatch semver minor review maintainer - re-send behaviour clients see changes

Blast radius. Built as feat/v1-identifier-match 8d0f9a22; ships inside draft PR #8859 (bf/16.0.0-null-removes), the 16.0.0 re-send and merge PR. First scoped as one PR to dev with BF-169 (BFQ-169). lib/server/entries.js upsertQueryFor (301-319 at fade2299): match identifier first, as treatments do, then sysTime+type. lib/server/devicestatus.js create (92-172 at fade2299; insertMany unordered after #8758's withoutStoredIds at 57-90): a status whose identifier is already stored writes nothing and is answered with the stored _id (decided 2026-10-26; 8d0f9a22 replaces the stored status's fields, so the bundle changes it), the rest are inserted as today. Tests for both. No change to treatments, API v3 or the websocket.

What an operator sees. An app that labels each glucose reading or loop status with its own id can send it again without a second copy being stored.

Why minor. Versioning policy section 2, question 10: the same write stores a different set of records (a re-send that today adds a second entry or devicestatus becomes a match on the stored one). By rule R3 one minor row makes the release a minor, and 15.0.9 is decided as a patch (RT-VERSION, RT-COUNT-COMPAT), so it cannot go into 15.0.9.

Gates.

docs.title: RT-CONNECT-PIN-CUTS — BF-65 - cuts 1-3 ship the leaking connector to upgraders first
docs.text:
state (claimed) merged-upstream repo cgm-remote-monitor branch official/dev base official/master@c6a0d8ed worktree externals/cgm-remote-monitor-official semver patch review maintainer, plus the security reviewer who takes BFQ-CONNECTOR - it is the same disclosure, shipped by a different route ships to operators today no (pre-release) register BF-65 blocks on P0-TAG

Blast radius. One line of package.json on each of three cut tips.

What an operator sees. The first two releases on the planned upgrade path are presented as low-risk maintenance releases. As the branches stand, upgrading to either of them leaves you on the same version of the connector (the part of Nightscout that fetches readings from services such as Dexcom Share or LibreLinkUp) that writes your CGM account credentials and glucose readings into the server log. Moving each branch to the fixed version is a one-line change, and it should happen before those releases are cut.

Why patch. a dependency pin moves to a newer patch of the same package

Gates.

  • [static] sh tools/queue/gates/connector-pin-with-control.sh official/dev,official/master
  • Met when official/dev and official/master pin the released nightscout-connect 0.1.0 and the v15.0.8 tag, read beside them as the built-in bad control, is reported BAD (it pins the v0.0.13 tarball). Replaces the cut-tip gate, which refused to report once every cut merged with the 0.1.0 pin and all its refs agreed.
  • NO GATE — The pins are measured; the release ordering is quoted from release-readiness §5 and was not re-derived. So "ships the leaking connector to upgraders first" is an inference from combining the two, and nothing gates a claim about the order of releases. All three cuts pin the v0.0.13 tag, so the fix is the same one-line change as dev's.

Evidence.

  • docs/30-design/remedial/nightscout-backfix-register.md

Notes. 2026-10-27: merged-upstream. Cuts 1-3 merged into dev pinning nightscout- connect 0.1.0 (cut 3 #8844 on 2026-10-26); the five cut heads, dev 8dbb60c2, master and v15.0.9 all pin 0.1.0, and only v15.0.8 and old non-cut branches pin v0.0.13 (measured). The gate is re-pointed at dev and master with v15.0.8 as its bad control (6 checked, 2 failing, both v15.0.8's: met). Register BF-65 merged 2026-10-26. 2026-10-25: cut 2's part is met. #8837 merged as eb44a9c2 and official/chore/build-runtime-separation af7ba73a pins nightscout-connect v0.1.0. Gate on official/ (run 2026-10-25 after git fetch official, dev b29f1bf7): 8 checked, 1 failing - cut 3 official/chore/compose-mongodb6 ebb690cf still pins the v0.0.13 tag; cut 1, cut 2 and dev pin v0.1.0, and the axios override is inside the connector's range on all four. Cut 3 takes the pin at its catch-up merge (RT-REBASE). 2026-10-21: cut 1's part is met. official/chore/retire-jsdom 806ff2f0 (#8828) pins nightscout-connect v0.1.0 through the catch-up merge of dev 04d435eb; the published bce12ecc pinned the v0.0.13 tag. Gate on official/: 8 checked, 2 failing, both on cuts 2 (b6e8c7cd) and 3 (ebb690cf), which take the pin at their own catch-up merges (RT-REBASE). Open on the published cut tips, which still pin the v0.0.13 tag tarball. The fix exists to pin: nightscout-connect 0.1.0 (released 2026-09-24, P0-TAG), which origin/dev pins exactly since #8762. It is applied when the cuts are rebased onto dev (RT-REBASE); the rehearsal branches pin connector prereleases and move to exact 0.1.0 then. docs.title: RT-NODE-FLOOR-TESTED — BF-58, BF-59 - the enforced Node floor is not the Node anything exercises
docs.text:
state (claimed) merged-upstream repo cgm-remote-monitor branch official/dev base official/master@c6a0d8ed worktree externals/cgm-remote-monitor-official semver n/a review maintainer ships to operators today no (pre-release) register BF-58, BF-59

Blast radius. Dockerfile (builder and runtime FROM lines), the .github/workflows test-job matrix and package.json engines, on the cut tips. No production source.

What an operator sees. As the pushed modernization branches stand, Nightscout refuses to start on Node (the JavaScript runtime it runs on) older than 22.23.2 or 24.20.0 and exits immediately with a message. The container image those branches build uses the floating "node 22" image, which on 2026-09-21 resolved to Node 22.22.0 - below that minimum - so a container built from them starts, prints the message and stops. That looks like a crash and is not data loss. A wider minimum that the current image satisfies has been prepared but not published; see the notes. The release notes should name the message so you recognise it.

Why n/a. CI and image configuration. It changes no declared surface. The Node floor itself is classified on RT-1 and this item does not restate it.

Gates.

  • [static] NODE_FLOOR_REF=official/dev node tools/queue/gates/node-floor-tested.js
  • BF-59. The lowest Node engines permits (semver minVersion) is named on a node-version line of dev's .github/workflows/main.yml, and so is the newest major engines names (the floor-and-ceiling policy). On dev 8dbb60c2: 22.23.4 and 26, 3 checked, 0 failing. Red on cut 3's ebb690cf, where the matrix had dropped 22.23.2.
  • [static] NODE_FLOOR_REF=official/dev node tools/queue/gates/node-floor-consistency.js
  • BF-58. RT-1's instrument on dev: no floating Docker tag under a patch floor, and every file stating a floor agrees with engines. On dev 8dbb60c2: Dockerfile node:24.22.1-alpine, 9 checked, 0 failing. Red on bce12ecc (node:22-alpine under ^22.23.2).
  • NO GATE — Neither gate pulls or builds an image. Whether node:24.22.1-alpine starts the server is checked by CI's docker-build-pr and Validate Docker image jobs, not here.

Evidence.

  • docs/30-design/remedial/nightscout-backfix-register.md

Notes. 2026-10-27: merged-upstream. Every cut is on dev (cuts 2-5 merged 2026-10-26), so no published branch carries the old floor pair. The two origin/chore/ gates (and their controls) are replaced by gates on official/dev: node-floor- tested.js, new, for BF-59, and RT-1's node-floor-consistency.js for BF-58, measured on dev 8dbb60c2 with controls ebb690cf and bce12ecc. The default CI run tests Node 22.23.4 and 26; 24.22.1 and 26.12.1 run only in the extended matrix. 2026-10-25: cut 1 merged into dev (RT-1, eb72a1d3) with AndyLow91's 6a146a4c, which makes the floor a patch floor again: engines.node is ^22.23.4 || ^24.22.1 || >=26.12.1 ("require Node Brotli security patches"), superseding the decided ^22.12 || >=24. On eb72a1d3 the two findings do not arise: the Dockerfile pins node:24.22.1-alpine for builder and runtime (32489dc5), so no floating tag can resolve below the floor (BF-58), and the test and browser matrices include the exact floors 22.23.4, 24.22.1 and 26.12.1 beside 22, 24 and 26 (BF-59). The two gates below still read origin/chore/ refs and are left as they are; they measure the cut tips, and cuts 2-5 take the new floor at their catch-up merges (RT-REBASE, RT-2). The node-floor-consistency gate (RT-1) reads 8/9 on dev: its one BAD line is its own .nvmrc parser reading "24.22.1" as the majors 24, 22 and 1. 2026-10-21: cut 1's part is pushed. official/chore/retire-jsdom 806ff2f0 (#8828) declares ^22.12 || >=24 (dfbb611b, from ed21961f), its test and browser matrices are ['22','24'], and the Dockerfile stays node:22-alpine; node-floor-consistency.js with NODE_FLOOR_REF on 806ff2f0 is 9/9 ok (RT-1). What the two gates below mean has changed: they ask whether CI runs the exact patch floor 22.23.2 and 24.20.0, which matters only under a patch floor. Under the minor floor a floating major alias cannot resolve below 22.12, so cut 1 has no patch boundary for CI to guard (its main.yml says so), and the first gate, re-run 2026-10-21, still passes because it reads origin/chore/retire-jsdom, which is bce12ecc here; against 806ff2f0 the same grep exits 1. The exact floor was run by hand: Node 22.12.0 3209/3/0 on 8c117dd4. The second gate stays red on cut 3 ebb690cf, which, like cuts 2, 4 and 5, still enforces ^22.23.2 || ^24.20.0 and takes cut 1's floor at its catch-up merge (RT-REBASE); BF-58 and BF-59 stay open on those tips until then. The gates are left as they are; they should be rewritten (or this item narrowed to cuts 2-5) when the next cut is caught up. Open on the published cuts; a fix is prepared and not pushed. BF-58 (high): every pushed cut enforces ^22.23.2 || ^24.20.0 while its Dockerfile uses node:22-alpine, which on 2026-09-21 resolved to v22.22.0, so a container built from any pushed cut refuses to start. Pushing to dev or master fires main.yml's docker-build and publishes to Docker Hub, so merging a cut as it stands publishes the non-booting image rather than failing CI. BF-59 (low): from cut 3 onward the test matrix drops to ['22','24'], so a regression exactly at the floor would go uncaught; there is none today (cut 4's unit suite is 310/0 on 22.23.2 and 24.20.0). RT-1 carries BF-58 as a no-gate; this item is the work. Decisions: - 2026-09-21 (maintainer): engines.node becomes ^22.12 || >=24. Committed as ed21961f on rt/cut1 and merged up to rt/cut2 b5bf7d77, rt/cut3 c313f5b1, rt/cut4 95bb6295 (externals/work/crm-cuts), not pushed. Node 20 is left out deliberately: it works (310/0) but reached end of life 2026-04-30. >=24 admits odd and future majors deliberately, and tests/runtime-policy.test.js says so; prereleases stay out via semver's default. The Dockerfile is unchanged: under a minor floor the floating major tag is correct, as docs/runtime-upgrade.md describes. The defect is the floor, not the image tag. With runtime-policy.js stubbed to a no-op, cut 4's unit suite is 310 passing / 0 failing on 20.20.0, 22.12.0, 22.22.0, 22.23.2, 24.15.0 and 24.20.0, and cut 1's Playwright suite is 21/0 on Node 20.20.0. The only real break is 18.20.8, and it is not Nightscout's code: all 15 failures are ERR_REQUIRE_ESM from sanitize-html requiring the ESM-only htmlparser2; require(esm) is unflagged in 22.12 and backported to 20.19, exactly where the results flip. The dependency-derived floor is ^20.19 || ^22.12 || >=24. docs/runtime-upgrade.md (a95c2ce5, 2026-09-05) says the minimum patches "reflect the supported release baseline at the time of this change" (22.23.2 and 24.20.0 were 8 and 10 days old then) and that the image should track "the official major tag", which a patch-level floor makes impossible. Prepared fix, verified: runtime ACCEPTED inside node:22-alpine (v22.22.0); 18.20.8 and 20.20.0 refused, 22.12.0 / 22.22.0 / 24.15.0 / 24.20.0 accepted, confirmed by running lib/server/server.js on each; cut 4's suite including tests/runtime- policy.test.js is 332/0 at 22.12.0 and 24.20.0; widening engines to >=18 as an ablation takes the boundary test from 22 passing to 11 passing / 11 failing. The two gates measure the pushed origin/ branches, not rt/cut*. node-floor- consistency.js asks semver whether a major is permitted and gates the actual incompatibility (a floating major tag plus a patch floor inside that major); NODE_FLOOR_REF lets it measure a prepared branch. For any future run use n exec <version> <cmd>, not n install, which switches the machine default under other live sessions.

docs.title: RT-BOOTERROR — BF-63 - the page that reports a boot error crashes on cut 4's boot errors
docs.text:
state (claimed) gate-not-met repo cgm-remote-monitor branch - base origin/dev@a8888f0d worktree externals/cgm-remote-monitor-official semver patch review maintainer, and it should be reviewed WITH RT-5, because the message it destroys is that cut's mitigation ships to operators today no (pre-release) register BF-63

Blast radius. lib/server/booterror.js error-line map (one expression), plus lib/server/bootevent.js:330 and :335 on cut 4 - the only two bootErrors.push sites in the tree that omit err.

What an operator sees. When Nightscout cannot start it shows a page explaining why. For one shape of start-up error that page itself fails, so instead of the sentence telling you what to fix you get nothing at all. The error that triggers it is the one a MiniMed CareLink user hits on the planned release that removes the built-in CareLink connection - the message that would tell them to set their country. Losing that message is what makes this worth fixing before that release, not after.

Why patch. A crash fix in an error renderer. No declared surface moves. The call-site half on cut 4 is part of that cut's own classification.

Gates.

  • [static] node tools/queue/gates/booterror-shape-coverage.js --ref official/chore/mime-exposure-review
  • FAILS on cut 4: its booterror.js lacks dev's null-err guard (cut 4 is behind dev), and its bootevent.js has err-less push sites that produce the failing shape. Goes green when cut 4 carries the guard (a dev merge or rebase); the register asks for err at the call sites as well. The gate runs the map callback lifted from the ref's own file, with three control shapes that must render.
  • [static] node tools/queue/gates/booterror-shape-coverage.js --ref official/dev
  • PASSES: origin/dev's renderer shows a desc-only boot error instead of throwing (e6a50e9a, merged with #8753).
  • [static] node tools/queue/gates/booterror-shape-coverage.js --ref official/master >/dev/null && exit 1 || exit 0
  • CONTROL, PASSES because the gate FAILS on origin/master (15.0.8), whose renderer has no guard and throws on both err-less shapes. It shows the gate distinguishes a guarded renderer from an unguarded one.
  • NO GATE — Nothing renders the actual error.html template. The gate exercises the map that builds each error line, which is where the TypeError is thrown, but a full render needs EJS, express and a views path. The fix must be BOTH halves - pass err at both call sites AND make the renderer defensive - with a regression test asserting a desc-only boot error renders as HTML. Fixing only the call sites leaves the next caller to rediscover it.

docs.text:
state (claimed) merged-upstream repo cgm-remote-monitor branch feat/api3-domain-validation base official/dev@b29f1bf7 worktree externals/work/crm-v3validate-1600 semver minor review maintainer, and the AndroidAPS, Loop and Trio developers on the refusal shape

Blast radius. New lib/server/write-validation.js (pure rules); hooks in lib/server/treatments.js create (v1 batch: store valid items, refused slots in place), lib/api3/shared/operationTools.js validateDomain (v3 create, PUT, PATCH on the merged record), lib/api/treatments/index.js (400 mapping), lib/server/env.js (the setting). Default off: no behaviour change. Socket dbAdd/dbUpdate not covered.

What an operator sees. A new optional setting, WRITE_VALIDATION. Nothing changes unless you set it. With log, Nightscout stores temporary targets as today and writes a log line when one breaks a rule that holds for every app (for example a low target above the high target, or mg/dL numbers labelled mmol/L). With reject, it refuses such a temporary target; most apps that upload to Nightscout do not show you that refusal and lose the record, so reject is for operators who accept that. This is not medical advice; talk to your care team about how you set temporary targets.

Why minor. a new opt-in setting; default behaviour unchanged

Its red controls, reported by the lane: on dev's lib/ 12 of the first 20 fail (expected 400, got 201/200); all-or-nothing batches fail the mixed-batch case; leaving refusal objects out fails on the reply length Loop needs; the default set to reject fails the 5 default-off cases.

Notes. 2026-10-26, 10:23:14Z: merged. AndyLow91 merged #8841 (feat/api3-domain- validation, head 5901961c) into dev as e09bca3b (gh pr view 8841); 11 files, +918/-11 against its first parent 207a8352. His 5901961c ("validate effective Temporary Target updates") is on top of this item's commits e8125d89, 6e842c07 and a2e5fe49. WRITE_VALIDATION stays off by default. Open in the PR body: socket dbAdd and dbUpdate are not covered (draft #8854 extends the rules to socket add, update and unset), a refusal the person can see, whether to normalise units beyond temp targets, and the plausibility thresholds (30 mmol/L, 20 mg/dL). CI: push run 40307014804 passed and published at 10:32:31Z. Filed 2026-10-25 by session f4 from the v3-validation lane. Draft: local branch feat/api3-domain-validation a2e5fe49 (e8125d89, 6e842c07, a2e5fe49) over dev b29f1bf7; head 90fd47d0 after merging dev 428b20b7, not pushed. Decided 2026-10-25 (maintainer): D1 the setting shape; D2 a v1 batch under reject stores its valid items, keeps one object per item in order with refused slots without _id plus a refused member and a Warning 299 header, and answers 400 when every item is refused; D4 a double-labelled record is refused with a message naming the field and the units to send. Open: D5 (N1 or N2 and the conversion constant, MOD-UNITS-CANONICAL), D6 (thresholds 30 mmol/L and 20 mg/dL). docs.title: RT-PR-8815 — #8815 - a bearer token whose subject was deleted is refused instead of stopping the server (awss1i; BF-171, fixes #8225), merged for 15.0.9
docs.text:
state (claimed) released repo cgm-remote-monitor branch awss1i:wip/stale-token-crash base official/dev@fade2299 worktree - semver patch review maintainer ships to operators today yes register BF-171

Blast radius. lib/authorization/index.js resolve (+5/-2): a verified JWT counts as a login only when resolveAccessToken finds its subject; otherwise the existing failed- credential path. Plus three tests in tests/api.security.test.js and a CHANGELOG entry. Server-side only.

What an operator sees. If an app kept a sign-in token after that token's subject was deleted (for example you removed it on the admin page, or your database was reset), Nightscout could stop as soon as the app connected, and stop again after every restart, for up to 8 hours. That token is now refused like a wrong one, you see a "Failed authentication" notice, and Nightscout keeps running.

Why patch. A request that stopped the server now gets 401 (API v1, verifyauth, both sockets); no input that answers 2xx today changes, and the token already had no access. API v3 answers such a token 401 instead of 403, a status change on an already-refused request: the same kind of question as #8772's (policy section 9 table), for the maintainer.

Gates.

  • [static] git -C externals/cgm-remote-monitor-official merge-base --is-ancestor 93a74ce5 official/dev

On 93a74ce5 the same requests get 401 and the server stays up; API v3 401 (403 before). The PR's three tests copied onto fade2299 fail there and pass on 93a74ce5 (19 passing). Blast radius. lib/api3/storage/mongoCollection/modify.js replaceOne and updateOne (after writing the target by _id, remove the other stored forms of the same id), the cached wrapper in lib/api3/storage/mongoCachedCollection/index.js, and lib/api3/generic/{update,patch}/operation.js if the storage calls change; tests in tests/api3.delete-every-form.test.js or a sibling.

Gates.

  • Holds while v3 replaceOne/updateOne remove no other stored form (the helper the v1 writes use for it is staleStringForms). A presence check only, inverted: it goes RED when the merge lands and must then be replaced by a behaviour gate.
  • NO GATE — Behaviour needs a booted server and a MongoDB. Measured 2026-09-25 by the #8758 freeze review on ab7b22d6: v3 PATCH edits one copy and PUT replaces one, each leaving two records; on 63dd716c (BF-117 sort) both write the ObjectId copy (tests/api3.delete-every-form.test.js, PATCH in both storage orders) and still leave the string copy. Re-measured 2026-09-25 on origin/dev e3adc91d and 15.0.8 (mongod 7.0.43, both insertion orders): still open. v3 PATCH and PUT edit the ObjectId copy and leave n=2. Websocket dbUpdate edits both copies and leaves n=2 (15.0.8: ObjectId copy only, n=2). v1 PUT is the only write that merges (n=1 on e3adc91d, n=2 on 15.0.8). Evidence.

  • docs/30-design/remedial/nightscout-backfix-register.md
  • reports/consumer-impact-15.0.9/clients-8758.md

Notes. Follow-up to BF-117, queued 2026-09-25 at the maintainer's request. The v1 rule to match: treatments/food/activity/profile PUT upsert the ObjectId form, then delete the string forms of the same id (object-id-forms staleStringForms). For v3 the target is the document writeFilter picks (the v3 document with the identifier, else the ObjectId copy); the forms to remove are the other documents filterForOne matches that have no identifier. Decide whether PATCH, which sends only some fields, should merge too: the removed copy is the older one, so no newer field is lost, but a field present only on the string copy would be. Record every removal in v3 history (srvModified), or a follower keeps the removed copy. Until this lands, #8758's advice names the profile editor and the Reports treatment list as the way to merge a pair. The v3 PUT refusal on v1-born records without app is filed as BF-136 (BFQ-136, fixed in 15.0.9). Decisions: - 2026-09-26 (maintainer): after 15.0.9.

docs.title: UI-STALE-SECRET-HASH — A stale API secret hash stored in the browser blocks a valid ?token= link, and the dialog says only "Wrong API secret"
docs.text:
state (claimed) merged-upstream repo cgm-remote-monitor branch bf/16.0.0-stale-secret-hash base official/dev worktree externals/work/crm-stale-secret semver patch review maintainer

Blast radius. The browser's stored apisecrethash (localStorage) is sent with requests and takes precedence over a ?token= in the page URL; the client authorization code in lib/client (exact file to be located by the fix).

What an operator sees. A follower or caregiver opening a valid token link on a browser that once stored a different API secret sees "Wrong API secret" with no hint.

Why patch. client sign-in behaviour, no API change

Registered as BF-223 (BFQ-223). Choice: a refused saved secret is removed and the page retries with the link's token (or none) and says why; an accepted secret still wins over a token (existing contract test). Red on dev: 3 of 5 new tests in tests/browser/status-bootstrap.test.js; green with the fix; test:browser 684/0, test:unit 1883/0; break-it: reverting the two lib files fails exactly the 3. Blast radius. Fixed by 89d19b5b in #8838: the case's stand-in for the profile's zone is a UTC profile, plus two cases that run the report with the real lib/profilefunctions.js and a named zone. The defect was tests/glucosedistribution.test.js:116 on dev eb72a1d3, the case "includes the first selected interval when earlier hours are excluded", added by ba5f7f4b (AndyLow91, "test(reports): cover distribution counts and statistics"), the head commit of #8812 (cpruijsen, merged 2026-10-25 as bb56989c, issue 7659). Test code only, unless the failure turns out to be in the report.

What an operator sees. Nothing. No operator-visible change.

Why n/a. test only; the report applies the profile's time zone as intended (read- derived)

Gates.

  • [static] git -C externals/cgm-remote-monitor-official merge-base --is-ancestor 89d19b5b official/dev
  • official/dev contains 89d19b5b (BF-177's test fix; #8838, merged 2026-10-25 19:42:01Z as 2bc298b9); red if dev is rewritten or the merge is reverted out of history
  • NO GATE — Seen 2026-10-25 by the peer session preparing deps/16.0.0-security-refresh (Node 24.22.1, npm 11.19.1, MongoDB 7.0.43): npm test on dev eb72a1d3 is 3378 passing / 3 pending / 1 failing, the failure is this case ("expected '213.5' to be '117.5'"), and it passes with TZ=UTC and fails with TZ=America/Los_Angeles. GitHub CI runs in UTC, which is why CI is green. A gate would run this one file under a non-UTC TZ (it needs the checkout's node_modules, so it is not wired here).

Evidence.

  • docs/30-design/remedial/nightscout-backfix-register.md
  • releases/cgm-remote-monitor-16.0.0/contents.md

Notes. 2026-10-25: #8838 ("16.0.0 test and CI hygiene", chore/16.0.0-test-ci-hygiene, head 039be646, 10 commits on dev a20469dc) merged into dev at 19:42:01Z as 2bc298b9 (gh pr view 8838). Merged to dev, not released. 89d19b5b makes the case's stand-in a UTC profile and adds two cases that run the report with the real lib/profilefunctions.js and a named profile zone (America/Los_Angeles 213.5, Pacific/Auckland 249.5). The file passes, 8 cases, under TZ=UTC, America/Los_Angeles, Pacific/Auckland and Asia/Kolkata; with the old stand-in the original case fails in the three non-UTC zones, and with the report reading the hour in UTC both new cases fail in every zone (the PR's runs). America/Los_Angeles gives 213.5, the original failure's number, so the report was right and the test was wrong: verified by running it, which supersedes the read-derived claim below. Not covered: a profile with no time zone, where the report filters on the browser's zone, as before. Filed 2026-10-25 as BF-177 (register §1b) from the deps refresh's test runs (its branch fails the same case). Read: the test's stub applyTimezone returns moment(value) in the machine's zone, while the readings start at 00:00Z, so the selected hour 1 holds different readings in each zone; the report applies the profile's zone (lib/profilefunctions.js applyTimezone) and is not wrong in a non-UTC zone, read-derived and not run in a browser. The fix is test-only (UNVERIFIED): local-time readings or a fixed-zone stub, and the file run under two TZ values.
