docs.title: BFQ-176 — BF-176 - axios is only a devDependency and lodash is undeclared, so a production install of dev (16.0.0 line, cut 1 merged) stops at boot when IMPORT_CONFIG is set
docs.text:
state (claimed) merged-upstream repo cgm-remote-monitor branch bf/axios-runtime-dependency base official/dev@eb72a1d3 worktree externals/work/crm-axios-fix semver patch review maintainer ships to operators today no (pre-release) register BF-176

Blast radius. One commit 43ed462a on dev 04d435eb, package files and one test file only (+53/-2). package.json moves axios from devDependencies to dependencies at the same ^0.34.0 and declares lodash as exactly 4.18.1, the version its existing override pins (the overrides block is unchanged). package-lock.json: the two root entries, plus "dev": true on node_modules/@types/tough-cookie, which npm sets when it recomputes the lockfile (TypeScript declarations only; its one non-dev dependent is a peerDependency that legacy-peer-deps=true does not follow; cut 1's lockfile already has it). Five tests in tests/dependency- axios.test.js (+48). No runtime code changes. Full suite 3574/4/0 on Node 24.15.0 and MongoDB 7.0.43 (dev baseline 3569/4/0, plus the five tests).

What an operator sees. IMPORT_CONFIG is an optional setting that tells Nightscout to load extra settings from a web address when it starts. For about an hour and a quarter on 2026-10-25 the development branch (dev), and the dev Docker image published from it at 17:15 UTC, had a defect: a site that uses IMPORT_CONFIG and is installed the usual production way (the Docker image, Azure, or any install that leaves out development packages) stopped during startup with the message "Cannot find module 'axios'". The fix was merged into dev at 17:44 UTC, and the dev image published at 17:53 UTC has it. If you pulled the dev image in that window and use IMPORT_CONFIG, pull it again. No release was affected: 15.0.9 and earlier start and apply the imported settings normally, and the fix is not in any release yet (merged into dev is not released).

Why patch. Packaging only: axios moves from devDependencies to dependencies at the same version range and lodash is declared at the version already installed; no API, setting or stored-data shape changes. On 15.0.x the production tree already contains axios 0.34.0 and lodash 4.18.1 through other packages, so the installed runtime set does not change.

Gates.

  • [static] git -C externals/cgm-remote-monitor-official merge-base --is-ancestor f3d73f43 official/dev
  • official/dev contains #8834's head f3d73f43 (merged 2026-10-25 17:44:48Z as 93f152bd); red if dev is rewritten or the merge is reverted out of history
  • [static] RUNTIME_REQUIRES_REF=official/dev node tools/queue/gates/runtime-requires-declared.js
  • every package that server code loads (server.js, bin/*.js and lib/ except the browser-only lib/client, lib/report and lib/report_plugins) is declared under dependencies on official/dev, with webpack, webpack-dev-middleware and webpack-hot-middleware allowed only inside lib/server/app.js's NODE_ENV === 'development' block; red on v15.0.9, dev eb72a1d3 and cut 1 806ff2f0 (axios only a devDependency, lodash undeclared). On dev 2bc298b9, 41 checked, 0 failing (2026-10-25)
  • NO GATE — The boot itself is not a queue gate: it needs npm ci --omit=dev, MongoDB and a local config server (minutes). Run by hand 2026-10-22 on v15.0.9, cut 1 806ff2f0 and the fix branch 43ed462a, see the register's BF-176 detail. cut 2's tools/validate-pruned-runtime.js (d660e272's message) boots the pruned tree with IMPORT_CONFIG in cut 2's CI.

Evidence.

  • docs/30-design/remedial/nightscout-backfix-register.md

Notes. 2026-10-25: #8834 merged into dev at 17:44:48Z as 93f152bd (head f3d73f43; gh pr view 8834). dev no longer has the IMPORT_CONFIG boot crash. The window on dev was eb72a1d3 (16:29:06Z, the merge of #8828) to 93f152bd (17:44:48Z). dev's Docker image was published in that window: push run 40211895500 on eb72a1d3 ran Publish to Docker Hub at 17:14:58Z to 17:15:18Z, so the dev image published then carries the crash. Push run 40217943528 on 93f152bd published the next dev image at 17:53:06Z to 17:53:31Z. The push run on a20469dc (#8835) failed in two Firefox browser cells and skipped publishing; the push run on 2bc298b9 (#8838, run 40227267487) passed every cell and published the dev image at 19:48:15Z. Merged to dev, not released. The gate now reads official/dev; webpack joined its development-guard allowlist the same day for cut 2 (RT-2), and the control gained a stray require('webpack') outside the guard. 2026-10-25, 17:28Z: the maintainer pushed bf/axios-runtime-dependency f3d73f43 and opened #8834 ("axios and lodash are runtime dependencies (IMPORT_CONFIG boot crash on 16.0.0 dev)") against dev; open, checked with gh pr view 8834. 2026-10-25, later: measured by the BF-176 session (Node 24.22.1, npm 11.19.1, MongoDB 7.0.43). Crash confirmed on dev eb72a1d3: with IMPORT_CONFIG set, the Dockerfile's install commands and npm ci --omit=dev exit 1 with "Cannot find module 'axios'" at bootevent.js:114; unset, both boot; full npm ci with it set boots with the imported settings. bf/axios- runtime-dependency is now f3d73f43 (43ed462a plus a merge of dev eb72a1d3; 0 behind, 2 ahead, 3 files; not pushed), where every arm boots with the settings applied. Tests with TZ=UTC: branch 3384/3/0, dev 3379/3/0; tests/dependency- axios.test.js 30 passing, 4 failing with dev's package.json. runtime-requires- declared on dev: 41 checked, 2 failing (axios, lodash); on the branch 0 failing. The gate control gains dev eb72a1d3 as a negative (ee7a3cb49, merged into this records branch). The paragraph below said these were pending. 2026-10-25: the exposure moved from cut 1 only to dev and the 16.0.0 line. #8828 (cut 1) merged into dev as eb72a1d3 before this fix went to dev, so dev now carries the condition BF-176 predicted for cut 1: on eb72a1d3 package.json still lists axios ^0.34.0 only under devDependencies and declares no lodash (read with git show official/dev:package.json). No release carries it (ships_to_operators_today stays false; 15.0.9 boots, see below). dev's push CI run 40211895500 published the dev Docker image, so anyone running the dev image with IMPORT_CONFIG set is exposed. A peer session is confirming the boot failure on eb72a1d3 and merging dev into bf/axios-runtime-dependency; its measurements, the new branch head and the PR number are pending and are not recorded here. The state stays ready-to-push as a claim until that session reports. Filed 2026-10-22 from a colleague's read of package.json, then reproduced. The read hypothesis was that 15.0.x fails; it does not, because minimed-connect-to-nightscout depends on axios and npm hoists that 0.34.0 copy to node_modules/axios in every production install (npm ls axios --omit=dev). Cut 1 (RT-1, #8828, 806ff2f0) removes the MiniMed bridge, and its lockfile then marks node_modules/axios dev: true; with IMPORT_CONFIG set, npm ci --omit=dev and the Dockerfile's commands both exit 1 at augmentSettings. Register §1b, kind (b). lodash is covered by the same fix: lib/utils.js requires lodash/escape and lodash is not declared. It is supplied transitively today by node-cache, jsonwebtoken (through @parse/node-apn) and minimed- connect-to-nightscout on 15.0.9 and dev, and by node-cache and jsonwebtoken on cut 1 (read, and verified with npm ls lodash --omit=dev on both installs), so nothing fails today. Route (2026-10-22): a PR to dev from bf/axios-runtime- dependency, and #8828 takes it in its next catch-up merge of dev. The branch conflicts with 806ff2f0 in package.json and package-lock.json (git merge- tree); on cut 1 the resolution also drops the dev flag from node_modules/axios and node_modules/proxy-from-env in the lockfile. Proved on cut 1 by hand: with the axios move applied to 806ff2f0, npm ci --omit=dev plus IMPORT_CONFIG boots and applies the imported settings. Not pushed; PR body drafted outside the repository. Cut 2 already moves axios (d660e272, "axios is a runtime dependency, at dev's ^0.34.0"), found by its tools/validate-pruned-runtime.js. The widened gate on d660e272 still reports lodash undeclared and webpack a devDependency required inside the development guard of lib/server/app.js (:340); both are for cut 2's next catch-up, not for this item.

docs.title: BFQ-179 — BF-179 - postinstall runs webpack, now a devDependency, so a production install of dev fails (dev b29f1bf7, cut 2)
docs.text:
state (claimed) merged-upstream repo cgm-remote-monitor branch chore/compose-mongodb6 base official/dev@b29f1bf7 worktree externals/work/crm-bf179 semver patch review maintainer ships to operators today no (pre-release) register BF-179

Blast radius. package.json scripts.postinstall (:47 on dev b29f1bf7), and possibly the build and packaging path if the prebuilt bundle is shipped instead. Install-time only; no runtime code.

What an operator sees. Not in any release. On the development branch (dev), installing Nightscout without its development packages (for example with npm ci --omit=dev, npm install --production or NODE_ENV=production) fails with "webpack: not found", so the site cannot be installed that way. The official Docker image and the Azure deploy script install the development packages first and are not affected. 15.0.9 installs normally.

Why patch. packaging and install scripts only; no API, setting or stored-data change

Gates.

  • [static] git -C externals/cgm-remote-monitor-official merge-base --is-ancestor 200c1361 official/dev
  • official/dev contains BF-179's fix 200c1361 (merged 2026-10-26 as ad05e140); red if dev is rewritten or the merge is reverted out of history
  • NO GATE — Reproduced 2026-10-25 by hand (Node v22.23.4): npm ci --omit=dev on dev b29f1bf7 exits 127 "sh: 1: webpack: not found", on v15.0.9 c6a0d8ed exits 0 (control). A full install takes minutes and needs the network, so it is not a queue gate. A static gate would read official/dev's package.json and fail while postinstall runs webpack unguarded with webpack outside dependencies.

Evidence.

  • docs/30-design/remedial/nightscout-backfix-register.md

Notes. 2026-10-26, 10:59:10Z: merged with cut 3. AndyLow91 merged #8844 (head 0d54d072) into dev as ad05e140 (gh pr view 8844); his 0d54d072 ("Require every page bundle in prebuilt postinstall fallback") is on top of 200c1361. CI: push run 40311624772 passed and published at 11:09:23Z. BF-179 never reached a release; 15.0.9 builds its bundle on a production install. 2026-10-25: cherry- picked onto cut 3 as 200c1361 and in PR #8844 to dev (session -f8's cut 3, chore/compose-mongodb6, head 200c1361). 2026-10-25: fixed as 1cf70838 on local bf/179-omit-dev-install (one commit on dev b29f1bf7, not pushed); to be cherry-picked onto cut 3 by session -f8. postinstall runs bin/postinstall.js: build when the tools are installed, keep an existing bundle with a warning when they are not, otherwise exit 1 naming npm ci --include=dev then npm prune --omit=dev --ignore-scripts. Measured (lane): npm ci --omit=dev exits 1 with that message; npm ci builds the 16 bundle files byte-identical to dev's; docker build gives the same bundle. Decisions for the maintainer: keep- prebuilt vs always fail, and the 16.0.0 release-note line. The boot error with no bundle at all is BF-188. Filed 2026-10-25 by session f4 (register §1b, kind b: a defect in a release-train cut). Cut 2 (#8837) moved webpack to devDependencies; postinstall still runs it. Reach of the first-party Dockerfile and bin/azure-deploy.sh is read (they run npm ci --include=dev, then npm prune --omit=dev --ignore-scripts). docs.title: BFQ-180 — BF-180 - a careportal temp target on an mmol/L site is converted to mg/dL twice when the hidden BG field holds a value
docs.text:
state (claimed) merged-upstream repo cgm-remote-monitor branch bf/16.0.0-client-alarms base official/dev@b29f1bf7 worktree externals/work/crm-alarms-1600 semver patch review maintainer ships to operators today yes register BF-180

Blast radius. lib/client/careportal.js filterInputs (:145-161, clear #glucoseValue when the BG field is hidden) and/or lib/client-core/careportal/normalize-treatment.js (:66-70, label the converted targets mg/dl). Browser code, so a rebundle.

What an operator sees. If your Nightscout site shows glucose in mmol/L, a temporary target entered in the Careportal could be saved wrongly when a BG value had been typed into the form earlier: Nightscout stores the target in mg/dL numbers but labels it mmol/L, so the chart shows an impossibly high target (about 1785 for a 5.5 target). AndroidAPS ignores such a target without telling you, so the temporary target you set in Nightscout does not reach AndroidAPS. Until a fix is released, check that a temporary target you enter in Nightscout appears as expected in AndroidAPS, or set it in AndroidAPS directly.

Why patch. stored temp targets get their correct units; no API shape changes

Gates.

  • [static] git -C externals/cgm-remote-monitor-official merge-base --is-ancestor bb1ad38e official/dev
  • official/dev contains BF-180's fix (the careportal temp target converted once) bb1ad38e (merged 2026-10-26 as 85e5108a); red if dev is rewritten or the merge is reverted out of history
  • NO GATE — Reproduced 2026-10-25 through the real functions (careportal gather and normalisation, v1 prepareData, ddata) on dev b29f1bf7, not in a browser: typed 5.5/5.5 with a leftover glucose 6.1 is stored 99.09 labelled mmol and charted 1785.09. The fix branch has no commit yet; a gate would run that flow and assert the stored units are mg/dl or absent, with the leftover-glucose arm as the red control on b29f1bf7.

Evidence.

  • docs/30-design/remedial/nightscout-backfix-register.md

Notes. 2026-10-26, 10:33:08Z: merged. AndyLow91 merged #8842 (bf/16.0.0-client- alarms, head 148db86b) into dev as 85e5108a (gh pr view 8842); 16 files, +455/-28 against its first parent. CI: push run 40308300225 passed and published at 10:42:51Z. Merged is not released. 2026-10-25, later: fixed as bb1ad38e on local bf/16.0.0-client-alarms (head b7bf55e8 after merging dev 428b20b7, not pushed): the careportal clears the hidden glucose field and labels converted targets mg/dl. Reproduced in a real browser on dev b29f1bf7 and v15.0.9 c6a0d8ed (1785.09 charted). Severity set to medium in the register: silently ignored by AndroidAPS, charted far off-scale. Filed 2026-10-25 by session f4 from the BF-175 measurement. AndroidAPS (externals/AndroidAPS 7e1d537d) reads units mmol as mmol/L x18 and drops a temp target outside 72-180.16 mg/dL with a debug log only (NsIncomingDataProcessor.kt:172-179), read, not run. v15.0.9: same code by reading. Fix in progress on the alarms lane's local branch bf/16.0.0-client- alarms (not pushed). Also named in the drafted note to the AndroidAPS developers (with BF-152 and BF-164).

docs.title: BFQ-181 — BF-181 - one future srvModified pins the shared write clock ahead, across restarts
docs.text:
state (claimed) not-started repo cgm-remote-monitor branch - base official/dev@b29f1bf7 worktree - semver patch review maintainer ships to operators today yes register BF-181

Blast radius. lib/server/srv-dates.js next() and restore() (BF-144's a28fcecb, in v15.0.9): how far ahead of wall time a stored value may seed the clock, and what to do with an existing future-stamped record.

What an operator sees. Nightscout gives every saved record a "last changed" time from the server's clock, and apps that sync from Nightscout use those times to ask for what changed since they last looked. If one record in the database carries a time in the future (for example one saved by an older Nightscout version that accepted the time a phone sent), every later record is stamped just after that future time, even after a restart. What this does to syncing apps such as AndroidAPS has not been measured yet.

Why patch. server-side stamping only; no API shape changes

Gates.

  • NO GATE — Reproduced 2026-10-25 with a booted server and MongoDB 8.0.34 (dev b29f1bf7; v15.0.8 92d08342 for the stored value). A gate needs a booted server and a database seeded with a future srvModified, and the decided behaviour first.

Evidence.

  • docs/30-design/remedial/nightscout-backfix-register.md

Notes. Filed 2026-10-25 by session f4 from the BF-95 srvModified lane. +24 h injected: later writes 86,400,000 ms ahead, still after deleting the record and restarting. Upgrade arm: 15.0.8 stored a client-sent srvModified of 2100-01-01 verbatim; dev booted on it stamped new writes at 2100-01-01. Unmeasured: API v3 history cursors such as AndroidAPS's, treatments and devicestatus from 15.0.8, a 15.0.9 boot, a real clock step. No fix prescribed.

docs.title: BFQ-182 — BF-182 - on cut 3 (driver 7), boot against MongoDB 4.2 or older retries forever with no HTTP server
docs.text:
state (claimed) merged-upstream repo cgm-remote-monitor branch chore/compose-mongodb6 base official/chore/compose-mongodb6@ebb690cf worktree externals/cgm-remote-monitor-official semver major review maintainer ships to operators today no (pre-release) register BF-182

Blast radius. lib/storage/mongo-storage.js isRetryableConnectionError (:48 on ebb690cf and 72c156fb) and the boot error path: a driver refusal of the server version becomes a fatal boot error instead of a retry. Cut 3 only.

What an operator sees. Not in any release. A future Nightscout release with the newer MongoDB driver (cut 3) does not work with MongoDB 4.2 or older. As cut 3 stands, such a site keeps retrying the database connection forever: the website never comes up, uploads fail, followers see no data and server alarms do not run, and only the host's log says why. The fix in progress makes Nightscout stop with an error page that names the problem. Check your MongoDB version before upgrading to a release that includes this change.

Why major. driver 7 drops MongoDB servers older than 4.4 (cut 3's change); the fix only makes that refusal visible

Gates.

  • [static] git -C externals/cgm-remote-monitor-official merge-base --is-ancestor 8f238fc5 official/dev
  • official/dev contains BF-182's fix 8f238fc5 (merged 2026-10-26 as ad05e140); red if dev is rewritten or the merge is reverted out of history
  • [static] git -C externals/cgm-remote-monitor-official cat-file -e 99fa8b1e^{commit}
  • -f8's fix commit on wip/cut3-onto-16.0.0 exists in the shared clone; red if the local branch is lost before it is pushed (a rebase changes the id, and this gate must then name the new one)
  • NO GATE — The defect needs a MongoDB 4.2 container and driver 7: reproduced 2026-10-25 (init() on 72c156fb against 4.2.24 not resolved after 45 s; 4.4.24 connected in 28 ms; driver 5.9.2 against 4.2.24 connected in 32 ms). Not a queue gate.

Evidence.

  • docs/60-research/modernization/mongodb-server-compat-matrix-2026-10-25.md
  • docs/30-design/remedial/nightscout-backfix-register.md

Notes. 2026-10-26, 10:59:10Z: merged with cut 3 (#8844, merge ad05e140, head 0d54d072; gh pr view 8844). Driver 7 and its boot error page arrive in dev together, so dev never carried the endless retry. MongoDB 4.4 or newer is required to start (maintainer, 2026-10-25). 2026-10-25: fix 8f238fc5 in PR #8844 to dev (session -f8's cut 3, chore/compose-mongodb6, head 200c1361). 2026-10-25: the driver x server matrix is done (docs/60-research/modernization/mongodb-server-compat-matrix-2026-10-25.md): driver 7.7.0 refuses 3.6.23, 4.0.28 and 4.2.24; 4.4.24 to 8.0.34 boot and pass integration 2013/0/1; with the fix (7b636ce6 on wip/cut3-onto-16.0.0, the rebased form of 99fa8b1e) refused servers get the boot error page (HTTP 500 at 32 to 50 s, process alive, no retry). Decision (maintainer): driver 7 in 16.0.0, MongoDB 4.4 or newer required to start. Filed 2026-10-25 by session f4 from the defaults-calendar lane (C3-2; register §1b, kind b). The maintainer asked for confirmation that compatibility with MongoDB 3.6 to 4.4 holds; a driver x server matrix is running, and the entry claims only 4.2.24 and 4.4.24. -f8's cut 3 agent is adding a fatal boot-error path (99fa8b1e on wip/cut3-onto-16.0.0, local, not pushed, not checked by session f4).

What an operator sees. When an app connects to Nightscout's API v3 live-update channel with a wrong or expired access token, Nightscout writes that token into its server log. docs.title: BFQ-196 — BF-196 to BF-199 - API v1 error paths and the README's read window, found by PR #8858's route audit
docs.text:
state (claimed) not-started repo cgm-remote-monitor branch - base official/dev@c08cbe03 worktree - semver patch review maintainer ships to operators today yes register BF-196, BF-197, BF-198, BF-199

Blast radius. lib/api/notifications-api.js (install sendJSONStatus on the router), lib/api/entries/index.js echo_query (check the storage name), lib/api/profile, food and activity delete-by-id callbacks (answer the storage error), and one README sentence. Server-side and documentation only; one themed PR.

What an operator sees. Small corrections to how Nightscout's older API (v1) answers some mistakes: an app without permission to acknowledge an alarm is told "unauthorized" instead of getting a server error, a mistyped debug address gets "not found", and deleting a profile, food or activity record reports a database failure instead of reporting success. The README's description of how many days a read covers is corrected from two to four. Nothing that works today changes.

Why patch. error answers become accurate status codes; no successful response changes shape

Gates.

  • NO GATE — Reproduced 2026-10-26 on the PR #8858 branch d46ef808 by its route audit (325 requests per run, held outside the repository): notifications/ack without a credential -> 500, echo/notastore -> 500, the echo query's $gte at now - 345600000 ms. BF-198 is read. A test per route would assert 401, 404 and a non-200 on a storage fault; control: c08cbe03 fails each.

Evidence.

  • docs/30-design/remedial/nightscout-backfix-register.md

Notes. Filed 2026-10-26 by session -b7 from the route audit behind PR #8858 (API documents for 16.0.0), which documents each behaviour as it is. All four read on v15.0.9 c6a0d8ed. Bundle into one PR, or add to an open API v1 fixes PR of the same theme.

docs.title: BFQ-184 — BF-184 - API v3 /status apiPermissions reports only wildcard permissions
docs.text:
state (claimed) not-started repo cgm-remote-monitor branch - base official/dev@b29f1bf7 worktree - semver patch review maintainer ships to operators today yes register BF-184

Blast radius. lib/api3/specific/status.js: the for...in loop over the collections map (:43) passes keys where permsForCol reads col.colName (:17-31). One function, server-side.

What an operator sees. Apps can ask Nightscout's API v3 which collections their access token may read or change. The answer is wrong for tokens limited to particular collections: such a token is reported as having no access at all, although its requests work. Tokens with full access are reported correctly. Nothing about what a token can actually do changes.

A pool-membership table in PostgreSQL holds one heartbeat row per member (ordinal, expected members, ring slice, lease expiry). A member evaluates its slice only while every live row agrees on the member count and no two live rows share an ordinal; otherwise it stops its own cycle and alerts. No per-tenant lock; duplicate evaluation is bounded to one heartbeat interval after a membership change and the evaluator's outputs are idempotent by contract. A read-only private operational module must expose configured mode/count/ordinal/rule/slice separately from observed membership, heartbeat freshness/conflicts, eligibility and actual workload progress. BF2-AUTH — bf2/auth-hardening - bf/auth + bf/throttle + the client-ip.js backport behind TRUST_PROXY state (claimed) released repo cgm-remote-monitor branch bf2/auth-hardening base origin/dev@74fc6619 worktree externals/work/crm-bf2-auth semver major review SECURITY - the maintainer and Andy (decided 2026-09-23). Blast radius. #8754 head 708af170 (2026-09-24, with #8763) against dev 153e5658: 30 commits, 22 files, +2120/-101; with the pending #8764 follow-up, 25 files, +2167/-105. lib/authorization/{index,delaylist,storage,endpoints}.js; lib/server/{client- ip,env,app,websocket}.js; lib/api/status.js; lib/api3/{security,alarmSocket,storageSocket}.js; package.json and lock (proxy-addr declared, forwarded-for kept); README.md and docs/proposals/trusted-proxy-migration.md; tests authdelay, authsubjects, client-ip, env and server.security-headers. Measured with the GitHub compare API.

What an operator sees. Not released. This combines several login and access fixes planned for 15.0.9. Editing a subject (an access entry on the admin page) no longer writes that subject's access token into your database in readable form; tokens already written that way stay until you act (see P0-C-REMEDIATE for what to do). Editing a subject on the admin page no longer wipes its notes or its creation date. After a failed login, Nightscout still makes the next request from that address wait before it checks the password, as earlier releases do; the wait now also follows the password or token that failed, and the list of recent failures is bounded and cleared on a schedule. A new setting, TRUST_PROXY, tells Nightscout which proxy in front of it to trust, so that the address it counts failed logins against is one a visitor cannot make up; explicit TRUST_PROXY settings accept forwarded addresses that carry a port (the form Azure App Service is reported to send). If you change nothing, Nightscout works out visitor addresses as it does today, and it says in its log at startup that the protection against password guessing is weaker until TRUST_PROXY is set. None of this is medical advice.

Why major. Inherits P0-C's major (the BF-47 allow-list), unless the maintainer's BF-47 decision puts that behind a compatibility flag, which would make this minor (a new setting, today's behaviour by default).

Before #8763: It carries dev 153e5658 (merged in by e32f7a1c); f6f361b1, which puts the failed-login wait back before the credential check, as in earlier releases; 9c6cde72 (an explicit TRUST_PROXY accepts a forwarded address that carries a port, the form Azure App Service is reported to send; unset is unchanged); b5f61f19 (the proxy guide recommends 1 on Azure); and e549e1a6 (an API v3 failed-login key test through the trust its app inherits). Full suite 2570/3/0 at e549e1a6 (session -66); CI green on b5f61f19. That fix is part of #8754 and 15.0.9. Destination 15.0.9 (backfix-2 plan section 1a, 2026-09-23). Owed before merge: the security review and a combined run on #8754's head once #8764's follow-up is merged; the latest combined run (rc-15.0.9-combined-010, 3046/0/3) used #8754 at ef3404fd. What it carries: bf/auth (BF-17, P0-C) and bf/throttle (BF-30, P0-J) by ancestry; the client-address module and TRUST_PROXY setting cherry-picked (-x) from chore/nightscout-modernization (06c83f2f, 395f3207), with 8b975b41 a port so that with TRUST_PROXY unset the address comes from forwarded-for exactly as on dev (395f3207's default differs in four cases, BF-88); the subject-edit fix 7103f657 (BFQ-47) as its last content commit. The failed-login delay: the wait comes before the check, as in earlier releases; failures are also counted per credential; the list is bounded and swept on a schedule. The throttle keys on data.ip, which comes from client-ip.js, so one setting governs both. BF-30 is closed only when TRUST_PROXY names a boundary; with the default it remains open, and the branch says so in its boot message and PR body. Semver stays major for BF-47 (a compatibility flag, sketched in the PR body, would make it minor; the maintainer decided none). Contributor-facing. Status 2026-10-02: every file under this directory is a DRAFT. Nothing here has been tagged or published.

This directory holds the tag messages, release notes and contents records for releases of cgm-remote-monitor and nightscout-connect, one directory per release.

Directory Describes Status cgm-remote-monitor-15.0.9/ official/master..official/dev at 4bca2ac2 (100 merged PRs); released 2026-10-21 as tag v15.0.9, master c6a0d8ed released; release-notes.md is the GitHub release body; connector pinned exactly to the released 0.1.0 (#8762); what remains is in ROADMAP §1; how it was made: colophon cgm-remote-monitor-16.0.0/ official/master..official/dev, at eed31dca on 2026-10-27 (42 merged PRs, all five cuts among them); the next release (maintainer, 2026-10-21) in development: contents, decisions and the integration record are living; the verification record's selection is set (captured at the tag); testing notes, tag message and release notes are written once a candidate is named nightscout-connect-v0.0.14/ the retired local tag v0.0.14 (649a7de) superseded: no 0.0.14 will be published; the line is 0.1.0 (queue P0-TAG) _template/ copy to start a new release directory —

docs.title: Why these files live here
docs.text:
The maintainer's rule (2026-09-15):

CHANGELOG.md is a release OUTPUT, generated by GitHub tooling between releases. Branches must never hand-edit it.

So a branch carries code and a commit message. Three artefacts then need a home until the release is cut: the annotated tag body, the user-facing release notes, and the record of what is in the release. This directory is that home.

These drafts complement the generated changelog; they do not replace it. The generated changelog is authoritative for what merged. The notes carry what a generated list cannot: what a user will notice, what they must do, what to check afterwards, and what is still broken. At release time the two are reconciled — see Reconciliation at release time.

docs.title: Open item: CHANGELOG on dev
docs.text: cgm-remote-monitor dev carries a hand-written ## [Unreleased] section in CHANGELOG.md (71 lines added since 15.0.8, from 12 commits by upstream contributors, measured with git log official/master..official/dev -- CHANGELOG.md). That is in tension with the rule above. The maintainer needs to decide whether the rule stands (and the section is replaced by the generated changelog at release time) or whether contributor-written entries are accepted, in which case the reconciliation below must also diff against that section.

docs.title: Convention
docs.text:
releases/
  <product>-<version>/
    tag-message.txt     the annotated tag body, git convention: short subject,
                        blank line, body. Plain text. No markdown headers.
                        Contributor-facing; may be terse and fully technical.
    release-notes.md    the user-facing draft. Plain language, every term
                        defined, every safety caveat preserved. See "Audience".
    contents.md         which PRs and register entries make up the release;
                        the semver facts; what is unsettled.
    decisions.md        optional; the maintainer's decisions that shape the
                        release, each stated as it stands.
    testing-notes.md    optional; the call for testers of a release candidate.
                        Part 1 user-facing (plain language), part 2 for
                        operators and tool authors. Living until the tag.
    verification-record.{json,md}   optional; see VERIFICATION-RECORDS.md
    verification-selection.txt      the queue ids the record is captured over,
                        and the capture command
  _template/            copy this to start a new release directory

Directory names use the product's own version spelling: cgm-remote-monitor-15.0.9 (no v, matching package.json), nightscout-connect-v0.0.14 (with v, matching the tag). The tag keeps the repository's existing convention: cgm-remote-monitor has both spellings (15.0.8 and v15.0.8, lightweight tags on the same commit 92d08342); connector tags are v0.0.13.

docs.title: Audience
docs.text:
File Audience Rules tag-message.txt contributors, maintainers, anyone reading git show <tag> full technical depth; terse is fine; name commits by SHA contents.md maintainers and reviewers full technical depth; every figure says how it was measured release-notes.md people managing their own or a family member's diabetes plain language; define every term; preserve every safety caveat; never simplify algorithm or alarm behaviour in a way that could mislead someone relying on it; no individualised insulin dosing advice; say that Nightscout is not a medical device and this is not medical advice; point to the care team where a change could touch therapy decisions; describe any defect still live on a shipped release by effect only

These rules are docs/30-design/modernization/semver-and-release-versioning-policy-2026-09-15.md §5.6; §3.3 of the same document gives the worked example ("Your reservoir alarm now works" is not an adequate note, because it does not say that a new alert arrives, when, at what level, and how to turn it off). All drafts here must also meet docs/00-overview/DEFINITION-OF-DONE.md criterion 10.

docs.title: Version numbers here are proposals
docs.text: 15.0.9 is decided (RT-D3 answered; nightscout-connect 0.1.0 released 2026-09-24, P0-TAG). Every other number in this directory is a proposal. The analysis behind them is docs/60-research/modernization/gt4-semver-classification-2026-09-15.md (classification) and the versioning policy above. Both are drafts awaiting maintainer adoption. The directory name is the planned number; each contents.md states the facts that bear on the number.

docs.title: Reserved slots for releases whose numbers are not settled
docs.text:
The modernization parcels have no agreed numbers. When each is cut, create its directory with the number the maintainer chooses. Until then these are named placeholders, not versions:

Placeholder Contents Policy's proposed number (§8.3) — not adopted DEPRECATION_RELEASE MiniMed shim shipped non-fatally, Dexcom escape hatch preserved, ?count=0 warned rather than rejected, subject allow-list warned 15.2.0 RUNTIME_RELEASE parcel 1 chore/retire-jsdom — Node floor, MongoDB 4.4 out of CI, jsdom to Playwright 16.0.0 BUILD_RELEASE parcel 2 chore/build-runtime-separation 16.1.0 DEPENDENCY_RELEASE parcels 3 + 5 17.0.0 INGESTION_RETIREMENT_RELEASE parcel 4 chore/mime-exposure-review — legacy Dexcom and MiniMed retirement 18.0.0

Note that ?count=0 rejection (#8738) is already merged to dev and therefore ships in 15.0.9 unless reverted; the DEPRECATION_RELEASE row was written before that merge. The maintainer reports that the legacy MiniMed path (mmconnect) has been broken for some time and that legacy Dexcom Share is intended to map to nightscout-connect; the ingestion-retirement risk grading has not been redone on that basis.

Two constraints hold whatever numbering is chosen:

  1. Parcel 4 is contained in parcel 5. Measured with git merge-base --is-ancestor across all consecutive pairs: the parcels are linear, each contained in the next, so "ship 5 but hold 4 back" is not achievable as a merge.
  2. The runtime break and the ingestion break must not be in the same release. An operator debugging a site that will not start should not simultaneously be debugging why their glucose data stopped.

docs.title: Reconciliation at release time
docs.text:
Before a release is published, someone does this and records that they did:

  1. Generate the changelog with the GitHub tooling, from what actually merged.
  2. Diff the generated list against contents.md. Anything in the generated list that contents.md does not name either merged after the notes were written or was never reviewed. Both are worth knowing before publishing.
  3. Re-read release-notes.md against the generated list. Every behaviour change in the generated list needs a line in the notes or a written reason it does not.
  4. Check every version number against the number actually being cut.
  5. Check the register (docs/30-design/remedial/nightscout-backfix-register.md) for entries whose status moved since the draft was written, and for entries the release leaves open that the notes should name under "Known issues". Anything still live on the previous release is described by effect only.
  6. Check the commit messages that feed the generated changelog for claims the register has corrected.
  7. Re-cut the annotated tag from tag-message.txt if the text changed. A tag other people have already fetched is superseded, never moved.

docs.title: Nothing in this directory ships anything
docs.text:
Writing a file here is not a release. A release is three separate human decisions:

# Decision Reversible? 1 Merge the code — a PR merge into dev (and the release PR into master) yes, git revert 2 Push the tag — the tarball becomes downloadable effectively no 3 Publish the package — npm publish no

They are set out in docs/30-design/remedial/maintainer-release-brief-2026-09-15.md §2, with the commands a human runs. For nightscout-connect, decision 2, not decision 3, delivers the fix, because every cgm-remote-monitor pin is a GitHub tarball URL and none resolves from npm. For cgm-remote-monitor, a push to dev or master triggers a Docker image publish and is itself a publication event.

Drafts. Require maintainer review before anything is tagged, published or relied upon. Nightscout is not a medical device and nothing in this directory is medical advice.

It is superseded: 15.0.9 is now official/master..official/dev 74fc6619 (see cgm-remote-monitor-15.0.9/contents.md), and no record of that tree has been captured. --check --from-json on it reports DRIFT for the .md: the Markdown was edited by hand after capture (a bf/coercion SHA footnote), contrary to invariant 3, and now also carries a one-line superseded notice. The JSON still matches its own render. A new capture needs a selection that describes the merged release, which --parcel phase0 no longer does, and runs unit gates in the external worktrees.

Audience: contributors and maintainers. This file is fully technical. The operator-facing half of a release is release-notes.md, not this.

docs.title: What a verification record is
docs.text:
The quality-system record of what was actually checked when a release was cut — and, just as much, of what was not.

It is not a plan, not a changelog and not a claim. For every item in the release it carries the branch and the commit SHA that item resolved to, every gate and what that gate actually said when it was run, the register entries the release touches with each entry's basis, the test commands with their output summaries, and a mandatory section naming what was not verified and why.

releases/<product>-<version>/
  verification-record.json    the record. Machine-readable, the source of truth.
  verification-record.md      generated FROM the json by the generator. Never hand-written.

Generator: tools/queue/verification-record.py, the seventh tool under tools/queue/, beside manifest.py, validate.py, emit.py, status.py and vacuity.py. It reuses status.py's gate executor rather than reimplementing it, so a gate result in a record is the same measurement make queue-status prints, not a second implementation free to drift from it.

docs.title: Why it exists
docs.text:
Three properties of this programme that prose cannot hold:

  1. Rule 3 — read-derived versus reproduced. A read-derived claim is a hypothesis; a reproduced one is evidence. So the record classifies every register entry it carries by basis, and where an entry's status cell does not say, the record prints unstated rather than guessing. It will not infer a reproduction from measurement-shaped prose: inferring one is exactly the laundering rule 3 exists to stop.
  2. The claimed state and the measured state are different things. Every item prints both — state (claimed) from the manifest and verdict (measured) from running the gates — and every disagreement between them is enumerated in the gaps section.
  3. A gate that was skipped is not a gate that passed. SKIP, NO-GATE and FAIL are three distinct outcomes and none of them renders as a pass anywhere in either half.

docs.title: When it is captured, and the rule that it is never edited
docs.text:
A record is captured once, at release time, from the state that is actually being cut.

A verification record is never edited after it is captured. If something changes — a gate starts passing, a branch moves, a register entry is upgraded from read-derived to reproduced, a gap is closed — that is a new record with a new captured_at, not an edit to the old one.

A record that is edited after the fact is not a record. It is a claim about the past that nothing can check, and it is strictly worse than no record at all, because it reads like evidence. Both files carry that rule in a header comment. If a record has ever been shared outside this machine, it is superseded by the new one, never overwritten — the same rule this repository applies to a tag other people have already fetched.

The captured_at timestamp is passed in as an argument. Nothing in the generator calls a clock. That is what lets a record be re-derived and diffed instead of trusted.

docs.title: Capturing one
docs.text:
python3 tools/queue/verification-record.py \
    --release cgm-remote-monitor-15.0.9 \
    --captured-at "$(date +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%S%:z)" \
    --parcel phase0 \
    --out-dir releases/cgm-remote-monitor-15.0.9

Selection is by --id, --parcel or --state. By default only static and unit gates are run; --integration and --network opt the other kinds in, and whichever kinds were not run are named in the record's own header and in its gaps section. The default is deliberately the conservative one: on the capture machine (2026-09-15) most integration gates could not run, because the worktree mongod ports did not match their configuration.

Verify an existing record, and prove the Markdown really came from the JSON:

python3 tools/queue/verification-record.py --check --from-json <record.json>

docs.title: The three invariants the generator enforces
docs.text:
# Invariant How it is enforced 1 The gaps section may not be empty if not_verified is empty the generator writes nothing and exits 2. There is no override flag, because the flag would be used. 2 The timestamp comes from outside --captured-at is required; the file never reads a clock. 3 The Markdown is generated from the JSON render() takes the record dict and nothing else; --check re-renders and diffs.

Invariants 1 and 3 are proven by execution, not by inspection — see below.

docs.title: Rule 2: the generator is proven non-vacuous
docs.text:
A check that has never failed is not yet evidence. --self-test takes the real manifest, finds an item in the selection whose gates all pass, writes a copy of the manifest with one of that item's gates replaced by exit 7, captures a second record from the copy, and asserts six things about it. Nothing is written to the real manifest or the real release directory.

python3 tools/queue/verification-record.py --self-test \
    --captured-at 2026-09-15T23:55:00-07:00 --parcel phase0

Reproduced, 2026-09-15:

BEFORE  P0-B  verdict=PASS  gates 2/2
        gates[0] PASS  git -C externals/... merge-base --is-ancestor origin/dev bf/cache
        register: BF-06=claimed-fixed-gates-pass, BF-07=claimed-fixed-gates-pass
AFTER   P0-B  verdict=FAIL  gates 1/2
        gates[0] FAIL  exit 7
        output tail: ABLATION: this gate is broken on purpose
        register: BF-06=claimed-fixed-but-a-gate-failed, BF-07=claimed-fixed-but-a-gate-failed
  OK   item verdict moved PASS -> FAIL
  OK   the broken gate is recorded as FAIL
  OK   the failing command's own output is in the record
  OK   the Markdown shows the failure, not a pass
  OK   register entries moved off claimed-fixed-gates-pass
  OK   the gaps section grew

The failure reaches all four places it must: the gate, the item verdict, the register closure state of both entries that item carries, and the gaps section — and the injected command's own stderr is quoted in the record, so the failure cannot be mistaken for a different one. Invariant 1 was ablated separately: a record whose not_verified array was emptied by hand is refused with exit 2 and no file is written.

docs.title: How far two captures can be diffed
docs.text:
Two captures of this release were diffed field by field. Stable: resolved SHAs, commits-ahead counts, every gate outcome, every item verdict, every register closure state and basis, the counted test summaries, and all 76 gap entries. Moves: the gate transcripts output_tail, output_bytes and output_sha256 (25 of 164 transcript fields), because the commands are not deterministic — mocha prints its own millisecond timings and node prints its pid.

One field that is a conclusion rather than a transcript moves with them: output_summary.last_line, for a gate whose last line of output is a benchmark duration. So diff two captures on outcomes, verdicts, bases and gaps. Do not diff them on digests, or on a last_line that quotes a duration. The digest is there to let a reader bind a full log they hold to this capture, not to let two captures be compared byte for byte.

docs.title: Changes
docs.text:
2026-10-27, from the 16.0.0 dry run. Each was reproduced on the 16.0.0 selection, --self-test passes with --parcel phase0 and with --id BFQ-177 --id BFQ-173, and --check on the 15.0.9 record still reports only its documented hand-edit drift.

  • Register statuses. merged, partly merged, released, partly released and landed now count as claims of a fix, alongside fixed and partly fixed. Since the register adopted those words (2026-09-21), no merged or released entry could reach claimed-fixed-gates-pass, so every one was listed as not demonstrated, and breaking a gate left the gaps section the same size: the self-test's "the gaps section grew" assertion failed on the 16.0.0 selection, on the unmodified generator too.
  • A failing gate is a gap of its own (gate-failed), whatever the register says.
  • A base that moved past its pin (base: official/dev@<sha> while dev has moved on and still contains <sha>) is the gap base-moved-past-pin, no longer branch-unresolved; a pin that dev no longer contains is still unresolved.
  • A branch or base that exists only on the upstream remote resolves through official/<name>, and the record names the ref it used (resolved through).
  • Register cells holding an escaped \| are one cell (BF-58's status read as \).

docs.title: What a record does not do
docs.text:
It does not ship anything, and it does not assert that a defect has reached an operator. A fix reaches operators when it is released in a tagged release, which is outside the record. The 2026-09-16 record was taken from local, unpushed branches and says so per item.

It also does not replace the register, the queue or the release notes. It is the cross-section of all three at one instant, with the measurements attached.

Draft tooling, 2026-09-15; status updated 2026-09-22 and 2026-10-27. Requires maintainer review before it is relied upon. Nightscout is not a medical device and nothing here is medical advice.

docs.title: _template — how to cut a new release directory
docs.text:
Living document, last changed 2026-09-16 at 0efd51eae.

This directory is a template, not a release. Nothing in it describes anything real.

The convention — why these files live in this repository rather than in the shipping repositories, who each file is written for, and what happens at release time — is in ../README.md. Read that first. This file is only the mechanics.

docs.title: Cutting a new one
docs.text:
cp -r releases/_template releases/<product>-<version>

Then, in the new directory:

  1. Delete README.md — this file does not belong in a release directory.
  2. Fill in contents.md first. It is where the measuring happens, and the other two files are written from it. Writing the notes first tends to produce confident prose about things nobody checked.
  3. Write tag-message.txt from contents.md. Contributor-facing; terse is fine.
  4. Write release-notes.md last, from the tag message's numbered list of operator-visible changes. Every item on that list needs a line in the notes.
  5. Delete every <!-- comment --> and <placeholder> as you go. A comment or an angle bracket left in a file means that section was not written — that is the intended signal, so do not delete them wholesale at the end.

docs.title: The three files must agree
docs.text:
They are written for three different readers and they describe one release, so they drift. Before the directory is considered done, check across all three:

  • the count of operator-visible changes is the same in tag-message.txt and release-notes.md, and the numbering matches contents.md;
  • the version number appears the same everywhere, including the directory name — and if it is not settled, all three say it is not settled;
  • no caveat is softened between contents.md and release-notes.md. Carry the safety-relevant sentences across verbatim;
  • every register entry named in contents.md that produces a visible change has a line in the notes, and every "known issue" in the notes is traceable to an entry or is explicitly labelled as not having one.

docs.title: Things that are easy to get wrong
docs.text:
• Do not hand-edit CHANGELOG.md in the shipping repository. It is generated. That rule is why this directory exists.
  • Do not allocate a BF- id. The register is allocated centrally and moves hourly across sessions. Describe the defect; let the register owner number it.
  • Do not invent a version number to avoid writing "this is not settled". The unsettled ones have named placeholders in ../README.md; they are names, not versions.
  • Do not create a directory for a release whose number the maintainer has not chosen. Use the placeholder name from that table, or wait.
  • Label every figure reproduced or read-derived. An unlabelled figure is treated as unlabelled, not as reproduced.

Template, 2026-09-15. Drafts only; nothing in releases/ has been pushed, tagged, merged or published.

docs.title: Provenance — read before trusting any figure below
docs.text:
Every claim in this file is labelled reproduced or read-derived.

  • reproduced — something was executed and the output observed. Say what was run, against which SHA, and what it printed.
  • read-derived — obtained by reading source. Legitimate, and weaker. Measured across this programme: every claim that had to be retracted was read-derived; not one that began with a reproduction has been.

Never present a reading as a run. A figure with no label is treated as unlabelled, not as reproduced.

State explicitly what was NOT done, in particular: no vendor account exists on this machine, no live run against any vendor was made, and no live migration is claimed. An omission here reads as a claim.

docs.title: 7. Process and methodology
docs.text:
The programme borrows the design-control vocabulary of medical-device quality systems as a working method (document control, definition of done; the ecosystem-wide proposal is QUALITY-SYSTEM). Borrowing the vocabulary is not a claim of conformity with any standard.

The 2026-09-16 record is marked superseded and no 15.0.9 record has been captured DOCUMENT-CONTROL, DEFINITION-OF-DONE, verification record release decision agents prepare and stop; people push, merge, tag and publish release README

docs.title: 8. How this builds confidence
docs.text:
This section is for a reader outside the project: someone whose family relies on a Nightscout site, or a developer of an app that reads from or writes to one. Nightscout is a secondary display: it shows glucose and therapy data that other devices and apps produce. For each kind of risk, the table says what was done and what it does not cover.

risk what addresses it what it does not cover A fix breaks an app that talks to Nightscout A census of 40 client projects read what each sends and expects. A replay lab sent those exact requests to 15.0.8 and the candidate side by side; three findings that looked like breakages from reading the code did not reproduce. Where a fix would have broken a real client (oref0's and GluPredKit's count), the old behaviour is kept behind a named setting, on by default, with a deprecation warning. Clients outside the 40, and private scripts. The census reads each client at its upstream tip, not every version in use. Some changes are deliberate corrections and are listed as such in the release notes. A fix introduces a new defect Every fix ships with tests (2,033 more passing than 15.0.8 on fade2299). Break-its undo a fix and check that its tests fail for the right reason. The suite runs in six cells of Node and MongoDB versions. An A/B soak runs 15.0.8 and the candidate on the same traffic and flags every difference not explained by an intended change. Seven defects introduced by fixes were caught and fixed before release. Run 023, the six-cell run on fade2299, passed: 3566/0/4 in all six cells. The fifteen merges after run 020 up to fade2299 were each checked on one cell or in CI before it (run 021 covered the first thirteen in six cells, run 022 the tree with #8806, run 023 the tree with #8807). The last merge, #8815, was checked in CI only: on its PR and in master's nine-cell CI on the release merge c6a0d8ed. The soak is compressed (minutes standing for hours) and synthetic. Break-its of most fixes ran on their own branches, not on the integrated tree. Behaviour on real devices The maintainer walked user journeys in a browser with 15.0.8 side by side (11 scenarios passed). Real sites ran the candidate as the real-time soak: as of 2026-09-29 one Loop, one Trio and one AndroidAPS user ran 7000eb18 for about two days with no errors, and on 2026-10-02 the maintainer reported stable behaviour from AndroidAPS, Trio and Loop users of dev through the week. These reports are informal; how many sites and for how long is not recorded. On 2026-10-21 the maintainers decided that many days on varied real set-ups with no complaints from the testing cohort stand in place of the browser checks not done separately, which include a remote bolus, LoopCaregiver from its own app, the clock views, the pump pill, alarm labels, reports during a percentage profile switch, the Day to Day report, the Food Editor on a touch screen, a temp basal cancelled while a page is open (BF-94), a treatment tooltip on an mmol/L site with an mg/dL profile (BF-124), and a clock opened from the menu with a token on a site that requires sign-in (BF-127). Security defects Fixes for defects live on 15.0.8 are merged: live-update access, the query operator allowlist, login hardening, error replies without internal detail, bounds on two little-used request types, storage errors that ended the process, and dependency advisories. This repository is public, so those defects are described by mechanism and outcome only until a release with the fixes ships. One such defect has no fix in 15.0.9 (BF-72). Every fixed defect is still present on sites running 15.0.8 until they install 15.0.9. npm audit --package-lock-only on the v15.0.9 lockfile, run 2026-10-21 after the release, reports 28 findings (14 high, 0 critical; 15 / 10 / 0 with --omit=dev); #8806 cleared the one critical. The triage in contents covers the 26 (11 high) measured on 4bca2ac2 earlier that day; the high entries now include source-map-js (GHSA-68fv-2mgg-jv7q), which that triage does not cover. What's left open 27 items are listed in "What is NOT in 15.0.9" and carried in the release notes as known issues or deferred by decision. 37 register entries in scope are not closed: 18 known issues, 5 whose documentation is merged for 15.0.9 with a code half later, 1 with a fix prepared for after 15.0.9, 4 partly fixed, 6 only on unreleased branches or tooling, and 3 found in the BF-124 and BF-127 work (2 after 15.0.9 by decision, 1 not decided) (§6).

docs.title: 10. Method and history
docs.text:
Paving the cowpaths. 15.0.9 follows the rule that a specification describes what clients actually do: take a census of what clients send, turn those shapes into tests and replay probes, fix defects without breaking those shapes, and where a fix would break one, keep the old shape behind a named setting with a deprecation signal. The examples and sources are in the snapshot §8.

The MongoDB driver upgrade. 15.0.9 is the second release this year prepared this way; the first was the MongoDB driver upgrade (#8421) that shipped in 15.0.7 on 2026-04-29. Figures and links are in the snapshot §9.

Head fdf88f4e #8796 ca6fcfaf 2026-10-02 BF-155 a failed database read on GET /api/v1/activity or /api/v1/profile/current ended the server process; it is now answered with a 500 and the server keeps running. lib/api/activity/index.js and lib/api/profile/index.js (server only) and the new tests/api.read-storage-failure.test.js. Live on 15.0.8, so described by mechanism and outcome only. Its own CI: 14 passed, 2 skipped. Head e20b66ba #8799 f105f688 2026-10-02 BF-46, BF-48, BF-49, BF-50, BF-51, BF-74, BF-78, BF-81 (documentation) README and azuredeploy.json describe the settings the code reads: the API3_* settings, including the six API3_AUTOPRUNE_<collection> settings that permanently delete older records (BF-46), the webhook settings (BF-48), the HSTS setting's spelling (BF-49), ENTRIES_COLLECTION (BF-50), the supported Node versions (BF-51), the default roles and the login prompt (BF-78, BF-81); the API v3 swagger text states that the settings collection is stored as sent (BF-74). No code changes; BF-50 and BF-51 are closed by it, the others keep their code half open. Its own CI: 14 passed, 2 skipped. Head e42144ff #8800 74942ec6 2026-10-03 BF-94 the browser kept the last temp basal it looked up in a module-level variable, so an open page went on showing a temp basal that AndroidAPS (API v3) or Trio had shortened or cancelled until the temp's original end; lib/profilefunctions.js now keeps it per instance and resets it when the treatments are replaced (updateTreatments), and the new tests/profile-temp-cache.test.js covers it. Measured in Chromium (tools/lab/bf94-browser): ca6fcfaf and v15.0.8 show the stale temp alike, and the fixed tree clears every stale case in that harness. Its own CI: 14 passed, 2 skipped. Head a06e75d6 (2a64c500 merged with dev f105f688) #8801 68262e86 2026-10-03 BF-124 fixes #5940. The chart tooltip of a treatment with carbs or insulin converted its BG whenever the display units differed from the profile's units, ignoring the units the record was saved in, so on an mmol/L site with an mg/dL profile a careportal BG of 5 showed as 0.3 (and 90 as 1621 the other way round). lib/client/renderer.js treatmentTooltip now converts from the record's own units (any spelling containing mmol read as mmol/L), falling back to the profile's units when the record has none; the new tests/client.renderer.tooltip-units.test.js (14 tests, 7 of which fail on 74942ec6) covers it. Display only: no stored data changes. Its own CI: 14 passed, 2 skipped. Head affbc8fd; 2 files, +162/−3 #8802 1ad03e29 2026-10-03 BF-127 fixes #7377. On a site that denies anonymous reads, a clock view opened from the Clock menu by a viewer using an access token was blank: the menu links were plain paths and the clock page looked for a token only in its own address. The four Clock menu links now carry the page's token, URL-encoded (lib/client/browser-settings.js); a clock whose requests are answered 401 says "Not authorized" instead of drawing nothing (lib/client/clock-client.js, views/clockviews/clock.html, clock-shared.css), and the clock designer's "Open my clock view!" link URL-encodes the face and the token (views/clockviews/clock-config.html; CodeQL js/xss-through-dom alert 126 fixed, alert 127 dismissed by the maintainer as a false positive). New tests/clock-token-link.test.js (11 tests). Measured in Chromium on a denied site with a readable token: the three clocks are blank on 68262e86 and draw on the branch. Its own CI: 13 passed, 2 skipped, CodeQL passed. Head b13b7a3a (9238fd32 and the CodeQL fix); 6 files, +291/−1 #8806 43289dde 2026-10-07 BF-162 proxy-addr 2.0.7 → 2.0.8 (GHSA-jqcg-44mw-7w3h, critical, fixed in 2.0.8): an explicit TRUST_PROXY list that names an IPv6-notation subnet with zero leading bits (an IPv4-mapped-IPv6 subnet with a short prefix, or an IPv6 subnet with leading zero bits) compiled on proxy-addr 2.0.7 to trust every address; 2.0.8 trusts only the named block. The path is new in 15.0.9: lib/server/client-ip.js (added 2026-09-06) compiles the subnet list, while 15.0.8 enables trust proxy unconditionally and never compiles a subnet, so 15.0.8 cannot reach it. A plain IPv4 subnet (10.0.0.0/8), the default, true, false and a hop count are unaffected. package.json (^2.0.8), package-lock.json and one new tests/client-ip.test.js case. Its own CI: green across Node 20/22/24 × MongoDB 4.4/5/6, the npm 12 job, Docker and CodeQL. Head 7dd4f400; 3 files #8807 fade2299 2026-10-08 BF-168 the context (lower) chart's time window could not always be dragged all the way back to the current time. d3's brush reads its drag range from the <svg> element's own size, which is the browser default 300×150 when the chart is drawn before the page lays out, and chart.update() never re-read it; the brush now declares an explicit extent from the chart's own scale and height, and update() re-reads it and rebinds the overlay (lib/client/chart.js). Display-only — no stored-data or API change — and the same behaviour is on 15.0.8. Two new tests/dependency-d3.test.js cases (drag-back-to-now, mouse and touch) prove it; no package change, so dependencies and npm audit are unchanged. Its own CI and CodeQL: green. Head b919af9f; 3 files (lib/client/chart.js, tests/dependency-d3.test.js, tests/fixtures/d3-chart.js) #8815 4bca2ac2 2026-10-20 BF-171, by awss1i (fixes #8225) a bearer token whose subject was deleted, or lost with the database, stopped the server on the next request that carried it and again after each restart until it expired: authorization.resolve returned the null resolveAccessToken gives for a missing subject, and every caller read .shiros from it. The token now takes the failed-credential path (401, the "Failed authentication" notice, the failed-login delay); API v3 answers it 401 instead of 403. Live on 15.0.8, described by mechanism. Three tests in tests/api.security.test.js; its own CI and CodeQL green. Head 93a74ce5, the same tree as 4bca2ac2 #8741 bcd171cb 2026-09-20 — (external contributor) credential and identifier settings kept as strings (leading +, leading zeros)

#8754 (bf2/auth-hardening, head bae655a0, merged as 4f705217; 34 commits, 25 files, +2167/−105 against 153e5658). Besides bf/auth, bf/throttle and the client-ip.js backport it carries f6f361b1 (the delay's position), 607d51b0 (the proxy guide, docs/proposals/trusted-proxy-migration.md), 9c6cde72 (forwarded addresses with a port), b5f61f19 (the proxy guide recommends TRUST_PROXY=1 on Azure App Service), #8763 (d0a3d628, e3354218) and #8765 (bringing #8764, 71987bb4). What it carries:

  • BF-17. A subject save no longer writes accessToken/accessTokenDigest/digest. Existing rows keep them until the subject is next saved; clearing a row does not retire the token. The gate node tools/queue/gates/bf17-remediation-note.js guards the notes' rotation text (17 checked, 0 failing on 2026-09-24), and tools/queue/gates/bf17-rename-row-control.sh is its control (exits 1).
  • BF-30, the failed-login delay. The wait comes before the credential check, as in earlier releases. Failures are counted per client address and also per credential. The list is bounded and swept on a schedule (lib/authorization/delaylist.js).
  • TRUST_PROXY (BF-30, BF-88). Unset resolves the client address as dev does (forwarded-for, pinned by 8b975b41), and a boot message says the delay does not protect against guessing. false = direct connection only; a comma-separated list of IPs/CIDRs = the trusted boundary; a whole number = that many hops; true = every hop (Express's meaning, 81623f9b). The subnet aliases loopback, linklocal, uniquelocal are refused at boot (lib/server/client-ip.js). Setting it behind a TLS-terminating proxy that is not trusted causes an https redirect loop. Explicit TRUST_PROXY settings accept forwarded addresses that carry a port (the form Azure App Service is reported to send); unset is unchanged (9c6cde72).
  • BF-47. Subject and role create()/save() write only an allow-list of fields (declared correction, below); a save that omits notes or created_at keeps the stored values (7103f657).
  • Every read of the auth collections stopped printing its query options to stdout (ce82f0cd).
  • One TRUST_PROXY policy (#8763, RT-TRUST-ONE-SOURCE). Every client-address consumer reads one policy compiled per env; lib/server/client-ip.js exports only trustFor(env) and clientIPFor(env); API v3 logins key from env, not the mounted app's trust proxy. No behaviour change.
  • Loop remote-command sender address (#8764 via #8765, RT-LOOP-REMOTE-ADDRESS). The remote-address in Loop pushes follows TRUST_PROXY through clientIPFor(env) instead of the connecting address. Loop stores it on remote overrides, so the caregiver's address is kept in treatments, readable by anyone with read access to the site. The release notes say so.

docs.title: Version number: 15.0.9
docs.text:
Decided 2026-09-22 (queue RT-VERSION; decisions). The release is 15.0.9, the number dev's package.json already carries. #8738 (as amended by #8748 and #8761), #8743 and #8754's subject/role field allow-list ship as declared corrections in the release notes.

Decided 2026-09-24 (maintainer; queue RT-COUNT-COMPAT): tolerate the count shapes real clients send and keep 15.0.9 a patch. #8761 implements it: API_V1_COUNT_LEADING_NUMBER and API_V1_COUNT_ZERO_WINDOW, each on by default (lib/server/env.js), expected to default to false in a future release.

The facts the classification rests on, for the record:

  • Under gt4-semver-classification-2026-09-15.md the dev content is at least a minor (DEBUG_LOGGING, CONNECT_DEBUG, routine debug logging off by default, new lib/api2/loop-notification-errors.js, the two API_V1_COUNT_* settings); #8754 adds TRUST_PROXY.
  • Dev-channel deployments already report 15.0.9 from /api/v1/status (lib/server/env.js → lib/api/status.js). The release notes say so.
  • The modernization cut branches also carry 15.0.9 in package.json; each cut is renumbered when it is rebased (decisions).

docs.title: 8598 and the tag. **The maintainers
docs.text:
(the maintainer and Andy Low) decided on 2026-10-21 that the candidate is ready:** it has run for many days on varied real Nightscout set-ups with no complaints from the testing cohort, and that stands in place of the hand checks listed in item 1, which were not done separately. The new follow-redirects advisories and BF-172 are known issues by the same decision. The list as it stood on fade2299 (2026-10-08) follows for the record.

  1. docs.title: Reading these counts
docs.text:
A vulnerability count on its own does not say whether Nightscout is exposed. Each count above measures something narrower than it looks:

  • One advisory is counted once for every package that depends on it. npm audit reports a finding for the vulnerable package and one for each package above it in the tree. On 295f1177, one ajv advisory accounts for 6 of the 17 findings, and one request advisory, with the form-data and uuid advisories beneath it, accounts for 5.
  • Build tools are counted as run-time packages. The bundle is built at install time, so webpack, its loaders and browserslist are in dependencies. Their findings (6 of the 17: ajv, schema-utils, style-loader, browserslist, baseline-browser-mapping, postcss-selector-parser) concern input those tools read from the repository's own configuration, not anything a Nightscout site receives.
  • An advisory counts whether or not Nightscout reaches the vulnerable code. Both sanitize-html advisories need an element the sanitizer's configuration does not allow, and the request findings apply only when a legacy bridge is switched on.
  • Dependabot measures the default branch, which is the last release. Of its 80 open alerts, 68 are already fixed on dev and stay open until the release merges to master.
  • Advisories arrive after the code ships. form-data 2.5.6 was released on 2026-06-12, after the 2.5.5 pin was written on 2026-05-10, so a count taken on a fixed tree rises without any change to the code.

What a count does show is the backlog to triage. The measured result for 15.0.9 is the table below: which findings reach a running site, and what is done about each.

docs.title: The 11 high findings on 4bca2ac2
docs.text:
Re-measured 2026-10-21 on the release head. The 9 high of fade2299 (next section) are unchanged; two are new, both from advisories published 2026-10-20 against a lockfile that did not change. With --omit=dev the same two advisories also mark nightscout-connect, axios-cookiejar-support and minimed-connect-to-nightscout high, as packages above follow-redirects, which is why that count rises from 5 to 10.

advisory high nodes reach in 15.0.9 disposition GHSA-q3jh-wrc6-jgq8 and GHSA-8r9p-f939-6h3c (follow-redirects 1.16.0, held by the override in package.json) follow-redirects, axios (2); with --omit=dev also nightscout-connect, axios-cookiejar-support, minimed-connect-to-nightscout credential headers survive a cross-origin redirect only when headers are given as an array (q3jh) or a declared sensitiveHeaders name contains ^ or \| (8r9p). Read, not run: axios 1.20.0 (the connector's) passes headers as an object (lib/adapters/http.js:957) and sets sensitiveHeaders = [] (:1056); axios 0.34.0 (minimed-connect-to-nightscout, and the top-level dev dependency) passes a plain object and no sensitiveHeaders; neither nightscout-connect v0.1.0 nor Nightscout's lib/ uses follow-redirects directly known issue by the maintainer's decision (2026-10-21), named in the release notes; fixed in 1.16.1 (a patch release, one override value), taken up after 15.0.9 GHSA-x3q4-9hxx-gx8m (sanitize-html < 2.18.0; moderate, listed here because it is new) — run 2026-10-21 on 2.17.5 with lib/server/purifier.js's options: the advisory's <noscript> case lets <img src="http://…"> and <a href> through, both already allowed by the configuration when written directly; onerror is still stripped. docs.title: The 9 high findings on fade2299
docs.text:
The candidate's 9 high findings (2026-10-08; unchanged from 43289dde, whose lockfile fade2299 shares byte-for-byte) are four advisories. npm audit lists each once for the vulnerable package and once for each package above it in the tree.

advisory high nodes reach in 15.0.9 disposition GHSA-86w9-cpqp-85rv (node-forge 1.4.0) node-forge, @parse/node-apn (2) node-forge loads only through @parse/node-apn (Loop remote commands), to parse the site's own APNs key and certificate; the advisory is about signature verification, which Nightscout never calls BF-154 (low): no fixed release; @parse/node-apn 8.1.0 (the latest) still pins node-forge 1.4.0, so the update waits for an upstream fix and is carried with the modernization work (below) GHSA-vfj7-8cjw-p6xm (braces ≤3.0.3) braces, micromatch, chokidar, nodemon, eslint-webpack-plugin (5) a deeply nested bracket pattern on the three query endpoints (/times, /times/echo, /slice) makes that one request answer 500; the site keeps running and nothing is read or written. Present on 15.0.8 BF-161 (known issue, decided 2026-10-07): no fixed release; a nesting-depth limit is planned after 15.0.9 GHSA-vc2v-76pw-4v95 (compression 1.8.1) compression (1) per the advisory, a slow memory leak when many responses are cut off before they finish (not measured here). Present on 15.0.8, which locks compression 1.8.1 too BF-163 (known issue, decided 2026-10-07): fixed upstream in 1.8.2, taken up in the modernization releases GHSA-68fv-2mgg-jv7q (source-map-js) source-map-js (1) build time only: source-map parsing during the webpack build, not in any request path — the same build-tooling class as the moderate findings above the fix is breaking-only and comes with the modernization work; not a new known issue

The --omit=dev run keeps the 5 highs a running site loads: node-forge and @parse/node-apn, braces, compression and source-map-js; micromatch, chokidar, nodemon and eslint-webpack-plugin are dev-dependency tooling.

docs.text: BF-147: 26 lockfile version changes, all patch or minor; npm audit 20 → 8, no highs; the production bundle is byte-identical; full suite on its branch 3512/0/4, npm ci on Node 20.20.0, 22.23.2 and 24.20.0 and the npm 12 job. moment stays at 2.30.1 by decision (2026-10-01): no request input reaches moment.locale on dev (BF-31), and 2.31.0 changes parsing and locale display output.
