docs.text: and working DIY and production/service environments are reported.

docs.title: Interpretation limits
docs.text:
• The compatibility matrix measures synthetic request and storage outcomes; it does not prove that an individual client's deployed version behaves as its source code suggests.
  • Client-impact counts are source-shape matches from the pinned client catalogue, not adoption, active-user, or production-traffic counts.
  • A measured difference is not automatically a regression: the compatibility report labels intended behavior, fixes, and defects separately and links each finding to its evidence.
  • PR checks, post-merge branch checks, local full-suite runs, and the synthetic compatibility matrix are separate evidence. Passing one does not substitute for another.

#8836 (read from the PR body and git show; the runs are AndyLow91's). Six commits (git log 2bc298b9..df2f37ab): e0872924 (dependency and credential findings), two merges of dev (f09cb431, 15a84907), be806a57 (privacy for GET authentication), 78aacc15 (CI) and the merge df2f37ab ("Merge dev CI hygiene while preserving the 14-job matrix"). What it changes, by mechanism:

  • body-parser ^1.20.6 → ^1.20.9 (lock 1.20.6 → 1.20.9): the PR body states that a malformed compressed request body can terminate the server, and adds child-process regression probes for it and for compression 1.8.2 (on dev since #8835). 15.0.9 locks body-parser 1.20.6 and compression 1.8.1 (git show official/master:package-lock.json), the versions these replace.
  • The page's first status request no longer carries the API secret hash or token in its URL: it sends them as api-secret and Authorization headers (lib/client/index.js), and lib/api/status.js reads them there. Query-string credentials are still accepted for existing clients. 15.0.9's lib/client/index.js:58 appends the credential to the status URL.
  • Logs and responses: credential-bearing request URLs and error details are redacted (lib/server/log-privacy.js, new), CSP reports are sanitised before logging, Referrer-Policy: no-referrer is set whether or not CSP is on, Cache-Control: no-store is set on status responses and before redirects and authorization (lib/middleware/credential-cache.js), and setup-mode errors use the production error handler.
  • Dependency floors: dompurify 3.4.17, moment 2.31.0, fast-uri 3.1.9, ip-address 10.7.5, serialize-javascript 7.1.4, csv-parse 7.0.3 (development), nyc's nested uuid (lock versions on dev, reproduced). The PR body reports npm audit affected-package entries 23 (full) and 16 (--omit=dev) before and two after, both in the one chain with no patched release: @parse/node-apn → node-forge 1.4.0, GHSA-86w9-cpqp-85rv; the body says no remotely reachable path was established and keeps APNs as it is (read-derived; not re-run).
  • CI: the 20 mutable action references pinned to commit SHAs; superseded pull_request runs cancelled; publishing waits for every test job; a manual extended mode that never publishes. The runtime Docker stage deletes npm and npx.
  • Tests on the PR head (read from the body): Node 24.22.1 against MongoDB 6.0.27, 3474 passing, 3 skipped, 0 failing, with coverage; 51 focused privacy and header cases on Node 22.23.4 and 24.22.1.

#8833 removes only the Run Tests (22, 4.4) matrix entry and updates CONTRIBUTING.md, README.md, docs/runtime-upgrade.md and docs/test-specs/browser-tests.md (daee0c9e, merge 9ac9d534). Its body states that dev requires only Run Tests (24, 6), and that master still requires Run Tests (22, 4.4), which an administrator must remove before the next release PR into master (read; the protection read above agrees).

After ee94b148: AndyLow91's merge of dev fd3792e5 (2efd78ac, "Merge dev security and CI updates into Cut 2"; conflicts in .github/workflows/main.yml, lib/server/app.js, package.json and package-lock.json per the body), 62b1509d (the env-runner nyc fix: --all=false on the inner nyc and docs/test-specs/env-runner.md; author Ben West, the same patch as the peer session's bd941200 by git patch-id) and AndyLow91's af7ba73a ("fix: preserve Maker delivery across recipient failures": Maker keys are sent in parallel and one key's error no longer stops the other keys or the later events; each request has a 10 s deadline; the log line names the event instead of the request URL, which carries the Maker key; 5 files). 15.0.9 logs that URL (lib/plugins/maker.js:111 on official/master). AndyLow91 merged dev eb44a9c2 into it (90e2cfde, "Merge dev and align test tiers with Cut 2") and added ad8a73e2 (invalid tier or file selections exit non-zero before any test starts). The tier check and the harness tier run in the main backend CI jobs. npm test and test-ci are unchanged.

#8840 (read from the body; issue 8156). On a 23- or 25-hour day the Loopalyzer built 276 or 300 five-minute bins instead of 288, so every series was rejected and the charts were blank; ranges that included such a day dropped that day's series. The fix anchors the axis on a 24-hour local day and bounds per-day slots to 288 (lib/report_plugins/loopalyzer.js, docs/test-specs/loopalyzer-dst.md, two test files). Commits: HeartCoreDev's 63ad23be, AndyLow91's merge of dev a383f0f9 and his 5be6f217 ("align DST curves with local clock markers"). The body reports 13 of 13 slot tests failing before the change and 20 of 20 passing after (TZ=Europe/Berlin). The PR head's run 40240553524 needed a maintainer approval on attempt 1 (action_required, a fork PR) and passed on attempt 2.

The 2026-10-26 merges (read from the PR bodies and git log <merge>^1..<merge>^2; the runs are the authors'):

  • #8841: e8125d89, 6e842c07, a2e5fe49 (bewest) and AndyLow91's 5901961c ("validate effective Temporary Target updates"). Rules for every app, checked only when WRITE_VALIDATION is log or reject: targets above zero, bottom not above top, units mg/dl or mmol (client spellings accepted), each target plausible for its units (above 30 labelled mmol is a mg/dL number; below 20 labelled mg/dl is a mmol/L number), durations zero or more. Under reject a v1 batch stores its valid items and answers 200 with one object per item, the refused ones without _id and with a refused member, plus Warning: 299. App-specific limits (AndroidAPS's 72–180 mg/dL) are not applied.
  • #8842: BF-92 (5fb199b3, with BF-190), BF-93 (91d9a4db), BF-180 (bb1ad38e, the careportal temp target converted once and labelled mg/dl), BF-159's token half (72f3cc09) and BF-160 (2556b35b). On a page showing ---, a non-glucose alarm (pump, loop, age, stale data, CGM error codes and the rest outside the default group) is now presented when either the page's high or low alarm for its level is on; glucose alarms with no reading stay unpresented. The PR body asks reviewers to confirm stale-data and CGM-error alarms on a page showing ---.
  • #8844 (cut 3): merged from 0d54d072, AndyLow91's commit over his own merge of dev into cut 3 (831c32fc). Driver 7 with an explicit batchSize: 1000 on bulk reads, BF-182's boot error page (8f238fc5), BF-179 (200c1361), jQuery UI 1.14.2 widgets and native help tooltips, Compose mongo:6.0.27 (a database major upgrade for an existing Compose deployment).

Its last commits restore the CORS preflight's 200 text OK (ad56423d), give browser jobs 15 minutes (f4abce3c) and set HOME for the Firefox date probe (a77cb146). The body leaves live Pushover emergency delivery, acknowledgement and cancellation, alarm de-duplication over its real window, APNs delivery to a phone, production hosting, upgrade and rollback, and physical-device accessibility as maintainer-owned acceptance work.
  • #8854: eleven commits by AndyLow91 over dev 47723cda, from 880b7369 to 246313e4, merged after the four outcome-B points (decisions), which he agreed to on the PR at 20:32Z. By mechanism: the six v1 and internal collection modules, the legacy socket and API v3 go through the persistence boundary (lib/storage/write-step.js, a wrapper over the driver collection that keeps existing replies and validates the effective result of $set and $unset); it emits a data-free storage-write-committed event marked internal and unstable, with no consumer; the opt-in Temporary Target rules also apply to the socket's add, update and unset, and under reject the socket answers a refused item with a refused slot in input order, as API v1 does; a non-mutating stored-data inspection (lib/storage/read-contract.js) can add a Nightscout-Data-Warnings header to API v3 reads, off unless API_V3_DATA_WARNINGS=true and called experimental; a read-only diagnostic command (scripts/diagnose-data.js) and a write-boundary check (scripts/check-write-boundary.js); guards for malformed cache values, authorization identities and history timestamps; Mocha runs that find zero tests fail (--fail-zero). Not asked for: 246313e4 adds a failed slot on socket treatment arrays under reject for an item whose write cannot be confirmed (open item 11). The merged tree's client replay is R16 in the integration record: 0 differences from 47723cda in 201 cells.

#8860, the glucose pentagon (read from the PR body and git diff --stat 7ad3a67f 8dbb60c2; not run by this programme). The Distribution report gains the Comprehensive Glucose Pentagon's five component values, a reference polygon, CGM coverage, the reading count and the prognostic glycemic risk (PGR), in both glucose units, both report themes and print (lib/report/pentagon.js, pentagon-view.js, agp-data.js, lib/report_plugins/glucosedistribution.js). Fixed 70–180 mg/dL thresholds; it reads the original CGM observations before the report's one-minute filter, time-weights them, collapses exact same-source duplicates and withholds the score for conflicting simultaneous readings or indistinguishable alternating streams. The score is withheld below 70 % elapsed coverage, below 16 h 48 min of observed data, or when an hourly filter excludes part of the day; the PR body calls these "implementation guards, not validated clinical PGR thresholds", and says the numerical checks "do not constitute third-party clinical validation" and that independent review of the incomplete-data method and clinical presentation remains advisable. It adds the Nightscout Reporter licence notices (docs/third-party/) and the method in docs/test-specs/glucose-pentagon.md. The PR's CI on ad593fce passed every job; the merge's did not (Identity, CI on 8dbb60c2).

docs.title: Version: 16.0.0, major
docs.text:
Decided by the maintainer on 2026-10-21 (RT-VERSION answered). Surfaces touched (versioning policy §6.2), read from the merged PRs. A ticked box is a surface the merged code touches; an unticked one marked owed has a candidate change whose classification is not recorded yet:

  • S1 the HTTP API and the realtime socket contract: #8797 stores records the socket used to drop as copies; #8845 makes API v3 refuse a client body _id with 400 (BF-170), answers a v1 re-send with its stored _id (BF-165) and merges a profile re-sent with its _id instead of answering 500 (BF-166); #8852 answers malformed API v1 profile uploads with 400 and caps them at 10,000 records; #8841 adds refused slots to v1 batch replies under WRITE_VALIDATION=reject, and #8854 the same slots, and a failed slot, to socket replies under reject, and the opt-in Nightscout-Data-Warnings header on API v3 reads; cut 5 moves the routes to Express 5 (the query parser keeps allowPrototypes: true and sets arrayLimit: 1000 and parameterLimit: 1000, lib/middleware/configure-request.js:8-9; read-derived: Express 4's extended parser used qs's default arrayLimit of 20)
  • S2 plugin interface, boot sequence or client bundle: cut 2 (#8837) splits the client into page bundles and replaces the boot sequence and the client event bus with native code (a third-party plugin that hooks into the page is to be tested before upgrading; no plugin was run against it); #8849 makes boot wait for its indexes; #8831 adds an opt-in theme
  • S3 environment-variable surface: new THEME=modern (#8831), WRITE_VALIDATION (#8841), API3_SETTINGS_STRICT_READ_ENABLED (#8845) and SHOW_SECONDS (#8555); a start-up warning when SECURE_HSTS_HEADER_INCLUDE_SUBDOMAINS is set (BF-49); leftover legacy bridge settings stop the site with a page naming the replacements (cut 1); DEBUG_MINIFY no longer has an effect (cut 2)
  • S4 stored document shape, owed: #8845's BF-166 changes what a profile re-sent with its _id stores (merged with $set where it failed before), and #8842's BF-180 changes how a careportal temp target on an mmol/L site is stored; neither is classified here
  • S5 Node or MongoDB runtime floor, major: lib/server/runtime-policy.js reads engines.node and exits at boot outside ^22.23.4 || ^24.22.1 || >=26.12.1, which stops Node 20, 21, 23 and 25, and 22.0–22.23.3, 24.0–24.22.0 and 26.0–26.12.0. Driver 7 (cut 3) refuses MongoDB 3.6, 4.0 and 4.2 (BF-182's boot error page); the README states 5.0 through 8.0. CI on dev (job names of push run 40369632641): Run Tests (22.23.4, 8.0), (26, 5.0), (24, 6), (22, 6); Tests without a database (22.23.4), (26); Maintained MongoDB (26, 8.0.29); browsers on Node 26 × Chromium, Firefox and WebKit
  • S6 an ingestion path, major: the legacy Dexcom Share bridge and MiniMed CareLink (mmconnect) are removed; Dexcom Share data comes in through nightscout-connect
  • S7 alarms or notifications, owed: #8842 (BF-92) presents device and other non-glucose alarms on a page with no reading where none was presented before, which is the policy's question 8 (MINOR, never waivable, rule R2: at least a minor and a release note); #8816 changes how long a snooze lasts on a page that is not signed in; cut 2's af7ba73a changes how IFTTT Maker events are sent to several keys; cut 5 replaces the Pushover client and the notification cache and moves APNs to 8 (live delivery not checked, #8605's body)
  • S8 the version string: 16.0.0
  • S9 what the client computes and shows a person: BF-172, BF-173 and BF-174 change the Bolus Wizard Preview and the Careportal Bolus Wizard where the profile and display units differ, or where a profile other than the active one is chosen; #8812, #8808 and #8840 change report figures; #8851 changes how dose labels round; #8542 adds the AGP report

Not on the list, and recorded for the release notes: #8836 changes response headers (Referrer-Policy, Cache-Control), where the page sends its credentials, and removes npm from the runtime Docker image.

Classification: MAJOR, because of S5 and S6 (cut 1) and S5 again (cut 3's MongoDB floor). Directory name says: 16.0.0. Settled? Yes, by the maintainer, 2026-10-21.

docs.text:
As of dev 47723cda (2026-10-26), with item 11 from 7ad3a67f, and items 1 and 12–15, the entry bar and the repository settings brought to dev 991b0654 on 2026-10-30. The decisions already made are in decisions.md. Whether cuts 3–5 ship in 16.0.0 is answered: all three are merged into dev, so they ship in 16.0.0 unless reverted.

Required before the tag (maintainer, 2026-10-26, session -66; queue RT-16-RELEASE): (a) a live Pushover and APNs delivery check (RT-16-LIVE-ALARMS); (b) a real-rig soak on dev (RT-16-RIG-SOAK); (c) the BF-72 and BF-161 fork fixes merged and published with 16.0.0 (BFQ-72, BFQ-161). November 2 status: cohort testing is in progress; completion evidence for these gates is not yet recorded. The earlier "not started" characterization is superseded, not a reason to restart or discard existing tester observations. BF-193 is not a pre-tag requirement; its fix shape is decided (debug-gated payload logging through DEBUG_LOGGING, decisions) and merged 2026-10-27 as #8856 (dev eed31dca). The maintainer's definition of done before the tag (2026-10-27, RT-16-RELEASE) adds (d) a short quiet period on dev with the final candidate, days not weeks, and states (b) as cohort confirmations from dev users (AndroidAPS, Loop, Trio, xDrip+, a follower app, an mmol/L site).

The entry bar (maintainer, 2026-10-29; scope widened 2026-10-30): every single-tenant item of the next-gen plan may join the 16.0.0 merge list, in priority order, once its matrix result is as stated, its red controls and ablations pass, a revert has been rehearsed, and it has had time on dev with its cohort check. A miss at the tag rolls to 16.1.0, or to 17.0.0 if it changes a default. On 2026-10-30 no item in In flight has cleared it; #8874 is first in the order.

Decisions open, with their owner:

  1. BF-161 advisory scope is decided; private integration remains blocked. The recorded 2026-10-27 decision is to cover BF-161 and BF-151 together and publish once with 16.0.0. Current private targeting/full-suite blockers are in security readiness; no merge or publication is claimed. Queue BFQ-161 is blocked, not awaiting a ready-to-review packet.
  2. BF-72 remains private and blocked. Disclosure-safe test preparation, valid private PR targeting and final full-suite integration are outstanding; see security readiness. Queue BFQ-72 does not authorize publication.
  3. BF-95 (maintainer): a notice for readings that arrive dated ahead of the server clock, or the status quo. Packet: bfq-95. 2026-10-25 (maintainer): verify srvModified first; on dev it is a server receipt time on every live path (caveat BF-181).
  4. Dependabot configuration (maintainer): version updates targeting dev, dismissing alerts that are fixed on dev or not reachable, or releasing more often. Packet: dependabot-config.
  5. BF-49's alias and dead settings keys (maintainer; #8849's open items, BFQ-ENV): whether SECURE_HSTS_HEADER_INCLUDE_SUBDOMAINS becomes an alias, and what to do with the five settings keys nothing reads.
  6. #8842's open items (maintainer): on a page with a reading, a non-glucose alarm is still gated by the high or low setting on the reading's side; and the reviewers' confirmation of stale-data and CGM-error alarms on a page showing ---.
  7. #8841's open items (maintainer): a refusal the person can see under reject, normalising units beyond temp targets, the plausibility thresholds (30 mmol/L, 20 mg/dL); and WRITE_VALIDATION set to any value other than log or reject reads as off with no message (parseMode, lib/server/write-validation.js:42-46 on dev), so a misspelt reject turns checking off silently.
  8. The query-string array limit under Express 5 (maintainer): cut 5 sets arrayLimit: 1000 (lib/middleware/configure-request.js:8-9), where 15.0.9's Express 4 parser used qs's default of 20 (read-derived); no decision on the value is recorded.
  9. A recorded waiver for the MongoDB 3.6–4.2 drop (maintainer): the versioning policy §5.4 sets 2 releases and 180 days for a runtime floor that can stop data arriving; MongoDB 4.4 was deprecated in 15.0.9, and 3.6, 4.0 and 4.2 stop serving with 16.0.0 (driver 7, decided 2026-10-25). The decision is recorded; a waiver of §5.4's window, with its reason for the release notes, is not.
  10. BF-194 (maintainer): API v1 removes units from a treatment with no glucose value before WRITE_VALIDATION runs, so a v1 temp target sent in mmol/L is stored with mmol/L numbers and no units and reads as mg/dL, in every mode, on 15.0.9 and dev (reproduced, integration record R15): keep the units, convert, or refuse. Queue BFQ-194. 2026-10-27 (maintainer): survey the clients first, then likely enforce mg/dL at write (convert a target labelled mmol and relabel it); survey running. Decided 2026-10-27 (maintainer): convert and always label. docs.title: For the release notes
docs.text:
A draft list of what the release notes must say; the notes themselves are written last, once the candidate is named.

  • (#8865, if merged) Nightscout stops cleanly on SIGTERM and SIGINT on every start path: it closes its connections and exits 0, or exits 1 if it is still open after 8 s. In the Docker image, docker stop takes well under a second instead of 10 s and a forced kill. One case changes outcome: a container under restart: on-failure that receives SIGTERM from something other than docker stop used to ignore it and keep running; it now exits 0 and stays stopped. The image's command is nightscout single (the same server as node lib/server/server.js, which still works as an explicit command); tooling that matches PID 1's command line sees the new name. nightscout is a new executable with single, healthcheck, version, env and diagnose data; nightscout serve is reserved for a multitenant Nightscout, which is not built yet, so every role exits 64.

  • (BF-213, if merged) Sites with PUMP_ENABLE_ALERTS get pump alarms at the severity Loop assigns to its pump status, with Loop's text: "No Insulin", "Pod Expired" and Medtronic "Signal Loss" now alarm, which they never did. Candidate note, read from #8865 at 1b2801f7 by session -7d, not run: a custom entrypoint or command that puts node in front of the image's default command now runs node nightscout single and fails to start.

  • The Node floor ^22.23.4 || ^24.22.1 || >=26.12.1, and the message the server prints when it refuses to start.

  • The legacy Dexcom Share and MiniMed CareLink bridges are removed; leftover bridge settings stop the site with a page naming the replacements; Dexcom Share data comes in through nightscout-connect.
  • MongoDB 4.4 or newer is required to start (cut 3, driver 7): on 3.6, 4.0 or 4.2 the site does not serve data and shows a page naming the database server's version and the minimum it needs (BF-182); the fix is to upgrade MongoDB. 5.0 through 8.0 are the supported, tested range; 4.4 starts but is untested.
  • MongoDB 8.0 itself does not start on Linux kernels 6.19 to 7.0.13, which includes Ubuntu 26.04's Linux 7.0: it logs "MongoDB cannot start: Linux kernel versions 6.19 and newer has a known incompatibility" (MongoDB's SERVER-121912, not a Nightscout change). On such a host, run MongoDB 5.0 to 7.0, or keep the database on a host with an older kernel, until MongoDB supports it (BF-202).
  • Production-only installs (npm ci --omit=dev or NODE_ENV=production) that worked on 15.0.9 do not build the client bundle since cut 2 (webpack and Babel are devDependencies). BF-179 (planned for cut 3) turns the failure into a message naming the fix (npm ci --include=dev, then npm prune --omit=dev --ignore-scripts); it does not restore the old behaviour. The project's Dockerfile and azure-deploy.sh install dev dependencies and are not affected.
  • Docker Compose starts mongo:6.0.27 instead of mongo:5.0.32 (cut 3): for an existing Compose deployment this is a database major-version upgrade (docs/runtime-upgrade.md).
  • Express 5 and Helmet 8 (cut 5), and the query-string array limit (above, open item 8).
  • The opt-in THEME=modern dashboard (#8831) and the opt-in SHOW_SECONDS clock (#8555).
  • The opt-in WRITE_VALIDATION for Temporary Targets (#8841), what log and reject do, that most uploaders lose a refused record without showing an error, and that an unrecognised value means off.
  • The opt-in API3_SETTINGS_STRICT_READ_ENABLED (#8845, BF-152 step 1), and that an AndroidAPS 4.0 follower using a read-only token it was not given by AndroidAPS is refused when it is on.
  • Record identity (#8845): API v3 refuses a client body _id with 400 (BF-170); API v3 PATCH, PUT and POST reach a record with an empty stored identifier (BF-145); a v1 re-send is answered with the stored _id (BF-165); a profile re-sent with its _id is merged instead of failing (BF-166).
  • A null in an update removes the field (write contract Q1b, decided 2026-10-26; with BF-195's fix): what is stored changes for a re-send that matches a stored treatment, entry, profile, food or activity record, for an API v3 PATCH and for a socket dbUpdate, where 15.0.9 stores the null. A create and a replace (v1 or v3 PUT) still store a null as sent. Arrays are replaced whole. The merge is nested: a profile re-sent with part of its store keeps the named profiles it leaves out; to remove one, send store: {"<name>": null} or replace the profile with PUT (as the profile editor does).
  • A device status re-sent with an identifier that is already stored is not stored again and does not change the stored record (no new srvModified); the reply carries the stored _id, on API v1 and v3. API v1 entries and device status match a re-send on identifier, as treatments do; an entry whose identifier matches nothing still matches on its time and type.
  • Quieter server logs (BF-193): each write is logged as a summary, not the record. Set DEBUG_LOGGING=true to see the records clients send; debug logs then contain health data. Log lines change text.
  • API v1 profile uploads (#8852): malformed entries and binary bodies answer 400, and a batch is capped at 10,000 records, as on the other bounded v1 upload routes.
  • BF-92 (#8842): a page showing --- now presents device and other non-glucose alarms (a MINOR change under the policy's rule R2, with this note); BF-190, BF-93, BF-180, BF-159's token half and BF-160.
  • The first start on an empty database waits for index creation (about 3 to 4 s on MongoDB 8.0), and a long index build logs a warning after 20 s and carries on (#8849).
  • Dose labels round correctly on midpoints (#8851).
  • The Bolus Wizard Preview and Careportal Bolus Wizard unit fixes (BF-172, BF-173) and the profile picker (BF-174); BF-09 (the socket's duplicate check keeps zero temps, cancels and zero amounts); #8816's snooze; #8812 and #8808's report figures.
  • The glucose pentagon and PGR in the Distribution report (#8860): what the five values and the risk figure are, that the report withholds them when too little of the period has readings, and the PR's own caveats carried verbatim: the withholding rules are "implementation guards, not validated clinical PGR thresholds", PGR is a research metric, and the numerical checks "do not constitute third-party clinical validation". It is a report figure, not a treatment recommendation; talk to the care team before acting on it.
  • One stored-text change from sanitize-html 2.18.1 (#8835): a malformed empty <textarea></textarea/> followed by an image with an event handler is now stored as the image tag without its handler (<img src="x" />), where 2.17.5 stored nothing (the empty string). The other 34 corpus inputs are stored identically.
  • Cut 2 (merged): page bundles, build and runtime separated (npm ci with development dependencies, then prune), no late minification, DEBUG_MINIFY without effect, the load-failure panel, and a third-party plugin that hooks into the page to be tested before upgrading.
  • Cut 2's IFTTT Maker change (af7ba73a): every key and every event is attempted when one fails; the log names the event, not the key.
  • The known issues at the tag.

Import should finish metadata before admitting traffic; do not omit attribution, substitute stable IDs or trust stale JWT metadata. Root remains an explicit principal without an invented subject name. Characterization and limits are in R28. Classify demonstrably nonrepresentable submitted data as tenant-only 400, recognized unavailable services as 503, and unclassified/internal stored-state failures as 500 maintainer, 2026-11-04 ST-PG No blanket mapping of TypeError or unsupported-adapter errors. Preserve existing single/Mongo behavior. This improves refusal classification; it does not establish Mongo/PG input parity or broad client retry compatibility. Measure actual HTTP JSON edge cases and legitimate client shapes; do not reject fields merely because their names are unfamiliar or coerce/drop data to achieve parity. Existing parser/purifier, branch-sensitive create/update grants, resend behavior and tenant-local configured pruning remain required.

docs.title: Runnable preview and parallel CRUD delivery (2026-11-04)
docs.text: decision who, when queue as it stands Prioritize substantial runnable multitenant implementation and full entries CRUD in parallel; tests and records belong to those deliverables, not separate prerequisite packet chains maintainer, 2026-11-04 ST-PG, T30-WIRING, TEN-LAB, PLAT-SERVE Build an explicitly bounded nightscout multitenant api process using accepted tenant/PG/provider components alongside remaining actual entries mutation/history routes. Complete CRUD, production HA, durable registry and every owner capability are not prerequisites for building the bounded experimental runtime. They remain requirements for their respective capabilities and complete milestone promotion. Preserve single/Mongo and report supported/unsupported preview capabilities explicitly. Apply the established POST attribution and narrow refusal policy consistently to tenant CRUD writes maintainer, 2026-11-04 ST-PG, T30-WIRING Subject mutations require exact current name: missing metadata401, genuine authority outage503; root stays explicit without an invented subject name. Marked nonrepresentable submitted data400, recognized storage outage503, internal/unclassified failure500. Preserve single/Mongo and shipping read-then-write, seconds-floor/invalid-date precondition behavior. Refuse unsupported PG path operations rather than approximate Mongo semantics; no blanket exception conversion or new update language. Enable the API role only through explicit operator preview configuration and credential environment references maintainer, 2026-11-04 PLAT-SERVE, T30-WIRING, TEN-RESOLVE Implement nightscout multitenant api with already-provisioned schemas/tenants, read-only readiness/privilege checks, existing PG/Vault/current authority components and owned shutdown. Configuration describes tenant/provider bindings and credential environment-variable names, not secret values. Direct aliases reject proxy selectors by default; canonical mode requires explicit trusted immediate-peer configuration. No implicit migration, provisioning, single/Mongo fallback or owner/operator/realtime/evaluator role enablement. Static operator configuration is not a durable registry, automatic activation, production service identity or HA acceptance.

docs.title: Future fields and controller registration
docs.text: The specified registration contract already provides typed declarations, per-element version/capability negotiation, must-ignore grammar members, namespaced extensions and declared legacy carriers (sections 2-5). It is specified, not implemented. It can describe and negotiate future controller fields; it does not make an otherwise unrepresentable value storable, bypass authorization or authorize arbitrary schema execution. Legacy POST does not acquire a registration prerequisite. Unknown representable fields and unsupported storage shapes are different contracts; future schema upload does not waive current compatibility testing.

docs.title: Owner authority and local verification (2026-11-05)
docs.text: decision who, when queue as it stands Adopt explicit tenant-owner management authority, bounded delegation and reviewed roles; separate use from delegation. Enforce project catalogue, operator ceiling and actor delegation authority, including proposed role changes in the management transaction. No implicit elevation of data/root credentials. maintainer, 2026-11-05, owner-authority chat MT-CONFIG-MIN, T30-WIRING Owner authority contract is the state of record. Separate management audience/listener; explicitly provisioned headless credentials first, interchangeable human identity. Full ceiling/transfer/role implementation remains open. Adopt initial human management limits: 10-minute access token, 30-minute idle/12-hour absolute session, authentication within 5 minutes for reveal/ownership changes/privileged issuance. Preserve existing 8-hour device exchange and unattended machine renewal. maintainer, 2026-11-05, owner-authority chat MT-CONFIG-MIN, MT-IDENTITY-PLAN Current authorization on the next protected operation remains mandatory across workers; expiry is not revocation. Values are adopted policy, not measured production optima or implemented human sessions. Amend D22: new tokens are verified locally with public keys; non-exportable private signing keys stay in the secrets component. PostgreSQL holds current tenant/session/credential/grant/policy and key-acceptance state. Cache public keys, never stale grants. maintainer, 2026-11-05, owner-authority chat MT-SECRETS-CONTRACT, T30-WIRING Ordinary new-token operations do not call Vault. Existing tokens may continue during Vault outage only with trusted cached keys and current PostgreSQL authority; issuance/secret operations refuse; unavailable authority refuses reads/writes. Ed25519 is the prototype, pending production JOSE/provider interoperability. Distinguish first-party credential records from recoverable secrets: use PostgreSQL metadata/one-way verifiers where compatible; retain encrypted legacy derivation material while needed. Vendor/cloud/connect/APNs values remain recoverable by authorized consumers under the secrets component. maintainer, 2026-11-05, owner-authority chat MT-SECRETS-CONTRACT, T30-WIRING Transit protects keys; tenant-bound ciphertext/references remain in PostgreSQL. JWTs are credentials, not signing keys. No change to single-tenant MongoDB/legacy defaults, provider KV selection, release admission or production enablement.

docs.title: B7 durable multitenant delivery (2026-11-06)
docs.text: decision who, when queue as it stands Adopt B7's durable multitenant delivery design direction and executable entry bar. Use tenant-local durable checkpoints, commit-coupled ordering, at-least-once replay and idempotent consumers. Run experiments to inform scalability/performance; per-tenant costs are an architectural hypothesis, not a measured capacity. maintainer, 2026-11-06, B7 approval chat ("let's approve as appropriate"; experiments should inform scalability/performance) MT-RUNTIME-PLAN Contract and experiment questions. Design direction adopted; recovery controls and workload-specific capacity remain UNMEASURED. Notification/checkpoint crash boundaries and intermediate-transition retention require explicit experiments. Provider selection, hard-delete recovery, multi-node failover, default enablement, M5/M6 promotion and release admission remain separate.
