docs.title: Multitenant completion execution
docs.text: decision who, when queue as it stands Complete the roadmap in capability/criterion lanes and coherent implementation batches, with targeted checks and early uncertainty proofs. A covers data/control/clients (M0–M4), B durable runtime (M5), C synthetic operations (M6). maintainer, 2026-11-06, completion batches adopted and completion-focused coordination reaffirmed Existing multitenant items; milestone scope and manifest claims unchanged The completion schedule and criterion matrix define delivery. Coordination rules keep helper changes, fixtures and controls within one owned capability. Focused checks support implementation; the coordinator freezes the combined candidate for comprehensive full/browser/enabled-corpus acceptance and final prcheck. Preserve failures and diagnose narrowly before freezing planned repairs; do not repeat broad campaigns per leaf, control or resumption. Repair/preflight setup-only failures before retrying the intended campaign. Early architectural/critical-boundary proofs remain, with explicit exit conditions. Report criteria closed, remaining blockers and next join/owner with evidence links, using one evolving lane handoff and coherent batch acceptance record. Exact-source attribution, meaningful controls, milestone criteria, notification/production gates and publication authority remain unchanged.

docs.title: Multitenant promotion bars (2026-11-06)
docs.text:
Decided in the open-decisions discussion (note).

decision who, when queue as it stands M2 is held to the roadmap's cell: tenant-local config and versioned writes, unknown-tenant refusal, A's token fails on B by signature, no environment/root/key leakage, separate owner/data/operator routes. The dashboard's four additions (human issuer/refresh, existing-grant clamping, tenant lifecycle, production trust for resolution) are M6 criteria and move there in the dashboard and status overlay maintainer, 2026-11-06 (open-decisions item 2, "roadmap cell") T30-WIRING, T30-TENANT-ADMIN, TEN-RESOLVE R72 accepts actual typed/versioned owner settings and comprehensive OWNER/DATA/operator separation; M2 promoted under this bar. Human issuer/refresh, wider catalogue/lifecycle and production trust retain M6 scope. M4 promotes on executed headless clients plus source-pattern replay for the rest, with the "no all-client claim" line in the record; an Android emulator lab (xDrip+, AndroidAPS) is a batch C item, not an M4 prerequisite; iOS execution stays out of the automated lab maintainer, 2026-11-06 (open-decisions item 4) TEN-LAB, M4-CLIENT-LAB R72 accepts M3 and then M4 through actual pinned headless clients and source-pattern replay. No all-client claim; Android emulator C, iOS outside automated execution. The optional subject-reader catalogue-clamping mode ("selected owner mode", joined dormant in R62, measured against actual clients in R63) is dropped. It breaks backward compatibility: a tenant's own API_SECRET, sent as the api-secret header by cgmsim and most legacy uploaders, has no subject row under the mode and is refused (503 observed). The maintainer wants backward-compatible solutions only: a tenant's api-secret gets 200 on its own tenant resource. Per-subject clamping, if it returns, comes through the M6 lifecycle work (lifecycle packet Q4) in a form that keeps existing credentials working maintainer, 2026-11-06 (open-decisions item 1: "I don't recall creating these modes; this mode would destroy backwards compatibility and should be dropped; we want backward compat solutions") MT-CONFIG-MIN, T30-WIRING, T30-TENANT-ADMIN Removed and joined in accepted/published 74d7b3fc on draft #8898. R72 preserves own-tenant legacy API_SECRET compatibility and management-writer fences. R62/R63 remain historical source-attributed measurements; no replacement reader mode is introduced. Batch C's backup/restore and upgrade/rollback get their own lane now, opened by the open-decisions session off 83582e87, depending only on the migration runner and R62's populated restore lab; bounds wait for the benchmark window and the final-tree review for the frozen C candidate maintainer, 2026-11-06 (open-decisions item 5, "new lane now, this session") MT-RUNTIME-PLAN, MIG-RUNNER Representative entries/clock proof on f77c025f passes its native boundary. Original Claude worktree preserved; broader catalogue/durable backup/operations acceptance remains separate C work. Its application source is not joined to the A candidate. Numeric bounds and performance budgets are deferred to batch C: no threshold is approved now; M1 may promote with "resource bounds: deferred, measured in C" stated; one controlled benchmark window (benchmark flag on, quiet machine, steady state, independent stored-count oracle) sets thresholds. The PostgreSQL sort-key cap stays at 5 and is recorded as an intentional PG-only difference maintainer, 2026-11-06 (open-decisions item 3) ST-PG, MT-RUNTIME-PLAN R65's figures stay descriptive. The benchmark window has no lane yet. Tenant deletion keeps the tenant's Transit keys and export artifact for a retention window, then an operator destroys the keys (lifecycle decision 1, option (a)): executing a deletion removes secret and audit rows only after the artifact holds every ciphertext and key reference; keys are never deleted at execute time, so a restore within the window recovers credentials in full; at the window's end key destruction cryptographically erases the artifact's secrets. Retention window: 30 days, the recommended default; the maintainer set no other value maintainer, 2026-11-07, via session -8c ("a") MT-RUNTIME-PLAN, Batch C mechanism measured in R69 on fd827e35 (keys retained, artifact decrypts after re-import); the destroy step and the restore-after-window refusal are UNMEASURED and are the first controls when wired Restore preserves the original tenant ID; cloning/import into another tenant is a separate operation with new destination secrets and credentials. Clinical/data import and synchronization do not migrate credential authority. Cross-tenant cryptographic remapping requires a separately reviewed contract. maintainer, 2026-11-06 (restore-versus-clone reply in the completion review) MT-RUNTIME-PLAN, Batch C / M6 Existing original-tenant import binding remains. R69 retains its historical executed source and results; representative backup/upgrade proof remains at its entries/clock scope. Cloning implementation and native acceptance are UNMEASURED. This adds no M1–M4 gate. Bounded snapshot reconciliation first for M5 current-state recovery: reconcile the full admitted current identity/absence set in a consistent tenant snapshot, with explicit row/byte refusal. Preserve existing hard-delete, activity timestamp and write-result behavior. Retained change/deletion journals, every-transition semantics and notification delivery remain separate contracts. maintainer, 2026-11-06 ("Bounded snapshot reconciliation first (recommended)") MT-RUNTIME-PLAN, M5 Adopted after the separate0bcdec22 native characterization reproduced stale deleted projection and unstamped activity refusal. Product reconciliation implementation/native acceptance remains UNMEASURED; scan cadence/capacity thresholds remain C. This adds no M1–M4 gate or production/default enablement. First-preview ownership changes are operator-assisted. Self-service co-owner addition and ownership transfer are later enhancements, not first-preview gates. Keep explicit owner relationships, last-owner protection, audited private-operator execution and no automatic operator access to owner secrets. Prefer a minimal working base with incremental enhancements; a scope deferral remains explicit and does not waive other milestone criteria. maintainer, 2026-11-06 ("Operator-assisted ownership changes are fine for the first preview"; incremental enhancement from a simpler base is acceptable) T30-TENANT-ADMIN, M6 Operator-assisted transaction/recovery and native acceptance remain UNMEASURED. The roadmap acceptance families specify required evidence. Human session, alarm delivery and resource policies are separate decisions. Use one shared optional OIDC integration for single-tenant and multitenant Nightscout, with provider-backed renewal first and separate authorization adapters. Provide equivalent human-authentication/renewal support in both modes; single-tenant opt-in should use ENABLE=oidc or an equivalent explicit feature flag, with ENABLE=oidc the preferred interface. Identity verification/session integration is shared; local single-tenant authority and current tenant-scoped multitenant authority remain distinct. Preserve existing data/machine credentials and do not infer root or management authority from login. maintainer, 2026-11-06 (shared OIDC, provider-backed renewal, equivalent optional single/multitenant support) MT-IDENTITY-PLAN, T30-TENANT-ADMIN, M6 Shared integration contract owns placement and parity acceptance. No Nightscout-owned rotating refresh credential is required initially. Login/callback/exchange/renewal, cookie transport, upstream logout, idle activity and outage acceptance remain UNIMPLEMENTED/UNMEASURED; no provider, route spelling, browser UI or production enablement is selected by this decision. During an OIDC provider outage, existing valid Nightscout human access may continue only until its existing token or session expires, subject to current local authority on every operation. Do not extend token/session lifetimes or allow new provider login or renewal while unavailable. Preserve the management-token ceiling of 10 minutes and sensitive-action authentication freshness requirements; local logout/revocation remains effective. Provider-only revocation can remain unknown until expiry or recovery. Apply equivalent behavior to optional single-tenant and multitenant OIDC; existing API_SECRET/device access keeps its current contract. maintainer, 2026-11-07 ("Allow existing valid access until expiry") MT-IDENTITY-PLAN, T30-TENANT-ADMIN, M6 Policy adopted; shared OIDC outage integration remains UNIMPLEMENTED/UNMEASURED. Acceptance must prove existing valid access, expiry without extension, login/renewal refusal, local logout/revocation and authority-store failure refusal during provider outage, sensitive-action freshness, recovery and enabled/disabled single/multitenant parity. Current management verification uses a 600-second ceiling and a current authority snapshot; these existing mechanisms alone do not prove the OIDC outage contract. Alarm acknowledgement/snooze suppresses the alarm group/level tenant-wide for the first preview, preserving single-tenant behavior. Retain the original absolute expiry across restart; ignore repeats during the active suppression window rather than extending it. Per-user/per-device suppression is a separate enhancement. maintainer, 2026-11-06 ("Tenant-wide suppression (recommended)", answering the scope/expiry/retry question) MT-RUNTIME-PLAN, M5 B7 alarm contract retains API persistence/D23 forwarding and existing level/default semantics. R73 accepts the bounded persisted/restart/actual-consumer effects. The existing client protocol has no durable request identity; this decision does not promise deduplication of a delayed retry after expiry or exactly-once external delivery. Historical row retention remains separate operational work. Use durable notification requests and retries for the explicit multitenant preview. Persist a tenant-bound stable request intent before dispatch and retry the same identity after ambiguous sends. Preserve existing tenant-wide suppression/original expiry, normal deduplication and single-tenant behavior. Verify notification-consumer impacts in the joined M5 candidate. maintainer, 2026-11-06 (direct reply in completion-coordination chat: "Let's proceed with durable notification requests and retries, preserving existing suppression and single-tenant behavior") MT-RUNTIME-PLAN, M5 B7 handoff contract distinguishes persisted intent, attempt, adapter acceptance and device delivery. Ambiguous acceptance can produce duplicate external notifications; clinical write identity does not deduplicate them. Failed clinical cycles create no ordinary clinical request; independently authorized committed ACK/snooze controls may create a control-clear request. Current authority/configuration and suppression govern dispatch. R73 accepts joined controlled-consumer, restart, isolation and shutdown effects. No exactly-once external guarantee, provider, retry cadence/capacity or production enablement is selected. First-preview tenant deletion requires an explicit request and operator confirmation, permits cancellation until execution starts, and has no mandatory pre-deletion waiting period. The owner request does not authorize execution on the owner interface. Keep verified export/recovery prerequisites and the separate adopted 30-day post-deletion key/artifact retention. maintainer, 2026-11-06 ("Operator confirmation, no mandatory wait (recommended)", answering the explicit request/cancellation/wait question) MT-RUNTIME-PLAN, M6 Lifecycle acceptance must prove current tenant/operator authority, explicit confirmation bound to the request/artifact, no effect after cancellation, and atomic cancellation-versus-execution claiming. No fixed waiting timer or proposed 14-day cancellation window is required. R73 accepts bounded synthetic SQL confirmation/cancellation/execution/rollback controls. Complete production authority/recovery/key-retention admission remains M6; artifact retention is not the cancellation period.

docs.title: Human sessions and tenant restore direction (2026-11-07)
docs.text:
The OIDC provider-outage decision owns existing-access, expiry, renewal and local-revocation policy.

decision who, when queue as it stands Test allocator-preserving original-tenant restore first; preserve other tenants' current state. A bounded shared write pause is acceptable for the preview only if measurements establish it is needed and its recovery protocol is explicit. maintainer, 2026-11-07, session/restore discussion and pause-risk clarification TEN-RESOLVE, MT-RUNTIME-PLAN, M6 First test exact original insertion ordinals with the existing live allocator unchanged; no tenant-local rewind or regenerated public record identity. Equivalent internal-order representations remain proposals requiring consumer/compatibility review. Keep the tenant-local history clock independent. A pause must cover admitted writers/in-flight work, refuse unsafe resumption after interruption and verify restoration before reopening. A deadline alone cannot authorize resumption; no deterministic recovery duration, numerical outage budget or blanket global-fence admission is inferred. Compare narrower tenant exclusion and alternatives before introducing a shared pause. Product identity-bearing tenant import remains unsupported pending implementation and evidence. Prior discriminator.

docs.title: Tenant-local restore continuation and consumer compatibility (2026-11-07)
docs.text: decision who, when queue as it stands Proceed with same-deployment original-tenant restore while preserving other tenants' current state and supported relative ordering. maintainer, 2026-11-07, tenant-local restore clarification and subsequent insertion-state simplification TEN-RESOLVE, MT-RUNTIME-PLAN, M6 Retain the tenant-local history clock. Tenant-local insertion semantics owns the allocator design direction. The existing-allocator proof remains source-attributed feasibility evidence. Read-only advisory preflight cannot authorize execution: complete held-A serving/writer exclusion and revalidation remain required. Shared-pause allowance remains conditional; no global restore pause is selected.

docs.title: Tenant-local insertion semantics (2026-11-07)
docs.text: decision who, when queue as it stands Require insertion order only within a selected tenant/collection; no cross-tenant ordering or globally meaningful insertion number is required. Pursue tenant-local insertion state to remove shared allocator maintenance from tenant restoration. maintainer, 2026-11-07, consumer/Byzantine-fault discussion and explicit simplification request TEN-RESOLVE, MT-RUNTIME-PLAN, M6 Preserve public record IDs, documents/history and supported per-tenant first-match/natural ordering. Existing mobile/data clients retain tenant-local behavior; private ordinal values are not a public identity. Prototype per-domain forced-RLS counter rows and invoker triggers without new service, per-tenant sequences, SECURITY DEFINER or dependence on optional history-clock composition. Source/native feasibility precedes migration/role/readiness/lifecycle integration and final joined acceptance. Current shared-allocator preflight is retained as bounded evidence, not selected as the target architecture. The one-time operator schema conversion requires ordinary DDL exclusion; no global restore pause is selected.

docs.title: Same-ID restore history continuity (2026-11-07)
docs.text: decision who, when queue as it stands Publish normal history updates and deletion records during same-ID logical restore so existing clients converge automatically. maintainer, 2026-11-07, explicit choice after the reproduced stale-cache protocol TEN-RESOLVE, MT-RUNTIME-PLAN, M6 Preserve the authoritative live history floor before destructive changes. Compare current and captured tenant records; publish restored/changed values and post-backup deletions above issued cursors, preserving public IDs, clinical fields and per-tenant relative ordering. Exact raw snapshot server metadata is a separate physical-backup contract. Reconcile current authority, checkpoints and retained caches deliberately; do not rewind them indiscriminately. Publish effects only after the actual outer restore transaction commits; ambiguous commit outcomes require verification, not automatic replay/reopening. Preserve other tenants' current state without a global pause. Protocol evidence establishes the problem, not implementation acceptance. The initial guarantee covers identities retained in the live tenant or artifact, matching existing retained-history behavior. Identifiers already hard-purged from both sources are outside that guarantee; no new universal identity journal or all-time/all-client cache guarantee is required. Missing or invalid authoritative live floors still refuse.

docs.title: Restore across separate service processes (2026-11-07)
docs.text: decision who, when queue as it stands Preserve separately deployable API, realtime, evaluator and tenant-admin processes for restore integration. maintainer, 2026-11-07, deployment clarification MT-RUNTIME-PLAN, MT-DOC-DEPLOY, M6 The maintainer expects container/process composition, potentially Compose or jsonnet and shared private sockets. No particular packaging generator is selected. A single-process cohort was a prototype limitation, not an adopted deployment requirement. Extend actual participant registration, tenant-local operation draining and cache/socket invalidation across configured processes. Separate processes do not by themselves require a new database-enforced fence; assess concrete bypasses under the declared credential and ingress trust boundary. An observed-session census is diagnostic/refusal, not physical exclusion of future raw clients. Preserve tenant B and existing clients without a global pause; cross-process native acceptance remains required.

docs.title: First-preview owner surface (2026-11-07)
docs.text:
Decided in the owner-surface discussion (packet read from the M5 head f0fac99a, the dev census and the schema candidate). The D22 floors restated on 2026-10-27 stand and were not re-asked: API_SECRET/API_SECRET_FILE and IMPORT_CONFIG refuse under multi; TRUST_PROXY and API3_SECURITY_ENABLE are deployment floors; DEBUG_LOGGING is pinned off; DBSIZE_* and TREATMENTS_AUTH are not offered; BASE_URL is derived; API3_AUTOPRUNE_* is pinned off unless an operator sets a minimum; anonymous roles are limited to denied, readable and status-only.

decision who, when queue as it stands First-preview owner-writable settings are the projected display catalogue: the client keys the tenant environment already projects (lib/server/tenant-app/environment.js:6-16 on f0fac99a: units, time format, day start/end, night mode, show seconds, edit mode, raw BG, custom title, theme, the alarm enables and minute windows, time-ago warnings, pump battery warning, language, scale, show plugins/forecast, focus hours, heartbeat, clock delta/last time, authentication prompt) plus the plugin enable list, each typed and under operator open/bounded/pinned policy. Every other name is unsupported on the owner surface and refuses by name. maintainer, 2026-11-07 ("Projected display keys (Recommended)") MT-CONFIG-MIN, T30-TENANT-ADMIN, M6 Only DISPLAY_UNITS and SHOW_SECONDS are implemented and measured (R72). The remaining keys are operator-static JSON per tenant today (lib/server/serve/preview-config.js:135); their owner-writable path, operator policy rows and the evaluator/presentation consumers reading a committed change are UNIMPLEMENTED/UNMEASURED. The full per-tenant census class is not declared implemented. Glucose thresholds (bgHigh, bgTargetTop, bgTargetBottom, bgLow) and the four alarm enables are owner-writable in the first preview, stored in mg/dL, bounded 30–600 as decided on 2026-10-29, partial threshold input refused, an operator default per threshold. This supersedes the 2026-10-27 "hidden until the alarm gate" direction now that R73 accepted the durable M5 evaluator and alarm suppression on one host. maintainer, 2026-11-07 ("Owner-writable, bounded (Recommended)") MT-CONFIG-MIN, MT-RUNTIME-PLAN, M6 UNIMPLEMENTED/UNMEASURED. Required evidence: the evaluator consumes a committed owner threshold on its next cycle, a partial or out-of-bounds write refuses without a partial row, and a mmol display setting never rewrites a stored mg/dL threshold (BF-67). Live external delivery remains the separate provider decision. Owner credential management is single-tenant equivalent within the data-plane catalogue: an owner creates and revokes subjects and defines roles from any Shiro permission string single tenant accepts, wildcards included (*, *:*:read, api:treatments:*), under the operator ceiling if one is set. Role permissions are evaluated by the same shiro-trie checker as single tenant (lib/tenant-authorization/postgres.js:41-46, lib/tenant-authorization/access-postgres.js:70-76). Shipped default roles are provisioned per tenant as single tenant ships them (lib/authorization/storage.js:239-245: admin = *, readable = *:*:read). Management authority is the owner relationship, not a data permission string. maintainer, 2026-11-07 ("Single-tenant equivalent (Recommended)"; amended the same day: "it should accept wildcards, same as single tenant", replacing the wildcards-expanded, 37-terminal form first recorded) T30-TENANT-ADMIN, M6 The ceiling check is measured (R53) but only over the 37-terminal universe: lib/subject-admin/owner-policy.js:38-41 refuses any permission outside it, so the implementation lane must replace the set-intersection ceiling check with a Shiro-implication check that accepts wildcard grants under a wildcard or concrete ceiling, and the R53 controls must be re-run on that. Subject creation, credential issuance, role creation and per-tenant default-role provisioning are UNIMPLEMENTED/UNMEASURED. Anonymous roles stay clamped to :read (lib/tenant-authorization/postgres.js:51-55). This replaces the "reviewed roles first, role editing later" phasing in owner-authority.md. Clients holding today's admin token keep data-route behaviour under *; management calls through the authorization API differ by design. A proposal to tighten permission strings (refusing wildcards, bounding roles to a terminal catalogue) applies to single and multitenant alike and is handled as a separate proposal. The multitenant effort targets the same behaviour as single tenant; it does not introduce a stricter permission model on its own. maintainer, 2026-11-07 ("If there's a proposal to tighten, it should probably affect both, let's treat such a proposal separately; this large effort has been towards same behavior") T30-TENANT-ADMIN, M6 No such proposal is open. The terminal-universe bound in lib/subject-admin/owner-policy.js and its README ("wildcard role permissions refuse") is an artefact of the R53 bounded acceptance, not a product decision, and is superseded by the row above. No owner-configurable integrations in the first preview. The four lab kinds (push relay, app push, webhook, CGM connector) and the secret-reference schema stay ready; the owner surface lists them as unsupported. Revisit after the live notification provider is admitted. The first integration kind is the tenant-side Nightscout connector, operator-entered in the first preview. maintainer, 2026-11-07 ("None in first preview (Recommended)") MT-SECRETS-CONTRACT, T30-TENANT-ADMIN, M6 No integration code is owner-reachable on f0fac99a; the notification component takes an explicitly supplied adapter and selects no provider. Operator-side kind limits and host allow-lists remain the schema candidate's measured lab contract, not product code.

docs.title: First-preview external delivery channel (2026-11-07)
docs.text:
Decided in the live-notification-provider discussion (packet read from the M5 head f0fac99a: lib/server/pushnotify.js, lib/tenant-notifications/README.md, lib/server/serve/roles.js:81-87 and the pinned nightscout-connect 0.1.0 Nightscout source driver). The 2026-10-27 outbound-endpoint floor stands: connector endpoints under an operator allow-list or public-address rule, BASE_URL derived.

decision who, when queue as it stands The first multitenant preview admits no live push provider. Alarms reach the unchanged client over the socket (in-app). The first external channel is Nightscout-to-Nightscout synchronization through the existing nightscout-connect Nightscout source driver (CONNECT_SOURCE=nightscout, source endpoint, optional source API secret), in both directions, outbound admitted first: a family's existing single-tenant site pulls from the tenant using a pre-issued tenant reader credential (an existing-client read, no new tenant code); the tenant-side connector (tenant pulls from the family's existing site) is built as the first integration kind in the declared vcpool connector role, writing through the tenant's own API as a tenant-bound subject with operator-entered endpoint/secret held as tenant secrets. Pushover and Maker are deferred; Pushover is next when a push provider is taken up. Loop APNs is a command channel, not an alarm provider, and the arbitrary-host webhook plugin stays out until a host allow-list exists. maintainer, 2026-11-07 ("in-app alarms or Nightscout configuration for nightscout-connect nightscout:nightscout sync"; "Let's do Nightscout-Connect using the Nightscout backend first"; "Both; admit outbound first (Recommended)") MT-RUNTIME-PLAN, MT-SECRETS-CONTRACT, M6 Outbound direction is covered by M4's measured existing-client surface but no connector sync has been run against a tenant: UNMEASURED. The driver's auto-creation of its nightscout-connect-reader subject does not work against a tenant until subject creation lands, so the first preview issues the reader credential first. The vcpool role has no start and no per-tenant code: UNIMPLEMENTED. No push adapter exists. Integration credentials are split into parts per kind; a part is operator-owned or owner-owned, and neither side can read the other's parts. When Pushover is adopted, all its parts are owner-owned by default (the family's own application token and keys, single-tenant equivalent), with an operator-owned alternative where a kind needs it. maintainer, 2026-11-07 ("Owner-owned, all parts (Recommended)"; "some plugins we may need flexibility for operator to own it, and/or for owner to bring their own, without leaking operator creds to the owners and vice versa") MT-SECRETS-CONTRACT, M6 The schema candidate's lab measured per-kind owner/operator credential parts and the no-plaintext scan; product code holds no integration credentials yet. Secret reveal remains a separate reauthenticated permission under owner authority. Initial notification and connector operating bounds are the single-tenant constants (15-minute normal dedup, one-hour receipt window, 30-second minimum retry, the connector's existing page size and poll alignment) together with the durable component's existing explicit page/payload/inflight/attempt-timeout/retry-delay limits. Retention, backlog, cadence and egress budgets are measured in the batch C benchmark window before any production or capacity claim. maintainer, 2026-11-07 ("Single-tenant constants first (Recommended)") MT-RUNTIME-PLAN, Batch C No budget value is approved as a pass threshold; functional passes establish none. External delivery is admitted by probes and tests appropriate to the channel, not by a human-observed device. Nightscout-to-Nightscout sync is admitted by a lab sync between the frozen candidate's tenant and a local single-tenant Nightscout in each direction, with an independent stored-state oracle and a second tenant shown untouched. A push provider, when adopted, is admitted on synthetic consumer proofs plus a recorded request/response contract; its first live delivery is on an operator's own deployment. maintainer, 2026-11-07 ("we prioritized Nightscout:Nightscout plugin, can't we use probes/test as appropriate") MT-RUNTIME-PLAN, M6 R73 measured the durable handoff with a synthetic consumer only. The two-direction lab sync is UNMEASURED and needs a local single-tenant Nightscout beside the candidate; credentials for any lab come only from the environment.

docs.title: M6 human session effects (2026-11-07)
docs.text:
Decided in the human-session discussion (packet read from the M5 head f0fac99a: lib/server/serve/owner-preview-authentication.js:7-19 (600-second management ceiling, bearer only), lib/server/subject-management-app.js:70-86, lib/tenant-authorization/access-postgres.js (read-only current-authority snapshot; access_sessions carries purpose, expires_at, active and no idle timestamp), lib/client/hashauth.js:244-256 (secret hash in localStorage; sign-out forgets it locally) and lib/client/browser-settings.js:166-182 (?token= carried on links); no cookie infrastructure exists in the application). The shared OIDC, provider-outage and 2026-11-05 lifetime rows stand and were not re-asked. Everything below is adopted policy; human login, sessions, cookies and provider logout remain UNIMPLEMENTED/UNMEASURED.

decision who, when queue as it stands The adopted idle (30-minute) and absolute (12-hour) lifetimes apply to the human management session only; data viewing is unchanged. Ambient and always-on displays keep today's non-expiring data credentials (secret hash, read token, 8-hour device exchange with silent renewal) in both modes, and a viewer signed in through OIDC receives a data session with no idle limit. Any successful authenticated request on a management route advances the management idle deadline; data polling, socket keepalives, stream delivery, health checks and renewal never do. maintainer, 2026-11-07 ("1? How easy is this to change later?", after asking whether an idle lifetime had been decided and that always-on tablets must not be affected) MT-IDENTITY-PLAN, T30-TENANT-ADMIN, M6 The lifetimes were adopted on 2026-11-05 for management access; this row fixes their scope. Change cost: lifetimes are per-purpose policy values and route classification is a per-route attribute, so widening idle to data sessions or changing the numbers later needs no schema or client change (read-derived from the purpose column and the adopted policy table; the lifecycle writer that enforces idle does not exist yet). Check and touch happen atomically; a touch never resets the absolute deadline or the 5-minute sensitive-action freshness. Headless callers need no activity. An explicit client activity signal may be added later on top; it is not required. Where a server-side session exists, logout commits Nightscout session invalidation first, then clears the browser credential, then calls the provider's logout when it has one; where no server session exists, sign-out stays browser-only as today. Provider-originated logout is applied when the provider sends a verifiable signal bound to the configured issuer and the mapped session; providers without a logout or revocation signal are admitted with the limitation disclosed (provider revocation becomes visible at expiry or renewal). Logout never revokes unrelated device credentials or other sessions implicitly; an all-sessions logout, if offered, is a separate explicit action. maintainer, 2026-11-07 ("1 or 3 as appropriate", confirmed as this reading) MT-IDENTITY-PLAN, T30-TENANT-ADMIN, M6 A provider timeout after the local commit cannot restore the session; a provider response alone never counts as local revocation. If the session store is unavailable, clear the browser material and return an explicit local-revocation-unconfirmed result. Legacy secret-hash and ?token= sign-in (hashauth.js:252-256) keeps its current local-forgetting meaning and is not repurposed. Acceptance: two workers share one session, logout through one, replay through the other and protected stream delivery refuse; break durable invalidation and the copied token must stay authorized (red). No propagation delay is promised. Concurrent renewal is fenced and idempotent per session. Renewal re-checks idle, absolute, revocation and current Nightscout authority inside one transaction on the session row; expired or revoked state is never resurrected; concurrent renewals of a live session all succeed with tokens bound to the same session; renewal never resets the absolute deadline or authentication freshness. A new session after explicit re-authentication is distinguishable from rolling renewal. maintainer, 2026-11-07 ("Fenced, idempotent per session") MT-IDENTITY-PLAN, T30-TENANT-ADMIN, M6 No Nightscout-owned single-use rotating grant is introduced (the shared OIDC row defers it); last-writer-wins without fencing is rejected because a renewal racing a logout could issue a token after revocation committed. Acceptance: expire or revoke before a pending renewal releases and no usable token appears; break the fence and a new accepted token must appear (red); verify stored absolute and fresh-authentication timestamps independently of the helper that writes them. Both browser transports are supported, with the HttpOnly cookie as the default when OIDC is enabled; headless bearer is unchanged. The human session rides an HttpOnly, Secure, SameSite cookie scoped to the serving host with CSRF/origin checks on state-changing routes. Direct-token mode remains available so the legacy client behaviour and single/multitenant parity hold under OIDC optionality. Both modes receive the same acceptance in single and multitenant. maintainer, 2026-11-07 ("3, 1", confirmed as both with cookie default: "this ordering supports OIDC optionality and keeps single and multitenant the same") MT-IDENTITY-PLAN, T30-TENANT-ADMIN, M6 The application has no cookie layer today; cookie mode adds cookie parsing, CSRF/origin checks and browser tests (scope, logout, back button, cross-tab); direct-token mode needs the equivalent replay and session-boundary tests. A page-script compromise can read a direct token but not an HttpOnly cookie, which is why cookie is the default. Existing management bearer authentication (owner-preview-authentication.js) is not replaced. No provider, library or route spelling is selected.

docs.title: M6 deployment and trust (2026-11-07)
docs.text:
Decided in the deployment-trust discussion (packet read from the M5 head f0fac99a: lib/tenant-resolution/index.js and README.md (direct-alias rejects proxy headers; canonical-internal requires an exact synchronous trusted-peer predicate on every request; measured R33), lib/server/serve/preview-config.js:92-148 (peer list by socket address; one static Vault token per tenant from an environment reference), lib/secrets/vault-transit.js:29-49 (HTTPS required except loopback; async getToken seam; no renewal), lib/server/client-ip.js (single-tenant TRUST_PROXY, empty by default), the compose deployment lane (deploy/multitenant/* on b029f5d8: four role containers, nginx, PostgreSQL, Vault over HTTPS from a local CA, one-share unseal, bootstrap-issued scoped tokens; image built, cold compose smoke UNMEASURED) and the Ory proof (Kratos, Hydra, PostgreSQL, a mail catcher and the lab's own Node login page; 23/23). Everything below is adopted policy; no real edge, operator CA, service login, provider over HTTPS or production deployment has run.

decision who, when queue as it stands The reference deployment trusts its edge by immediate peer address, and one explicit peer list serves both tenant selection and client-IP trust. Canonical-internal mode runs with the edge on a private network and the app trusting the immediate peer by socket address. The same list feeds TRUST_PROXY; an empty TRUST_PROXY refuses to start a multitenant role. Direct-alias remains for a single edge that passes the public Host through. Authenticated transport (mTLS, unix socket) is a later adapter behind the same predicate, not a precondition. maintainer, 2026-11-07 ("Peer-list trust, one list for both") TEN-RESOLVE, T30-WIRING, M6 Today the preview peer list and TRUST_PROXY are separate settings; joining them and the empty-refusal are implementation. Forwarded selectors stay refused outside the trusted peer; conflict and spoof fail closed as measured in R33. Public domains, certificates and the edge implementation remain deployment concerns. One secrets provider, Vault Transit, at every stage, so no record is ever re-encrypted between stages; the service-login adapter is the one code item and is required before production use. Developer: dev-mode Vault on loopback HTTP as the lab runs. Staging: the compose deployment as built (local CA over HTTPS, one-share unseal, static scoped tokens from bootstrap). Production: the same compose and configuration shape with an operator or public CA, multi-share or auto-unseal custody, and a service login with lease renewal behind the existing getToken seam. Every other transition is configuration. maintainer, 2026-11-07 ("All of these options are good; is it increasing work? Can we do 1 and then add the other incrementally?") MT-SECRETS-CONTRACT, T30-WIRING, M6 Incremental by construction: the login adapter may land in staging as soon as it exists (that is ordering, not extra work), and the adopted built-in encrypted signer remains a later additional provider behind the same interface. Ciphertext is bound to its provider key, so a tenant that later moves between providers must re-encrypt every record; that cost is why the ladder keeps one provider. Static tokens are operator-rotated with no renewal; loopback HTTP stays lab-only. Nothing here changes single-tenant MongoDB or legacy defaults. Generic OIDC adapter; Authentik is the intended reference provider because it bundles the login UI, the OIDC provider and administration in one deployment, subject to passing the same proof Kratos passed; Kratos stays the measured fallback reference. The adapter contract is issuer, audience, subject and session claims and optional back-channel logout; any conforming provider is configuration. Single tenant uses the same adapter under ENABLE=oidc. maintainer, 2026-11-07 ("Is 2 easier to test/develop since it includes login UI? Otherwise 1.") MT-IDENTITY-PLAN, T30-TENANT-ADMIN, M6 Read, not run: every Authentik claim. Kratos is headless by design, so its reference needs a separate self-service UI; the Ory proof used the lab's own Node page. Before Authentik ships as the reference, repeat the Ory proof's isolation, revocation, cookie and logout cases against it on the generic adapter, including the local-first logout row. If it fails, Kratos configuration ships as the reference. No first-party login UI is added either way. A deployment is admitted for production use by a written trust record plus spoof, conflict and outage probes run against its live edge and Vault. The trust record names edge peers, TLS and CA, Vault authentication and unseal custody, identity provider and TRUST_PROXY. The maintainer reviews the reference deployment's record once; any other deployment is admitted the same way by its operator. Real-data and default role enablement remain separate approvals. maintainer, 2026-11-07 ("Probes per deployment plus a trust record") MT-RUNTIME-PLAN, T30-WIRING, M6 The probes exist as synthetic resolver and lab controls; running them against a live edge, an HTTPS Vault and a provider is UNMEASURED. The compose deployment's CREDENTIALS.md is the seed of the reference trust record. Admission is not milestone promotion.

docs.title: Tenant-local startup admission (2026-11-07)
docs.text:
decision who, when queue as it stands A suspended tenant must not prevent other tenants from becoming ready when shared service processes restart. Resolve this coupling as a defect. maintainer, 2026-11-07, explicit rejection of the shared-role restart limitation TEN-RESOLVE, MT-RUNTIME-PLAN, M6 Start shared infrastructure while deferring only the suspended tenant's clinical admission. Preserve that tenant's unavailable responses, unresolved recovery state, leases, orphans and commit/invalidation uncertainty; do not clear a phase or serve stale output to make startup succeed. Shared schema, binding, ledger, ACL, datastore and transport failures still refuse startup. Acceptance requires fresh replacement processes to serve tenant B through actual HTTP, realtime and evaluator paths while tenant A remains unavailable and its protected state is unchanged. Running B continuity alone does not satisfy this criterion. Source implementation and native restart acceptance remain open; this does not adopt a broader HA or raw-private-writer guarantee.

Draft, 2026-10-26; rows added 2026-10-30 and 2026-10-31. Requires maintainer review before it is relied upon.

docs.title: Exclusive application ownership of PostgreSQL (2026-11-08)
docs.text: decision who, when scope as it stands Nightscout has exclusive application ownership of its selected PostgreSQL namespaces. Supported writers are its declared internal components and explicit provisioning, migration and lifecycle tools using their admitted contracts. Other direct database writers are unsupported; their effects are undefined behavior. maintainer, 2026-11-08, explicit ownership-contract instruction Multitenant PostgreSQL; consistent with single-tenant Nightscout's unsupported external MongoDB writers Ownership is collective across the application, not a single process or database connection. Internal components must preserve tenant binding/RLS, current authority, canonical write semantics, operation admission/drain and restore invalidation. Use application interfaces for commands across component ownership boundaries; direct storage access remains appropriate for admitted reads and component-owned persistence. Maintain scoped roles, private credentials and explicit maintenance authority. The cooperative protocol need not exclude an independently authorized raw SQL writer outside this supported contract. No stronger arbitrary-writer fence, new storage privilege or runtime acceptance follows. Component ownership and internal APIs describe the design direction and existing implementation boundaries.

docs.title: Deployment portability and public-name requirements (2026-11-08)
docs.text: decision / requirement who, when scope as it stands The bounded deployment should be expressible with ordinary Kubernetes resources, without requiring a particular Ingress or discovery implementation. Kubernetes packaging and potential Jsonnet bindings are distinct from distributed application ownership or HA. maintainer, 2026-11-08, deployment-target clarification Multitenant topology and production preparation Preserve the accepted cohort, transport, authority and recovery semantics. A public address can lead to the deployment's HTTP edge. Concrete Pod/resource layout and its restart/replacement behavior require qualification; no Kubernetes execution or HA acceptance is inferred. Binding contract. Separate permanent and ephemeral public names from private tenant identity; a shareable public address needs explicit strong human authentication and access policy. The target includes controls for anonymous allow/block, authenticated-group authorizations and potential scheduled permissions. maintainer, 2026-11-08, public-name/access clarification Public browser/access-policy surface Keep current owner/data/device boundaries. Exact alias-policy defaults, group mapping, schedule precedence/time semantics and admitted feature scope remain design/acceptance work; no policy engine or implementation is selected. Load-bearing metrics and synchronized-work/recovery experiments must address herd behavior. Public-name and load contract.

docs.title: Endpoint/API capability scope and orchestration boundary (2026-11-08)
docs.text: decision / direction who, when scope as it stands Plan and queue selectable UDS/HTTP(S) endpoints and fixed-roster independent API scaling, preserving restore and existing clients. maintainer, 2026-11-08 MT-ENDPOINT-TRANSPORT, MT-API-FIXED-ROSTER Implementation plan defines source/instrument boundaries and planned controls. Runtime implementation and acceptance are not started/UNMEASURED. Keep service routing separate from per-instance restore addressing; no transport trust/default chosen implicitly. Keep evaluator work singly owned; reuse orchestration primitives rather than building another membership service or scheduler. Kubernetes is an architecture frame and Jsonnet/deployment proof may be deferred. maintainer, 2026-11-08, scope clarification Architecture and implementation plan Current evaluator remains singleton. Predictable bounded work may favor singleton deployment when measured headroom and restart availability suffice; this sizing rule is distinct from logical single ownership. Future StatefulSet-style stable identities may supply disjoint partition identities; actual assignment/reassignment is a separate contract when pursued. The scoped native fixtures consume an explicit roster and test application lifetime/restore semantics. Grid topology and coupling guide distinguishes platform inputs from application invariants.

docs.title: REST API component and replica placement (2026-11-08)
docs.text: Decision Basis and scope Acceptance boundary Keep v1/v2/v3 REST routers/adapters together in one stateless request-serving api component. Replicas repeat the same configured admitted route set; replica count and Compose/Kubernetes placement are separate from API versioning. Maintainer requested this clarification after the source assessment; component contract links read-derived ed2 composition. Owner versus DATA audience/listener/credential boundaries remain; evaluator, realtime, connectors and private maintenance retain their responsibilities. Architecture clarification, no runtime change. Stateless instances still drain actual responses and invalidate reconstructible state during maintenance. No extra route/client coverage, API replication, Kubernetes, production or HA acceptance.

docs.title: Plan restructuring and process simplification (2026-11-09)
docs.text:
decision who, when scope as it stands The deployment tree (deploy/multitenant: Compose, nginx, bootstrap, restore, UI) lives in the sibling repository nightscout-deploy. Core keeps application code, the Dockerfile and a pointer. The move is not gated on re-running acceptance; the ed2 evidence keeps its attribution because the files are relocated, not changed. maintainer, 2026-11-09 (confirms item 1 of the deploy-companion note) Deployment packaging, edge, identity-provider profiles, secrets sidecars, operator CLI Imported with history on 2026-11-09 (bindings/compose/multitenant, byte-identity check against ed2). Deployment-trust work items carry repo: nightscout-deploy in the queue. Core's copy is removed when the Compose binding renders from a plan (deploy roadmap wave 2). Vault connectivity uses Vault Agent as a sidecar: auto-auth (AppRole in Compose, Kubernetes auth in that binding), token sink file, renewal and templating belong to the Agent. The application reads the token from the sink at call time and keeps its small Transit client. maintainer, 2026-11-09, "use established dependencies" Secrets ladder (supersedes "service-login adapter before production" as application work) Core supports tokenFile read at call time (MT-VAULT-TOKEN-FILE). The registry/fixed-replica Agent conversion and finite native lifecycle proof belong to DEPLOY-VAULT-AGENT: exact APIs read the serving sink; private provisioning and management credentials remain separate. No hand-rolled login or renewal in core. Final combined acceptance and capacity remain open. Native acceptance runs through a disposable harness, not a grant ceremony. Containers (PostgreSQL, Mongo, Vault) are started per run by digest and removed by the reaper; the run records the source commit it executed, its commands and its red controls. Lead reservations, grant JSON, chat-ID attestations and freshness windows are retired. maintainer, 2026-11-09, process-drag review Every native campaign from here on, starting with the owner/OIDC nine-stage matrix The prepared nine stages, their oracles and mutant controls are kept; the driver's grant/reservation preconditions are removed. Cleanup is a container lifetime, not a custody attestation. First application: MT-OIDC-NATIVE. M6 is split into four bounded milestones and a production milestone: M6a identity and owner API, M6b lifecycle and keys, M6c deployment trust (deploy repo), M6d connector sync; M7 production readiness holds the operating envelope, the Android lab, endpoint transport and API scaling, and the Kubernetes binding. Umbrella queue items whose accepted scope is on draft #8898 are closed as superseded; their remaining scope moves to one capability item each with one gate. maintainer, 2026-11-09 Roadmap milestone table, dashboard, queue Preview release needs M6a to M6d. M7 is required before any production cohort, not before the dormant alpha. Closed items keep their gates and evidence; MT-M6A-JOIN owns the coherent join and final campaign on #8898. The M7 operating envelope is measured, not declared. Benchmark the one-host reference at stepped tenant counts and publish the numbers; contrast the cohort against the deployment shapes operators run today at equal synthetic load; prove that API, realtime, evaluator, PostgreSQL and the Vault Agent each scale horizontally or vertically as intended, with no hidden binding. Limits are set from the measurements afterwards. maintainer, 2026-11-09 ("we just need to benchmark what the numbers are") M7 (MT-BENCH-BASELINE, MT-BENCH-CONTRAST, MT-SCALE-UNBOUND) Supersedes the "operator proposes workload first" ordering in the decision index and the production critical path. Workloads stay synthetic and pinned (cgmsim, oref0 replay, browser polling, reconnect floods); established load tooling; an independent stored-count oracle; the disposable-harness pattern. Any component whose scaling is capped by a shared singleton, lock, cache or file is a file:line finding, handled as a defect or design change, never a waiver. Prior provider tenant counts or incident figures are not imported. Evaluator scaling: a feature flag with two environment variables, the member count and this worker's ordinal, partitions tenants by hash onto a fixed slice; each evaluator works only its slice. Flag off means one evaluator owns every tenant, as today. Operator-configured, in the Consul bootstrap-expect style; a StatefulSet supplies the ordinal, the renderer sets the count. Exclusivity comes from a pool-membership table, not a per-tenant lock. maintainer, 2026-11-09 (discussion of ring/ordinal partitioning; per-tenant lease rejected as unnecessary overhead) Evaluator role, Compose and Kubernetes bindings; M7 MT-EVALUATOR-PARTITION Each member keeps one heartbeat row: ordinal, expected member count, assigned ring slice, lease expiry. Before each cycle a member reads the table; it evaluates its slice only while every live row agrees on the member count and no two live rows share an ordinal, and otherwise stops its own cycle and raises an alert. Cost is one row update per member per heartbeat instead of one claim per tenant per cycle. Duplicate evaluation is then bounded to one heartbeat interval after a membership change, and the evaluator's outputs are idempotent by contract (computed view keyed per tenant; notification intent with stable identity and suppression), so a brief overlap produces no duplicate clinical effect. A per-tenant commit fence is not required; if MT-SCALE-UNBOUND measures a duplicate external effect in the overlap window, that measurement reopens the question. Plain modulo is adequate; consistent hashing is an optimisation to measure. One AppRole per deployment for the Vault Agent, not one per tenant. Tenant separation at Vault is not a goal; it is provided by application authority and row-level security. The Agent's policy is a path pattern over the Transit mount, not a union of per-tenant policies. maintainer, 2026-11-09 ("if we are expecting potentially thousands of tenants, it needs to scale against one AppRole for the deployment") M6c DEPLOY-VAULT-AGENT; closes the open question in the decision index At thousands of tenants a per-tenant Agent or per-tenant token means thousands of containers or renewing leases; neither scales. The policy union is replaced by fixed path patterns in local delivery fa558353154c875312da984926a4efd83dfcbef6, with actual Agent renewal, reauthentication and refusal/recovery proof. The M7 profile seam derives the current six-key schema; the earlier two-key estimate is superseded. Actual capacity key-count observations remain separate from schema expectation.

| The OIDC browser client looks for a human session only when the page server marks the page as OIDC-enabled (<meta name="nightscout-human-sessions">, rendered when app.locals.humanSessions is set). Sites without OIDC start exactly as before. | maintainer, 2026-11-09 ("opt-in discovery ... fine") | M6a MT-M6A-JOIN, head 74036ba6 | A probe on every page produced a 404 console error and asynchronous startup on every default-off site, which failed the dom, browser and serving-status tests. Cost: a multitenant page server that wants browser sign-in must render the marker; the Compose UI does not yet. | | An owner may revoke (DELETE) subjects on their own site through the owner capability. | maintainer, 2026-11-09 ("owner DELETE ... fine") | M6a MT-M6A-JOIN, head 74036ba6 | The owner capability code in the candidate already permitted it; the tests now assert it. Same behaviour in single-site and multitenant modes. | | Direction for single-site OIDC: ENABLE=oidc switches it on; anonymous visitors keep AUTH_DEFAULT_ROLES; an operator-supplied list (environment or file, CSV/TSV/JSON) maps signed-in identities to existing roles such as careportal + readable; signed-in people not on the list fall back to a configured role such as readable. | maintainer, 2026-11-09 (direction); design settled in the lane 2026-11-10 | MT-OIDC-SINGLE-PROVISION | Fixed on local branch codex/oidc-single-provision-20261110 4b81f59d, joined into codex/m6b-join-20261110: OIDC_IDENTITIES / OIDC_IDENTITIES_FILE (CSV, TSV or JSON) keyed on issuer + provider subject, or an email the same issuer marks verified; OIDC_FALLBACK_ROLES for unlisted signed-in people (unset: refused, as before); a principal binds to an auth subject and reads its current roles; single-site may sign with a local Ed25519 key, so Vault is optional there. Evidence. Not pushed. | | The single-site identity list is authoritative: each start re-applies the listed roles and removes the bindings and subjects of list-managed people no longer on it. | maintainer, 2026-11-10 | MT-OIDC-SINGLE-PROVISION, single-site only | As built in lib/human-session/provision.js on 4b81f59d. An admin-UI role edit to a list-managed subject lasts until the next restart, and the subject's notes say so. Chosen over add-only, where removing someone from the file would leave their access in place. People bound outside the list are not touched; a list entry that collides with such a binding refuses at start. |

docs.title: Internal service API contracts and listener ownership (2026-11-09)
docs.text: decision who, when scope as it stands Internal APIs use shared transport with separate service contracts, request/response schemas, named clients and documentation. Each listener owns an explicit operation set; a component with a public contract opens a second listener/port for its private contract. Unix sockets and explicitly configured internal HTTP are supported. HTTP access policy belongs to the deployment; no new bearer authentication convention is introduced. maintainer, 2026-11-09, internal IPC/API refactor discussion Realtime authority/writes, alarm delivery, lifecycle participant coordination; public/private listener separation Incorporated in joined candidate dc795bd1515f11808a8d0732f2be9925cb2ffcd1; its recorded acceptance retains executed scope. UDS/HTTP schemas, clients and endpoint references exist; network qualification beyond loopback remains unmeasured. Current topology and remaining composition work distinguish private application/lifecycle purpose from listener allocation. Direct application calls retain existing authority; an optional JSON-to-status/header edge adapter does not imply an authentication redesign or mandatory gateway hop. Communicating peers require coordinated upgrade. No dev merge or operator release is claimed.

docs.title: Deploy companion, internal listener, activity policy and #8898 timing (2026-11-10)
docs.text: decision who, when scope as it stands nightscout-deploy (github nightscout/nightscout-deploy, pushed 2026-11-10) is the home of the Compose deployment tree from the next #8898 batch on, not from deploy wave 2. Core keeps only the fixture its own native and CI tests boot; #8898 drops or shrinks deploy/multitenant accordingly. maintainer, 2026-11-10 Refines deploy-tree-lives-in-nightscout-deploy; #8898, deploy repo Removes the byte-identity sync between the two copies. Changes that today land in deploy/multitenant/config.js (for example the ownership_operator grants) are written so they port to a deploy-repo overlay. Which core tests need the fixture is read from the tests in the batch, not assumed. The nightscout-deploy README addresses an operator: what runs today (Compose binding, Vault Agent overlay), how to run it, the core commit it pins. Placeholder directories stay, each saying in one line that it is not started; programme vocabulary (waves, gates) moves out of the front page. maintainer, 2026-11-10 ("looks written like a rough draft") nightscout-deploy README, roadmap, stub READMEs The pushed README (cda3826) is anchored to ed2ced00, calls the organisation home and licence "intended/pending" although both are now in place, and 7 of 13 areas are 4–8 line notes. Restore into a new deployment ends by calling ensure for each tenant and reports itself unfinished until that succeeds. maintainer, 2026-11-12 (chose "Resume op + check before closing") proposed MT-RESTORE-RESUME, MT-RESTORE-PREFLIGHT Reproduced at J debcc2c7 on deploy branch claude/recovery-drills-20261112 d479f77f: four interruption kinds left the tenant closed indefinitely; leftover markers from a killed api turned a restore into a permanent closure (lib/tenant-lifecycle/maintenance-window.js:143, :151-161). The only exit today is whole-deployment recovery, which loses every tenant's writes since the backup. Multitenant only. When PostgreSQL goes away, a role reports itself unhealthy while it cannot answer a tenant request, reconnects with backoff, rebuilds the tenant state it caches, and catches pool errors. It exits only when it cannot recover within a bound; then the restart policy takes over. maintainer, 2026-11-12 (chose "Health tells the truth + recover in place") proposed MT-DATASTORE-RESTART-RECOVERY Reproduced on the same drills: after a PostgreSQL restart every tenant was refused (edge 503) until all roles restarted, while container health stayed healthy; one earlier run saw tenant-admin exit on an unhandled pool error. Pools without an error listener read at lib/server/serve/index.js:97, lib/pool-membership/postgres.js:74. Workload plans for remote and capacity runs use real time (acceleration 1); local harness checks may accelerate. Overload studies use the hot-tenant family or more tenants. maintainer, 2026-11-12 (chose "Refuse remotely") proposed MT-WORKLOAD-FAMILIES Measured locally on deploy branch claude/workloads-20261112: at 60x on 12 tenants 77% of requests failed and the run was marked invalid, a shape that says nothing about tenant capacity. Implemented at c70c4386 with two break-it controls. Multitenant upgrades: the platform rolls the processes (Kubernetes rolling update, canary or blue-green; a restart sequence in Compose). Core supplies the shared-database part: two-step migrations (add first; remove only after no old version runs) so old and new code share one schema, a one-shot migration job (a Kubernetes Job or Helm hook), and pre- and post-checks (backup exists, no tenant closed or mid-restore, no shard move running; tenant census and per-tenant health afterwards). The recovery drills rehearse an interrupted migration and a rollback before the remove step. A new deployment remains the path for large jumps. maintainer, 2026-11-12 (asked why Kubernetes practices don't already solve this; adopted "migrations + checks, platform rolls") proposed MT-UPGRADE-OPERATOR-COMMAND Read at J: no in-place upgrade command exists and lib/tenant-operations is not wired to one (deploy branch claude/recovery-drills-20261112 d479f77f). One PostgreSQL holds every tenant, so every rollout runs old and new code against one schema. One deployment plan, in nightscout-deploy. Core publishes the contract a plan must produce (the role configuration schema and the provisioning CLI/REST interface) and keeps only a small test plan for its own tests. nightscout-deploy checks its plan against that contract instead of byte-matching core's file. Order: core publishes and checks the schema; deploy switches to contract checks; core moves its tests to the test plan and deletes deploy/multitenant/config.js. Hosting providers can build their own plans against the same contract. maintainer, 2026-11-12 (asked what is best for maintenance, testing and adoption by hosting providers; adopted "contract in core, plan in deploy") MT-STATIC-MODE-RETIRE (proposed), core-static-plan-retired Read at deploy 2e9afbb6: bindings/compose/SOURCE.md, SOURCE.delta.patch and tools/compose-identity-check.sh require core's deploy/multitenant plus a patch to equal the deploy copy byte for byte, so every plan change is made twice.

docs.title: Nightscout 16.0.0 - release notes (DRAFT)
docs.text:
Living document, last changed 2026-11-03 at 22d0bdd41.

Draft for maintainer review, 2026-11-03. Not a release announcement. The version is decided: 16.0.0. The current release candidate is official/dev 4a482627bfdafb1fef8dcbe0ac6c484811cae563. Informal testing is underway; private security integration and final release acceptance remain pending. No tag or v16 release is published.

Nightscout 16 modernizes both the backend and frontend: shared storage and write contracts, more consistent record identity and re-send handling, refreshed runtime dependencies and browser bundles, and an optional responsive modern theme. It also includes reporting, notification and interoperability fixes. It is not an automated-insulin-delivery algorithm upgrade, and it does not require all connected apps to release together.

Nightscout 16 is designed to preserve interoperability with existing clients without coordinated client upgrades. New item-result replies are opt-in. Identity, re-send, deletion and unit-handling fixes have documented behavior changes; non-default strict/rejection settings need separate client checks. This is not a guarantee that every future client feature works on older servers.

Nightscout is not a medical device and nothing here is medical advice. These notes complement the generated changelog, which records what merged. The technical contents carry the full compatibility and known-defect record. Final notes must be reconciled against the actual release tree, not assumed complete from this draft.

docs.title: Runtime and installation changes can stop your site starting
docs.text:
Node must satisfy ^22.23.4 || ^24.22.1 || >=26.12.1. This does not mean every version newer than 22.23.4 is accepted: Node 23, 25 and earlier 26 versions are outside that range. The image uses Node 24.22.1.

MongoDB 5.0 through 8.0 is the supported/tested range. Driver 7 can start on 4.4, but 4.4 is unsupported and untested. MongoDB 3.6, 4.0 and 4.2 no longer serve data; the boot error page names the version and minimum. Compose changes its default from MongoDB 5.0.32 to 6.0.27: follow the upstream runtime upgrade guide, including database upgrade steps and backup/restore, rather than treating it as an ordinary image-only update.

The legacy built-in Dexcom Share and MiniMed CareLink bridges are removed. Leftover bridge settings stop the site with a page naming replacements. Dexcom Share is supported through Nightscout Connect; confirm your source's replacement and configuration before upgrading.

Source installs need development dependencies to build browser bundles: npm ci --include=dev, then npm prune --omit=dev --ignore-scripts after the build. An initial production-only install no longer builds the browser code. The provided Docker build handles the build/runtime split; its runtime image contains no npm or npx. Third-party page plugins need upgrade testing.

docs.title: Some alarms and displayed values change
docs.text:
A page showing --- can now present device and other non-glucose alarms. For sites with PUMP_ENABLE_ALERTS, pump alarms use Loop's reported severity and text: "No Insulin", "Pod Expired" and Medtronic "Signal Loss" now alarm, which they never did. Warn people receiving notifications before upgrading; verify delivery, acknowledgement, cancellation and alarm settings on your setup. Do not infer phone delivery from a passing automated test.

The Bolus Wizard Preview and Careportal Bolus Wizard correct mixed display/profile unit handling, and the calculator uses the profile selected by its caller. Zero temporary basals, cancels and zero amounts are retained by the corrected socket duplicate check. Temporary Targets are stored in mg/dL labelled mg/dl, including targets uploaded with mmol/L labels. These fixes can change stored or displayed results; review the testing guide for your units and connected apps. This is not advice about insulin dosing; discuss questions about therapy with your care team.

docs.title: Record identity is clearer, but not identical to 15.0.9
docs.text:
Re-sends recognized by identity normally replace the live stored record: omitted fields can be removed. Explicit edits and API v1/in-process entries have path-specific rules. Default WRITE_DELETED_RESEND=stay keeps identity-matched deleted records deleted instead of recreating them.

WRITE_IDENTIFIER_INDEX=try attempts a unique identifier index at startup; existing duplicate identifiers are reported as counts, not automatically deleted. Setting off does not remove an existing index. drop removes it. Back up first and rehearse rollback on a disposable deployment.

Operators and app authors should read the compatibility boundaries before choosing non-default write settings. There is no single setting that restores every 15.0.9 behavior.

docs.title: Fixes and optional improvements
docs.text:
The merged work fixes report counting and daylight-saving handling, dose-label rounding, notification/live-update behavior and late or duplicate Pushover callbacks. The new Statistics Summary/AGP report and glucose-distribution report additions are described in contents.md.

The glucose pentagon/PGR withholding rules are "implementation guards, not validated clinical PGR thresholds"; PGR is a research metric and the numerical checks "do not constitute third-party clinical validation". It is a report figure, not a treatment recommendation; talk to the care team before acting on it.

THEME=modern selects the optional responsive dashboard; existing themes remain. SHOW_SECONDS is optional. Runtime/database/library refreshes and page bundles modernize internals without making either option mandatory.

docs.title: Notes for people running sites and writing apps
docs.text:
Legacy API v1 replies remain the default. Requesting Nightscout-Write-Results: items or ?results=items opts into an item-results envelope; an uploader must understand per-item outcomes before using it. A successful HTTP batch response does not prove every item was stored.

WRITE_VALIDATION defaults to off; log and reject are optional. Most uploaders lose a refused record without showing an error. An unrecognized validation mode reads as off. Socket refusal/failure slots under reject are experimental; test uploader retries before enabling rejection. Unset WRITE_IDENTIFIER is not identical to explicit lenient; strict is opt-in. API v3 refuses a client body _id with 400.

API3_SETTINGS_STRICT_READ_ENABLED is optional: an AAPS 4.0 follower using a read-only token not supplied by AAPS is refused when it is on. Do not enable it as a prerequisite for upgrading ordinary clients.

DEBUG_LOGGING=true includes uploaded records in logs, which can contain health data. Normal write logs use summaries. Do not publish raw diagnostic logs or tokens.

The image command is nightscout single; SIGTERM/SIGINT now stop connections cleanly. Under restart: on-failure, a SIGTERM not originating from docker stop now exits successfully and can leave the container stopped. Custom entrypoints must not prepend node to nightscout single. The command name for future multitenant roles is nightscout multitenant (renamed from the reserved nightscout serve; update experimental invocations); no multitenant role is enabled in 16.0.0. This is not a production multitenancy release.

docs.title: Known issues and release acceptance still open
docs.text:
Restricted-token browser issue nightscout/cgm-remote-monitor#8829 is nonblocking by maintainer decision. Its reporter reports failure on dev; neither maintainer reproduced it, and the maintainer reports working DIY and production/service environments. It remains open for environment-specific follow-up, not claimed fixed.

BF-72/BF-161 private fixes, their final combined-tree checks and coordinated release-time disclosure remain pending. Live Pushover/APNs, cohort outcomes, upgrade/rollback and final-candidate quiet-period acceptance are not closed by 24-48 hours of informal use alone.

The full residual-defect list is in contents.md. Draft proposals for controller registration, nonresident profiles, APNs background pushes and new reports are not promised by these notes.

Before final publication: reconcile every operator-visible change and unresolved defect with the tagged tree and verification record; add final security notices, accepted residual risks, hosting/kernel caveats, backup/rollback instructions, and maintainer approval. Record the runtime-floor policy waiver. This draft is useful preparation, not a completed release sign-off.

docs.title: Nightscout 16.0.0 — testing notes for the release candidate
docs.text:
Living document, last changed 2026-11-03 at 7ecc8b0d6.

Working cohort guide, 2026-11-03. The current 16.0.0 release candidate is official/dev 61eb37335954ae42c91345a0823bd67331025165. Informal testing has already started: the maintainer reports multiple testers have run the code for over 24-48 hours. No v16 tag or release is published. Record the exact commit/image each tester actually ran rather than assuming it is this one. The measured automated runs remain in the integration record; release scope is in contents.md.

The maintainer reports that contributed patches were already tested before submission and are high-confidence; live testers will inform further acceptance. The rows below reconcile that existing confidence with build/scenario evidence, not a requirement to restart all testing or a claim that the patches were untested. Live cohort/operational execution belongs in separate sessions; this session clarifies contracts and reconciles the records.

docs.title: Part 1: people using a site
docs.text:
Use the connected apps and displays you normally use. Report missing readings, duplicates, unexpected displayed values, browser reconnect failures or alerts that did not arrive or stop as expected. Include app/server versions, display units, approximate observation interval and what happened, without personal records, credentials or screenshots containing health data.

Check your usual phone and desktop views, including an optional modern theme only if you chose it. Keep independent device alerts enabled; do not rely on an experimental Nightscout build as your only alarm source. This is not dosing advice. Do not create test treatments on an active-care site.

docs.title: Part 2: operators and app authors
docs.text:
Collect a cohort row for AAPS (include 4.0.0 master/client roles and existing supported versions), Loop, Trio, xDrip+, a follower and an mmol/L site. Multiple roles can be covered by one setup, but label each outcome separately.

Evidence field What to record Server SHA, immutable image tag/digest, Node/MongoDB versions; do not use latest_dev alone Client/environment App version/build, API v1/v3/socket, role/permissions without tokens, browser/proxy where relevant Configuration Units and relevant WRITE_*/strict-settings modes; default versus opt-in Interval Start/end and build changes; distinguish elapsed time from confirmed scenario coverage Outcome Scenario, expected/observed result, pass/fail/not exercised, sanitized issue/reference Candidate transition Previous build, new final/security-integrated build, affected checks repeated

Capture ordinary uploads and reads, stable record identity on re-send, reconnect and backfill, time/unit display, deleted-record behavior, and whether queues retry or lose refused items. Exercise writes, conflicting identities and partial-refusal cases only on a disposable site with synthetic records. For API v1 verify the legacy array without opt-in separately from the Nightscout-Write-Results: items envelope. Test AAPS strict-settings and non-default rejection modes separately; do not enable them on every cohort.

Operator-led live checks must record Pushover emergency delivery, acknowledgement, cancellation and duplicate-window behavior, and APNs delivery to a phone. Record service/scenario/build/outcome, not credentials or patient payloads. Automated callback tests are not a substitute.

Rehearse backup, upgrade and rollback on a disposable deployment, including identifier-index startup with duplicates. WRITE_IDENTIFIER_INDEX=off keeps an existing index; verify the documented drop/rollback sequence explicitly. After security integration, pin the final tree/image and repeat affected acceptance checks. Earlier cohort observations remain useful as earlier-build evidence, not automatic acceptance of the new tree.

#8829 is nonblocking by maintainer decision (November 2). Its reporter reports persistence on dev, but neither maintainer reproduced it and many DIY and production/service environments work (maintainer report). Keep a sanitized browser/proxy/role comparison as separate follow-up; do not claim a general regression, root cause or a fix.

The pre-tag live-alert, final-tree and cohort/rollback gates remain. No completed cohort row or final-candidate approval is asserted by this guide.

Contributor preparation update: BF-227 / #8895 fixes late, duplicate or expired Pushover callbacks returning 500 for no-longer-held receipts. Known alarm acknowledgment remains once-only and the diagnostic is unchanged. Recorded local tests passed 54 targeted / 59 integration-tier cases.

docs.title: 8896 repairs entries fixture ordering and compares only successful index
docs.text:
built/present states as equivalent; 37 focused entries tests passed. The local start-path rerun timed out before /api/versions and is not a pass. Full hosted PR and integrated-dev CI/CodeQL passed; the push workflow published the development image, not a release. See integration R19/R20 and current readiness.

For the eventual named-RC call, retain live Pushover emergency delivery, acknowledgment, cancel and duplicate-window checks, and APNs delivery to a phone. Offline callback tests do not satisfy these. A real-rig soak, representative REST plus WebSocket/reconnect, identity cohort and rollback remain required; private BF-72/BF-161 acceptance is pending. #8829 itself is not a release gate. Continue existing informal testing; a formal named-RC call should identify its immutable build. Do not close #8829 from green CI alone.
