docs.title: What changes for you
docs.text:
A plain-language summary for people who run their own Nightscout site, for themselves or for a family member. Nightscout is not a medical device, and nothing here is medical advice. If your numbers look wrong, check with your care team before you rely on them. Nothing here tells you how to dose.

A few words used below:

  • Treatment: a saved carb entry, insulin dose, temporary target, note and similar.
  • COB / IOB: carbs on board and insulin on board. Nightscout estimates both from your treatments and shows them in pills on the main page.
  • AndroidAPS (AAPS): an automated insulin delivery app. Its Nightscout connection, NSClient, copies treatments and readings between the phone and your site.
  • API v1 / API v3: the two ways apps talk to Nightscout. The Nightscout web pages (careportal, bolus wizard), Loop, Trio, xDrip+, xdripswift and OpenAPS use v1. AndroidAPS uses v3.
  • Deleted record (soft delete): when AndroidAPS deletes a record, Nightscout keeps it with a "deleted" mark (isValid: false) instead of removing it. That mark is how other copies of AndroidAPS learn about the delete.

docs.title: What was wrong
docs.text:
1. AndroidAPS did not receive what other apps wrote. After its first sync, AndroidAPS asks Nightscout only for "what changed since last time". Nightscout answered that question only for records written by AndroidAPS or other v3 apps. It left out carbs, insulin, temporary targets and notes entered in the careportal or bolus wizard, including ones a caregiver entered. It also left out glucose readings uploaded by xDrip+, xdripswift or nightscout-connect, and every edit made through v1. So AndroidAPS never got them, unless someone ran a full sync.
  2. A deleted entry kept counting on the site. Carbs or insulin that AndroidAPS deleted stayed in Nightscout's COB and IOB, on the chart, in reports, and in what followers and other apps read. In our lab, 40 g of carbs showed COB 40 g, and after AndroidAPS deleted them COB still showed 40 g. That happens on 15.0.8 and on the 15.0.9 candidate. A deleted profile could also stay the "current" profile.

docs.title: What this change does
docs.text:
• AndroidAPS now receives careportal, bolus wizard and caregiver entries, readings from other uploaders, and edits made through v1, on its next regular check. It no longer needs a full sync for them.
  • When a v1 app edits a record that AndroidAPS created, the record keeps the label AndroidAPS knows it by, so AndroidAPS updates its copy and does not add a second one.
  • A record that AndroidAPS deletes, over either kind of connection, no longer counts. It disappears from COB and IOB, from the chart and reports, from what followers and v1 apps read, and from "current profile". COB and IOB then show exactly what they show when the record is deleted from the careportal.

docs.title: What to check after you update
docs.text:
• Carbs and insulin you entered in the careportal will now reach AndroidAPS, if AndroidAPS is set to accept them. On a phone that loops, AndroidAPS takes carbs and insulin from Nightscout only if "accept carbs" and "accept insulin" are switched on in its NSClient settings. Both are off unless you turned them on. The AAPSClient follower app always takes them, and does not show these two settings. If you have been entering the same meal both in the careportal and on the phone as a workaround, AndroidAPS may now see it twice. Check the phone's treatment list after the update.
  • AndroidAPS applies what it receives according to its own settings. For carbs it already knows about, it accepts a deletion and a shorter duration, but not a changed amount (AAPS SyncNsCarbsTransaction.kt:20-34, read).
  • Records written before the update are not changed. AndroidAPS gets only what is written or edited after the update.
  • Deleting in the careportal (or by Loop, Trio or xDrip+) still removes the record completely, and AndroidAPS still does not hear about it. An entry deleted that way keeps counting on the phone. This stays as it is by decision. Delete the entry in AndroidAPS as well. An entry you delete in AndroidAPS stops counting on your site, and other phones running AndroidAPS hear about the delete, if they are set to accept carbs and insulin.

docs.text:

Reproduced on archived application 1990f453e09303d9dcf3394f0f50a42c3ce4052b with alignment gate instrument 2d7ea7a3c95ae924745b9e9d66d2af33371a21f3. The granted slot executed exactly two native controls, then one fresh restoration. The joined campaign's earlier seven-case positive remains separate; it was not repeated before these controls. Synthetic data only.

Run Native result Required symptom Identity control 0 passing / 0 pending / 1 failing Physical two-row/two-kind assertions pass first; clinical reading is 111 instead of 222 Bootstrap control 0 / 0 / 1 Independently stored reading123 exists first; recovered clinical reading is undefined instead of123 Fresh restoration 7 / 0 / 0 Complete prepared evaluator cohort passes

Both red failures are explicit ERR_ASSERTION results with their named clinical messages. Strict classification requires the one selected test, expected native exit, exact symptom and no pending cases. Import/setup/SQL/timeout/TypeError or unrelated assertion failures cannot establish a semantic red. No runtime or classifier mismatch occurred in this slot.

Identity removes only id_kind from the actual durable replay map key. The clinical computation then loses the newest ObjectId reading while the independent physical rows retain both identities. Bootstrap replaces the full-bootstrap lower bound with the advanced previous checkpoint, losing an independently stored current reading when the projection is empty. Each invocation starts from a fresh whole-source archive with lockfile-matched private dependencies; source worktrees are never changed. Restoring the product source restores all seven native cases, including independent physical-table property comparisons, retained A/B results, downstream failure/retry, explicit later-time reevaluation and actual producer death after commit before publication.

The gate applies one scratch-only test-oracle adaptation consistently to all three archives: the clinical123 assertion accesses bgnow?.mean rather than bgnow.mean. It still requires123. This makes an absent clinical object produce the intended explicit assertion instead of an unrelated TypeError; no positive semantics or product code is changed by this adaptation. docs.title: Selected-owner bounded actual-client measurement — 2026-11-06
docs.text:
Living document, last changed 2026-11-06 at b115d2844.

Reproduced on archived CRM 8713395992e07b4dd2cde61ee972e9a15c8ada8c using the separate selected-subject instrument, commit 7aae38a7de56c0c0367c524b354d4169f4d3e107. The archive-only intersection ablation exited 1 with its exact intended failure; fresh restoration exited 0. Both source compilations matched all 94 cgmsim runtime JavaScript files against the pinned source. Application source, default instrumentation and production configuration were unchanged.

Actual operation Unselected reference Selected reader oref0 existing subject-token uploads: entries, treatments, devicestatus Three admitted workflows Three admitted workflows; paired response summaries, exits and normalized stored values identical Next oref0 entries upload after operator ceiling emptied HTTP 200; three new synthetic records stored HTTP 401; independent stored state unchanged on every domain of tenants A and B cgmsim unchanged root-secret entries upload HTTP 200 HTTP 503; independent stored-state equality assertion passed

The initial catalogue contains six concrete reviewed terminals: read/create for entries, treatments and devicestatus. Actual SQL provisions the role/policy rows with existing denied-anonymous defaults before serving. The lab bootstrap selects the existing owner-reader constructor explicitly and checks readiness through its provisioned subject. It exposes no production selection or management listener.

Restored run records the admitted paired cells and explicit policy differences. oref0 uses its pinned binary's supported token= carrier. The strict comparison covers HTTP status/response array length summary, client exit, identifiers' kinds, method/path/carrier and normalized stored values. It does not compare every raw reply-body field. The canonical cell normalization separates generated primary IDs and top-level server timestamps; nested synthetic values remain compared. oref0's curl exits zero for the denied HTTP response; protocol status is measured separately.

Selected tightening oracle retains raw before/after SQL snapshots and shows status 401, protectedRefused=true, storedUnchanged=true. The unselected oracle shows status 200 and the expected additional stored records. Removing the ceiling intersection from the archived source retains the grant: the red selected oracle shows status 200, protectedRefused=false, storedUnchanged=false. The failed run preserves both predicate failures. This is a sensitive real-client/SQL control; no classifier exception or repair was used.

Pinned cgmsim always hashes its input into an API-secret header and has no existing subject-token carrier. Root exclusion is deliberate; 503 is the observed current mapping and still needs compatibility disposition. The root no-effect assertion compared independent all-domain SQL snapshots during the successful run; those root snapshots were not separately serialized. This evidence does not establish admitted selected cgmsim compatibility or satisfy a universal no-negative-impact condition for root-credential clients. Selected-mode activation remains disabled.

Runtime was claimed at 22:09:53Z and released at 22:11:44Z. Independent exact-identity audits verified 13 red-run containers and six mounted volumes, then 14 restored-run containers and six mounted volumes, absent. Both observers reported zero errors; the positive observer caught 13 containers and its manifest identified the additional short-lived client. No deletion was necessary; the host returned to 462 volumes. Unknown pre-existing fixtures were preserved. Instrument hashes and capacity are retained in metadata.

This is bounded evidence for three oref0 token uploads, immediate current-ceiling revocation and the actual cgmsim root boundary. Other admitted workflows, clients, access tokens, sockets, TLS, retry soak and performance remain unmeasured here. The newer publication candidate 83582e876dd193f4448f44c28e379fb5464a26c7 was not run by this instrument; these measurements remain attributed to 8713395. Current batch publication is independent of this prospective activation evidence.

docs.text:
Record

Reproduced bounded proof on clean application c0e8ad3c562f5d6df3652bf2ba8d161fc1f69cf6. This separately authorized continuation followed the stopped corpus attempt; its passing result neither waives that failure nor completes final acceptance.

Existing tools/lab/postgres-foundation/harness.js ran once, unchanged, against the selected worktree's actual PostgreSQL connection module and typed identity codec. Exit zero; empty stderr. PostgreSQL 16.15 and PgBouncer 1.25.2 used the locally available pinned images recorded in the JSON companion. No source fix, dependency replacement, alternate image or repeat was needed.

Check group Passing Failing Connection, RLS and transaction pooling 9 0 Typed identity candidate 4 0

Two independent application clients reused exactly one backend in transaction-pooling mode, default_pool_size=1, with server_reset_query_always=0. Checks cover tenant-isolated reads/writes, unbound refusal, cross-tenant write/TRUNCATE refusal, rollback, binding cleanup, and dirty/missing/null fields. Typed checks preserve ObjectId/string twins and case distinctions, kind-scoped deletion, and invalid-kind/encoding refusal.

The controls demonstrated the intended broken states and restored comparators within this run:

  • Disabling actual RLS exposed foreign rows through the same pooler; restoring RLS hid them.
  • Granting BYPASSRLS caused the application's startup-role rejection.
  • Mutating the actual connection binding to session scope leaked the tenant to an unbound pooled client; clearing it and restoring the original binding restored isolation.
  • Flattening the actual codec's identity kind reproduced a uniqueness collision; the original codec stored both kinds.

Record

docs.title: Question and result
docs.text:
Can two actual nightscout multitenant api CLI processes be interchanged on one operator-managed machine without losing history visibility? Selected entries CRUD, current grants and process replacement pass, but the broader claim fails: two already-running processes can assign equal history timestamps to sequential committed records, and an exclusive history cursor then omits the later record.

Both processes boot before the characterized writes. A new-format tenant data token authenticates actual HTTP requests. First process POST succeeds; an independent PostgreSQL connection reads its raw stored srvModified. HTTP history returns that record and establishes the cursor before the second process POSTs a different identifier. Both replicas then omit the later record from /api/v3/entries/history/<cursor>, although addressed GET returns it successfully.

Parent reproduced observation Result First raw PostgreSQL srvModified 1793948823488 Second raw PostgreSQL srvModified 1793948823488 Later record missing after exclusive cursor, queried through each replica true, true Later record addressed GET succeeds through both replicas Next write through the first process 1793948823489 Write after restarting the second process 1793948823490 Foreign tenant stored state unchanged

The fixture uses an explicit child --require preload and NS_PREVIEW_REPLICA_CONTROL=history-clock with a shared millisecond value. Only Date.now() callers whose stack includes lib/server/srv-dates.js see that value. The actual allocator and storage code are unmodified. Authentication, expiry, provider and timeout clocks remain real. This makes the scheduling condition deterministic; no frequency under normal wall-clock load is measured.

Read-derived mechanism: lib/server/srv-dates.js:35,62-68 keeps a per-process tenantClocks map and advances against wall time; restoreResolved:76-87 hydrates from persisted values at boot. lib/server/serve/preview-domains.js:68 restores before serving. lib/api3/generic/history/operation.js:74-84,103-104 uses an exclusive predicate for the URL cursor. Same-process advancement and restart hydration do not coordinate already-running allocators. No clock fix is selected.

docs.title: Capability and fixed resource boundary
docs.text:
Only successful Ed25519 mathematical proofs are reused. Every call still resolves its current trusted key descriptor and checks issuer/audience/purpose, current FIPS mode, tenant, claims and expiry. Every authentication still obtains current DB authority. No credential decision, grants, claim acceptance or negative result is cached. There is no TTL/grace/revocation policy change.

A proof matches exact signed bytes and signature plus the current public material. The identical immutable native KeyObject has the identical material. A different object must match exact public DER before any reuse. A new object under the same kid with changed material performs fresh crypto and refuses the old signature. DER work occurs only on a potential hit across different objects, avoiding unconditional encoding cost on cold misses.

One process-wide LRU has at most 256 positive entries, one MiB of ASCII encoded proof keys and optional DER, and 16 KiB per entry. Native public-key references are bounded by that same entry count; there is no per-tenant cache or separate encoding LRU. Larger inputs stay uncached. Encoded byte accounting is not a claim about V8 object overhead, native heap or process RSS.

docs.title: Allocator-preserving tenant restore: bounded SQL feasibility
docs.text:
Living document, last changed 2026-11-07 at 911c5d89f.

Reproduced synthetic programme evidence, 2026-11-07. Application source f0fac99a2fccee259c9a76eba0123058bf288d96, tree 09dd7baf52d51f2725e7cac732fabd3f8280b482. PostgreSQL 16.15. Observations, instrument, closure and prior attempts retain this bounded run. This report does not admit product tenant restore or promote M6.

docs.title: Question and result
docs.text:
Can a same-deployment tenant A restore keep original internal insertion values without touching the shared allocator, while tenant B continues writing? Yes in this controlled entries SQL fixture. A was deliberately quiescent; B's actual application lower-port writes ran before, inside and after A's restore transaction. No shared write pause or sequence-maintenance statement was used.

The instrument imports the exact application's entries catalogue, restricted NOBYPASSRLS connection/tenant binding and lower entries writer. The research restore uses explicit SQL over an operator connection. It does not invoke or bypass the product lifecycle importer: that importer's identity-bearing refusal remains unchanged. Fixtures use synthetic string IDs and documents.

Experiment Physical observation Original values / ordinary and fresh restored run A restores ordinals 1,3; its next canonical insertion receives 6. B retains old rows at 2,4, commits at 5 during restore and at 7 afterward. All pre-restore B rows compare exactly by raw tenant/document/type/ordinal. Allocator preservation Live value 4 becomes 5 solely because B inserts during restore. Explicit A restoration consumes no sequence value; no setval or ALTER SEQUENCE runs. Unsafe artifact / wrong binding Artifact floor above the covered live floor and wrong sequence OID refuse before row/sequence effects; B remains unchanged. Admission is restricted to positive increment-one, noncycling CACHE 1 behavior and the same table/sequence binding. Interruption Injected failure after A's first insert rolls A back completely; independent B's committed insertion remains. Meaningful floor-control red Removing the floor refusal lets new A ordinal 5 sort before restored 1001,1003. The physical numeric-order oracle detects the intended misordering. Meaningful foreign-preservation red Deliberate B document corruption fails the independent exact pre-existing-B comparator. Separate logical-restore proposal Artifact A ordinals 1001,1003 become fresh internal values 5,7 by replaying sorted rows and omitting the identity column; documents/relative order remain equal and B continues at 6. Public record IDs remain unchanged. Original raw ordinals deliberately differ; this is not physical artifact fidelity.

docs.title: Cold replica precondition: source-only possible mechanism
docs.text:
Living document, last changed 2026-11-12 at 9559c64a6.

Reproduced on exact clean core 2d0ae0354a38b4a88f43bc2ae5ec60c085058f64: a valid registry-mode serve-then-warm API process can be globally ready while an accepted tenant is not yet initialized on that process. This is a possible mechanism, NOT the established cause of the original stock failure. No original request timestamps/upstream identities exist to establish that cause. No production or fixture file was edited; no retained resource, HTTP server, PostgreSQL, Vault or restore operation was queried/executed.

docs.title: Exact mechanism
docs.text:
• lib/server/serve/registry-tenants.js:72 exposes an empty binding-key iterator in registry mode; materialization happens through the resolver (:59–62) and per-tenant prepare (:71), independently in every API process.
  • preview-api.js:128–140 constructs startup from that iterator and uses startup.admit before request work. pool-config.tenantReadiness({}) selects the adopted default serve (preview-api.js:75–78).
  • tenant-startup.js:111 snapshots initial keys. A newly accepted tenant gets its cell only at :115–118; cold admit queues initialization and immediately throws typed TENANT_WARMING/retryAfter at :203–213.
  • tenant-startup.js:234–235 reports configured cells, and global ready=true in serve mode, including when a tenant has no cell yet. It is not proof of every API×tenant tuple being warm.
  • The HTTP mapping of that typed error to 503/Retry-After is read-derived from lib/server/tenant-app/index.js:17,128–130; the probe itself does not run HTTP.

docs.title: Read-only chronology and limits
docs.text:
Safe classification was captured from timestamped private API logs, current role identity and the restore demo's final JSON, without issuing new HTTP warming requests or changing roles/state.

  • API1 logged ready1/failed0 at17:25:16.685; ready2 was not logged until 17:31:32.223. API2 had logged ready2 since17:25:13.626.
  • Both roles logged ready1/deferred1 around17:31:34.438, then ready2 by34.615. Failed stock log modification time was17:31:35.359.
  • The internal restore demo artifact reports state passed and bCommittedDuringRestore:true. The outer settings assertion nevertheless failed; its later B152-frame/same-session assertions were not reached.
  • Warm log loggedAfterMs is boot-relative after-ms, not a measured individual tenant initialization duration. Global current role health is not historical per-tenant warmth; no tenant ID is attached to the ready-count log.

These facts support, but do not prove, the read-derived cold-replica precondition hypothesis: initial serve-ready roles may initialize a tenant on its first request, and edge-routed setup may not touch every replica. They do not assign the three warming responses to a replica/tenant cell or to before/during the restore. No initial warm-state cause is established or excluded merely by counts.

The source fixture starts four settings readers, breaks a worker on its first error and starts restore once aggregate successes reach four. It retains neither per-worker initial success nor direct per-replica initialization proof. Hence its original capture cannot distinguish cold setup from a measured continuity regression. Source-only controls and a bounded explicit precondition must be evaluated before prescribing a fixture-only repair. Any warming/error during the claimed measured interval must remain a failure; blanket retries or longer measurement deadlines would not resolve this evidence gap.

docs.title: Boundary and mechanism
docs.text:
Global process health and one successful public-edge request cannot establish that every API replica has initialized both tenants. The fixture now performs protected status GETs on each exact API service and seed tenant before any sockets, JWT exchange or strict HTTP work. Only typed 503/TENANT_WARMING is pending within one shared 20-second request-phase readiness budget; all other refusals and transport/parse failures fail setup. HTTP200 must be an object with status: 'ok' and no error field. Late success after the monotonic deadline also fails.

A disposable image client joins only the owned backend network. It receives three read-only mounts (two helpers and one mode-0600 credential input), no operator, database, Vault or IPC configuration, and an explicit host UID/GID. The host verifies exact container/project/service/workdir/image/source identities and requires the complete readiness matrix. After helper cleanup, it checks the same roster again and refuses changed/lost container IDs, boot times, images or labels. These are bounded observations, not a promise against future replacement. Metadata inspection and cleanup have separately bounded commands outside the request phase. The credential file is removed afterwards; a leftover client is removed only after exact operation-label/image checks.

The original four eager B settings readers still use the public edge with the original request timeout/cadence. Every worker must succeed before restore spawns. Any error during measurement remains a failure, including warming. The fixture retains its 120-second total timeout and stock/frame/session/restore assertions. Bounded sanitized metadata records request start/end, worker, stage, typed response, first successes and restore child spawn/exit. Public-edge upstream identity remains explicitly unknown. No production proxy or application behavior changes.

docs.title: Verdicts
docs.text:
question answer 1,000-tenant milestone (m7-capacity-gate) Met on both heads. Every 1,000-tenant run (8) finished with every role healthy, the stored-count oracle GREEN with zero uncertain writes, all probe writes delivered, and all tenants evaluated after the full restart. Socket caps differ by run (table below). 3,000-tenant gate Not met on core 5c60aec6 + deploy d1c7aca on this host. Deploy and the idle window succeed at 3,000; under the real cadence with 2 sockets per tenant, 99.8% of HTTP requests fail (p50 10.2 s) and 134 of 6,000 sockets prime in 300 s (r1, measured). What runs out first at 3,000 The api's single JavaScript main thread, driven by realtime's socket-authorize path, with heavy allocation. With sockets present (x2, x3) the api's event-loop utilisation is 0.993–0.995 and its process uses 4.4–4.5 cores, of which 0.94–0.96 is the main thread and 3.4–3.5 V8 worker (GC/compiler) threads; authorize throughput stays at about 140–215/s whatever the pool size (measured). With HTTP only (x1) the api's 8-client operation pool binds first: requests wait their 5 s pool timeout while the main thread runs at 0.74 (measured). PostgreSQL is not the limit (1.8–4.5 cores, 3–5 active backends on average; measured). Where the api main thread saturates About 1,350–1,400 tenants under this workload (real cadence + 2 sockets per tenant). Derived, an extrapolation: b4's api main-thread utilisation of 0.73 at 1,000 tenants, scaled linearly to 1.0. No run was made at that N. 5,000 and 10,000 Not run (the 3,000 gate failed first).

Reference to beat (from the decision): about 100 tenants per node for tenant-per-pod.

docs.title: Attribution and reproduced mechanism
docs.text:
The actual shipping observation used core d8d6b547bb17fc91e440bcab48f323a81a6cd66c, deployment 962fbdbe8617ed8abe63cad7039fde70f91fcbce, and fresh paired image sha256:5b785befb5a5a89689148cbbc50c2159506a7a831b9a382a7238350a3f3684b9. It is a synthetic, independently owned Compose project with one API, one unsharded realtime role and three fixed evaluator participants.

A failed restore left the synthetic A tenant suspended. Investigation retained that phase and did not replay restore or reopen the tenant. A focused cache invalidation against that already suspended tenant produced successful replies from every participant, followed by realtime status HTTP 503. The peer/operation/status capture retains only bounded operational metadata. It is not an HTTP body or clinical trace.

The initial hypothesis came from lib/storage/postgres-connection.js: connection construction adds its resource record with datastore: null before awaiting role and physical backend identity admission. The synchronous cohortDatastore() refuses any such record. Realtime's short-lived persisted settings readers can overlap a lifecycle status observation.

The native discriminator reproduces that mechanism using an actual operation window and PostgreSQL connections: a baseline snapshot is valid, holding another connected constructor before identity publication makes the snapshot refuse, and releasing admission restores the same datastore. The capture records both outcomes. This is reproduced native initialization behavior; the peer status capture independently measures the actual deployment refusal. No private error body was substituted for a measured handler cause.

The exact source/stock restore failure artifacts and suspended state remain local. They have not been replaced with a passing result on the later source.

Source contract: core docs/d6-change-feed.md; deployment helper: lib/change-feed/postgres.provision.

docs.title: Implemented boundary
docs.text:
• Dedicated multitenant feed-reader role, outside serving processes and tenant operation cohorts. An EXECUTE-only non-replication login calls fixed-slot wrappers owned by an exact NOLOGIN/NOSUPERUSER/NOBYPASSRLS/REPLICATION identity.
  • Reviewed operational function catalogue, pinned for restore census. Wrapper body, owner, result/security/config/grants, publication table/filter/DML shape, slot and finite resource settings are checked. NULL numeric arguments refuse.
  • Metadata-only pgoutput decoder for the write clock and activity table. Complete committed transactions produce coalesced tenant hints. Notification commit precedes slot acknowledgement; unsafe/oversize/incomplete batches do not acknowledge.
  • SQL-session loss reconnects with the same safety checks. LISTEN commits before reconciliation. Reader/listener loss and new generation enter visible degraded recovery. Healthy and degraded recovery both use fixed page budgets.
  • Realtime detects the hinted tenants, with separate bounded cold/retry work. Evaluator recovery accepts a subset, retains clinical due timers and separate per-tenant evaluation-gap deadlines. Delivery recovery is paged in feed mode; active retry work uses tracked active tenants.
  • Activity hints are independent of data writes. Existing pause/suspend control semantics remain: read/socket/evaluator work stops, pause permits uploads, suspend refuses uploads, resumption reacquires. changeFeed requires an activity reader.

Verdict: selected current properties agreed between evaluator and API. Realtime produced a different output: the browser record frame, preserving controller predictions. docs.title: Boundary and results
docs.text:
Application f0fac99a2fccee259c9a76eba0123058bf288d96, tree 09dd7baf52d51f2725e7cac732fabd3f8280b482; Node v22.23.4, PostgreSQL 16.15. Actual evaluator/realtime source modules and restricted PostgreSQL readers ran, plus the actual properties HTTP handler with a synthetic preauthorized context. This is not acceptance of the complete public authorization/role stack.

Two reseeded campaigns used one child and one PostgreSQL process, crossing Loop, OpenAPS and treatment-only provenance with small (34–35 records) and history (758–759 records) inputs. Acquisition paths had two warmups and five retained samples per campaign/cell, in alternating order. Tick cells had one sample per campaign. These are not independent process repetitions. Selected property hashes matched between reseeds in all six cells: 360 metric rows and six intended controls. Per-cell distributions and source/closure attribution are in the portable measurements, without private paths, credentials or Docker identities.

Probe Reproduced result Decision implication Current values Required bgnow, delta, direction, IOB, COB and device uploader-battery properties agreed at the JSON wire boundary. Loop IOB/COB were 1.25/18; OpenAPS 1.75/21. These six families are scoped reuse candidates, not proof of every plugin/property. Realtime Latest SGV agreed with BG for this single-uploader fixture; raw controller predictions remained present. Properties cannot replace the record/frame contract. This is not a general multi-uploader bucket-mean rule. Time without writes At +45 minutes, IOB changed from 1.25/Loop to 1.425/Care Portal with the same checkpoint; API agreed at the later instant. A checkpoint-only cache is incorrect. Time, expiry and provenance matter. Corrections Journey-shaped carb create/edit/delete changed COB 60 → 90 → 30; evaluator/API agreed and realtime reflected edit/absence. Require invalidation/absence recovery. Writes were fixture-persisted shapes, not client-ingress acceptance. Units/history Under mmol settings, delta retained mg/dL −2 with scaled/display −0.1; evaluator/API agreed. Retro BG differed from current. Preserve units/formatting policy and historical/on-demand semantics. Future input Evaluator acquisition included a future row; framed API/realtime excluded it. Current BG still agreed. Input policy and result equivalence differ. Source inspection explains the sandbox/BG bucket exclusion of future readings.

Source paths at the pinned application: lib/data/tenant-projection-evaluator.js calls views.evaluateCycle; lib/server/realtime/projection.js calls snapshot.load/dataWithRecentStatuses, without the derived-property phase; lib/server/tenant-app/derived-frame.js runs selected setters without notification phases. Observers wrapped selected plugin factories, not every computation. Measured evaluator cycles observed nine setter/six notification-check calls; API nine/zero; realtime zero/zero. Zero selected realtime setter calls does not mean no computation: recovery, transformation and frame construction still run.

Controls detected actual BG-setter corruption, checkpoint-only stale reuse, cross-tenant result substitution, reuse after disabling IOB, a stale frame after physical deletion, and partial SQL input failure. All passed restoration. Assertion controls required their intended AssertionError/message; unrelated API/SQL failures could not count. Full grant revocation, adversarial isolation and offline client-cache recovery are outside this comparison.

docs.title: Mechanism and controls
docs.text:
Read-derived source ordering explains why a frame is not a durable-completion barrier: notification state commits attempting before calling its adapter, then commits accepted after the response in a separate transaction. A fixed 1500-ms sleep cannot guarantee that latter commit. The acceptedAt field is an application finishedAt timestamp captured before finish commit; creation-to-acceptedAt is not measured SQL commit latency. The earlier leaf's numeric difference is only a field difference, not a commit-observation claim.

The observer explicitly waits only for expected absent/pending/attempting changed effects or incomplete fanout. It immediately refuses duplicated effects, clears, wrong identity/configuration, cancelled changed effects, unknown states and unexpected transport uncertainty. Uncertain is nonterminal in the durable protocol; its rejection is a conservative requirement of this clean proof. No assertion catch/retry loop exists. The original strict final oracle file is unchanged and is required for success.

The original B401 frame wait's absolute 20-second budget is shared with completion and capped by original durable repeat deadlines. At least 1500 ms after the exact frame is observed remains mandatory, including repeated invariant checks. Each SQL call has remaining-budget Docker CLI and PostgreSQL session statement_timeout controls; no durable database setting changes. Both deadlines are rechecked after reads and before final return. Final typed rows/fanout and read/copy/validation timestamps plus count and a last-16 trajectory are retained on PASS/FAIL; rows and fanout inputs have explicit bounds.

Fanout is copied before primary SQL for incomplete observations, so a newly received event is not paired with an older SQL view. At candidate PASS, complete durable rows are already known: the observer recopies latest fanout and reruns the strict oracle before returning. This closes a reproduced draft-observer gap where an event received during final SQL was omitted. This is an instrument gap, not a reproduced runtime duplication finding.

Focused union: 25 pass, zero failures, one explicitly unselected shipping integration skip. No native runtime acceptance is claimed. Controls cover in-flight-to-accepted, missing frame/fanout, immediate sticky violations, post-read monotonic/repeat deadline refusal, SQL budget construction, and original socket/overlay/oracle contracts. Removing the minimum interval from a scratch copy goes red at assert(h.time>=1500) in the ablation. The duplicate-during-final-SQL control on original 3b goes red with Missing expected rejection in its original capture; exact repaired source passes that same test. These controls distinguish the observation bugs, not application clinical semantics.

docs.title: Preserving the source's existing deadline domain
docs.text:
The runtime already exposes dueAt/dueReason in health; the previous private DTO omitted them. The export adds observations, not instructions to evaluate. The first draft required integer deadlines. Existing tenant environment accepts finite numeric pump.warnClock (environment.js typed extended setting), while lib/data/evaluator-due.js computes pump-clock-warn from that minute value. For synthetic warnClock=1/7, at 1700000000000, actual nextDue produces 1700000008572.4285. Existing runtime arm accepts finite deadlines, so narrowing the observational response to integers refused a source-valid scheduler value.

The same preservation invariant runs actual nextDue and actual DTO: original acae exits one with inspection refusal, corrected 47b exits zero preserving exactly that fractional value and reason. The control uses synthetic component inputs; it is not a public settings/API or clinical test. No value is rounded and no scheduling/state policy is modified. Corrected DTO and schema both accept finite nonnegative number/null, with no integer/MAX_SAFE restriction, and refuse missing or malformed observations. Reasons remain typed ASCII at most 128 characters. Null due time requires null reason.

docs.text: The lane stopped before implementation, on the condition its brief named: the evaluator's notification output is not idempotent across two overlapping members. The evaluator-static-partition decision accepts duplicate evaluation "bounded to one heartbeat interval after a membership change" because "the evaluator's outputs are idempotent by contract (... notification intent with stable identity and suppression)". The shipping producer gives a new alarm effect, and so a new delivery request, on every pass in which the evaluator output it reads came from a different runtime than the previous pass. The decision says a measured duplicate external effect reopens the question; this is that measurement. No code was committed. The queue, decisions.md, contents.md and the register are unchanged.

Anchor Measured value Application branch codex/internal-service-api-20261109 Application commit dc795bd1515f11808a8d0732f2be9925cb2ffcd1 Parent candidate 0fc5abf99ec34b80eba9f482c5cc197c51c737f9 Fetched official/dev 4a482627bfdafb1fef8dcbe0ac6c484811cae563 Alignment source before this record 928a2d43ef7379a86aca2ac762941e7ea7c5abc2

HTTP accepts explicitly configured origins, including DNS, link-local and private addresses, with a separate optional bind address and explicit trust: network. Deployment owns HTTP reachability. No bearer credential convention was added; service/version headers identify contracts and are not credentials. Existing public routers do not mount these private operations. Each internal contract opens its own server/socket or HTTP port.

Existing UDS configuration remains valid. Environment-reference endpoint alternatives are available for API socket forwarding, realtime API/alarm endpoints, evaluator notification routes and lifecycle participant endpoints. Application documentation and curl examples are in docs/internal-service-api.md on the application branch. docs.title: Exact reproduced predicate
docs.text:
The immutable predicate projection binds the original188539-byte proof by hash. All three snapshots cover500 owners. Successful TIME totals advance0→0→23. All23 observed opportunities have successful TIME progress; no final-only opportunity exists. One tenant, zero-based ordinal22 in the sorted inspection selector, causes the refusal twice: first and midpoint counters are0, final counter1. Acquisition stays1, failures0 and all six job flags are false. The final due is null.

Its already observed due falls352.118ms after the start of the final fetch bracket and598.710ms before its end. The950.828ms bracket covers four RPC pages. docs.title: Completed capability
docs.text:
NS_M7_DIAGNOSTICS=1 selects process/role aggregate JSON log snapshots, default five seconds; NS_M7_DIAGNOSTICS_INTERVAL_MS accepts 1000..60000. Default OFF creates no worker, timer, clock reads or pool/client/async function wrappers. There is no new HTTP endpoint, schema, SQL, authority cache or credential policy.

The normal PostgreSQL connection foundation, raw lifetime pool, raw membership pool and raw registry provisioning pool have constructor-only observation hooks. Public total/idle/waiting counts are read directly; checkedout is total minus idle. Observed outstanding client.query calls are separate from held clients. They include client-side query queueing and are not pg_stat_activity state. Query instances/custom submitters and config-owned callbacks are untouched and mark SQL coverage UNMEASURED. Direct pg.Client use, including the feed reader, is explicitly outside pool coverage and UNMEASURED.

Fixed gauges distinguish shared worker lease handles, queued critical-section cells, active critical sections and outer body/response lifetimes. Admission, registration, API authorization, realtime RPC/private authorization and marker completion have separate fixed histograms. Body-response and completion timers are inclusive; admission is a registration subspan. Independent overlapping histograms have no request-level pairing: do not subtract percentiles or sum nested spans to infer exclusive cost or causal order.

Resource bounds are 64 tracked pools, 13 buckets per fixed stage, and one transferred output buffer no larger than 8 KiB. Only selected source role names and process PID are labels. No tenant, token, request/socket ID, URL, SQL or error text is retained in snapshots. Overflow, unsupported forms and missing/zero observations are UNMEASURED. Closed pools leave the registry.

The selected sink uses one unref'd worker, empty environment and no inherited application preloads. Busy/backpressured stdout drops snapshots instead of queuing JSON. Raw output failures/partial writes/EPIPE mark missing telemetry; the sink never wraps or closes application stdout. Shutdown does not await logging or promise a final flush. Enabled diagnostics add fixed per-process work/thread overhead; no zero-overhead or performance claim is made.

docs.title: Startup connection pressure — 2026-11-12
docs.text:
Living document, last changed 2026-11-12 at bcce3b52e.

Reproduced startup failure; capacity and new-instrument native TIME remain UNMEASURED. This diagnostic restarts the same owned15-container, two-tenant native stack on core9db/deploymentd76/image293. It changes no pool, PostgreSQL, worker, settings or workload configuration. Existing evaluators can naturally process retained data; the diagnostic performs no fresh uploads, clinical scenario or TIME capture.

The observation records44 successful bounded connection-census queries. PostgreSQL reports100 maximum connections, three superuser-reserved slots and zero other reserved slots. Sampled client occupancy peaks97, including the sampler's one admin connection, then falls to46. At the peak,96 service clients are idle and the observer is active; at the final sample45 service clients are idle. Occupancy reaches46 about10.3seconds after the failed barrier and stays there through the passive observation. Sampling at1Hz does not establish the absolute peak.

The single strict API×tenant readiness barrier returns503 AUTHORITY_UNAVAILABLE; both its actual child and outer phase return1. The complete bounded PostgreSQL log filter independently captures a reserved-slot FATAL roughly13ms before that response. The numeric SQLSTATE and a per-request backend-PID link were not captured. The event and census support startup admission pressure; they do not establish a leak or prove the exact failing request's backend error. An earlier last1000-line log projection omitted this event and cannot prove its absence.

After35.0001seconds of passive observation, the controller stops and retains all15 containers. Its outer0 means the diagnostic completed, not that readiness or acceptance passed. The observer adds real connection overhead and can shift a threshold. These measurements are not throughput,500-tenant capacity, per-role CPU or sampler-free cost results.

Read-derived setup distinction: deploymentd76 bindings/compose/multitenant/demo.sh:51–54 starts APIs, completes HTTP priming and publication, then starts the remaining roles. The retained-stack restart used raw API health followed immediately by the remaining workers and the strict barrier. Its early pool occupancy differs from that normal setup interval. The decay is consistent with the source dependency's idle-pool eviction; it does not prove connection ownership or future load behavior.

A separately recorded startup-settlement qualification is a proposed next experiment. This record does not pass that experiment, fix the immediate-startup failure, change connection limits or authorize an application acceptance waiver. The collector repair and existing application acceptance retain their actual source and scope.

docs.title: Outcome
docs.text:
Realtime sends a frame only when a tenant's view changes, authorizes a socket when it connects and then only on events, primes concurrent connects late instead of disconnecting them, and comes back after a restart at 50 and 100 tenants. No client change: lib/client is untouched, frames stay full (delta:false). Measured on the one-host Compose reference against the base head:

base cb1b751d this lane 6f31c94b frames per idle connected socket per minute (1 tenant × 20) 20.0 0 subject authorizations per connected socket per minute (1 × 20) 20.1 0.099 realtime DB-ms per minute, 50 tenants × 20 sockets idle 44,989 83 sockets primed when 1000 open (50 × 20) 14 / 1000 at 50 ms stagger (986 server-disconnected) 1000 / 1000 opened at once, none disconnected realtime after docker compose restart realtime, 50 tenants exit 78, never back running; reconnecting clients 1000/1000 in 32.8 s realtime start at 100 tenants exit 78 at deploy running; restart survived, 200/200 back in 35.1 s

Restart root cause (reproduced): at boot realtime warms and refreshes every configured tenant at once, each inside an operation window that takes a client from the lifetime pool (max 8, 5 s connect timeout, operation-cohort-config.js:49). On a loaded PostgreSQL one window waits longer than 5 s, pg-pool rejects with timeout exceeded when trying to connect at operation-window.js:103, the startup Promise.allSettled treats any rejection as fatal (runtime.js:43-45 and tenant-startup.js warm, both at cb1b751d), and preview-realtime.js turns it into PreviewConfigError → exit 78. Shown with a diagnostic copy of preview-realtime.js that prints the swallowed error (runs/base-n50-restart-diagnostic.txt). It is not caused by the previous process: a fresh up of the stopped container failed the same way. The perf-db lane reproduced the same mechanism independently with unbounded warm at 200 (perf-db record).

Not fixed here, measured in both heads: graceful shutdown with sockets attached overruns the 10 s bound (still open 10000 ms after SIGTERM: PipeWrap, PipeWrap, Timeout, …, then the watchdog exits 1; runs/base-n50-realtime-lifecycle.txt, runs/after-n50-realtime-lifecycle.txt). Without sockets the base restarted in 5 s with no overrun. The mechanism was not examined.

docs.title: Mechanism and meaningful control
docs.text:
Armed output at t0 sets repeatAt=t0+60000. At t0+1000 the same configuration is transiently ineligible. Output, alarm-state digest and normal effect origin stay identical, but repeatAt disappears. Identical content/configuration/checkpoint recovered at t0+4438 is not fresh, yet satisfies at >= (prior.repeatAt ??0). It emits the exact same effectIdentity under a NEW origin derived from ['producer-transition-v2',['repeat',next,null],0], then sets deadline t0+64438.

The caller turns missing/nonmatching current output into eligible:false while retaining authoritative configuration; the reducer's !armed(cycle) clock-drop therefore covers unavailable output as well as actual normality. This is not an ownership-policy or cache explanation. The producer's ordinary state lock and atomic intent commit do not restore the lost deadline.

The unchanged-output invariant is RED on that actual source sequence: UNCHANGED_OUTPUT_MUST_WAIT_FOR_ORIGINAL_REPEAT_DEADLINE. A single-field causal control preserves the original repeatAt before identical recovery; the SAME source reducer/invariant is GREEN, retaining original effect origin and deadline. This modifies only test-owned previous state, not product code. It establishes the lost-clock dependency, not the full eventual repair contract.

Nine actual reducer scenarios, with assertions and complete results:

  • Same content without unavailable gap: original origin/deadline retained.
  • Transient ineligible gap: deadline disappears and identical effect gets new origin.
  • Original deadline preserved: no early repeated effect.
  • Genuine due boundary59999/60000/60001: no early repeat, one at60000, no replay at60001.
  • Gap followed by genuine due output with original deadline: repeat still occurs.
  • Changed configuration: explicit existing reset path/new identity and origin.
  • Known normal empty clinical output: clear, stable clear origin across empty polls, repeat clock absent.
  • Normal then real alarm: legitimate fresh origin, unaffected by original repeat slot.
  • ACK while ineligible: actual control clear; identical recovery preserves that exact clear origin and emits no normal alarm during the active ACK.

The script computes and asserts the exact repeat-null cause origin. The runtime owner separately published native matching-origin metadata at its retained clinical-origin-cause-match.json, SHA2888e3c578271ed6001a03e83d8ee1ae376fbf4b25f21f4e008f770b7d0aa9ef (two accepted-request matches). This lane read that metadata but did not produce its database observation or independently rerun native state. Native acceptance, current-authority/late-effect/phase/restore protection and the eventual patch remain runtime-owner/root criteria.

docs.title: Contract and mechanism
docs.text:
The measured identical-metadata witness rules out a universal immediate in-place freshness guarantee from filesystem metadata alone. The adopted hybrid contract keeps generic/operator hot-file compatibility: parsedFile defaults to bounded read-through, comparing bytes and parsing only changed text. Static/lab realtime configuration and admission retain next-call visibility of same-size in-place edits, without sleeps or forced timestamps. Their configured file-size cost is explicit. Earlier static-roster zero-read performance measurements do not prove that freshness property and are not a production registry cost model.

The redundant outer realtime cache also bypassed the current byte limit. Its removal is independently measured by a synthetic configuration over 65,536 bytes: a lower current bound now refuses the next read even when the file is unchanged. The source-derived outer-cache ablation produces a missing-expected-rejection failure. The generic parse-on-change expectation remains immediate; it was not weakened to admit stale same-size edits.

Production registry realtime reads its role file at boot, then obtains each current tenant from the admitted registry set and authoritative settings reader. The actual registryMode composition discriminator makes 200 per-tenant calls after deleting the boot file: zero boot-file reads and zero roster-key enumerations, while 200 settings reads still occur. SQL/resource adapters are explicitly doubled. This measures the composition/cost seam; it does not claim native database acceptance.

Only machine-owned placement metadata opts into atomic-publication caching. The actual publisher already writes a complete temporary file, fsyncs it, renames it and fsyncs its directory. The reader retains one descriptor for the accepted inode, preventing inode reuse after multiple unobserved replacements. This closes the ABA gap that zero stale samples alone could not rule out. Bytes and cached identity come from the same bounded-reader descriptor. A concurrent path rename is measured: the opened publication is coherent and the following call sees the new publication. The old handle closes before replacement acquisition; observed peak and retained descriptors are both one. Cache hits still validate the current byte limit and target metadata. In-place writes are unsupported for this atomic machine publication contract.

Valid symlinks remain compatible for both modes. Target replacement/repoint, missing/nonregular targets, invalid JSON, current bounds and permission refusal are covered. EACCES is instrumented because CI may run as root; mode changes and all descriptor cleanup use real files. Independent byte-growth coverage defeats a false pre-read size and observes the existing read-limit refusal. No unbounded reader or separate byte-reading implementation was introduced.

Runtime close paths release placement handles in realtime, evaluator consumers, operation cohorts and central role composition, including failed boot and failed shutdown. Finalization is fallback only. Reader factories are process/role resources, not tenant resources: realtime role configuration, evaluator consumer route configuration and operation-cohort configuration can each own one handle, up to three in their co-resident process. Direct load/loadRoutes callers close explicitly.

Source mechanisms: lib/server/realtime/contract.js:38, lib/server/serve/config-file.js:73, lib/server/realtime/config.js:48, lib/realtime-placement/index.js:115; runtime cleanup is pinned in result.json.

docs.title: Realtime: server-side disconnects after a full role restart (read-only diagnosis, 2026-11-11)
docs.text:
Living document, last changed 2026-11-11 at ae22aeb5d.

Contributor-facing. A read-only diagnosis: code read plus the counters the capacity instrument already wrote for run b3. Nothing was run for this record. Every code claim is read-derived. Figures marked measured (b3) are copied from the b3 instrument output, not re-measured here.

Anchors. - Core workspace/capacity-fixes-20261111 at 5c60aec6: batch head 0392acf9 plus 5517cb6c, 12fa221d and 5c60aec6. The worktree is clean. - Run b3 at 1,000 tenants used image nscap:5c60aec6-d1c7aca, with realtimeMaxSockets 2000 from the deploy log. - Its local run directory is capacity-5c60-20261111/b3-n1000 under externals/work/ (untracked). - The realtime overlay preview-realtime-stats.js differs from core lib/server/serve/preview-realtime.js only by the 1 s DIAG line. realtime-config-stats.js adds only read timers.

docs.title: Verdict
docs.text:
The 499 server-side disconnects fit the process-wide socket cap, lib/server/realtime/protocol.js:352. They do not fit an authorization path.

How the cap produces them (read-derived): - In b3, maxSockets was exactly tenants × 2 = 2000, which equals the number of clients. - After the restart, the probe clients each opened a second engine session, after the edge restart cut their first one. - Realtime keeps an engine session it has not yet seen die. A polling session is detected only by the engine.io ping timeout: pingInterval 25 s + pingTimeout 20 s in engine.io 6.6.10, node_modules/engine.io/build/server.js:48-49. So for up to about 45 s, stale sessions (ghosts) count in states. - states reached the cap. Each new connection was then accepted at the namespace level, and bind answered it with socket.disconnect(true) (protocol.js:352). The client sees io server disconnect and stops for good. - When the ghosts expired, states fell to the 1501 live sockets and stayed there.

The authorization paths keep the socket connected and retry on not-ready, timeout and warming. That is the decided model, already in the code.

docs.text:
Living document, last changed 2026-11-07 at fa183067b.

2026-11-07. Reproduced source protocol, with actual write-clock allocator and API3 history handler/filter, recording storage/transactions, stubbed authentication and a synthetic client-cache model. This is not PostgreSQL or a mobile binary run. Observations retain synthetic inputs and actual outputs.

The executed source is f0fac99a2fccee259c9a76eba0123058bf288d96. The root independently replayed the protocol against joined 92641bd002ada37d78b165f2dd86f44ad4e8baef; both relevant modules are byte unchanged from that source, and observations compare exactly. Original instrument SHA256: f8037266d2c2e332f4f48b57e65077177e9b8f1a0019c2926ba43184987e2e8d. Original capture SHA256: e0da086a55bf38e0608f7ee7ae509db383a76162a8ed3a305ab8a0d9384d59bf. The private instrument/capture live in the session handoff. Initial invalid-date setup refusal is retained there; it is not a semantic control pass.

Case Actual history behavior Synthetic cache consequence Restore old clock and raw document metadata The next allocated stamp remains below the prior client cursor; actual URL history filter returns no rows. A post-backup-only row remains cached; a restored older value also remains stale. Retain live clock floor only A subsequent new write gets a stamp above the cursor and appears in history. Previously restored values and hard removals still have no forward history events; both stale-cache cases remain.

Mechanism: lib/storage/postgres-write-clock.js:60 locks last_stamp, then line 67 allocates max(requested, floor + 1). This guarantees progress from its current stored floor, not from a discarded historical floor. In lib/api3/generic/history/operation.js:65, URL cursor filtering selects records with a greater srvModified. Copying old metadata cannot advertise changed values or synthesize tombstones for records removed by restore. Internal evaluator snapshot reconciliation does not reset an external client's history cursor.

Pending policy: prefer publishing ordinary history updates and deletion records so existing clients converge; alternative exact snapshot metadata needs an explicit, reliable client reset/resync procedure. Retaining the clock floor alone is insufficient. For automatic convergence, compare current and artifact state before destructive changes, retain the authoritative issued floor, and measure changed-value/deletion delivery and retry behavior. No public metadata restamping or reset policy has been adopted in this record.

Joined source currently refuses new clock-bearing full imports before SQL with LIFECYCLE_HISTORY_CONTINUITY_REQUIRED (lib/tenant-lifecycle/index.js:235). Counter-only component proofs remain separate; full same-ID restore is not accepted. Other tenants must retain their current state, without a global pause.

docs.title: Contract and source
docs.text:
Adopted direction: only per-tenant/collection relative order is required. No examined public/client consumer requires global insertion numbers. Public record IDs, stored documents, history timestamps and supported first-match behavior remain separate contracts.

lib/tenant-lifecycle/tenant-insertion-sql.js builds explicit transaction-scoped operator conversion SQL for entries, food and selected socket-order treatments, devicestatus and profile catalogues. Existing rows retain their original ordinal; a forced-RLS per-tenant counter seeds from each tenant's maximum. DROP IDENTITY removes the native shared sequence. An invoker trigger allocates only the bound tenant's insertion state, preserves explicit operator restoration values, and rejects ordinal/tenant changes on UPDATE. No SECURITY DEFINER, new service, per-tenant sequence or optional write-clock dependency is added.

The unchanged canonical lower writer and real profile reader consume this source. Normal serving uses column INSERT excluding the ordinal; a separate restricted restore connection may insert original ordinals. An explicit effective ACL check refuses inherited grants that would restore serving ordinal-write authority.

docs.title: Registry-backed UI admission — 2026-11-12
docs.text:
Living document, last changed 2026-11-11 at 92b9ba040.

Reproduced against deployment source 167332002bc2811b7b4bd656a9d9479e4fcf5554 (codex/ui-registry-20261112, base parent5935b42), core source and instrumentation d20354797e368b03af171f4417ead60a6282d098. Local/unpushed original history.

The standalone browser-page UI previously used a seed-generated static alias projection. Version2 UI config selects the product registry resolver through a dedicated lookup+revision identity, without tenant enumeration, registry attributes, clinical/settings/secret grants or a static roster. Static version1 remains supported. Parent owns generated role/config/environment/Compose binding and joined census.

NS_UI_TEST_CORE=/absolute/path/to/pinned/core node bindings/compose/multitenant/ui-registry.test.js
NS_UI_REGISTRY_NATIVE_TEST=1 NS_UI_TEST_CORE=/absolute/path/to/pinned/core node --test bindings/compose/multitenant/ui-registry.integration.test.js

unit-final.log: 4 passing, no skips. Actual product resolver verifies positive and negative revision cache invalidation, bounded positive/negative cache eviction, unknown/private/untrusted forwarded selector refusal, explicit config/authority refusals, bounded in-flight work and idempotent owned close. Invoke the unit file as shown: a local Node22 --test invocation reported only file-level success; that opaque run was not counted as executed unit evidence.

native-final.log: 1 passing compound native case, no skips. Own PostgreSQL16 container with pinned image (source fixture records exact digest), no existing services/Vault selected. Actual product registry catalogue/functions and connection, actual UI HTTP handlers, core templates and existing production assets. The UI identity cannot SELECT planted clinical data or registry rows or execute tenant enumeration. An alias initially refused is registered while UI runs, then serves HTML after revision observation. Private/internal names, unknown aliases and cross-tenant forwarded selectors refuse. Modern theme, GET assets/no CORS wildcard, POST refusal and credential-free health remain. Removing A refuses A while B serves. Planted clinical-column SELECT and changed lookup owner refuse new startup. A real UI CLI child exits0 on SIGTERM and its owned database sessions disappear. No credential appears in child output. Observed registry commit→explicit poll→HTML for a synthetic alias: 10 ms; this tiny harness is not a deployment/capacity bound.

freeze-revision-red.log: actual source mutation at1673320 disables scheduled and explicit revision observation after startup. Existing alias and initial unknown refusal succeeded, but the newly registered previously-negative alias returned 421 where native test required200. Exit1 is a semantic admission failure, not setup. Original source bytes restored in finally; final exact-head native run above passes. All owned processes/containers/scratch overlays removed. SHA256 manifest retained.

Setup/instrument corrections before final source: the migration runner required an explicit runtime password field; PostgreSQL evaluated a sequence privilege call on a non-sequence before relation filtering (now CASE-guarded); product resolver startup intentionally exposes TENANT_REGISTRY_UNAVAILABLE for unsafe lookup owner rather than its underlying catalogue error. These exploratory failures were not counted as semantic controls or final acceptance.

No fresh browser bundle build, full browser suite, full provisioning ceremony, restore census, full enabled corpus or capacity campaign ran in this lane. UI native overlay used this lane's previously copied private core bundle artifacts; joined deployment must build/qualify its own image and pass lifecycle census.

docs.title: How pages get here
docs.text:
Rule: rich pages are committed here; artifacts are only for private drafts.

An HTML page meant for the site (an interactive explainer, a dashboard, a figure that needs JavaScript) is committed to this directory. make site copies every git-tracked .html file here into the built site at the same path and lists it in the nav under Pages, titled by its <title>. Hosted artifact links are for private drafts only; a page that other people rely on lives here, under review like any other file.

The build adds <meta name="robots" content="noindex, nofollow"> to a page that does not carry one, and make site-check fails if any output page lacks it. Pages here are also subject to tools/site/exclusions.yaml.

Keep pages self-contained (inline CSS and JS, or files committed beside them) and free of personal or health data, like everything else in this public repo.
