docs.title: Vault Transit feasibility lab
docs.text:
Living document, last changed 2026-11-06 at 773c8bc59.

Implements the first bounded check for MT-SECRETS-CONTRACT, under the multitenant roadmap. Synthetic payloads and disposable loopback Vault only. The harness creates an isolated random mount, policies and consumer tokens, and removes only those resources on completion. It does not inspect existing secrets.

Run a disposable Vault development container with a randomly generated root token and a loopback-only published port. Pass its address and token through VAULT_ADDR and VAULT_TOKEN (never commit them), then:

node tools/lab/vault-transit/harness.js

Nonzero exit means failure. Successful output contains check names and the Vault version, never tokens, key material, ciphertext or revealed values. Do not treat development-mode storage, its root bootstrap token or HTTP as a production configuration.

The lab checks real Transit encryption/HMAC, non-exportability, scoped ACL refusals, wrong-key failure, rotation/rewrap and token revocation. A deliberately broader consumer demonstrates that the cross-tenant check detects an overbroad policy. The application still needs an authenticated tenant/consumer boundary, ciphertext/reference store, JWT encoding/version policy, audit and operational acceptance. Generic Transit decrypt is not an owner reveal API.

docs.title: mt-bench — Nightscout multitenancy micro-benchmarks
docs.text:
Living document, last changed 2026-11-10 at 3ec0260a0.

Seed harness for the experiments in docs/archive/tenancy/nightscout-multitenancy-discussion-2026-09-09.md.

These are micro-benchmarks used to rank hypotheses, not the full multi-tenant load harness described in §8 of that document. They answer narrow questions: how expensive is a cold tenant wake, does SQLite-in-WASM help on the server, does a columnar representation pay, and does SQLite-file-per-tenant survive a thousand tenants.

docs.title: Synthetic tenant
docs.text:
gen.js builds one 48-hour window shaped like real Nightscout data:

  • 576 SGV entries (5-minute cadence, xDrip/Dexcom field set)
  • 600 treatments (temp basals with duration/absolute/mills/endmills)
  • 576 devicestatus documents (Loop-shaped, including 72-point predicted.values arrays)

Field sets were taken from externals/cgm-remote-monitor-official/lib/data/ddata.js and the retention windows in lib/server/cache.js:26-31. It is synthetic: treatment heterogeneity and real upload burstiness are not modelled, which is exactly what the full harness in §8 must add.

docs.title: compose-baseline: MT-BENCH-BASELINE harness
docs.text:
Living document, last changed 2026-11-10 at ee1621b38.

Contributor-facing. Measures the one-host multitenant Compose reference (core deploy/multitenant) at 1, 10, 50 and 200 synthetic tenants with one hot tenant, and records the numbers. It claims no limits. Results: reports/tenancy/bench-baseline-2026-11-10/.

docs.title: What it measures
docs.text:
measurement instrument file in the run directory p50/p95/p99 latency per client shape, failure rate, dropped iterations k6 (k6/workload.js, grafana/k6:1.3.0) k6-summary.json, k6.log socket fanout: write sent to dataUpdate received, hot tenant and cold tenants probes/fanout.js (socket.io-client from the core lockfile) fanout.json reconnect recovery after a realtime restart: stock client, then a retrying client probes/fanout.js fanout.json recovery CPU and RSS per role, idle window and load window docker stats every 2 s (probes/sample.sh) docker-stats.tsv PostgreSQL backend states, wait events, ungranted locks pg_stat_activity, pg_locks every 2 s pg-activity.tsv, pg-locks.tsv statements and DB time per role; per-tenant window leases per second (evaluator and realtime cycle rate) pg_stat_statements, reset per phase pg-by-role-<phase>.tsv, pg-ops-<phase>.tsv, pg-statements-<phase>.tsv disk per tenant-day table growth over the run's rows (oracle/disk.sh) disk-before.txt, disk.txt stored-count oracle superuser psql in the postgres container, no API (oracle/oracle.sh) oracle-stored.tsv, oracle.txt host label: CPU, cores, RAM, disk, Docker, load average, other containers bench.sh host-before.txt, host-after.txt

summarize.js folds a run directory into summary.json.

docs.title: Client shapes (per tenant, per 5-minute CGM cycle)
docs.text:
shape request per cycle xDrip+/cgmsim uploader POST /api/v1/entries?token= (1 sgv) 1 Loop/oref0 uploader POST /api/v1/devicestatus?token= (Loop-shaped, 72 predictions) 1 AAPS-style uploader POST /api/v3/treatments, Bearer JWT exchanged once 1 follower apps GET /api/v1/entries/sgv.json?count=1 5 GET /api/v1/devicestatus.json?count=1, GET /api/v1/treatments.json?count=10, GET /api/v1/status.json 1 each browser socket Socket.IO polling, authorize with the exchanged JWT, as lib/client/index.js:1165,1218 probe

BENCH_ACCEL compresses the cycle (1 = real cadence, 10 = one cycle per 30 s). The hot tenant (index 0) carries BENCH_HOT_FACTOR (10) times every shape. The probe holds SOCKETS_HOT (20) sockets on the hot tenant and one on each of up to SOCKETS_COLD (40) other tenants, opened 250 ms apart, and posts one sgv every PROBE_INTERVAL_MS.

v1 POST /api/v1/treatments is not driven: the reference tenants do not enable careportal, so it answers 401, as a single-tenant site without careportal does (lib/api/treatments/index.js:287).

docs.title: External traffic generator — isolated profile
docs.text:
Living document, last changed 2026-11-12 at be962719d.

Contributor-facing source capability. Runtime and cloud behavior are UNMEASURED until the remote owner runs a reviewed smoke. The current colocated pilot is unchanged.

The new joined-external-generator-v1 profile uses one application/PostgreSQL host and one generator. Both k6 and the stock Socket.IO traffic move to the generator. SQL, stored-count controls, evaluator inspection and role restart stay on the app host. A controller mediates fixed, ordered, run/nonce/cell-bound phases over its existing SSH connections. No private inspection or SQL RPC is exposed to traffic.

Traffic runs as nsload without sudo, supplementary groups or a Docker socket. The trusted root supervisor launches only the pinned k6 image, fixed script, read-only scoped tenant input, fixed workload and bounded run. The stock SDK is installed from the exact application lockfile and verified by its resolved entry. The public edge binds only to the selected private VPC address. Database and private application listeners retain the original internal binding.

Request-to-frame durations use the generator's monotonic clock. Restart-to-frame observation starts at the generator arm and therefore includes controller delay. A connected old socket with a post-arm frame cannot pass recovery: the observer requires a new disconnect/connect generation and a later frame, plus the actual app restart acknowledgement. App-local helpers prove the real role restart and fresh evaluator work independently. Cross-host clock subtraction is not used.

The per-write SQL latency poller is NOT_RUN in this profile. Strict evaluator progress and recovery remain app-side, but they are different observers. The old writeToEvaluationMs diagnostic is explicitly UNMEASURED. Load query/CPU deltas therefore reflect both placement and observer changes; they cannot be attributed solely to moving generators. Common traffic, correctness and idle metrics retain their stated scopes. No result automatically grants capacity acceptance.

Preparation and the two-node driver live in nightscout-deploy under tools/perf-cloud/prepare-external-generator.js. The new extension descriptor is hashed separately from the unchanged base joined instrument. Its producer file allowlist is checked against the actual controller transfer interface before keys or deployment. Unsupported layouts, a second generator and separate PostgreSQL refuse. A later PostgreSQL split or retained per-write correlated SQL observer is outside this increment.

Focused source controls (no Docker, cloud, npm install or application campaign):

python3 -I -B tools/mt-bench/external-generator/test_contract.py
node --test tools/mt-bench/external-generator/test_recovery.cjs

They cover bounded partial-line/EOF handling, run/node/nonce/sequence mismatches, metric envelope compatibility, completeness failures, producer transfer equality, readiness ordering, server recovery/oracle refusal and real reconnect semantics. The deployment repository's existing npm run test:perf-cloud includes the self-contained controller controls. Controls use synthetic fixtures; source-only passes do not qualify real networking, imports, resource use or cloud teardown.

Enabled idle uses the base adapter's failure-bookend helper. It attempts the existing AFTER snapshots when assessment refuses and preserves the original failure. The sampler-disabled and enabled windows remain 60 and 120 seconds.

The app-side helper inherits current idle assessor module4/artifactv2, the one bounded selected-owner completion tail AFTER successful original cost bookends, and SQL request-bracket metadata through adapter.enabled_idle and adapter.phase_snapshot. The base instrument pins this shared implementation; the external descriptor and cell observer profile name the exact idle policy. Tail cost is separate from the original60/120-second windows. No generator-side poll, new SQL query, global tail-quiescence claim or application-clock change is introduced. Missing or unresolved completion remains refused.

docs.title: Joined M7 capacity adapter
docs.text:
Living document, last changed 2026-11-12 at af1bd379f.

This prepares the next measurement; it does not establish a capacity result. The prior capacity record and authorization/allocation profiles retain their own source scope. No prior working-tree lib mount or bootstrap patch is reused here. Only committed paired core/deployment sources can serve a run.

A separate fresh-image diagnostic permits bounded useful tests before full acceptance without claiming acceptance or capacity.

The coordinator must finish the coherent candidate and its full acceptance, then hand over a quiet host. This lane does not stop foreign containers, including a peer's nsauthz-base-n1000, or start a capacity campaign during other work.

docs.title: Source and ownership
docs.text:
adapter.py prepare creates a unique detached core worktree from a full commit, archives the deployment's committed Compose tree over its deployment directory, and writes the product build overlay marker. Every remaining core input must pass the shipping build's two-source admission. There is no borrowed node_modules: probe dependencies use a separate owned install of the exact committed core package.json and lockfile with npm ci --include=dev --omit=optional --ignore-scripts --force. The serving image still prunes development dependencies. generator-provenance.json pins host Node/npm paths, hashes and versions, manifests, client entry/version/hash; actual stock-client resolution is checked before deployment traffic and each workload. The controller must preserve that host toolchain across cells/profiles. Preparation failures retain private prepare-commands/ raw stdout/stderr even before owner.json exists; prepare-failure.json contains only a sanitized error code. Generator installation output is private under generator-commands/. The image's core/deployment labels and immutable image ID are checked. Serving mounts cannot replace /opt/app or any subtree; all existing binding mounts must resolve within this cell's own private state. External/shared resources refuse. Ambient NS_/BENCH_/NODE_OPTIONS settings cannot silently alter the experiment.

Every cell has a random project nonce, private worktree/state, randomly selected loopback port and ownership labels on its containers/networks/volumes. Cleanup verifies ownership before removing only that project and its recorded worktree. An ownership/source mismatch refuses rather than forcing cleanup. No attach mode or foreign teardown command exists. Raw state/config contains synthetic credentials; keep the entire work directory private and outside any checkout. Do not commit it.

Build, deploy and traffic require a source-matched frozen acceptance receipt:

{"kind":"joined-acceptance","status":"UNMEASURED","pair":{"core":"FULL_COMMITTED_CORE_SHA","deploy":"FULL_COMMITTED_DEPLOY_SHA"},"evidenceSha256":"SHA256_OF_COORDINATOR_ACCEPTANCE_RECORD"}

The example deliberately refuses. The coordinator supplies PASS only after acceptance; provisional source heads are never silently substituted. The receipt is an attribution gate, not a new permission dialog. A build/initial deployment also requires load below the chosen quiet threshold and zero foreign running containers. During owned workload, foreign-container checks continue; the owned workload's own load average is measured instead of rejecting its expected CPU. Host inventories include container IDs/labels, image IDs, load, RAM, Docker/context, kernel and process names/CPU/RSS, never command arguments/environments. Only local Unix-socket Docker contexts are supported: host metrics must describe that daemon.

docs.title: Fresh-image functional diagnostic before full acceptance
docs.text:
Living document, last changed 2026-11-12 at 094dcc182.

This is an explicit diagnostic authorization/result scope. It does not fabricate joined acceptance, unlock a capacity run or satisfy pilot/ladder gates. The remote controller owns all cloud activity and enforces its current maintainer-authorized spending/deadline policy. This instrument creates no cloud resources. Use only the coordinator's selected committed source pair and matching image/instrument identity. Do not substitute an older image or source mount.

A diagnostic receipt has this shape (replace identity placeholders from committed source/adapter.py manifest; the placeholders deliberately refuse):

{"kind":"joined-diagnostic","status":"AUTHORIZED_DIAGNOSTIC","pair":{"core":"FULL_CORE_SHA","deploy":"FULL_DEPLOY_SHA"},"instrument":"INSTRUMENT_CONTENT_SHA256","limits":{"tenants":2,"apiReplicas":2,"trafficSeconds":180}}

Absolute maximums are10 tenants,2 API instances and180 seconds client traffic. The coordinator may authorize lower limits. The default cheap case is2 tenants. The receipt permits only build, deploy and diagnose for this profile; it is rejected by CAP run, remote pilot and full ladder authorization. A diagnostic result cannot be reused as a receipt. Full acceptance remains NOT_RUN.

python3 tools/mt-bench/m7-joined/adapter.py prepare \
  --directory /private/new-diagnostic-cell --profile fresh-image-diagnostic \
  --core-repo /sources/core.git --core-commit "$M7_CORE_SHA" \
  --deploy-repo /sources/deploy.git --deploy-commit "$M7_DEPLOY_SHA" \
  --image "$M7_PAIRED_IMAGE" --receipt /private/diagnostic-receipt.json \
  --tenants 2 --replicas 2
python3 tools/mt-bench/m7-joined/adapter.py build /private/new-diagnostic-cell
python3 tools/mt-bench/m7-joined/adapter.py deploy /private/new-diagnostic-cell
python3 tools/mt-bench/m7-joined/adapter.py diagnose /private/new-diagnostic-cell
python3 tools/mt-bench/m7-joined/adapter.py check-diagnostic /private/new-diagnostic-cell/diagnostic.json
python3 tools/mt-bench/m7-joined/adapter.py down /private/new-diagnostic-cell

The shared shipping deployment logic is reused: infrastructure/bootstrap, admin/feed, provision, restore commissioning, API instances, DATA prime, local private publisher, remaining roles/UI/nginx. Exact instance health and source/binding errors stay errors; this diagnostic adds no surrogate or weakened role. A selected sharded placement continues to refuse without its committed controlled-replacement helper. Matching UID/GID1000, local Docker/Git and image prerequisites from REMOTE-SEAM.md still apply. A busy host is captured as diagnostic-only, not falsely called a quiet capacity host. This permission does not authorize a local/cloud capacity campaign.

The fixed client criterion uses the owned exact-lock generator Socket.IO library and registered hostname URLs with loopback-DNS Agent, never127URL/extraHeaders.Host. It exchanges the DATA credential, GETs status, primes one stock polling socket per tenant, POSTs one current synthetic SGV per tenant, and requires that tenant's frame to carry the new timestamp. It observes an actual legacy realtime container restart and requires unaided stock reconnect plus current frame, then GETs status again. There are exactly 4N successful criterion DATA HTTP requests on success, plus separately counted recognized warming probes; stock polling/reconnect is bounded by the traffic deadline. No manual reconnect workaround or k6/performance window runs.

Client acknowledgements use load/client-acks.json (not a claimed k6 run). Independent SQL stored counts must match; the same owned row-marker RED/restore GREEN control is required. PASS needs every HTTP/prime/frame/restart/recovery/oracle criterion and source/image/instrument/host identity. diagnostic.json is kind m7-joined-fresh-image-diagnostic, with fullAcceptance:NOT_RUN and capacity:NO-MEASUREMENT. Exit0 plus M7_DIAGNOSTIC_PASS_ONLY has only this meaning. Exit1/refusal, an incomplete observation, missing frame or failed recovery is never PASS. It cannot satisfy check-pilot or check-campaign.

Artifacts: common source/ownership/deployment logs, diagnostic host inventory, load/diagnostic.log, bounded observations/partial stage, client acknowledgements, independent stored oracle/control and diagnostic.json. Credentials remain in private custody. Host job PID/start identity is recorded so down stops only its own runner; the controller owns outer budget abort, evidence checkpoint and VM teardown. Build/ bootstrap time is outside the client-traffic deadline and stays within the controller's separate spend/deadline policy. No actual fresh app/image diagnostic is implied by a passing mocked/fixture instrument check.

Fresh generator installation and actual client resolution run before infrastructure startup. A development-pruned serving image is valid: its node_modules is never borrowed by the generator. Preserve private prepare-commands/, prepare-failure.json, generator-commands/, generator-verifications/ and generator-provenance.json on failure. Raw stdout/stderr can contain credentials; do not publish these directories.

Explicit diagnostic HTTP calls retain load/diagnostic-http.json even on refusal. The bounded trail contains at most4N+512 records and262,144 serialized bytes: request number, logical stage, zero-based tenant index, method, fixed route class, response status, a bounded uppercase typed error code, and a sanitized local failure code. It records no URL, exchange path, query, host, tenant identifier, request/response body or token. The private file is mode0600; diagnostic observations link it and retain the terminal instrument code. In-flight records can have null status when no response arrived. This trail describes explicit DATA HTTP calls, not Socket.IO internals.

GET status retries only an actual503 response with exact typed TENANT_WARMING. The first refusal remains recorded and classified in the current run. Polls use 200ms cadence inside the existing global deadline, with at most512 recognized warming probes globally; reaching the probe limit refuses. Exchange, mutation, 401, unknown503 and untyped503 refusals stop immediately. No credential fallback, role change or deadline extension exists. This policy follows the measured API cold-start contract; it does not retroactively classify historical remoteD.

HTTP accounting version2 requires successful criterionHttpRequests=4N (also retained as dataHttpRequests), separate warmProbeHttpRequests, and physicalHttpRequests=criterionHttpRequests+warmProbeHttpRequests for a passing result. Trail records equal physical requests and retain the explicit byte bound. Failed results can also contain refused or pending requests, so they do not claim that passing equation. Warm responses alone never satisfy HTTP, write, SQL, frame, observed restart or stock-recovery criteria. Historical profiles/results keep their original instrument source; no old capture is reinterpreted as version2.

On terminal cleanup the owned Socket.IO HTTP agent rejects late queued polling requests before destroying its sockets. Agent.destroy() alone permits later requests to create new referenced sockets. Actual spawned CLI controls cover an HTTP refusal after one stock socket connects with no frames; failure exits with its original diagnostic code rather than waiting for the traffic deadline. Python retains that safe terminal code and reports process termination or exit timeout separately. This does not force process exit or change the traffic budget.

docs.title: Source-paired profile provenance
docs.text:
Living document, last changed 2026-11-12 at 198ad1534.

This instrument capability does not authorize a campaign. The coordinator still pins the exact source pair, image, instrument and acceptance receipt. Existing 094 diagnostic evidence is immutable and does not acquire these new fields.

python3 tools/mt-bench/m7-joined/adapter.py capabilities emits the tracked, versioned capabilities.json, without Docker or cloud access. The reserved deployment transport must verify this contract and the committed adapter.py manifest content hash before activating its pilot. This lane does not change that transport or activate a pilot.

prepare --diagnostics off|on --diagnostics-interval-ms 5000 defaults to off. The interval range is1000..60000ms. Only NS_M7_DIAGNOSTICS and NS_M7_DIAGNOSTICS_INTERVAL_MS are set; ambient NS variables remain excluded. The frozen Compose environment, generated private environment overrides and actual running-container environment are checked. Unsupported numbered worker roles refuse rather than silently escaping diagnostics/log inventory.

After infrastructure bootstrap and before provisioning, fingerprint.cjs reads the actual private state/primer/config.json, requires the exact synthetic seed shape without settings/overrides and checks the pinned provisioning source's blank settings insert. It verifies nine source blobs against the paired core commit, then constructs the default tenant environment from those source bytes. No SQL seed, owner setting mutation or additional HTTP request is used.

Fingerprint schema1 hashes a fixed, bounded projection: units; ordered enabled plugins; timeFormat/dayStart/dayEnd, focusHours/heartbeat; display/alarm booleans, alarm minute arrays/timeago minutes; four BG thresholds; devicestatus advanced and days. Other strings, authentication, credentials, runtime state, identifiers, times and the full status document are excluded. Whitelisted values exist only in RAM. Exported evidence contains only schema/hash, exact source-blob IDs and a seed-shape proof. This is a selected-settings fingerprint, not a claim to hash every server setting or every extended plugin option.

The existing generated k6 r_status response supplies observations. Successful 200 bodies over128KiB or malformed/missing selected fields are invalid. A changed hash is a functional failure. Zero valid observations is UNMEASURED and cannot pass. Metrics are settings_fingerprint_observed, settings_fingerprint_invalid, settings_fingerprint_mismatch; the adapter writes settingsFingerprintObservation with counts and verdict to its summary. No status body, whitelist projection or per-tenant label is exported by this seam. k6 itself retains its existing transient response handling.

settingsFingerprint also records the exact six Transit purpose/type schema from pinned registry rules. transit.keyCountObservation is UNMEASURED: source schema is not an observed Vault key count. Registry defaults include their current complete enabled-plugin list, rather than the historical static lean five-plugin profile. The source hash records that difference without overriding new defaults to imitate the historical workload.

profileSelection contains version, settings schema/hash/source provenance, diagnostics selection, topology and a canonical SHA256 over those fields. It deliberately excludes tenant count and API replica count. All pilot levels and all same-workload API-scaling cells must carry the exact same object/hash. Changing diagnostics, settings or realtime/evaluator topology creates a distinct profile; it cannot be called API replication alone. Pilot --replicas 1|2|4 selects one fixed count across500/750/1000 (default1); profileReplicas records that choice. Fixed2 is a pilot profile, not evidence of API scaling. Full-ladder strictness remains distinct from a coordinator-pinned capacity milestone.

Current topology is registry-default with verified vault server command and no Vault Agent overlay. Server observations are never named Agent observations. The existing Agent overlay conversion and component-scaling axes remain outside this default-profile capability. No overlay is activated here.

Before teardown, the adapter captures private fixed-role log tails with5seconds per role,64KiB per role and512KiB total caps. It kills timed-out/bounded producers and records truncation, timeout, return code and failures in private role-logs/manifest.json. Files are0600/directories0700; they can contain secrets and must not be published. Missing or truncated output proves no absence. Log collection failures do not replace the existing teardown operation. k6 resource observations are retained under windows.*.loadGenerators, separately from serving roles; exited k6 RSS is UNMEASURED, never fabricated. Missing serving snapshots, RSS or samples make measurements incomplete.

Focused checks:

M7_PROFILE_TEST_CORE=/private/owned-pinned-core \
M7_PROFILE_TEST_COMMIT="$CORE_SHA" \
python3 -m unittest discover -s tools/mt-bench/m7-joined -p 'test_*.py' -v

The explicit core fixture needs its own exact-lock dependencies. It starts only the actual status router over local HTTP with synthetic authorization, then executes generated workload shapes under deterministic HTTP mocks. This proves projection compatibility and mismatch detection; it is not the full serving stack, stock k6 scheduler, capacity or component scaling acceptance. Ordinary unit discovery without the explicit core fixture skips that source-specific case and cannot be cited as its proof.

docs.title: Remote controller seam
docs.text:
Living document, last changed 2026-11-11 at 668db69bb.

The controller owns cloud creation/transport/bundling, checkpoints and teardown, and enforces the maintainer-authorized controller-selected spending/deadline policy. This adapter makes no cloud API call and does not estimate or waive that ceiling. Do not start it before the coordinator supplies the accepted core/deploy tuple and frozen acceptance receipt. A budget/deadline abort is incomplete evidence, never a passing capacity result. An explicitly authorized bounded fresh-image diagnostic can precede full acceptance; its separate receipt/result contract cannot unlock pilot/CAP.

docs.title: Host and source prerequisites
docs.text:
• Linux, local Unix-socket Docker Engine/Compose v2, cgroup v2, /proc, Bash, GNU date/coreutils, procps, OpenSSL, tar, Git, Python3.11+, a source-supported Node version and npm. Exact Node/npm paths, binary hashes and versions are pinned for the generator; changing them refuses a workload or subsequent ladder cell/profile. npm registry access is needed for the separate owned exact-lock install (private cache; lifecycle scripts disabled).
  • Run the product's local preparation as UID/GID1000, matching the shipped app/ bootstrap user and private0700 state. Another UID refuses before deployment; the controller provisions the matching account/Docker access. Do not broaden private permissions to compensate.
  • A checked-out committed alignment instrument with its Git identity/index and reused tracked capacity/compose-baseline files. adapter.py manifest lists exact paths/hashes. A copied directory without Git attribution is insufficient.
  • Core and deploy repositories (bare is acceptable) containing the exact full commits. The adapter creates its own detached worktree and archives deployment from its commit, not a peer worktree. No borrowed node_modules/source mount.
  • Matching paired application image already transported/built, or build it through the adapter after source acceptance/quiet-host handoff. Both source labels and immutable image ID must match. Have the committed binding's pinned infrastructure images and a k6 image available; k6 is resolved to its immutable local ID.
  • Enough disk for image layers, one active core checkout, owned lockfile generator dependencies, private PG/Vault volumes and raw logs. The controller budgets/checks available RAM, disk and runtime before spend. Captured host identity must stay identical across all pilot steps; a new/replaced daemon or hardware profile cannot silently join.

The adapter refuses other running containers; it records competitor/process metadata without stopping them. A provider control-plane container must be resolved with the coordinator before handoff rather than hidden from the record. The private outputs contain synthetic custody material. Keep state/checkpoints private; only selected sanitized evidence belongs in a public record. The controller preserves raw artifacts and provenance before destroying its owned VM, subject to its budget/deadline.

docs.title: Explicit pre-acceptance baseline collection
docs.text:
Living document, last changed 2026-11-12 at 7219ad70b.

This opt-in admission permits measurement while functional acceptance is pending. It never grants functional or capacity acceptance. The existing accepted path remains the default. The selected profile is still remote-pilot: unchanged 500/750/1000 counts, API1/RT1/EV1, Vault Server, diagnostics OFF/5000, HOT10, two sockets/tenant, 120s idle and 300s load. Source ownership, exact image, quiet-host, settings, stock clients, SQL accepted-write oracle, clinical/output, strict recovery, cleanup and failed-level stop predicates remain unchanged. The fresh-image diagnostic's <=10 tenant boundary is unchanged.

A coordinator supplies exactly:

version: 1
kind: joined-measurement-authorization
status: AUTHORIZED_UNACCEPTED_MEASUREMENT
pair: {core: <full source commit>, deploy: <full deployment commit>}
instrument: <exact current content SHA256>
imageId: <actual qualified sha256 image ID>
runId: <exact controller run identity>
functionalAcceptanceAtAuthorization: PENDING
purpose: PRE_ACCEPTANCE_BASELINE_ONLY
limits:
  tenantCounts: [500, 750, 1000]
  apiReplicas: 1
  realtimeReplicas: 1
  evaluatorReplicas: 1
  maximumRunMinutes: 180

Extra fields, acceptance claims or an acceptance evidence digest refuse. This is not a manufactured joined-acceptance PASS. The controller retains its existing global run deadline/fleet ownership and resource accounting; the source binds run/image/180-minute limit in each manifest and verifies actual image identity before deployment. This receipt contains no independent expiry timestamp; it does not authorize bypassing the controller's existing run deadline.

Prepare adds these explicit flags to the normal source command:

--profile remote-pilot --measurement-mode unaccepted
--run-id <controller-run> --image-id <actual-qualified-ID>
--maximum-run-minutes 180 --tenants 500 --replicas 1

Repeat only the prescribed count with the same immutable receipt/pair/image/ instrument/run identity. build, deploy and run commands are unchanged. campaign.py pilot accepts the same measurement/run/image/minute flags; all and replica ladders cannot select this admission. Parent transport uses its own existing ownership/deadline orchestration; no new shipping sequence is added. adapter.py measurement-capabilities returns a separate explicit version-1 support descriptor. The existing cap4 capabilities.json remains byte-identical.

A cell is m7-joined-unaccepted-measurement-cell; an aggregate is m7-joined-unaccepted-measurement. Both carry measurementMode unaccepted, functionalAcceptance UNACCEPTED, functionalAcceptanceAtAuthorization PENDING, capacityAcceptance NOT_GRANTED, runId and maximumRunMinutes. collectionStatus COMPLETE/FAILED is separate from the original correctness verdict PASS/FAIL. A completed measurement with a failed correctness predicate still fails and stops progression. Early failure retains raw artifacts plus a bounded typed unaccepted-collection-failure.json; it never rewrites existing summary data or invents successful work. No raw credentials/commands are added to public errors.

check-unaccepted-measurement uses the same pilot cell predicates and validates only complete bounded collection. Its success string explicitly says NOT_ACCEPTANCE. Accepted check-pilot, check-campaign and the actual receipt gate reject this scope, including otherwise valid unaccepted cells wrapped in an accepted-shaped record. Gate acceptance-only validation stays self-contained; its marker refusal does not import a missing capacity module in a standalone copied-validator control. Later same-candidate acceptance requires a separately reviewed qualification; never overwrite or relabel the original unaccepted captures.

Focused tests use recording-only fixtures and no Docker/cloud/application run. control_unaccepted.py image removes the receipt's image-equality guard in memory; control_unaccepted.py accepted-gate removes actual cell-gate scope refusal. Each must turn its named test red, then untouched source must pass. No source file or production authorization is modified by those controls.

docs.title: Explicit M7 component profiles — integration interface
docs.text:
Living document, last changed 2026-11-12 at 77e91b02d.

This is a pure declaration capability. It neither enables a topology nor runs a measurement. Every identity and comparison retains runtimeProof: UNMEASURED. It cannot substitute for the producer's freeze, runtime, SQL/isolation, settings, evaluator-progress, recovery or acceptance gates. The existing producer remains unchanged. MT-SCALE-UNBOUND remains open.

docs.title: Sources and boundary
docs.text:
Built from alignment 8f839da964fb3274a4428c994a43132b58ea3f24, with read-only shipping inspection of deployment eea9b6cac96d42b48237c00c226394f9bfe37cfb and immutable producer c8a7a9b04a165b96a9659a9306df3d03be02a081. The separate API lane owns moving evaluator-progress producer/receipt changes. Only this module, its schema, tests and interface document belong to this lane. No runtime/deployment, adapter, provenance, capabilities or receipt file changes.

The adopted evaluator shape is fixed partitions with one selected owner per tenant. This declaration supports standalone and fixed worker topologies. It adds neither PostgreSQL HA nor realtime failover. An optional Agent remains a separate process alongside the Vault server; server observations cannot count as Agent observations.

docs.title: Mongo isolation PoC — enforced-filter seam vs. bypass, and aggregation-as-view
docs.text:
Living document, last changed 2026-11-10 at 3ec0260a0.

Backs the maintainer's specific pushback on §6.1/§6.2 of nightscout-multitenancy-discussion-2026-09-09.md: "most of the change is a tenant discriminator, and Mongo's projections/aggregation can cover what Postgres joins/views do — does multitenancy really require leaving Mongo?"

Two things measured against a live MongoDB 7 container, not asserted:

  1. Does a single enforced-filter repository seam actually hold, i.e. is (a) from §6.1's three Mongo options ("application-only isolation behind a single enforced query-builder seam") actually leak-proof if every call site is disciplined to go through it — and does it still leak the moment one call site (mirroring today's ctx.store.collection(env.entries_collection), lib/server/entries.js:203-205) bypasses it.
  2. Can Mongo's aggregation pipeline reproduce a Postgres-join/view use case — correlating treatments (temp basal) with entries (glucose in the same window), which is the kind of query a Postgres view or JOIN would be reached for.

docs.title: Running
docs.text:
docker run -d --name mongo-iso-poc -p 27117:27017 mongo:7
sleep 3
node seed.js
node test.js
docker rm -f mongo-iso-poc

docs.title: Mongo views PoC — is there a server-enforced RLS equivalent after all?
docs.text:
Living document, last changed 2026-11-10 at 3ec0260a0.

Backs a maintainer's pushback on nightscout-multitenancy-discussion-2026-09-09.md §6.1: "Mongo's projections and tooling should be equally feasible; people just find tables more familiar."

§6.1 concluded that "MongoDB has no server-enforced per-document ACL comparable to RLS", and §6.1.1 tested an application-level seam and found it leaks on bypass. Neither tested the mechanism MongoDB actually provides for this: a read-only view whose pipeline reads $$USER_ROLES (7.0+), with users granted find on the view and no privilege on the base collection.

Measured against a live MongoDB 8.3.9 container, not argued.

docs.title: Running
docs.text:
docker run -d --name mongo-views-poc -p 27118:27017 mongo:8 --auth
sleep 6
docker cp setup.js  mongo-views-poc:/tmp/ && docker exec mongo-views-poc mongosh --quiet --file /tmp/setup.js
docker cp test.js   mongo-views-poc:/tmp/ && docker exec mongo-views-poc mongosh --quiet --file /tmp/test.js
docker cp limits.js mongo-views-poc:/tmp/ && docker exec mongo-views-poc mongosh --quiet --file /tmp/limits.js

docs.title: Admission commissioning
docs.text:
Living document, last changed 2026-11-12 at 43bbc7c7f.

This first executable episode qualifies wiring and normal retirement only. It uses core074 and deployment3d13 with the independently audited32b image. It does not claim the full clinical admission episode or native acceptance.

profile.cjs admits the exact source/overlay before evaluating the actual expanded configuration. The explicit qualification topology is API2/realtime2/evaluator2, four realtime shards and16 synthetic tenant slots. The finite source profile retains actual requested pool ceilings and held lifetime lanes, direct group ceilings4 (persistent feed clients separately1), metadata observers2, control1, bootstrap2, and one API generation of uncertain overlap. It derives PostgreSQL314 from258 current-worker credits,48 overlap,5 external and3 reserved. These are configured ceilings, not measured connections or a production recommendation. Cold admission1/pending9 with25..75ms jitter is an explicit functional experiment; source startup producers remain4. Unknown/source/roster/capacity changes refuse.

docs.title: Executable boundary
docs.text:
Commands below take an owner-private prepared directory/spec, not public secrets:

node profile.cjs PRIVATE_SOURCE_INPUT NEW_PROFILE_OUTPUT
python3 commissioning.py prepare PRIVATE_PREPARED_ROOT NEW_PLAN_OUTPUT
python3 commissioning.py dry-run PRIVATE_PLAN NEW_RECORDING_OUTPUT
python3 commissioning.py preflight PRIVATE_PLAN NEW_PREFLIGHT_OUTPUT
# Only after the coordinator reviews and authorizes the exact plan:
python3 commissioning.py run PRIVATE_PLAN NEW_EPISODE_OUTPUT

All output directories are new and mode0700. Inputs are regular nofollow private bounded JSON files. The plan pins the qualified image/qualification bytes, controller and separate collector fingerprint, source pair, prepared-file digests, nonce project, source environment, proposed port/subnets and program file hashes. The actual source profile, state and image must agree; old479/90f does not qualify this episode. The prepared image tag is already bound to the qualified ID.

The real run first checks the local Docker context, all Docker network ranges, IPv4 routes, existing project resources, listener ports and declared address capacity. It repeats that check immediately before allocation; default forwarding is recorded separately from allocated networks. It never picks an alternative or changes a foreign resource. A collision or unknown input refuses. The preflight is a snapshot, not an atomic reservation against another owner.

The fixed sequence starts only PostgreSQL/Vault as infrastructure, waits for source health, runs infrastructure bootstrap once with --no-deps, binds the controller, and starts admin/API/API2 through the shipped controller. Actual health children run with already-existing worker claims; claim file bytes must remain unchanged. Three charged tagged captures bracket start, a clean API stop/restart and retirement. Matching private ACK/source/nonce/full tags and ledger retirement are checked. No tenant or clinical DATA is provisioned. The full11-role profile remains declared even though this first episode starts only three workers. Unstarted roles are not silently removed from the budget.

Normal worker stops use the controller. Finally capture validates every exact CID, StartedAt, project, working directory, service and image before stopping. Each failed row is retained while later owned rows still receive cleanup attempts. A successful bounded full Docker roster can prove that an old known CID was removed, without inferring PostgreSQL credit retirement. Infrastructure and an unbound/failed worker may need an exact-CID emergency stop; this cleanup never refunds a generation or claims a clean ACK. This fallback is part of the concrete plan for coordinator review, not ordinary restart authority. A timed-out host command can leave Docker daemon work uncertain: the result keeps that uncertainty even when the current retained containers are stopped. No cleanup removes containers, networks, volumes, claims, locks or history. If preflight failed before allocation, cleanup performs no Docker search/stop.

Host commands have a fresh process group, a retained WNOWAIT leader through TERM/KILL/drain/reap, finite deadlines and kernel file-size limits. The episode has900 seconds (90 reserved for cleanup),384 host commands (64 reserved) and32MiB host output (8MiB reserved). Each of three nested read-only collectors has its own existing120-second/16MiB bounds; at most three held commissioning workers yield at most15 nested commands. Thus nested raw capture allowance is another48MiB, not included in the host32MiB. Health is polled every two seconds under a 90-second per-readiness instrument bound. The regular command allowance covers the worst-case six readiness schedules. Parent collector stdout/stderr has its own 2 MiB per-call bound, counted in host output; the 48 MiB allowance is internal raw collector files. These are instrument/resource bounds, not product latency SLOs.

docs.title: NRG resolution PoC — cost of a sidecar host→tenant resolution hop
docs.text:
Living document, last changed 2026-11-10 at 3ec0260a0.

Backs §9.4 of nightscout-multitenancy-discussion-2026-09-09.md: ~/src/nightscout-roles-gateway (NRG) is a real, already-built external gateway that resolves an expected_name (hostname) to a tenant/upstream via a two-table SQL join, then enforces RBAC/group-policy/schedule rules, and hands NGINX an x-upstream-origin header (lib/routes.js:327-330, lib/policies/index.js:33-49). This measures the concrete cost of that hop, mirroring its actual query shape, against the alternative of folding host→tenant resolution directly into cgm-remote-monitor's own request path (§5.1/§9.1's tenant-resolution middleware).

docs.text:

docs.title: RLS PoC — Postgres row-level security, measured against a live container
docs.text:
Living document, last changed 2026-11-10 at 3ec0260a0.

Backs §6.1 and §10.2 of nightscout-multitenancy-discussion-2026-09-09.md: does Postgres RLS actually do what Nocturne's code claims, at what cost, and how does it compare to the isolation Nightscout gets today from MongoDB with an application-only filter? Reimplements Nocturne's verified pattern (externals/nocturne/src/Infrastructure/.../NocturneDbContext.cs:14-64, Migrations/20260227034745_EnforceMultitenancy.cs:66-76, Interceptors/TenantConnectionInterceptor.cs) with knex/pg instead of EF Core, because that is Node's tool for this, not a description of the .NET version.

docs.title: Index
docs.text:
Living document, last changed 2026-09-09 at 19544b5d3.

Rust counterpart to the Node micro-benchmarks, answering "would a non-Node host help?".

Fixtures are shared with the Node scripts. Generate them first:

node -e "const {mkTenant}=require('../gen');const fs=require('fs');const os=require('os');
  const d=process.env.MTBENCH_WORK||os.tmpdir()+'/mt-bench';fs.mkdirSync(d,{recursive:true});
  const t=mkTenant();fs.writeFileSync(d+'/t.json',JSON.stringify(t));
  fs.writeFileSync(d+'/sgvs.json',JSON.stringify(t.sgvs));"

Then:

cargo run --release -- time        # parse throughput, three representations
cargo run --release -- mem-value   # RSS for 200 tenants, serde_json::Value
cargo run --release -- mem-typed   # RSS for 200 tenants, typed structs
cargo run --release -- mem-col     # RSS for 200 tenants, columnar struct-of-arrays

Memory modes run one representation per process on purpose: the allocator reuses freed pages, so measuring several shapes in one process understates the later ones badly.

Dependency versions are pinned low because the machine used had rustc 1.68. On a modern toolchain, drop the = pins in Cargo.toml.

docs.title: Tagged admission measurement
docs.text:
Living document, last changed 2026-11-12 at 06e3473ea.

The proposed instrument measures the selected connection-admission candidate. It does not change the reference measurement selector. Its first implemented boundary is a read-only intake in tagged_admission.py. It attributes the source observer's authenticated connection counts to exact ledger generations and capabilities. The result always states nativeAcceptance: UNMEASURED and grants no lifecycle authority.

The intake checks the exact core/deployment pair, image, plan hash, PostgreSQL identity and epoch, original process container ID and start time, held-generation roster and complete tag set. It retains the raw observer rows. Empty counts do not release credits. A preauthentication backend can be absent from the database census. Original application names remain UNKNOWN unless an actual snapshot from the same incarnation supplies them. There is no live state.json: the worker callback currently updates memory, and shutdown writes a private ACK. An ACK from a different incarnation cannot supply a mapping.

The controller contract lives in the deployment repository at bindings/compose/multitenant/CONNECTION-BUDGET.md. The intake is pinned to the reviewed pair in its constants. A new deployment observer command needs its own reviewed source pin before the intake admits it. Do not substitute a similar source or change the old selector's refusals.

docs.title: Controller-owned driver boundary
docs.text:
The smallest real driver must use the deployment's fixed controller API:

node "$BINDING/connection-budget-cli.js" "$STATE" bind
node "$BINDING/connection-budget-cli.js" "$STATE" start "$DECLARED_SLOT"
node "$BINDING/connection-budget-cli.js" "$STATE" observe
node "$BINDING/connection-budget-cli.js" "$STATE" stop "$DECLARED_SLOT"

observe is present in the exact deployment source pinned by the intake. The earlier 10014 source supports only bind/start/stop. Do not call ports.observe directly: that bypasses the controller lock and durable observer reservation. Do not substitute an uncharged psql command. The observer reports authenticated PostgreSQL connections only.

The driver must first verify the prepared pair and private files against the actual built image and retained source-input attestation. It must retain exact controller command results, direct process exit codes and immutable raw files in an ignored run workspace. A failed or uncertain effect stops the driver; it does not retry, remove locks, force a stop or refund a generation.

Episode Controlled effects Required actual capture Initial startup Start declared slots in dependency order through the controller; process initialization may overlap after starts Observer snapshots, actual source health, exact container identities, readiness and held-generation counts Full application restart Stop exact declared workers, collect matching ACKs, then start new generations Old CID/start-time custody, retirement decisions, new incarnations and finite recovery Partial restart Stop and start the selected role through the controller Before/after observer snapshots and independent healthy tenant B observation during the interruption Storm Run the declared request workload against the admitted services, within its pinned bounds Sample counts, reserved observer costs, overflow refusals and recovery; never infer preauth absence from SQL TIME and isolation Use the clinical owner's source-pinned bounded workload and observer Fresh accepted input, changed acquisition/checkpoint, finite due time, tenant isolation and unchanged authority checks

The clinical owner must supply the actual healthy-B and TIME capture interfaces. A role marked running, an empty census, or source-only tests cannot replace those observations. Each episode retains its own actual source, workload and instrument identity. Full/browser/clinical acceptance and final prcheck remain coordinator owned. No episode has run through this new instrument yet.

tagged_capture.py is the smallest capture driver. It invokes the reviewed CLI observe, inspects the exact expected image ID and reads its source labels, then runs docker inspect for exact ledger container IDs. Every container must use that verified image; container-label inheritance is not assumed. It retains the CLI output and an atomic ledger snapshot, then checks actual container custody. A nonzero inspect result is UNKNOWN, including a missing container; its credits remain held. Each capture uses a new private directory, a maximum of 90 seconds and 4 MiB of output per command. One capture has at most 128 held generations, 131 commands, 16 MiB of raw command output and 120 seconds of elapsed time. These are instrument limits, not product capacity limits or performance targets. Each command deadline uses the smaller of 90 seconds and the remaining episode time after reserving four seconds for exit and cleanup. It records direct process exit codes and refuses incomplete captures. It does not run lifecycle effects. The coordinator places captures before and after the controller commands above. Same-incarnation shutdown ACK joins and the clinical healthy-B/TIME adapters are separate remaining boundaries.

Run a read-only capture only after the coordinator admits the exact prepared pair:

python3 tools/mt-bench/tagged-admission/tagged_capture.py \
  "$PRIVATE_SPEC" "$NEW_CAPTURE_DIRECTORY"

The owner-readable-only JSON spec contains kind equal to m7-tagged-admission-observation-v1, absolute controllerCli and state paths, the reviewed controllerCliSha256, an independently pinned collectorSha256, and expected. The collector fingerprint covers these five source, test and contract files; it is recorded separately and must remain unchanged through the capture. It does not enter the legacy instrument fingerprint. The expected object contains that same kind, the independently checked source pair, immutable image ID, project, working directory and plan hash. It must come from the qualified prepared image and private plan, rather than copying whatever a new observation reports. The output directory must not exist. The driver records the spec and all direct command results before validating them. A failed capture directory is retained unchanged; a new episode needs a new directory and owner decision.

docs.title: ns2parquet
docs.text:
Living document, last changed 2026-04-11 at f0bdab912.

Convert Nightscout diabetes data (JSON) into columnar Parquet files optimized for research, ML pipelines, and analytics.

Handles data from any AID system — Loop, AAPS, Trio, OpenAPS, or CGM-only setups — and produces a uniform 5-minute research grid with 49 features aligned across patients.

docs.title: Install
docs.text:
ns2parquet requires Python 3.10+ and three packages:

pip install pandas numpy pyarrow

Then run from the repository root:

python3 -m tools.ns2parquet --help

docs.title: ns2parquet Data Dictionary
docs.text:
Living document, last changed 2026-04-12 at 18f504675.

Schema version: ns2parquet v0.3.0

All glucose values are in mg/dL. All timestamps are UTC, millisecond precision. All durations are in minutes. All absorption times are in minutes.

docs.title: Collections
docs.text:
File Records Description entries.parquet CGM readings Sensor glucose, meter BG, calibration treatments.parquet Insulin/carb events Bolus, carbs, temp basal, overrides devicestatus.parquet AID controller state IOB, COB, predictions, pump status profiles.parquet Therapy schedules Basal rates, ISF, CR, targets (expanded) settings.parquet Site configuration Units, plugins, BG thresholds grid.parquet 5-min research grid All features aligned to 5-min intervals

All files include a patient_id column for multi-patient filtering.

docs.title: nsprobe
docs.text:
Living document, last changed 2026-09-23 at 207cad1b3.

Aggregate-only probes that a Nightscout data holder runs on their own data, to confirm or correct the schema claims this repository measured on its own 11-site corpus. The data stays with the holder. What comes back is counts, shares and site-counts in a fixed format that nsprobe compare sets beside this repository's numbers.

  • AGENTS.md: instructions for a coding agent on the holder's machine, including the rules on what may leave it.
  • questions.yaml: the 18 questions (Q00 to Q17), the claim each tests, what our corpus shows, and what an answer would change.
  • reports/nsprobe/baseline/: the same probes run over this repository's corpus.
  • Brief for data holders: docs/60-research/collaboration/external-data-validation-brief.md.

docs.title: Commands
docs.text:
From the repository root:

PYTHONPATH=tools python3 -m nsprobe layout    --src RAW --dest CORPUS --key PRIVATE/key.json
PYTHONPATH=tools python3 -m nsprobe run       --root CORPUS --out OUT --contributor LABEL
PYTHONPATH=tools python3 -m nsprobe census    --root CORPUS --out OUT
PYTHONPATH=tools python3 -m nsprobe warehouse --config warehouse.yaml --out OUT
PYTHONPATH=tools python3 -m nsprobe check     OUT
PYTHONPATH=tools python3 -m nsprobe compare   OUT

Make targets: nsprobe-test (synthetic data), nsprobe-baseline (regenerates reports/nsprobe/baseline/ from externals/ns-data/patients).

docs.title: nsprobe: instructions for a coding agent working on a data holder's machine
docs.text:
Living document, last changed 2026-09-24 at 5ca3c009c.

You are running on the machine of someone who holds Nightscout data: raw exports from many sites, a flattened analysis warehouse, or both. The Nightscout ecosystem alignment repository (this repository) wants that data to confirm or correct the schema claims it measured on a small corpus. The data never leaves this machine. What leaves is a directory of aggregate JSON files that you generate with nsprobe, check with nsprobe check, and hand to the person you work for. They decide whether to send it and where.

The questions, and the claim each one tests, are in questions.yaml. Read it first.

docs.title: Rules that do not bend
docs.text:
1. Raw data stays put. Never copy documents, rows, CGM traces, profiles or device logs into a commit, an issue, a pull request, a chat message, a log you paste, or a file outside the data holder's own storage. This applies to this repository and to any repository of theirs.
  2. Only nsprobe output is returned. If a task below needs a number that nsprobe does not produce, compute it as a pooled aggregate (counts, shares, rank correlations), apply the same site threshold (a value is named only if at least 3 sites or users produced it), and write it as JSON in the result directory so nsprobe check scans it.
  3. Run python3 -m nsprobe check <out> last, and stop if it fails. Fix the cause, never the checker.
  4. Secrets come from the environment. The warehouse DSN is read from $NSPROBE_DSN (or the variable dsn_env names). Never write a DSN, API secret, token or site URL into a config file, script, commit or result.
  5. The site key is private. nsprobe layout writes a file mapping S001... back to real site names. It identifies people. Keep it outside the corpus and outside the result directory, and never return it.
  6. Results may become public. This repository is public. If the result directory is contributed here, every number in it is published. Tell the person you work for this before they send anything.
  7. This measures data shape, not therapy. Nothing here evaluates whether anyone's settings or dosing are right, and no result should be phrased as if it did.

docs.title: nsschema — evidence-driven schema tooling
docs.text:
Living document, last changed 2026-11-10 at 3ec0260a0.

Turns real Nightscout documents into evidence about what the document model actually is, reconciles that against specs/openapi/, and generates the typed artifacts the modernization work needs from a single source.

docs.title: Why
docs.text:
docs/archive/tenancy/nightscout-multitenancy-discussion-2026-09-09.md §6.4 identifies the problem this package exists to solve: a field's type is currently declared, or implied, in four places that drift — the OpenAPI spec, any boundary validator, a mongoose Schema, and the Postgres column type. The fix is one source of truth with generated consumers. Before committing to a source of truth, though, the spec has to be right: §6.5 found a real bug class caused by a hand-maintained field list diverging from the data.

So: measure first, commit second.

docs.title: CGM ingestion retirement — preserved evidence harnesses
docs.text:
Living document, last changed 2026-09-16 at 1a10007b4.

Why this directory exists. These are the harnesses that produced the reproduced findings behind the decision to retire the legacy Dexcom bridge and MiniMed CareLink ingestion paths (modernization parcel 4). They were written into a session scratchpad under /tmp and would have been lost. A completeness critic flagged that on 2026-09-15: the evidence for deleting a CGM ingestion path was not durable. Preserved here on 2026-09-16.

This matters because of a rule this programme earned the hard way: every backfix-register claim that had to be retracted was derived from reading source, and not one that began with a reproduction has been. These files are the reproductions. Without them, the findings below revert to read-derived — which is the evidential class that keeps being wrong.

docs.title: Provenance and status
docs.text:
• Copied verbatim from the session scratchpad; not yet reviewed, tidied, or wired into any runner. Treat them as raw evidence, not as maintained QC harnesses.
  • Some are one-shot probes with hard-coded paths into externals/work/* worktrees and will not run unchanged. Promoting the load-bearing ones into real harnesses beside the existing tools/qc/*-arm.js files is outstanding work.
  • No vendor endpoint was contacted and no real account or credential was used in producing any of these. Fixtures are synthetic throughout; the one credential-looking string is synthetic-account / synthetic-password, and the one database URL reads PGPASSWORD from the environment against 127.0.0.1.

docs.title: Write compatibility between two cgm-remote-monitor trees
docs.text:
Living document, last changed 2026-11-01 at 44cb0a899.

Contributor-facing.

These tools compare what the write-contract matrix (tools/qc/write-contract-matrix.js) measures on a release tree and on a later tree, explain every cell that differs, and turn the result into the datasets of the living site page 16.0.0 write compatibility. Every record the matrix writes is synthetic test data in a throwaway database.

docs.title: Where things are
docs.text:
