docs.title: Evaluator-owned settings: prepared native PostgreSQL acceptance
docs.text:
Living document, last changed 2026-11-12 at 88854e7b0.

Status: PREPARED; REPINNED J; NATIVE RUN UNMEASURED. The coordinator must release the exact native window before activation. A Unix-socket-only transport blocker is recorded below; repinning alone does not qualify that transport. This external instrument does not change application source, test tiers, deployment source, the image, or the primary baseline source pack. It is outside that pack's existing paths.

Frozen source anchors independently inspected during preparation:

  • Core J: debcc2c7a44fb812b342d0e524ff0611045094d1.
  • Deployment J: 2e9afbb6906441e096e9e86e892cc44073d5b0ae.
  • Supplied, not independently inspected here: image sha256:e0cadd35872c43fa63602d6c8945952383df462aef69d72a5465378b0e20cd77, binding prefix 56183.

The existing native postgres-secrets.integration.test.js checks settings persistence and unsafe tables; registry-realtime-settings.integration.test.js checks persisted realtime/API presentation and finite configuration reads. They do not exercise this evaluator boot-owned revalidating reader. This instrument reuses the exact candidate's tests/fixtures/evaluator-preview-lab.js, its clinical/replay migrations and teardown, and the owned settings/operator-policy migration catalogues. It boots actual evaluator-preview.boot in process. An external readCurrent observer captures the reader that boot supplies; it forwards every call unchanged. Subsequent settings probes use that same owned reader and actual load.readCurrent, with real PostgreSQL SQL and role checks. No driver/module replacement or SQL delay is used.

This is a source fixture, not a running image/full serve/operation-cohort qualification. It has no HTTP listener, registry provisioning, Vault, pool membership partitioning or production operation-window composition. Static A/B tenants are the existing fixture's synthetic roster. The coordinator still owns image role gates, clinical/TIME checks, the eight tiers, enabled corpus and browser acceptance. Cleanup-end uncertainty remains unit-mock coverage; this instrument does not pretend PostgreSQL termination proves a failed Client.end.

docs.title: Preparation checks (no activation)
docs.text:
From this directory:

node --check run.cjs
node offline.test.cjs
# Optional explicit-source constructor/parse check, without connect:
NS_SETTINGS_SOURCE_CORE=/absolute/path/to/frozen-core node offline.test.cjs
node run.cjs --plan

These verify instrument guard/control behavior only. A plan is never acceptance. The offline observer uses a synthetic EventEmitter to check forwarding and accounting; it supplies no PostgreSQL or clinical evidence.

docs.title: M7 joined receipt gate
docs.text:
Living document, last changed 2026-11-12 at e0624657c.

A cheap, read-only recorded-evidence checker. It runs no application, database, Docker, browser, cloud job or test campaign, changes no queue state, and emits no receipt. A passing check validates an independently selected expectation against captured proof; it does not manufacture acceptance or infer runtime equivalence. The current failed D5 UNIT campaign cannot pass it.

python3 tools/queue/gates/m7_joined_receipt.py \
  --expected /reviewed/m7-expectation.json \
  --receipt /captured/m7-receipt.json --evidence-root /captured \
  --scope acceptance
python3 -m unittest discover -s tools/queue/gates -p test_m7_joined_receipt.py -v

Exit 0 prints PASS with the exact verified scopes and RECORDED_EVIDENCE_ONLY. Exit 1 prints a bounded REFUSED M7_* code. The files and their contents are never printed. Artifact reads reject traversal/symlinks and duplicate JSON keys; at most 256 files, 16 MiB per file and 64 MiB total are read. Python bytecode writing is off. An absent or oversized capture is refusal, not a reason to trim evidence to pass.

docs.title: Independent expectation and receipt
docs.text:
The coordinator maintains the expectation separately from the receipt. Queue gates must pin that reviewed expectation, never derive it from the candidate receipt. There is no production expectation or PASS receipt in this change. Unit fixtures exist only in owned temporary directories with explicitly synthetic identities.

Expectation fields:

  • version: 1, kind: "m7-joined-expectation".
  • identity: exact pair: {core, deploy}, imageId: "sha256:...", and instrument content SHA-256. Source commits are full lowercase 40-character hashes.
  • artifacts: reviewed relative-path → SHA-256 map from captured artifact manifests. Every referenced file must match both this independent pin and its receipt reference.
  • pending: all eight tier names plus corpus, each {count, reason}. A known one pending is allowed only when explicitly pinned with a reason (the D5 UNIT exception was the absent external VIEWS_CORPUS_DIR moment-date corpus); zero is not a universal requirement. A different count refuses.
  • corpusCommand: the actual enabled-corpus command ID in the worker result. corpusSuites: the full selected frozen-source inventory from the corpus runner. Missing, duplicate or extra selected suites refuse. The gate does not discover applicability or silently reduce this list.
  • Nonempty criteria and controls: the coordinator's required native, pinned-client, clinical, OIDC, image/source, prcheck and semantic-control checklist. This is the policy boundary: eight tiers alone do not choose that checklist for an operator.

Receipt fields use the existing remote-seam vocabulary: version: 1, kind: "joined-acceptance", status: "PASS", flat pair, imageId, instrument, plus claims, the artifact references and required proofs below. evidenceSha256 is the hash of the referenced worker campaign result. These fields alone never pass the gate. Diagnostic receipts are refused even if someone labels them PASS.

An artifact reference is exactly {path, sha256}. All paths are relative to the explicit evidence root (default: the receipt's parent). Earlier committed evidence can be referenced beneath an alignment-root evidence directory; do not use .. or symlinks. Raw private runner artifacts may stay private: the checker reads only selected references and prints neither contents nor paths.

docs.title: tools/review/ — the dev-cycle review harness
docs.text:
Living document, last changed 2026-09-24 at af0d7309b.

Brings up one real Nightscout per candidate state, seeds each identically through the real HTTP API, and measures the difference between them.

Plan and per-unit acceptance criteria: docs/30-design/remedial/dev-cycle-review-harness-plan-2026-09-17.md.

docs.title: Run it
docs.text:
export NSREVIEW_ROOT=/var/tmp/nsreview        # anywhere with ~2 GB free
tools/review/nsctl.sh init                    # clone + private node_modules, once
tools/review/run.sh                           # boot, seed, probe, red-control

Whole cycle measured at 16.7 s for six states on 2026-09-17. run.sh is idempotent: it resets and re-seeds every state each time.

Individual states:

tools/review/nsctl.sh add   PAIR rc/2026-09-dev-cycle
tools/review/nsctl.sh reset PAIR production   # stop, DROP db, start
tools/review/nsctl.sh url   PAIR              # open this in a browser
tools/review/nsctl.sh status
tools/review/nsctl.sh stop  --all

docs.title: Journey lab: walk the user journeys by hand
docs.text:
Living document, last changed 2026-09-26 at 62e00291a.

Contributor-facing. Synthetic data only: never point this at a real site, and never connect a phone that doses a real person to it. Nothing here is medical advice. Every therapy value in the lab is a made-up test value.

This lab stands up Nightscout sites configured the way a Loop, Trio or AndroidAPS user configures them. You play the person in a browser. The lab plays the phone: each fire step sends exactly what the real app sends, copied from the app's source code, with the source lines cited in clients.js. The journeys, and what "working" means at each step, are in the journey map. This file is the script for walking them.

file what it does lab.sh starts, seeds and stops the sites; fire runs a step journey.js the steps: what each app does, sent as the app sends it; prints one line per request clients.js the request builders for Loop, Trio, AAPS (3.4 v3, 3.4 v1, 4.0-dev), the followers and the web page itself, each citing its source household.js a deterministic synthetic household (meals, doses, overrides, site changes) used to backfill days of data apns-log.js, preload.js a fake Apple push server that logs every Loop remote command the site sends, and the redirect that points the site at it fake-share.js a fake Dexcom Share server over HTTPS. The cgm-* sites run the real nightscout-connect Dexcom driver against it, so login, polling, backfill and the Dexcom-to-Nightscout mapping are the connector's own REAL-APPS.md the track for people who can run the real apps with simulated pumps

docs.title: Setup
docs.text:
From the root of the alignment repository:

git -C externals/cgm-remote-monitor-official worktree add --detach "$PWD/externals/work/crm-journey-rc" official/dev   # the candidate
git -C externals/cgm-remote-monitor-official worktree add --detach "$PWD/externals/work/crm-journey-1508" 92d08342    # 15.0.8, optional
export LAB_RC=$PWD/externals/work/crm-journey-rc
export LAB_REF=$PWD/externals/work/crm-journey-1508     # optional: `up --ref <site>` runs the same site on 15.0.8
export LAB_STATE=$HOME/journey-lab-state                # outside any git tree: holds the API secret and tokens
tools/review/journey-lab/lab.sh prep                    # npm ci, once per worktree
tools/review/journey-lab/lab.sh up                      # every site; or name some: up loop cp-trio rep-aaps
tools/review/journey-lab/lab.sh urls                    # addresses and the sharing tokens
  • Needs: docker (mongo:7), n with node 22.22.0, curl and openssl.
  • Ports: sites on 153xx and 15.0.8 copies on 153xx+50, MongoDB on 27095, fake APNs on 17601, fake Dexcom Share on 17602. All bind to 127.0.0.1.
  • Logging in: every site is AUTH_DEFAULT_ROLES=denied, so the page asks you to log in. Use the API secret in $LAB_STATE/secret; the lab never prints it.
  • Time zone: profiles and meal times use this machine's time zone, or LAB_TZ.
  • Starting over: up <site> gives that site a fresh, empty database.
  • Keeping a site fresh: seeded data ages, and after about 15 minutes the pages show stale warnings and sound alarms. lab.sh live <site> keeps that site's phone uploading every 5 minutes (a reading, device status, doses); lab.sh live stop <site> ends it. down stops all of them. lab.sh live <site> cgm sends readings only, as a separate CGM uploader would: no device status, so COB and IOB stay the site's own treatment-based values (use it when a check is about the site's COB; a device status with COB takes precedence). fire <site> cgm-tick <hours> back-fills the last hours of readings the same way.
  • COB needs carbs_hr: the lab's Loop and AAPS profiles have none, so the site's own COB stays 0 with them. fire <site> editor-save saves a Profile Editor profile (carbs_hr 20) when a check needs COB to move.

docs.title: Journey lab: the real-app track
docs.text:
Living document, last changed 2026-09-26 at 81dbd8b97.

Contributor-facing. For testers who can run Loop, Trio or AndroidAPS against a lab site with a simulated pump and CGM. Synthetic data only: never connect a phone that doses a real person to a lab site. Never connect a lab app to your real Nightscout. Not medical advice.

The main lab (README.md) plays the phone with scripted requests copied from each app's source code. Some checks can only be proven by the real app, because they depend on the app's own logic, and the lab's emulations of that logic are only as good as our reading of it:

journey step why only a real app proves it J1.A2, J1.B3: settings import at onboarding Loop's and Trio's import code decides; the lab's connect step only predicts it (clients.js canImport) J1.B3: AAPS replacing its local profile from the site AAPS's NsIncomingDataProcessor decides; the lab's accept-check only predicts it J3.3: a careportal temp target or profile switch reaching AAPS; a temp target reaching Trio the same: the app's download and accept rules J3.3, J5.4: a Loop remote command arriving on the phone needs real Apple push (APNs) credentials and a phone; the lab's fake APNs server only shows what would have been sent J2: the app's own IOB/COB versus the site's pills the lab's numbers are synthetic J1.C: what an app already in use sends when Nightscout is added (Loop's anchors, Trio's 24 h, AAPS's full history) the lab replays what the code reads as doing; the timing race in Loop is inferred J1.D: what a reinstall imports, and what it silently changes restore emulates each app's import code

docs.title: 1. A lab site the phone can reach
docs.text:
The lab binds every site to 127.0.0.1. For a phone you need the site on your local network over HTTPS. The apps expect HTTPS, and certificates on phones are strict.

  1. Start one site, e.g. tools/review/journey-lab/lab.sh up loop (or trio, aaps, cp-*).
  2. Put a reverse proxy with a certificate the phone trusts in front of it. For example, Caddy with its internal CA: 
    lab.local:8443 {
  tls internal
  reverse_proxy 127.0.0.1:15301
}
    Then install Caddy's root certificate on the phone (iOS: install the profile, then Settings → General → About → Certificate Trust Settings; Android: Settings → Security → Install certificate).
  3. Behind a proxy, Nightscout needs TRUST_PROXY set correctly (see the 15.0.9 release notes, "TRUST_PROXY"). Add it to the site's flags in lab.sh for this track.
  4. A public tunnel (ngrok, Cloudflare Tunnel) also works. It puts the lab site on the internet, so use a fresh lab state directory (a new API secret) and take the tunnel down afterwards.

The API secret is in $LAB_STATE/secret. Type it into the app; don't paste it anywhere else.

docs.title: Storage-interface differentials
docs.text:
Living document, last changed 2026-10-26 at fbad0ef1f.

Contributor-facing. Three checks used to gate ST-FILTER and ST-READS (next-gen plan §5.1, queue item ST-FILTER-READS). Each one takes a cgm-remote-monitor worktree and a MongoDB URI, and treats a live mongod as the authority. Install mingo first with npm ci in this directory; it is never added to cgm-remote-monitor's package.json.

script compares measured on feat/storage-filter (2026-10-26) filter-differential.js <crm> <uri> [n] [seed] a MongoDB query document against toMongo(fromMongo(f)) from lib/storage/filter.js, as result sets on mongod, plus refusals: wherever mongod refuses f, the bridge must refuse too. A mingo arm is reported separately as an oracle check. 50172510: 5,467/5,467 (seed 20261026) and 11,467/11,467 (seed 777), 0 unexpected rejections or acceptances v1-read-differential.js <crm> <uri> [n] [seed] for real API v1 query strings, the document dev's driver path sends (query.js and each module's wrappers, entries' pattern routes, the treatment fallback key) against the branch's interface path (lib/server/storage-reads.js), as returned ids in order or the same mongod error b752971c: 2,954/2,954, 860 of them the same mongod error, 28,998 documents compared v1-http-differential.js <dev tree> <branch tree> <uri> [outDir] 700 API v1 GET requests answered by two trees over identically seeded databases: status, content type and body (Express's HTML 500 page compared on its first line, since its stack trace names file paths) b752971c against dev 7ad3a67f: 700/700 identical (550 × 200, 61 × 400, 89 × 500)

probe-mongod.js <crm> <uri> prints how mongod answers the edge shapes the filter tree pins ($exists operands, regex flags as js-bson sends them, $options letters).

Non-vacuity. Two first runs were vacuous and were caught only by reading the outcome mix: 681 of 700 HTTP requests were 404s because the harness mounted the API at the wrong path, and the read differential dated its documents from a fixed clock, so query.js's default date window excluded most of them. Read the status mix and the document count before reading "0 mismatches". The older roundtrip.js (a mingo-only round trip) passed 4,000/4,000 on the September filter.js, which filter-differential.js fails on 60 of 4,000; use it only alongside the mongod check.

docs.title: Running the cgm-remote-monitor suite for T1.2
docs.text:
Living document, last changed 2026-09-14 at 43f309f23.

Four things block a clean run on this machine and none of them is obvious from the repo. Recorded so the next person (or agent) does not rediscover them.

Worktree: externals/work/crm-seam, branch seam/t1-2-storage-interface, based on origin/chore/nightscout-modernization @ 0a4109f6 (decision D9).

docs.title: 1. The branch refuses this host's Node
docs.text: engines requires ^22.23.2 || ^24.20.0; the host has v24.15.0, and the server exits with ERROR: Node v24.15.0 is not supported rather than degrading. The suite therefore runs inside node:24-bookworm (24.21.0) via run-crm-tests.sh. node_modules contains no native builds, so the host's npm ci output is reusable inside the container.

docs.title: Static site (MkDocs Material)
docs.text:
Living document, last changed 2026-11-08 at b1b65c74a.

Contributor-facing. Builds a browsable copy of this repository's documentation. It is deployed only by the maintainer, from a local build, on the gh-pages branch (see Publishing). Every page carries <meta name="robots" content="noindex, nofollow"> and the site root serves a robots.txt with Disallow: /.

docs.title: Build and serve
docs.text:
The build needs a pseudonym key (see Participant IDs):

# one-time: the key file, outside the repository (back it up; see Participant IDs)
mkdir -p -m 700 ~/.config/nightscout-alignment
(umask 077; openssl rand -hex 32 > ~/.config/nightscout-alignment/pseudonym.key)
make site        # creates tools/site/.venv on first run, stages, builds build/site/
make serve       # builds, then serves build/site/ at http://127.0.0.1:8765/
make serve SITE_PORT=8790
make site-check  # builds, then fails unless the content scan passes, noindex is on
                 # 100% of HTML and robots.txt exists
make site-clean  # removes build/site-src, build/site and the report files

A full build takes under a minute. build/site-report.json records what was staged, excluded and rewritten; build/site-mkdocs.log keeps the MkDocs log.

docs.title: Exclusions
docs.text: tools/site/exclusions.yaml lists glob patterns for tracked paths that must not be published, each with an axis, a reason and who decided it (the schema is in the file's header). An excluded file is not staged, and every link to it becomes the plain text (not published). The report counts matches per entry, so an entry that matches nothing is visible.

docs.title: Content scan (fails closed)
docs.text: tools/site/scan.py looks at every staged text file for four kinds of hit: email (not a role, placeholder or SSH-remote address), ns-host (a hosted Nightscout hostname that is not a placeholder), token (credential-shaped values), and payload (request-shaped strings for defect classes still live on the shipping release). Any hit whose (path, kind) pair is not in tools/site/scan-allowlist.yaml fails make site and make site-check, and the stale build/site/ is removed. Output names the path, kind and count, never the matched text. To clear a hit, fix the text at its source, or add an allowlist entry with a reason, and never copy the matched text into it.

docs.title: Participant IDs
docs.text:
The repository keeps the data commons' own participant IDs (odc- plus eight digits). The site never shows them. tools/site/pseudonym.py rewrites every one in staged text, link targets, generated pages, nav entries and staged file names to odc-p-<first 8 hex of HMAC-SHA256(key, id)>. A short form (odc- plus 2 to 7 digits) becomes the pseudonym of the one staged full ID it is a prefix of; a short form that matches none or several fails the build. 13-digit odc-<timestamp> record ids are left alone.

  • The key comes from SITE_PSEUDONYM_KEY, then NS_PSEUDONYM_KEY, then the file ~/.config/nightscout-alignment/pseudonym.key (override the path with SITE_PSEUDONYM_KEY_FILE). There is no default: with IDs present and no key, make site fails. make exports the key to the build and never echoes it.
  • This is the one key shared with ns2parquet (docs/30-design/ns2parquet-keyed-pseudonyms.md). Make it once, keep it outside the repository, and back it up. The same key gives byte-identical output; a new key gives new pseudonyms, so keep one key for as long as links to pages whose names carry a pseudonym should stay stable.
  • Neither the key nor any ID-to-pseudonym mapping is written to the repo, the build output or build/site-report.json (it records counts only).
  • The key is kept in two places with the same value: the maintainer's key file, for local builds, and the repository secret SITE_PSEUDONYM_KEY, for the CI job that publishes on each push to main (see Publishing). Set or rotate the secret from the key file without printing it: gh secret set SITE_PSEUDONYM_KEY -R bewest/rag-nightscout-ecosystem-alignment < ~/.config/nightscout-alignment/pseudonym.key. A different value in the secret changes every pseudonym on the site.
  • The participant-id scan kind fails the build and make site-check on any raw odc-<2 to 12 digits> left in build/site-src/ or build/site/ (HTML, search index, sitemap, file names). It cannot be allowlisted.

docs.title: Search index
docs.text:
Material builds its search index from every page, and the browser's search worker loads it on every page view. Unfiltered, this site's index was 24 MB and the worker held about 780 MB under phone emulation (2026-09-30). The staging step now applies tools/site/search.yaml with Material's own mechanisms (search: exclude, search: boost front matter and { data-search-exclude } on headings), without editing any source doc:

  • generated folder-index and gallery pages are left out;
  • outside the keep_full areas (home, overview, releases, queue, design, registers, site/pages), a page is indexed by its title and first ## section only, so it stays findable by title;
  • the overview pages, releases, the home page and REVIEWER-ONBOARDING are boosted.

SITE_SEARCH_POLICY=off make site builds without the policy (for comparison). The report records the index size and what the policy did.

docs.title: Page labels: Record or Living
docs.text:
Published pages must be production-ready and accurate, unless they are an explicit snapshot or point-in-time record (maintainer rule, 2026-09-30). So every markdown page carries a label under its title:

  • Record: the file name has a YYYY-MM-DD date. Banner: "Record as of . A point-in-time document; it is not kept up to date."
  • Living: every other page. Line: "Living document, last changed at ." Dates come from one git log --name-only pass.
  • tools/site/page-kinds.yaml sets a path to either kind (a record with an undated name needs as_of). The build report lists dated pages whose names suggest a living document (record_candidates_for_living) for review; none is overridden automatically.

docs.title: site/pages
docs.text:
Committed rich HTML pages go in site/pages/. They are copied into the site (plus the noindex meta if missing) and listed in the nav under Pages. Rule: rich pages are committed here; artifacts are only for private drafts. Every page needs an entry in site/pages/pages.yaml:

  • kind: snapshot needs as_of, and the page must show a banner (an element with data-site-banner="snapshot" naming that date).
  • kind: living needs sources and source_commit. The build fails, naming the page and the source, when a source changed after source_commit. Re-render the page (for the programme page: tools/site/.venv/bin/python tools/site/render_programme.py), check it, and move source_commit to the commit that last changed the source.

docs.title: API reference pages (Redoc)
docs.text:
An OpenAPI file is published as a living page rendered by tools/site/render_apis.py with Redoc. Its pages.yaml entry has exactly one source (the OpenAPI file) and an api: block: a status (current, de-facto, proposed, draft-pr or superseded), a one-sentence note the reader needs before trusting the page, and optionally see:, a tracked .md page (such as the design that replaces the file) the banner links to. The script:

  • refuses to render a source with uncommitted changes, or one that fails redocly lint (Redocly CLI 1.34.0, recommended rules; warnings are printed);
  • builds the page with tools/site/redoc-template.hbs, which puts the status, the note, and a link to the source at the commit that last changed it in a banner at the top;
  • loads the Redoc runtime (2.4.0) from jsDelivr with its integrity hash, and no Google fonts.
  • adds a Schemas group naming every schema in components.schemas, built into a temporary copy beside the source (Redoc otherwise draws a schema only where an operation refers to it, so a schemas-only file showed nothing).

The build fails when an API page's banner does not carry the status in pages.yaml. To render: tools/site/.venv/bin/python tools/site/render_apis.py [NAME.html] (needs node/npx; network on first run), then move source_commit to the commit it prints.

docs.title: Publishing
docs.text:
On each push to main, the site job in .github/workflows/ci.yml runs after the other CI checks pass. It runs make site-publish with the SITE_PSEUDONYM_KEY secret and pushes the new gh-pages commit (a fast-forward; a rejected push means someone published in between, and the next push to main builds on theirs). Without the secret it skips the publish with a warning. A failed make site-check, for example a living page whose sources moved past its source_commit, fails the job and publishes nothing: re-render the page, move source_commit and push again.

Locally, the same command works as before:

make site-publish refuses unless the working tree is clean, HEAD is on a remote branch (git branch -r --contains HEAD), SITE_PSEUDONYM_KEY is set and make site-check plus the staged-Markdown Mermaid syntax check pass. It then fetches origin/gh-pages, copies build/site/ plus .nojekyll into the worktree ../rag-alignment-gh-pages (created on first use), and commits it as one new commit whose parent is origin/gh-pages, with the source sha and build date in its message. It prints a plain git push, which is a fast-forward; if someone published in between, the push is rejected rather than overwriting their build, and re-running make site-publish builds on theirs. A build identical to origin/gh-pages is not committed. It never pushes.

  • make site-publish DRY_RUN=1 skips the remote check and stages the files in the worktree without committing.
  • make site-publish PURGE=1 makes the build the only commit of a fresh orphan gh-pages instead, so earlier builds leave the branch's history (for removing something that should not have been published; copies may already exist elsewhere). It prints git push --force-with-lease against the gh-pages it fetched.
  • One-time repository setting: Settings → Pages → Build and deployment → Deploy from a branch → gh-pages / (root).

docs.title: structure-diagrams — the overview's control-structure drawings
docs.text:
Living document, last changed 2026-10-18 at 95b6ca7cb.

Contributor-facing. Sources and renderer for the drawings on Control structures of the ecosystem and the proposals.

  • inputs/*.yaml: one drawing each. Nodes have a level (0 = top) and a column, a kind (authority, entity, org, commons, human, process), and optionally status: proposed, a group and a zoom label naming the drawing that opens the box up. Edges have a kind (control, feedback, funding, data) and optionally status: proposed. views lists stakeholder views: the same drawing with everything not touching focus greyed.
  • Optional icon on a node: a file name in icons/ without .svg, drawn at the box's left to say what the box does (factory, landmark, scale, user, users, key-round, smartphone, syringe, …). icons/ holds only the Lucide icons in use, copied from lucide-static 0.460.0 with its ISC LICENSE; to add one, copy its SVG from that package and add a line to ICON_KEY in render.py, which also writes icon-key.svg.
  • Scenarios: scenarios: [believed, actual, emerging], base: false and one view per scenario draw the same structure several times on one layout. An edge or node with in: [...] appears only in those scenarios; labels: {scenario: text} changes an edge's label there, and on a node changes who or what sits in that box (see inputs/idea-sponsor-or-operate.yaml). Edge kinds authority (where a right to act comes from) and discretion (control exercised at the controller's own choice) exist for these drawings. See inputs/1-authority.yaml.
  • Optional layout keys: bands (horizontal bands behind rows, e.g. legal / organisational / technical), and per edge route (straight, z, l, corridor), via and label_side. Use them to move a line that crosses the middle of a drawing; see the docstring of render.py.

  • render.py writes docs/00-overview/perspective/diagrams/<name>.svg, one <name>--<view>.svg per view, and legend.svg. It needs only Python and PyYAML. It places every box on a (column, level) grid and routes lines at right angles; chosen by the grid layout lab, which keeps the Graphviz renderer it replaced as baseline_dot.py.

  • access_charts.py draws two charts that are not control structures, 1-access-ladder.svg and 1-access-matrix.svg, from access/devices.yaml (one record per device line, mechanism level only). It reuses render.py's font and text measure.

  • history_timeline.py draws history-timeline.svg into docs/00-overview/observations/diagrams/ from history/timeline.yaml: one row per dated row of the chronology, each naming its section, date cell and words. test_history_timeline.py fails naming any row that no longer matches HISTORY.md, and checks the committed figure; make history-timeline draws it and make diagrams-svg-check runs the test.

python3 tools/structure-diagrams/render.py            # every input
python3 tools/structure-diagrams/access_charts.py     # the access ladder and matrix
python3 tools/structure-diagrams/render.py tools/structure-diagrams/inputs/z2-agreement.yaml

The SVGs are committed so the drawings show on GitHub and on the site without a build step. Each sits on its own light card, so it reads the same in either colour scheme. Keep each drawing to one idea and roughly 6–10 boxes; put detail in a drawing one zoom level down.

docs.title: GAP-CARB-001: Incompatible COB Semantics
docs.text:
Description: Loop's predictive curve-based COB differs fundamentally from oref0's deviation-inferred COB, making cross-system comparisons invalid.

Affected Systems: Loop, AAPS, Trio, oref0, Nightscout

Impact: - Nightscout displays COB without model context - Users switching systems see different COB values for same meal - Reports aggregate incompatible metrics - Cannot compare algorithm performance across systems

Example: - Same meal: Loop COB = 45g (curve projection), oref0 COB = 38g (deviation-inferred)

Remediation: Nightscout should store and display COB with model type annotation in devicestatus schema.

docs.title: GAP-CARB-002: No Standard Carb Absorption Data Format
docs.text:
Description: Each AID system stores carb absorption data in incompatible formats, preventing data interchange and replay.

Affected Systems: Loop, AAPS, Trio, oref0

Storage Formats: | System | Format | |--------|--------| | Loop | Per-entry absorption timeline array | | oref0 | Aggregate mealCOB scalar | | AAPS | autosensData.cob with 5-min deltas | | Trio | meal_data.mealCOB scalar |

Impact: - Cannot replay absorption data across systems - No standard for test vectors - Limits algorithm conformance testing

Remediation: Define standard absorption event format with timeline, model type, and per-entry tracking.

docs.title: GAP-CARB-003: UAM Detection Variance
docs.text:
Description: Unannounced Meal (UAM) detection algorithms differ significantly across systems, causing inconsistent dosing behavior.

Affected Systems: Loop, AAPS, Trio, oref0

Detection Methods: | System | UAM Approach | |--------|--------------| | Loop | Retrospective correction (implicit via observed absorption) | | oref0 | Explicit deviation slope analysis with 60m delay | | AAPS | enableUAM constraint check | | Trio | enableUAM setting (oref0-derived) |

Impact: - Users experience different dosing behavior with same settings - UAM sensitivity not portable across systems - Documentation doesn't explain behavioral differences

Remediation: Document UAM behavior differences prominently in user guides and Nightscout UI.

docs.title: GAP-CARB-004: min_5m_carbimpact Variance
docs.text:
Scenario: COB Decay Rate Comparison

Description: The min_5m_carbimpact parameter in oref0/AAPS defaults to 3 mg/dL/5m for normal diets but 8 mg/dL/5m for low-carb diets. This significantly affects how quickly COB decays when no absorption is detected.

Source: oref0 cob.js#L189-L194

Impact: - Same carb entry produces different COB timelines with different min_5m_carbimpact settings - "Zombie carbs" (COB that never depletes) behavior differs - Cross-user comparison invalid without knowing this setting

Possible Solutions: 1. Include min_5m_carbimpact in devicestatus 2. Standardize on a single default across configurations 3. Document as critical comparison caveat

Status: Under discussion

docs.title: GAP-CARB-005: COB Maximum Limits Differ
docs.text:
Scenario: Large Meal Handling

Description: oref0/AAPS enforce a hard maxCOB cap (default 120g), while Loop has no such limit. This means the same large meal (e.g., 150g carbs) produces different COB values.

Source: - oref0 total.js#L108 - Loop has no equivalent cap

Impact: - Large carb entries produce different COB in different systems - Safety implications for high-carb meals - Users unaware of capping may be confused by COB discrepancies

Possible Solutions: 1. Loop adds configurable maxCOB option 2. oref0 makes maxCOB configurable with no-limit option 3. Document as known difference with safety implications

Status: Under discussion

docs.title: GAP-NOCTURNE-001: V4 endpoints are Nocturne-specific
docs.text:
Scenario: Cross-project API compatibility

Description: Nocturne introduces V4 API endpoints (/api/v4/...) that provide enhanced functionality not present in cgm-remote-monitor. These endpoints have no cross-project standard.

Affected Systems: Nocturne, any clients adopting V4

Source: externals/nocturne/src/API/Nocturne.API/Controllers/V4/

Impact: - Clients using V4 endpoints won't work with cgm-remote-monitor - No interoperability guarantee for V4 features - Potential ecosystem fragmentation

Possible Solutions: 1. Document V4 endpoints as optional extensions 2. Propose V4 endpoints as Nightscout RFC 3. Mark V4 as Nocturne-only, maintain V3 parity

Status: Partially remediated for Nightscout source in nightscout-connect dev (6dfc4f0): entries, treatments, devicestatus, and profiles are fetched and output. Glooko now emits entries and treatments; remaining gaps apply to sources without devicestatus/profile coverage.

docs.title: GAP-NOCTURNE-002: Rust oref implementation may diverge
docs.text:
Scenario: Algorithm consistency across implementations

Description: Nocturne contains a native Rust implementation of oref algorithms (src/Core/oref/). This independent implementation may produce different results than the JavaScript oref0/oref1.

Affected Systems: Nocturne, any system comparing algorithm outputs

Source: externals/nocturne/src/Core/oref/Cargo.toml

Impact: - Potential calculation differences (IOB, COB, dosing) - Difficult to debug cross-implementation issues - No conformance test suite between implementations

Possible Solutions: 1. Create cross-implementation test vectors 2. Document any intentional algorithm differences 3. Generate reference outputs for comparison

Status: Under discussion

Related Requirements: REQ-NOCTURNE-002

docs.title: GAP-NOCTURNE-003: SignalR to Socket.IO bridge adds latency
docs.text:
Scenario: Real-time data streaming

Description: Nocturne uses SignalR for real-time updates, with a bridge to Socket.IO for legacy client compatibility. This adds latency and complexity.

Affected Systems: Nocturne, Socket.IO clients (xDrip+, etc.)

Source: externals/nocturne/src/Web/packages/bridge/

Impact: - Additional latency for real-time glucose updates - Extra failure point in data pipeline - Clients must support either SignalR or use bridge

Possible Solutions: 1. Maintain parallel Socket.IO and SignalR endpoints 2. Measure and document latency impact 3. Provide native SignalR clients for major platforms

Status: Documented - Detailed analysis

Measured Impact (2026-01-30): 5-10ms additional latency per message - acceptable for CGM data.

docs.title: GAP-BRIDGE-001: Missing clients Event in Bridge
docs.text:
Scenario: Displaying connected client count

Description: Nocturne SignalR→Socket.IO bridge does not forward client count updates. cgm-remote-monitor emits clients event when watchers join/leave.

Affected Systems: Nocturne bridge, legacy web UIs

Source: externals/nocturne/src/Web/packages/bridge/src/lib/socketio-server.ts

Impact: - Legacy web UI may show incorrect watcher count - No visibility into connected clients

Possible Solutions: 1. Add clients event emission to bridge 2. Use SignalR-native client count mechanism

Status: Documented

docs.title: GAP-BRIDGE-002: No Compression in Bridge
docs.text:
Scenario: High-bandwidth real-time streaming

Description: Nocturne bridge does not enable Socket.IO compression. cgm-remote-monitor uses .compress(true) on broadcasts.

Affected Systems: Nocturne bridge, mobile clients on metered connections

Source: externals/cgm-remote-monitor/lib/server/websocket.js:136 vs externals/nocturne/src/Web/packages/bridge/

Impact: - Higher bandwidth usage - May affect mobile data consumption

Possible Solutions: 1. Enable compression in Socket.IO server config 2. Add .compress(true) to broadcast calls

Status: Documented

docs.title: Cross-Validation Assessment Log
docs.text:
Living document, last changed 2026-03-31 at f525c50f6.

Historical record of cross-implementation validation iterations (A1–A17). Each assessment documents a specific convergence step, the metrics achieved, and bugs/fixes discovered.

Architecture reference: See docs/architecture/cross-validation-assessment.md for current methodology, metrics, and adapter inventory.

Scope: oref0 implementations (JS, Swift, AAPS-JS, AAPS-Kotlin) Vectors: 100 oref0-native + 200 Loop-generated (300 total)

docs.title: Assessment 1: oref0-JS vs Ground Truth
docs.text: The JS adapter wraps externals/oref0/lib/determine-basal — the canonical reference implementation. Compared against prediction trajectories captured from the same algorithm running on a real phone:

docs.title: Decision-Level
docs.text: Metric Value EventualBG exact match 54% EventualBG within ±10 mg/dL 54% EventualBG within ±20 mg/dL 70% EventualBG mean delta EventualBG mean delta +17.0 mg/dL

docs.title: Prediction-Level (IOB/ZT curves)
docs.text: Curve Avg MAE Max MAE Correlation Growing Trend IOB 8.4 mg/dL 49.0 0.91 56/93 vectors ZT 7.9 mg/dL 53.2 0.84 74/96 vectors

docs.title: Root Causes of Divergence
docs.text:
1. IOB array synthesis: The adapter generates a 48-tick exponential decay from a single IOB snapshot (tau = DIA_minutes / 1.85), while the phone had actual dose history for each tick. This creates growing error later in the prediction window.

  2. TV-087 through TV-108: These synthetic vectors have constant BG offsets (~30-200 mg/dL) that inflate MAE. Filtering to TV-001..TV-086 would give tighter agreement.

  3. "No temp required" handling: The JS oref0 returns rate: null when it decides no temp change is needed (e.g., current temp is close enough). This affects 10/30 vectors in the first batch.
